a swamp, a garden with permanent moisture, e.g. Twakasyanga kale mapopwe mubuntolo. = We have already planted maize in the moist garden.

rheum in the eyes, discharge of mucus, pl. mantongwe, e.g. Meso ako alaa buntongwe. = Your eyes are rheumy. *Bana baniini balaa buntongwe nibabuka cifwumofwumo.* = Children have rheum in the eyes when they get up in the morning.

humanity, human qualities, the human personality, e.g. *Buntu bwesu bulakatazya nkaambo mapenzi ajanika mubuumi bwesu mmanji.* = Our human nature is difficult because the sufferings which are found in our life are many.
common humainty, (which we all share) e.g. *Ncibotu kuzyiba kabotu buntususu.* = It is good to understand our common humanity.
variety of goods, e.g. *Iswebo kaindi eyi nyika njomubwene yakazwide bunono, ibuntyolela-ntyolela butaambiki.* = For us long ago the land which you see was full of good things and plenty of food.
smell (pleasant or unpleasant), e.g *Mubwa navwima utobelezya bunumfwu bwatunyama naa tuyuni mutwali kwiinda.* = When a dog is hunting it follows the scent where little animals or birds were passing.
smell (good or bad), e.g. *Ndamvwa bununke bwanyimbaa-salama.* = I could smell the stink of a polecat.
salvation, e.g. *Bununu bwa munjile mbana.* = The salvation of the wild-pig is its children. (The young can come out of the burrow first and may be killed thus saving the mother.)
cotton thread, cotton yarn, e.g. *Amundipe bunweba nsume cibaki cangu.* = Give me cotton thread so that I sew my garment. Also *intali*
a ball of cotton, e.g. *Ndakaula cibulunge cabunweba butuba jilo.* = I bought a ball of white cotton yesterday.
a group of small game, e.g. *Musyokwe ndajana bunyama bulibungene.* = In the bush I found a group of animals gathered together.
animal-like, e.g. *Ooyu munene ujisi micito yabunyama.* = This old man has the behaviour of animals.
tufts or clumps of burnt grass, e.g. *Utani kweendeli mubunyandwa, ulayaswa.* = Do not pass through the tufts of burnt grass, you will be pierced. Also luya.
trepidation, e.g. *Akaambo kakuciswa oyu mwana ulaa bunyangulusigwa.* = Because of sickness this child is in a state of trembling.
ticklishness, e.g. *Utani kundijati kunsi aamaulu, ndimvwa bunyeele.* = Do not touch me under the feet, I feel tickles.

flutes, e.g. *Bana basobana bunyeele bwamatete nobeembela mpongo.* = Children play reed-flutes when they are herding goats. **bunyembe-nyembe** precocity, (i.e. having developed certain abilities or inclinations at an earlier age than usual), e.g. *Kasankwa kangu kalaa bunyembenyembe.* = My little boy is a precocious child. Also bunsengwe-sengwe.
anger, e.g. *Bunyeme bwamuntu bulibonya kumeso.* = The anger of a person is seen in the eyes.
sensitivity, e.g. *Kunsaa maulu ndilaa bunyenguluka.* = The soles of my feet are very sensitive. Also -bunyeele.

small black ants, e.g. *Bunyenyene bwanjila mucisyu.* = Small black ants have got into the relish. *Bunyenyene bulakatazya kwiibula mucibwantu.* = It is hard to take small black ants out of the sweet-beer. Also butandansinga.

poison for arrows or spears, e.g. *Kondibikkila bunyete kumasumo angu.* = Will you put poison for me on my spears. *Banyama bapati balajaigwa abunyete.* = Big animals are killed by poisoned arrows. Also bunete.
brotherhood, sisterhood, e.g. *Bana bali kulwana mubunyina.* = The children were fighting among their own.

the bicycle chain and freewheel, e.g. *Wakandipa kacinga kakwe kapya, nkujana kaciide kulila bunyololo.* = He gave me his new bicycle to find it was just producing the sound of a new bike from the chain and freewheel.
tuft of burnt grass, also bupondondo, zisese (pl. mantoolwani, sing. intoolwani tuft of unburnt grass left by fire, also mancaalizya)

treachery, e.g. *Nkobali bamwi basimbi bajisi nsoni zyabunzele.* = There are some girls who have a shyness which is full of treachery. *Kuti kakuli zyabunzele zicitika, uyakukusisa.* = If some treacherous things are going on, she will hide it from you.
bees-wax, e.g. *Mumpako mutwali kulida buci, twajana bunzuka bunji.* = In the hole where we were collecting honey, we found plenty of bees- wax as well.
fragments, e.g. *Cibiya capandauka mubupaanzi-paanzi.* = The clay pot has been broken into fragments.
small sores on head, dandruff, e.g. *Bupaapa buli mumutwe wangu bula-baba.* = The sores on my scalp are itching.
necklace of small shells, e.g. *Bana babamami bakali kusama bupande-pande munsingo kaindi.* = The children of chiefs used to wear necklaces around the neck in the past.
remnants of shell or skin, as of millipede, e.g. *Ndajana bupande-pande akafwida jongola.* I found the remnants of the shell where a millipede died.

cleverness, cunning, e.g. *Ncendakamulekela mukaintu wangu mbupanusi.* I divorced my wife because of her craftiness. *Uleelede kubaa bupanusi mudolopo kutegwa batakubbidi.* = You need to be on your guard in town so that they do not steal from you.
cooked and sliced dried sweetpotatoe, e.g. *Kojika ceele cabupapa bwacimbwali.* Prepare porridge with slices of sweet-potatoe.

delicacies, e.g. *Bakaunka kucidumba kwakali kuulwa budodoodo abumwi bupapaapa bwamisyobo-misyobo kabati bakalye.* They went to the thatched shelter where they were selling nice food and other delicacies of different sorts so that they could eat.
remnants of shells, e.g. *Bupapa-papa bwanjili bwakali kucaala mulonga nowakali kuzula.* = The remains of shell fish remained behind when the river was high.

conflict, rebellion, e.g. *Mazuba ayo njamweenzya kakuba, pesi nyika yasanduka, bupasi bwakomena cini-cini.* = In those days one could walk freely, but the world has changed, conflict has grown indeed.
seniority, e.g. *Kuvwola mapopwe batobelezya mubupati bwamuntu.* = When giving maize (food for work) they follow the order of seniority.

treachery, e.g. *Bupelenge bwakucenga bantu bapati tabupi kupona kabotu nkaambo bapati inga balasinganya akaambo kakucengwa.* = The treachery of cheating elders does not give one a good life because the elders can curse through being deceived. Also bumpelenge.
suffering, e.g. *Bupenzi bwabantu bataboni mbupati nkaambo zyoonse balangila kucitilwa.* = The suffering of the blind is great because in all things they look to be assisted.

disturbance of peace, e.g. *Mucisi camwami Siatwiinda kuli bupili*ngani.* = There is trouble in the chieftaincy of Siatwiinda. *Bupilingani* bunyonganya bukkale bubotu. = Chaos unsettles peaceful living.
immoral or incorrect conduct, e.g. Bantu bayandisya kubelesya maanu *aabupizili* mukuyandaula *buvwubi.* = People love to use corrupt intelligence in acquiring wealth.
tufts of burnt grass, e.g. Ncibotu kusama mpato kuti koyanda kweenda kabotu *mubupondondo.* = It is good to wear sandals if you want to walk easily on tufts of burnt grass. Also bunyandwa.
state or style of life, e.g *Buponi* bwababbi mbwakuumwa lyoonse. = The life of thieves is in being beaten always.
property-grabbing, e.g. Awalo mukowa wa Bansaka kubupusyi basa! = The Bansaka clan are property-grabbers.
beer on the second day of brewing when it is still sweet, e.g. Twaboola kuzikunywa *bupyaapya.* = We have come to drink sweet beer. Also cipyaapya, matimba.
misbehaviour, e.g. Kasankwa katalomene lyoonse kajanwa *mubupyupyungu.* = A dishonest boy is always caught up in misbehaviour.

hunger for meat, e.g. Kunywa bukoko cipa *busa* kapati. Drinking beer gives a great desire to eat meat. Ndafwa *busa.* I have a longing for meat. Kocijaya mbaambi, katulya nyama, twacimvwa *busa.* Kill a duiker, let us eat the meat, we have a longing for meat.
gum of *mbala* tree, (used to fix spear shafts), e.g. *Bataata* babikka *busaki amasumo.* My father is fixing shafts on the spear-heads with gum.
fluid which causes pain, as snake venom, e.g. *Busaki bwanzoka zimwi mbuli cisasa mbubi.* The venom of certain snakes such as a puff-adder is bad. Also bunyete.
type of edible root, e.g. Tuya kukusya *busala kuloonde.* = We are going to dig the *busala* tuber in the bush. Also lusala, lwidi.
power, effectiveness, e.g. Sena ulasyoma micelo yacintu cisiya *mubusalalo* bwayo kuponya malwazi? = Do you have faith in traditional medicines in their power to cure diseases?
cleanliness, e.g. *Busalalo bwaamunzi* bucesya malwazi. = Cleanliness at home lessens sickness.
fertility, e.g. Kuli *busani* bubotu mumuunda wangu mupya. = There is good fertility in my new field. Eeci cibanda cakalijisi *busani* bubotu kuzisyango. This plain had fertile soil for crops.
boyhood, male genitals, virility, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulibwene bu*sankwa* ncayandisya kulwana. = This boy is aware of his virility and that is why he likes fighting a lot.
a look-out platform, e.g. Mudaala uyamina buyuni *abusansa.* = The old man on the platform is scaring off the birds. Also ngazi
stand of a stadium. e.g. Twakakkede a *busansa* nitwakali kweebelela bbola. = We were sitting in the stand when we were watching the football match.

a platform made of poles rough table for firewood, dry meat or maize, scaffolding, a traditional table, e.g. Amubambe *busanza* bwakubikkila nkuni. = Make a platform on which to place the firewood. Kamuya mukagonke bwalo tuyake *busanza.* Go and cut poles so that we build a storage platform for maize. Also buzalo, cisanza, cizali.

the name given by the midwife, it may refer to the time the child is born. It is the popular name in distinction to the clan name (nguli) e.g. Eli zina lyaabusasa ndipati kumuntu oonse, banji-banji baitizigwa mazina aya. = This popular name is important to every person, many are called by this name.
semen, e.g. Busasi bwabasankwa bamwi tabukwe nguzu zyakuzyala bana. = The sperm of some men is ineffective for producing offspring.
e.g. carelessness, e.g. Mukaintu ulaa busasi, tabanzi kabotu mapopwe mubutala. = A woman who is careless, does not extract maize from the bin neatly. Also buyamba.

sense of commitment, loyalty, e.g. Nindakatumwa kuya kwaanga bataata, ndakabula busayi nkaambo ndakayoowa kutandwa. = When I was sent to arrest my father, I had no sense of loyalty to him because I feared to lose my job.

dregs, as of light beer, e.g. Kozipa buse nkuku. = Give the chickens the dregs of the light beer. Amundigwasye buse bwabukoko nkasanine ngulube. = Please help me with the dregs of the beer so that I feed the pigs. Also busiwa.
a funnel-basket, e.g. Mukaintu wangu akandilukile busebe. = Let my wife make me a funnel-basket. Also musase
meal already sifted, (adj.) e.g. Koleta busu busebe tujisye nsima. = Bring sifted mealie-meal so that we cook nsima.
yeast, e.g. Basimusika babamba tumbuwa abuseezyo. = The marketeers are making buns with yeast. Also bumena.
wild seeds, e.g. Kulya kwabana babayuni ninsozi abusekeseke bwamusyokwe abwamaila. = The food of little birds is grasshoppers and the seeds of the bush and of millet.
bran, e.g. Kotupa busenga tukuku. = Give the chicks bran. Baama baakuleta busenga kucigayo. = Mother has brought bran from the mill. Also buseezyo, bwando
negotiations, e.g. Kumamanino nkujana bamukasya bazyali bamusimbi, busese bwafwa. = In the end it is only to find that the parents of the girl refuse, the negotiations have ended.
very small spots, e.g. Aaya makowa alaa buseseese. = These cucumbers have small spots.
revulsion, e.g. Muntu ulaa da ulaa busesemwa. = A person who is preganant feels revulsion. Also busesi
nausea, e.g. Nindabona tubi twamubwa ndabaa busesi. = When I saw the dog's droppings I felt nauseated.
zyamu bwakamupa busesi. = The remains of water-insects made him feel like vomiting.
a plant with edible tuber, e.g. Ingulube ilabuyanda buseza. = A pig likes an edible tuber.

smoke, e.g. Kujikila munanda kuli busi. = There is smoke when cooking in the house. Aba bana bazwa muŋanda ilaa busi. = These children come from a home which has smoke, i.e. which is industrious. Eeyi nanda yakali kusuka busi kuzwa kumatalikilo. = This house was emitting smoke from the beginning. (i.e. It was always prosperous.)
(as an idiom) Myootokala omu mu Lusaka bwakali busi. = There were a lot of cars in Lusaka.

fruit of Tamarind tree, e.g. Sunu mujike ceele cabusiikka. = To-day you should cook Tamarind porridge. Ulaa nkazi mbuli muntu ulya busiikka. = You are as stubbourn as a person who had eaten the fruit of the Tamarind tree.
heritage, e.g. Tunsiyansiya mbusiilanwa bwazilengwa. = Traditions are the heritage of customs.
base, as of tree or column, e.g. Kavwuma kajisi busiko buzyandamene. = A palm tree has a sturdy base.
night, pl. insiku, e.g. Busiku bwainda ndamvwa kulila kwasyuumbwa. = Last night I heard the growl of a lion. Linyo lyangu lyali kucisa _busiku boonse_. = My tooth was paining the whole night.
a collection of big black warrior ants, e.g. Ndalumwa _busilibi_ mumuunda. = In the field I have been bitten by big black ants. Also _insilibi_.
See _busilibi_
foolishness, e.g. _Busilu_ bwako bukupa kutacibona ncootumwa. = Your stupidity makes you not see what you were sent for. Also _bufwubafwuba_.
cruelty, e.g. _Busimba_, kulisumpula, inceya a butolo tazikatuleli munyika. Cruelty, pride, bad behaviour and laziness, will not rule us in this world.
girlhood before initiation, female genitals, _wabusimbi_ first-born, e.g. (When the speaker is a woman) Ooyu mwana ngowabusimbi bwangu. = This child is my first-born.
what prints a design, e.g. Ivwili lyancinga yangu lyakaleka kusimba nkaambo _busimbo_ bwakamana. = The wheel of my bicycle has stopped making tracks because the tyre-threads are worn.

negotiations for marriage, e.g. Kaindi basankwa bakali kusala beenzinyina kubeleka mulimo _wabusimposo_ kutegwa bakakwate kabotu. = Long ago men would chose friends to carry out the work of negotiating a marrriage for them.
pus, e.g. Cicisa cangu cizwa _busina_. = Pus is coming out of my sore.

ground broken and not yet sown, e.g. _Mubusinde_ tuyakusyanga ndongwe. = We are going to sow groundnuts in the ploughed land. Imvwula yaakuwa tuyakusyanga mapopwe _mubusinde_. = When the rain starts we will plant maize in the ground which was ploughed (in the cold season).
grass for weaving, e.g. Kamuya mukalete _businde_ bubotu tuluke kasasa. = Go and bring good grass for weaving so that we weave a mat.
small flying termites, e.g Inkuku zilya _businkamatwi_ buzwa mulubuwa. = The chickens are eating the small flying termites which are coming out in the court-yard.
prophesy, e.g. Kaindi kwakali _businsimi_ bwini-bwini. = Long ago there was true prophecy.
a very small edible mushroom growing in fields, e.g. Twajika bowa butegwa _busise_. = We have cooked small mushrooms called _busise_.
a type of fruit, e.g. Bataata balayanda kulya _busise_. = My father likes eating _busise_ fruit.
hidden beer, e.g. Bukoko bwabantu boonse bwamana, kwacaala _busise_ bwabataata. = The beer for all the people has finished, there remains the hidden beer of my father.
dregs, e.g. Inkuku amuzipe _busiwa_ bwabukoko. = Give the chickens the dregs of the beer. Also _buse_.
madness, e.g. _Busondosi_ bwakwe bumupa kwiide kulila mwana oyu. = The madness of this child makes him/her just cry. Also _busincinko, bugausi_.
a bud, a sprout, eye, as of potatoe, young maize, e.g. _Busonga_ bwamapopwe bwamanwa bakwale. = The partridges have finished the young shoots of maize. Also _busonje, busonge, mumena_
wisdom, cleverness, e.g. Musankwa ulya wakasondoka akaambo ka_busongo_ bwakaindilila. = That man went mad because of his intelligence which went out of control.
a bud or sprout of grain, e.g. _Busonje_ bwamapopwe tabuli kabotu mwaka uno. = The shoots of the maize are not good this year.
meal, flour, pl. masu, e.g. *Busu bwamaila bulanona.* = Mealie-meal from millet is tasty.
powdered medicine, e.g. *Musilisi upika busu bwamusamu ansalu-nsalu.* = The herbalist rubs powdered medicine into the tatooes.
*busu bwabuluba* = pollen of cotton, e.g. *Inzuki zilya busu bwabuluba mumuunda.* = The bees eat pollen of the cotton in the field. Also *lusu*.
what is pulverized or powdered, e.g. *Busu-busu buzwa mumasomo aaciluli bulokela acibuye.* = The powder coming out of roof-poles has fallen on the floor.

a female hairstyle of small bows which was used in the Gwembe Valley, e.g. *Basimbi bapukilana busuki mumitwe.* = The girls are helping each other to make hairstyles. *Wakajana musimbi mubotu kalipukila busuki bwakwe mumutwe.* = He found a beautiful girl doing her own hairstyle.
finches, e.g. *Nditeya busumwe.* = I am trapping finches. Also *bucwencwe*.
a pattern, design, e.g. *Busumwe bwacisani camwana mbubi.* = The pattern of the child's dress is bad.
cotton thread, e.g. *Kondipa busumyo nsume saka.* = Give me cotton thread to sew the sack.
barreness in women, e.g. *Bamakaintu bamwi busundi bubapa kuneneya naakukoka.* = The barreness of some women makes them either grow fat or lose weight.
impotency in men, e.g. *Muntu wa busundi tazyali mwana.* = An impotent man does not produce a child.

power, zeal, energy, e.g. *Busungu bwamuntu bulibonya mumilimo njacita.* = The enthusiasm of a person is seen in the work s/he does. Ndime ntengwamubili, *busungu buli mucamba.* = I may have an insiginificant body, but there is energy in the chest. *Mwini Leza nguwakabubikka busungu mumisamu njobasebenzya naakailenga* = God himself is the one who has put power in the medicines which they use when he created the medicines.
destructive power, e.g. *Busungu bwabusaki bwamulala bulakonzya kujaya muntu ciindi cisyoonto.* = The virulence of the venom of a black mamba snake can kill a person in a short time.
zeal, enthusiasm, e.g. *Ooyu mwana ulijisi busungu-sungu mukubeleka.* = This child is industrious. Also *bunsengwe-sengwe*.

something hidden and only shown to somebody who agrees to be tied by the neck. e.g. *Ndjisi busungwa-sungwa, utasungwi tabulyi.* = I have something I do not want to show to anyone unless I tie him by the neck, who is not tied does not participate.
stench from bowels. Also *lusozi*
midges (minute species of insects swarming in rainy season), e.g. *Bana bajata bususubwi buuluka mu lubuwa.* = The children are gathering midges flying about courtyard.

midges, e.g. *Ooyu munanga wakamubumbila akumupa tubiya totatwe Makala: kamwi kakali kampeyo, kamwi kakali kantomba, katatu kakali kabususuli.* = This witch-doctor moulded and gave Makala three little pots: one for the cold, one for small-pox and one for midges. *Nobakamujaya mucende akumufwunda kwakadilimuka buyo bususuli, tiibakajene nyama mukati.* = When they killed the bull and skinned it, only midges poured out, they did not find meat. Also *bususubwi*.
stench from bowels, e.g. *Aano mpekkede ndamvwa busuzi.* = Here where I sit I smell wind from the bowels. Also lusozi
not difficult, e.g. Yakali nkondo *yabuswa*. It was an easy war.
a collection of edible ants, e.g. Basimbi bakalongela *buswani*. = The girls packed a collection of edible ants.
malt (grain that has been steeped, germinated and dried for brewing beer.) Mukaintu ubamba *buswezyo*. = A woman is making malt for brewing the beer. Also buseezyo, bumena.
truthfulness, e.g. Majwi amwiiyi ngabuswini. Atujulwida kunyika ya*buswini bupya*. = These words are true. They open for us the way to a world of new truth.
taking things for yourself without approval, e.g. *Busyaakulipa mbu-*
Taking things without approval is bad.
orphanhood, e.g. *Busyaala* buleetezya. = Orphanhood is pitiable. Also bumucaala.
face, pl. masyu, e.g. Ooyu mwana *busyu* wakakozya bausyi. This child resembles the father facially.
a hunting bow, pl. mata, e.g. Kobweza *buta* tukavwime. = Get the bow so that we go hunting.
a trigger guard on a gun, e.g. *Buta bukwabilila cipani cantobolo. The triggerguard protects the trigger of a gun.
bird-lime, e.g. Koteya tuyuni *abutaba*. Trap the birds with bird-lime. Also bulimbo.
wastefulness, carelessness, e.g. Langa *butaka* bwako mbobuzwide. = Look at how complete your prodigality is.
raised grain store, grain bin, e.g. *Butala* bokwesu bwapya. Our grain-bin is burnt. (Various types of granaries: kafwubu, cinkuntu, cibbule, cimuumbwa, citula, cikulimba, cizinge.)
rough metal, crocodile skin, e.g. Kaindi bamakuwa bamwi bakali kuyandaula meja anzovwu, *butale* a bazike. = Long ago some whites were searching for elephants tusks, crocodile-skins and slaves.
a stairs, a bridge, a tree lying across a river, e.g. Tubelesya *butalitali* kuya munanda yamujulu. = We use stairs going to the upper floor of the house.
ulanduke your steps carefully so that you cross over along the tree trunk. Kubamba mugwagwa beelede kuyaka *butalitali*. To build a road they must also include a bridge. Also matambiliko.

enthusiasm/eagerness to speak, eat or act, e.g. Bamwi bantu *mbabutambo kukwaambaula*. Some people are eager to talk. *butambo kubanyama* = eagerness to kill a lot of game; *butambo kusongwaala* = eagerness to speak before one's turn
a man-eating lion, e.g. Inombe zyalikunyita masiku nkaambo *butambo bwainda munsi aciba. The cattle were mooing at night because a lion passed near the kraal.
greed, a child who rushes to get hold of a thing when it is being given to another, e.g. *Butampa* mbubi bupa kusulaikwa. Snatching things is bad, it causes one to be hated.
a grouping of animals. e.g. Kwainda *butanga bwajombe kuya*

A herd of cattle passed going westwards. *Butanga bwarjombe zyangu* tabujisi mucende. My herd of cattle is without a bull. Ndabona *butanga bwabasyuumbwa mucoonde. = I have seen a pride of lions in the bush. Bumwi busiku kwakasika *butanga bwanzovwu*. One night a herd of elephants arrived
a flock of birds, e.g. Ndajana *butanga* bwatuyuni mulubuwa Iwangu. = I found a flock of birds in my yard.
gluttony, e.g. *Butangazi* ncilengwa cibi. = Gluttony is a bad habit. Also bulyato
very small black ants, e.g. Mwana walumwa *butandansinga*. = The child has been bitten by small ants.

impatient avidity, as for certain food: -lya *butangazu* = eat without chewing e.g. Mwana oyu watingwa nyama nkaambo kabutangazu bwakwe. = This child has been choked by meat because of its impatient greed.
willfull disobedience, selfishness, e.g. *Butani* tacili cintu cibotu. = Selfishness is not a good thing. cf. bukazi
greed for meat, e.g. *Butavwu* bwa Sicibende bwakali kuya kumbele muya ciindi. = The greed for meat of Sicibende was increasing as time passed. Also butewu
attractiveness of lights and colours, e.g. Koonse nkwaalanga *mbutayi-tayi* bwamaanda. = Everywhere he looked there were the shining lights of the houses.
slipperiness, e.g. Mubondo ulaa *buteezi* amubili. = A barbel fish has a slippery body.

widowhood, the unmarried state of living in seclusion = *kukkala butema*, e.g. Kukkala *butema* cipa kuubauba kubasankwa kufwumbwa wayanda kusika amunzi. = Living alone makes it easy for men, whoever wants to come to the home. Also bunkungulume.

a simple structure or frame-word, as for drying meat or firewood, e.g. Eeyo nyama koiyanika *abuteme*. = Dry that meat on the rack. Bakali kuyaka *buteme* bwakubikkila nkuni. = They used to make a simple structure for firewood.
a type of tree bearing a fruit orange-like in appearance. = Oobu *buteme* buzyede kabotu mwaka uno. = This *buteme* tree has a lot of fruit this year.
sickness, e.g. *Kuli butenda bwakasika munyika yoonse.* = There is a sickness which has reached every part of the world
what is minced or cut up into small pieces, e.g. *Kotendaula butendu-tendu bwanyama kutegwa iyanikwe kabotu.* = Cut the meat into small pieces so that it can easily be hung up to dry.
frustration e.g. *Kubeleka kabotu takunjizizyi nzala a butengwana.* = To work well does not allow hunger and frustration to enter.
slipperiness, e.g. *Mubondo ulaa butesi bunji.* = A barbel fish is very slippery. Also buteezi
clemency, e.g. *Butete bwamuntu bupa kuti bantu banji bamuyande.* = The kindness of the person causes many people to like her/him.
a reed bed by a river, e.g. *Mukateme butete mumbali amulonga.* = Go and cut the reeds beside the river.
greed for meat, e.g. *nombe tazyeelede kunikoona musyokwe akaambo kabutewu bwavwula mucisi.* = The cattle should not be sleeping in the bush because the land is full of greed for meat. Also butavwu
slipperiness, a slippery place, e.g. *Mumusena mukunka meenda muli butezelele.* = In the vlei where the water flows it is slippery. Also buteezi, nteezi
mire, marsh, e.g. *Mulonga niwakazwide kapati kwakacaala butimba mumbalimbali.* = Wet mud remained on the banks of the river which overflowed. Also butyopolo, butipa
pus from an ulcer, e.g. *Sunu acuute kwazwa butimbatimba.* = Pus came out of the abcess today. Also busina
marsh, morass, e.g. *Butinti buli kudambwa tabumani meenda.* = The marsh at the dam has water which does not dry up.
marshy land, e.g. *Butipa mbu- botu kunyika loozi Iwakuvwumbya maa- nda.* Marshy land is good for dipping fibres for thatching houses. Also *butimba*.
laziness, e.g. *Muntu ulaa butolo tavwoli mali manji pe.* A lazy person does not earn much money.

spots like a bush- buck's or a guinea fowl's, e.g. *Inkanga ijisi butombo-tombo amubili.* A guinea- fowl has spots on its body. *Imvwula niyatalika kuwa kwalikulibonya butombo- tombo ansi.* When the rain began to fall, spots were seen on the ground.

taboos, e.g. *Munzi ooyu wakali wabantu basyoma mumizimo amubutondi bwaandeene.* This village was of people who belived in spirits and in vaious taboos. **Butonga** Tongaland, e.g. *Butonga bujisi zilengwa atunsiyansiya zinji.* Tongaland holds customs and many traditions.
cotton, e.g. *Ku Gwembe bala- ula kabotu butonge.* In the Gwembe they are eagerly buying cotton. Also *butonje*.
complaints, murmurings, Also *butongoosi*

a defect, e.g. *Mubili wangu ulaa bu- tongo.* There is something defective with my body. *Incinga yangu ilaa buto- ngo, nsyekonzyi kwiibelesya.* My bicycle has a defect, I cannot use it. *Bakakupe nombe mbotu iinyina butongo.* Let them give you a good cow without any defect. *Cintu nocibota buti mpaali amwi mpocili abutongo.* No matter how good a thing may be, there is some way in which it is defective.

cotton, cotton-wool, e.g. *Ko- bikka butonje mumatwi kutegwa musamu utazwi.* Put cotton-wool in the ears so that the medicine does not come out. *Uuno mwaka bantu bakalima butonje bunji.* People grew much cotton this year. Also *buluba*
mire, mud, e.g. *Mwana wali- nanika butope.* The child has smeared itself with mud.
disgrace, shame, e.g. *Bulwati bwakwe bwamuletela butuni naawumwa kumudaala.* His love of fighting has brought him disgrace when he was beat- en by an old man. Also *butani, buungu*.
valour, bravery, e.g. *Ku- konzya kujaya nzoka mbuli mulalala nkubaa bututubwi.* Having bravery makes one able to kill a snake such as a black mamba. Also *busicamba*

menstruation, e.g. *Tee cipa kuti baambe kuti musimbi wamita nkukakilwa kuunka kubutwa, kutabonwi mwezi.* What makes people say that a girl has conceived is when she does not men- struate, does not have her monthly period.
slavery, captivity, e.g. *Butwanga bwakaindi bwakali bwakwa- angwa munsingo mumulongo omwe.* The slavery of the past was to be tied by the neck in one line.
a sensation of blood returning to part of the body which has been numb, e.g. *Impeyo niizwa mumubili inga kulimvwisya butyantyantya.* When coldness leaves the body there is a ting- ling feeling.
disappointment, e.g. *Bu- tyompwa bwabana mbwakumaninina.* The disappointment of the children is ex- treme.
mud, e.g. *Moombe wapatila mubutyopo.* The calf is stuck in the mud. Also *ntimba*.
a morass, e.g. *Moombe wa- patila mubutyopola.* The calf got stuck in swampy ground.
cracking of the knuckles, e.g. Ndali kulizya butyotyo bwaminwe. = I was cracking the knuckles of my fingers.
lightness e.g. Buuba bwamukuli bwakandipa kuti ndicikonzye kutanta mulundu mulamfwu. The lightness of the load allowed me to climb the steep hill.
grass for weaving, e.g. Bana bajwa buugwa bwakuluka nsambo a nsangwa. = The children are collecting grass for weaving braclets and baskets.
a collection of little insects/ reptiles, e.g. Cisyu cili mumbewu cilaa buuka. The relish which is in the garden is full of insects.
swarms of insects, e.g. Kwaanka kuuluka buukauka. = Swarms of insects began to fly.
a little knot used in running noose, a slip-knot, a noose, e.g. Tuteya tuyuni abuulyu. = We are trapping birds with a noose. Also bufwizu.
ground mists, vapours, the firmament, atmosphere, e.g. Nyika yoonse kuli buuma. = There is a mist over all the land. Also sikunku, sitelebwe.
solitude or loneliness of widowhood, e.g. Baama bakkede buumba. My mother lives all alone. Mwanaangu wakafwa undipa buumba. = My child who died gives me loneliness. Ulaa buumba = S/He is lonely.

what is complete or whole, (adv.) e.g. Ooyu mwana nsima uyimena buumbulu. = This child swallows the food whole. Mwana wakauleta buumbulu mиngu wako. The child brought your pumpkin in a complete condition (untouched).
life, e.g. Buumi bwangu bulinyongene akaambo kakuciswa. = My life is upset because of ill health.
sandflies, e.g. Basankwa nibakali kusya musenga, buumputu bwakali kubakatazya. When the men were digging sand the sandflies were troubling them.
gunpowder, e.g. Basankwa baya kukuula buunga. The boys have gone to buy gun-powder. Buunga bwantobolo mbutete. The gunpowder is wet. Also bunga.
a day, e.g. Ndakaciswa kwabuunsi bomwe. = I was sick for one day. Also buzuba.

greed, covetousness, stinginess, e.g. Inzala tiiyabanjilila bina Moonga akaambo kabuunyu. = Hunger did not affect the mother of Moonga because of her stinginess, i.e. She had been hoarding rather than sharing.
feel sorry for someone, e.g. Ndaba abuusu nindabona mudaala ubwezede mapopwe musaka. I felt sorry when I saw the old man carrying maize in a sack.
fear, e.g. Bana bakaindi bakali kuba abuuwa kucita zintu zitondwa. = In the past children feared to do something forbidden. Also buwa.

intelligence, a special skill e.g. for song, craft, human relationships, e.g. Musankwa uulya ujisi buuya mukwiimba. = The boy has a talent for singing. Cuku wakaisungununa nengo, nkabela wakagambwa buuya bwakwe. Cuku untied the ant-bear and was amazed at its ability.
mistake, error, e.g. Buuyu butaanzi tabulizyi mbelele. A lamb is not guilty of its first mistake.

kindness in helping others, e.g. Buuza bulanenga (a proverb) = Kindness cuts. Buuza bwangu bwakapa kuti mapopwe mubutala amane. My kindness led to the emptying of the maize-bin. Basimunywewu tabajisi acintu pesi kwiinda mubuuza bwabo balikutantamuna zintu zibyaabi zikonzya kunyonganya bamwi. = The ants have not got any thing, but through their cooperation they can drive away bad things which might confuse their fellow-ants.
a head-pad of grass and reeds, e.g. *Kondibambila buvwale*. = Make me a headpad of grass and reeds. Also *nkata, bubale, cihale*.
infancy, e.g. *Ooyu mwana buwwanda tabumani, takomeni kabotu pe*. = Infancy does not end for this child, s/he is not growing well.
the trap-door of a fish-trap, e.g. *Inswi zyazwida abuwwazi*. = The fish escaped through a trap-door of the fishtrap.
habit of gossiping, e.g. *Buvwizi bwakwe bwamuletela bunjaka*. = His habit of gossiping brought him trouble. Also *-vwiya*.

an envelope, e.g. *Nabulongo naakamvwa kuti mukati ka buwulupu buya mwakali mwaanda wampondo wakaindilila kukkomana*. = When Nabulongo felt that in the envelope there was a hundred pounds, she was even more happy.

a charm against thieves, e.g. *Muziba zyanombe mumwi kuli buwwumo kutegwa kazitabbigwi*. = In some cattle kraals there are charms to prevent them being stolen. (When used as a verb, e.g. *Munene wakavwuma nombe kuti zitalumwi basyuumbwa*. = The old man used charms so that his cattle would not be eaten by lions. Also *-vwuma*)
promiscuity, e.g. *Buvwuule bumupa kutakkala kabotu*. His/her promiscuity brought him/her an unpleasant life.
the great escarpment west of the Middle Zambezi, e.g. *Buwe butalikila ku Gwembe kuya kujwe*. = The We territory begins from Gwembe going eastwards.
hunting, e.g. *Buwezi tabutyompyi nokuba kuti tojayi*. = Hunting is not discouraging even if you do not kill.

a blister, a boil, e.g. *Ndaa buya kunsi amaulu*. I have a boil under my foot. *Buya bwakwe mbukali nkaambo mulilo wakamuumpa wakali munji*. = His burns are severe because the fire which burnt him was extensive. Also *twizya*.
thrush, the disease of lips and mouth, sores on tongues of children, e.g. *Mwana wakali kupenga kapati akaambo kabuyaaya*. The child was suffering a lot because of thrush. Also *bulolomwa*.
pompom, as of messengers hat, Also *bundawala*.
bridge made of timber poles, e.g *Ncinga yanyikila abuyalo bwamulonga Magoye*. The bicycle has fallen into the Magoye river at the bridge.
a fish stockade, e.g. *Baama bajana nswi zinji mubuyalo*. Mother finds many fish in the fish stockade. Also *buyeelo*.
a fence, e.g. *Buyalo bwambewu bwapya*. The fence of the garden was burnt down. Also *buyeelo*.

negligence, carelessness, e.g. *Akaambo kabuyamba bokwa Mutinta, cisyu caida kale*. The relish was burnt because of Mutinta's carelessness. Kujanika kuti amwi masena akasanduka zyakaba zimpa-yuma akaambo kabuyamba. = It is found that through negligence some places have become deserts.
cooked meat, e.g. *Koapula buyani tulye*. Share out the cooked meat so that we eat.

the sensation felt in the gums after eating masuku fruit or certain other foods, e.g. *Busiikka mbondalya bwandibamba buye mumenyo*. = The tubers I have eaten have caused my teeth to tingle. Also *bunyeele*.

a fish stockade, a barrier across a flow of water for catching fish (made of reeds etc.) cf. *buyalo*, e.g. Kamubamba buyeelo kutegwa tuteye kabotu nswi. = Make a barrier so that we can trap the fish easily. Also Iwaando

a collection of eggs, as of fish, frog spawn etc., e.g. *Mumubondo ndajana buyi bunji.* = In the barbel fish I found plenty of eggs. *Buyi bwazenimutendu, muswi wamu Luvwubu, cikabe cilalilo cangu.* = The eggs of a shark, the big fish of the Luvwubu, will be my supper.

a collection of small mischievous spirits, e.g. *Mudaala nawona inga ulota buyobela.* = When the old man sleeps he dreams of a group of annoying little spirits. *Bamutumina buyobela ncaafwambaana kufwa.* = They sent him bad little spirits that is why he died quickly. Also buyowela, kayobela.

fear, e.g. *Akaambo kabuyofwu ndayoowa kuzwa anze naalikukuwa mubwa.* = I failed to come out because of fear when the dog was barking. *Kuti kolaa buyofwu, inga kolota kapati.* = If you have fear, you dream much. Also buyoofwu.

snake-poison, poison from the bones of a dead snake, e.g. *Ndakayaswa buyoka bwanzoka kunsi amaulu.* = I was pierced with the poison of a snake under my foot. *Buyoka bwanzoka tabuyandi kumukilwa pe.* = It is not advisable to delay in being treated for snake-poison. Also busaki.
fear, e.g. *Akaambo kabuyoofwu, nsyindakaunka kumuunda endikke jilo.* = Because of fear I did not go to the field alone yesterday. Also buyofwu.

pieces of metal and skin tied to a dancing belt, e.g. *Moonde naakali kuzyana wakasamide lutambo Iwakajisi buyowele.* = When Moonde was dancing he was dressed with a belt which had pieces of metal and skin. Also bubamba
endurance, stiffness, e.g. Ncinga yakandaalila kuccowa akaambo ka*buyumu bwamaulu.* = I failed to ride the bicycle because of stiffness of the legs.

a difficulty, e.g. *Tiindakalanduka mumusunko wangu akaambo kabuyumu-yumu bwamisunko.* = I did not pass the examination because the exams were difficult. *Bakajana buyumu-yumu kutanta mulundu akaambo kaloonde Iwakajatene kapati.* = They found difficulty in climbing the hill because the undergrowth was so matted.
a collection of small birds, e.g. *Buyuni bwaamana maila mumuunda.* = The birds have finished the millet in the field.
fishing-nets, e.g. *Kamusanzya buzamba, bwabaa tombe.* = Wash the fishing-nets, they are dirty. *Bakawaala buzamba bwabo mumeenda.* = They threw their nets into the water. Also lusabwi.
a platform, raft, e.g. *Kamubwaanga buzavwo bujate, atani kuloki mapopwe.* = Bind the platform so that it holds well and the maize does not drop off. Also bwalo.
subterfuge, deception, evasion of truth, e.g. *Kaambo aka kalijisi buzelengani.* = This affair is deceptive.
slavery, e.g. *Bensiku besu bakali kutolwa mubuzike.* = Our ancestors were taken into slavery.
stupidity, foolishness, e.g. *Buzilaisi tabuligwi. Pakamana.* = Foolishness is not eaten. Be alert. (i.e. If you are stupid you won't earn a living.)

a variety of paths made by cattle on their way to water, e.g. *Kuvwula kwabuzilazila bwaņombe candipa kuzimininwa nzila iya kumulonga.* = The multitude of tracks made by the cattle caused me to miss the way to the river. Also bukondokondo.

guts, sinews, small tendons of tail, e.g. *Buzingo bwakumucila wasokwe* mbuyumu. = The sinews of a monkey's tail are very strong. Mucembele aitwa kutumbusya mukaintu umyongwa, weelede kuti kajisi buzingo. = The midwife who is called to assist the mother to give birth, ought to have a sinew for tying the umbilical cord. Also bukango. (Note: Kaindi bakali koosa kooze kaloozi Iwamubuyu, nkakwaanzya lukombo-kombo. = In the past they used to weave a fibre from a baobab tree, that is what tied the umbilical cord.)
a brood of snakes, e.g. Buzoka bunji bulapya ciindi nolipya syokwe. = Many broods of snakes are burnt during the time the bush is burnt.
friendship, e.g. Kuvwiya takubonyi buzolani bubotu, kuletela lusulano. = Gossiping does not make friendship, but rather brings hatred. Also bulongwe.
friendship, kusanzana buzoIwani = contract a friendship, e.g. Twakapangana buzolwani bwakulembelana magwalo. We made an agreement to correspond. Also bulongo, bulongwe
a day, daylight, e.g. Ndakalicisidwe kapati buzuba lyakafwa mwami Mweemba. I was very sick on the day when Chief Mweemba died.
jealousy towards anyone who seeks to deprive you of your husband, wife or lover, e.g. Bamuka Chicenga balaa buzuba. The wife of Chicenga is full of jealousy.
verdict, e.g. Bantu beelede kuunka anze bakalindile buzubuluzi, balaitwa akale. The people ought to go outside and await the verdict, they will be called later.
bees wax, e.g. Kosinka cibulo cameenda abuzuka. = Block the hole in the water-container with bee-wax. Also bunzuka.
a mash of crushed nuts and salt, e.g. Buzuka bwandongwe zikange bulanona. = A mash of groundnuts and salt when fried is delicious. Also coonde, bunzuka.
life, vitality, e.g. Buzumi bwabanyama bacela mani mbwakupenga ciindi sokwe nilyapya. The life of animals who graze grass becomes hard at the time when the bush is burnt.
bird-lime, e.g. Tuteya tuyuni abuzunda. We trap birds with bird-lime.
in, e.g. Buzundi bwamukaintu bulakatazya kusilika. = The barreness of a woman is hard to cure. Also busundi.

east, morning, e.g. Inkondo yabasitukumba yakatalikila kubuzwezuba. = The war with the Balozi started in the morning. nombe zyako zyazyila kubuzwezuba. = Your cattle have come from the east. Also kujwe.
generation, e.g. Bana ba buzyalwe obuno bazyalilwa mumapen aamalwazi. = The children of this gen eration are being born amidst sufferings and diseases. Also muzyalani.

dancing ability, e.g. Buzyani bwakwe bwakakondelezya bantu banji. = His dancing ability delighted many people. (Wakabamba zibelesyo zyabuzyani bwakwe zitegwa masangu-sangu, nsaka, mucila wamunyumbwe, mabbensu atukutu twabasaazwe abanyimbaasalama, cingowani cacikutu cabbule ncaakasekka cicila casuntwe amunimba wankulyukuku, andandala njaakabamba atobo lyantale. = He prepared the instruments of his dancing ability called masangu-sangu, a rattle, a tail of a gnu, strips of the skin of skunks, the skin-hat of a honey-badger in which he had stuck the tail of a hyena and the feather of a touraco, and a drum which he had made from the skin of a crocodile.)
ticklish sensation, e.g. Utani kundigumi munkwa, ndaa buzyeele. = Do not touch me in the armpits, I feel tickles. Also bunyeele
generosity, e.g. Ooyu mucembele ulaa *bwaabi*. = This old woman gives without stint.
width, e.g. *Bwaamba* bwacibuye mbupati. = The width of the floor is great. Also bwamba, bwanza.
affluence, abundance, e.g. *Bwaambi* bupa kulela bantu banji. = Affluence allows one to look after many people.
strings of a hide, e.g. Bataata bakazambaila *bwaambilo* bwacikutu carnjombe. = My father wrapped up the strings of the hide of the cow. Also ntambo
lust, e.g. *Bwaamu* bujanika kapati akati kabakubusi. = Lust is found mostly amongst the youth. Also nkwela.
glue made from tendons, e.g. Kamundipa *bwaamwa* ndibbatike bbuku. = Give me glue to stick the book together.
a wall or partition, e.g. *Bwaanda bwamaanda angu buleelenye. = The wall of my houses is all of the same level.
crushed maize, e.g. Tuya kukugazya *bwaando* bwakusanina ngulube. = We are going to grind bran for feeding the pigs. Also masembe
branding, e.g. *Bwaando bwagombe* zyangu bulalizyibya. = The branding of my cattle is reveals that they belong to me. pl. of caando

a charm, a ritual medicine, a magic mixture, (plants are said to possess it.) e.g. Bamadaala bakaindi bakali kuyandisya kulya *bwaanga* kutegwa batakafwambaani kufwa. = The old men of the past liked a lot to eat a magic mixture so that they would not quickly die.
power, e.g. Nkujana boonse *bwaanga* mbwaakajisi mulombwana bwaide kumumwaika. = It was to find that all the power which the man had was just dissipated
a forest of mopani trees, e.g. Mukagonke masomo *kubwaani*. = Cut the roof poles in the mopani forest. Banyama balacela *mbwaani*. = The animals are grazing among the mopani trees. Also Iwaani.

relish e.g. Wakalya nsima mu*bwaawo* bwamunsunkwindi. = She ate nsima with munsunkwindi relish. Wakaya kukusunza *bwaawo* bwanyama kucisaka bavwimi nkobakali kuvwima akujaya banyama amivwi. = She went to ask for meat for relish at the forest where hunters used to kill animals with arrows. Syaanasulwe amusimbi wakwe bakatolelwa nsima *abwaawo* bweyo munanda yabo. = The hare with his wife were given nsima with meat-relish in their house.
traditional dress of hanging strings, pl. maaya, e.g. Bakamwale kaindi bakali kusama *bwaaya*. = Initiates of long ago used to wear a traditional stringed skirt. Also manda, maaya.

Tuesday, e.g. Muli *Bwabili* kuli muswaangano wabakubusi. = On Tuesday there is a meeting of the youth. *Bwabili yakamupwaya akuulu nombe naakali kukama. = On Tuesday the cow kicked him on the leg when he was milking.
traditional hammock, e.g. Muvwimi wakabamba *bwalangwe* bwakoonena naakakatala. = The hunter made a hammock to sleep in when he was tired.

branch used as shelf, a bridge of sticks, a platform, a tray, e.g. Bana nobaleta zilyo *abwalo*, bapati balasala zilyo zinono. = When the children bring food on a tray, the elders choose tasty portions.
poles for roofing or flooring, e.g. Nobasankwa mukagonke *bwalo* bwaciluli. = Boys, go and cut roofing-poles. Atukagonke *bwalo* bwacisanza camapopwe. = Let us cut poles for flooring the maize bin.
a traditional court, e.g. Amutole kasalu kasiluwe kubwalo. = Take the skin of the leopard to the court.
breadth, e.g. *Bwamba bwananda tabuli kabotu.* = The width of the house is incorrect. Also *bwaamba.*
chief's power or territory, e.g. *Bwami bunjilwa abasimukowa.* = Succession to the chieftainship is restricted to the clan of the reigning chief.
lust, e.g. *Bwamu mbubi.* = Lust is evil. Also *bwaamu, kampuwempuwe, cikundani.*
a collection of little children, e.g. *Bwana bwali kusobanina mumeenda.* = A group of children were playing in the water.

childhood, e.g. *Muntu oyu ucicita zyabwana mupati oonse.* = This man is still doing childish things and he an adult. *Kunsiku eezyo, muntu wakali amyaka makumi obilo lyoonse wakali kubalilwa kubwana. Wakali kutegwa ono wakomena naakakwata.* = In those times a person who was twenty years was always considered to be a child. He was said to be adult when he got married.
a brood, as of chickens, e.g. *Bwana bwankuku bwafwa.* = A brood of chickens has died.

fresh and sour milk mixed, frothy milk curds, e.g. *Ndiyanda kulya bwanda.* = I want to eat curds. *Mweenzu wakali kulya musozya musyubule wamabisi malemulemu akajisi bwanda.* = The visitor was eating *musozya* which was pounded with thick sour milk which had curds. *Sicibende wakali kubuyanda bwanda mbuli mbobabuyanda bananyina boonse.* = Sicibende liked fresh and sour milk mixed like all his friends did. Also *mwaanda*
crushed maize, e.g. *Kamuzipa bwando nkuku.* = Give the chickens bran. cf. *masembe.*
Thursday, e.g. *Bwane mbuzuba bwakuswaya baciswa.* = Thursday is the day for visiting the sick.
poison, e.g. *Bakamubikkila bwanga mubukoko, ncaakafwa Maanya.* = They put poison in Maanya's beer, that is why he died. Also *ncefwu, bwaanga.*
youth, e.g. *Musobano wabbola ngwabwanike.* = The game of football is for the youth. Also *bwana.*
boyhood, boyishness, e.g. *Kusobana mumvwula ncisobano cakubwanikenike.* = Playing in the rain is a game for the young. Also *bwana.*
an armlet of wound thin wire, e.g. *Musimbi oyu usamide bwanza kukuboko.* = This girl is wearing an armlet of wound thin wire. Also *ninga, iseka, idanda.*
breadth, e.g. *Bwanza bwabutala bwakaceya.* = The maize-bin is not wide enough.
Friday, e.g. *Bwasanu tuya kukuzela.* = We are going fishing on Friday.
Wednesday, e.g. *Bwatatu Michelo wakalicisa muntenda yamu-mugwagwa.* = On Wednesday Michelo hurt himself in a road accident.
a dugout, a boat, a raft, a mat formed into a canoe, a big trough, e.g. *Bwato bwandilandusya alwizi Iwa Zambezi.* = A boat took me across the Zambezi.
fiery temperament, e.g. *Ooyu muntu ulaa moyo wakabwato-bwato, ulafwambaana kunyema.* = This man has a heart which floats easily like a boat, he is quick to become angry.
meat, e.g. *Bwayo mbubotu.* = Meat is good.
intractableness, e.g. *Ooyu musankwa ulaa bwazi.* = That boy is full of stubbourness. Also *nkazi.*

the violet tree, a type of shrub, spiny, blue-green leaves, masses of white-pinkpurple flowers from September to November. Flowers yeild oil also seeds yield oil used cosmetically or as a furniture stain. Roots are very poisonous. Other parts of tree used for magical and medicinal purposes. Also mufwufwuma.
a spectacle, e.g. Bamakuwa banji bakali kusika akaambo kabweebi bwabanyama bakajalilwa. Many white people were coming because of the view of the animals in the game reserve. Also bweebesi.
the itch, scabies, e.g. Mucibbadela bana banji baciswa bweele. = Many children are sick with scabies in the hospital.
vagrancy, homelessness, e.g. Bamwi bantu balya misamu ibaletela bweeleenzi. = Some eat traditional medicines which causes them to wander about.
fitness, suitability, e.g. Bweelezi bwacisani eci mbubotu. = The measurements of this dress are fine.
scabies, e.g. Mwana wakayambukilwa bweeli. = The child was infected with scabies. Also bweele.
one's turn in herding, e.g. Ngu Moonga ulaa bweembelo juunza. = It is Moonga's turn for herding tomorrow. Also bwembelo, mulizyi, bulizyi, bulizi.
a reward for keeping someone's property, e.g. Baacisya bakandipa nombe zyobilo zyabweembelo bwanombe zyabo bubotu. My mother's brother gave me two cows as a reward for keeping his cattle well.
shame, e.g. Musankwa waba abweeme nkaambo walikulila citalibonyi. = The boy was ashamed because he was crying for nothing. Also bweemye, bweemya.

shame, e.g. Cipa bweemya cakacita basibukoko ijilo nibakaumpa munzi wabantu. = It is shameful what the beer-drinkers did yesterday when they burnt down a village. Mulombe, wakakakwa musimbi zona, ulaa bweemya sunu. = The boy, who was rejected by a girl the day before yesterday, is ashamed today. bweemye shamefulness, dishonour, e.g. Ndaba abweemye naandifwubaazya mwana. I was ashamed when the child fooled me.
movement, progress, e.g. Bali kwaambilizya bweende bwamuswaangano. = They were reporting about the progress of the meeting.
water-melon, e.g. Munanda Mainza wakali kulondola nyangu, ntanga, bweengo andongo. = Mainza was arranging the beans, melons, water-melons and groundnuts in the house. Also bwengo
spermatozoa, e.g. Bweenze bwamusankwa mbobubamba mwana mumukaintu. = The sperm of a man makes a child in a woman. (taboo) Also busasi.
the tail of a fish, e.g. Bweeye bwanswi bulamuka kubizwa. = The tail of a fish is slow in cooking.
good skill, as in catching of fish, e.g. Baama balaa bwela mukuzela. = My mother has good skill in catching fish.
scent (good or bad), e.g. Aawa kununka bwema bwanyimbaasalama. = Here there is the smell of a polecat. Also bwemya.
one's turn for herding, e.g. Munene nguulaa bwembelo nsondo iboola. It is the old man's turn to herd next week. Also bweembelo, bulizyi.

aroma, e.g. Bwemya bwa nyama eeyi mbubotu nkaambo yajikwa kabotu. The aroma of this meat is nice because it has been well cooked. Wakamvwa nzala naakamvwa bwemya bwanswi. He became hungry when he got the smell of the fish.
path, passage, e.g. *Bwende bwakuya kumulonga nkugama kumbo.* = The way to the river is to head west-wards. Also *bweende.*
sesame, a tall annual herb-aceous plant with oil-rich seeds, pl. *myengo*, e.g. *Ijilo twakalya cisyu cabwengo.* = Yesterday we ate with a relish made from sesame seeds. Also *bweengo.*

scratches on legs caused by sharp grass, e.g. *Mumaulu ndilaa bwengo-bwengo bwakukwambwa tusamu-samu musyokwe.* = There are sore places on my legs which were scratched by small branches in the bush. Also *bweengo-bweengo, buvwalu-vwalu, mivwalu-mivwalu*
conjecture, estimate, e.g. *Ncindatali kwaamba masimpe ndalaa bwezyezya mumoyo wangu.* = The reason why I was not accurate is that I was just guessing.
a tuber eaten by a certain parasite, e.g. *Twajana bacembele basya bwidi mucisaka.* = We found the old women digging *bwidi* tubers in the forest. Also *Iwidi, lusala.*
a very small edible field mushroom, e.g. *Amukajwe bwidu kumuunda tujike.* = Go and uproot a small mushroom in the field.

the Ila territory, e.g. *Ku Bwiila kuli nombe zinji kapati.* = In the Ila region there are very many cattle. *Ku Bwiila bana mbamulombwana, kuno mbamukaintu.* = In Ila land the children belong to the husband, here they belong to the wife.

the smallest flying ants, e.g. *Bwiiliili bulazwa mvula niyatanga.* = Small flying ants come out with the first rains. *Tumembya tulayanda kulya bwiiliili.* Swallows like to eat small flying ants. Also *bwiilili.*
the smallest flying termites, e.g. *Bwiilili bwanjila mumeenda akaceede anze masiku ainda.* = Small ants have dropped into the water which was left outside last night. Also *bwiiliili.*
a talent for singing, e.g. *Nguzu zyabwiimbi ncipego cipati.* = The ability to sing is a great gift.
upright position, e.g. *Eeyi nanda taijisi bwiime bubotu nkaambo ilicengeme.* = This house is not upright because it is leaning to one side. Also *bwiimi.*
upright position, e.g. *Bwiimi bwananda tabuli kabotu nkaambo ilicengeme.* = The house is not upright because it is lop-sided. Also *bwiime.*
testimony, e.g. *Ooyu kamboni tajisi bwiiminizi bwakasimpe.* = This witness has not true testimony.
an outlet, e.g. *Inkukwe taakali kwiinzizya bwiindo.* = The rodent did not miss the chance of an escape. cf. *mpwido*
marriage, e.g. *Bwiinga bwa Moonga a Matimba bwakali bubotu.* = The marriage of Moonga and Matimba was good.
a wedding feast, e.g. *Tuya kubwiinga kutalaa mulonga.* = We are going to the wedding feast across the river.
roving about, e.g. *Bwiingaizi bwakwe bwamuletela bucete munanda.* = His wandering has brought him poverty to the home.
pleasure, e.g. *Bwiinu bwaccuka bulafwambaana kumana mukanwa.* = The sweetness of sugar quickly disappears from the mouth. Also *bunone*
manner of calling, e.g. *Ooyu muntu tacizyi kwiita bantu pe, bwiite bwakwe mbwabukali lyoonse.* = This person does not know how to call people, his manner of calling is always harsh.
teaching, e.g. *Bwiiyi bwakwe tabuli kabotu pe.* = His teaching is not good.
a collection of mollusc shells, e.g. Mumbali-mbali aamulonga kuli _bwiliili_. = There is a collection of shells beside the river.
the manyene termites when flying, e.g. Bwakandinjila mumeso _bwiliili_. = The flying-ants flew into my eyes. Also _bwiliili_.

foresight, plan, e.g. Basimukowa bakakkala antoomwe ikuti bajane _bwiingisilo_ bubotu bwakulibambila nkolola yamwana musimbi. = The clan members gathered together to find a good plan to prepare the initiation ceremony for the young girl. (vb. -ingasila) Also muzeezo
a talent for singing, e.g. Nanja ujisi cipego _cabwimbi_. = Nanja has a talent for singing. Also _bwiimbi_.

a burrow or den of an animal, pl. mena, e.g. _Bwina_ bwambeba mbulamfwu. = The burrow of the mice is deep. Inondo yakatalika kuyandaula _bwina_ moyakali kukonzya kunjila. = The tortoise began to look for a hole where it would be able to enter.
lice on fowl, e.g. Inkuku zilijisi _bwinakuku_. = The hens have lice. Also namunyanu, pl. banamunyanu, _bwiinakuku_, muusule.
the Bakkuni people, e.g. Ndakazyibila buzumi bwa _Bwinemukkuni_. = I got used to the life of the Bakuni people.
porridge at marriage feast, e.g. Basimukowa wamusimbi baya kukujika _bwinga_ kumukwasyi mupya. = The maternal relatives of the bride are going to cook porridge at the new home. Also muzuba
the bride, ulaa _bwinga_ = bridegroom, ukwete _bwinga_ = bridegroom, Also _bwiinga_.
a lot (number), e.g. Mumusena muya kuli _bwizu bwingu_. = There is a lot of grass in the vlei. Also bunji
grass, straw, e.g. Tuyakukujwa _bwizu_ bwacitungu. = We are going to cut a tall type of grass for thatching a hut.

of grasses:_ insangaazi, matebe, lukata = good for grazing; matumbu, masanga (like thin reeds) = for making mats; _lubembe_ = for making small baskets; manyanja and _matumbu_ = for making salt from ashes; mukusa, lukukwa = for making strong ropes; muvwani, mukulajamina, kampumpwe, bunkungwa, buugwa, mampolwe, businde.

with three edges:_ nembaula or nambaula; grass found in swamps = luvwundu; couch grass = zinza; prickly grass = cisina; grass poisonous for cattle = mani maluluwe; bits of grass left on floor or courtyard = tukwisi-kwisi; grey grass seeds which stick to clothing = insoke or insina; lying in rows on a long stem with prickles downwards = idamatila or inama (Other types of grass: manyengele, coya casulwe, matumbo, camuzenene) hay = mani mayumu akaceswa.
See _bwizu_.
type of bird, the oriole, e.g. Nindakali kweendeenda mucisaka, ndakajana cinteente cabyontansuwa. = When I was walking through the forest, I found the nest of an oriole. Also bbyontansuwa.

a little clay bowl used in the past as a receptacle for nsima, e.g. _Caaba_ cakali cibotu kwiinda mitiba yasunu nkaambo kwali kunga musinza wamafwuta tuufwambaani kutontola nokuba kwaanga muli ncico. = The clay bowl was better than the dishes of today because it used to keep the gravy from cooling quickly or from sticking to it.

a heap of ashes and rubbish, e.g. Syaanasulwe wakacinjila _caala_ catwe akulitila twe amubili wakwe onse. = The hare brought forth a heap of ashes and poured ashes over his whole body. Also *cibbunta* (Koya ukatile twe acibbunta. = Go and pour the ashes on the ashheap)
a big toe or thumb, pl. *zyaala*, e.g. *Ndaa cicisa acaala cakumaanza.* = I have a sore on the thumb. Also *calarnanda*
pretence, e.g. *izina lyacaali*, a nickname
*muntu wacaali*, a vain person

a bundle of hunters' items, e.g. *Kondipa caalu camasumo atweembe.* = Give me a bundle of spears and axes. *Naakamvwa suntwe nkwalila, wakabweza caalu camasumo mpoona wakatijaanina kucaanda campongo.* = When he heard the hyena crying, he took a bundle of spears and ran to the goat's enclosure. Also *ntaala, cileye*.
the place of hunter's items, e.g. *Muwimi ujisi meja abanyama acaalu.* = The hunter has animal horns in his storage.
a strong metal hoe, pl. *zyaamba*, e.g. *Eeci caamba nciyumu kapati.* = This hoe is very strong.
an old hoe, e.g. *Eeci caamba tacibosyi nkaambo ncakaindi.* = This hoe is not sharp beause it is old.
a large gourd, like a gourd for milk (nsuwa), e.g *Kozuzya caamba eci ameenda.* = Fill the gourd with water.

a black hard-skinned insect played with by children who surround it in a circle and ask it where the rain is. pl. *zyaambaankutu*, e.g. "*Caambaankutu, imvwula ili kuli?*" = O insect, where is the rain? *Caambaankutu ulabakonda bana kwiindilila nkaambo ulabazyanina nobamusobanya. Nobamukambila nkwasi akumwiimbila Iwiimbo Iwamvwula, ulazyana. Caambaankutu mmuuka uzyana. Nobaimba akukamba bapululuzya mipululu, caambaankutu ulalizya misindo acikungu cakwe, ulazyana. = *Caambaankutu* delights the children because it dances for them when they play with it. When they clap hands and sing a rain-song for it, it dances. *Caambaankutu* is a big insect which dances. When they sing and ululate, *caambankutu* shakes its bottom and back, it dances. Also *cambaankutu, coombaankutu*.
a large clay pot for cooking nsima, e.g. *Ceele bacijikila mucaambikwa.* = They have cooked porridge in the large clay pot. Also *citentu*.
a saying, topic, subject of conversation, e.g. *Ciyanda kuba caambyo cakuti tunyina busu.* = It is becoming a topic of conversation that we don't have mealie-meal. Also *kaambyo*.
a traditional axe, e.g. *Ukandibambile caamilimo, mudaala.* = Old man, can you make me an axe.

skull, e.g. *Nseyoowi lufwu ccita mane nkabone mafwuwa acaampalala camutwe wamwanaangu mpaakabolela, nenja kulimvwa kuti ndimuntu.* = I do not fear death until finally I see the bones and the skull of the head of my child where they rot, that is when I will feel a human being. Also *cipompo, cipampa*.
dried relish, e.g. *Sunu bajika cisyu caampano.* = Today they have cooked dried relish.
a cake of preserved food or dried vegetable or tobacco, pl. *zyaampe*, e.g. *Cisyumani caampe cilanona kapati cabikkwa buntele.* = Dried vegetables are delicious when mixed with groundnut mash.
a disease of the head suffered by infants, e.g. *Ooyu mwana uciswa caamutwe, amumutole kubacembele bakamusilike.* = This child is suffering from a head disease, take him to the old woman to be cured.
a delapidated house. pl. zyaanda, e.g. Eeci caanda ncibi, taciyakidwe kabotu. = This house is bad, it has not been built well. Also nanda, pl. maanda.
a story/fable with song, pl. zyaano, e.g. Kotupa caano cako musa mbuli mbooyenda. Friend, give us an account of the way you travelled.
the leg of a bed, pl. zyaanda, e.g. Kacumbika wakakananamika kabotu kalo kakwe azyaanda. Kacumbika set up his bed on legs. Also zisanda.
kraal for goats or pigs, e.g. Mweelede kuyaka caanda campongo. = You ought to build a goats house.
ice, frost, e.g. Kuli caanda mumwezi wa Gandapati kono. = There is frost in the month of June this year.
a place to sleep, e.g. Naakaseluka wakayandaula caanda-odi, icaanda cakoonena. When he dismounted, he searched for a shelter, a place to sleep. Also cipanga-hodi
a chapter in book, pl. zyaandano, e.g. Eeli bbuku lilanoneenzya mucaandano cakusaanguna. This book is interesting in its first chapter.
an identification mark in people or animals, a design, e.g Caando carnombe zyangu cinyina bukozyanye. = The identification mark on my cattle is unique. caando casikwaze = the sign of the eagle.
a severe headache, e.g. Ooyu mwana uciswa caandulamutwe. = This child has a severe headache. Also mpandula-mutwe
the galago, lemur, night-ape, bush-baby, pl. bacaanga, e.g. Ndabona caanga mumusamu. = I have seen a bush-baby in the tree.
indecision, an obstacle, an impediment, e.g. Nibali kukosola makani, babaa caanga, baaleka. = When they were settling the matter, they came upon a problem, they have stopped.
a traditional hatchet, e.g. Basyaanene bajisi caankuni kuya kudilwe. = My grandfather has a traditional axe going to the funeral.
a small type of bee which makes honey in the ground, Also mabuwa, syaansi, e.g. Nitwali kusya caansi twajana buci bunji. = When we were digging for small bees we found plenty of honey.
a barbed spear, pl. zyaanza, e.g. Isumo lyacaanza lilakatazya kulijwa nolyayasa munyama. It is difficult to removed a barbed spear if it has pierced an animal. Also mumba.

horned head of cattle (alive or dead) pl. zyaanza, e.g. Caanza camusune wangu cilandikonda. The horned head of my ox gives me delight. Izyaanza zimwi bakazifwupula akuzibikka acuumbwe alimwi amicila imwi yakabikkwa acuumbwe. = They recovered some of the horned heads of cattle and put them on the grave and again some of the tails were put on the grave. caanza campongo = a horned head of a goat

one's appearance, e.g. Ooyu muntu ulaa caanza cabausyi. This person has the facial expression of his father. Nabulongo wakawaalide meso akwe acaanza camulumi wabo. = Nabulongo threw her eyes on the facial expression of her husband. Also cikozyanyo.

a structure for hanging something, e.g. Caanzikilo cazisani zyangu cakakosoka. The hanger for my clothes broke. Kamuya mukabikke zisani zyanu acaanzikilo. Go and put your clothes on the hanger. Caanzikilo cakali kulamatikwa kubwaanda, cakali kwiitwa kuti 'makolo'. The hangers or shelving was attached to the wall, it was called makolo. Wakali kusisa kkii kunsi amabbuku aakali acaanzikilo. = He was hiding the key under books which were on the shelf. Also mulenga.
an armlet of grass, pl. zyaaso, e.g. Kondilukila caaso. = Make me an armlet of grass. Also nsambo.
a cattle kraal, pl. zyaata, e.g. Kamucimwaya caata. = Break down the kraal. Also ciba, cimpati.
a tool, e.g. Muntu musongo ulabweza cakubelesya naya kumilimo. = An intelligent person takes a tool when going to work. Also cibelesyo.
inheritance, heritage, e.g. Cakukona cangu ninombe. = My inheritance is cattle. Also cikono.
something for writing with, e.g. Tandijisi cakulembya. = I have nothing to write with. Also cilembyo
something to dip into, e.g. Twakali kwiide kubuya nsima jilo nkaambo twakabula cakulisya. = We were just eating nsima yesterday because we had no relish to dip into. Also cilisyo.
food, pl. zyakulya, e.g. Cakulya mutacilisyi babwa, ndaboola inoino. = Do not let the dogs eat the food, I am coming right now.
an article of clothing, pl. zyakusama, e.g. Cakusama comwe camwana cuulwa nkuku zyobilo. = One article of clothing for a child is sold for two chickens. Also cisani.

a thumb, pl. zyala, e.g. Tulalilamba mate azyala zyesu zyamaboko akuzigumika antoomwe. = We will smear ourselves with saliva using our thumbs and touching them together. (a children's game) Muntu utiikkalwe nzinini acala cakwe nguujisi mubwa wakabba mai. = The person on whose thumb a fly is about to settle is the owner of the dog who ate the eggs. Also caala.
a big toe or thumb, pl. zyalananda, e.g. Ibbwe lyandipwaya acalananda. = A stone has smashed my big toe. Ndalipwaya nsando a calananda. = I have hit myself with a hammer on the thumb.
the chest, pl. zyamba, e.g. Camba ca Mutinta cilaangamene. = Mutinta's chest is expansive.
patience, fortitude, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu ulaa camba, tafwambaani kunyema. = This woman is patient, she does not anger quickly.
a large cooking pot, e.g. Insima ijikilwa mucambikwa. = Nsima is cooked in a large pot. Also caambikwa.
a porcupine, pl. banaminungwe, e.g. Nungu zyacaminungwe zilayasa. = The quills of a porcupine pierce. cf. cinungwe (nungu = one quill)
a river plant green relish used Nov. and June-July) and can be moulded into a cake, e.g. Baama bajikide camudonga. = My mother has cooked a river plant.
a murderer, a madman, e.g. Camukwapa bamwaanga sunu. = They have arrested the criminal today.

a plant (Cissus quandrangularis), weak mixture of water and crushed stem used to speed difficult delivery in goats or to heal Newcastle disease in chickens. e.g. Kamubikka camulunga-lunga munywida nkuku kutegwa zitaciswi. = Put the camulunga-lunga medicine where the hens drink so that they do not become sick. Also namununga.
a chameleon, e.g. Bamwi bantu balamuyoowa camuntambwe. = Some people are afraid of a chameleon. Also naluntaambwe.
a chameleon, Also naluntaambwe, camuntambwe.

chemical fertilizer, e.g. Uuno mwaka bantu bakalima kabotu nkaambo bakajana camutunzya. = This year the people had a good harvest because they found fertilizer. Kubelesya camutunzya cisampuzya bulongo. = Using fertilizer leaches the soil.
a shrub (it produces fire by friction), e.g. Mulilo taukatazyi kubamba acamuzaki. = It is not difficult to produce fire from the *camuzaki* bush plant.
a type of edible grass (Panicum maximum Jacq.) In Feb. the seeds are boiled as a cereal. e.g. Nsena-mulide *camuzenene* mubuzumi bwangu. = I have never eaten edible grass in my whole life.

a child (derogative usage, from *mwana*), e.g. *Cana cangu cilineneede kapati*. My baby is very fat. e.g. *Eeci cana tacililemeki nkaambo citukila bapati*. = This brat is not respectful because it curses the elders.

a woman with bad or unusual behaviour, e.g. *Canakazi cili boobu cilaa civwekuvweku maila ncaamana*. = Such a woman is careless that is why the millet is finished. *Eeci canakazi cilasunda nkaambo cisesya bantu*. = This woman is enter-taining because she makes people laugh. *Eeci canakazi cilasunda nkaambo nciinga sibasankwa*. = This woman is notorious because she is fond of men. *Mumulonga twajana canakazi cisondokede*. = We found a mad woman in the river.

curds, (a soft white substance formed when milk coagulates, used as a basis for cheese.) e.g. *Ooyu mwana ulaciyanda canda*. = This child likes curds. *Beembela balanywa canda nobazwa kukweembela*. = The herders drink thick milk when they herd. Also *bwanda, cibbobbe, cipwaza*.
frost, e.g. *Sunu kwali candwa mumusena*. = Today there was frost in the vlei. Also *caanda*.
grass, (derogative of *mani*) e.g. *Kamugwisya cani mucikkocci, mubikke ndongwe*. = Remove the old grass from the scotch-cart and put in groundnuts.
a veil, e.g. Bakazuminana kuti baule ulya *ccaccaacca* usiya. = They agreed to buy that black veil.
a blanket with a fringe, pl. *ma-ccali*, e.g. *Ipayi lyaccali lilakasaala kapati*. = A blanket with a fringe is very warm. Also *cali*
a matchet, e.g. Wakabelesya *cceba kukosola mutwe wasyuumbwa*. = He used a matchet to cut off the lion's head.
the passing of days, e.g. *Ma-zuba aya ngobwene nguccovwani azu-bulula tunji*. = These days which you see are passing by, revealing many things.

froth, lather or suds, e.g. *Ooyu mwana usobana meenda alaa ccovwu*. = This child is playing with water which has a lot of lather. *Wakasansamuna ccovwu lyansipa njaakali kusanzyizya*. = He wiped away the suds of the soap with which he had been washing. *Mubwa wasondoka uzwa ccovwu kumulomo*. = The dog that went mad had froth coming from the mouth.
a fool, e.g. Mebo nseli waccubi. = I am not a fool.

a barred owl, pl. *ba-ceeba-nombe*, (the only owl which is said to bring evil.) e.g. *Ceebanombe kuti kalila munsi ananda inga mmalweza*. = If a barred owl hoots near a house it is an evil omen. *Webo wiide kundibona mbuli kuti ndilazilaika mbuli ceebanombe calo citakonzyi kuzibauka mpocakkala kale*. = You see me as if I am stupid like a barred owl who cannot look around from where it is sitting.
a malachite kingfisher, pl. *baceebela*, e.g. *Ceebela ulalya tutaka mumeenda*. = The malachite kingfisher eats small fish in the water.
view, pl. *zyeebelwa*, e.g. *Ceebelwa mucipekupeku sunu ngu Shaka*. = What is to be viewed on T.V. today is 'Shaka'

a visual aid, a display, pl. zyeebezyo, e.g. Mwiiyi ubelesya ceebezyo nayiisya. = The teacher uses a visual aid when teaching. Kwakali zyeebezyo zinji ku Monze. = There was a lot of things on show at Monze.
time of plenty, e.g. Waka-lumbaizya mizimo yakwe yakamusisya aceebululwa cazyakulya. = She praised her spirits who had led her to a time of plenty.
a small locust-bird, pl. bace-ekela, e.g. Ndajana tanga lyabaceekela. = I found a flock of small locust-birds
a part of anything, e.g. Bacili kuyandaula ceela camootokala muzintoo-lo. = They are still searching for a spare part for the car in the shops. Also cibeela
porridge, thick porridge mixed with sour or fresh milk, e.g. Kamubapa ceele bana balye, bafwa nzala. = Give the children porridge so that they can eat, they are starving. Also cikandi
a big container for measuring grain, pl. zyeeleko, e.g. Eeci cibulo ncee-leko camapopwe. = This bucket is the measuring container for (distributing) maize. Also cipimyo
something to measure with, pl. zyeelekelo, e.g. Ceelekelo eeci cileelela nkaambo bantu tabatongooki. = This measure is acceptable as the people do not complain.
weighing machine
a measure, e.g. Ceelelo ncayelela oyu cili kabotu. = The measure by which this one measures is just.

a measure, a lid, e.g. Bapima kapenta nobaulisya inga ceelesyo ntusinsyo nomuba mututiba tuniini. = The lids of containers or little dishes are used by those who measure the little fishes when they are selling them.
the last in a sequence, e.g. Koya ukagonke cisamu ceelezya. = Go and cut the tree which is at the end of the line.

the outward appearance of a person, puppet, a showpiece, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngumwabikka acuuno nceelezyo buyo. = This person whom you have placed on the chair is only a puppet. Maanu mulaajisi, pesi tamwaabelesyi pe, bongo nobuliko mumutwe nceelezyo biyo. = You have intelligence but you do not use it, the brains are there but just empty.
the spirit of a dead person, can be expelled by traditional medicine or fumigation e.g. Ceelo camunene Bbaampi catukatazya swebo. = The spirit of the old man Bbaampi is troubling us. Also cilubi

grease from oily food, raw groundnuts pounded to pulp, e.g. Bana bajisi ceema kumilomo nkaambo balikulya yamafwuta. = The children have greasy mouths because they have been eating what is oily. Also cimwe.
a large household axe, a working axe, e.g. Ceembe eci cilabosya. = This axe is sharp.
a battle-axe, e.g. Tubamba ceembe-milonga. = We are making a battle-axe.
a second smaller stomach of fuminants, e.g. Kaindi ceembelelo cakali kulidwa kugobelo. = Long ago the second stomach of cattle was eaten at the male place of gathering.
a second smaller stomach of ruminants, e.g. Bamwi balalya ceembelo carjombe. = Some eat the second stomach of cattle. Also ceembelelo.
a bad smell from the human body, e.g. Ooyu muntu ulaa ceembezi. = This person has an unpleasant body odour. Also kaganko.

a musical horn, e.g. Bamacembele bayiisya kamwale kusiba ceembo. = The elderly women are teaching ---|--the initiate how to blow the musical horn. Kamwale usobana *ceembo* *munanda*. The female initiate is playing a musical horn in the house. Also *mweembo*. muntu tajisi *ceenzya* nkaambo maulu onse akatyolooka. = This person has nothing to walk with because all his legs were broken.

exhaustion, to be exhausted, e.g. Nindakamana kulunduka ndakafwa *ceempa*. = When I was finished running I was exhausted. Muntu walikutandwa syuumbwa wafwa *ceempa*. = The one who was chased by a lion has been overcome with exhaustion.

a slice of a comb with honey, e.g. Ndalomba mundaabile *ceeya cabuci* comwe. = I am asking that you give me one slice of honey-comb. Basankwa bacilya *ceeya cabuci*. = The boys have eaten a slice of honey-comb. Also *ciyeeya*
an edible mushroom, pl. *baceenda-bulima*, e.g. *Baceendabuli-ma mbowa bunona kapati*. = The *cee-ndabulima* are mushrooms which are very tasty. Also *bowa*.
tail of a bird, e.g. *Ceeye caka-yuni kaya cakajuka*. = The tail of that bird has been plucked out.
a leg, e.g. *Ceendo cangu cilizimbide mpundaliyasa keembe*. = My leg is swollen where I cut myself with an axe.
a facsimile, comparison, e.g. *Ceezyanyo caciteenge eci nceciya*. = The copy of this chitenge is that one. Also *cikozyanyo*.
a distance, e.g. Kuzwa ku Chikuni ku-sika ku Chiyobola tacili *ceendo cilamfwu*. = It is not a long distance from Chikuni to Chiyobola.
a measuring rule, e.g. *Ceezyo cakusyanga maila amaanza ndooye*. = A measuring instrument used when planting millet by hand is a string. Also *cipimyo*
an enclosed fire or heating system, a furnace, e.g. Kamuyungizya nkuni *muceengelo*. Add firewood to the boiler. Also *citofwu, cijikilo*.

waist-beads *cekeceke* a small fish with a sharp bone which makes sounds and struggles violently when caught, e.g. Bazubi bajaya *cekeceke akanyandi*. The fishermen caught a *cekeceke* fish with a net. Ulee-lede kucenjela nosungulula *cekeceke mukalobo*. You should be careful when unhooking a *cekeceke* fish. Also *cekwecekwe*.
a mark, e.g. Wakabikka *cee-ngwe cituba kusule ajekete ndyaaka-samide*. He made a white mark at the back of the jacket he was wearing.
belonging to the past, e.g. Cizyano *ceensiku cankolola cakali cibotu kapati*. The *nkolola* dance of the past was excellent. Also *censiku*.
a species of small fish dangerous to handle, e.g. Baalumi ba-alilwa kumujata *cekwecekwe*. = The men have failed to catch the *cekwecekwe* fish. Also *cekeceke*.
companion, e.g. *Ceenzyina acisyumani caampe mbuntele*. = What goes well with dried vegetable relish is mashed groundnuts. Also *ceenzinyina*.
a growth in the body, e.g. Mwida mwakaba *cela* - cikoto cicisisya. = In the stomach there developed a growth - an extremely painful lump. Also *cipelu*
good luck in agriculture e.g. Uuno mwaka kunokuli *ceenzya*. = This year there will be good luck in agriculture. Also *ceyo, ceenzyo*.
the nipple of woman's breast, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu ulaa cicisa *acele*. = This woman has a sore on the nipple of her breast. Also *nonso*.
something to help one walk, e.g. Ooyu *celo* a ghost, pl. *zileyo*, e.g. *Celo cila-*
bantu akubanyonganya. = The evil spirit enters people and confuses them. (In the Zambezi valley sorcerers are said to have control over many zyelo.) Also ceelo.
a thing of the past, e.g. Eeci ciimbo ncensiku. This song is of the past. Also ceensiku, cakaindi, cakale.

a grasshopper, pl. bacenze e.g. Basicikolo basobanya cenze. The pupils are playing with a grasshopper. Uuno mwaka kuli bacenze banji. This year there are plenty of grasshoppers. Also mpaso, cikwikwi, nsozi.
abundance of food, e.g. Mwakali kwakali ceo. Last year there was food in abundance. Mwaka ujisi mvwula mbotu ngwaceo. = The year which has good rain is a year of plenty. Also ceyo.

type of tree (Datura sp.), powdered seeds rubbed into incisions to relieve pain under skin. e.g. Muntu uciswa lusinga ucumbwa cesiamoyo. = A person who is suffering from a nerve-pain rubs powdered seeds into incisions.
a vervet monkey, pl. baceta, e.g. Baceta balalya mapopwe naacili matete. = The monkeys eat maize when it is still soft and fresh.
a year of plenty, e.g. Mwaka wacewo bantu bajisi cakulya cinji. = In a year of plenty the people have sufficient food. Also ceo, ceyo.
a period when there is no shortage of food. e.g. Myaka yobilo yainda yakali yaceyo. The past two years were years of plenty. Also ceo.
the language, Africaans, early form known as Taal. e.g. Bamadaala balikke mbabazyi Chibbunu mazubaano. = Only the old people know Africaans these days.
a Boer, (derogative) e.g. Kaindi lyacibbalo kuti Chibbunu cabbuka bantu bakali kutija. = Long ago when there was forced labour, when a Boer appeared the people used to flee.
the language of the Babemba people, e.g. Chibemba mmusyobo uumwi utakatazyi. Chibemba is another language which is not difficult. (for a Tonga person)
a clan name, e.g. Mukowa waba Chibuwa mmusyoonto mucisi muno. = The Chibuwa clan is very small in this territory.
the language of the Baila, e.g. Chiila nChitonga acalo. The Ila language is also Chitonga (i.e related to Chitonga)
The English language, e.g. Chikuwa ncabantu bamwi batuba mubala. = English is of another people who are white in colour. Also Chingisi.
God ("one prayed to for the rain-cloud"), e.g. Tukalombe mvwula kuli Chilombwamuyoba. = Let us go to pray to God for rain. Also Leza (for other names for God)
any non-Tonga language, e.g. Kufwumbwa musyobo utali Chitonga, nChilumbu. = Whichever tribe which is not Tonga is referred to by the Tonga as Chilumbu.
Dialect of Mukkuni (Tonga-leya), e.g. Chitonga Chinamukkuni ciliimpene acesu. = The Chitonga of the Mukuni people is different from ours. (i.e. another dialect.)
a language used in Eastern Province of Zambia and many Zambian towns, e.g. Kujwe lya Lusaka kujanika kapati Chinyanja. East of Lusaka is where Chinyanja is mostly found.
the local language of a place, (used as adjective) e.g. Cisyobo cinyezi kucooko cakumusanza kuno nChitonga. = The local language of the Southern Province is Chitonga.
the language of the Batonga, e.g. Bana bamwi balayanda kwiiya Chitonga muzikolo. = Some children like to learn Chitonga in the schools. Mulaka wangu nChitonga. = My language is Chitonga.
a European language, e.g. Bamakuwa boonse bakanana Chizungu. = All Europeans speak a European language
a cattle kraal, e.g. Muciba cokwesu tulaa nombe zyosanwe. = We have got five cattle in our kraal. Also cimpati, luba.

a mantle, cloth worn loosely around shoulders, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kusama cibaakani. = Long ago the people were wearing the cibaakani garment. Mudaala uyabikide cibaakani agwezyo. = The old man is wearing a cloth over his shoulder.

The first piece of cloth or top used by women to cover their breasts when Euopeans came, pl. zibaanda, e.g. Bamakaintu bakatalika kusama zibaanda nibakaboola bamakuwa omuno mucisi. = The women started to wear blouses when the Euopeans came to this country.
a jacket, e.g. Cibaci cangu cilaa tombe. Kondisanzyila cibaci cangu. = My jacket is full of dirt. Wash my jacket for me. Also cibaki.
a place, e.g. Cibaka eci ncibotu kuyakila cibbadela. = This place is good for building a hospital.
any piece of clothing, e.g. Cibaki cangu caba cakaindi. = My coat has become a thing of the past. i.e. has become worn.
a buttock ulcer, e.g. Mwana ulaa cibala atako. = The child has an ulcer on the buttock. Also cuute, ibbata
a beer store, e.g. Tuya kukuula bukoko kucibala. = We are going to buy beer at the beer-store.
a grass head-pad for carrying firewood, e.g. Amuluke cibale cakuyumunzya nkuni. = Weave a head-pad for carrying firewood.
a cataract in the eye, e.g. Ooyu musimbi taboni kabotu nkaambo ulaa cibale muliso. = This girl does not see well as she has a cataract in the eye. Also citube.
a chapter in a book, e.g. Cibalo casulwe anondo ncibotu. = The chapter about the hare and the tortoise is good.
caliu. = The third chapter was good.
to the side, e.g. Wakali kwiima acibalibali kweebela meenda ali muzyiba. = He was standing at the side admiring the water of the lake.

a grass-fence erected to protect from wind, e.g. Cibalu ncibotu kusinkila muwo. = A grass screen is good for blocking the wind. Basimbi baya kukujwa bwizu bwakuyaka cibalu cakulisitilizya muwo. = The girls are going to cut grass to build a grass-screen for protection from the wind. Also cilisitilizyo, cicinjilizyo.
method of doing something, as making beer, e.g. Eeci cibambi cakubamba tumbuwa tacili cibotu. = This method for making buns is not good.

a plain, open country with little or no trees, e.g. Kuzwa a Monze kuya ku Mazabuka kuli cibanda cipati. = From Monze to Mazabuka there is a big plain. Cibanda ca Moomba tacijisi zisamu zinji. = The plain at Moomba hasn't many trees. Kwakali cibanda naa musena mupati walo wakali kutegwa bbanda lya Himayuwe. = There was a plain or an extensive vlei which was called the great plain of Himayuwe.

a molar tooth, (grinding tooth at the back of the mouth) pl. bacibanda: e.g. Mwana uzwa bacibanda ulasoomona. = A child whose molar teeth are appearing gets diarrhoea. Bacibanda mukanwa bakamanide kulukuka. = The molar teeth in his mouth had all fallen out. (cibanda uyelezya = wisdom tooth, each of the four molars which appear at about the age of twenty)
a spirit, e.g. Simasabe nguwacibona ci-banda ncaali kutandaanya. = A possessed person is the one who saw a ghost which s/he was chasing.
a cake of meal, e.g. Bana bangu balya cibande. = My children are eating a cake of meal Also cibbuubbu.

an axe with cresent-shaped blade, carried as weapon when walking out, a big knife, e.g. Munene nayakukufwunda loozi utola cibanga. = When the old man goes to look for fibre he takes a big knife with him. Basyaneene batoleela acibanga kudilwe. = My grandfather took an axe with him to the funeral. Musankwa ugonsya cibanga zisamu. = The boy is cutting the trees with an axe.
a flat basket, e.g. Mukaintu waku Mulongaalwiili walikusambala cibango sunu. = A woman from Mulongaalwiili was selling a basket today.
