a nest of bees, e.g. Twabona cibangu canzuki mumpako yacisamu. = We saw a nest of bees in the hole of a tree.

the hole in a grain-bin for removing grain, e.g. Mwaakuyaka butala bwamapopwe, mukabikke cibanzyo cisyonto kutegwa bantu kabatabbi. = When you build a grain-bin, put a small hole for removing the grain so that people won't be stealing. Also cipulo (vb. -banza, remove grain from bin)

a friendly way of beginning marriage negotiations, the representative of the prospective bridegroom gives money to the girls' family. e.g. Muzyali wamusankwa utaanguna kupa cibanzyo kubazyali bamusimbi. = The parent of the boy first gives money to the parents of the girl.
instrument for knocking out teeth, e.g. Keembe ncicakali cibanzyo camenyo kaindi. It was the axe which was the instrument for knocking out the teeth long ago.
a mark or scar, pl. zibata, e.g. Wakalijisi zibata-bata mubili oonse mwaakali kuyasaulwa zipeni. = He had scars all over his body where he had been cut by knives.
an otter, e.g. Babwa bajaya cibawe. = The dogs have killed an otter.

a fence, an enclosure, e.g. Cibaya kumbewu tacili kabotu, ncozinjila nombe. = The garden fence is not good, that is why cattle enter. Basankwa basya zilindi zyakusimpa zisamu zyacibaya. = The boys are digging holes for inserting poles for a fence. Mainza uleepa syokwe munzila iya kucibaya canombe akuzibondo zyampongo ambelele. = Mainza removes grass from the path going to the cattle enclosure and to the enclosure of the goats and sheep. Also cikwakwa.
ferocious person, e.g. Ooyu Mudyaka cakali cibbabbani camulombwana citazundwi matanga. = This Mudyaka was a ferocious man who was not conquered by crowds of people.
a hospital, e.g. Baneene baya kukusilikwa kucibbadela. = My grandfather has gone to the hospital for treatment.

a kick, e.g. Bamuuma cibbakala wasandamuka oyu. = They have given him a kick and he turned upside down. Mbongolo yanduuma cibbakala amwiindi. = The donkey kicked me on the calf of the leg. (See vb.-bbakila) Ino naacili kukokobela kugusya mali, musilikani wakatalika kulyata cibbakala kumatako. = Now as he was slow to take out the money, the policeman began to kick his bottom. Also mulazyi, musembele.
a kick, pl. zibbakela, e.g. nombe azyalo zyuuma zibbakela. = Cattle also can strike with kicks.
sticks pointed together to support load on head, e.g. Baama babamba cibbale cakuyumuzya nkuni. = My mother made a structure for carrying firewood.

forced labour, e.g. Mazuba acibbalo akali kuyoosya kubakubusi abamanene bacilimvwide. = The days of forced labour were fearful for young and old men, who were still strong. Kaindi-kaindi bantu bakali kutolwa cibbalo bakali kupegwa kubeleka milimo miyumu. = Long ago the people who were taken on forced labour were made to work on very difficult projects. Cibbalo camwakali cakandeempya akundicelesya kubeleka milimo yangu. The forced labour of last year made me suffer and be late for doing my work.

a patch on clothes, or any piece of material, e.g. Kondipa cibbampi eco mbikke cigamba abuluke. = Give me that piece of material so that I put a patch on the trousers. Also cimami, cigombo, citwibi, cigamba.
moneyto persuade people to talk, a consultation fee, e.g. Bataata bakapa mukwaabo mali aacibbanuna mulomo kutegwa baambauzyanye. My father gave his son-in-law money to persuade him to talk to him.

tanamup acibbanuna mulomo. = The one who brought the girl for marriage did not yet give her the money 'for opening the mouth'. Kuti koyanda kubuzya kaambo kakukatazya kumwami, nkusaanguna kumupa cibbanuna mulomo. = If you want to get help from the chief concerning a matter which troubles you, you should first of all pay him a consultation fee.
charm used by a jealous person to make another impotent, e.g. Wakamuteezya cibbayi, ncatazyali. = He bewitched him by using a charm, that is why he does not have children.

anything for carrying a baby on the back, e.g. Mwana komubbazya cibbazyo cakwe nkaambo ncecipati. = Use the baby's cloth to carry it on your back for it is big enough. Cibbazyo camwana oyu cili kuli ubbedwe. The cloth for carrying this child is with the one who is being carried. Also ngubo.
lion-cloth, e.g. Langa cibbesu cangu cadonkoka. Look my lion-cloth has been torn. Also mubangi
cheese, e.g. Cibbobbe cilaa busani bubotu mumubili wamuntu. = Cheese has good nutrients for a person's body.
frothy fresh and sour milk mixed in calabash, e.g. Kosanganya mukupa amabisi kutegwa kube cibbobbe. = Mix fresh milk with sour to make thick sour milk.
a commotion, e.g. Cakaide kuba cibbobboobbo. There was just a commotion.
lily, pl. mabbolombombo, e.g. Mwana uulya uyanda cibbolombombo cili mumeenda. = That child likes the waterlilys in the water.
a waterlily, pl. mabbolo-mombo, e.g. Cibbolomombo eci cileebeka. = This lily is beautiful.
a big swelling, e.g. Uyakubaa cibbozu munsingo. = You will have a big swelling in your neck.
a parcel, e.g. Bana nibakamubona, bakalunduka kuti batambule cibbudu cakaangidwe ancinga. = When the child-ren saw him, they ran to receive the parcel which was tied on the bicycle.
a pair of shorts, e.g. Cibudula ncibanduulila cakomena. = The shorts which they bought me is too big in size. Mwana komusamika kabotu cibbudula. Dress the child properly with shorts.
a shoe brush, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Cibbulasho eeci ncakupukutya mabbusu. This brush is for polishing shoes.
a ground-nut bin, e.g. Amundiyakile cibbule cakubikkila nyemu. = Build me a bin for storing groundnuts. Cibbule cabaama cizwide ndongwe. = The groundnut store of my mother is full.

the emerald-spotted dove, e.g. Ndajana cibbululu musyokwe neeli kunkuni. I found an emerald-spotted dove in the bush when I was collecting firewood. Cibbululu cilauluka mbubwena mbuli nziba. An emerald-spotted dove flies like an ordinary dove.
relationship by kin, e.g. Moonde a Mwiinde mbacibbululu. = Moonde and Mwiinde are related by blood.
a brick-bench, e.g. Basankwa bakakkala acibbumbile. = The boys sat on the brick-bench.
hand without fingers or stump of leg, e.g. Muntu ulaa cinanta ujisi cibbumpu cajanza, nokuba cibbumpu cakuulu. = A person who has leprosy has a stump of a hand or a stump of a leg.
muntu takwe minwe, ncibbumpu buyo. This person has no toes, it (the foot) is just a stump. Also cibbumpununu.

a hand without fingers or a mutilated finger a foot without toes, e.g. Bamuka baacisya bakazyala mwana ulaa cibbumpununu. = The wife of my uncle gave birth to a child with toes missing. Also cibbumpu.
an ash heap, e.g. Eeli twe ukalisowele kumuunda kutali kucibbunta. = Throw this ash on the field and not on to the ash-heap. Also cibbuta, itantala.
an ash heap, e.g. Koya ukalete nkuni kucibbuta. = Go and bring firewood to the ash-heap. Also cibbunta.

a heavy parcel, a number of articles bundled together at random, e.g. Cibbutu ciyumwide bacembele cilalema. = The parcel carried by the old woman is heavy. Sikansondo ujisi cibbutu cazigwete-gwete. A madman is carrying a parcel of assorted articles. Ooyu uyumwide cibbutu cazisani kuya kwabo. This one is carrying a bundle of clothes to her/his home.

a cake of meal, e.g. Kamuzitwa mbula mubambe cibbuubbu. = Pound the mbula fruit so that you make a cake. Bana balya cibbuubbu cambula. = The children are eating a cake of mbula fruit. Yakali nsima ndala yamaila muceme, aboobo niyakayokwa yakaide kuba mbuli cibbuubbu. = It was the left-over food of millet and so when it was roasted it just became like a cake of fresh-crushed maize.
a pond containing many crabs, e.g. Eciya cizyiba ncibbwankala. = That pond is one which contains many crabs.
part/piece of something, e.g. Amundaabile cibeela calingo ndipe mwana. Give me a slice of mango so that I give it to the child.
a heron, e.g. Ngucibeengelele wabula nswi. It is a heron which has no fish. Also lubengelele
calf in the womb, e.g. Inombe ilaa cibele. The cow is in calf.
a cow's udder, e.g. Inombe yokwesu ilaa cibele cipati. = Our cow has a large udder.

a disease which can afflict an infant, e.g. Cibele mbulwazi bucisa mwana kuti bamatumbu banyonsezya antoomwe bana kuti umwi kacingilidwe aamusamu mubi. = Cibele is a disease which afflicts a baby if many women are suckling many children together if one of them has a dangerous protective charm.
the thigh, e.g. Mulwazi ulaa cicisa acibelo. = The patient has a sore of the thigh.
Saturday, e.g. Ndamwaambila kuti akaboole zoona mu Cibelu kutegwa tukayoome. = I told him to come the day after tomorrow, on Saturday so that we chat.

gap between teeth, e.g. Linyo lyakali kucisa lyakajugwa aboobo kwakacaala cibende. = The tooth which was paining was removed, consequently a gap remained between the teeth. Wakalukuka, kwaile kucaala cibende. = When he lost a tooth, a gap just remained.
notch in lip of pot, e.g. Eeyi mpoto ilaa cibende yakakomoka. = This pot which has a notch on the lip has been chipped.

a machete, e.g. Cibenga camudaala catyoka mwiini. = The matchet of the old man has had its handle broken. Mucembele utumbusya ubelesya cibenga antela somo libosya ndyakusisya kalindi kakuzikkila macembele. = The midwife uses a machete or a sharp knife-like instrument to dig a hole to bury the afterbirth.
an energetic person, e.g. Ooyu mwaalumi ncibenge camilimo. = This man is energetic in his deeds. Also similimo.
a European knife, e.g. Eeci cibesyi tacibosyi pe. = This knife is not sharp. Also mesi, ntibba, cipeni.

a clay cooking pot, e.g. Musamu wakusamba mwana unyike mucibia. = Soak the medicine for washing the child in a clay pot. Cibia ncibotu kujikila muteezi. = A clay pot is good for cooking okra. Also cibiya.

wood cut to make a clearing, a heap of firewood, e.g. Nkuni zyakujisya mukabweze acibibi cili kumuunda. = Get firewood for cooking from the heap in the field. Bacembele bali kukudoneka cibibi. = The old woman was burning a heap of branches. Tuyakukuumpa cibibi kumapande. = We are going to burn heaps of branches in the newly prepared field.
a good patch of mealies, cibibi camapopwe.
a patch of leprosy, pl. zibika, e.g. Muntu wakali kuciswa cinanta ulaa cibika amubili. = The man who had leprosy had a patch on the body.

a rabbit with a short tail, a rockrabbit, the dassie, a rock badger, pl. bacibila, e.g. Babwa banji bajaya cibila nitwali kuvwima. = Many dogs killed a rockrabbit when we were hunting. Mubwa ulaluma bacibila mumabwe. = The dog caught rock-rabbits among the rocks. Cipumpumene akati kabbwe ngucibila. = "The one seated in the middle stone, is a rock rabbit." (a riddle) Uyakucibona cakamubuzya mucila cibila. = You will see what raised the tail of the rock-rabbit.
an unfinished hoe-head, e.g. Mubwa ndamuumya cibimbi camwiini. = I was using a hoe-head to beat the dog.
a measure of cloth, e.g. Eeci cibimbi ncakusumina mwana cisani. = This piece of cloth is for sewing the baby's dress. Also cibbampi, cibibi.

an earthenware container used to receive a portion of meal, e.g. Bamaama nobakali kuziya mapopwe aziyo, bakali kubelesya nkando, nkabela busu bwakali kulokela mucibimbili. = When mother was grinding maize on a stone with a grinding stone, the flour was dropping into the clay container. Also cibumbili
a length of cloth Also cibibi

a small tortoise, e.g. Kwainda cibinda uyabukwakwaila kweenda. = A tortoise passed, crawling as it went. Cibinda wakalya bowa bosanwe akusiya bobile buyo. = The tortoise ate five mushrooms and left only two.
master of craft, one who has wisdom and courage in judgement, e.g. Mudaala wafwa mumunzi mwa Cheelo wali cibinda. = The old man who died at Cheelo's village was a real craftsman.

the traditional illness of a person who has not undergone the ritual of cleansing, e.g. Mukamwanaangu wakabaa *cibinde* nkaambo wakakaka kusala-zigwa. = My daughter-in-law suffered from the ritual illness because she refused to be cleansed. Webo *cibinde* cilakucaa-lila, tookasalazigwa. = A ritual illness will remain in you because you were not puri-fied.
a clay vessel for putting in milk when milking, e.g. Kotila mukupa *mucibinzilo*. = Put the milk in the clay milking pot. Also cibizilo, cibisilo.

something for driving animals, e.g. *Cibinzyo* cajombe mmuluso antela mmukkwilo. = What drives the cattle is a flexible stick or a whip. Basune kobauma *acibinzyo* kutegwa beendesye. = Beat the oxen with a stick so that they move more quickly.

a pot for any use, a clay cooking pot, e.g. Muteezi unona kujikila *mucibiya*. = Okra is nice when cooked in a clay pot. *Cibiya* cakabumba bacembele ncibotu. = The clay pot made by the old woman is beautiful. Musimbi ulaiya ku-bumba *zibiya*. = The girl is learning to mould clay pots.
control, dependence, e.g. Uli *mucibiya* camunanga. = You are under the treat-ment of a witchdoctor. i.e. You are receiv-ing the medicines prepared in his pot.

a zebra, e.g. Musyokwe mutwa-bede, twabona *cibize* uzyede bana bobile. = In the bush where we were, we saw a zebra who had given birth to two. Myee-ngwe ilaali *cibize* ili mbuli businde. = Lines which are on a zebra are like land ploughed for next year's use. Also namuwawa, imbizi.
a clay pot for storing milk or water, e.g. Kotila meenda akunywa mu-*cibizilo*. = Pour the drinking water into the storage pot. Also cibinzilo, cipempa.
hair-ball vomited by cattle, pl. *zibobo*, e.g. Inombe zikkuta kapati zilaluka *zibobo* masiku. = Cows which are full, vomit hair-balls at night.
growl of a lion, e.g. *Cibobo* casyuu-mbwa cilayoosya. = The growl of a lion is terrifying.
luck, e.g. Chitebenta wakalaa *ciboko* cibotu kukuvwuba nombe. = Chite-benta had good luck in keeping cattle. Also coolwe.
a type of reddish sorgum, e.g. Batonga bakujwe balima *cibolwe*. = The eastern Batonga plant a sorgum known as *cibolwe*. Also cikolwe, nkolwe.
measles, e.g. Moonga uci-swa *cibombo*. = Moonga has measles. Also cifwumu, cibombwe.
a piece of the *mubombo* tree, e.g. Koleta cikuni *cacibombo* eco tusikke. = Bring that piece of *mubombo* so that we insert it (in the fireplace).
impurities left after skimming castor oil, fat that floats to the top, e.g. Mwamana kuzenga mafwuta, *cibombo* mutacisowi. = When you are finished taking out the fat, do not throw it away.
measles, e.g. Kwakasika bulwazi bwacibombwe aboobo bana baniini beelede kukwabililwa. = There is a break-out of measles and so the children need to be protected. Also cifwumu.

sheep or goat kraal, pl. *zi-bondo*, e.g. Masiku mbelele ziloona mu-*zibondo*. Sheep sleep at night in the sheep-kraal. Silinde wakaswaya nkumba kumunzi wayo. Wakaijana iyaka *cibondo* cambelele. Silinde visited the snail at it's village. He found it was building a sheep-kraal.

a kind of edible leaf or flow-er, e.g. *Cibondwe* cilaligwa mbuli cisyu. = The *cibondwe* leaf is eaten as a relish. Baama baamba kuti tukaletelezye *cibon-dwe* kumuunda. = Mother said we should bring along this *cibondwe* relish. Also cimowa, bboonko.
a mirror, e.g. *Mukandu-ulilizye cibonebone kudolopo.* = You can please buy me a mirror. Also cimbone-mbone, ciboniboni, cimbonimboni.

a disease of the anus, e.g. *Ooyu ncadingaama uciswa cibongozi.* = The reason why he bends down from time to time is that he is suffering from a disease of the anus. *Ooyu mwana ncatalyi kabotu ndiza uciswa cibongozi.* = This child has no appetite perhaps because it has a disease of the anus.
a mirror, e.g. *Eeci ciboni-boni cilandicenga.* = This mirror is deceiving me. Also cimbonimboni
a small type of bee which makes honey in a tree, e.g. *Bana balida buci bwaciboza mumutumbi.* = The children are gathering honey of the small bee from the *mutumbi* tree.

a single reed, pl. *zibu*, e.g. *Kobapa cibu bacembele bafwebele.* = Give the old woman a reed so that she can smoke. *Cibu cilabelesegwa kulizya namalwa.* = A reed is used in beating a small friction-drum. Also *lubu, lutete.*
a cattle sickness causing beasts to keep their tails up, e.g. *Aaka koombe kaciswa cibubu.* = This little calf has a disease called *cibubu.* Also *simusinginya* (a type of insect)
manufactured beer (as opposed to village beer), e.g. *Kunywa cibuku mazuba oonse kuleta cisi ansi.* = Drinking manufactured beer every day brings the country down.
a prophecy, e.g. *Cibukusyo camudaala cakalitondezya nikwakainda mezi yobilo.* = The prophesy of the old man was fulfilled when two months had passed. Also *moone, businsimi*
a container, e.g. *Mapopwe amakweelele mukaabikke mucibule.* = Put the unhusked cobs of maize in the small maize-bin. Also *citula*

any piece of manufactured metal, e.g. *Cibulo* citesya meenda mumugoti canyikila. = The bucket for drawing water has dropped down into the water. Ndayaswa *cibulo* kunsi akuulu. = I have been pierced under the foot by a piece of metal.
nimbleness, e.g. Mweemba weenda *cibulubulu* mbuli mpongo. = Mweemba walks as nimble as a goat. Tombela uyenzya *cibulubulu*. = A lizard moves nimbly.
a ball of thread, e.g. Baama balijisi *cibulunga* cabunweba. = Mother has a ball of thread.
a ball of thread, e.g. Ndiyanda *cibulungwe* cisubila. = I want a red ball of thread. Also *cibulunga*.

a railway platform, any constructed object, e.g. Citima kuti casika bantu inga bapilingana *acibumbili*. = When the train arrives, people become agitated on the platform. Bali kulindila citima bakkede *acibumbili*. = Those who are waiting for the train were seated on the platform. Also *cibimbili*.

the pot and the hole inserted in front of the grinding stone into which the material falls when ground. Busu bwamaila ngaakali kugaya mucembele bwakali kulokela *mucibumbili*. = The millet flour which the old woman was grinding was falling into the container placed in front of the grinding stone.
a low blackberry bush, e.g. *Cibumbu* cili munsi anzila cilizyede kapati. = The blackberry bush which is beside the path is full of fruit.
a rough, temporary roof, a roofed shelter without walls, e.g. Sikuyamina ukkala *mucibumbu*. = The one who guards the crops sits in a rough shelter. Also ngazi
a roof resting on the ground, e.g. *Cibumbu* cili ansi zyacoola mpongo. = The roof resting on the ground is demolished by goats.
the lower part of the stomach on the outside, e.g. Wandibbakela acibumbu. = She has kicked me on the lower part of the stomach. Also bbumbu
a sheller, e.g. Kamuleta cibumbuluzyo kutegwa tufwambaane kubuulula mapopwe. = Bring a sheller so that we can quickly shell the maize.
a stump of a limb, pl. zibumpununu, e.g. Zibumpununu cajanza akuulu zilacisa akaambo kazicisa zitaningapona. = The stumps of hand and leg are paining because of the sores which have not yet healed.

a type of tree, a willow tree (salix subserrata) found in all parts of Zambia, silvery foliage, branches used for basket-making, the bark of branches used to make whistles. Roots used for treatment of headaches and fever, leaves used as a laxative. e.g. Mwana waciswa mutwe mumusyide miyanda yacibumbya kutegwa anywe. = The child is suffering from a headache so you should dig up the roots of the cibumbya tree for it to drink. Also lilongwe, musompe, mvwule.

a crowd of people or herd of animals, e.g. Masiku bantu beelede kweenda cibunga kutali omwe-omwe pe. = At night people ought to move in a group not singly. Kukuzikka mwami wakafwa kwali cibunga cabantu. = At the burial of the chief there was a crowd of people. Cibunga cabananja cijisi buyo mucende omwe. = A herd of lechwe had only one bull. Also tanga

a meeting place, e.g. nanda yangu ncecibunganino munzi oonse. = My house is a meeting place for the whole village. Muswaangano wamunzi ulabeda kucibunganino kumulundu. = A meeting of the village will be held at the meeting place at the hill.
a cake of meal, e.g. Ndiyanda kulya cibunge canzembwe. = I want to eat a cake of millet.
The Pleiades (a cluster of stars in constellation Taurus), e.g. Cibungululu canyenyezi cabbila kale. = The Pleiades has already gone down. Also mulalabungu.
the waist, e.g. Cibuno cangu ndazyana inga ciile kuniaba. = Whenever I am dancing my waist twists very well. Cibuno cabuluke obu ncipati kuli ndime. = The waist of this trousers is too big for me.
a child born feet first, e.g. Musanda ngu Chibuno nkaambo naakazyalwa wakaletezya cibuno. = Musanda is (named)
because when he was coming out of the womb, he came feet first.
fame, e.g. Syuumbwa ulaa cibusya akaambo kabukali. = The lion is famous for its ferocity. Also mpuwo.
a place for hiding, e.g. Moyo wasimpongo wakali kukalyo kakapatamikidwe kucibutilo. = The heart of the herdsboy was with the food which had been stuck in a hidden place.
bare open place, clear place in veld where game sleep at night, e.g. nombe zilalyookezya acibuwa ciindi casikati. = The cattle are resting on a clear patch of ground at noon.
baldness, e.g. Basyaanene balaa cibuwa mumutwe. = My grandfather has a bald head. Also mpanza.
a broad pot for storing and cooking beer, e.g. Cibuya cabukoko capanduka. = The pot for storing beer has broken. Also citalo

the bare floor, e.g. Lyadilwe bamacembele inga balikkede acibuye. = When there is a funeral the old women sit on the floor. Inzoka twaijaila acibuye munanda. = We have killed a snake on the floor in the house. Cibuye tapi. = The floor does not provide. (proverb)

sweet-beer, a drink which is based on crushed maize-grain, a drink which is still unfermented before be- coming beer, pl. zibwantu e.g. Lyankolola _cibwantu_ cilanyugwa kapati. = At an initiation sweet-beer is taken. Tuya kuku- gaya masembe _acibwantu_. = We are go- ing to grind maize for sweet-beer. _Cibwa- ntu_ cakanyina mulolo munji, busiwa mbobwakali bunji. = The sweet-beer had not much watery solution, but the dregs were plentiful. Bantu balasya miyanda akwiibikka muzibwantu. Basya munkoyo, masyabe, mulalansana, ndaziyaumbi ana- kabombwe. = People dig roots and put them into the sweet-beers (cooked crushed maize-grain). They dig munkoyo, masyabe, mulalansana, ndaziyaumbi and nakabombwe. Also cinamalo, mukande

brown, porous rock, e.g. Mabwe _acibwembala_ ajanika munsi ami- lundu = A type of porous rock is found near hills. Mumbali-mbali amulonga Lu- fwuwa kuli _cibwembala_ calo. = Beside the Lufwuwa river there is a porous type of rock.
a ring of fat around the stomach, e.g. Ooyu musimbi wabaa _ci- bwembwe_ akaambo kakulya kabotu. = This girl has a ring of fat around the sto- mach because of eating well.
traditional goat-skin skirt, e.g. Kaindi bamakaintu bakali kusama _zibwie_. = Long ago the women wore skirts of goat-skin. Also cipaya, cikwiye
clay milk vessel, e.g. Mukupa uli _mucibwizilo_ usanganye amabisi. = The milk which is in the clay milk-container should be mixed with sour milk. Also cibizilo.

a place of refuge, e.g. Kuli baacisya _nciciccijilo_ ndalubizya kuli ba- taata. = When I make a mistake with my father there is a safe-haven at my uncle's. Ecino cisi caba _ciccijilo_ cababbi kuzwa kuzisi zyabantu. = This country has be- come a place of refuge for thieves from other countries.

a filter for filtering ash (mu- sika) and water to make soda, e.g. Ino _ciceleko_ camusika cili kuli? = Where is the ash and water filter? _Ciceleko_ cili aciluli cacikuta. = The ash-and-water filter is on the grass roof of the hut. Also cicelesyo

a filter, e.g. _Cicelesyo_ ca mu- sika eci bakacipwaya bana. = The child- ren broke this ash-filter. e.g. Mwana ko- mupa _cicelesyo_ atole kubacembele. = Give the child the filter for her to take to the old woman.
something which causes delay, e.g. Ndalifwambaanide kusika amu- gwagwa pele zimbayambaya caba _cice- lezyo_. = I arrived at the road early but the transport there delayed me.
a freshly made, unburnt, pot, e.g. _Cicelwa_ tacibikkilwi meenda nkaambo inga cayaaya. = An unburnt clay pot can- not hold water as it can disolve. Also ncelwa.
a hag, e.g. Eciya _cicembele_ cilalowa. = That ugly old woman uses witchcraft.
a fishing spear with many barbs, e.g. Wayaswa _cicenya_ mwana- angu. = My child has been wounded by a fishing spear. Also muumba
a cross, e.g. Jesu baamu- gagaila _aciciinkano_ kukalundu. = Jesus was nailed to a cross on a little hill. Also ciingano.
a filter Also cicelesyo.
a verandah pole, e.g. Kamwale kamumuyaamika _acicinda_. = Make the initiate lean on a verandah pole. Also cisanda, cipanda

a wind-shelter, a fence, e.g. Madeede mumbewu bakaayakila _cicinjilizyo_ kukwabilila mpeyo. = They protected the tomatoes in the garden from the cold by building a grass fence. *Bacinjilizya cicinjilizyo kutegwa nombe zitasotoki lukwakwa kuya kucisyu.* = They introduced a fence so that cattle cannot jump over the barrier and go to the vegetable garden. Also cibalu, lukwakwa, cicingilizyo.

a wound/sore, anything painful, mentally as well as physically, e.g. *Ulaa cicisa, ncatakoowunkila kucisobano.* = S/he has a sore, that is why s/he is not going to the concert. *Ndaa cicisa akuulu akandiyasa keembe.* = I have a wound in the leg where the axe cut me.
bump, bruise, e.g. *Bina Mutinta nibakamana kuumwa, Mainza wakabona nkobakajisi cicubbu ankumo.* = When the mother of Mutinta had been beaten, Mainza saw that she had a bump on her forehead.
bruise, e.g. *Ulange ooku wajana bamwi balo azicuzu-cuzu mbuli wakab-beukide.* = Looking there he found some with bruises like someone who had been in an accident.

a rag, a torn cloth, working clothes, e.g. *Caile kuba cidabilo cisani cakwe oyu.* = This one's garment has just become a rag. *Baneene bandituma kubasanzyila cidabilo.* = My grandmother has sent me to wash her working clothes.

a drunkard, e.g. *Mwana waali mubotu caile kuba cidakwa.* = The child who was good has just become a drunkard. *Cimwi cidakwa calumwa mubwa kubukoko.* = One drunkard was bitten by a dog at the beer-party. Also mukolwi.

armlet of wound thin wire, pl. *zitanda*, e.g. *Basimbi bayanda kusama milemba, zidanda atukuze.* = Girls like wearing face-veils, wire-armlets and strings of beads. Also idanda, pl. madanda; ilanda, iseka.
a weakness in the legs, e.g. *Ooyu mwana takeendi kufwam-baana nkaambo kakuti ncide-mpwedempwe.* = This child will not walk early because of a weakness in the legs.
a stamp which shows identity of document, e.g. *Twakabikka acidinto cesu acipepa.* = We put our stamp on the paper.
a boy, e.g. *Cidoombe wali kulwana kale nibali kweembela.* = A boy was already fighting when they were herding. Also mulombe

a trap, (a pot filled with water with a stick across the mouth so that the rat falls into the water), e.g. *Katuteya cidoongwe munanda muli mbeba.* = Let us set a pot-trap in the house where there are rats.
something with which you drill a hole or make an opening, e.g. *Koleta cidonkozyo tudonkole mwiini wajamba.* = Bring a drill so that we can make a hole in the axe-handle.

a package, parcel, bag, e.g. *Munanda kuli cidubulu camapopwe.* = In the house there is a bag of maize. *Konditukka cidubulu amutwe nkaambo cilalema kapati.* = Help me put this bag on my head because it is heavy. Also cibbudu, cifwunte.
a grass enclosure, e.g. *Bataata babamba namakati mucidumba.* = My father is preparing boiled tobacco within a grass enclosure.
a carcass of an animal, e.g. *Cidumbu camunyati cakabola.* = The carcass of the buffalo is rotting. Also mutumba, mutunta.
a type of snake (a horned adder), e.g. *Bavwimi bajaya ciduntila.* = The hunters killed an adder. Also ciduntula, cilundula
a goad, something that urges or forces one to do something, e.g. *Inzala ncidunsyo cakubeleka anguzu.* = Hunger is a goad which makes one work hard.

glory/fame, e.g. Munzi okwa sibbuku Chidyata ulaa cidusya. = The village of the headman Chidyata is famous. (When used as a verb. -dusya, e.g. Kuvwuba cidusya muntu kuti azyibwe kapati. = Wealth causes a man to be famous so that he is widely known.)

a type of snake, the horned adder e.g. Simonga ulatentuuka bacipile, bacisasa, baciduntula, imbooma abalala naembela. = When Simonga is herding he fears vipers, adders, horned adders, pythons and black mambas Also ciduuntula
a viper, e.g. Ciduuntula ulya nkasaalo yakwe. = A viper eats its own sweat. Also ciduntila, ciduntula, ciduntuli
a mixture of noises, like many voices talking together, e.g. Cakali buyo cidyabbu-dyabbu. = There was a confusion of noises.
a bruise, a contusion, (an internal injury leaving skin unbroken), e.g. Aandipwaya bbwe kwaba cifwamu. = There is a bruise where the stone hit me. Also cicubbu.
picture, sketch, e.g. Nceeci cifwanikiso carnanda njeyanda kuyakilwa. = This is a picture of the house I want built.
a roof resting on ground, e.g. Amucibikke ananda cifwapi eco. = Put that roof resting on the ground on to the house. Also cibumbu.
a chip of wood, a piece of plank, e.g. Eeci cifwapu ncakubamba cijatilo cacipeni. = This piece of wood is for making the handle of a knife.
a chip of wood, pl. zifwapula, e.g. Kosikka zifwapula eezi mucikko. = Stoke the fire with these chips of wood.
chicken-pox, e.g. Mwana ooyu wafwumuka cifwayuka mubili woonse. = This child has an eruption of chicken-pox over the whole body. Also cifwayu, cifwumu.
a shotgun, a shot, e.g. Basankwa basobanya cifweefwe. = The boys are playing with the shot-gun. Also cifwefwe.

a grave, e.g. Basya kale cifwene mobatiizikkilwe baneene. = They have already dug a grave where they are going to bury my grandmother. Cifwene cakuzikkila mwana camuka kumana kusyigwa akaambo kakuyuma kwanyika. = The grave for the child has been delayed in being dug because of the hardness of the ground. Also cuumbwe, kabanda.
rubbish, e.g. Kamucuumpa cifwenteele eci. = Burn this rubbish. Also caala.

a carnivorous wild-cat, e.g. Kwainda cifwi awa, naa kkiti wamusyokwe. = A wild-cat passed here or a bush-cat. Cifwi wazimana nkwilimba zyokwesu. = The wild-cat has finished off all our pidgeons. Also nole.

stomach, e.g. Eeyi nombe ilaa cifwu cipati. = This cow has a huge stomach. Ucisanzye kabotu cifwu campongo kotanacijika, nkaambo cilaa tombe linji. = Wash the stomach of the goat well before you cook it, because it is full of dirt.
the slough of a snake, e.g. Oomu mubwina mulibonya cifwubula. = In this hole the cast-off skin of a snake is visible. Also cikwa canzoka (vb.-fwu-buluka, kulikwama)
heap of ears of corn, e.g. Kamubikka cifwufwu camaila munsi abutala. = Put the heap of millet beside the granary.
something for kneeling on, e.g Twakabwezelela mapepe manji akubamba cifwukamino mpotupailila. = We collected many feathers and made a cushion on which we prayed.
the nest (of a hen or other bird or fowl) on the ground, e.g. Mutinta mbokwakanyina cisyu, wakabweza mayi obile mucifwuko. = Since Mutinta had no relish, took two eggs from the nest.
cadilim= The nest of the hen has fallen down.

a clay pipe, e.g. Imfwuko ifwebela bakaapa ncifwuko*fwuko* buyo. = The pipe my grandmother smokes is just a clay one. *Cifwukofwuko cifwebela mucembele capya mulilo.* = The pipe which the old woman smokes has been burnt by the fire.
a platform for drying food, e.g. Amufwambaane kubamba cifwuli tuyanike mabele. Quickly make a platform so that we dry the millet. Also cifwuuli
loss of appetite due to exhaustion, e.g. *Ndaba acifwulifwuli akaambo kakukatala.* = I have lost appetite because of exhaustion.
anvil, e.g. Koleta cifwulilo tusensemune keembe. = Bring an axeanvil so that we sharpen the axe.
blade of knife, e.g. Mundibikkile mukobezyo acifwulo eci. = Put a handle on this blade for me.

a dry lump of clean dung, pl. zifwumba, e.g. Koleta cifwumba ucuumpe kutegwa mansenya azwe.= Bring dung and burn it so that the moquitoes go away. Beembezi bali kuumana zifwumba kuciba. The herders were beating each other with lumps of dung in the kraal.
second stomach of ruminant, e.g. Bamadaala batakwe menyo balayandisya kulya cifwumbilizya. = Old men without teeth like to eat the second stomach of cattle. Also lujalila

dung beetle, e.g. *Cifwumbula cibamba zikoto mumafwumba.* = The dung-beetle is making balls of cattledung. *Cifwumbula cali kubumba maziu aarjombe.* = A dung-beetle was moulding the cattle-dung. Also haafwumbula.
tomorrow, e.g. *Cifwumo tuyakukuzela kudamu lya Maseke.* = Tomorrow we are going to net fish at Maseke dam.
the early morning, e.g. *Cifwumofwumo twafwumide kukwiida cisyu kumbewu.* = We had gone, early in the morning, to water the vegetables in the garden.
protuberance from ground like a root, e.g. *Ndalinontola acifwumpu cili munzila.* = I have hit myself against a stump which was on the path. Also mfwumpu.

chicken-pox, measles, e.g. Bana baleetezya kuti baciswa cifwumu. = Children are pitiable if they suffer from measles. Kwakasika bulwazi bwacifwumu, aboobo bana banji mucibbadela mbabaciswa. There was an out-break of measles, and so many children are sick in hospital.

a bird's crop, i.e. the pouch in a bird's gullet where food is stored or prepared for digestion, e.g. Mubwa walya cifwunci cankuku. = The dog ate the crop of the chicken. *Cifwunci cankuku atuyuni inga cizwide cakulya.* The chicken's crop is usually full of food. Also cifwuunci.
a traditional custom, pl. zifwunda, e.g. *Cifwunda cakusalazya mukamufwu tacili cibotu.* = The custom of purifying the husband or wife of the deceased is not good. Also ciyanza.

a type of disease, e.g. Musilisi wakasilika mukaintu musamu wazifwunda, ziposo, zyeelo azipuku, azilengwa zimwi. = The witchdoctor cures a woman with traditional medicines for diseases like zifwunda, ziposo, spirit possession, bad spirits, and through other practices.
a line, e.g. Nobakasika kumbali amunzi bakeenga cifwunda nkobaya alimwi ankobazwa. When they reached near
the preliminary fee paid to witchdoctor on arrival for assistance, e.g. Munanga wakapegwa *cifwu-*

kutiasye. = The witch-doctor was given a preliminary fee as soon as we arrived so that he would help us. Bataata, kamutoleela aci*fwundananga*, ndiza munanga oyu ulabbadelwa kusonda. = Father, take along the opening payment, perhaps that witchdoctor is paid for divining.
tradition, e.g. *Cifwundo cakubangwa cakali cibi. = The tradition of knocking out the teeth was bad. Also cilengwa

a woman's skirt or dress, e.g. Janza lyamulombwana lyakatintimene buya *mucifwunga*. = The hand of the man was half-way around (the waist of) the woman's dress. Bantu bakali kuti ngusyaazyana usama *cifwunga* cabakaakwe masiku. = The people said he was a night-dancer who wore the skirt of his wife at night. Muka Chimbwali mbwaakasikila nkuluma mulumi wakwe meno kukuboko kumwi katukila akusamununa *cifwunga* akati kabantu. = The wife of Chimbwali as soon as she arrived she bit her husband with her teeth on the arm and while cursing took off her dress before the people.
a bale, package, parcel, e.g. Ndali kubbadelela *cifwunte* mu cimbaya-ambaya. = I was paying for the parcel in the vehicle. Also -cidubulu

a grass-container in which meat or groundnuts are tied up and preserved, e.g. Bavwimi baletelezya *acifwunte*. = The hunters brought along a grasscontainer for the meat. Mudaala naazyila kukuvwima, *cifwunte* canyama wacibikkide agwezyo. = When the old man came back from hunting he had put a grass-container of meat on his shoulders.

a still-born child, e.g. Musimbi ulya wakazyala *cifwunti*. = That girl gave birth to a still-born child. Mukaintu wangu wakatumbuka *cifwunti*. = My wife delivered a still-born child. Also kasowe, cifwuntu, katombe.

a trap, e.g. Mbeba zilya mapopwe twakazibikkila *cifwupu*. = We have put out a trap for the rats which are eating the maize. Nditeya tuyuni *acifwupu*. = I am trapping little birds with a trap. (A branch to which is attached a long string leading to where the hunter is hiding. When the birds come to eat the food placed beside the branch, the hunter suddenly pulls it, killing the birds.) Also civwupu
the contents of the bowel and stomach, e.g. Musune wazimbilwa mapopwe waluka *cifwusi*. = The ox which was constipated with the maize has vomited out its stomach contents.
what is dull, e.g. Ooyu mwana tali musongo, ncifwuswamakowa. = This child is dull, he shold be thrown away as a bitter cucumber.
a foot, e.g. Bumvwa bwakamuyasa *acifwuta*. = A thorn pierced him on the foot. Also cituta.
fat, e.g. Nsumba yarņombe ilaa *cifwuta* cinji. = The cow's hoof has plenty of fat. Also citoma.

a heap of ears of sorgum, e.g. Basicikolo basusa maila kuzwa aci*fwuufwu*. = The pupils are collecting millet from the heap of sorgum ears. Mubbi watija *acifwuufwu* camaila. = The thief has run away with a heap of sorgum.
a species of short-legged chicken, e.g. *Cifwuuli* wangu wakatula mayi manji. = My short-legged chicken has laid many eggs.
a platform for drying millet, e.g. Koya ukayanike maila acifwuuli. = Go and put the millet out to dry on the platform.
a bird's crop (the pouchlike enlargement of the gullet in birds), e.g. Nkuku zimwi cifwuunci inga ncipati. = The crop is large on some chickens. Also cifwunci.
a bone, e.g. Nyama yacifwuwa ilanona. = Meat on the bone is tasty.

a knot, pl. ziga, e.g. Wamana kutunga bunweba munyeleti, waange ciga kumamanino. = When you have finished threading the needle, tie a knot at the end. Azwa buyo macembele, sikutumbusya ulabweza buzingo (ntali) akwaanga lukombo-kombo muziga zyotatwe. When the afterbirth comes out, the midwife takes a tendon and ties the umbilical cord with three knots. =

stage, section, place where one stops when reading, as after a sentence or a phrase or a clause, e.g. Ciga aciga mucaano cilembedwe inga kuli ncocipandulula. Each paragraph of a story has something to say.

a tin, a can, e.g. Cigabba camusamu mucibikke kutasiki bana. = You should place the tin of medicine out of reach of the children. Amulete ciqabba tusibikile meenda akusamba kumeso. = Bring a tin so that we put water on the fire for washing our faces.
a watch/clock, time, e.g. Cigadi cangu caleka kubeleka nkaambo canjilwa meenda amvwula. My watch has stopped working because rain water got in. Ncigadi nzi? = what time is it? Also cikati

a species of sorgum, e.g. Ku Buwe basyanga kapati cigaligali. = The people of the Gwembe Valley mostly grow a special variety of sorgum. Maila acigaligali taaligwi buyuni. = The cigaligali type of sorgum is not eaten by the birds. Also cikalekale, cigalegale.
a patch, e.g. Ndalomba mundibikkile cigamba abuluke. = Please put a patch on my trousers for me. Oobu buluke buyandika kubikkwa cigamba agondo. This trousers needs to have a patch put on the knee.
a watch, the time, e.g. Casika cigati, atweende tukalyookezye. = The time has arrived, let us go and rest. Also cigadi.

a digging-spike at the foot of a spear-shaft, e.g. Muyaki usidila mpanda zyangazi acigawa. The builder dug narrow holes for the forks to uphold the platform with the spike of a spear. Also cigoyo, cisisyo.
a mill, e.g. Basimbi baya kucigayo cifwumo. = The girls are going to the mill tomorrow. Basimbi bagaya busu acigayo camaanza. The girls are grinding flour with a hand-grinder.
a slasher, e.g. Chimbwali ncigebba, cilatumana mumukowa. = Chimbwali is a slasher who wipes out the clan.

a trouble-maker, brigand, e.g. Ooyu mwana ciyakuba cigebenge akukomena. This child is going to be a trouble-maker when s/he grows up. Kunkolola masiku kwali cigebenge cali kutukila bantu. At the initiation last night there was a trouble-maker who was insulting people. Mucisi ca Singani mumunzi mwa Hankandu, bakabona cigebenge cijisi nombe zyakubba ciindi cakubucedo kakucisiyasiya. In the chieftaincy of Singani, in the village of Hankandu, they saw in the early morning when it was still dark, a criminal with stolen cattle. Also cigwebenga.
a spring-trap, e.g. Tuteya nsya acigece. We are trapping duikers with a spring-trap. =
a hanging, e.g. Mujayi uyakukujaigwa *aciqece.* = The muderer will be killed by hanging. Also cisilazya, cigeje.
a scissors, e.g. Amundipe *cigele* njanda kugela bana masusu. = Give me the scissors I want to cut the children's hair.

a drum ensemble who play the drums with sticks when soldiers are marching, e.g. Bamasole nobafwoolwa balizya *cigibbu* kutegwa kabeenda kabotu. = The drum is sounding when the soldiers are marching so that they march in step. Also cigubbu.

a heap of things mixed up together, e.g. Musyokwe zisamu inga *nciqobegobe* kuvwula kwalo. = In the bush the trees are hooked together in their abundance. Koya ukayandaule muu- ngo *acigobegobe* munanda. = Go and look for the wooden spoon amidst the heap of things in the house. Also cidyobe-dyobe, (mudobe-dobe, a crowd of mixed people).
the midday meal, e.g. Ulaa- fwaafwi kulya *cigoboko* mbulyasika waa- lya zuba. = You are about to eat the midday meal as the sun has reached that point. Also cikoboko.

a temporary flat roof made of poles and grass, e.g. nanda ya- badaala mwiivwumbe buyo *cigobwedwa* kutegwa tukagonke masomo aciluli. = You should put up a temporary flat roof on the old man's house so that we can cut roofing poles. Also civwuli

a patchwork, e.g. Babelesi balagonka akubungika minsale yasima, inga ulajana muunda oonse *ncigogoogo* buya. = The workers cut and gather the ripe sugar-cane, you find the whole field is just a patchwork.
a white lily, pl. magolo- koko, a creeping-plant, e.g. *Cigolokoko* cili mulukwakwa Iwambewu cakayuma. = The creeping-plant on the fence in my garden has dried up. Also cikolokoko.
sex, e.g. Bausyi bakajanwa ba- cita *cigololo* amubelesi wakumpulasi mu- cimpati campongo. The father was found having sex with a farm-worker in the krall of the goats. Also nkwela.
a depression, e.g. Nci- nga yangu yatyoka niyanjila mucigolo- longwa. My bicycle was damaged when it went into a depression.
a patch, e.g. Eeci *cigombo* ncakubikka kumatako acibbudula ca- mwana. = This patch is for putting on the backside of the child's shorts. Also cigamba.

a roof built on poles without walls, e.g. Banyina musimbi bakali kuziya aziyo *mucigombwa.* The mother of the girl was grinding mealie-meal in an open shelter. Imwi nyama yakayanikwa aku- siswa *mucigombwa* kutegwa suntwe ataiboni. Some meat was hung up and hidden in a walless shelter so that the hyena could not see it. Nzweluuke waka- jisi nanda mpati *acigombwa* cipati. = Nzweluuke had a large house and a big wall-less roofed structure. *Mucigombwa* mwakali zibumbwa nzyaakali kulondweda zipopwe anzembwe. = There were bottle grain-containers in the wall-less house where he was storing the millet and the maize. Also cigongola

a type of possession dance, e.g. Basankwa a basimbi balayanda kuya kukuzyana *cigome* muntu naanjilwa masabe. Boys and girls like to go to dance the *cigome* when a person is poss- essed by masabe spirits.
a bucket, a drum or container of liquids, e.g. Kamutola *cigomo* kucikala bakamutilile meenda. Take a bucket to the well so that they pour water in it for you. Also cingomo
a lump of clay, a clod, e.g. Baama bakamuwaala *cigomwe* cabulongo mwana. = Mother threw the lump of clay at the child.
a kind of hair style, e.g. *Masusu aya ngoobamba cigonyenwa akweelela kapati.* = This hair which you have made into new style suits you.

a bee-skep (straw or wicker bee-hive), e.g. *Bataata bakabikka cigoogo mumusamu kumbo amunzi kuteya nzuki.* = Father has put a bee-skep in a tree to the west of the village to catch bees. Also cikooko.
a type of fish, pl. *bacikoto*, e.g. *Inkwazi tiibalumi bacigoto.* = Fish eagles do not eat *cigoto* fish.
lumps, pl. *zigoto/makoto*, e.g. *Bamwi basimbi tabacizyi kujika nsima. Ziindi zinji bajika yazigoto.* = Some girls do not know how to cook nsima. Very often they cook lumpy food. Also cikoto
a type of drum, e.g. *Basikalumamba balikulizya cigubbu nibali kufwoolwa.* = The soldiers were beating a drum when they were marching. Also *cigibbu*.
hand pump, e.g. *Mumunzi mwa Sinandu nkocili ciguju cameenda.* = In the village of Sinandu there is a hand-pump for water.
a gecko or lizard, e.g. *Candiyoosya cigulugulu calede munsi anzila.* = The gecko frightened me which was lying near the path. Also *syaazikulukulu, syazibumbu*.
the thumb, e.g. *Ndayaswa bumvwa acigumo nindali kutyola nkuni.* = I was pierced by a thorn on the thumb when I was breaking firewood. Also *calananda*.

a cow without horns, e.g. *nombe yokwesu njiinga cigumpu taiko muluba.* = Our cow, the hornless one, is not in the kraal. *Mukwaale, akaambo kakuti ncigumpu, takatazigwi kunjila mulukwakwa Iwamambewu.* = *Mukwaale*, because it is hornless cow, finds no problem in going through the fence of the gardens. Also *imvwuma*.
what causes death of flock, e.g. *Nkuku zyangu zyanjilwa cigumuna cakwiile kufwa.* = My chickens have absorbed some deadly substance which just makes them die.
retrenchment, e.g. *Nsezyi naa cakandiimpa buti cigumuna cakuleka kubeleka.* = I don't know how the retrenchment passed me.
a step at the door, e.g. *Muyake cigunguzyo amulyango kutegwa katunjila kabotu murnanda.* = Build a door-step so that we can enter the house easily. Also *cikunguzyo*.

any instrument used to clear a field, pl. *zigunkuzyo*, e.g. *Ndalomba mukandibambile zigunkuzyo zyakugunkauzya muunda omunene.* = Old man I am asking you to make me a tool for clearing the field. *Basankwa babweze zigunkuzyo tukagunkaule mumuunda.* = Let the boys take tools so that we clear the field. Also *cigunkauzyo*.

an obstacle deliberately placed in the way, humps, e.g. *Amugwagwa akosola bana basicikolo bakabikka zigunkuzyo kutegwa zimbayambaya kaziteendesyi.* = On the road where the children cross they placed obstacles so that the heavy traffic would not be speeding.
a fish which gives an electric shock, e.g. *Bazezi baca cigunya mulusabwi.* = The fishers caught an electric eel in the net.

disgraceful behaviour, e.g. *Cilapa bweemya kuli bamukowaako kucita cintu cigunya.* = It brings disgrace to your relatives when you do something shameful. *Ooyu mwana waamba cintu cigunya akati kabantu mumuswaangano.* = This child said something shocking among the people at the meeting.

a goods train, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Cainda **cigusu** kacijisi malasya kuya kumigodi. = A goods train passed carrying coal to the mines. Tuya kukutansika nombe *mucigusu* ciya kunyika kutegwa tukasambale kumigodi. = We are going to get the cattle to mount the goods train going to the north so that we can sell them at the mines. Kufweba kwakali kukasigwa pesi walo ulajana busi buzwa ku-mulomo wakwe akumpemo yakwe mbuli **cigusu** ceenda. = Smoking was forbidden but as for him you would find smoke coming out of his mouth and from his nose like a goods train.

the sound of a shot or a gong, e.g. Ndiza kuli mubbi wajaigwa nkaambo twafwuma kumvwa **cigutulo** cantobolo. = Perhaps a thief has been killed because we heard early in the day a shot from a gun. e.g. **Cigutulo** cakuti basicikolo bazwe calila kale. = The gong has already sounded for the pupils to come out. Also mugutulo
early shoot of edible mushroom, e.g. Amundiyokele **ciguugu** cabowa comwe. = Roast a young mushroom for me. Also cikuku.
handle of spoon or knife, e.g. Nguni wakatyola **ciguwa** cacipeni cangu? = Who broke the handle of my knife. Also mwiini, ciini.
a head skin-disease, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa **ciguyula** mumutwe. = This child has a skin disease of the head. Also cigwenyembe.
a crow, e.g. *Cigwaa-ngala* wakabweza mayi obilo mucifwuko. = A crow took two eggs from the nest. Also cikwaangala
an empty head of sorgum, pl. *zigwaa-ngala*, e.g. Bayuni baalya maila oonse kwacaala *zigwaangala* zyalo. = The birds have earten all the sorgum there only remains the empty heads.

a lizard (said to bite), e.g. Bana balaciyoowa *cigwaba*. = Children are frightened of a lizard. Kutuba kumeso wiile kubee *ncigwaba*. = The face is as white (with dust) as if you were a lizard. Also cikwaba.
a heated discussion, e.g. Alya anze cakaba *cigwagwaagwa*. = There outside began a heated discussion.
a knob-billed duck, e.g. Ndajaya *cigwalugwalu* musyokwe. = I killed a knob-billed duck in the bush. Also cikoyokoyo, cisunkankumo.

a criminal, pl. *zigwebe-nga*, e.g. Bana bamwi sunu zyakaba *zi-qwebenga*. = Some children to-day have become criminals. *Cigwebenga* catiibbide mudaala mucitima bacuuma. = They beat the criminal who was about to steal from the old man on the train.
a scab on sheep or calves, e.g. Boombe babaa *cigwegwe*. = The calves have a scab disease. Also cinkwankwa
mange or scab, e.g. Bana babaa *ciqwenyembe* mumutwe. = The children have a scab on the head.

a swarm of locusts, e.g. Uuno mwaka kulalangilwa kuba *cigwigwi*. = This year there is likely to be a swarm of locusts. *Cigwiqwi* cakainda mwakali cakamana mapopwe mumyuunda. = The swarm of locusts which passed last year destroyed the maize in the fields. Also cikwikwi.

the green pidgeon, e.g. Nindafwusa bbwe mumusamu *ciqwilinti* cauluka cakutalikwaya. = When I threw a stone into the tree, a green pidgeon flew off agitated. Nindakali kuteya nziba kumuunda ndakaca *cigwilinti*. = When I was trapping doves in the field I caught a green pidgeon. Also cikwilinti, inkwilinti, cimwanga.

a type of tree which bears green fruits, e.g. Bamakaintu balayandisya kulya ceele cabikkwa bana bacigwilinti. = Women like a lot to eat porridge on which has been put the fruit of the cigwilinti tree. (the fruit is crushed into powder and dried)
a dangerous fish, e.g. Cigwinta mmuswi uli buyani? = What kind of fish is a cigwinta? Also cigwinya.

a large dangerous electric fish, e.g. Mukati kakanseenga mwakali muswi ugambya utegwa cigwinya. Kanseenga koonse kakazula bukali bwacigwinya. Cigwinya wakatyoloola tuumba toonse, wakabagwinya. Taata wakati cigwinya tatyankwi, tagumwi akasamu pe, ulagwinya! ulagwinta! = In the middle of the trap there was a big extraordinary fish called cigwinya. The whole trap was full of the anger of the cigwinya fish. The cigwinya broke all the fishing spears and became a danger to them. My father said the cigwinya fish cannot be pressed, it cannot be touched with a stick, it becomes ferocious and gives an electric shock.
a washing pot, e.g. Kotila meenda mucihali ulete kuno. = Pour water in the washing pot and bring it here.
a heated discussion, e.g. Alya anze cakaba cihihiihi. There outside there was a heated discussion. Also cigwagwaagwa.
a head-pad made from sticks, e.g. Ambeyo amundibambile ciholi. = Make me a head-pad as well.

hair gathered into long cone (Ila), pl. ziholyo, e.g. Bavwimi bakali kusama ziholyo kutegwa kabalibonya musyokwe damfwu. = Hunters were wearing the long hair cone so as to be seen in tall bush. Also kagolyo.
a watering can, e.g. Kamuya mulete ciidizyo oku mwiide. Go and fetch the watering-can over there and water. Kondipa ciidizyo nkaide cisyu mumbewu. Give me the watering can so that I water the garden.
a ring of colour, e.g. Cikwaangala ulaa ciigu munsingo. = A crow has a ring of colour on the neck. Also ciingu, cizingu.
a coloured line, e.g. Babelesi beenga ciigu akati-kati kamugwagwa. The workers are drawing a coloured line in the middle of the road. =

a dog's collar, e.g. Mubwa wangu ulaa ciika cituba munsingo. My dog has a white collar around its neck. Also ciingu, cibika. ciilikilo a base, e.g. Ciilikilo cananda yangu tacili ciyumu pe. The foundation of my house is not strong.

a cock's spur (hard projection on cock's leg), e.g. Ciimbi camukombwe ucili mwana ncifwiifwi. The spur of the cock which is still young is short. Nindali kuvwuna bakombwe bali kulwana, umwi wandiyasa ciimbi amunwe. = When I was trying to separate the cocks who were fighting, one pierced me in the finger with its spur.
a song/tune, e.g. Ciimbo cakaanza Ncimunya cimvwika kabotu. = The song which Nchimunya composed sounds good. Ciimbo eco ncomwiimba ncamvwula. That song you are singing is a rain-song.

habit, behaviour, e.g. Cheendega taakaleka kubba nkaambo cakali ciimbo ncaakakomena aco. Cheendega did not stop stealing because it was the habit which he had grown up with. Ciimbo cako ncocita muntolongo tacikonzyi kukujanya Iwaanguluko. Your behaviour in prison will not give you freedom. Ijilo wakacita ciimbo cibi kapati, kulazika lubono anze. = You acted in a very bad way yesterday in leaving valuable things outside.

We are the Bakonka clan. Ba- cijayakasya medical root for hastening zovwu mbanyama bakkala muziinga zipa- menstrual courses. = Ooyu musimbi muti. = Elephants are animals who live in kamupe cijayakasya. Give this girl the medicine for hastening menstruation.

a door, e.g. *Cijazyo* cananda yangu cilalijala cilikke. = The door of my house closes itself. Mpongo zyacijula ci*jazyo* cananda akulya busu. = The goats broke the door of the house and ate the mealie-meal. Also citendele.
a weapon, e.g. Ndipe *cijazyo* eco ndijaye nzoka. Give me that weapon so that I kill the snake.
cooked sweet potatoes, e.g. Baama bamupa *cijege* mweenzu. = Mother gave the visitor sweet potatoes. Also zimbwali.
cooked cassava, e.g. Bama Lozi balayandisya kulya *ciiege*. The Lozi people like very much to eat cooked cassava.

a cooking pot or utensil, e.g. *Mucijikilo* omu kuli makololo. = There are burn fragments of food in this cooking pot. Kondisanzyila *cijikilo* kutegwa ndikange nswi. = Clean the pot for me so that I fry the fish. Also citentu

a style of cooking, e.g. *Cijiko* eci tacili kabotu kuti kakuli beenzu. = This manner of cooking is not good, if there are visitors. *Cijiko* cabacembele ncabulondo. = The way of cooking of the old woman is careful and neat.

something to be cooked, pl. majiko; *cijiko cadilwe* = anything cooked at a funeral, e.g. Kudilwe lyamuvwubi kwakali *majiko* manji. = At the funeral of the rich man there were many things to be cooked.
kitchen, e.g. Kamunjila mucijikilo. = enter the kitchen.

an infectious disease, (similar to cipele) e.g. Taakali kunjila muminzi mwakali manunununu antomba, *cijoolo* amaIwazi ayambukila amwi. She would never enter a village where there were rumours of smallpox, *cijoolo* or other infectious diseases.
bags, pl. zijumba-jumba, e.g. Bakabona *zijumba-jumba* zyabusu zyakali ambali akamando. = They saw the bags of flour beside the beer.

anything used for opening something like a tin, door or cupboard, e.g. Kamundipa *cijuzyo* ndijule kagabba aka. Give me the opener so that I open this tin. Kobapa *cijuzyo* bauso bajule mubutala. Give the tool for opening the bin to your father so that he opens it.
anything used for taking pot off fire, e.g. Kobelesya *cijuzyo* kujula mpoto kutegwa utapyi. = Use an instrument for taking off the pot so that you are not burnt.
a type of womens dance, e.g. Basimbi bakali kuzyana ci*kaambekaambe* kunkolola. = The girls were dancing the cikambekambe at the initiation.

string of beads around loins (part of body on both sides of spine between false ribs and hip bones), e.g. Bamakaintu bamwi basama *cikaba*. = Some women were wearing waist-beads. Also mitenta, ciyabala.
a flat piece of animal fat, e.g. Amundigwasye *cikaba* camafwuta nkabikke mucisyu. = Help me with a piece of fat so that I go and put it in the vegetable relish.
a beaded shoulder-belt worn by girls.

food, e.g. Mudaala wakazyiba kuti *ncikafwu*. = The old man knew that it was food. Bulongo bwa Zambia bukwete *cikafwu* alubono loonse luli muno munyika. The soil of Zambia contains the food and all the wealth which is in this land.
woman (derogatory), e.g. Makaba wakakwata *cikaintu* citacizyi kujika. Makaba married a useless woman who did not know how to cook.

a hard-working woman, e.g. *Cikaintu* eci nciyumu kubeleka. This woman is cikaka the stomach, pl. zikaka, e.g. *Cikaka camwana cilazimba.* The stomach of the child is swollen. *Mumadilwe balayanda kulya zikaka zyaņombe.* = At funerals they like eating the stomachs of cows. Also *cifwu.*

a claw hammer, e.g. Koleta cikakamizyo tugagaile mpikili amulembo waampulungwido. Bring a hammer so that we hammer a nail for the window curtain. Also *cigagamizyo, cigagaizyo, cikankamizyo; cikakamizyo cacisamu* = a mallet (a wooden hammer)

a shallow well, water-hole, e.g. *Meenda tuteka mucikala kumbewu.* = We draw water from the garden well. *Meenda ali mucikala akondoolwa ngulube.* = The water in the shallow well has been stirred up by pigs.
stiff dry inedible porridge, e.g. *Kobapa cikalananda babwa.* = Give the dogs the hardened porridge. *Insima yayuma cikalananda.* = The nsima is too dry. Also *cigalananga, cigalanganga.*

a type of plant (Boerhavia diffusa), bark of root used for scorpion bite not very effective e.g. *Cikalamatongo mmusamu wantuntumaanzi.* = *Cikalamatongo* is a medicine used for malaria. Also *cikkalamatongo*
hardened porridge, e.g. *Koya ukasowe cikalato kudindi.* = Go and throw the hardened porridge into the pit. Also *cikalananda.*
a particular variety of sorgum resistant to birds, e.g. *Uuno mwaka twakasyanga cikalekale.* = This year we planted a particular type of sorgum. Also *cigaligali.*
balance, scales, e.g. *Tupime mwana acikali.* Let us weigh the child on the scales. Also *cikkelo, cipimyo.*
a bunch, e.g. *Ootu tuyuni tuyandika kujaya mucikama ciindi comwe, nocinga cavwula cilisyo.* These little birds need to be killed in a group at the same time so that there would be enough relish.
a patch, e.g. *Yayaswa ncinga, mbikke cikamba.* The bike is punctured, let me put on a patch. Also *cigamba*
a type of dance, e.g. *Kumucado waba Mweene bamacembele bakali kuzyana cikambilano.* = At Mr.
wedding the old women were dancing the *cikambilano.*
a manner of clapping hands, e.g. *Cikambililo camvwula ncakuvwobela buya.* = The manner of clapping the hands when at the rain-shrine is done with cupped hands (to show respect)
a present given to placate or thank a chief, e.g. *Bantu bamwi bakali kutola cikambilizyo kumwami wabo.* = Some people were taking a present to thank their chief.
a type of dance where one sings and dances and the encircling group respond. e.g. *Mweemba nguwakasaanguna kuzyana cikambilo.* = Mweemba was the first to dance the *cikambilo.*

a type of bird, the blue jay or purple roller, e.g. *Tumba waalya mayi acikambwe.* = An owl has eaten the eggs of a blue jay. *Muyuni cikambwe ulauluka cabulengalenga.* The blue-jay flies in a lazy fashion.

a container used for milking, e.g. *Zyasika nombe, amulete cikamino tukame.* The cattle have arrived, bring the milk-container so that we milk. *Mutinta, kosanzya cikamino.* = Mutinta, wash the milk container. Also *mulewu*
a medicinal root for bathing wounds, e.g. *Eeci cicisa ukacisanzye acikambi.* Bathe this wound using the *cikambi* medicinal root. Also *cikampi*
a medicinal root for bathing wounds, a pad of hay or straw applied to wound/poultice, e.g. *Cicisa eco kocisanzya acikanci.* = Wash that wound with the *cikanci* root.
food spat out after chewing, e.g. *Ndaciswida cikanci nindamana kulya munsale.* = When I had finished eating the sugarcane I spat out the remains.
bee bread, (honey or pollen used as food for bees), pl. *makanci,* e.g. *Kosowa makanci abuci.* = Throw away the beebread.
the skin, e.g. *Cikanda cakwe ncibotu nkaambo nciteteete.* = Her skin is beautiful because it is soft.
sheath for knife, e.g. *Kobikka cipanga mucikanda calyo.* = Put the sword into its scabbard.
a farmer, e.g. *Muzeezo wakuya kumunzi kuya kuba cikanda-bulongo, ngwacanakazi.* = The plan of going home to be a farmer is for a woman.
one who works in mud, i.e. difficult circumstances, e.g. *Cikanda-kanda wakaatola.* = The one who is willing to work in the mud reaps the benefit.
present expected for good work, e.g. *Basankwa babinga nombe bapegwa cikandamaulu.* = Boys who drive cattle are given a present.

porridge with sour milk, e.g. *Nobakamana kukanda cikandi, bakamubikkila cimwi wisi mucinyanda akumupa ncico awo mpaakakkede.* = When they had finished preparing the porridge, they served some for the father where he was seated.

a dispute/talk, pl. *makani, nkani* (Kalomo area), e.g. *Twakaunkide kucikani kumwami.* = We went with a dispute to the chief. *Cikani cikananwa abetekwa bulale ncibi.* A dispute which is being discussed concerning a case of adultery is not good.

a group of people, pl. *zikanka,* e.g. *Kunkolola inyama ilapegwa muzikanka, acimwi cikanka cilapegwa nyama yeelede.* At the initiation ceremony the meat is distributed according to groups, each group receiving a suitable amount.
a joint of meat with bone, e.g. *Mudaala wakapegwa cikantizi kudilwe.* The old man was given a piece of meat on the bone at the funeral. Also *cikankatizi, cituli*
a beaded shoulder belt worn by girls, e.g. *Musimbi wangu wakalivwabika cikapi cabulungu agwezyo.* My girlfriend was wearing a beaded shoulder-belt.

about 8.00 hrs., e.g. *Casika ciindi cacikasaalizi, tuzwisye nombe.* = When it is about 8.00 hrs., let us take out the cattle. *Izuba lyasika acikasaalizi, mumuzwisye anze mulwazi.* = When the sun has risen at about 8.00 hrs. you should take the patient outside.

time when cattle go out to graze (about 9.00 hrs) e.g. *Kuti kubule ukama kusikila zuba lisike acikasaazi, muzizwisye nombe.* If there is no one to milk by 9.00 hrs, take the cattle out. Also *cisaasa.*

bundle of dried meat or fibre, e.g. *cikata camitendu* = a bundle of dried strips of meat, e.g. *Kamuya mukalete cikata caloozi tuvwumbe nanda.* = Go and bring a bundle of fibres so that we thatch the house. *Wakapiluka acikata camiyanda.* He returned with a pile of roots.

a coil, pl. *zikata, cikata calutende* = a coil of runners, *cikata canzoka* = a coiled snake. e.g. *Inzoka yakalivwungaide atala amai pele buyo mutwe nguwakanongomene atala acikata cayo.* The snake was curled up over its eggs but it was only the head which was raised up over its coil.

a broken shell or potsherd, pl. zikaye, e.g. Kamubikka mulilo mucikaye tuumpe musamu. = Put fire in a potsherd SO that we burn medicine in it. Mumubikkile mulilo mucikaye mulwazi. = Put fire in a potsherd for the sick. Kaindi nyama bakali kupedwa muzikaye nkaambo kwakanyina mitiba. = Long ago they were given meat in pieces of shells because there were no plates.

a piece of wood or metal used for the base for making fire by friction, e.g. Koleta kapisyo a cikazi, tupike mulilo. = Bring a friction stick and the wooden base so that we produce fire. Wakagonkolola cisamu ciyumu camusekese kucita cikazi amane ngooyu nkucigwamagwama ku-panga kalindi kampikilo. = He cut a dry stick from the musekese tree to make a base for the fire, there he is removing the outer part to make a hole for the fire. Also lupika
a butchery, e.g. Kuli nyama mbotu kucikelekele. = There is good meat at the butchery.
a boat made of planks, e.g. Tubelesya cikepe notuloba. = We use a boat made of planks when we fish. Also cikwepe

a clay stool, e.g. Cikkalabalemu ncuuno cabulongo cibumbwa ku-mbali acikko munanda. A cikkalabalemu is a clay stool, which is moulded near the fireplace in the house. Mucembele wakamutola musimbi murganda akumukkazika acikkalabalemu. = The old woman took the girl inside the house and made her sit on a fireside clay stool.
a container, pl. zikkali, e.g. Bakali kwiile kusiya makoko aabo muzikkali akutija. They were just leaving their beers in containers and running away.
a place for sitting down a chair, e.g. Murnanda yamilawo cikkalilo cimwi cakazauka. In the court-house one of the seats was torn. Amubape cikkalilo beenzu. Give a seat to the visitors.
sitting and waiting for a long time, e.g. Ndafwa cikkalizi. = I am fed up sitting and waiting here. Also cilindizi, cikkalilizi, cizungu.
position, e.g. Utakkali acikkalo cangu pe. = Do not sit in my place.

a yoke pin, pl. zikkeyi, e.g. Bakaiya mazina azintu zyakali kubelesegwa ciindi cakubelesya nombe mbuli majoko, zikkeyi, zitolopo amaketani. = They learnt the names of things which were used when they were using cattle such as yokes, pegs, reins and chains.
the fireplace, e.g. Kamusibika nsima acikko tujike cilalilo. Put the nsima on the fire so that we cook the evening meal. Kamubikka nkuni zipati-pati acikko. Put large pieces of firewood on the fire.
a scotch-cart, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Musunge basune acikkocci kutegwa mutole mulwazi kucibbadela. = Yoke the oxen to a scotch-cart so that we take the patient to the hospital.
hook at end of chain, e.g. Cakkomonoka cikkomya nitwali kulima. = The hook at the end of the chain became detached when we were ploughing.

a boxing match, a boxing ring, e.g. Ncitwamuka kuboola, twali kulangilizya cikkweya kudolopo. = We were late in coming because we were watching a boxing match in the city. Basankwa bana Namangoma mbabaluulwa kucikkweya kulwana. = The boys of Namangoma are famous for fighting in the ring.

the main portion of the bridewealth given by the bridegroom to the relatives of the bride, e.g. Ciko ndubono lupegwa kwabo musimbi ciindi naatwalwa. Oolu lubono ndwakuula milimo yamusimbi eeyo njayakubeleka. Alimwi a bula bwakwe. Ciindi notwaamba bula bwamukaintu, twaamba bana bali mwida, abo mbaya kuzyala kooko nkwaatwalwa. = Ciko is the wealth given to the family of the girl when she gets married. This wealth is to be offered as a payment for all the works which she will do. Also it is about her womb. When we say womb of the woman we refer to the childen which are in the womb, the ones which she will produce over there where she is married.

type or breed of a beast, e.g. Kumpwizi muzeezo wakali kulanganya zyiko zyanombe mboziimpana kukuzyala boombe. Wakasala ciko cabu Bbolani aciko cabu Tonga. As regards the heifers he was studying to see the breeds of the cattle as to how they differed in producing calfs. He chose a Bbolani breed and a Tonga breed.

garment hanging loosely, pl. zikobakoba, e.g. Bamwi bayanda kapati zisani zikobakoba. = Some prefer clothes which hang loose. Mukaintu uli bubi weelede kusama cikobakoba. = A pregnant woman should wear loose clothes. Also makobo

a garment, e.g. Cikobela camwana cakatundila amasuku. = The childs garment has been stained with masuku fruit. Eeci cikobela nciyumu, tacikafwi kufwambaana. = This garment is strong, it will not wear out quickly.
low ground excavated by water, e.g. Kamutola nombe zikacele kucikobo. = Take the cattle so that they graze in the depression.
the midday meal, e.g. Casika ciindi cakulya cikoboko. = It is time to eat the midday meal. Also cisusulo, cigoboko
ear-ring, e.g. Kondisamika cikobwela kumatwi. Put the ear-rings on my ears. Also mankwinta-nkwinta.

the elbow, e.g. Wanduuma cikokola nitwali kuuma bbola. = S/he struck me with an elbow when playing ball. Ndakacuzuka cikokola nindakawa ijilo. My elbow was bruised when I fell yesterday. Also kakokola.

a charm said to increase the appetite, e.g. Sicibende wakajana kuti mwinakwe wakali acikokola: tulyo toonse twamwinakwe twakali kufwambaana kumana ansangwa. Sicibende found that his wife had a charm to increase the appetite: all her food-stuffs were quickly finished in the basket.

a school, e.g. Cikolo mazuba ano ncibotu nkaambo cipa kupona kabotu. = School these days is good because it helps to live well. Cikolo cakwiiya kujika zilyo cakaliwo kaindi. = A school for learning how to cook food was there long ago.

characteristic, trait, e.g. Cikolo-cikolo cikozya nyina. Micito ukozya banyina. Kuti banyina kabali batolo, a mwana waba mutolo mbuli banyina. = If a mother is lazy, the child will be lazy like the mother. (Kalenga Bimbe, Sikakoonze muleezyegwa. Sikakoonze ncaakacita wakaciiya kuli Bimbe.) cikolokolo coughing, bronchitis, e.g. Mwanaangu uciswa cikolokolo. = My child has a cough.
a scab from not washing, e.g. Ciindi campeyo bana balabaa cikololo amubili akaambo kakuyoowa kusamba. = During the cold season the children get scab on the body because they are afraid to wash.

cikololo camusozya = the burnt remains of stew in a pot cikoloto debt, e.g. Mebo ndilaa cikoloto kucintoolo cabo. I am in debt at those people's shop. Wakatola cikoloto. = He paid the debt. Wakalya cikoloto. = He incurred a debt. Wakabweedezya cikoloto = He paid back the loan. Also cikwelete.
a type of sorgum, e.g. Oomu mumuunda kwakasyangidwe cikolwe mwakali. = In this field the cikolwe type of sorgum was planted last year. Also nkolwe.

a broad shallow hole, pit, dent, e.g. Basune banywa meenda akatelekela mucikomba. = The oxen are drinking water which ran into a shallow hole. Mainza wakali muvwimi ubelesya zikomba kuteya banyama. Mainza was a hunter who used pits to trap animals. Ulaa cikomba amwiindi mpaakaliciside. = This one has a dent in his shin where he was wounded.
a scab, dried mucous, pl. zikombe, e.g. Bana batasambi balaa zikombe. Children who do not wash have scabs. Also cinkombe
place where people pray for their needs, e.g. Tuya kukukombela mvwula kucikombelelo. = We are going to pray for rain at the place of petition. Also cikombelo.
a place of prayer, e.g. Tukapaile kucikombelo. Let us go and pray at the place of the spirits.
a clan or matrilineal group, e.g. Mucikombo cesu basimbi tabavwundikwi. In our matrilineal group the girls are not initiated. Also cikoto
cikombo cabbuyu = thumb of the left hand
the umbilical cord, e.g. Cikombokombo camwana tacinaloka. = The child's umbilical cord has not fallen off. Also lukombokombo, luliya.
a hereditary trait, e.g. Chaazu taakali kuleka kubba nkaambo cakali cacikombokombo. Chaazu does not stop stealing because it is a trait he inherited.

a brick-mould, e.g. Cikombole cuumya zitina ncipati kapati. = The mould for making bricks is very big. Ndiyanda kuti mubezi akandibambile cikombole. I want the carpenter to make me a wooden brick-mould.
skin of animal, e.g. Nobakasika kumbali amulonga, bakakaanga kacembele cikomo cansimba kumeso. = When they reached near the river, they blindfolded the old woman with the skin of a musk cat.
an heirloom, inherited property, e.g. Baama bakandisiila cikonano campongo. My mother left me a goat as inheritance. Also cinkono

a mixture of fermented and non-fermented meal in water, e.g. Baya kukutila cikonde kucuumbwe camufwu. = They are going to pour a mixture of watered meal on to the grave of the dead person. Lyakafwa basyaanene bakakopa buyo cikonde kumaninzya dilwe. = When my grandfather died they made cikonde to conclude the funeral. Also cikondole
badly prepared food, e.g. Ooyu mwana wajika kale cikonde cansima. = The child has already half-cooked the nsima.

armlet, e.g. Bakamwale balasamikwa zikonde ezi zyansambo kuteeti kabalibonya kuti bakajailwa nombe zineneede zilaa mafwuta. The initiates are made to wear armlets of grass so that the people may know that fat cattle were killed for them at their initiation.
See cikonde.
a cake made by termites underground, e.g. Nitwali kusya sikaulu, twajana cikonga cipati kunsi. = When we were digging for a small type of bee, we found a termite-cake.
a landmark, signpost, e.g. Cikonkwani ca Munali cijanika kumilundu. = The Munali sign-post (historic site) is found among the hills. (inkanka = surveyor's peg) Also cikwaankwani

a skill or trait which is handed down within a certain clan, e.g. Cikono camusankwa oyu nkubeza nkaambo basyaanyinakulu bakali kubeza. = What this boy inherited is the skill of carving because his grandfather was carving. (It is different from *lukono* which refers to material objects which are inherited by clan members when a person dies.)
the spotted design of a hawk, e.g. *Nkuku zyangu nzyacikonze.* = My chickens have the spotted design of a hawk.
a piece of faeces, pl. *zikonzo*, e.g. *Mubwa walya cikonzo camwana.* = The dog has eaten the baby's excrement.

a likeness, resemblance, e.g. *Aaba bana balaa cikonzya cabausyi.* = These chidren resemble the father. *Bamwi bamakaintu balaa cikonzya kuzintu nzyobabona nobali amada.* Some women take on a resemblance to things they see when they are pregnant. Also *cinkozya*.
a scarecrow, e.g. *Umwi mulimi wakafwala cisamu mbuli muntu kuti cibe cikonzyo cabaceta.* = A certain farmer carved a piece of wood as a human being to scare away the monkeys. Also *syaamankwamu*.
a drum of bark used as a bin/bag/container, e.g *Mwamana kwaatebula maila mwaabikke mucikooko.* = When you finish harvesting the millet put it in a container.

a sickness derived from not eating what others eat, loss of appetite, e.g. *Aaka kana ncikoolo ncokakokede.* = The child is thin because of not eating what others eat. *Baneene bakandipa musamu wacikoolo kutegwa ntalike kulya nyama yankuku.* = My grandmother gave me a medicine which takes away loss of appetite so that I would begin to eat chicken.
a headache, e.g. *Cikopo cilananuka. Cikopo cilaanzamuka. Cikopo cilaanduka.* The headache is throbbing. I have a splitting headache.

a measuring tin for beer, e.g. *Wamana kunywa bukoko, undipe cikopo nkaambo nceulisyila bukoko.* When you have finished drinking the beer, please give back the measuring-tin because it is the one I use for selling beer.
mental dullness, e.g. *Kanchele walo kuzwa mubbuku lyakamwi kusikila mubbuku lyacisambomwi cakali cikopo camutwe.* From Grade one to Grade six Kanchele was dull.
a section of a field, e.g. *Uuno mwaka tuya kulima cikoso camuunda mputwakalimide ndongwe.* = This year we are going to plough a section of the field where we planted groundnuts.

the end, termination, final judgement, last breath of living person, e.g. *Twaambo nitwakasika acikosokelo, mujayi bakamupa mulandu wanombe zyone.* When the discussions reached the final judgement, they gave the murderer a punishment of paying four cattle.
*cikosokelo camilandu* = court assizes (periodical sessions for administration of civil and criminal justice)
catarrh or mucous in chest, e.g. *Ndatiisole kukola, cikosoko tacizwi amoyo.* When I tried to cough, the phlegm was not released from my throat. Also *cinkoolwa, cikosokoso*.

identity document, e.g. *Ndali kukuzwisya cikosole camutwe ku Bbooma.* = I had gone to take out a registration card at the Civic Centre. Mutinta wakagusya cikosole camutwe akutondezya musilikani.* Mutinta took out her registration card and showed it to the policeman. Also *cinyongole*.
short form e.g. *Twaambo otu twakalembwa mucikosolo.* These matters were written briefly.
anything used for cutting, as a scissors/shears, e.g. *Kobelesya cikosozyo kukosola bunyweba nkaambo bula-*
kuti ukosole amaanza. = Use the scissors to cut the thread because it will cut you if you try and break it by hand.
a lintel, transom, e.g. Akaambo kakulampa kwangu, ndikotama buya kunjila *acikotamino*. = Because of my height, I bend down while entering under the lintel.

a lump, a swelling or hard growth in humans or in animals, e.g. Ulaa *cikoto* mwida mwana ooyu. = That child has a hard lump in the stomach. Mwida lyangu kuli *cikoto* cilimvwisya alimwi cilacisa. = In my stomach there is a lump which can be felt and it hurts. Munsima ndajana *cikoto* cabusu cipati. = In the nsima I found a big lump of uncooked flour.
a knot, e.g. Bamukowa balyaanga *cikoto* nibanjililwa penzi. = The matrilineal relatives bind themselves in a knot when they are in problems.
a clan or matrilineal group, e.g. Bazyamba mmukowa uulyaangide *cikoto*. = The Bazyamba are a clan which are tied with a knot, i.e. are united. Also cikombo.
wound copper, iron wire

an eye-brow, an eye-lid, e.g. Cisamu candicisa *acikoye*. = A stick has hurt my eye-lid. Kuti *cikoye* cabimbabimba inga kuli bakuvwiya. = If your eyelid is trembling it means that there is someone talking about you.
a type of bird, the sandgrouse, e.g. *Cikoyokoyo* cilauluka musinzo mulamfwu kuya kuyandaula meenda akunywa. = The sandgrouse flies a long distance going to find water.
resemblance, e.g. Micito yokwa Simeenda ilaa *cikozya* cabausyi. = The deeds of Simeenda resemble the father's. Also cinkonzya.

example, comparison, e.g. *Cikozyanyo* ncaapa cileendelana ancaamba. = The example s/he has given corresponds to what s/he says. Bayi batwaambila *cikozyanyo* casyuumbwa. = The teacher gave us an example of a lion. Also mukozyanyo.

maize stalk without the cob, e.g. Kobweza *cikuba* ume musune oyo. = Take a maize stalk and beat that ox. Wamudyokozya *cikuba* mulisyo mweenzinyina. She stabbed her friend in the eye with a maize stalk. Also cimbololo,

luck in farming, e.g. Baacisya balaa *cikuba* aboobo balaalima mapopwe manji. = My uncle has good luck in farming and so has plenty of maize. Ooyu muntu ulaa *cikuba* ncalaa mapopwe manji myaka yoonse. = This person has luck in farming that is why s/he has much maize every year. Naakasika kumuŋanga Chikupa wakati, "Omunene ndiyanda mucelo wa*cikuba*." = When Chikupa arrived at the witchdoctor he said, "Old man, I want medicine for success in farming."
girl's plaited hair, e.g. Ooyu musimbi *cikuba* camasusu cili kumutwe ncibotu. = This girl's plaited hair is beautiful.
a type of disease, e.g. Bacembele baciswa *cikubakuba*. = The old woman is suffering from the cikubakuba illness.

age of maturity, e.g. Bana nibakaunka kusobana, basankwa ibakali kuyanda kusika *acikubukilo* bakasyaala balayota mulilo abapati. = When the children went off to play, the boys who were about to reach the age of maturity remained warming themselves at the fire with the elders.

an open valley, e.g. Mweelede kumupa ciindi kutegwa ambe zyoonse zili kumoyo. Kuti wamwiinganina, inga zimwi zyafwidilila, zyaunka *mucikuka*. You ought to give him time so that he says all that is in his heart. If you restrict him, perhaps some things will be lost and go into the open valley. (i.e. become irretrievable)
beer, e.g. Bwaca buyo buzuba mbocinywa cikuku kulaboola bantu bamwi bategwa banasyimukwe. As soon as it dawns, the day when the beer is ready for consumption, some people known as in-laws will come.

a pretense, e.g. Mukombwe wakati, "Ndicita cikuku-cikuku ne-ndoona natanasika amulyango. Ndipeta mukosi mubbaba nkabela asika umwaambile kuti muvwiminyoko ndamugonka mukosi." = The Cock said, "I will act like a chicken when sleeping before he arrives at the door. I will hide my neck in the wings and so when he arrives tell him that you have cut off his fellowhunter's head."
a flock of little birds, e.g. Ndalikuyamina cikuku-kuku mumaila. = I was scaring away a flock of little birds from the millet.
a broom/brush, pl. zikukuzyo, e.g. Kamutema zikukuzyo mukukule lubuwa. = Cut brooms so that you can sweep the court-yard. Konditemenezya cikukuzyo camulubuwa. = Cut me a broom for the court-yard.
a salt-lick, salted or alkaline earth which cattle lick, e.g. nombe zilya cikula munsi aamulonga Kasiya. = The cattle are licking at the salt-pan near the river Kasiya.
original, e.g. "Cikulukulu njenanda." = The first wife is the home. (a proverb)
what is cast-off (wife, clothes etc.), e.g. Wajokelela cikulukulu ncaakalekede. = He returns to the thing which he cast off.
a lock or padlock for door, e.g. Kocitenda buyo cikulukulu nkaambo cijuzyo cazimina. Just cut a padlock because the key is lost.
something of long ago, e.g. Ciimbo eco ncoimba ncikulukulu. = That song you sing is of long ago.

a place where hair is cut and clothes dicarded (in the cleansing of a witch), e.g. Baya kukukululwa masusu kucikulwido. They are going to have their hair cut at the barbers. Ooyu mudaala kamumutola kucikulwido akagelwe masusu. Take this old man to have his hair cut at the barbers.

cloth made of animal skin, pl. zikumba, e.g. Amulyango bamwi bajazya zikumba zyarņombe. Some use animal skin to close the door. Bantu bensiku bakali kusama zikumba. = In the past people used to wear animal skins. Bamakaintu bakaindi bakali kusama zikumba. The women of long ago used to wear dresses made of animal skin. Also cikutu.
addled eggs, e.g. Eeli iji tiilyakakonkonwa, bana nobalijika bajana biyo cikumba. This egg was not hatched, when the children boiled it they found it addled. (hard yoke)
a sledge, e.g. Wakamulazika mucikumbaansi. = She laid him down on the sledge. Also cilayi
a cloud, e.g. Cikumbi camvwula cilasiya. The rain-cloud is black. Cikumbi camvwula casika afwaafwi. = The rain cloud has come near.

eight days of cloud cover, e.g. Cikumbi lusele nociliko inga kulatontola. = When there is an eight-day cloud cover it becomes cold indeed. Cikumbi lusele cilaba mwaka amwaka. = Every year there is an eight-day cloud cover.

a place specially made for incubation, a nest on the ground, e.g. Mucikumbilo kuli mayi kkumi. There are ten eggs in the nest. Cikumbilo cankuku cadilimuka. = The chickens incubator has fallen down. Also cifwuko (for hens), cinteente, (for wild birds)
