a place where beer is brewed, e.g. Bamuka Jeeke bakayanika mimena munanda yacikumbilo cabukoko. = Jeeke's wife dried the yeast in the house where beer is brewed.
container for brewing beer, e.g. Mwaunka kubacembele mukaletelezye acikumbilo cabukoko. = When you go to the old woman's home, bring along a container for brewing beer.
a manner of asking for something e.g. Cikumbilo cakwe ncabulemu. = Her manner of asking is polite.
a threshold, e.g. Muyaki wakaciyaka kabotu cikumbizyi. = The builder built the threshold well. Also cikunguzyo.

the big toe, e.g. Cikumo cangu cilacisa nkaambo ndalinontola. = My big toe is paining because I tripped up over something. Ndayaswa bumvwa acikumo. = I was pierced by a thorn on the big toe. Also calananda cakumaulu.
lust (a taboo word) e.g. Utani kubelesyi mulaka wacikundani. = Do not be using lustful language. Also buvwuule, kampuwempuwe.

a bunch, bundle, cluster (of drying maize, fish, dry meat, bananas), e.g. Bacijata cikungo canswi nibali kuzela. = They caught a great number of fish when they were fishing. Wacimana kucilya cikungo camabbanana coonse. = He finished off the whole bunch of bananas.
a mob of people, e.g. Ndajana cikungo cabantu balindilila kuula mapopwe kudolopo. = I found a crowd of people waiting to buy maize in the town. Also kkungo.

the base of the spine, the back of an animal, e.g. Banduuma musako kucikungu. = They have beaten me on the lower back with a stick. Mwana wabba cikungu cankuku. = The child has stolen the back of the chicken. Kamucaala nobacingwindi, nobabwa bamicila acikungu. = Stay well you useless ones, you dogs with tails growing from the base of the spine.
cloak, a long garment, pl. zikungu, e.g. Bapaizi basama zikungu. = Priests wear long garments. Also cibaki.

abdomen of a black insect, e.g. Ooyo ulaa nguzu anyamune cikungu casimunyewu kutegwa bantu kabamuyoowa akumwaamba "bubbala nombe". = The one who has strength should lift up the abdomen of a black insect so that people will fear him and know that he is powerful.

sleeping in a group, as when people sleep together at a funeral, e.g. Bantu adilwe baona cikungubulo. = People sleep in a group at a funeral. Bana boona cikungubulo acibuye. = The children are sleeping in a group together on the floor. Also kkungubulo.

a threshold, doorstep, e.g. Eeyi nanda mwiibambile cikunguzyo. = Make a threshold for this house. Bukoko ameenda akupiila zyakali kutilwa a cikunguzyo kakwiitwa mazina abantu bakafwa kaindi. = Beer and water for an offering were poured at the threshold calling upon the names of the people who had died long ago. Also cikumbizyi.

a log, e.g. Kamusikka cikuni eci uyake mulilo. = Stick this log in the fire so that it lights up. Ndaunkide kukuleta cikuni ncindakasiide jilo musyokwe. = I had gone off to bring the firewood which I had left in the bush yesterday.
an ear of sorgum after it has been beaten, pl. makunka, e.g. Komuleka musune acilye buyo cikunka eco. = Let the ox eat that ear of sorgum.
bleeding gums, e.g. Menyo aabaama akamana kuloka akaambo kacikunka menyo. = The teeth of my mother have finished falling out because of the disease of bleeding gums. Also muhibu.
a beaded head-dress, e.g. Bamwi bamananga basama *cikunka* cabulungu kumutwe. = Some witchdoctors wear a head-dress of beads.
beaded head-dress Also cimpaampwa.

salt-pan, pl. zikunyo, e.g. nombe zilya *cikunyo* acuulu. = The cattle are licking the salt-pan on the termite-hill. *Muzikunyo* mubwa ubweza bafwulwe. = The dog finds tortoises in the salt-pan. Also cikula.
a worn-out hoe, pl. zikuta, e.g. Kocizwisya *cikuta* mumwiini omo tubikke limbi jamba. = Remove the old hoe-blade from within the handle so that we put another.

a temporary grass-thatched dwelling, e.g. Cikuta cabaneene wacuumpa mwana. = A child burnt down the grass hut of my grandmother. Oomu *muzikuta* basimbi mobakali kuyiila kujika. = It was in these grass huts that the girls learnt how to cook. Cakali ciindi camupeyo, bana abamakaintu bakalibungene acikko *mucikuta* bayota mulilo. = It was the cold season, the children and the women were gathered at the fireplace in the grass-roofed shelter warming themselves at the fire. Also cigongola.
a garden/ a small fertile field, e.g. Sunu mukalime *cikuti* camudaala. = Today you should plough the little garden of the old man. Also kkuti, mubunda.

a valley, depression, glen, pl. zikuti, e.g. Nyika kuno ilukidwe *zikuti*. = The land here is woven with valleys *cikutu* a hide not yet softened, an old skin, e.g. Babombeka *cikutu* caņombe basankwa. = The boys have softened the hide of an animal. Babwa balya *cikutu* camoombe wakafwa. = The dogs have eaten the hide of a dead calf. Also itobo

a place for making a fire, e.g. Bakutula mulilo *kucikutwilo*. = They have lit a fire at the fireplace.(Ila) Mulilo ukunkile *acikutwilo*. = Light the fire at the fireplace. Mulilo tuumani *acikutwilo* eci. = The fire never goes out in this fireplace. Also cikko.
early shoots, e.g. Mwana wabona *cikuuku* cabowarjanda. The child has seen the young mushrooms. Also ciguugu, cikuku
a skin, pl. zikuye, e.g. Bamaneene bakaindi bakali kusama *zikuye*. = Our grandmothers of long ago used to wear animal skins. Also cipaya, cisalu, cizwato, cikwiye.
a fig tree, (Ila) e.g. Bayuni balya nkuyu *mucikuzu*. The birds are eating figs from the fig tree. Also cikuyu.

a shell or covering of anything, like the shell of a tortoise, the slough of a snake, e.g. Nondo ilaa *cikwa* ciyumu kapati kupwaya. = The tortoise has a very hard shell to break. Bana basobana *cikwa* cankumba. = The children are playing with the shell of a snail.

mildew, a destructive growth of minute fungi on plants, or paper, clothes or leather, e.g. Kuti cibwantu cakkala kaindi munongo, inga caba *cikwaalala*. If sweet beer sits for a long time in an earthen pot, it becomes infected with mildew. Also nkubi.
a crow, e.g. *Cikwaangala* waamana mayi ankuku mucisekwe. = A crow has finished the eggs of a chicken in the crate. Also cikwangala, (cikwaangala buwe = a black crow)
a sign-post, pl. zikwaankwani, e.g. *Cikwaankwani* citondezya mugwagwa uya kucikolo cipati cakawa. = The sign-post showing the road to the university has fallen down. Also cikwankwani.

a rough skinned reptile, such as a toad or a lizard, pl. zikwaba, e.g. Akati aamabwe muzilundu kujanika zikwaba. = Among the stones in the hills reptiles are found. Babwa bajata *cikwaba* mumusena. = The dogs have caught a reptile in the vlei. Also mbulumusanza (large lizard)

anything that gives cover, a canopy, e.g. Ciluli cananda *ncikwabilizyo* camvwula kuti itanikunjili munanda. = The roof of a house provides a shelter from the rain so that it does not enter the house. Cimbayambaya cacibbadela cijisi *cikwabilizyo*. = The hospital vanette has a canopy.
a shield, a stick to parry blows, e.g. Intobo *ncikwabyo* camasumo. = A shield is a barrier against spears.
bali kulwana maanza cali *ncecikwabyo* cabo. = The boys who were fighting used their hands as to defend themselves.

noise, e.g. Nguni oyo ucita *cikwala* amunzi wangu? = Who is that one making noise at my home? Nkaambonzi muyuni oyo ucita *cikwala* cili boobo? = Why is that bird making a noise like that? Also cigwata.
long spotted line on any animal, e.g. Moombe wakazyalwa jilo ulaa *cikwalala* amusana. = The calf which was born yesterday has a long spotted line on it's back.
smallpox, e.g. Nokwakamana mpeyo kwakabanjila *cikwalibbani*. = When the cold was over smallpox infected them. cf. intomba.
a purse/wallet, a match-box, e.g. Kamundaabila *cikwama* camancisi. = Give me a box of /matches. Koya undiletele *cikwama* camali. = Go and bring me my purse. Also mpotomona.
a creature who lives in caves, e.g. Syaanasulwe wakatamba ci*kwamaala* abamwi bakkala mumabwe. = = The hare invited a cave-dweller and other reptiles who live among the rocks.
a type of fish, bream, e.g. Ndaula *cikwamba* kumusyika nkaambo balwazi ncobayanda. = I bought a bream at the market because that is what the patients want. Also mpende.

a deep scratch left by thorns or dogs claws, e.g. Aandiluma babwa kwacaala *cikwambu*. = There remains a deep scratch where the dogs bit me. Cisamu candivwalula *cikwambu* akuulu. = The stick marked me with a deep scratch on my leg.

a troublesome spirit sent to bring problems to a thief, e.g. Muntu wakabba mali wakaapilusya jilo nkaambo *cikwambu* cakamupenzya kumuuma. = The thief who stole money returned it yesterday because a spirit was afflicting him by beating him.

an open bleeding wound, e.g. *Cikwamu* cilaa musana cilacisa. = The bleeding wound on my back is painful. Bulowa bunji bulazwa *acikwamu*. = Much blood is coming out from the open wound. (See verb, -kwamuka)
a type of bird, the crow, e.g. Muyuni *cikwangala* ulalya nyama ibolede. = The bird, the crow, eats rotten meat.

what is raw or unripe, e.g. Ooyu mwana wajula cisyu kacicili *cikwange*. This child took the relish off the fire when it was still uncooked. Batupa cakulya *cikwange*. = They have given us uncooked food. Also inkwange, imbisi, cibisi
a sign-post, e.g. *Cikwankwani* cacikolo cesu cili munsi anzila. = The sign-post for our school is near the path.
bubbling, e.g. Mweenzu ucikkala biyo nkumvwa *cikwasa* citi 'kwakwa-kwa'. = When the visitor had just seated himself there was heard a bubbling sound going 'kwa-kwa-kwa'.
present given to boys at girls' initiation dance, e.g. Basankwa boonse bapegwa *cikwata-buta*. = All the boys at the girl's initiation dance have been given food.
an inner compartment in a grave, e.g. Kaindi zifwene zyakali kubambwa mbuli *cikwati* mukati. Long ago graves were made with a coffin-shaped compartment inside.
a disease, the mange, e.g. Zimwi mpongo zyakaba *acikweekwe*. = Some goats got the mange. Also cinkwankwa
a traditional game that is played in which children dance by turning around. e.g. (a riddle) Zungulu-zungulu *cikwekwe*. Nimbalo.
a long, thin-bladed dancing axe, pl. *zikwelebe*, e.g. Bamwi bantu bazyanya *zikwelebe*. Some people use dancing-axes when dancing.

a debt, credit, e.g. Bantu balaa *cikwelete* kuli ndime mbanji. = The people who are in debt to me are many. Bantu bajisi *cikwelete* kuli ndime tabajosyi pe. = People who are in debt to me do not pay back at all. Also cikoloto.
attractiveness, magnetism, e.g. Mulaka wakalijisi *cikwelezyo* cakali kubotesya bantu banji bakamumvwa kaambaula. His speech had a magnetism which delighted many people who heard him talk.
a whetstone, e.g. Eeli bbwe *ncikwengelo* cazipanga. = This stone is for sharpening big blades. Amundikwengele cipeni *acikwengelo* awo. = Sharpen this knife for me on that whetstone there.
boxing ring, e.g. Lottie Mwale wakacizyi kapati kufwusa nyindi naanjila *mucikwenya*. Lottie Mwale knew how to box when he entered the ring. Also *cikkweya*

boat made of planks, pl. *zikwepe*, a ferry, e.g. Nobakasika ku Zambezi bakajana bantu, mbaaba balanduka mulonga *azikwepe*. When they reached the Zambezi they found people, there they are crossing the river in boats.
zilatant cikwepe*, mpoona zilalandu-sigwa kuzwa kunkomwe imwi kusikila kuli imwi. = Cars and lorries go on to a ferry and are then taken across from one side to the other.
stairs e.g. Musankwa wakabasololela kuya *kucikwepe*. The boy led them going up the stairs.
plastic nappy, pl. *zikwesa*, e.g. Wakaula *zikwesa*. He bought plastic nappies.
a broad-bladed straight-edged working axe, e.g. *Cikwese* cangu cakafwumpa. My working axe is blunt.
a of fibre before it is stripped, e.g. Kamuya mulete *cikwibba caloozi* mwamana mucifwundunune. Go and bring an unstripped fibre and when you have done that strip it.

a swarm of locusts, e.g. Uuno mwaka ngwacikwikwi zisyango zilamana. = This year is for locusts, the crops will be finished. *Cikwikwi* cakainda mumuunda wangu akulya mapopwe onse. = A swarm of locusts came by my field and ate all the maize. Also cigwigwi.
pidgeon hut, e.g. *Mucikwilimba* kuli nzoka. There is a snake in the pidgeon hut.
a green pigeon, e.g. Mukasamu muya kuli *cikwilinti* cakkala. = A green pidgeon is sitting in that tree. Also cigwilinti.
putty, e.g. Amubikke *cikwizo*
Put putty on the windows. Also cikunyo.
organized hunting activity, a general hunt when the bush is set on fire, e.g. Banalumi boonse bakaya kucila ku Chisoboyo. = All the men have gone to the hunt at Chisoboyo. Also ncila.
a gross stomach, e.g. *Cila cangulube ncibi, taciligwi.* = The stomach of the pig is bad, it is inedible. Also *ida*

a rough grass hut, shelter, pl. malabba, e.g. *Kamuyaka cilabba bakkalile bantu adilwe.* = Build a temporary shelter for the people to stay in at the funeral. *Kunkolola bakayaka cilabba cipati.* = At the initiation they built a big shelter. *Kumalabba abamasilikani ndakabona miIwi yazilwanyo.* = At the police-camp I saw piles of weapons.

a fable without a song, an enigma, e.g. *Kamundipa cilabiko comwe ndimvwe.* = Give me one riddle to hear. *Cilabiko cakatulabika basyaaneene cilakatazya.* = The riddle which grandfather told us is difficult. Also kalabiko, kalabi.
inability to sleep, e.g. *Jilo masiku ndakalaa cilabila, kwiina nindaona kabotu pe.* = Last night I had insomnia, I did not sleep well.

any rubbish or useless thing, pl. zilabisi/malabisi, e.g. *Ooyu ncacita ncilabisi lyoonse.* = What this one does is always rubbish. *Eeci cisani ncilabisi ciide kuzauka.* = This garment is useless, it is just in tatters.

a sledge or sleigh, e.g. *Baya kucigayo acilai lyoonse.* = They always go to the mill with a sledge. *Basankwa bagonka cilai cakususizya meenda.* = The boys are cutting a sledge for carrying water. Also cilayi.

appetite for something, e.g. *Sunu ndaa cilakalaka cakulya sulwe.* = Today I have an appetite for eating a rabbit. *Ndimvwide cilakalaka cakulya nyama.* = I feel an appetite for eating meat. Also cinunki.
a passionate kiss, e.g. *Ibbuku lyakajisi cifwanikiso camusankwa amusimbi bakali kulyana cilakalaka.* = The book had a picture of a boy and a girl kissing one another passionately.
the palate, e.g. *Ndabaa buyaaya kucilakula.* = I have sores on the palate. Also malagilo
the leaf of a young palm tree, pl. zilala, e.g. *Akaya kalala kajisi zilala zibotu.* That young palm tree has very nice leaves

drought, e.g. *Uuno mwaka kuli cilala bakwesu.* = This year there is a drought, my friends. *Mazuba akazyalwa mwana ooyu kwakaliindide kale myaka yobile kakuli cilala, ooyu waali mwaka watatu danga eeli kalizumanana.* = During the days when this child was born, two years of drought has passed, this was the third year for this drought to continue.
the evening meal, e.g. *Kofwambaana ukalete busu, tujike cilalilo.* = Hurry and bring flour so that we cook the evening meal.
a rat's nest, e.g. *Ndajana cilalo mumuunda.* = I have found a rat's nest in the field. Also manswa.

the afterbirth, e.g. *Naakamana kutumbuka cilalo cakamuka kuzwa aboobo mutumbu wakapenga kapati.* When she has given birth the afterbirth was slow to come out and so the mother suffered severely. Also camacembele, macembele.
a type of bird, the falcon, e.g. *Cilamalama tacikkomani kukkala mucisaka, ciyandisya kukkala mucibanda.* = The falcon does not like to live in a forest, it prefers to live in the open plain.
a coloured or painted mark, e.g. *Cilambo eci cili mbuli caamalila.* This mark is like one of the funeral marks. *Cilambo cankuku eyi ncibotu.* = The marking of this chicken is beautiful.
the insignia of a chief, e.g. *Kwakali bantu banji mwami mupya naakapegwa cilambo cabwami.* There were many people when the chief was given the insignia of chieftainship.
a hollow or depression, e.g. *Ngulube zilikanda mumeenda aka-kkalila mucilambwa.* = The pigs are wallowing in the water which has settled in a depression.
a solitary red spot on cow, e.g. *Musune okwesu ulaa cilambwa ankumo.* = Our ox has a red spot on the forehead. Also cilambo, mubala, kaama, caama.
a drought, e.g. *Uuno mwaka ncilanga, kwiina mvwula.* = This is a year of drought, there is no rain. Also cilala.
afternoon, e.g. *Beenzu bakasika acilangabwaaseme.* = The visitors arrived in the afternoon. Also cilangankumo
about 13.00-15.00 hrs., e.g. *Izuba lyasika acilangankumo, tuya kukusyanga ndongwe kumuunda.* = When the sun is opposite the forehead, we will go to plant groundnuts in the field.

a residential place for families, farms, e.g. *Eeci cilawo ncipati kapati.* = This farm is very big. *Ooyu mwana akaambo kabubbi unyina cilawo cakukkala.* = This youth, because of thieving, has no place to stay.
a shed, a shelter for sleeping, e.g. *Basankwa bayaka cilawo cakoonena bana.* = The boys are building a shelter for the children to sleep in. Also cilabba
a place or space, e.g. *Lyadilwe lya Mainza Choona cilawo cakaceya nkaambo bantu bakali banji kapati.* = At the funeral of Mainza Choona there was no room as the people were very many.
a garment, e.g. *Cilaya ca-mwana caligwa mpongo.* = The child's garment was eaten by a goat. Also cisani, cikobela, cibaki.
a piece of metal, e.g. *Kamuleta cilaya tusye zilindi zyacisanza.* = Bring a piece of metal so that we dig holes for a maize granary. Also cisisyo, cigawa, cigoyo, mungwala.

a vehicle on runners instead of wheels, a sledge, sleigh, a conveyance of any kind, e.g. *Cilayi cakutola kumuunda cilifwide aboobo kuyandika kugonka cimbi.* = The sleigh for transport to the field is broken and so it is necessary to cut another.
old name for the railway line, e.g. *Cilayi nicakasika ku Mazabuka basankwa banji bakali kujatwa cibbalo.* = When the railway line reached Mazabuka many boys were caught for forced labour.
a patch of grass which has grown where the veld has been burnt, e.g. *Basune mubatole kukucelela kucilazya mumusena.* = Take the oxen to graze to the patch of grass in the vlei.
a patch of grass which has not been burnt, e.g. *Aano mazuba kuli basulwe banji musyokwe lyacilazya.* = Today there are many rabbits in the unburnt veld.
an axe, e.g. *Eeci cileba cilabosya kapati.* = This axe is very sharp. *Mwiini wacileba cangu watyoka.* = The handle of my axe is broken. Also keembe.
See cilebyo.

a thing which causes one to stumble, e.g. *Imfwinzyo nzyobaanga munzila ncilebyo cibi kapati.* = The grass which they tied across the path is a great impediment. *Munzila iiya kumeenda, kuli wakabikka bbwe lyacilebyo.* = On the path going to the water, someone has put a stone which can cause one to stumble.

anything slaughtered at the initiation ceremony, e.g. *Ankolola yamwanaangu bakajaya nombe yomwe yacilebyo.* = At my daughter's initiation ceremony they killed one ritual cow. (-leba nkolola = kill something for that intiation ceremony) e.g. *Tiindakasika ankolola nkaambo ndakabula cilebyo.* = I did not go to the initiation ceremony because I had nothing to kill. Also cilebya, cilebe.
a cartilage, firm elastic tissue, gristle, e.g. Nsekonzyi kulya nyama eyi, ncilekete calo. = I cannot eat this meat, it is just gristle. Also mulambi.
degree, step, stage, pl. malele e.g. Kubala mabbuku ncilele cakusumpuka mubuzumi. Reading books is a step in making progress in life.

a cripple, a handicapped person or animal, paralytic, e.g. Ooyu mwana mbwaakazyalwa ncilema. = This child is lame from birth. Eeyi mpongo yakazyala cilema citakwe kuulu komwe. = This goat gave birth to a lame kid with one leg missing.

a heavy load, e.g. Mwana muniini tabwezi cilema. A young child cannot lift a heavy load. Sena ulijisi cilema ceelede kubikkwa munsi? Inzya, tulijisi bbokesi. = Have you something heavy that needs to be put behind. Yes, we have a box.
bunches of figs (nkuyu), e.g. Makwilinti alayandisya kulya cilemba-lemba. = The green pidgeons like to eat figs.
a fig tree, fig(s), e.g. Cilembela cili mumuunda bakacigonka. = They cut down the fig tree in the field.
a medicinal root (unidentified), e.g. Mulwazi bakamusilisya musamu wacilembela. They healed the patient with a medicinal root.
something to write on, e.g. Sicikolo talembi nkaambo wabula cilembela. = This pupil does not write because she has nothing to write on.
notched edge of a fragment used for decorating pottery, e.g. Ndabula cilembio, ndali kuyanda kubamba zibiya zyangu. I have no piece of pottery for decorating, I wanted to work on my pots.
an instrument for writing, e.g. Cilembyo cangu caleka kulemba. = My pen has stopped writing.

a liquid which becomes turbid when mixed with another substance, e.g. Mabisi ayo utabikki mumusozya nkaambo cilaba cilenda akaambo kakupya kwamusozya. Do not put that sour milk in the samp because it will be turbid as the samp is still hot.
a pillar, pl. zilende, e.g. Twakajana bana baliyubide kunze acilende. = We found the children hiding behind the pillar.
a vision, e.g. Beembezi bambelele bakabona cilengano cakabayoosya kapati musyokwe. The shepherds saw a vision which frightened them in the bush.

a custom/habit/tradition, e.g. Ooyu ulaa cilengwa cakutukila bapati. = This one has the habit of insulting the elders. Ooyu mwana ciyanda kuba cilengwa cakwe cakubba. = It is becoming a habit for this child to steal.
a striking and unusual happening, either good or bad, e.g. Eeyi mpongo yakazyala cilengwa-lengwa. = This goat gave birth to a deformed kid.
a living creature or inanimate object, e.g. Uulemene tasekwi nkaambo ncilengwaleza. A lame person should not be laughed at because s/he is created by God.
a bundle of grass or firewood, e.g. Amunditukke cileye cankuni. = Help me lift a bundle of firewood on to my head.
a beard, e.g. Cilezu cabasyaneene cituba mvwi. The beard of my grandfather has grey hair. Ooyu cilezu cili mbuli camujembwe wampongo. = This man's beard is like a goat's.

the first part of the mafwenezya marriage payment, e.g. Bataata bali kutola mali acilezu koomusimbi ngweyanda kukwata. My father was taking the first part of the marriage payment to the family of the girl I want to marry.
a curtain which protects from wind Also cilibebekezyo.
plenty of money, e.g. Muleli ulaa cili cinji mumasi aandeene. = The leader has vast amounts of money in different countries.
a working axe, e.g. Koleta ciliba tugonsye nkuni. = Bring the axe so that we cut firewood with it. Also cileba.

a bundle of dried maize stalks, pl. ziliba, e.g. Kaindi bana basankwa bakali kusobana ziliba zyamakuba mumeenda. = Long ago boys used to play with bundles of dried maize stalks in the water. (the bundles float and can carry the children)

a boat or raft made of light materials, pl. ziliba, e.g. Chuungabuluba wakabamba ciliba catusamu amabu mayumu, mpoona mayuwe akamutola asyoonto-syoonto kuya kumbo. = Chuungabuluba made a raft of sticks and strong reeds, thereupon the waves took him gradually to the west. Mumaanzi malamfwu balombwana bakali kubelesya ziliba. Bali kunga bajana mpaali malamfwu baleta ziliba akutalika kucotela. = In deep waters the men would use rafts. Wherever they found it was deep they would bring rafts and begin to paddle.

a cloth protecting against the wind, e.g. Eeci cilibebekezyo ncakukwabilila muwo. This cloth is for protection against the wind. (When used as a verb, e.g. Kolibebeka kalembo nkaambo kulatontola = Cover yourself with a piece of cloth because it is cold.)
an eating place, e.g. Kobikka cakulya mucilido cabanyama. Put the food in the trough of the animals.
a style of eating, e.g. Cilido cakwe ncibi. = His manner of eating is bad.

an offence, e.g. Wakanjila mucilijazyo nkaambo wakayanda muka muntu. = He was guilty of an offence because he loved the wife of another. Mulomo lyoonse ncilijazyo. The mouth is always a way of getting yourself into trouble.
an unexpected and undesired happening, e.g. Ndayeeya kuti cilainda kugwasya kumukwata biyo nokutanaba cililenga. I think it is better just to marry her before anything happens unexpectedly.

a permanent alluvial garden, e.g. Lungu luli mucilili cangu Iwakaneneka. = The pumpkins which are in my garden have grown small ones. Mutumbu wakanjila mucilili, mvwula noyakalaba matanga onse akalibonya mucilili. The suckling mother entered the field and when the rain produced lightning all the melons were seen. Cibila wakajisi cilili candongwe munsi acilundu. The rock rabbit had a fertile plot of groundnuts near a hill. Basimbi balasya mbeba mucilili causyi. = The girls are digging for rats in their father's garden.

a place to weep at, e.g. Cibaka eci ncilililo cibotu. = This place is good for weeping. Cilililo camwami wesu ciya kubeda kumunzi wakwe mupya. = The weeping place for our chief is going to be at his new home.
a cripple, e.g. Muntu wauma mwana wamuseka kuba cilima. = The man beat the child who laughed at him for being a cripple. Also cilema.

an instrument for ploughing, e.g. Uuno mwaka nsejisi cilima pe. This year I don't have any tool for ploughing. Cilima moomu mubusinde ndijamba lyanombe. = What was used for this upturned land was a plough. Also cilimya.
a musical instrument (an accordion), e.g. Cilimba kuti calila inga wamvwa canoneenzya. When you hear an accordion playing you have a sweet feeling.
a Valley dance which was performed by boys and girls in the evening in the cold season. The elders taught them the dumming.

a horizontal piece of wood beside the spirit-gate on which people sit, e.g. Kobaambila beenzu bakkale _acilimba_ cili munsi alwaanga. = Tell the visitors to sit on the piece of wood near the spirit-gate. Aba beenzu bakakkala _acilimba_ etanda cisamu ciingene alwaanga. These visitors sat on the log which was put across the spirit-gate.

an agricultural product, e.g. _Cilime_ camuunda oyu mbutonje. = The crop of this field is cotton. _Cilime caka-_ _komena kabotu mwaka wainda mbuluba_ _bulikke butayandi mvwula nji._ = The only crop which grew well last year was cotton which does not need much rain. Also cisyango.

the hot, dry season, e.g. Cisyu cacilimo kanji-kanji inga ncaampe. = The relish of the dry season is usually dried vegetables. Kanji-kanji _cilimo_ mpongo tazyeembelwi. Most of the time during the dry season the goats are not herded.

a hole, e.g. Ndanjila _mucilindi_ nindali kweenda sunu. = I went into a hole when I was walking today. Basicikolo basya _cilindi_ cakusowela tombe. = The school children are digging a pit for throwing rubbish.

a fine which has to be paid if the wife dies before the _lobola_ was paid. e.g. Moonga wakapegwa mali manji akukwa _cilindi_ naakafwa mwinakwe. Moonga was paid a lot of money when his daughter died as the _lobola_ had not been paid.
a state of sitting and waiting for a long time, e.g. Ndafwa _cilindizi_ walo ngwelindila tabooli kufwambaana. = I am tired of waiting and the one I am waiting for does not come quickly.
a blind snake, e.g. Ooyu weenda mbuli _cilingalinga_. = This one walks like a blind snake. Mutacijayi _cilingalinga_ nobana, tacilumi. Children, do not kill the blind snake, it is harmless.

a person who does things without thinking, e.g. Muntu oyu _ncilingalinga_ uide kucita kufwumbwa naba mwana ncaamwa-ambila. This person is like a blind snake, s/he just does whatever s/he is told even by a child.

a shroud or cloth for wrapping around a person who is alive or dead, e.g. Mulwazi mumuputaile mucili_putaizyo_ cili amulenga wazisani. Wrap the patient in a shawl which is on the clothes-rack _ciliputizyo_ a hood, e.g. Kondipa cili_putizyo_ cangu. Give me my head-cover.
a screen protection from wind, e.g. Tweelede kuyaka _cilisitilizyo_ nkaambo mpeyo iyanda kutalika. We ought to build a screen-barrier because the cold season is about to start.

medicine for protecting oneself against witchcraft, pl. _zilisitilizyo_, e.g. _Cilisitilizyo_ cazyeelo mbaa nacalwa. The medicine for protection against the evil spirits is nacalwa. Bamadaala banji balijisi _zilisiti-_ _lizyo_ kutegwa kabataloogwi kufwambaana. Many old men have charms to protect themselves so that they are not easily bewitched.

relish which supplememts the basic food, e.g. Ino sunu bana bangu tulalisya _cilisyo_ nzi? Now today, my children, what relish can we use? Ndalomba _cilisyo_ nkaambo nsima ndajika kale. I am asking for relish because I have already cooked the _nsima_.
an excuse, e.g. Kalonda kaya caba _cilitamizyo_ cakutaunka kucikolo. That scratch has become an excuse for not going to school.

a wooden head-rest used in the past as a pillow, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kubelesya *cilitulisyo* nibakalikoona. = Long ago the people used a traditional wooden head-rest when they were sleeping. Also cuuno camuseko.
a pillow, e.g. e.g. Butonje mbwendabelesya kubamba *cilitulisyo*. = It is cotton which I have used to make a pillow.
a type of bird, the lark, e.g. *Ciliwe* nciyuni cikondelezya nocilila. = The lark is a bird which causes delight when it sings.

a young uninitiated girl before puberty, pl. *ziliya*, e.g. Wamita cicili *ciliya* mwanaangu. = My daughter has been impregnated when still uninitiated. Kaindi cakali kutondwa kuti *ciliya* camita. = Long ago it was taboo for an uninitiated girl to become pregnant. *Ziliya* mbasimbi bayanda kusika mumisela. = *Ziliya* are girls who are about to become of age.
indemnity, security against damage or loss, compensation, e.g. Bakandilungila nombe yomwe *yaciliyo*. = They paid me one cow for damages.
a trace, identification, e.g. Musune wakabbigwa ulaa *cilizyibyo* kumatwi. = The ox which was stolen has an identification mark on the ears.
a funeral gift, e.g. Kaindi inombe ncecakali *cilizyo* cabantu bakaboola mumadilwe. = Long ago a cow was the gift which people brought who came to a funeral.
a manner of crying, e.g. *Cilizyo* camucembele oyu cileetezya. = The way that old woman weeps is pitiful.
an uncomfortable sleeping place, a bad bed, e.g. *Cilo* cako ncibi. = Your bed is bad. *Cilo* camunene cakabumbwa. = The old man's bed has been destroyed by termites.

excess of rain, flooding, e.g. Zyafwa zisyango *acilobe*. = The crops were destroyed by the heavy rain. Mwaka umwi kwakali *cilobe* mucisi cesu akaambo kakuwa kapati mvwula. = One year the land was flooded in our area because the rain fell heavily.
a type of bird, the barred owl, e.g. Masiku ainda kwali kulila *cilola* mumango. = Last night there was a barred owl hooting in the mango trees. Also ceebarnombe, ifwulampeyo, ifwibampeyo.
the medium of a witch which has a distorted animal form and which is fed by the witch. e.g. *Cilomba* ca mulozi cakalumwa mubwa. = The medium of the witch was attacked by a dog. Also domba

a petition, e.g. *Cilombo* cakulombela baciswa catola ciindi kapati mucikombelo akaambo kabantu baciswa bakalomba kulombelwa. = The petition for the sick took a long time in the chapel because of the sick people who asked to be prayed for.
the hot, dry season, e.g. Ciindi cacilomo kunyina mvwula. = There is no rain during the dry season. Also cilimo.
a disfigured lip, e.g. *Cilomo* camwana cilibbebbenyene. = The child's disfigured lip is folded up.
a worn plough-blade, e.g. Koya ukandeetele *cilomo* cajamba ndifwule keembe. = Go and bring me the worn out plough-blade so that I forge an axe.
a wound/sore/ulcer, e.g. Akuulu ndaa *cilonda* citamani. = I have an incurable sore on my leg. Also cicisa.
a pot for cooking any kind of food, e.g. Mukalombe *cilongo* kubacembele kutegwa tujikile cibwantu. = Ask the old woman for a cooking pot so that we brew light beer. Also cibiya.
eternal, e.g. Banji baya kuloba *cilongo* muzyolelwa mukalambwe kamulilo. = Many will perish in the eternal fires of hell.
friendship, e.g. Moomba asuIwe bakajisi *cilongwe* cizuunyene. = The turkey-buzzard and the hare had an enduring friendship.

a dream, e.g. Masiku nindali koona ndalota *ciloto* cakujaigwa. = At night when I was sleeping, I dreamt about being killed. *Ciloto* cakwe cakali cakuti bana bakwe abakomenzye amulyango omwe alimwi kabakumbetene mbuli babunyina kakunyina kusalaulana. = His dream was that his children would grow up in one home and again embracing one another in fellowship without favouritism.
witchcraft, e.g. Ooyu muntu ulaa meso *acilozilozi* alabalangala akuyoosya kapati. = This person has the eyes of witchcraft which are transparent and terrifying. Also bulozi.
an evil spirit, pl. *zilube*, e.g. Bantu banjilwa *zilube* balayoba nizizwa muli mbabo. = People possessed by *zilube* spirits, shout as they come out of them. Also cilubi, ceelo.

that which terrifies, e.g. Mubwa ulya wandilanga ameso *acilubulubu* mbuli kuti wasondoka. = That dog looked at me with eyes that terrified me as if it was mad. Nzala yakaindi yakali ya *cilubulubu*, yasunu tiikonzyi kweezyanizigwa anjiyo. = The hunger of the past was terrible, the hunger of today cannot be compared to it.
a thing which is forgotten e.g. Baneene bakandaambila cintu *cilubwa*. = My grandmother told me something which is forgotten.
forgetfulness, e.g. Mundiyeeyezye kukabweza kasako kangu nkaambo mebo ndilaa *cilubya*. = Remind me to take my stick with me because I am forgetful.
a coop for chickens, e.g. Bana bakukula *aciluku* cankuku. = The children are sweeping the chicken coop.
a roof, e.g. *Ciluli* cananda cilazwizya kapati. = The roof is leaking very badly.
a thanksgiving prayer, e.g. Umwi akati kanu atupe *cilumbu*. = Let one among you give us a prayer. Also cilumbo, cilombo.
a roan antelope, pl. *bacilumbulumbu*, e.g. Cifwumofwumo kwainda tanga lyabacilumbulumbu mumyuunda. = In the morning a herd of roan antelope passed through the fields. Also lumpelembe, nkwalata.

male descendants, e.g. Swebo mbotwakali kuba tuzyalwa buyo *cilumiceenze*, tunyina bacizi, tuli basankwa balo. = We since we were born have only had male descendants, we have no sisters, we are only men.

a bite, the custom when mourning by which male members of the relatives of the dead person, bite a piece of meat specially cooked for the funeral and spit it out again. e.g. Eeyi nyama nja*cilumo*, mubape bana boonse balume. = This meat is for ritual biting, (i.e. you bite it and spit it out again), give it to the children so that they can bite it. (This ritual is carried out by those who did not attend the funeral who ask the spirit of the deceased not to come to disturb them.)
payment to make medicine work, e.g. Munanga wakati, "Kondipa buyo kkumi lyazyuulu zyamakkwacca, cibe *ncecilumyo* camusamu". = The witchdoctor said, "Just give me K10,000 so that the medicine works."
a type of tree, e.g. Mucilunda omuya muli cinteente cakayuni. = In that tree over there there is the nest of a little bird.

simple form of traditional drafts with stones, e.g. Oyu mwana mbwatazyi misyobo minji-minji yansolo kabaide kusobana musyobo omwe biyo utasyupi, *wacilundika.* = As this child did not know the many different types of drafts, they just played one simple type called cilundika. (Bakali kuunga aumwi wasala cilindi comwe cakulundikila mabwe anikweenda. Umwi ayenda akulala wakali kulekela mweenzinyina kweenda. Pele mbubonya obo bakali kuya. Aboobo oyo wakali kufwambaana kwaamanizya mabwe akwe kwaabikka mucilindi, nguwakali kujaya cisolo)
a low hill or mound, e.g. Tuya kukucela bowa *kucilundu* cokwa Mainza. = We are going to collect mushrooms at the hill of Mainza.

a cake of tobacco, e.g. Ndakasankamuna cikata catombwe kuti mbambe *cilundu.* = I took a handful of a bundle of tobacco so that I could make it into a cake. Bataata ndabaulila *cilundu catombwe.* = I bought my father a cake of tobacco.

a type of snake, the horned adder, e.g. Beembela bajaya *cilundula.* = The herders killed a horned adder. Inombe zyosanwe zyakajaigwa anzoka yiitwa kuti *cilundula.* = Five cows were killed by a snake called a 'horned adder.' Eeyi nkoli yakazambaidwe nzoka yakubeza itegwa *cilundula.* = The stick was entwined with a carved snake which is called the horned adder.
a group of hills, a hilly area, pl. *zilundulundu,* e.g. Eeyi nyika njotulima *njacilundulundu.* = The land we are cultivating is hilly.
the fixed posture of looking upwards, e.g. Mulwazi ukkede muciimo *cacilungamo.* = The patient is sitting in a fixed position looking upwards.
a rack, e.g. *Acilungamo* bakali kwaanzika tupanga a misako yakulwanya. = They were hanging blades and sticks for fighting on a rack.
a type of snake, the horned adder, short jumping, said to kill cattle, e.g. Umwi mweembezi wakalumwa *cilungula.* = One shepherd was bitten by an adder. Also *cilundula*
noon, e.g. Izuba lyasika *acilungulungu,* mundaambile kutegwa nkasambe. When it is noon-time, tell me so that I can go and wash.
a feast of meat, e.g. Kunkolola kwali pobwe *lyaciluvwu-luvwu.* = At the initiation ceremony there was a feast of meat.
eating meat in an impolite manner, e.g. Bakali kulya nyama *muciluvwu-luvwu.* = They were eating meat in an impolite manner.
an angry mood, e.g. Basimbi caba *ciluwu-luvwu* nibaandana nkaambo banyemezyanya. The girls parted in an angry mood because they annoyed one another.
an island, e.g. Inswi twalikuzilobela *kuciluzi* cili kumbo mumulonga. = We have been fishing from the island on the western side of the river. Also *cciluzi, kasumbu.*
what is right, e.g. Mwana utaciti *ciluzi* ulatongookwa lyoonse abazyali bakwe. = A child who does not do what is right is always complained about by his/her parents.
an illness or disease, e.g. Mazuba ainda aya ndali kuciswa *cilwazi*
During these past days I have been suffering from the illness of diarrhoea.

an evil omen, e.g. *Cilwezya* cacitika kumuunda candiyoosya nkaambo musune mubombe walitondezya bukali mbwataciti lyoonse. = An evil omen which occured at the field terrified me, a meek ox behaved in a fierce manner which it never does.
a heap, pile, e.g. Mulundike buyo *cilwi* camapopwe comwe. = Collect just one heap of maize.
a weapon, e.g. Ijamba lyamaanza *ncilwisyo cakugusya nsaku mumuunda.* = A hoe is a weapon in the fight to remove weeds with in the field.
cannabis, e.g. Cisubulo cipati cilaboola kumwana unywa bukoko antela ufweba *cilyabayuni.* = Big punishment comes to the youth who drinks beer or smokes dagga. Also *lubanje*
type of bush fruit, e.g. *Cilyabeembela mmucelo uligwa kapati a beembela nombe.* = *Cilyabeembela* is a fruit which is eaten by cattle herders.
inside part of cattle, a stomach, e.g. *Cilyabeembela caamba cibeela cimwi cili mukati kanombe.* = *Cilyabeembela* means a certain part which is within a cow. Also *ceembelelo*
a spirit-gate, e.g. Basimasabe baalilwa kunjila *acilyango kumalende.* = Those possessed with masabe spirits were unable to pass through the spiritgate of the rain-shrine.

a spirit-gate, a passage for the spirits, a funeral responsibilty of the bamausyi or father's clan of the dead person, e.g. Muntu ukkala *kucilyangu* ciindi cadilwe uyanda kukona. = A person who sits at the spirit-gate during the funeral, wants to inherit wealth.
the sole of a shoe, e.g. *Cilyato cabbusu lyangu cakatyoka.* = The sole of my shoe is broken.
a glutton, e.g. Eeci cana *ncilyato ncocineneede.* = This child is a glutton, that is why it is fat. Also *mulyato.*
a footprint, e.g. Nceeci *cilyato* camuntu wandibbida mapopwe mumuunda wangu. = Here is the footprint of a person who stole maize from my field. Also *matende, mano.*
habit of eating anything, e.g. Eeci *cilyelyeelye ncibi.* = This habit of eating anything that is set before you is bad.
food, e.g. Sunu ndali kulya *cilyo cibotu kapati.* = Today I was eating excellent food.
a resting place, e.g. Nitwasika *acilyookezyezyo cesu twalyookezya.* = When we reached our resting place we took a break.
eating in a disorderly manner, e.g. Ncibi kulya cimaccu-maccu. = It is bad to eat in a careless manner. Also *cimwanku-mwanku*
a bribe concerning adultery, e.g. Uulya mwaalumi wakapa mukamuntu mali *acimambi.* = That man gave money to another man's wife as an agreement to adultery.
a patch on clothes, e.g. Buluke bwangu bweelede kubikkwa *cimami mpubwakapya.* = A patch should be put on the place where my trousers got burnt. Also *cigamba, cimamo.*

a patch, pl. *zimamo,* e.g. Acalo *cimamo* cagondo lyabuluke bwangu cakazauka. = Even the patch of the knee of my trousers got torn. Musimbi ulandikaka akaambo kazisani nzyesama zilaa *zimamo.* = The girl rejected me because of the clothes I wear which are full of patches. Also *cigamba, cimami.*

handle for hot iron thongs, an instrument for picking hot things from the fire, e.g. Kobelesya *cimanisyo* kujata musyisyi wajamba nkaambo ulapya. = Use a thongs to pick the blade of the hoe because it is hot. Also *cimakizyo, lumano, lulwasyi, lukwasyo.*
a partner in adultery, e.g. *Cimansa* cileta bunjaka mumunzi. = Adultery brings enmity to the village. Also *cimambi.*
a child who is starting to walk, e.g. *Cimatakweenda* koonse kubumba nsima tacizi. A child who is beginning to walk does not know how to mould the nsima to eat.
scab on sheep or calves, e.g. *Toonse toombe tulaa cimbalangwe*. = All the calves are infected with a scab disease. Also cigwegwe, cigwenyembe, cimbeembe.
lorry, an open van or pick-up, e.g. *Cimbayambaya cajisi mubili wamuntu wakafwa cabbeuka*. = The truck carrying the body of a dead person overturned.
scab on sheep or calves, e.g. *Ndali kuula musamu wacimbeembe*. = I had gone to buy medicine for the scab disease. Also cigwegwe, cimbalangwe
tadpole, pl. bacimbilimbimba, e.g. *Bacimbilimbimba bazyalwa kapati ciindi camainza*. Tadpoles are spawned in great abundance during the rains.
a sjambok, whip, e.g. *Bamasilikani babelesya cimboko kuumya bantu batyola milawo*. = The police use a whip to beat people who break the law.

sweet part of green mealie or sorgum stalk, pl. *zimbololo*, e.g. *Mwaunka kumuunda, mukandiletelezye acimbololo cakulya*. When you go to the field, bring me the sweet part of a maize stalk to eat. *Zimbololo zyakatalika kuyuma-yuma*. = The sweet part of the mealies began to dry up. Also *insinde*
stalk bearing no grain, e.g. *Uno mwaka makuba manji akaba zimbololo*. = This year many stalks had no cobs.
a small type of bee which makes honey in the ground in places called mabuwa, e.g. *Tuya kukulida cimbolombomu*. = We are going to collect honey from the *cimbolombomu* bee. Also sikaulu, syaansi.
mumps, e.g. *Mwanaangu uciswa cimbolomu*. = My child has the mumps. *Mwana wabolomana nkwaciswa cimbolomu*. The child was swollen because it was sick with the mumps.
eye-socket without eye, e.g. *Ndakwata musimbi ulaa cimbolyo*. = I am married to a girl with one eye missing.
pride in good looks, finery, style, outward appearance, e.g. *Mwiiyi wabulimi ulaa cimbonyo-bonyo*. = The agricultural instructor dresses in style. Also mambonwa.
any round object, e.g. *Mweene ulaa cimbulunga camutwe*. = Mweene has a round head.
the stage before puberty, e.g. *Ooyu musimbi wakamita cimbulwe*. = This girl conceived before the natural time.

conception before normal monthly period starts while breast feeding, e.g. *Mukaintu ulya ncagonka bana umita cimbulwe*. = The reason why that woman weans her childen quickly is because she conceives before her normal monthly period.

a toilet, e.g. *Omuya mucimbuzi kuli nzinini zinji*. = In that toilet there are many flies. *Uli biyo mbuli nombe iitacizyi acimbuzi kuti cili kuli?* = You are like a cow which doesn't know where the toilet is.
means of communication, e.g. *Mumiteende, muli sikapepele amuzimbwakata moonse, nguwe walo uyoomwa*. In the newspapers, on the wireless and in all the media, he is the one who is being talked about.
a traditional stool, e.g. *Basicikolo balicizyi kufwala zyuuno zyacimbwalakasa*. The school children know how to carve traditional stools.

a sweet potatoe, e.g. *Uuno mwaka tuyanda kuya kusimpa cimbwali cinji*. = This year we want to go and plant plenty of sweet potatoes. imbata = red; kambala or kandolo = grey; bupapa = cooked, sliced and dried; other names of sweet potato: _kalya-balumi, kapili_.

a cloth for covering the hips, skin with corners off, a measure of cloth, e.g. _Cimbwambwa camulembo eco ncaksusumina mwana cisani_. = This length of cloth is for sewing a child's dress. _Mucembele ngwindakaswaanya jilo wakasamide cimbwambwa_. = The old woman who I met yesterday was dressed in a cimbwambwa.
plant used to heal sores on anus, e.g. _Mwana ulaa zicisa kumutako, mukamuside cimbwelele wakumusilisya_. = Dig cimbwelele roots to heal the child who has sores on its anus.
a crawling insect, e.g. _Ndajana cimbwide ukalaba munsi ameenda_. = I found an insect crawling near the river.
the beloved, e.g. _Ndilembalugwalo kuli cimeko wangu_. = I am writing a letter to my sweetheart.
signs to attract, e.g. _Musimbi ulaa cimeko uongelezya basankwa_. = A girl who who uses signs entices boys.
a feather beginning to come out, e.g. _Tukuku twakatalika kumena cimenenwa_. = The chicks have started to produce their feathers. Also _kafwintila_.
a succulent, sweet or tasty thing ('make the mouth water'), e.g. _Musiikka upa kubaa cimenyamate nokuba kuti tonaulya_. = Musiikka fruit makes the mouth water even though you have not yet eaten it.
a stump, e.g. _Kulinontola acimfwumpu cilacisa kapati_. = To trip over a stump can be very painful.
the back when bent inwards, e.g. _Mukaintu wainda waalya ulaa cimini_. = The woman who passed there has a bent back.

a goat given in compensation by a boy who has made a girl pregnant, e.g. _Musankwa wakamisya mwanaanu uyakuleta cimisye-misye cifwumo_. = The boy who made your daughter pregnant is bringing a goat to-morrow. Also _cimisemisya_
scent, smell, odour, e.g. _Aansi onse akacaala aile buyo kununka cimoko camulilo wamvwula_. = All over the ground was just left the smell of the fire of the lightning.

agility, e.g. _Musimbi wamunjanda kunyina ambi mpalangwa kunze kwakulangamicito acimoko camumagondo akwe_. = As regards a woman of the house (a permanent wife) there is nothing else which needs to be considered apart from her deeds and the agility of her knees. (i.e. What matters is that she is a hard worker.)
infertile sorgum plant, pl. _zimololo_, e.g. _Bana balya zimololo mu-muunda_. = The children are eating plants in the field. Also _cimbololo_.
a carbuncle, e.g. _Ndabaa cimonko atako_. = I have a carbuncle on a buttock.
a pinch, pl. _zimoni_, e.g. _Kamwale bakali kumusyamba zimoni mujanda kavwundikidwe_. = They used to pinch the initiate when she was in seclusion.

a type of edible leaf or flower, a spinach type of relish eaten in the rainy season, e.g. _Tulaleteleezya cimowa caku-jika twazyila kumuunda_. = We will bring along cimowa relish when we come from the field.
a beaded head, e.g. _Bamwi bamanjanga basama cimpaampwa kumitwe_. = Some witchdoctors wear beads on their heads.
a piece, e.g. _Kondipa cimpaanzi calingo_. = Give me a piece of mango. _Komukomweda cimpaanzi camuungu mwana_. = Break off a piece of pumpkin for the child. Also cipaanzi.

a crown of beads, pl. zi-mpalimba, e.g. *Mwami wesu usama cimpalimba kumutwe.* = Our chief wears a crown of beads. *Bakamwale bakaindi bakali kusama zimpalimba mumitwe.* = The initiates of long ago were wearing crowns of beads on their heads.
a piece of wood, e.g. *Kondigonkela cimpampansya.* = Cut a piece of wood for me.
artifact, e.g. *Zimpang-aliko zya Butonga zyakalubwa.* = The artifacts of Tonga culture have been forgotten.
a prodigy, e.g. *Musankwa ulaa cimpanganyiko ulalibonya mumbusongo bwakwe.* = A talented child is recognized through its intelligence.

insolence, rudeness, pride, impertinence, e.g. *Taakwe naakali kubateelela bapati. Ciindi coonse wakali acimpangwe.* = He never obeyed the elders. All the time he was insolent. *Ooyu musune ulaa cimpangwe.* = This ox is un-cooperative.
a head-cloth, e.g. *Bacembele basamide cimpaninga.* = The old woman is wearing a head-scarf.
a broken piece of calabash used for eating, e.g. *Mubwa umusaninine mucimpanzi.* = Feed the dog in the broken calabash. Also cipaanzi, cimpaanzi, cipapa.
a cattle kraal, e.g. *Tuyanda kubamba cimpati.* = We want to make a kraal. Also ciba, luba.
a pen for sheep or goats, e.g. *Kamuzinjizya mpongo mucimpatya.* = Bring the goats into the enclosure. Also ibbondo.
a desert, e.g. *Mu cimpayuma kanji-kanji kunyina bwizu azisamu zikomena kabotu.* = Usually in a desert no grass nor trees can grow well.

a type of tree (Ozoroa retulata), white latex exudes from broken leaf-stalks and damaged bark exudes drops of creamy resin, a gum can be obtained from the fruit, and there are medicinal uses for roots, leaves and bark, but overdoses are reputed to be fatal. e.g. *Nkucenjela kunywinsya mulwazi musamu wacimpempe.* = It is necessary to be careful when giving a patient medicine from the *cimpempe* tree. Also *musambwe*.

underwater cave, e.g. *Inswi nozibakakila bantu kujata muziba, balaziba kuti cigwinta nkwali kucimpetu caziba, unyonyonganya nswi nzibayanda kujata.* = When the fish prevent people from catching them in the pool, the people realize that there is a *cingwinta* fish in a corner of the pool which agitates the fish which they want to catch.

trace of a tear, pl. *zimpololo*, e.g. *Beenzinyina nobakabona zimpololo kumeso bakazyiba kuti wakali kuya bulila kale.* = When his friends saw the traces of tears on his face they knew that he had been going along crying. Also *mibbyolombyombyo*
a measuring rule, e.g. *Cimpimisyo camapopwe mazuba ano tacili cibotu.* = The way of measuring maize nowadays is not just.

moveable pole used for shutting entrance to kraal, e.g. *Musune naasotoka kuzwa anze, cimpingili comwe cakatyoka.* = When the ox jumped out of the kraal, one pole was broken. *Kokkala awo acimpingili, utani kuyoowi nokuba kulisenda.* = Sit there on the pole of the gate, do no be afraid or embarrassed. Also *mucinjiili*.
a child born feet first, e.g. *Ooyu mwana ngucimpini.* = This child was born feet first. Also *cipini, cibuno*.
a short piece of wire, e.g. Kondipa cimpiningila caluwayile, ngange cijazyo amulyango. = Give me that short piece of wire, I want to tie the door.
devastation, e.g. Mudaala wakabaa cimpobe naakamvwa makani ayoosya alya. The old man was devastated when he heard that terrible news. Also cindebwe
side of the head, e.g. Chimuka wakaumwa cisamu mucimpobe ncicakacengama. Chimuka was struck by a stick on the side of the head, that is why it is dented.
pl. zimpuka, evil spirit of the dead, witch's creature, dangerous reptile or insect. e.g. Cimpuka ncecimupa kujaya bantu. It is an evil spirit which causes him to kill people.
deafness, e.g. Baneene bakaba cimpuku nkaambo kakukomena. = My grandmother has become deaf because of old-age. Also cuulutwi.

manevolent spirit, pl. zimpuku, e.g. Cimpuku kuti casulama tacizwi nocuumpizigwa. If the manevolent spirit turns downwards it does not come out even when it is fumigated, (If a cimpuku spirit has dwelt in a person for a long time, it is difficult to expel it.) Also ceelo, cilube, cipuku.

a mutilated toe, e.g. Mweenzyi wacitima wakanyongolwa minwe yakumaulu acibulo canjanji aboobo wakaba cimpunyu. = The driver of the train had his toes damaged on the railway track and as a result he has a mutilated toe.

a stump of a finger or a toe, e.g. Ooyu musankwa tajisi minwe kucituta, kwakacaala cimpunyunyu. This boy has no toes on his foot, a stump remained. = cimpwampwa animal skin, bald patches, e.g. Eezi mpongo zilaa cimpwampwa amibili. These goats have bald patches on their bodies. Also cinkwankwa.

arm with hand cut off, mutilated finger, e.g. Uulya musankwa ncaide kuwa akaambo kakukolwa ngucimpyunyunyu. = That boy who just falls down because of being drunk, has only one arm. = cimuma a dumb person. e.g. Amumuvwiile cimuma ngooyu ulaamba. Answer the dumb person he is saying something. Also cimuumu.
a low bush bearing an abundance of black berries on the ground in October and November, the fruit is mumbu, e.g. Cisyiko cacimumbu cakasyuuka. The blackberry bush has new shoots. Also kasiko kamumba
a large bottle-shaped grain-bin, e.g. Wakanjila mucimumbwa akugwisya nzembwe yakutwa. = She entered the bottle grain bin and took out grey millet for pounding.
den of crocodile, e.g. Mumwaka wadanga umwi, zilyo zyaciwena zyakamana mucimumbwa cakwe. In a certain year of drought, the food of a crocodile was finished in its den.
a dumb person, e.g. Cilakatazya kwaambaula amuntu cimuuma. = It is difficult to talk with a dumb person.

a bottle grain-bin, e.g. Mapopwe aali mucimuumbwa akabola. = The maize which is in the bottle grain-bin rotted. Mumwaka umwi wadanga zilyo zyaciwena zyakamana mucimuumbwa cakwe. In a certain year of famine the food got finished in the grain-store of the crocodile. Also cimumbwa.
madness, e.g. Cimuunyu cakwe mwana oyu cimupa kulya tubi twakwe. The insanity of this child makes it eat its own excrement.
a mixture of masuku juice and sour milk, e.g. Musinza wamasuku wakali kuvwelwa amabisi caba _cimvwe_. = The juice of masuku fruit was mixed with sour milk to become a cocktail.

white hair, e.g. Tazili mvwi zyabupati pe, eci swebo tuciita kuti 'ncimvwibala'. Naceya muntu ulakonzya kumena _cimvwibala_, mbocibele ncamumukowa. They are not the white hairs of old age, we say that this thing is ncimwibala. No matter how young a person the hair can go white, that is how it is, it is a clan characteristic.
a shady place, e.g. Wakakkala mucimvwiide akupumuna. = She sat in the shade and rested. Also _cimvwule_
type of relish, e.g. Insima bakasunsya silende abacimvwinye. = They dipped the nsima into the silende and _cimvwinye_ relish.
a type of beetle, e.g. Bacimvwinye balilya mizindo. These kind of beetles eat their own anuses.
a shadow, a shady place, e.g. Alubuwa lokwesu kunyina _cimvwule_
At our court-yard there is no good place for shade. Also cinzwiide, _cimvwiide_.
an edible green insect, e.g. Bana bajata _cimvwunyu_. = The children are collecting green edible insects.
a door made of reeds, e.g. Bacembele bajazya _cimwenye_ acaanda cabo. The old woman closes her house with a grass-reed door. Also iswaaswa, cisengezi, citendele.
shade, e.g. Twali kulyookezya mucimwide. We were relaxing in the shade. Also _cimvwule_.
a green pidgeon, e.g. Ndajaya _cimwanga_. I have killed a green pidgeon. Also inkwilinti, cikwilinti.
partner in adultery, e.g. Mazubaano ajisi ntenda kubaa _cimwansa_. = There is a danger in modern times of being a partner in adultery. Also cimansa, cimambe.
shining fat at the lips after eating an oily meal, e.g. Koya usambe _cimwe_ kumulomo. Go and wash the fat off your mouth. Also _cimwengela_

a thing which glistens, pl. zimwengela, e.g. Waakubujana kuli bwaawo bwanyama busakamuna mate mukanwa? Toonse twaba azimwengela kumilomo. Where did you find such meat which makes the mouth water? We will all have shining lips. Also _cimwe_.
a dumb person, pl. bacimwinye, e.g. _Bacimwinye_ balamvwana akati kabo. = Dumb people communicate among themselves. Also cimuunye, cuumunye.
indigestion, also a pain in the stomach caused by emotional upset, e.g. Ndaciswa _cimyongela_. = I have indigestion.
colic, e.g. _Cimyongola_ cilacisa kapati. = Colic hurts terribly. Also _cimyongela_
colic, indigestion emotional pain, e.g. Ooyu mwana cimulizya ncimyonzi. = This child is crying with colic pains.
emblem, sign, image, a teaching aid, e.g. Bana baiya mubbuku taanzi beelede kubelesyelwa _cinaanizyo_
The children in Grade One should be taught through the teaching aid. Also cilubukizyo.

medicine given by husband to another man who is trying to have sexual relations with his wife, e.g. Moomba wakateegwa _cinaili_ ncatacikonzyi kusobana amukaintu wakwe. Moomba was caught by the _cinaili_ charm so that he was unable to have sex with his own wife.
a gramophone, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kukonzya kusobanya _cinakakwakwa_ bakali basyoonto. = Long ago there were very few people who were able to play the gramaphone. Also mulenga.
light beer, e.g. Kunkolola twanywa buyo cinamala. = At the initiation we only drank light beer. Also cibwantu, mazyewu, bbwatu.
a type of tree, e.g. Bamwaaba balya mbula mucinamalama. = The jackals eat mbula fruit in the cinamalama tree. Also cinamalambwa, cinyamwaba.
numbers, e.g. Cinambala coonse bakacibbatula. = They removed all the numbers.

a weaved container for carrying various things, e.g. Ndisuma cinampwido. = I am stitching a bag for carrying things. e.g. Nceeci cinampwido ubwezele ndongwe. = Here is a container with which you can carry the groundnuts. Also cinyampwido, cinamwido, cinyamwido.
a whitish termite, e.g. Bana basobana cinanabasimbi. = The children are playing with the white termites. Also cikonga.
a honeycomb in ground formed by black insects, e.g. Nobali kusya bulongo acuulu, kwajanika cinanabasimbi. = When they were digging an anthill a honey comb was found.
leprosy, e.g. Bantu baciswa cinanta bakkala balikke. The people with leprosy live in isolation. Also cinsenda, ciswaya, mulilo wa Leza.
a dwarf, short bushman, e.g. Nitwali kweenda mumugwagwa twaswaangana cinasimpiningile aboobo twayoowa. When we were walking on the road we met a dwarf and so we were afraid.

a thorny wild nut, pl. zincenya, e.g. Ndayaswa cincenya kunsi akuulu. = I have been pierced on the sole of the foot by a thorny wild nut. Nyika kumena buyo zincenya. = The land is only producing thorny wild nuts. Ntolongo wakaseka kumwi kadingeme kulijwa cincenya. = Ntolongo laughed while bending down to extract a thorn. Also cincenga

fear of punishment, a paralyizing fear, trembling due to sickness or weakness, e.g. Ndabaa cindebwe nindamvwa undiita mbuli kuti mbaataata. = I felt fear when I heard someone calling me as if it was father. Also cintebwe, cimpobe.

a portion, e.g. Mubikke cindinina cameenda mucibulo. = Pour some water in the bucket. Isaka lyakazwide mapopwe kwacaala cindinina calo, manji abbigwa. = The sack which was full of maize has only a little remaining, much has been stolen. Also cidinina.

a type of millet, e.g. Kuti koyanda kulya cindobe nkusaanguna kusyubula nzembwe wamana uzibikke mumeenda atontola. Uzitole aziyo akutalika kuziya kumwi kotila atweenda tusyoonto kutegwa kaciteteeta. Wamana kucita boobo inga wabikka tuccukela tusyoonto akutalika kulya. If you want to eat cindobe you pound nzembwe and then you put in a little cold water. You take it to the grinding stone and begin to grind while you are pouring in the little water to make it soft. When you are finished that you put a little sugar and begin to eat.
a groundnut plot, pl. zindongo, e.g. Balimi balalima zindongo azilili zyalutanga. Farmers plough groundnut plots and alluvial gardens for planting pumpkins. Also cindongwe.
a groundnut plot cindubwa forgetfulness, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu ulaa cindubwa. = This woman is inclined to forget. Also cindubya, cilubya.
scrap, e.g. Utabikki cindulundulu abulo bwako. = Don't put the scrap on your bed.
a luggage, e.g. Kondigwasya kubweza *cindunduli* *eci*. = Help me carry this luggage. Also *cibbudu*
a jar, e.g. *Kobikka meenda akunywa mucinembwa*. = Put the drinking water in the jar.
pubes, lower part of abdomen covered with pubic hair from puberty. *Ndakalumwa cuuka acinena*. = I have been bitten by an insect on the lower part of my abdomen.
an antbear, e.g. *Sunu bavwimi bajaya cinengwa*. = The hunters killed an antbear today. Also *sicinengwe*.
something slender, waist, e.g. *Doombwana wakalimukumbete mucinengu mukaintu*. = Doombwana embraced the woman about the waist.
a drum used for liquids, e.g. *Mubikke cingololo mucikkocci mukatekele meenda*. = Put the drum in the scotchcart so that you can go and draw water. Also *cingongoolo*.

a large stinking bug often found in deserted kraals and in pumpkin vines, pl. *bacingulungungwa*, e.g. *Kununka cingulungungwa mucisyu omu*. = There is the stink of a large bug within the relish. *Lungu balumana bacingulungungwa*. = The stinking insects have finished the pumpkin leaves.

a dustbin, e.g. *Bacisikolo beelede kutila cingungulu buzuba abuzuba*. = The school children should empty the dustbin daily. *cinguni* stubbourness, rebelliousness, disobedience, e.g. *Ulaa cinguni* = He is stubbourn.
an instrument used for digging a hole, e.g. *Eeci cingwala tacibosyi pe*. = This digging instrument is not sharp. Also *cigoyo*.
useless person, e.g. *Kamucaala nobacingwindi*. = Good bye you useless people.

the liver, e.g. *Mwamana kufwunda mpongo, cini mubayokele bana balye*. = When you are finished skining the goat, roast the liver for the children to eat. Also *muni*. (also used as adjective, e.g. Chitonga *cini-cini* = true or genuine Chitonga)
Alsouni*

a method of divining where two suspects place spittle on their thumbs and where flies alight on the guilty one. e.g. *Mebo ndilizi nzila yakusonda imwi mfwiifwi, iitegwa cininaanzi, iikonzya kubelesegwa mumanjaka*. = I know a method of divining called *cininaanzi* which can be used to remove dissension. (where the two suspects each place spittle on their thumbs and flies alight on the guilty one to end the quarrels.)
inter-penetration, e.g. Chitonga ncobakanana cilivwelengene amyaambo yacinjilane-njilane. = The Chitonga which they speak is mixed up with various foreign words.
dry, stiff inedible porridge, e.g. *Mucipe babwa cinkalantu*. = Give the dried up porridge to the dogs. Also *makololo*.

a traditional cream for anointing body or skin-cloth, made of musikili seeds which were roasted and crushed, e.g. *Wakananika ngoma zyakwe acinkanda*. = He rubbed his drums with cream. *Cinkanda bakali kumwiita kuti mwido akaambo kakusiya kwawo*. = They used to call this cream *mwido* because of its black colour. *Zimwi nseke musimbi ulacita cinkanda wakunanika ngubo zyampongo, zyakusama azyakubbazya bana*. *Insete azyalo zyakali kunanikwa cinkanda*. *Insete bakali kuzisama kungoma akuzipelu basimbi insiku*. = The girl makes the cream from some seeds for smearing goat-skin, clothes and materials for carrying babies on the back. Even the stringed aprons were rubbed with cream long ago. The girls used to wear the stringed aprons for the ngoma and cipelu dances.
Also *cinkandangilo*

insolence and bad-manners, e.g. *Nditakweelebi kukubandikila sunu kutegwa cinkangu cikujisi cikumanine limwi.* = I tell you directly today so that the bad manners which you have may finally leave you.
a clot of dried blood, e.g. *Ndajana cinkanza cabulowa munzila.* = I found a clot of dried blood on the path.
area, pl. *zinkodyo*, e.g. *Twana twasikoswe twakali kweendeenda koonse-koonse kuzinkodyo (kuzyooko) zyananda.* The small rats were moving in all places all over the house.

a plant whose pounded roots are used for smearing and stopping holes in clay pots after burning them before they cool, e.g. *Eezi zibiya muzizile cinkolonkozya.* Smear these pots with the powdered root-mixture.

a large clay pot for cooking vegetables, pl. *zinkomba*, e.g. *Cinkomba cacisyu capwaika.* The big pot for cooking vegetables is broken. *Baama babumba zinkomba.* My mother makes large clay pots for cooking vegetables.

a shrub which provides relish, a relish which becomes slippery when cooked, e.g. *Mulwazi uyandisya kulya cinkomba.* = The patient likes eating the *cinkomba* relish. Also muteezi, lunkomba, mudelele, citezi.
the white of an egg, e.g. *Mwana walya cinkombe caji.* = The child has eaten the white of an egg. Also mungunga utuba, musinda utuba

a scab, dirt or mucous formed when one does not wash for a long time, e.g. *Ciindi camupeyo bana babaa cinkombe amubili nkaambo kakutasamba-samba.* = During the cold season the bodies of children have scabs through lack of regular washing. Also *cikololo* = scab over wound, dried mucous. Also ikwa, inkoonkonde, ibbabbani, ipapa.

an amulet worn around the neck, (a small object that you wear because you believe it will protect you from evil or injury), e.g. *Baama bamusamika cinkonde mwana.* My mother has put an amulet on the child. *Uleelede kuti asowe cinkonde cabwana asame cabupati.* He ought to throw away the amulet of childhood wearing an adult one.
a beaded or straw necklace, pl. *minkonde*, e.g. *Basimbi bakalisamide minkonde munsingo.* = The girls were dressed with beaded necklaces around the neck.
cheap soap, e.g. *Mwatalika kusanzya zisani zyabana mubelesye cinkondya.* When you start washing the children's clothes use *cinkondya* soap.
lumpy food, e.g. *Nsima njajika lyoonse ndibbyo, cinkone, cuungabusu nakuba kuti mukonde.* The meal that she always cooks is under-cooked, lumpy, unstirred flour, or even raw.
what is inherited, e.g. *Kuvwima caba cinkono mumukowa wabo, boonse balavwima.* The activity of hunting has become an inherited trait in their clan, all are hunting. Also cikonano.
a shelled maize-cob, e.g. *Utacisikki cinkonsi eco.* = Do not insert that shelled maize-cob. Also cinkonti.
a shelled maize-cob, e.g. *Cinkonti eco kocisikka mucikko.* = Stick that empty mealie-cob in the fire.
the knuckles, e.g. *Bayi bamuuma cinkonya mumutwe Moonga.* = The teacher beat Moonga with knuckles on the head.
the first dice thrown at divining, e.g. *Ndakawidwa cinkonzi.* = I lost at dice. Also cinokozi.
tendency to become alike, e.g. Kuti mukaintu ulaa da kalaa cinkonzya, tayelede kulanga mulema. = If a pregnant woman is susceptible of taking on likeness, she should not look at a lame person.
spittle, phlegm, e.g. Kuti waswida cinkoolwa, weelede kucivwukkila amamvwu. = If you spit phlegm you should cover it with soil. Also luzingo
a barbed spear, e.g. Ndajana muzezi wanswi uzezya cinkosi. = I found the fisherman fishing with a barbed spear. Also muumba.
dignified behaviour, (ety. Sindebele, nkosi = a dignified person), e.g. Ooyu mwana bulemu bwakwe mbwacinkosi-nkosi. = This child has an honourable disposition. Also cami-cami
a section, as of a field, e.g. Bakabikka bufwumba acinkoso camuunda wakwe. = They put manure on a section of his field. Also cikosolo, cikoso
a picture as used for identity card. e.g. *Cinkosole* cako cakaleka kulibonya kabotu. = The picture on your identity card has faded. Also cinyungu, cinyongole.

a tendency to produce similarity of whatever she looks at, e.g. Ooyu musimbi ulaa cinkonzya, wakazyala mwana ukozya musyoonto wakwe. = This woman tends to reproduce similarity, she bore a child who resembles her younger sibling.

caterpillar, pl. zinkubala, e.g. Wabaa nzi mwana ncayanda kukwata Mu Bemba? Uyanda kutulisya zinkubala twanooyoomuswaya! = Why does the child want to marry a Bemba? He wants us to eat caterpillars when we visit her!
a gourd, an old water calabash, e.g. Kondipa meenda mucinkuli nywe. = Give me water in a gourd so that I drink.

the outcome of divination concerning the cause of death as revealed in the witch-doctor's gourd, e.g. Kudilwe lyamwana batuma bantu bobile baya ku cinkuli. = At the funeral of the child they sent two people to go to the witch-doctor to find the cause of the child's death.
an edible leaf/flower used as relish, e.g. Basimbi baya kukucela cinkulumwanza. = The girls have gone to collect a type of relish.
a thatching grass (Pennistum purpureum), e.g. Inanda eyi yakavwumbizigwa cinkulwe. = This house was thatched with cinkulwe grass.
a place underneath, e.g. Kamuzyaangilila mpongo mucinkuma cabutala. = Tie the goats under the maize granary. Also jungusi
medicine to cure stomach pains Also cinkumwe
medicine to cure stomach pains, e.g. Mwida nimwakali kucisa ndakanywa cinkumwe. = When my stomach was sore I drank medicine. Also cinkumwa
nakedness, e.g. Bantu bansiku bakali kweenda acinkuna. = The people of the past went naked. Also cinswe.

a grain storage container made of bark, mud and grass, a pot for storing solids, e.g. Muzwisye mapopwe mucinkuntu akujika magwaza. = Remove maize from the store to cook magwaza. (maize-grain cooked whole without being pounded) Kwakali zinkuntu zyakuyobweda mabbono maniini-niini anyemu. = There were bark-mud-grass containers for storing castor oil seeds and groundnuts. Also kafwuba.

a strong energetic person, e.g. Ijilo ndakaswaanganya cinkuntumina camusankwa. = Yesterday I met an energetic man. Bubala cakali cinkuntumina camulombwana, sunu wakoka akaambo kabulwazi. = Bubala was a well-built man, today he is thin due to a disease.
a sturdy man, e.g. Moonga naakacili mwana, cakali *cinkutu*. = When Moonga was young he was a sturdy man.

an innocent child, childlike innocence, pl. *zinkuunku*, e.g. Ciimo camwana oyu ncacinkuunku. = This child has an innocent character. Kusonda lufwu Iwamuntu kweelede kutumwa bantu bapati balaa *maanu*, kutali mpwitamamina ezi, *zinkuunku* nzyookatuma. = To divine the death of a person, big people with wisdom ought to be sent, not ones with running noses, innocent children, whom you have sent.
bread, e.g. Mukabape bataata *cinkwa eci*. = Give my father this bread.

type of bird, a garden warbler, e.g. *Cinkwaambila* tacuuluki kapati. A garden warbler does not fly much. Also cikaambilwa. (*Cikwaambilwa cakasowa mwana amukuwa*. = The warber, as it does not fly quickly but rests every now and then was followed by the child of a whiteman. The child thought it could catch it because of its slow movement. But it went on and on until the child was lost.)
the mange, a scab, e.g. *Cinkwaankwa mbulwazi bwampongo*. = The mange is a disease of goats. Also *cinkwankwa*.
a mask, e.g. Mwana wali kuyoowa *cinkwamu* casamide Muuma. = The child was afraid of the mask which Muuma was wearing. Also *syaamankwamu* (a masked person)
the mange a scab, e.g. Mpongo zyokwesu zyakamana kufwa ci*nkwankwa*. = Our goats are dying of the mange.
a small hatchet, e.g. Bataata baluba *cinkwebele* kudilwe. = My father forgot his small hatchet at the funeral. Also *kaleba*
a small parrot, e.g. Ci*nkwele* waamana maila mumuunda. = The parrot has finished the millet in the garden.
dagga, e.g. Aaba balombe bakali kucita maleele ciindi nobakali kukolwa 'cilyo *cacinkwele*'. These boys were doing astounding things when they were drugged with the food of the parrot, i.e. dagga.
light green in colour, e.g. Inombe yokwesu njacinkwizilili. = Our cow is light green in colour.

dirt on a person who does not wash, e.g. Ciindi camupeyo bana baniini bamwi babaa *zinkwizilili* amibili yabo akaambo kakutasamba tunji. = In the cold season some little children have patches of dirt on their bodies because of not washing regularly.
a footprint, pl. *mano*, e.g. Ndali kutobelezya *cino* mwainda mubbi. = I was following the footprint where the thief passed. Also *itende*, pl.*matende*

the first dice thrown at divining, e.g. Uusonda utalisya *cinokozi*. = The diviner starts with the first dice, *cinokozi*. (The second is *sikwame*, the third is *kalume*, the fourth is *intuba*) Also *cinkozi*.
be disappointed in finding the food finished, e.g. Ndakaugwa *cinokozi*. = I was disappointed with lack of food.
a grindstone for sharpening objects made of iron or metal, e.g. Kamutola tweembe twanu *kucinoneno*. = Take your axes to the grindstone. Also *cikwengelo*.
a trap, a stumbling block, e.g. Munzila iya kumeenda kuli wakabikka *cinontozyo*. = Someone set a trap on the path going to the water.
syphilis, e.g. Bulwazi bwa*cinoono* bulajanika kubantu bavwuule. = Syphilis is found in people who are promiscuous.
something tasty or sweet, e.g. *Ndali kulya cinoono kwa Juunza.* = I have been eating something tasty at Mr. Juunza's place.

a hard painful growth on the instep of the foot, e.g. *Nceteendi kabotu nkaambo ndaa cinowe kunsi aakuulu.* = The reason why I cannot walk properly is because I have a hard painful growth on the sole of my foot.

a type of tree, the African blackwood (*Dalbergia melanoxylon*), cf. *musonkomono*. It is very hard and heavy and is slightly oily. Locally it has been used for turnery, carving, walking sticks and inlay work, and is much in demand for making musical instruments. The heartwood yields a red dye and the roots are alleged to have aphrodisiac properties. e.g. *Zyuuno zyacinsale nziyumu kapati.* The stools made of African blackwood are very strong.
infertile grain stalk, e.g. *Twakaula mapopwe acinsayila, taakamena pe.* = We bought infertile grain, it did not germinate at all. Also *cinsayilila cinsayilila*. See *cinsayila*.
a lack of reverence or respect, e.g. *Mukamwami ulaa cinseengwe.* = The wife of the chief lacks respect. Also *cinsengwe*
a type of possession dance, e.g. *Kaindi bamacembele Basoli bakalikuyanda kuzyana cinseengwe.* = Long ago the Soli women liked to dance the *cinseengwe*.
colostrum (i.e. first secretion from the mammary glands after giving birth) e.g. *Eeyi nombe mwiikame cinsema.* = Milk the first milk of this cow.
song of Basoli or Bene-mukuni peoples,
a Lenje dance, e.g. *Balenje mbabazyana cinsengwe.* = The Balenje people are the ones who dance the *cinsengwe*. Also *cinseengwe*.
lack of respect Also *cinseengwe*
uninitiated girl, e.g. *Musimbi oyu wakamita kacili cinsilwe.* = This girl conceived when she was still uninitiated. Also *ciliya*.

a disease said to afflict a man who has had sexual intercourse with a girl who is below the age of puberty, e.g. *Basimbi bacili baniini tabeelede koona a basankwa bapati nkaambo inga baciswa cinsiluwe.* Girls who are still young should not have sex with elderly men because they will contract the disease *cinsiluwe*. Also *mpela*.
the gum, e.g. *Cinsiniini cangu cizwa bulowa.* = My gum is bleeding.
rabies, e.g. *Kaluumwaya uciswa cinsuungwe.* Kaluumwaya is suffering from rabies. Also *cisungwa, cizungubwebwe*.
a rat's nest, e.g. *Muzwisye cinswa cambeba mubutala omu.* Remove the rat's nest from within this maize-bin. Also *manswa, cinswaanswa, cilalo*.
a rat's nest, e.g. *Ndacuumpa cinswaanswa cali mumapopwe.* = I have burnt the rat's nest which was in the maize. Also *cinswa*.

nakedness (lit. what I spit on) or the private parts of the human body, e.g. *Sikansondo ulaa cinswe tayandi kusama pe.* = The mad person is naked and does not wish to dress. *Bakamusiya a-cinswe ulilede ansi.* = They left him naked lying on the ground. Also *cintanda*.

a type of vegetable used as relish during famine, an inedible constituent of some flowers, e.g. *Cinsyungwa cakazwa maluba coonse aboobo ceelede kujikwa ciindi cilamfwu* = The *cinsyungwa* plant has flowered and so it has to be cooked for a long time as it is bitter. Also *luyuni*
an edible vegetable. e.g. Wakacela cinsyuungwa. = She collected cinsyuungwa leaves.

nakedness, e.g. *Muloongo uleenda cintanda.* = Muloongo is walking naked. *Kuti ntaunki mumakuwa ndaceenda ncobeni cintanda.* = If I do not go to the white people (for work) I will surely go naked. Also *cinswe*.

a rough dwelling with temporary roof, e.g. *Amukunke mulilo mucintangali.* = Make fire in the shack. *Bana bayota mulilo mucintangali.* = The children are warming themselves at the fire under the temporary roof.
a little basket used in the past as a dish, e.g. *Kaindi bantu bakali kulida mucintanza.* = Long ago people were eating from a small woven plate. Also *insangwa*.

immobility due to fear, collapse of muscles, e.g. *Ndabaa cintebwe nindabona syuumbwa, caala kutija.* = I was transfixed with fear when I saw the lion so that I was unable to run away. Also *cindebwe*.
a nest, e.g. *Ndabona bana bakayuni mucinteente.* = I have seen young birds in the nest.
mashed groundnuts cooked as porridge and used as relish, e.g. *Baneene bayanda kujikilwa cintele.* = My grandmother wants mashed groundnuts to be cooked for her.
a disease of the vagina, a secretion from the vagina which though abnormal can be treated. e.g. *Mutinta uciswa cintele cabakaintu.* = Mutinta has a gynaecological problem.
See *cintele*.
a snare for small animals, e.g. *Kwale wakacegwa nindakamuteya cintembo.* = A partridge was caught when I trapped it with a snare.
soft ripe grain, e.g. *Cintembwe nicakabizwa, bantu bakafwu*tuka.* = When the new soft sorgum became ripe, the people were saved. Also *maila matete*
a nest above ground, e.g. *Ndabona cintente cakayuni.* = I have seen a bird's nest. Also *cinteente*.
arm with hand cut off, e.g. *Kwaanza kwangu bakakunyongola kucibbadela aboobo cakaba cintimbwi.* = My hand has been cut off at the hospital and so my arm is handless. Also *cimpyunyunyu*
an animal whose tail has been cut, e.g. *Mubwa wakagonkwa mucila ngucintimbwi.* = A dog whose tail has been cut is called *cintimbwi*.
a traditional male wrap-round skirt, pl. *zintindi*, e.g. *Baalumi mbabakali kusama zintindi kaindi.* = It was the men who were wearing the *cintindi* garment long ago.
a spring of water, e.g. *Meenda amucintolo alatontola kapati.* = The water from the spring is very cold.

a store or shop, (ety. Eng.) e.g. *Tuya kukuula busu kucintoolo kwa Simoomba.* = We are going to buy meal at Simoomba's store. *Musimbi wuulisya mucintoolo wafwa.* = The girl who sold in the shop has died.
a thing, e.g. *Eeci cintu candikatazya kuyandaula.* = It is hard to search for this thing.
a nest of a species of termites, e.g. *Nceeci cintuluntumba.* = Here is a termite nest.
a porcupine, e.g. *Babwa bayoowa kumuluma cinungwe.* = The dogs fear to attack a porcupine. Also *inungu*.
perfume, e.g. *Kuli ununkilila cinunkililo awa.* = There is someone who is exuding perfume here.
pleasant or unpleasant smell, e.g. *Cinunko camafwuta aya ncibotu.* = The smell of this lotion is good. *Cinunko camafwuta aya civwundausya kumoyo.* = The smell of this ointment is revolting.
that which saves, e.g. *Nkoli yangu yakandinununa kuzwa kubabbi, yakaba cinununzyo.* = My knob-kerri saved me from the thieves, it was the thing which saved me.
a thumb or a toe, e.g. *Cinwenanda cakazwa Iwala.* = The nail of the thumb has come off. Also *calananda.*
a type of caterpillar, e.g. *Cinyabulede nceejana mumani akeepwa ncipati.* = The caterpillar which I found in the grass that was cut is a big one.
a wooden dish, e.g. *Mukansondo wakasunsa mucinyanda.* = Mukansondo dipped into the dish.
an animal, e.g. *Cinyama cainda waawa cilayoosya.* = The animal which passed here is frightening. Also *munyama.*
a type of tree, e.g. *Ndisamide nkaya yacinyamalama.* = I am wearing bangles made from the cinyamalama tree. Also *cinyamwaaba, cinamalama.*
a receptacle for carrying various things, e.g. *Baama bayumwide nkuni acinyampwido.* = My mother is carrying firewood in a receptacle.

a fruit eaten by jackal and cheetah and used to increase flow of milk in cows, e.g. *Bantu balalya cinyamwaaba abalo bamwaaba mbubona.* = People eat *cinyamwaaba,* and also jackals. Also *cinamwaaba, ciniamwaaba, mfwulimuninga, nsipi, nkoomwa.*
a wooden dish, e.g. *Nibakamana kukanda cikandi, bakamubikkila cimwi wisi mucinyanda.* = When they had finished preparing the porridge and sour milk they put some in a wooden plate for his father.

a bracelet of palm leaves, pl. *zinyanga,* e.g. *Bamwi banalumi bakayanda kusama zinyanga kumaboko kutegwa bataloogwi.* = Some men wear bracelets on their arms to protect themselves from witchcraft. *Bamwi basama zinyanga zyabulemu.* = Some wear the bracelets so that they receive honour.
bad smell, as of snake, e.g. *Aano acibaka kulimvwisya kununka cinyeu.* = In this place there is a bad smell. Also *cinioze.*
the back of a hen, e.g. *Icinyombwe cankuku taakali kuciyanzya alimwi abbaba.* = He did not give away the back of the hen, neither the wing.

a present on conclusion of a cattle sale, bank interest, reward, recompense, e.g. *Kuti nkuku zyangu zyakabbigwa ukazibone, njakukupa cinyonamucila.* = If you see my chickens which were stolen, I will give you a reward. *Kuti undeembelele kabotu nombe zyangu, ndiyakukupa cinyonamucila.* = If you herd my cattle carefully I will give you a present of a cow.
gripe, intestinal pain, e.g. *Mukaintu wangu ulaa cinyonena ncatamiti kufwambaana.* = My wife has abdominal pains that is why she does not conceive quickly. Also *cimyonzi, cipala.*

an identity document, registration card, e.g. *Kucikolo bayanda cinyongole.* = They want an identity document at the school. *Ndaunka ku Bbooma kukujana cinyongole.* = I am going to the Civic Centre to find an identity card. Also *cikosole.*
the third stomach of a cow, called the omasum, e.g. *Beembezi mbabeelede kupegwa cinyonkelo kuti balye.* = The herders should be given the omasum to eat. Also *ceembelelo.*
an offence or crime, e.g. *Musimbi oyu ulaa cinyonyoono cakutukila.* = This girl has the defect of insulting.
hoopoe's crest, e.g. _Inkunkuunku ilijisi cinyonzololo cibotu._ = The hoopoe bird has a beautiful crest. Also _cisunka._
