a cramp, numbness, a tingling feeling, e.g. _Ndaba acinywe kukuboko kwalulyo._ = I have a tingling feeling in my right arm. _Mudaala waba acinywe kukuulu nkwaalimbide._ = The old man has a tingling feeling in the right leg which he was pressing on it. Also _cinwe_
drinking vessel, e.g. _Koleta cinywido tunywide cibwantu._ = Bring a mug so that we drink light beer.
a shadow/reflection, e.g. _Zinzemweemwe nzifwiifwi sikati._ = Shadows are short at midday. Also _cinzimweemwe._
a cricket, e.g. _Ndamujaya cinzi._ = I have killed a cricket. Also _nyenze._
shadow, e.g. _Cinziinzimwa cako ncecimvwule camoyo wangu._ = Your shadow is the shelter of my heart.
a shadow or reflection, e.g. _Nceeci cinzimweemwe camubwa._ = Here is the shadow of a dog. _Sincinko ulanga cinzimweemwe cakwe._ = The mad person is looking at his/her shadow.
an indistinct object, e.g. _Cinzinzimwa tiicaboneka kabotu pe._ = The indistinct object was not clearly seen.
a type of traditional Ila dance, e.g. _Tuya kukuzyana cinzonoono._ = We are going to dance the _cinzonoono._
a type of disease, e.g. _Muntu uciswa cinzonoono tayendi kabotu, ulakwazaama kweenda._ = A person who has the _cinzonoono_ disease does not walk well, he walks akwardly.
a cattle disease, e.g. _nombe zyakaswaigwa bulwazi bwacinzovwu._ = The cattle have been infected by the _cinzovwu_ disease.

an unruly person or beast e.g. _Ooyu musune ulaa cinzulu ncobamuyoowa kumusunga._ = This ox is rebellious that is why they fear to yoke him. _Malende taakali kunjilwa cinzulu inga waloba._ = The rain-shrine was not entered by a rebellious person, if so he would be lost.
rough talk, uproar, e.g. _Kababoola kutegwa tukanane cisalala kuleka cinzulu-nzulu eci cili lino._ = Let them come so that we can talk smoothly without this present hullabaloo.
a basket, e.g. _Kobweza cinzuma ukaule cisyu kumusyika._ = Get a basket so that you can go and buy relish at the market. _Kamubikka mango mucinzuma._ = Put the mangoes in a basket.

a shade, e.g. _Ndikkede mucinzwide carnanda._ = I am seated in the shade of the house. _Mudaala uyusa zuba mucinzwide._ = The old man is sheltering from the sun in the shade. Also _cinzwiide, cimvwule._

a kind of traditional dance, e.g. _Tuya kukuzyana cinande kunkolola masiku._ = We are going to dance the _cinande_ at the initiation ceremony tonight. _(Acinande kwakali kunga okalamuka omusankwa otijaana canguzu kuya kumulongo wabasimbi. Waakusika kuya wamududa musimbi mwaletana akati mwazyana mwazyana mwasotoosyanya, mwamana wamutola wamusindikila musimbi nkwaazyila luno nta.)_ = We are going to dance the _cinande_ at the inititiation ceremony tonight. (At the _cinande,_ you, the boy, suddenly jump up and run energetically to the line of girls. When you reach there you touch a girl and dance with her to the middle of the arena, you dance and jump about together, finally you bring the girl back, guiding her to her original place.)

state of being dressed neatly or in finery, e.g. _Bana bamazuba ano balaa_ cipaale. = The young people of this generation dress in fine clothes. Kusama akweenda kwakwe koonse kwakali kwacipaale. = All her dressing and life-style became luxurious and extravagant.
a fraction of a whole, a slice of pumpkin or melon, e.g. Kondikomweda cipaanzi camungu. = Cut me a slice of pumpkin.
alertness, e.g. Wakabona mumvwi waloka munsi akuulu kwakwe mbuli waawa, eci cakamupa cipakami. = He saw an arrow falling beside his leg just there, this caused him agitation.

house of unmarried boys, eating place near boy's dwelling, e.g. Eeyi nsima kotola kucipala. = Take this nsima to the boys eating place. Masiku nobakatala kwiizya acipala cabo baya munanda yabo kukoona. = At night when the boys are tired of chatting at their meeting place they go to their house to sleep. Also igobelo.

period pains, a gynaecological problem, e.g. Ndaciswa cipala mwida. = I am suffering from period pains. Mukaintu ooyu ulaa luswa mbuli kuti ujisi cipala mwida. = This woman has a menstrual flow as if she had a gynaecological problem. Mukaintu ulaa cipala takonzyi kumita. = A woman who has this gynaecological problem cannot conceive.
a feast of game meat, e.g. Tuyooba acipali mumunzi wesu nsondo iboola. = We will have a feast of game meat in our village next week.

an edible tuber, e.g. Akaambo kanzala bantu bakucisi kuno bakatalika kulima cipama. = Because of the hunger the people of this area have started planting the cipama tuber. (It is like the lusala tuber) Kaindi muminzi bakali kusambala tombwe, zipama, ndiya, masyabe, mbeba, buci, nswi, zisuwo a bukoko.

a young uninitiated girl, e.g. Mucembele wakati, "Eeci cintu cakacitika candiyeeyezya ciindi nindakali cipamba." = The old woman said, "This thing which has happened reminds me about the time when I was a young uninitiated girl." Mainza wakasobana zisobano zinji naakali cipamba, anaakali musimbi. = Mainza played many games when she was uninitiated and when she was a girl. Also ciliya.
a platform, a platform for storing grass or for drying grain. e.g. Ndakatuma basankwa bobile kundiyakila cipampa. = I sent two boys to build a platform for me. Also buzalo, busanza, cizali.
a patch, e.g. Undisumine cipampi abuluke. = Stich a patch for me on the trousers. Also cigamba.
izina lyacipampi = nickname, e.g Mwana watobela kuzyalwa kubafwu banji upegwa zina lyacipampi. = A child who is born following many who have died is given a nickname. Also ceelo.
a large ladle, a serving wooden spoon for scooping nsima from the pot, e.g. Kondisanzyila cipampuzyo kutegwa ndipampuzye nsima. = Clean the large ladle for me so that I scoop out the nsima.
a portion of food, e.g. Ubikke cipampwido camuntu omwe. = Put out a portion of food for one person.
a dish into which cooked nsima is put, e.g. Koleta cipampwido ndikubikkile nsima. = Bring the dish so that I put nsima in it for you.

a supporting v-shaped pole, e.g. Eeyi nyama koyaanzika acipanda. = Hang this meat on the pole. Ndatuma basankwa botatwe kuyakukuleta cipanda cacisanza. = I sent three boys to fetch a pole for the granary.
newly broken ground, e.g. Mucipande tuyanda kuya kusyanga mapopwe. = We want to plant maize in the newly broken land.
an edible mushroom, e.g. *Cipande mbowa bwaampwa, pesi bulaligwa abutete.* = Cipande is a mushroom which is dried, but it can be eaten while still fresh.

a children's disease where they suffer from an enlarged head, e.g. Ooyu mwana uciswa *cipande* amutwe muleelede kumutola kukusilikwa cakufwambaana. = This child is suffering from an enlarged head, you should take him quickly to be cured.
a panga or machete, e.g. Kogonsya buyo *cipanga* kugonka nyama nkaambo keembe kunyina. = Use the machete to cut the meat as there is no axe.
a waiting room, e.g. Twalede kucipangahodi nkaambo citima casika akaandabwe. = We lay down in the waiting room because the train arrived at midnight.

an agreement, contract, covenant, e.g. Basicikolo taakwe nibakatobela *cipangano* cesu. = The pupils never followed what we agreed to. Ndijisi *cipangano* amweenzuma. = I have an agreement with my friend.
a span of oxen, e.g. Amusaangune kusunga *cipani* cangu nceyakulimya. = First yoke my span of oxen with which I am going to plough. (a very long span, *lupani*)
the hammer or trigger of a gun, e.g. Ndamvwa calila mbuli *cipani cantobolo.* = I have heard the sound of a gun being triggered off. Also lunkalaba.
a choir or dancing group, e.g. *Cipani cabaimbi cabucesya kwiimba adilwe.* = The choir sang until dawn at the funeral.
a clan or matrilineal group, e.g. *Mucipani* cesu bamaacisya boonse bakamana kufwa. = On our matrilineal side all our uncles have died.
iron around butt of gun, e.g. Musilikani wanduumya *cipanti cantobolo.* = The policeman hit me with the butt of the gun.
kraal, e.g. *nombe nkozili mucipanti.* = The cattle are there in the kraal. Also cimpati.
a fraction/half, e.g. Nceeci *cipanzi* camali ako. = Here is a share of your money.
a fragment of a pumpkin or melon, e.g. Kobapa *cipanzi* camungu baama. = Give mother a portion of the pumpkin.
a chip of stone or pottery, e.g. Kobikka mulilo *mucipanzi cacibiya.* = Put fire in a potsherd. Also cikaye.

a dried piece of calabash, a broken shell, e.g. Kozibikkila *mucipapa* meenda nkwilimba. = Put water for the pidgeons in the dried potsherd. Utola kuli *cipapa canondo?* = Where are you taking the broken tortoise shell. cipapa camutwe = a skull Also cipompo.
dull, e.g. Wakalizyi kuti mweenzinyina cakali *cipapa camutwe.* = He knew that his friend was dull.
a wedge, e.g. Kondipa *cipapalo nditabe munkulwa wacisanza.* = Give me the wedge so that I raise the floor planks to make it level with the others.
a splinter of wood, e.g. Ndanjilwa *cipapu* muliso nindali kugonka. = When I was cutting wood a chip of wood entered my eye. Also cifwapu, cimpampansya
a hospital or clinic. e.g. Ku Lusaka kuli *cipatela cipati.* = There is a big hospital in Lusaka. Baama batola mwana kucipatela. Also cibbadela, cipitolo
a feast of game meat, e.g. Bantu banji basika kucipati. Many people came to the feast of game meat. Also cipanti.
a washing basin, e.g. Kobikka meenda mucipati kutegwa basambe beenzu. = Put water in the washing basin so that the visitors wash.
a fan, e.g. Ncibotu kubelesya cipauzyo ciindi nokupya. = It is good to use a fan when it is hot. Also civwupauzyo.

a skin of an animal which has been removed and dried, an animal skin used as a skirt or wrap, pl. zipaya, e.g. Caceya cipaya cakubbazya mwana. = The skin for wrapping the child is too short. Kaindi basimbi bakaleka kusama maaya, bakatalika kusama zipaya zyajombe azyampongo azyabanyama bambi. = In the past the girls stopped wearing the fibre skirt, they began to wear the skins of cattle and goats and other animals. Also cisalu
a sacrifice, e.g. Oobu bukoko mbwacipayilo. = This beer is for sacrifice. Also cipailo.

the place on which a sacrifice is offered/altar, e.g. Cipayililo_ncintu cimwi cilemenede aboobo takweelede kusika kufwumbwa muntu. = An altar is something which is venerated, and so not just any person should approach it.
a ritual offering, sacrifice, e.g. Cipayilwa calwiindi mwaka uno cakazwa mumunzi mwa Milambo. = The ritual offering this year at the Iwiindi ceremony came from the village of Milambo. Also cipailo.
honeycomb without the honey, pl. mape, e.g. Mubwa walya cipe. = The dog ate the empty honeycomb.

road block, (Ety. Eng. Inspection) e.g. Wakajana basilikani baliimvwi munsi amusamu balindilizya kucita cipeekani camyootokala azimwi zintu zyeendela mumugwagwa. He found policemen standing near a tree waiting to make a roadblock for motorcars and other things which move along the road.
a gift, talent, e.g. Mebo ndijisi cipego cakwiimba. I myself have a talent for singing.

a film/movie, e.g. Twali kukulanga cipekupeku cakuzyalwa kwa Jesu. = We were watching a movie of the birth of Jesus, cipele leprosy, e.g. Cipele mbulwazi bunyongola minwe. Leprosy is a disease which cuts off the fingers. Also cinanta, cinkuntu, mankuntu, cinsenda, mulilo wa Leza.
a type of dance, e.g. Bantu baku Mapangazya bayandisya kuzyana cipelu. The people of Mapangazya like to dance the cipelu.
a swelling of the stomach, e.g. Namangala wakaciswa cipelu myaka minji. = Namangala suffered from a swelling of the stomach for many years.
television, e.g. Banyina bakamuulila cipelu-pelu ncaakali kubikka mukaanda kakwe. His mother bought for him a television which he was keeping in his room. Also cipekupeku

a cake of tobacco, e.g. Bantu nobazikkwa balabikkilwa zimwi zintu mucuumbwe, mbuli cipelwe catombwe amfwuko. When people are being burried some things are put into the grave, like a cake of tobacco and a pipe.
a rhinocerous, e.g. Cipembele wakazyala bana bobile. The rhino gave birth to two young ones. Also syaanyinga

a large clay pot for storing flour, or as containers for water, beer, milk, pl. zipempa, e.g. Zipempa zyakali zyakuyobweda busu. The big clay pots were for storing flour. Nobasimbi, cipempa mucivwuzye meenda. = Girls, fill the big pot with water.
safety pin, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Kondisongola a cipenente. Remove the thorn for me with a safety-pin. Also cipenete, cipenunzyo, cisongozyo.
co-sufferer, e.g. Koya ukalombe busu kuli Muunda *cipenzima*. = Go and ask flour from Muunda, my co-sufferer.
a dry piece of calabash, e.g. Indala bakaibikka *mucipepe* amalili mukati. = They put the left-over *nsima* mixed with sour milk in a piece of a gourd. Also cipapa.
a container for ritual beer, e.g. Bukoko bwakupiila bwabikkwa kale mu*cipiililo*. = The beer for sacrifice has been put already in the ritual container.
a nail, e.g. Konditambikizya *cipikili* comwe ndigagaile isomo lyacaala. = Give me a nail so that I hammer in the remaining roof-pole.
lever, stick across shoulders to carry load e.g. Kobikka *cipikuzyo* agwezyo kutegwa mukuli ukuubaubile. = Put a stick on your shoulder to take the weight of the load.

a puff adder, e.g. Babwa botatwe balumwa *cipile*. = Three dogs have been killed by a puff-adder. (*nkanga cipile* = the night adder; kapile-bunyangu, kapilisansa = small adder; cilungula = horned jumping adder, also ciduntila)
an inititation dance, e.g. Masiku aayinda twali kuzyana *cipilu*. = Last night we were dancing the *cipilu*. Also cipelu.
beer which is prepared in a short time, e.g. Makoko aakumbwa sunu ngacipilu. = The beers that are brewed nowadays are ready in an abnormally short time. (originally it took seven days)

a fragment of a spear, a spear whose handle is broken and only a short piece remains. e.g. Kobelesya buyo *cipimpila* eeco ciyeeme abwaanda. = Just use that part of a spear that is leaning against the wall.
a room, office, pl. *zipinda*, e.g. Eeyi nanda yakali a *zipinda* zinji. = This house had many rooms.
a bar of wood for door, e.g. Mubbi wajula *cipingizyo* akubba zintu zyali munanda. = The thief opened the wooden bar of the door and stole what was in the house.
a child born feet first, pl. *bacipini*, e.g. Kaindi bamacembele bakali kubajaya *bacipini*. = Long ago the old women would kill a child born feet first. also cimpini, cibuno.

a pin used by witchdoctors to write in the sand, e.g. Kusonda wakali kusonzya *cipini*. Pesi mukucapa taakali kucapya *cipini*. *Cipini* wakali kucisebenzya mutwaambo twabulwazi tusyoonto buyo. = Divining was done with a pin. But in delivery from witchcraft he did not use a pin. A pin was only used for matters of minor sicknesses.
a lever, e.g. Mukuli ooyu mmulemu, katubelesya *cipinisyo*. = This load is heavy, let us use a lever.
a latch, e.g. *Cipinizyo* cili amulyango wananda yangu nciyumu kapati. = The latch which is on my door is very strong. Also *mwiinzyo*.
section, e.g. Mucila wakasyukuta, kwakaide kucaala *cipipila* cakacila. = The tail of the rhino was scraped off, there only remained a section of the tail.
an emerald spotted dove, e.g. *Cipipwa* cikozya *nziba*. = The emerald dove is like a small pidgeon. Also cilipipi, cibbululu, ciibbili.
traditional goat-skin workaday skirt, e.g. Ijilo ndakaswaanya mucembele wakasamide *cipiya*. = Yesterday I met an old woman dressed in a traditional skin skirt. Also cipaya.
a gift, e.g. Ndakapegwa *cipo* cakubeleka kabotu. = I was given a gift for working well. Also cipego.
a feast, e.g. Kuli _cipobolo_ cakusekelela nombe yakazyala maanga. = There is a feast to celebrate the cow which gave birth to twin calves. Also ipobwe (vb. -pobola = feast)
a feast, e.g. Kuli _cipobwe_
kwa Moono. = There is a marriage feast at Moono's.

a mealie cob in sheath, pl. zipoka, mpoka, e.g. _Zipoka zijisi tukwapa._ = The cobs are begining to produce hair. _Cipoka nceeyokede acikko awa caida._ = The cob of maize which I have been roasting there has been burnt.
the pupil of the eye, pl. mboni, e.g. Mudaala ulaa gubilizi ampoka zyameso ncataboni. = The old man has cataracts on the pupils of the eyes, that is why he does not see. Also _mboni_
a traditional knife, e.g. Kondikwengela _cipoko ntenzye cisyu._ = Sharpen the knife for me so that I cut the relish with it.

an ankle, pl. zipokoto, (Ila) e.g. Malukwe akainda kubagwasya nkaambo akali kuvwumba maulu oonse kusikila muzipokoto. = The pairs of trousers helped them most because they were covering them down to the ankles. Also _ingo_
the venue for finishing rain beer at the _Iwiindi_ ritual, e.g. Kono _cipolo_
kulibuku. = This year the _Iwiindi_ ritual will end at the headman's residence.
the railway, e.g. Kayuni wakazyalwa lyakainda cipolo. = Kayuni was born when the railway was passing through. Also _cilayi._

name given to Zambian national football team, e.g. Nkamu yabasibbola bamu Zambia iitwa kuti _cipolopolo._ = The team of the Zambian national footballers is called cipolopolo. (ety. mpolopolo = a bullet (Chibemba)
a skull, e.g. Beembezi babwezela _cipompo_ camutwe wasokwe. = The herders picked up the skull of a monkey. Also cipapa, cipompo.
a beaded wrist-band, e.g. Muntu wakaindi wakasamide _cipondo kukuboko kwalulyo._ = A person of the past traditional life wore a beaded wrist-band on the right arm.
a wild boar, pl. zipongo, e.g. _Zipongo zyaamana mapopwe mumuunda._ = The wild boars have finished the maize in the field. Also sicipongo.
a clay seat or bed, e.g. Amukkale _acipopi aawo._ = Sit on that clay seat. Kumbali kumulyango kwakali _cipopi_ cakoona basimbi. = Near the door there was a clay bed for girls to sleep on.

the place selected for the conclusion of the drinking of ritual beer at the _Iwiindi_ ceremony. e.g. Uuno mwaka _cipuka ciyoozwida kwa Choona._ = This year the drinking of the _Iwiindi_ ritual beer will conclude at Choona. Also cipolo.
a young palm tree, e.g. Kondigonkela _cipuki cili kumbo._ = Cut the young palm-tree to the west for me.
a ghost, e.g. Naakamana kulibbunta mutwe nkujana watuba buu unakuti _ncipuku._ = When he had finished covering his head in ash he was completely white as if he was a ghost. Also _ceelo_

a hole, e.g. Eeyi nanda ilaa _cipulo mulutanta-mbeba._ = This house has a hole at the top of the wall. Musiye _cipulo mubwaanda bwacijikila kutegwa muwo kaunjila._ = Leave a hole in the kitchen wall for fresh air to enter.

a ritual meal which welcomes back and purifies one who has worked with foreigners away from the village e.g. Nobwakaca cifwumofwumo, banyina ausyi Chimuka bakatalika kubamba _cipulo casimakuwa._ Zuba lyasika amutwe, _cipulo_ cabizwa, basikulya boonse bayoboloka. = When the dawn came in the morning, the father and mother of Chimuka began to prepare the *'ritual meal of the one who has returned from work after a long time'*. When the sun reached its zenith, the meal was ready, all the guests gathered.
a sheller, e.g. *Bataata babelesya cipumbuzyo kubuulula mapopwe.* = My father uses a sheller when shelling the maize.
a stump of a finger or toe, e.g. *Mweene ulaa cipumpu camunwe.* = Mweene has a stump of a finger.
a child about three years old, e.g. *Musankwa wafwa wacili cipumpula.* = The boy who has died was still a young child.
a stump of a finger, e.g. *Acipumpunyu ndaa cicisa.* = I have a sore on the stump of my finger. Also cipumpu.
a low hill, e.g. *Ndajaya namusya acipuma.* = I have killed a duiker on a low hill. Also cilundu.
a swarm of bees, e.g. *Mumungo ndajana cipuma canzuki.* = I found a swarm of bees in the mango tree. Also ibbooma.
a heap of macenya termites, pl. *zipumuulu*, e.g. *Bateya nswa bajata buyo zipumuulu.* = Those who trap the flying ants have only caught the (biting) macenya termites.
a hornless ox, e.g. *Cisune cipumuulu twakacisambala jilo.* = We sold the hornless ox yesterday.
heavy dark rain, e.g. *Cifwumofwumo kwakawa cipumpwe.* = In the morning heavy dark rain fell.
a brush of cow's tail, pl. *zipunga*, e.g. *Bamami balayanda kweenzya zipunga.* = Chiefs like to walk with cows tails. (the symbol of their authority)
an edible grass *(Brachiara deflexa)* seed boiled as a . cereal in February. e.g. *Mumwaka wa-*
bantu bakali kulya cipunga-cidenene.* = In a year of famine the peo-ple were eating seed boiled as a cereal.
a spoon, (ety. Eng.) e.g. *Koleta cipunu cikwazya mpoto tulisye.* = Bring the spoon we use for scraping pots so that we use it to eat. Also conco
a wedding feast, e.g. *Nabwiinga bamujikila nkuku yacipupulu.* = They cooked a marriage-feast chicken for the bride. Also *bwiinga*
a winnowing fan, e.g. *Cipupuluzyo camapopwe cilidonkokede atako.* = The winnowing fan is broken at the base. Also cipupulusyo.

medicines used to weaken the activities of a witch, e.g. *Ndakabona mucape wakajisi cipupuluzyo ciyumu cakapupulula Haamasamu wakali kwiinda kulowa.* = I saw a witch-finder who had the strongest medicines for weakening medicine which made Haamasamu the greatest witch stop practicing witchcraft.
a craving for something, e.g. *Aaba bana balaa cipupya kukulya nsima nkaambo kanzala.* = These children are craving to eat *nsima* because of the hunger.
a small tied bundle, e.g. Wakati, *"Mwana, umubweze kabotu tombwe wauso muciputu eci."* = She said, "Child, take the tobacco in this bundle for your father carefully."
a wrapping, e.g *Mwana uuciswa bamuvwungaila muciputilo.* = They have wrapped the sick child in a wrapping.
a fan, e.g. *Murnanda mulapya, kobelesya cipuuzyo.* = It is hot in the house, use a fan.

a hole in cloth, boat, wall, fence, container, e.g. *Mbeba ziinda acipuyu cili amulyango wabutala.* = The rats pass through a hole which is in the door of the grain-bin. Mutiba uulida ulaa *cipuyu* atako. = The dish has a hole in the bottom. Also cipulo.
a head ornament of beads, e.g. Mucembele wakeelelwa naakasama *cipwampwa*. = When the old lady wore the beaded head-dress it suited her.
cheese, thick sour milk, e.g. Ooyu mwana tayandi kulya *cipwaza*. = This child does not like to eat sour milk.
beer on second day of brewing (still too sweet), e.g. Tuya kukunywa *cipyaapya* kwa Muleya. = We are going to drink which is not fully brewed at Muleya's.
sweet beer still hot after cooking, e.g. Amumupe *cipyaapya* mulwazi. = Give hot sweet beer to the patient.
warmth, e.g. Amunjile mumu*saansa* amumumuni wazuba. = Enter intoo the warmth and the light of the sun.
about 9.00 hrs, e.g. Ciindi casika kale *acisaasa*. = The time has already reached about 9.00 hrs. Also cikasaalizi, cuumpansansa.

the flying of a dove during laying period before incubation, e.g. Nziba *cisaasa*, usanga kubalombe, kubanene cilakaka. = You flying dove, you are flying for the young clever boys, but not for the aged.
stubborness, cheekiness, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ulaa *cisaaza*. = This boy is stubborn. Also nkazi, cimpangwe.
a traditional dance, e.g. Baila mbabazyana cizyano cacisaaza. = It is the Baila who dance the *cisaaza* dance.
dance sexually, e.g. Cilatondwa kuzyana *cisaaza* mucikombelo. = It is forbidden to dance sexually in the church.

a type of relish, e.g. Syaanasulwe amusimbi wakwe bakasuna mikusu yansima antoomwe akusunsa mu*cisabi* antoomwe akusowa mikusu mujungusi lyabulo bwabo antoomwe. = The hare broke a lump of nsima with his wife and together they dipped it in the relish and they together threw the lumps of nsima under their bed.
a forest, e.g. *Cisaka* ncotugonka nkuni cakapya. = The forest where we cut firewood has been burnt.
an old sack, e.g. Kamuleta *cisaka* tusansamune tombe. = Bring an old sack so that we clean off the dirt.
a platform or short palm tree for drying millet, e.g. Inkuku zilya maila ayanikidwe a *cisakabale*. = The chickens are eating millet which was put out to dry on the platform. Also cisangabale.

a pointed short stick, e.g. Komuuma *cisako* mubwa oyo ulangila cakulya. = Beat that dog with the stick who is longing for food. Nceeci *cisako* cakusuntizya ngoma. = Here is the stick for beating the drum.
a comb, e.g. *Cisakulo* cangu capya mumulilo. = My comb got burnt in the fire. Basicikolo bakacizimizya *cisakulo*. = The school-children have lost the comb. Also cilikamuzyo.
a hide, leather, dressed skin, e.g. *Cisalu* campongo mutacisowi kutegwa ciyanikwe. = Do not throw away the skin of the goat so that it can be hung up to dry. Also cipaya.
a pot for washing, e.g. Kobikka meenda mucisambilo camwana. = Put water in the baby's bath. Also nsambilo
a place for showering or washing, e.g. Bataata balasamba mucisambilo. = Father is washing in the bathroom.
the way one washes, eg. Cisambo camwana ulya taciluzi ncatasalali. = The way of washing of that child is not good, that is why it does not get clean. Also isambo
pole, post, e.g. Kosimpa *cisamu cananda.* = Insert the pole of the house.
a tree trunk, e.g. *Kamubweza cisamu* eco nobasankwa. = Young men, take that tree trunk.
any shrub about a metre or higher, e.g. Ndayubide kunze *acisamu* cili munsi anzila ncimwatandibona. = I was hiding behind the tree beside the path, that is why you did not see me.
aite plant or tree, a creeper. Also cizambayidwe, cizambilide. Some kinds: mubingabinga, namununga, mukata, ciwezyezyi, kaamu, kananza, lutende, munombyo, sinacooma.

a pole, e.g. Mali wakaa-dunukila munsi *acisanda* mumamvwu. = He spotted the money beside the leg of the bed in the soil. Wakazwa kukugonka *cisanda* cakuyakizya lukwakwa lwambewu yakwe. = He went out to cut a pole for building a fence for his garden.
a frock, e.g. Malita waka-samide *cisandulo* cibotu jilo kumazuba. = Malita wore a beautiful frock yesterday evening.
a mixture, e.g. *Cisanganya* camicelo eyi cilakola. = The mixture of these medicines is toxic.
moral corruption, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ulaa *cisangula.* = This man is morally corrupt.
a rough or old dish or basket, e.g. Mukaintu wakalukide *cisangwa* eci tacizyi. = The woman who has woven that basket does not know.
a cloth, e.g. Tuya kumusika ku-kuula *cisani* camwana. = We are going to the market to buy a garment for the child.
a cluster of fruit, a bunch, e.g. Ndaula *cisankata* camabbanana. = I have bought a bunch of bananas. Also cisankatilwa.
*cisankata caboya* = a horse's fetlock (the back part of its leg just above the hoof where there is a tuft of hair), e.g. *Cisankata* cabbiza eli ncipati. = The fetlock of that horse is large.

*cisankata camaluba* = bouquet, wreath, pl. *zisankata zyamaluba*, e.g. Basidilwe babikka *zisankata zyamaluba* acuumbwe. = The mourners put a wreathe of flowers on the grave. Also cikama camaluba *cisansayile* a comb of bees, the comb it-self, e.g. Kuli *cisansayile* canzuki mu-mango aali mulubuwa. There is a comb of bees in the mango tree in the court-yard. Also ibbooma
5 shillings (old currency), e.g. Bacembele bajisi *cisanu* camali. = The old woman has five shillings.
a type of water-pot, e.g. Meenda ali *mucisanu* abija nkaambo akkala kaindi. = The water in the pot is stagnant because it has stayed for a long time.
a low and temporary maize-platform after harvest, e.g. Mapopwe ali *mucisanza* amana nkwilimba. = The pid-geons have finished the maize on the maize-platform. Also cizali.

a branch placed as an obstacle, e.g. Kobikka *cisanzu* camamwa anzila iyinda mumuunda kutegwa bantu baleke kwiinda. = Put a thorn branch on the path going to the field so that the people stop passing through. Wakatalika kubamba *cisanzu* kucingilila nombe kuti zyoone. = He began to build a branch-barrier to protect the cattle so that they could sleep.
a low platform, e.g. Muka-mbausi wakaimvwi *acisanzya* mu Nsondo. = The preacher stood on a dais on Sunday.
a bin made of bark, e.g. Amukakwame makwa amubombo tubambe *cisanzya* cakuyobweda mapopwe. Remove the bark from a mubombo tree so that we make a bin for storing maize.
insolence, gross language or offensive behaviour, e.g. Mwana musimbi uulya ulaa _cisapi_. = That young girl is insolent.

a puff adder, viper, e.g. Musune okwesu walumwa _cisasa akuulu_. = Our ox was bitten on the leg by a viper. _Cisasa mfwuntyuma ubone tunji_. = The puff-adder standing erect sees many things. Also _cipile_.
a mat Also _lusasa_

container for sweet-beer, e.g. Naakateka bbwatu _mucisasikilo_ akafwulu wakajana kuti lilalelemuka. = When he drew the sweet-beer from the container with a calabash, he found that it was slippery (like cooked okra).
cold attributed to jealousy, e.g. Muka Sibbuyu ulaa _cisatabafwi_. = Mrs Sibbuyu is cold with jealousy.
a cluster of bees hanging on a branch, e.g. Zyakabaluma nzuki nibakauma _cisaula amalekani_. = The cluster of bees stung the boys when they hit them with catapults. Also _cisansayile, ibooma_.

a rat's nest out in the open, (nsaulu = a type of rat with a dark line along its back), e.g. Bana bakaumpa _cisaulu kutegwa mbeba zitazyali_. = The children burnt the rat's nest so that it would not bear offspring.

appearance, bodily welfare, e.g. Ncisyoonto ncokonzya kubona camapenzi ngookandipa, mmubili wangu ngookajaila _ciseba_. It is only a little that you see of the sufferings that you have given me, it is the appearance of my body which you have destroyed. Ncenciceeci camwayaula _ciseba cangu_. This is the very thing which has destroyed my appearance. Also _ciimo_
a hanging basket used for keeping churns and pots, e.g. Wamana kusanzya mpoto uzibikke _mucisebe_. = After washing the pots, put them in the hanging-basket.
a palm-funnel, e.g. Bataata baluka _cisebe cakutilizya mukupa munsuwa_. = My father is weaving a palm-funnel basket for pouring the milk into the gourd.
a bare place, good for winnowing, e.g. Kokukula _acisebelo_. = Sweep the place for winnowing.
a seive, e.g. _Cisebyo cabuntele calyatwa mpongo cafwa_. The sieve for buntele which was stepped on by the goat is destroyed.
a crate for fowl, e.g. _Muciseeke kuli nkuku zili kkumi_. There are ten hens in the crate. Also _ciseke_.
a very stupid or dull person, e.g. Ndakazyala _ciseese camwana_. = I have given birth to a fool of a child.

a different colour, e.g. Wakasama kaluke _kacisefwu_. He wore a small trousers of different colours. Syuumbwa ulijisi mubala mukasolo kakwe _wacisefwu_. The lion had a spot of a different colour on his hip.
a crate of fowl, a nest for fowl, e.g. Koleta mayi osanwe _muciseke_. = Bring five eggs from the fowl's nest. Also _ciseeke, cisekwe_.

a very great number (ety. many tiny seeds), e.g. Cimwi ciindi uyookonzya kutugwasya zilyo amusamu _waciseke uuwuzya zilyo mumyuunda amuzimumbwa_. She might help us with the medicine which makes the food in the field and in our grain stores become abundant. Mucembele oyu ulijisi _ciseke_, mwati nkulimina koonse kuya. = This old woman has a great crop, and all this has to be weeded.
a small whitish fish, e.g. Baama balicizyi kukanga _cisekele_. = My mother knows how to fry the small whitish fish.
a strong receptacle for carrying stones, e.g. Koleta _cisekelele tubwezele mabwe_. = Bring the container so that we take the stones away.
a cage, a crate of fowl, e.g. _Mayi ali mucisekwe cankuku aligwa mubwa._ = The eggs which were in the crate of fowl have been eaten by a dog. Also ciseke.
a half, e.g. _Sicikolo mumupe cisela camali aakwe._ = You may give the pupil half of his/her money.
a hole e.g. _Cisena eci mbuli kuti cinjila nzoka aboobo ceelede kusinkwa._ = It seems as if a snake has entered that hole and so it should be blocked. Also cipulo, bwina, cina.
an old thing, e.g. _Eeci cisuwo cakaba cisengele._ = This basket has become worn out.
a strong receptacle for carrying stones, pl. _zisengele_, e.g. _Bantu basusa mabwe azisengele._ = The people are transporting stones with strong receptacles. Also cisekelele.
a bandage for a broken limb, e.g. _Mu-Iwazi bakamwaanga cisengele mumabambo akatyoka._ = They bound the patient around the broken ribs with a bandage.
a nest for fowl, e.g. _Inkuku itula mucisengele._ = The hen is laying eggs in the nest.
irreverence, lacking respect, _ciimbo cacisengwe_ = a profane song, e.g. _Adilwe bakaintu baimba cisengwe._ At the funeral a woman was singing a disrespectful song.
a shelled mealie cob, pl. _zisenketi_, e.g. _Kamuleta zisenketi tukunkizye mulilo._ = Bring along a shelled mealie cobs so that we light a fire. Also cinkonti.
a tuft of grass, e.g. _Twakalisamide mpato nitwakali kweenda mucisense._ = We wore sandals when we were walking on the tufts of grass.
a lesion, injury, wound, e.g. _Ndabaa cisepu akuulu._ = I have an injury on the leg. Also cisyepu.
purse, e.g. _Ulacaalilwa cisepwe camali._ = He is left with a bag of money.
a large storage pot for grain, e.g. _Mapopwe ali muciseselo akabola._ = The maize which is in the storage pot has rotted.
a revolting or shameful thing, e.g. _Moonga sunu wacita cisesemyo munsi abanyina naawuma musimbi._ = To-day Moonga did a shameful thing in front of his mother when he beat a girl.
a skin disease, rash, e.g. _Kulya musiikka utabizwide cipa kubaa ciseseya amubili._ = To eat unripe musiikka causes a skin disease. Also cisasu
laughter, e.g. _Cisesyo camwana oyu cilandicima._ = The laughter of that child annoys me.
a basket, e.g. _Bantu banji tabacizyi kuluka cisewe._ = Many people do not know how to weave a basket.

country, territory, district, neighbourhood, e.g. _Mucisi cesu kuli luumuno, nkondo tainingatalika._ = In our country there is peace, war has not yet started. _sikatongo_ = owner of the neighbourhood. Also _katongo_
black/dark coloured, a reddish-violet coloured head of cattle, e.g. _Musune wangu ngwacisikili._ = My ox is dark-coloured. _Malita wakali mukaintu wacisikili._ Malita was a woman of dark complexion.
a base/stem/stump/trunk/plant, pl. _zisiko_, e.g. _Cisiko camusamu cadaduka aboobo musamu wawa._ = The trunk of the tree has been uprooted and so it has fallen down.
a piece of wood from which fire is drawn by friction, e.g. _Kaindi bakali kubamba mulilo kuzwa kucisikwa._ = Long ago they used to produce fire from a piece of wood by friction. Also _musiko_

red clay, e.g. Kamwale usila cisila camukula. The girl being initiated is grinding red clay for making ochre. Bamwi basimbi bakatumidwe kuya kuyandaula cisila cakukwiya mukula. Some girls were sent to look for red clay for grinding to make ochre.
iron trap for birds or animals, e.g. Kamupasulula mubwa wapatila mucisilazya. = Release the dog caught in the trap.
payment to witchdoctor before treatment, e.g. Kondipa mali acisilikilo nentanasya musamu. = Give me my fee before I dig the medicine. Also cilumyo.
the place where treatment by a witchdoctor is carried out, e.g. Banji balwazi basika kucisilikilo. Many patients arrived at the witchdoctor's place of healing.
a witchdoctor's fee, e.g. Kondipa mali acisikilo nentanasya musamu. = Give me my fee before I dig the medicine.
satiety, glutted state, e.g. Ndakkutisya cimbwali, ndaa baa cisilusilu. = I am full of sweet-potatoe, I am sated. Ooyu mwana ulya mucisilusilu. = This child eats foolishly.
a piece of charcoal, e.g. Ndalyata cisimbi cilaa mulilo canduumpa kunsi akuulu. = I have stepped on burning charcoal and it has burnt the sole of my foot.
a badly behaved girl, e.g. Eeci cisimbi tacilomene, cilatukila basankwa. = This girl is badly behaved, she insults boys.

notched edge of a fragment used for decorating pottery, e.g. Bana basobana cisimbio camucembele aboobo cazimina. The children have been playing with the pottery tool of the old woman and so it is lost.
an initition dance, e.g. Basimbi bazyana cisimbo munanda muli kamwale. = The girls dance the cisimbo in the house where the girl being initiated is.
a print, e.g. Bapulisa bakapima cisimbo camunwe wabantu boonse kwiinda mukunjizya munwe muinki. = The police took the finger-print of all the people by inserting the finger in the ink.
prickly grass, pl. zisina, e.g. Twakayaswa zisina zinji nitwakali kutebula. We were pierced by a lot of prickly grass when we were harvesting. (Also insina blackjack)
a field dug for the first time awaiting planting, e.g. Ngulube zyali kufwukaula mucisinde. The pigs have been rooting around in the newly plouged land.

a pile of stones which is built up at a spot where a dead person was placed for a short time and then carried away to residence. Anyone who passes adds a stone to the pile. e.g. Aawa abusena obu akatikati kazilundu alo akali cisinga-singa cipati. There at this place amid the hills there was also a large heap of stones to mark the place where someone had been been temporarily placed. Bakabikka milawo yakuti kufwumbwa muntu wainda acilawo eeci uleelede kuwaala kabwe nkaambo mpaacisinga-singa. = They made a law saying that whoever passed by this place ought to throw a stone (on the mound) because it was a place to be honoured where someone had temporarily rested.
a pole for blocking a gateway, e.g. Amusimpe cisingisyo awa. = Insert a gate pole here.
curse, imprecation, e.g. Cisingo ncibandisinga bataata candiyoosya. = The imprecation with which my father cursed me makes me fear.

upper jaw; mweebo = lower jaw cisinkamatwi a deaf person, e.g. Nkokuti ulya muntu ncaatavwiilila nendamwaanzya ngucisinkamatwi. = The reason evidently why that person did not answer me when I greeted him is that he is deaf. Also cuulutwi.
a bribe, e.g. Sibbuku wesu upegwa cisinkameso ncatakosoli kabotu twaambo. = Our headman was given a bribe so as not to judge the case fairly. Also cisinkamulomo
a blind person, e.g. Uulya muntu ngucisinkameso. = That person is blind.
a bribe, e.g. Mubbi wabapa cisinkamulomo bamasilikani kutegwa batamwaangi. = The thief bribed the police so that they would not arrest him. Also cisinkameso.

obstacle place on ground to make people go around it, e.g. Twakabikka kale cisinkilo anzila iyinda mumuunda. = We have already put a barrier across the path which goes through the field. Also cisanzu.
a cold in the head, e.g. Mazuba aunga luwo bantu banji inga baciswa cisini. = During the days when the wind blows many people caught a cold. Also cisyini.
the upper jaw, a toothless upper gum, e.g. Mukanwa mwangu menyo onse akamana kuloka, kwacaala buyo cisiniini. = In my mouth all the teeth have fallen out, only the gums remain. Also cinsiniini.
a clump of grass, pl. zisinsaile, e.g. Muyuni wakalubikka luno uyabusotauka zisinsaile atuvwuna. = The bird increased speed jumping over clumps of grass and bushes. Also cisinsayili
a tuft of grass, e.g. Eeco cisinsayili ucidikimune mamvwu kutegwa citasyuuki. = Shake the clay off that tuft of grass so that it does not germinate. Also cisinsaile, cisense.
a reproach, reproof, rebuke, e.g. *Cisinso* camudaala oyu tacili cibotu. = The way the old man rebukes is not good.
a plug, stopper, lid, e.g. Caya kuli cisinsya cacigumbuli cameenda? = Where is the lid of the container of water?
a plug, stopper, e.g. Kondipa cisinsyo cakagumbuli aka. = Give me a stopper for this container.
a burning ember a firebrand, e.g. Kondiletela cisisi camulilo mfwebe. = Bring me an ember of the fire so that I smoke.

a nose plug which is inserted in a hole in the septrum (manango), the cisita may be a reed or sorgum plug or a length of porcupine quill or the cisita may be bead-covered for special occasions, pl. zisita, e.g. Basimbi bakalongela tukuze, makwambe, zisita zyabulungu. = The girls come looking for cord necklaces, beaded waist ropes, beaded nose-plugs.
epilepsy, e.g. Ooyu mwana uciswa cisita (kasita). = This child is suffering from epilepsy. Also kasuntu.
a vegetable relish, e.g. Cisiungwa cilalula-lula. = Cisiungwa is a bitter relish. Also siungwe, ciyuni, luyuni.
antiquity, out-dated, e.g. Cisila eci ncacisiyesiye. = This ochre is out of date.
traditional custom yet still practised, e.g. Kuvwundika nkolola ncisiyesiye cabasikale. = The initiation ceremony has been handed down by the ancestors.
black complexion, e.g. Wakali musimbi mubotu wacisiyo-siyo mbuli banyina. = She was a beautiful girl with the black complexion of her mother.
a game, a play, a concert, e.g. Cisobano cali kusobana bana cilanoneenzya. = The concert done by the children was very pleasing.

traditional children's games: Nkaankakaye (One child passes a stone with two hands to the next until one of them drops it. The one who drops it then covers her head while the others hide and then she goes looking for them.); *Lembelembe musamu mugololo* (Swing, swing on the mugololo tree); *Nondo uyayi, namukwakwaile?* (describes how a tortoise walks); *mwana mubeebe* = hide and seek *cisolo* = played with stones and 20 holes; *namacaaca* = a game for girls; *intindi* = throwing sharp sticks at a tuber.
uncultivated bush, e.g. *Kwaba kumazuba ukacuumpe cisokwe cili kumuunda.* = When it is evening you should go and burn the bush in the field. Also *syokwe*
an ugly monkey, e.g. *Cisokwe cilya mapopwe mumuunda.* = A horrid monkey is eating the maize in the field.

a Bantu game played with stones in holes, e.g. *Cisyu caida nitwali kusobana cisolo.* = The relish got burnt when we were playing *cisolo*. -*lelula*, e.g. *Nibakali kusobana cisolo bakali kulelula mabwe*. When they were playing *cisolo* they were throwing the stones up. If the hand misses the stone when falling we say, "Walelula". (If you miss scooping out all the stones while the stone is falling)
a bush with blue edible fruit, e.g. *Ndajana cisombo cajisi nsombo zyakabizwa.* = I found a bush with ripe blue fruit.
pole of a roof, e.g. *Kulubazu lumwi lwaciluli kwakali cisomo catakakkede kabotu.* = On one side there was a roofpole which was not sitting properly.

a type of tree (*albizia versicolor*), pink to greenish yellow flowers which develop into crimson pods. The wood resembles *mukwa* and is easy to work but of low durability. Used for mortars. Unripe seeds and pods are poisonous to cattle. Soap made from roots. e.g. *Incili yacisomwe ilasumpwa kufwambaana.* = A mortar made from *cisomwe* wood is quickly holed by insects. cf. *muchaacha, munsomwe, mwangule*.
good germination in agriculture e.g. *Uno mwaka tulaa cisonga cibotu mumuunda.* = This year the seed has germinated well in the field. Also *ceenzya*.

any sharp thing used to extract a thorn, the sharp point of a stick, e.g. *Wamana kulisongola undipe cisongozyo ambebo ndisongole.* = When you have removed the thorn, give me that sharp pointed instrument so that I remove a thorn as well.
a thorny plant with blue flowers, e.g. *Cisonso candiyasa ajanza nindali kujwa bwizu.* = When I was cutting the grass, a thorny plant pierced my hand.
a hat, e.g. *Wakagusya cisote akupa munene, wakasama kulyezeka.* = He took out the hat and gave it to the old man, he wore it to see if it suited him.
a locust or a swarm of locusts, e.g. *Cisozi caamana maila mumuunda.* = The locusts have destroyed the millet in the field.
foul air from the anus, e.g. *Kuli wasula cisozi cinunka nsu!* = Someone has emitted bad air.

a big black marching ant, pl. *bacisozya*, e.g *Ooyu mwana wajata cisozya.* = This child caught a big black ant. *Bacisozya banjizya tusanga mucuulu.* = The black ants put blades of grass in the ant-hill. Also *cisinza*.

a type of tree (*euphorbia ingens*), giant cactus or candelabrum tree, grows on ant-hills, exudes a copious white latex which is used a bird-lime and the dried powdered stem is used as fetilizer, the wood is light and tough and nails well. e.g. *Mudaala ubamba ziswi acisu.* = The old man is making brooms from the wood of a big cactus tree. Also *muswi*
a traditional wooden milk vessel, e.g. Bana basunu tabacizyi cisuba. = The younger generation of today do not know the wooden traditional milk container.
the bladder, urinary, a container for urine, e.g. *Cisubilo* cangu inga cilacisa nesuba. = My bladder pains when I am urinating.

punishment, what is beyond endurance, e.g. Ndafwa *cisubu*. = I have had enough to bear. e.g. Mwana wajaya mpulungwido kucikolo wapegwa *cisubu* ncatakalubi. = The child who broke the window in the school has been given a punishment which he will not forget. Also cisubulo.
punishment, chastisment, penalty, e.g. Basicikolo bali kulwana ba-pegwa *cisubulo*. = The pupils who were fighting were punished.
childish innocence, e.g. Bana baniini balaa *cisukasuka*. = Little children are filled with innocence. Also bunkuunku.
a tall tobacco plant, e.g. = Ba-neene batyola matuvwu atombwe aci-*suku*. = My grandmother is picking to-bacco leaves from a tall tobacco plant.
sleeping with eyes open like a hare, e.g. Ooyu mudaala woona *cisulwe*. = This old man sleeps like a hare.
a lump, e.g. Komufwusila *cisu-ma* cansima mubwa. = Throw a lump of nsima to the dog.
hoof, or foot and hoof, e.g. Kamucijika *cisumba* caņombe eco. = Cook that cow-hoof.

anthill (less destructive kind of ant, they heap what they leave), e.g. *Cisumbwa* ncobasinguluzya zibuye zya-maanda bamakaintu. = The women smear the floors with the soil of the mound of the small black termite.
tuft of hair, crest, forelock, e.g. Ndabona muyuni ulaa *cisumpa*. = I saw a crested bird. Also cisunka.
beer made for first visit of husband to bride's home, e.g. Kwesu kuyakuba bukoko bwacisungu mwezi uboola. = Next month at my home there will be beer for the first visit of my brother-in-law.

anything slaughtered at an initiation ceremony, e.g. Kunkolola kweelede kuti kube muntu umwi musazinyina weelede kuleba. Ngonguwe nguutamba bantu mbayanda bamugwasye kuleba *cisungu*. = At the initiation there ought to be some relative who slaughter's something. He is the one who invites the ones he likes to join him in the work.
rabies, e.g. Babwa baciswa *cisungwa*. = The dogs have rabies. Also cinsungwe, cinsuungwe.
tuft of hair, sump, high hair on the head, pl. zisunka, e.g. Bantu bakaindi bakali kuyanda kulekela zisunka. = Long ago people liked to let tufts of hair grow on their heads. Also cisumpa.
crest of hoopoe bird, e.g. Inkunkunku ilaa *cisunka* cilamfwu. = The hoopoe has a long crest. Also cizonzoolo, cinyonzololo, lucililimba.
a knob-billed duck, Muvwimi wajaya *cisunkankumo*. = The huner killed a know-billed duck. Also cigwalugwalu.
a type of sickness, epilepsy, e.g. Mwana wa Kanyemba uciswa *cisuntu*. = The child of Kanyemba is suffering from epilepsy. Also kasuntu, kuwa, maamfwa.

the time of night when people are fast asleep, e.g. Wakajoka kunanda yakwe *acisuntukilo*. = He arrived back home at the time when people are fast asleep. Eeci ciindi cakali kuumina *acisuntukilo* cabacece. = This was the time when babies were already asleep.
a basket, e.g. Kamubikka mapopwe *mucisuo tubuulule*. = Put maize in the basket so that we shell it. Also cisuwo.
the morning meal, e.g. *Nitwatalika kulya cisusule twamvwa bantu balila.* = When we began to eat breakfast we heard people crying. Also cisusulo.
the morning meal, e.g Basi-cikolo bamwi balaunka kucikolo kabatalide *cisusulo*. = Some school children go to school without eating breakfast. (note. In some places *cisusulo* means lunch.)
time of early morning meal, e.g. *Basika amunzi cacifwumofwumo aci-suswido*. = They arrived at the village in the early morning

a mound of small termites or black ants, e.g. *Bana basya cisuu-mbwa*. = The children are digging up a mound of small termites. *Cisuumbwa cijanwa mumusena ncibotu kubambya cibuye cananda*. = The black ant-hills found in the vlei are good for making the floor of a house. *Maanu alazwa amucisuu-mbwa*. = Wisdom can come out from even a small ant-hill.
a large basket, e.g. *Catika cisu-wo cabusu*. = The basket of flour was spilt.
a meeting place, e.g. *Aano mputwasika mpaaciswaanganino ca-basibbuku Milembo abantu babo*. = Here where we have arrived is the meeting-pla-ce of headman Milembo and his people.
a whip, e.g. *Ndali kuuma mwana aciswepu*. = I was beating the child with a whip. Also ciswipu.
a bandage for broken limbs, e.g. *Kamwaanga musune watyoka mabambo aciswi*. = Bind up the ox with a bandage which has broken its ribs. Also cisengele
angle, as at corner, e.g. *Kobikka cibiya cacisyu kuciswi cacijikila*. = Put the pot of relish in the corner of the kitchen. Also kaswi.
a broom, e.g. *Ndaula ciswi cakuku-kuzya murŋanda*. = I bought a broom for sweeping in the house. Also cikukuzyo, cipyaango.
bad fish, e.g. *Ciswi ncindaula cakabola*. = The bad fish which I bought was rotten.
a whip, e.g. *Bayi banduuma aciswipu*. = The teacher beat me with a whip.
a marriage agreement, e.g. *Cisyabo cabo cakamana*. = Their marriage arrangement ended. *Cisyabo cabana baya cililomene*. = The love-pact between those young people is strong.
a love-affair, e.g. *Wakandilembela lu-gwalo kuti camana cisyabo*. = He wrote me a letter saying that the love-affair was over.
love-affair, e.g. *Kuzwa buzuba obu cakatalika cisyamwali cabo*. = From this day their love-affair began.

crop, *zisyango* = crops e.g. *mapopwe* = maize; *mabele* = millet; *magwili* = potatoes; *zimbwali* = sweet-potatoes; *mwanja* = cassava; *ndongwe / nyemu* = groundnuts; *tombwe* = tobacco; *mulotwe* = wheat; *nyabo* = beans; *buluba* = cotton.

unripe maize pl. *zisyanje*, e.g. *Musankwa wakali kukunya zisyanje akulya, amana waya ali limbi kusikila wakkuta*. = The boy was gnawing at the maize and eating, when he had finished he went to where there was another until he was full. Also cinyonje, pl. minyonje.
a lesion, e.g. *Cipeni canditenda cisyepu akuulu*. = A knife has made wound on my foot.
history, a story of the past, e.g. *Inzala yakono yasiya cisyimo cita-kalubwi*. = The hunger this year has left behind a story which will not be for-gotten.

a gum (from which teeth grow), e.g. *Cisyinini* camwana uyanda kuzwa menyo cilasiya. = The gum of a child from which teeth are about to appear is black. Gums issuing blood = *cikunka-menyo*, also *cinsiniini*
a salt-pan, a depression near a stretch of water where salt gathers as water evaporates, e.g. Bamaama baunka kukusya munyo *kucisyo*. = My mother goes to dig salt at the salt-pan. Also *ikuto*

a promise, e.g. Twaka-pangana cisyomezyo cakuti kunyina wi-inda mumuunda wamweenzinyina masiku nkaambo kabulozi bwavwula. = We made a pact that no one should pass through a neighbour's field at night because of the witchcraft is rampant.
sturdy, e.g. Ooyu Mudyaka cakali *cisyondomena* camulom-bwana. = This Mudyaka was strongly built.

vegetables, relish, pl. *zisyu*, e.g. *Ijilo twakabwenga cisyu cibotu*. = Yesterday we dipped into nice relish. Nseyandi kulya *cisyu cibisi* = I don't like eating uncooked vegetables. *Cisyu* cili mbuli *bbondwe, kayuniyuni, mpububu amaa-mbwa*, bantu bamazubaano bakazileka. = The people of nowadays have stopped using plants from the bush for relish like *bbondwe, kayuniyuni, mbububu*, and *maambwa*. Bana banji bakali kusunsa mucibiya mwakali *cisyu* canyama yamu-sefwu. Mbangaye buyo bakali kusunsa *mucisyu* canswi nkaambo bakali kuyoowa kuyaswa tufwuwa twanswi. Kunyina mwana wakaindulula kubwenga mucibiya mwakali *cisyumani*. = Many children were dipping into the dish where there was eland meat. Only a few were dipping into the fish-relish as they feared to be pierced by the little fish-bones. No child repeated dipping into the dish of vegetable relish. *-ampa* = make a relish into cakes to preserve it. Names of some herbs and plants eaten as relish or used for other purposes: *igambwa, pl, maambwa* (pumpkin leaves); *indulwe, madyulu, kadyumbwi, mukata, lumomba, cimowa* (eaten in rainy season); *kampubu* or *syaazipa* (with wild yellow flowers and later black seeds which stick to clothes) *muncile, mundyoli, cinkulumwanza, munkulwe, cotwe, kapa-ya-kamulamu, sonkwe, cisyungwa, itelele or lunkomba, kayunumbwi*; *mundambi* (cultivated for its leaves); *Mugulumya* (edible root); *buseza* (edible tuber); *mumpelempefwa* (eaten by cattle); *impoko* (for making salt); *munkoyo* or *muziinga* (for light beer); *impululwa, namunkulungu* (edible leaves); *mukusa* (for strong strings); *cinkolonkozya* (for blocking holes in clay pots); *musunkwindi* (*bukowa* seeds); *luntele* = crushed ground nuts. List of Gwembe Valley vegetable relishes: *Mubuyu, bonko, iboa, muneko, shunku, mucaca, lilumina, muneneotuba, tende-mulumi, tebelebe, tende, kakonkwa or tielele, kiuyu or njina, tubwani, siungwa, baba, mudelele, mupwepwe, sani, munongwa, munogo, kafuakanswi, bololonzia, mukambo, mbelebele, musebebe, cimbwelele, nampwisa, mundioli, mutumbululwe, siankende.*
vegetable relish, e.g. Bamwi bantu tabayandi *cisyumani* citajisi nyama. = Some people do not want vegetable relish which is without meat.

a vegetable plant, e.g. Oobu buntele mbwakubikka *mucisyungwa*. = These pounded groundnuts are for putting into *cisyuungwa* relish. Muzyukulu wamucembele wakacela *cisyuungwa*. = The grandchild of the old woman collected *cisyuungwa* relish. Also *luyuni, cisyuungwa*.
lead, e.g. *Mukuli wacisyuta ulalema kapati.* = A load of lead is very heavy. Also *lodo, loto, lotwe*.
a prop, a support, e.g. *Kamuleta citabye utabye ciluli.* = Bring a supporting pole to hold up the roof. Also *citabyo*.
a prop or support, e.g. *Kobikka citabyo aciluli ciyanda kuwa.* = Put a prop to the roof, it wants to fall. *Citabyo camaulu* = footstool Also *citabye*.
a small fish, pl. *zitaka*, e.g. *Nitwali kuzela, ndajaya zitaka zinji.* = When we were fishing, I caught a lot of little ones.
a shoal of small fish, e.g. *Citaka mumyoono cali kutuba mbuli mapopwe.* = The small fishes in the fishing-baskets were as white as maize seeds. **citalabalanga** a wonder, Also *citalatala*
a wonder or marvel, pl. *zitalatala*, e.g. *Inyenyezi nzitalatala zyamumulenga-lenga.* = The stars are the wonders of the sky.

a large clay pot, pl. *zitalo/matalo*, e.g. *Bukoko bwabasimunzi mububikke mucitalo.* = You should put the beer for the people of the village in the large clay pot. *Wakabumba nongo mpati itegwa citalo. Nkabela wakayaka akaanda kaIwaanga omo mwaakabikka citalo cakajisi meenda manji. Aaka kaanda akaba malende akwe.* = She made a large pot called a *citalo*. Then she built a little ritual house in which she put the clay pot with much water. This little house became her rain-shrine. *Inongo zyakali mumisela-misela. Kwakali matalo akukondoda bukoko alimwi azimwi kwakali nzyobati zipempa.* = The clay pots were of different kinds. There were large clay pots for brewing beer and again there were the clay pots which they called *zipempa*.
a head-scarf, e.g. *Bacembele basamide citambala cituba mbaamaama.* = The old lady putting on a white head-scarf is my mother.
a short rope, e.g. *Koleta citambo cakwaanga nombe tukame.* = Bring a short rope to tie the cow so that we can milk it.
a rough leather belt, e.g. *Mudaala wakalisamide citambotambo a jansi lipati akaambo kampeyo.* = The old man was wearing a rough belt and a big long coat because of the cold.
calumny, slander, e.g. *Bakaamba citamikizyo amuntu ulya.* = They slandered that person.
a false excuse, pretense, e.g. *Kuciswa kwabanyina caba citamizyo cakutaunka kucikolo.* = The illness of her mother has become an excuse for her not going to school.
a stamp for a letter to be posted, (ety. Eng.) e.g. *Mukanduulile citampa.* = Buy me a stamp. *Kobikka citampa alugwalo luya ku Lusaka.* = Put a stamp on the letter going to Lusaka.
a lid, e.g. *Koleta citampa campoto uvwunike cakulya.* = Bring the lid of the pot to cover the food.
a raised bed of earth in garden or field, e.g. *Tukasimpe cimbwali cambuto mucitampu.* = Lets go and plant seed sweet-potatoes in the raised plot.
a log, e.g. *Musunge basune kutegwa mukalete citanda cakusikka.* = Yoke the oxen so that you go and bring a block of firewood to put on the fire.
a block of firewood, e.g. *Kamusikka citande cipati kutegwa mulilo utazimi.* = Insert a big log so that the fire does not go out. Also *citanda*.
a herd, flock, e.g. *Twajana citanga cambelele cilacela mumusena.* = We found a flock of sheep grazing in the vlei.
a pond, lake, e.g. *Mpongo mukazinywisye meenda ku citangazyiba.* = Go and allow the goats drink water from the pond.
a hole in the ground around which grass grows, e.g. *Musune waceede mucitangazyiba mwazyibide kucelela.* = The ox has remained in the hollow where it used to graze.
a rough temporary roof, e.g. *Basankwa bobilo balikubikka citankili akatala kandongwe.* = Two boys were putting up a temporary roof on the groundnut granary. Also cintangali, citankaili, cibumbu.

a heap of ruins, rubbish, e.g. *Mucembele wakawaangula mutendu wanyama ibolede akuusowa acitantaala.* = The old woman got a dried piece of rotten meat from its hanging-place and threw it on a heap of rubbish.
a heap of ashes and rubbish, e.g. *Eeli tombe ukalisowele kucitantala.* = Throw this dirt on the rubbish heap. Also kabbunta.

a ladder, e.g. *Amubikke citantilo acisanza tuzwisye mapopwe abusu.* = Put this ladder against the grain-store so that we remove some maize for flour. Also malele citati a mat, e.g. *Mulwazi ulilede acitati camabu.* = The patient is lying on a reed-mat. Also kasasa.
a marvel, e.g. *Muka Moonga wakacita citazya naakabukidwe masabe.* = The wife of Moonga did an extra-ordinary thing when she was possessed by a masabe spirit.
a small bag of cloth or of beaten bark, e.g. *Zisani zyabacembele uzibikke mucitebe.* = Put the clothes of the old women in the bag.
of the Ndebele tribe, e.g. Nkoli eyi yakali acikoto mbuli kuti njacitebele. = This stick had a bulge at the head as if it were of the Ndebele tribe.
a woman's girdle of beads, e.g. *Aano mazuba bamakaintu banji tabasami citebwe muzibuno.* = Nowadays many women do not wear the citebwe around their waists.
any piece of unsown cloth, e.g. *Citeele cangu capya mulilo kumoombe.* = My piece of cloth was burnt by fire at the hem.
a ball of cloth which children play with, e.g. *Citeele cangu casweeka.* = My ball of cloth is lost.
a nest on high, e.g. *Kotanta mumusamu oyo waanzule bana bakayuni muciteente.* = Climb that tree so that you take down the bird's chicks from the nest. Also cinteente
a type of mushroom, e.g *Nitwazyila kumuunda, ndajwa citeezi munsi anzila.* = When we came from the field, I plucked a mushroom from near the path.
a plant used for relish, e.g. *Bana bamuka kuleta citeezi cakulisya.* = The children are late in bringing the citeezi plant for relish. Also cinkomba, muteezi, mudelele.

a swelling in right side of abdomen under the ribs. e.g. *Ku Choompa nkwakkala munene ucizyi kusilika citeku.* = At Choompa there lives an old man who knows how to cure a stomach swelling. Also cipelu.
the gutter of a roof, gutter-spout, drain-pipe, e.g. *Imvwula yatalika kuwa, mubikke cibulo kunsi acitelekezyo.* = When the rain begins to fall, place a bucket under the gutter.
one measure of cloth, pl. zitembe, e.g. *Mundigonkele mulembo wazitembe zyosanwe.* = Cut me five lengths of cloth.
an infectious disease, e.g. *Ndabaa citenda casikalileke.* = I have the infectious disease of AIDS.
a pumpkin, e.g. *Mudaala mumujikile citende comwe alye.* = Cook one pumpkin for the old man so that he eats.
sole of the foot, pl. *matende*, e.g. *Citende camudaala cilizimbide.* = The sole of the foot of the old man is in a swollen state. Also *cisindi*
a reed or maize-stalk door, e.g. *Kojala citendele amulyango kutegwa nkuku zitanjili.* = Close the door at the entrance to prevent the chicks from entering.
a nest on high, e.g. *Kamucoonza citendele casikakooze wazimana nkuku.* = Throw up a stick at the nest of the jackal buzzard who has finished the chickens. Also *cinteente*.
a snare, (a rough net of bark strip mounted on a circular stick-frame) e.g. *Muyuni ulya nkuku mumuteye citendele.* = Trap the bird which eats the chickens in a snare.
material used for womens traditional dress for wrapping around the waist, e.g. *Bataata, mukanduulile citenge cakusama.* = Father, buy me *citenge* material to wear. Also *mulembo*.
mashed beans, e.g. *Bana balayanda kulya citente.* = Children love to eat mashed beans. Also *cinyabo-nyabo*.
a large clay pot for cooking *nsima*, e.g. *Citentu cakali kujikila nsima.* = A large clay pot was used for cooking *nsima*. Also *caambikwa, cilongo*.
thicket, bush, e.g. *Mwana wayubide kunze aciteo kujwe amunzi.* = The child hid behind a bush to the east of the village.
a bed of reeds beside river, e.g. *nombe ziyandisya kucelela mucitete.* = The cattle love to graze among the reeds.
a reed-pipe or cigarette, e.g. *Bataata bakali kuyandisya kufwebela mucitete.* = My father used to like smoking through a reed. Also *cisanga calutete, musangu*.
okra, a plant with long-ridged seed pods, e.g. *Bana balayandisya kulya citezi.* = Children are fond of eating okra. Also *citeezi, lunkomba, munkomba, mudelele*.
a lid, e.g. *Kondipa citibisyo campoto.* = Give me the lid of the pot. Also *civwunisyo, citampa*.
a place of refuge, pl. *matijilo*, e.g. *Basilikani bakamujata nkaambo wakabula citijilo cibotu.* = The police caught him because he had no good hiding place.

a train, e.g. *Citima ciya kumusanza cafwambaana kwiinda sunu.* = The train from the north was quick to pass today. (*Citima tacili mbuli ndeke, nola acamutendele. Cileenda atubulo tobile. Cilijisi mundando wamaanda. Mumaanda muli zyuuno, malo, meenda azimbuzi. Amulilo mmuuli, busi bulasuka kunembo aco noceenda. Cilayanda meenda, mafwuta amalasa kuti ceende kabotu.* = A train is not like an aeroplane or a cart or a bicycle. It moves on a railway line. It has coaches moving in a line. There are seats inside, beds, water and toilets. Fire is even there and smoke is emitted from the front. In order to move it needs water, oil and coal.)
a brick, pl. *zitina*, e.g. *Citina cazwa amulyango candipwaya amunwe.* = The brick that fell out of the door-way smashed my finger.
a swampy place, e.g. *Tuyakukusyanga mapopwe mucitinti.* = We are going to plant maize in the swampy ground.

a tadpole, pl. *bacitinti*, e.g. *Mumwezi wa Kavwumbi-kaniini bacitinti balazyalwa mucitangazyiba.* = In the month of October the tadpoles are born in the pools. Also cintiinti, cimbilimbimba, mvwube. cito a ford, drift, bridge, e.g. Cimbayambaya cazabukila acito kuya ku Chisekese. = The truck crossed the drift going to Chisekesi.
a medicinal root that reddens water, a potion of reddened water said to bewitch, e.g. Bantu bakabikka citoba mucikala cameenda. People have put a potion of red-coloured liquid in the shallow well.
unsalted relish, e.g. Mumyaka yanzala bantu banji bakali kulya citoba = In years of hunger many people used to eat unsalted relish.

a charm said to strengthen the bond between lovers, e.g. Ndakupa mooni wakkumi lyamazuba, kolya citoba kuyeeya ndime kulikke. I give you a greeting of ten days, eat the citoba root thinking of me alone.
dried skin, e.g. Babwa bacilya citobo caanzikidwe mucisamu. = The dogs have eaten the dry skin which was hanging in the tree. Also cikutu.

a drink made in times of famine, e.g. Bakali kutwa masau antela busiikka mpoona bavwela meenda caba citobolo cakunywa. = They were pounding the fruit of the Tamarind tree and mixing it with water to become citobolo for drinking.
a stove or oven, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Amubikke nkuni mucitofwu kutegwa mulilo uvwule. Put the firewood on the stove so that there is enough fire.
supplies, stock, e.g. Musambazi wacintoolo taelede kuligwa citoko. = The shop-keeper should not run short of stock.
prison, e.g. Bamasilikani bakaunka kumujata Sinandu akumubikka mucitolokesi. = The police went to arrest Sinandu and put him in prison. Also ntolongo
a game reserve, e.g. Banyama bali mucitolongomani balakasigwa kujaigwa kakunyina pepa lizumizya. = The animals in captivity are not allowed to be killed without a licence.

reins, pl. zitolopo, e.g. Bakaiya mazina azintu zyakali kubelesegwa ciindi cakubelesya nombe mbuli majoko, zikkeyi, zitolopo, amaketani. They learnt the names of things which were used when using cattle such as yokes, pegs, reins and chains.
a sign, e.g. Munsi amugwagwa mupati bakabikka citondezyo cacikolo cili kujwe amugwagwa oyu. = Near the main road they have placed a sign for the school which is east of the road. Also mbaakani
a ruin, a deserted kraal, e.g Basankwa basusa bufwumba mucitongo. = The boys are gathering manure from the deserted kraal.
a roofless house, e.g. Asunu sincinko oyu ucoona mucitongooma. Even today the mad person still sleeps in a roofless house.
a store/shop, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Citoolo cabasyaanene cakajalwa ciindi nibakafwa. = My grandfather's store was closed when he died. Also cintoolo.

place of ancestral worship, a rain-shrine, e.g. Sena tolizyi kuti eliya zyiba ndelya Mubumbwa-Leza? Talinjilwa buyo, ndyacitowe likkala basangu. = Do you not know that this pool is fashioned by God. You just not enter it, it is a sacred place where the ancestral spirits live. Also malende.

the identification or pass of an African in colonial times pl. zituba, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kutela nibakali kubaa zituba. In the past people were taxed when they possessed an identity-card. Also citupa.
a cataract on eye, e.g. Muliso lyangu kuli citube. = There is a cataract in my eye.
the fist, e.g. Akaambo kakunyema kwabaama, mwana bamuuma cituku. My mother beat the child with her fist because of her anger Also mfwaindi.
a grain-bin, e.g. Mapopwe ali mucitula akasumpwa. = The maize in the granary has been attacked by weevils. Also cibbule.
a lump of meat without bone, a steak, e.g. Kaaze wabweza cituli canyama. The cat has taken a lump of meat.
a place for depositing offerings e.g. Bali banji bantu bali kutula zipego zyabo kucitulilo. = There were many people who were offering their gifts at the altar.
place for laying eggs, e.g. Inkuku yangu yatula kale acitulilo cayo. = The hen has already laid an egg in her place for laying eggs.
a traditional pillow or wooden rest to hold the head, e.g. Bacembele bayanda kubambilwa citulizyo. = The old woman wants a pillow to be made for her. Also citulisyo
a heap, e.g. Komwaya citulutulu cabulongo ceelane. Scatter the heap of clay so that it becomes level. Also cituntuulu.
a drill for boring wood or iron, e.g. Koya ukalombe cituluzyo kuli ba Moobe. Go and ask for a drill from Mr. Moobe. Also cidonkozyo
a watering-can, e.g. Meenda onse ngumwateka mwaatile mucitulwido. = All the water which you have drawn you should pour it in the watering-can. Also cituulwido.
a rough shelter, a roof resting on poles, e.g. Basinombe bacuumpa citumba camucembele. = The cattle-herders burnt down the rough shelter of the old woman. Also cidumba.
an owl, e.g. Ncibi omuntu kufwum-fwumana mbuli citumba. It is bad to sit in a stupid way like an owl.
basket, e.g. Nakooma wakabweza citumba cacisyu ncaakacelede wakatalika kucitenda. Nakooma took a basket of relish which she had harvested and began to cut it.

anniversary of birth, e.g. Busiku naakasisya myaka yotatwe yakuzyaIwa, Mwami Bimbe, usyi wakwe, wakacita kapobwe kakusekelela kuti mwanaakwe wakomena. Bantu nobakabungana bakakkomana kunywa tukoko twacitumbu kumaandaa mwami. When Busiku was three years old, Chief Bimbe, his father, made a little feast to celebrate the growth of his child. When the people gathered they were happy to drink the beer of the birthday-party at the chief's houses.

a bed used in child delivery, e.g. Muzibbadela moonse bamakaintu bayanda kutumbuka babalazika a citumbukilo. = In all the hospitals the women who are about to give birth are made to lie on the delivery bed.
a corpse already swollen, e.g. Beembezi bajana citumpa camoombe musyokwe. = The herders found the carcass of a calf in the bush. Also mutunta.

medicine sown into a piece of cloth which is tied to the arm as a charm and used for various purposes such as, protection, good luck, bewitching, strength in boxing etc. pl. zitumwa, e.g. Basankwa bakali kusama zitumwa nibakali kusobana nyindi kaindi. = The men were wearing charms when they were boxing in the past.
the hump of a bull, e.g. Mucende wabataata ulaa citunda cipati. = The bull of my father has a big hump.
a basket, e.g. Bakamwale balayiisigwa kubumba zıbıya akuluka *zıtundu*, bamwi nzycbati *zisuwe*. = The initiates were taught to mould pots and to weave *zitundu* baskets, which some call zisuwo.

a temporary hut in field, a shelter with thatched roof and no walls, e.g. Basankwa beelede kuyaka *citungu* cakuyaminina basokwe kumuunda. = The boys ought to build a look-out for scaring off the monkeys in the field. Bana kabaya bakayote *mucitungu*. = The children should go and warm themselves at the fire in the hut.
a medicinal root used for inflammations and for making food appetizing, pl. *zungulu*, e.g. Bamakaintu bakaletelela *zungulu*. = The women brought along the medicinal roots.
a small hill, e.g. Ndajana bowananda *acitunta*. = I found mushrooms on a small hill.

a ridge, e.g. *Cituntatunta* cadamu ciyandika kubambulula akubikka ambi mamvwu. = The dam wall needs to be remade and soil added. Mfwulumende yakali kulonzya bantu mumasena mapya *muzituntatunta* mutasiki meenda a mulonga wa Kariba. = The government was moving people to higher ground where the water of Kariba does not reach.

a raised mound of earth in garden as for sweet-potatoes, e.g. Ncinda-uka kuzyila kumbewu, ndali kumwaya *cituntaulu* cali mumbewu. = The reason why I have come late from the garden is that I have been leveling out a mound of earth which was in the garden. Also *cituntuulu, citampu, mubunda*.
a round object, e.g. Kondiletela cigabba *cituntuli* eco cili mulutantambeba. = Bring me that round tin which is on top of the wall of the house. Also *kabulunge*.

a raised bed of sweet potatoes, e.g. *Basicikolo basya cituntuulu.* = The pupils are digging a raised plot for sweet potatoes. *Cituntuulu camagwili calampisya.* = The raised bed of potatoes is too high. Also *cituntaulu*

a pass such as indigenes had to carry in colonial days, pl. *zitupa*, e.g. *Teesi cibotu, bazyukulu bangu, kuya kukubeleka kamutanapegwa zitupa abamakuwa ku Bbooma pe.* = It is not good, my grand-children, to go and work abroad without been given passes from the whites at the Boma. *Bamatata bakali kutela kwiinda mucitupa kaindi.* = Our forefathers paid tax through passes long ago.
a foot, an animals paw, e.g. *Syaazyana masiku bakamuyasa sumo acituta.* = They wounded the night-dancer in the foot with a spear.

a nest, pl. *zituuntu*, e.g. *Nkuku zyoonse zyakalitalikide kale kuseluka kuzwa mumasamu amuzituuntu mozyaali koona.* = All the hens had begun to come down out of the trees and nests where they had been sleeping. Also *citeente*
a cloth patch, e.g. *Kobikka citwibi mpucayauka cibbudula cako.* = Put on a patch where your shorts are torn. Also *cigamba.*
an instalment, pl. *zityogi-tyogi*, e.g. *Uleelede kubbadela cikwelete cipati muzityogi-tyogi.* = You ought to pay a big debt in instalments. Also *cityoki.*
a heap of things mixed up together, e.g. *Sikansondo walundika cityope-tyope mulubuwa Iwakwe.* = A mad person has heaped a collection of things in his courtyard. Also *cidyobe-dyobe.*
Also *cityope-tyope.*
a wall-less roofed house, a roof resting on the ground, e.g. *Mweemba wacuumpa civwabi.* = Mweemba has burnt the shelter. *Mucivwabi kwatula nkuku. = A hen had laid an egg in the shelter.
handful, e.g. *Ndasankamuna civwaki candongwe akuziyoka.* = I took a handful of groudnuts and roasted them.
a bad smell, e.g. *Kanji-kanji mubbunga lyabantu kuli civwambu.* = Most times there is a bad smell in a crowd of people. *Aawa kuli civwambu cibi.* = There is a bad smell here. Also cinunko.
a shelter, e.g. *Bakanjila mucivwavwa.* = They entered the shelter.
stubbourness, e.g. *Canakazi cili boobu cilaa civweku-vweku.* = That kind of a woman is full of stubbourness. Also nkazi
a mixture of things, e.g. *Koleta civwelanyo kutegwa cakulya cinunkilile kabotu.* = Bring a variety (of spices) so that the food has a nice aroma.

the mixture of fermenting beer the day before it is fully brewed, e.g. *Bakali kunywa civwele amantabe.* = They were drinking mixed and unmixed beer the day before it was ready. *Nokwakaba kulubundu-bundu, bakanyamuka batozya kumusanza kwa Chibeengelele kwaali civwele.* = When it became dark, they set of going south to Chibeengelele where there was a mixed gathering of people.

a mixture of something with water, e.g. *Nceeci civwelenganyo camisamu cakunywa civwelenganyizidwe ameenda kutegwa mulwazi abe abulowa mumubili.* = Here is a mixture of medicines mixed with water for the patient to drink so that he has blood in his body.
premature grey hair, e.g. *Jabala ucili mwana, eziya imvwi ncivwibala biyo.* = Jabala is still very young, that grey hair is just premature.
a fat insect or grub, e.g. *Eezi zyuuka ziitwa kuti bacivwinye. Izina ndeena lilakonzya kwaamba bubi bwazyo*
kutinye, nkulya kapati.* = These insects are called 'bacivwinye'. The name describes their badness because 'civwinye' means to eat a lot, explaining why they are named so. Also civwunye.
a type of bird, the babbler, e.g. *Simpongo weenena civwocive mumutumbi.* = The goatsherd spied a babbler in the *mutumbi* tree. Also civwoocciye.
dry soil, e.g. *Mapopwe twakaasyanga mucivwu ciyumu.* = We planted the maize in hard dry soil.
source of wealth, e.g. *Civwubilo cangu cakazwa mukuulisya mapowe.* = My source of wealth came from selling maize.

a custom by which the parents, while still alive, gives their children wealth to be kept by their uncle for them, e.g. *Bamwi bazyali balapa bana babo lubono kabacipona. Eeci cilengwa citegwa ncivwubu.* = Some parents give their children wealth when they are still alive. This custom is called civwubu. Also cikono.
any domestic animal or bird, e.g. *Kufwumbwa civwubwa ciyandika kubambwa akukwabililwa kumalwazi.* = Any domestic animal needs to be cared for and protected from diseases.
a hippopotamus, e.g. *Civwubwe wadingamuna bwato bwabazezi mumulonga mupati.* = The hippo overturned the fishermen's boat in the big river.

a tent, a temporary dwelling, pl. *zivwuka*, e.g. *Civwuka cesu catalika kuzwizya akaambo kakuvwula kwamvwula.* = Our tent has started leaking because of the heaviness of the rain. *Basimbi bakali kuyaka zivwuka kumbo amunzi.* = The girls were making temporary shelters west of the village. Munene wakatutuma tobasankwa kuya kugonka zisamu akuya kufwunda loozi kuti ayakilwe *civwuka*. = The old man sent us boys to go and cut old wood and to strip fibre in order to build a shelter.

hailstones, e.g. *Ijilo kwakawa mvwula yacivwulamabwe*. = Yesterday hailstones fell. *Eeyi mvwula yakajisi guwo a civwulamabwe*. = This rain had a strong wind and hailstones. Naakasola kutongooka kuti kuli wakamutendela cisani, yakakolomoka yacivwulama*bwe*. = When she tried to complain that her cloth had been cut, the hail-stones fell down. (i.e. She received a fierce reply.)
roof of hut, e.g. *Kambizyi kakavwupula civwuli cakaanda kampongo*. = The whirlwind tore off the roof of the goat hut. Also *ciluli*.

a type of container used for collecting honey, pl. *zivwulumuto*, e.g. *Wakacita civwulumuto amatuvwu amuloolo*. = He made a container from the leaves of the wild-sop tree. *Beembezi nibamana kulida buci, babamba umwi aumwi civwulumuto cakubikkila buci*. = When the herders had harvested the honey, they each made a container in which they put the honey. *Bakatalika kusuma zivwulumuto zyamatuvwu mugooni kuti babwezele buci*. = They began to sew together leaves from the *mugooni*. tree as a container so that they could take away the honey. Also *cintuunya*
hair gathered into a cone, e.g. *Bamwi basimbi balayanda kwaanga masusu abo civwuma*. = Some girls like to gather their hair into a cone.
a coconut, e.g *Kamubombola civwuma eci kutegwa caandane tulye kabotu*. = Beat this coconut so that it breaks up and we can eat it.
a bush, shrub, e.g. *Civwuna cimwi tiicakagonkwa mumuunda*. = One bush has not been cut in the field. Also *citewo*.
the peak of a circular roof, e.g. *Civwuna cakaluli kakatala tiicakavwumbwa*. = The peak of the roof of the small bin is not thatched.
first rains, e.g. *Mvwula yacivwunanombe yakatelekezya malambwa akulizya maande*. = The first rains were collected in the ponds and caused the frogs to make noise.
a lid, e.g. *Eeyi mpoto taijisi civwunisyo pe*. = This pot is without a lid.
a clump of trees, e.g. *Mumbewu yangu kwakazwa civwuntula camusangu*. = In my garden a clump of *musangu* trees have appeared.

a flat edible green insect which eats grain, pl. *bacivunye*, e.g. *Bacivwunye baamana mapopwe matete mumuunda*. = Insects have finished the green maize in the field. *Eci cili buyo mbuli umwi muntu akati kabo upedwe cuuno cipati mumfwulumende, ibantu bakumukatazya kuyanda milimo mbabaabo mbocizwa limwi abamukowaakwe. Pele nanjizya omwe, oyu muntu uba civwunye wakalilya mucila*. = This is like a certain man among them who is given a big post in the government, the people who trouble him looking for work are those who come from his own clan. But when one of them is given a job, this one is like a maggot who eats his tail. (i.e. he becomes a nuisance.) Also *civwinye*.
a maggot, e.g. *Inkuku yacilya civwunyu cazwa munyama yakayuma*. = The chicken has eaten a maggot which has come out of the dried meat.

a piece of dried branch tied to a string or rope, used as a trap for killing birds, e.g. *Civwupu cilabelesegwa mukuteya tuyuni. Civwupu cavwupuka civwupula tuyuni tunji akutujaya*. = The *civwupu* trap is used for catching birds. The trap is used by pulling the string (attached to a branch) with force so that the branch hits the birds and kills them.
a fan, e.g. Koyasya *civwupuuzyo* tuyanda muwo utontola munanda. = Switch on the fan, we want cool air in the house. Also *cipapanzyo*
a mouthful, e.g. Wakabikka *civwutu* cacikandi mukanwa. = He put a mouthful of porridge in the mouth.
a clump of trees
sound of a cataract in a river, e.g. Nindakasika munsaa mulonga ndakamvwa *civwuumo* cameenda. = When I arrived near the river I heard the noise of the cataracts.
outward appearance of a person, features, countenance, shape, complexion e.g. Ooyu musimbi ulaa *ciwa* cibotu. = This girl has a good appearance.
bead-fringe used on top of sikomoka skirt, e.g. Ndabona musimbi uujisi *ciwaula*. = I saw a girl having a bead- fringe on her skirt.

a type of plant (Eurphorba ingens), the stem laetex is used as fish poison. The boiled thickened milky laetex is mixed with *mwaani* sap and used as birdlime. The laetex is also an ingredient to improve a dog's hunting ability by rubbing its teeth with the roots. e.g. *Muciwawa* tamujaniki *matu* ajanika mu*misamu imwi*. = In the *ciwawa* plant you do not find the leaves found in other plants. Also *muwawa*.
noise, disturbance, e.g. *Mucikolo omu muli ciwawa*. = There is a disturbance in the school.
be short-tempered, e.g. Munene Denkete wakalaa *ciwawa*. = The old man Denkete was short-tempered.
fried dry maize, e.g. Bantu bamu Zambezi balayanda kulya *ciwaya*. = People of the Zambezi valley like to eat fried dry maize.
a criminal, e.g. *Ciwebenga* cakabba *nombe zyone*. = The criminal stole four cows. Also *cigwebenga*.
a large container, e.g. Mutinta, bweza *ciweemani* undeetele meenda ndilikube-kube amubili. = Mutinta, take the big container and bring me water so that I quickly rub my body.
a crocodile, e.g. *Ciwena waluma nombe yali kunywa meenda mulwizi*. = The crocodile attacked the cow which was drinking water in the lake.
confusion, e.g. Cakaile kuba *ciweweewe* nibakali kulwana bana. = Confusion broke out when the children were fighting.
a climbing plant, e.g. Ndajaya kayuni mpoona kaangila mumamvwa *aciwezezi*. = I killed a bird and then it hung on the thorns of a climbing plant.

plant used as a medicine for deliverance from spirit possession, e.g. Musamu oyu *waciwezezi* wakali wakutenta kati antela munyokwabo wanjilwa zyeelo. Aboobo wakali kutegwa 'mmutanda zyeelo' nkaambo kwanoonga naa muntu waumpilizigwa nguwo, inga zyali kumuzwa zyeelo ezyo. = This medicine, *ciwezi*, was for fumigating if perhaps spirits had taken possession of your relative. And so it was called 'that which drives out spirits' because if a person was fumigated with it the spirits would leave him.
the backbone of an animal, e.g. *Ciwezo* camunyati nciyumu nta. = The backbone of a buffalo is extremely hard.
a species of parasite tree, e.g. tree. *Ciwezyezyi* mmusamu ubelesegwa kusalazya bamukamufwu. = Ciwezyezyi is the medicine used to cleanse the widows or widowers. Also *ciwezezi*.
a big creeper, a poisonous thorn tree, e.g. *Mamvwa aciwezyizyi alayasa kapati*. = The thorns of the *ciwezyizyi* tree pricks a lot.
