a green relish used in cold season, e.g. Ciindi campeyo bantu balya cisyu caciwiyangongo. = During the cold season people eat the relish ciwiyangongo.
bad name, notoriety, e.g. Musankwa waba Moonga ulaa ciwo cibi akaambo kakubba. = The son of Moonga has a bad name because of stealing.
bad smell, e.g. Ndalikununkizya ciwo canyama inunka munzila nindali kweenda. = I got the bad smell of stinking meat on the path when I was walking.
a lot of noise, e.g. Bana nibakali kusobana cakali ciwowoowo. = When the children were playing there was a lot of noise.

the liquid at unfermented stage before it becomes beer, e.g. Bana baniini mbabanywa ciwunti. Little children are the ones who drink sweetbeer. Also cibwantu. = ciya gas, foul air, bad breath, e.g. Koya ukasambe mukanwa kutegwa cileke kununka ciya. Go and wash out your mouth to remove the bad breath.

support against which person or thing leans, pl. ziyaamino, e.g Ziyaamino zyazyuuno zyamipando zyatyoka mucimbayambaya nibazileta. = The frames of the chairs had been broken when they brought them in the lorry.
See ciyaamino.

a mixture of fermented and non-fermented meal in water, e.g. Baneene bakumba ciyaaya. = My grand-mother brews a drink from unfermented and fermented meal. Awa amunzi bakajana bantu basiluzyalo, bakasaanguna kubasomba ciyaaya. = There at the village they found kind people, who first offered them a mixture of fermented and non-fermented meal in water. Also cipyaapya.
a woman's girdle of beads, e.g. Ndabona nakalindu uyabikide ciyabala. I saw a young woman wearing a girdle of beads. Also cikaba

a song sung by one person, accompanied by friction drum or rattle, can be a sad or praise song, a song descriptive of some personal experience, pl. ziyabilo, e.g. Ciyabilo cakayabila mwana wa Himaambo musimbi, cakapa kuti bantu boonse boomoke kulila. = The song sung by the daughter of Himaambo made all the people cry. Balombwana bakali kuyabila ziyabilo zyaali kuyasa myoyo. = The men were singing ciyabilo songs which pierced the hearts.
what builds up, e.g. Mwana wakazyalwa ino bakamusamika musamu waciyakilizyo munsingo. They clothed the new-born baby with a medicine around the neck for strengthening the body.
bali kumuyasaula nsimbo zyaciyakilizyo amubili. = They made cuts on the patient for strengthening the body. ciyakilizyo camubili = what nurtures the body. Also cisitilizyo.
upright building pole, e.g. Kwabulila ciyako comwe caacikuta. = One pole of the hut is missing.
first streak of morning light, e.g. Sikutuswaya wasika aciyamaca. = Our visitor arrived at dawn. Also cinyamaca

root smoked by girls as love charm, an aphrodisiac, e.g. Kabunga kabasimbi kafweba ciyandankwela. = A group of girls are smoking a love-potion. Musimbi waula ciyandankwela. The girl has bought a lovecharm.
a fool, pl. ziyanga, e.g. Nsima tiinajikwa, ino bauso balalya nzi? Muli ziyanga. The nsima has not yet been cooked, what will your father eat? You are stupid ones.
a bird's crop (a pouch in a bird's gullet where food is stored or prepared for digestion), e.g. Mubwa walya ciyangilo cankuku. = The dog has eaten the bird's crop.

a custom or tradition, e.g. Batonga balaa ciyanza cakusekelela kooloka akulumba bamana kutebula kwiinda mukukumba maindi. = The Batonga have a custom of celebrating the eating of the first maize and thanking when they have finished harvesting by brewing beer for the ritual festivals.
a habit, the temperamant of a person, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa ciyanza cakubba nyama mumpoto. = This child has a habit of stealing meat from the pot. Also cilengwa.
bond, e.g. Mootokala taukwe ciyanze. A vehicle has no guarantee that it won't break down.

instrument for cutting pumpkin into pieces, e.g. Muka Sicibende wakalitamausya kuti wabula ciyasamutende. The wife of Sicibende pretended that she did not have the instrument for cutting pumpkin into pieces.
an instrument for making cuts to heal a person, e.g. Mukaule ciyasauzyo kutegwa mulwazi akayasaulwe cifwumo. Go and buy a razor-blade so that we can cut the patient tomorrow. Also mbeli
a head-ornament of beads, e.g. Ndaciluba ciyawala cangu kumulonga. I forgot my beaded headornament at the river. Also cimpwampwa

a type of dance at the initiation ceremony in which the initiate dances alone in the centre of the other women. e.g. Basimbi balasamikwa milemba kumeso nobazyana ciyayaale. = Girls wear a veil on their faces when they dance the ciyayaale.

a little brush, e.g. Nsefwa uisanzye aciyayizyo kutegwa isinkuke tusena twakasinka. = Wash the sieve with a little brush so that the blocked holes may be opened. (this brush can be made from ciswi, a type of plant)

the bank of a meandering river, e.g. Wakapiluka kutobelezya zyooko zyoonse kuti antela ulajana aciyeeleko mpaakayaama mwana mumatete pele wakajana kunyina acilibonya. She went back following all the places, thinking that she might find a meandering bank where her child might be resting in the reeds, but she found nothing to be seen.
a slice of honey-comb, e.g. Kondipa ciyeeya cabuci comwe buyo. = Give me just one slice of the honey-comb. Also ceya.
a thought, e.g. Ciyeeyo nceeli kuyeeya masiku candipa kubaa cilabila. = The thought I was thinking last night made be sleepless.
something which causes you to remember, e.g. Cipego nciyeezyo camweenzinyoko. A gift is a remembrance of your friend.
a honey-comb with honey, pl. meeya Also ceeya, ciyeeya
rain-cloud, pl. mayoba, e.g. Asunu kwaba kale ciyoba. = And to-day it is already overcast.
safe, e.g. Kondibikkila mali aya muciyobozyo cako. Put this money in your safe. Also ciyobwedo.
a cupboard or rack, store, record, e.g. Ciyobwedo camitiba cilaa magukusu manji. = The cupboard is full of cockroaches.
an earthworm, pl. ziyokaanzi, e.g. Nzeezi ziyokaanzi. = Here are earthworms.
a poker for the fire, e.g. Kobelesya ciyokolozyo kuyokolola mulilo kutegwa utapyi. = Use the poker to stir up the fire so that you don't get burnt.
a charm reputed to restore health, e.g. Muntu nalisitide ciyokolozyo, uyakufwa ---|--akale. = Even though a person's health is protected by a charm, he will die later on.
something which causes fear, e.g. Cinkwamu _nciyoosyo_ kubana baka-tazya kwiile kulila. = A mask is used to frighten children who are troublesome in crying for no reason.

commotion, such as the sound of wailing and lamenting, e.g. Cakaile kuba _ciyooyooyo_ nanda yoonse mu-cembele naakafwa. = There was a great outburst of weeping in the whole house when the old woman died.

chaff of winnowed sorghum, pl. ziyu, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu ulomba ciyu cakubikka mubukoko. = This woman is asking for sorghum-chaff to put in the beer. (Proverb, Bazike bakaabana ciyu = Slaves share the chaff.) Also masiki, masengasenga
a drought, e.g. Mwaka wakamana cakali _ciyumayuma_ aboobo uno mwaka kuli nzala ciyoosya. = Last year was a dry one and so this year there is a terrible famine.

a receptacle for carrying various things, e.g. Koya ukalombe _ciyu-mwido_ kuli bina Mooya kutegwa ubwezele cakulya. = Go and ask Mooya's mother for a container so that you can take the food. Matwi aanzovwu ayakuba _ziyumwi-do_ cabuci bwangu. = The ears of ele-phants will become containers for my honey.
a disliked/ unfortunate bird, e.g. _Ciyuni_ ciciswa cakafwa jilo. = The sick bird died yesterday
relish of a wild plant, e.g. Bacembele balayanda kujika _ciyuniyuni_. = The old women like to cook the relish known as _ciyuniyuni_.
a shelter, e.g. Bamakaintu bakajwe bwizu bwakuyaka _ciyusilo_ ca-mvwula kumuunda. = Let the women go and cut grass for building a shelter from the rain in the field.
tendency to reveal a secret, e.g. Mainza, kuti wanyema ulaa _ciyutuyutu_. = Mainza, if annoyed, reveals secrets.
the name of a tree, e.g. Muyuni uyaka cinteente _muciyuula_. = A bird is building a nest in the _ciyuula_ tree.
a bridge, e.g. _Cizabukilo_ cakalonga cakatolwa meenda. = The bridge of the stream was taken away by the water.
a platform, e.g. Koya uyanike maila _acizali_. = Go and put the maize out to dry on the platform. Also busanza, buzalo

a nest, e.g. Maji aankuku zyangu ncaatakali kulibonya _muzizangala_, wakali kwiide kusanina kalomba kakwe masiku. = The reason why the eggs of my hens were not seen in the nest was because she was feeding her boyfriend at night

a container for carrying chick-ens, pl. zizekwe, e.g. Naakaula nkuku zinji wakaluka _zizekwe_ nkaambo wakali ku-yanda kuti kasusa _cizekwe_ comwe-comwe kutola ku Monze. = When he had bought many chickens, he wove chicken baskets because he wanted to transport each basket taking it to Monze. Also cisekwe

what is held in the hand when ritually mourning by walking to and fro, pl. zizembyo, e.g. Kondipa _cizembyo_ cangu ndiyanda kuya kuzemba. = Give me my funeral rattle, I want to move up and down. Bakalibambila zisamo _azizem-byo_ zyangoma. = They prepared the fun-eral attire and the ritual sticks for dancing to the drum,
a pond or pool, e.g. Mpongo zya-ya kukunywa meenda _kuciziba_. = The goats have gone to drink water at the pool.
concussion, e.g. Wakabaa cizilo. = She was stunned. Also cizilu.
smear-marks, e.g. Balila balaa cizilo amubili. = The mourners have smearmarks on the body. Also cilambo.
a black stone for shining pottery. e.g. Baama bakali kubelesya cizilo kukwizinga zibiya. = My mother was using a black stone to shine pots.

loss of consciousness, e.g. Akaambo kanzala njindamvwide, ndabede acizilu. Because of the hunger I felt, I became faint. (musamu wakufwa cizilu = a general anaesthetic which induces sleep and insensitivity to pain when patient is undergoing an operation. e.g. Basilisi bapa musamu wakufwa cizilu nobapandula balwazi. = Doctors give a general anaesthetic when they are operating on patients.)
smearing, e.g. Eeyi nanda ilaa cizilulule cibotu. This house is beautifully plastered.

magic power, guardian spirit, e.g. Muntu oyu ulijisi cizimba cikali. = This man has powerfull magic. Cizimba cakwe cakali kumukwabilila kufwumbwa buyo cakali kuyanda kucitika kuli nguwe. = His spirit was protecting him whenever anything was about to happen to him.

a traditional medicine used by witchdoctors to cure diseases which resist treatment, e.g. Musondi wakati kwakaceede comwe, eco icakali ncecizimba cipati cakali kuyandika bunene icakali kwiitwa kuti musebelele. Bamwi bakali kucaamba kuti museensye. = The diviner said that there remained one charm which was the most powerful which was needed much for old age which was called musebelele. Some called it museensye.
a swelling, e.g. Ndabaa cizimbwa amubili woonse. I have a swelling all over the body.
a tendency to swell, e.g. Aandiluma kauka ndazimba kapati nkaambo ndaa cizimbya. = I swelled up a lot where the insect bit me, because I easily swell.
a departed spirit, e.g. Mudoombe wakakona cizimo causyi cakuvwima. = Mudoombe inherited his father's spirit in hunting.
mania, obsession, habit controlled by an evil spirit, inclination, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa cizimo cabukolwi. This child has an inclination to drunkeness. (cizimo cakubba = bad habit of stealing)
a hindrance to growth, e.g. Tombwe mmubi kubana baniini. Ulapa cizindwe cakutakomena kufwambaana. = Tobacco smoking is bad for children. It makes them grow slowly.
a coiled brass bracelet, e.g. Ndakaula cizinga cakusama kukwaanza. = I bought a coiled brass bangle to wear on my wrist.
a grain bin, e.g. Ooyu musankwa wakandilukila butala bubotu bwaçizinga. = This boy made me a good grain bin. (-zinga = coil strips of wood around to make a grain bin.)
dizziness, e.g. Bamakaintu bamwi balaa mada inga baciswa cizunguboombe. Some pregnant women suffer from dizziness. Also zyuungwe
a member, limb, joint, e.g. Cimwi acimwi cizo camubili cilaa mulimo waco. Each member of the body has its function.

habit, e.g. Wakanyamuka munene awo mpaakakkede kumwi oku katalekezyi cizo cakwe cakuvwukaula mucila. = The old man stood up from where he was seated without stopping the habit of waving the tail about.
a snake, derogatory, e.g. Cizoka cilaa mukondo oyu ncipati. The evil snake who has left this track is a big one.
a fishing-basket, e.g. Nditukka cizongo cakuzelezya nswi. = I am putting a fishing-basket on my head.
a handbag, a hamper, pl. zizongo, e.g. Musimbi ulaluka zisuwo azizongo. = A girl makes baskets and handbags.
the crest of a hoopoe, e.g. Inkunkuunku nkayuni kajisi cizonzoolo cibotu. The hoopoe is a bird which has a beautiful crest. Also cisunka, cinyonzololo.
old useless grass, e.g. Cizu cavwumbulwa acijikila mucuumpe. = You should burn the useless grass taken down from the kitchen roof.
a bridge, e.g. Zimwi nombe zilayoowa kuzabukila acizubukilo. = Some of the cattle fear to cross at the bridge.
a mat used in fishing, e.g. Cizubyo nceekaluba kumulonga cakabbigwa. The fishing mat I forgot at the river was stolen.
a mat used to partition room, a blind, a screen, e.g. Beenzu tabeelede kupenuna cizuli. = Visitors should not open the bedroom partition.
a basket, e.g. Baneene bakaula cizuma cibotu. = My grandmother bought a nice basket. Also cinzuma

a nesting coop, pl. zizumbo, e.g. Bana balayaka zizumbo zyatuyuni. The children build coops for little birds. Muzizumbo balabikka miliindo. Miliindo balaita kuti mai. In the coops they put rounded objects. They call the rounded objects eggs. Balaikumba mbuli tuyuni mbutukumba mai ato muzizumbo. = They sit on them as little birds sit on their eggs in the nest. Also kazumbo.

an agreement, pact, contract, covenant, e.g. Bayi bakabamba cizuminano abasicikolo babo cakuti utiikabainde mumusunko uyakupegwa mabbuku azilembyo. The teacher made an agreement with his/her pupils that whoever would surpass all in the examination would be given a present of books and pens. Also cipangano
a sound, e.g. Cizumo camvwula yalikuwa cali cikali. The sound of the rain which was falling was fierce.
state of sitting and waiting a long time, e.g. Ndafwa cizungu kulindila mweenzuma. = I am tired of waiting for my friend.
rabies in dogs, e.g. Kaluumwaya uciswa cizungubwebwe. = The dog Kaluumwaya has rabies. Also cinsuungwe.
become dizzy, e.g. Wakaba acizungubwebwe. She became dizzy.

a fainting fit, e.g. Mweetwa uciswa cizunguboombe. = Mweetwa is susceptible to fainting fits. Mwana walikuzinguluka ncaabaa cizunguboombe. = The child was going round and round, that is why she is dizzy. Naakali kweenda boobo wakali kwiide kuzeenteka kubee mwana waba acizunguboombe. When she was moving like that she was just staggering like a child who was subject to dizziness.
an evil spirit, e.g. Cizwa cali mukambizyi canjila mwana ncaaciswa. = The reason why the child is sick is because the spirit which was in the whirlwind entered her.
a spirit taken away by witch, e.g. Kulangika kuti cizwa camulwazi oyu cakabwezegwa amulozi. It seems as if the spirit of this person has been taken by a witch.
a dish-cloth, cloth for cleaning, e.g. Wakatula cizwaato ncaakali kupukutizya mootokala. = She put down the cloth with which she was shining the car.

an electric shock, e.g. Nindali kujika nsima acitofwu, cizwiimya catiindikwele nkaambo nsiindasamide mabbusu. When I was cooking nsima at the stove, an electric shock nearly pulled me because I was not wearing shoes.
a marriage engagement, e.g. _Ba Mutinta a Makweelele bajisi cizyabo ciyumu._ = Mutinta and Makweelele have a strong engagement. Also cisyabo.
a fowl's womb, e.g. _Eeyi nkuku nciyali kuumfwumana, iji lyakafwida mucizyalilo._ = That's why this hen was not active, an egg had broken in its womb.
a dance, e.g. _Tuya kucizyano cesu kunkolola._ = We are going to our dance at the initiation ceremony.
a shirt, e.g. _Mudaala wakabweza cizyempe wasama._ = The old man took a shirt and put it on.
a stupid or crazy person, e.g. _Wakeenda akoona musyokwe akuba cizyinya cibule maanu._ = He went and slept in the bush and became insane.
a member or limb, e.g. _Mutwe ncizyo camubili wamuntu._ = The head is a member of the human body. Also cizo.
a very large portion of meat, e.g. _Mwamana kufwunda musune, munditendele cizyo canyama._ = When you have finished skinning the ox, cut for me a large portion of the meat.
revenge, e.g. _Ncibi kujosya cizyole._ = It is bad to take revenge.
a twisting pinch, e.g. _Umwi sicikolo bayi bamusyamba cizyundula-bacembele asaya._ = The teacher gave one of the pupils a twisting pinch on the cheek. Also cimoni.
a spoon, e.g. _Amulete conco twaapuzye cisyu._ = Bring a spoon so that we share out the relish.

type of tree (_Boscia grandiflora_) leaves burnt as insect repellant and burned to deliver the sick from spirits. e.g. _Muntu wanjilwa zeelo umpililwa conswe._ = A person who has been entered by spirits has the leaves of the _conswe_ tree burnt (to drive them out).
a medicinal root for the disease cibongozi or cuufa, e.g. _Mumuyandawide musamu waconzwe Choona._ = Look for the medicinal root for Choona.
a disease in children, e.g. _Bana baciswa conzwe tabalyi kabotu._ Children who have the disease of _conzwe_ do not eat well.
a spike for killing hippo, e.g. _Bazezi bakaula cooba cakujazya bacivwubwe._ = The fishermen bought a spike for killing hippo.
a thorn tree with curved thorns, e.g. _Cisani camwana cavwakwa mamvwa acoobamfwe._ = The dress of the child has been hooked by the thorns of a thorn-tree.

useless person, e.g. Kachila _ngucoobbwani wamuntu._ = Kachila is a useless kind of person. Bantu bakumunzi boonse bakamubeda _bacoobbwani._ = All the people at the village became useless people to him.
a circle of hunters closing in, e.g. _Bavwimi bajaya banyama banji kucoobelo._ = The hunters have killed many animals by encircling them in an enclosed space. Also cila
a blind animal, e.g. _Eeci coombe ncoofwu._ = This calf is blind.
a turn in a river, pl. zyooko, e.g. _Mwana wakanyikila mumulonga wakasowelwa acooko._ = The child who was drowned in the river was thrown up where the river turns.

a hidden place, e.g. _Balaa nanda bakaisisa nsima kucooko nobakamubona mweenzu amulyango._ = The owners of the house hid the _nsima_ in a hidden place when they saw a visitor at the entrance. _Wakapiluka kumulonga kutobezya zyooko zyoonse kuyandaula mwaakwe._ = She returned to the river following along all the hidden places searching for her child.

province, territory, neighbourhood, e.g. _Kucooko cakumusanza bantu banji_ bakanana Chitonga. = In the southern province many people speak Chitonga. Ngoma zyakalila zyakuzyibya cooko coonse kuti kuli waloboka mumunzi. = The drums sounded to inform the whole neighbour-hood that someone had passed away in the village.
a bag, e.g. Mudolopo lya Lusaka bakandibbida coola. = In the city of Lusaka they stole my bag.
small barbel fish, pl. toola, e.g. Nindali kuloba ndajaya coola. = When I was fishing, I killed a barbel fish.
good luck, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa coolwe, bantu baide kumupa zisani. = This child is lucky, the people just give him clothes.

biggest black ant with four white spots on rump said to bring good luck = kauka kacoolwe, e.g. Basilisi bavwela kauka nkaanga coolwe mumusamu wamilimo. = The herbalists mix the big black ant with other medicines which brings good luck with the medicine to help one find a job.
a useless drum, e.g. Eeci cooma tacili kabotu pe. = This useless drum is no good.
a type of bird, the blacksmith plover, e.g. Coombamilangu ulakumba mumusamu omuya. = The blacksmith plover is sitting on her eggs in that tree over there.

insect played with by children who ask it where it rains, e.g. Aaba bana ncibamuka kuzyila kucikolo bali kusobanya coombankutu munzila. = The reason why these children are late arriving from school is that they were playing with an insect on the way.
See coombankutu.
a cow which has only a little milk, e.g. Sunu mutacikami coombeboya nkaambo mwana ulafwa nzala. = Do not milk that cow today as the calf will go hungry.
a cow which has no milk Also coombeboya.
a plaited wicker fishbasket, e.g. Twali kuteya nswi mumulonga acoonabudonga. = We were trapping fish in the river with a fishing-basket.
full moon, the time soon after the evening meal, (lit. when the babies are asleep), e.g. Bana banji baloona ciindi cacoonancece. = Many children sleep soon after the evening meal.
late at night when the elders sleep, e.g. Bapati boona acoonankalamba. = The elders go to sleep late.
moon appearing late in the night sky, e.g. Muntu wakajisi Iweendo lulamfwu wakazwa acoonamukunu. = The man who had a long journey started out when the moon appeared late in the sky.
weak at the knees, e.g. Musankwa wakaba acoondamazwi naakabona siluwe. = The man became weak at the knees when he saw the leopard.

a thicket or thick bush or forest, e.g. Eezi nkuni twazitebba mucoonde camwami. = We collected the firewood from the thick forest of the chief. Wakasika kucoonde ciitwa kuti Nabbole. Loonde olu lulayoosya kumuntu buyo. = He arrived at the forest called Nabbole. This forest is terrifying to a mere human. (oonde = small thicket) Also citeo Coonde calubu = a reed bed by a river, Also citete, cibu, butete.
a dense crowd, e.g. Nindakasika adilwe ndakajana coonde cabantu. = When I arrived at the funeral I found a dense crowd of people.

a mash of groundnuts or flying-ants, e.g. Coonde candongwe ncibotu kuzilazila acinkwa = Peanut butter is good to smear on bread. Coonde canswa ncibotu kulisya nsima. = Flying-ant mash is good to eat nsima with.
a mash of salted ground nuts, e.g. Bataata bayanda kulisya coondoonde nsima. = Father wants to eat nsima with mashed groundnuts.
a sleeping place, e.g. Ndaunka kukubamba cooneno cabana. = I am going to prepare a sleeping place for the children.
a castrated goat, e.g. Eeci coongo cilineneede kapati. = This castrated goat is very fat.

a disturbance, noise, e.g. Kwakaba coongo nibakalwana bantu kubukoko. = There was turmoil when people fought at the beer gathering. = Maulu aamubbi mmaubauba, taapangi coongo. The feet of a thief are soft, they do not make noise.
a black insect found at the beginning of the rainy season, e.g. Bacoonzamponono bakali kulila cakusabila. = The black insects were crying loudly.
a useless person, e.g. Muzwangana nzi ayooyo coonzamponono? = Why are you arguing with that useless fellow.

a type of bush, e.g. Syaanasulwe wakadwantuka akupuna kusule aciteyo cacoonzwe. = The hare jumped and went through the bush. Kusule ananda kwakali citeyo cacoonzwe mwakali kukkala sikoswe mucembele. = Behind the house there was a bush where an old rat used to live.
a spike for killing hippos, e.g. Bataata bakajisi coowe cakujazya bacivwubwe. = My father has a spike for killing hippos. Also cooba.
a type of relish, e.g. Cisyu cacotwe nsenacilide pe. = I have not yet eaten cotwe relish.
froth, e.g. Meenda aya alaa covwu. = This water has froth. Also ccovwu.
a mouse or house rat, e.g. Twajaya cucu munanda. = We killed a mouse in the house. Also imbeba, sikoswe.
influenza, e.g. Mbanji bantu baafwa lyakasika cucuta. = There were many people who died when the flu came.

a frog, e.g. Inkuku zyalya cula. = The chickens have eaten a frog. Cula wazwa bula, takwe busume. = If a frog's stomach comes out, there is no one who can stitch it up again. Igande = a bull frog. pl. maande; kanamatilabele = small kind of frog; Bafwumo = frog clan.
a frog Also cula.
a corpulent person, e.g. Mwiinga ngucuncumakala. = Mwiinga is a stout person.
type of green relish, e.g. Bana balaciyanda cisyu cacundwe. = The children want the cundwe relish Also mukazibea.
the carrion eagle or kooh vulture, pl. bacungwe, e.g. Cungwe ulayanda kulya nyama. = The kooh-vulture likes eating meat. Bacungwe tababonwi-bonwi. = Vultures are not often seen.
ringworm, e.g. Ooyu mwana uciswa cuubi mumutwe. = This child is suffering frm ringworm on the head.

a rag, pl. zyuubo, e.g. Izyuuboubo zyoonse kacembele kakasamununwa, kwakasyaala buyo kalapi abusyu. = All the old rags the old woman was stripped off, there remained only one piece of cloth covering the private parts.
disrespect, shameless, e.g. Basimbi abasankwa bamazubaano batondezya cuubuubu mumaleya. = The girls and boys of today are shameless in public.
any large insect or reptile, e.g. Kamugusya cuuka abulo bwamwana. = Remove the large insect from the child's bed.
a troublesome spirit, e.g. Kuli cuuka cindisikila masiku neona. = There is a troublesome spirit which visits me at night when I am sleeping. Also idomba.
a termite hill, e.g. Baama bateya nswa *kucuulu*. = My mother is trapping flying ants at the ant-hill.

the termite hill used as the place where the first ritual of female initiation takes place. e.g. Sunu kamwale bafwuma kumutola *kucuulu* kumwi kabauma ngoloolo. = Today they took the initiate early to the termite-hill while ululating.
a type of lizard, e.g. Ndajana nkaanga *cuulubwi* kalilede munzila. = I found the lizard lying on the path
a deaf person, e.g. Ccita naa *cuulutwi* wainda waawa wali kwaamba nzi? = I don't know what the deaf person was saying when s/he was passing.
a marriage payment or installment, e.g. *Cuumakkoma* ndolubono lutaanguna nakwatwa musimbi. = Cuumakkoma is the opening installment to be paid when a girl is getting married.
an extended stomach, e.g. Mulwazi wesu waile kubaa *cuumba* cabula. = Our patient has just developed an extended stomach. Also intunga, inzyo, ndondo

a sensation in gums after eating acidic food like masuku fruit, e.g. Imbubu nzyindakali kulya zyandipa kuba *acuumba*. = The imbubu fruit which I have been eating have left my gums tingling. Also buye

a biting maggot which becomes a reddish fly, e.g. Kabwa kaniini kalumidwe *cuumba kukuulu*. = The puppy has been bitten by a maggot on the leg. Oomu mwakali momukaanda - zyakaliti nsinsini, njina azyuumba mpu! = There in his little house, there were plenty of bed-bugs, lice and maggots.
a solitary person, e.g. Cikaintu *cuumba*
A solitary woman is pitiable. Also buumba.

a clay pot for carrying or storing water/milk, e.g. Mabisi woonse mwaatile *mucuumbu*. Pour all the sour milk into the pot. *Cuumbu* yakali nongo yakubikkila mukupa. = *Cuumbu* was a pot for putting the milk into from the milking pot. Also cibizilo, cipempa.
any round object, e.g. Ndaula cimbwali *cuumbuluumbulu* calo. I have bought a sweet-potatoe which is very round.
a small mound of hard black soil containing small white ants, e.g. Mumusena ukasale *cuumbusu* comwe cipati ncotiikalete. = Choose one big heap of termites which you should bring.
a grave, e.g. Mpubali kusya *cuumbwe* cakuzikkila mwami ali ayumu kapati. It was very hard where they were digging the grave to bury the chief. Also kabanda, cifwene, munzi.
a whipping stick, e.g. Bayi besu bakabambila limwi *cuumo* cakutuumya. Our teacher made a whipping stick for beating us. Also cuumyo
a wound caused by beating, e.g. Eeci *cuumo* ncibakanduuma ankumo cilacisa kapati. This wound on my forehead which they made while beating me is very painful.
a young baboon, e.g. Naboole usaanguna kuselusya bacuumpula mumusamu. = The mother-baboon first helped the young baboons down from the trees.

a hand without fingers, pl. *zyuumpumpu*, e.g. Kamumugwasya ku-tukka cileye cankuni musimbi nkaambo maanzaakwe *nzyuumpumpu* zyalo. Help the girl to put the bundle of firewood on her head because her hands are without fingers.
a pole or tree with bark removed, e.g. Cisamu cakusimpa amulyango waciba ceelede kuba cuumpute. = The pole for inserting at the kraal gate should have the bark removed.
describes emptiness, absence, e.g. Kasimpe mebo juunza bazikujana cuumputu. = Truly tomorrow they will find I have gone away.

something to beat with, e.g. Koya ukeete cuumyo, njanda kuuma mwana oyu. = Go and bring a cane, I want to beat this child. Kamutema zyuumyo tuume mapopwe aakusambala. = Cut canes with which we can thresh the maize for selling. (cuumyo cabbusumili = a flail)

land, territory, neighbourhood, e.g. Cuundu coonse cakamvwa kweema kwabantu. = The whole neighbourhood heard the lament of the people. Awa akali amusela wamwaka ciindi nkolola alwiindi nozitauminini mucuundu ca Butonga. = It was at that time of the year when initiations and agricultural rituals do not cease in the land of the Batonga.

a smell, e.g. Tiitwaibwene kuti nanda yapya, aboobo twamwa buyo cuunduundu cazisani zyapya. = We did not see that the house was burning, and so we only sensed the smell of burning clothes. Mupaale ulya wakali kusiya cuundundu ca nsende mwainda. = The well-dressed gentleman left a scent ofpefume where he passed.
exhalation, i.e. e.g. Basicikolo bakacita cuundwe nibakamana kulunduka. = The pupils were out of breath when they were finished running.
a deaf person, e.g. Sena taata nduwe cuundwe uutamvwi nobaamba bantu? = Is it that you are deaf, you who do not hear what people say?
porridge with too much meal in it, e.g. Nsima njajika lyoonse njacuungabusu. = The food which she cooked had always too much meal in it.

a pile of pumpkins, pl. zyuungu, e.g. Kumazuba basankwa balaunka kukuteya mbeba acilwi cazyuungu ncibakalundika banakazi kumuunda. = In the evening the boys are going to trap the rats at a heap of pumpkins which the women gathered in the field.
useless people, e.g. Nokuba kuti muziyiisye zyana eezi tazimvwi, nziinga bacuungutwi. = Even though you teach these brats they do not understand, they are deaf. Also cuulutwi
a type of bird, the kook vulture, e.g. nombe yakafwa musyokwe yakamanwa bacuungwe. = The cow which died in the bush was finished off by the vultures.
a stool, e.g. Komupa cuuno mweenzu akkale. = Give the visitor a stool so that s/he sits down.
a position of leadership, e.g. Kuti konyina cuuno, uli cuuno cayuuya ulaa cuuno. = If you have no position of power, you become the stool of that one who has power.
a traditional stool, e.g. Cuuno cambwalakasa ceelede kukkala baama lyoonse. = Mother is supposed to sit on a traditional stool always.
a wooden eliptical stool used as a head-rest, e.g. Chilala wakanduulila cuuno camuseko. = Chilala bought me a wooden head-rest. Also cilitulisyo.
an abcess/boil/tumour, swelling in scrotum, e.g. Ndali kukusilikwa cuute kucibbadela. = I had gone to be cured of an abcess at the hospital.
a cultivated edible root, e.g. Uuno mwaka tuyanda kuya kusyanga cuuwe cinji. = This year we want to plant a lot of edible root.
a bad smell, e.g. *Aawa kuli cuwo cibi, antela kuli mubwa wakafwa.* = There is bad smell, pehaps a dog had died. Also ciwo.
make noise, as children when playing, e.g. *Mwasobana kwategwa mulaa cwicwili, kamuzwa.* = When you play you are making noise, go out.
the womb, stomach, e.g. *Ciindi eci wakajisi buyo da lyamyezi yone.* = This time she was only four months pregnant. Also ida.
duck, e.g. *Idada lyakatula iji lyomwe jilo.* = The duck laid one egg yesterday. *Idada lyangu lyalumwa babwa.* = My duck was bitten by dogs.
a long seat or form, e.g. *Koleta damadama tukkalile azuba ku-tegwa tukasaalilwe.* = Bring a bench so that we sit in the sun and become warm.

a plant whose hairy leaves stick, or a a kind of grass which sticks to clothes, (can be made into a headpad to carry sticks) e.g. *Bana bakalikusobana a matu adamatila jilo.* = The children were playing with the leaves of the *damatila* plant yesterday. *Aba bana botatwe bakali kulamatilana muluyando mbuli damatila.* = These three children were sticking to one another in firiendship like a plant whose hairy leaves stick together.
a dam, pool, pond, lake, e.g. *Igande lyakaya mudambwa kukulangaula meenda akunywa.* = The frog went into a pond to search for water to drink.
a dam, e.g. *Ijilo twakajana ma-dada alayamba mudamu.* = Yesterday we found ducks swimming in the dam.
a hole, e.g. *Basicikolo bakali kusobanina mudandula jilo.* = The pupils were playing in a hole yesterday.
drought, e.g. *Mwaka wakainda kwakali danga.* = Last year there was a drought. Also ciyumayuma
a queue, a processsion, a line of people, e.g. *Bantu baimvwi mudebelwa bali kuula busu.* = The people standing in a queue were buying mealie-meal.
a tomatoe, e.g. *Ideede ndibotu kubikka mucisyu.* = Tomato is good for putting in relish.
undiscipline, e.g. *Wakali muntu utayandi kulela bana bakwe adekel-eke.* = He was a person who did not want to rear his children without discipline.
okra, e.g. *Nayenda mumagondo sikoo wakaba mbuli muntu wali kusani-nwa delele kwamyaka-myaka.* = When he walked his kness were weak like a man who had been fed on okra for years.
laziness, e.g. *Moonde ubelesya dengalenga amulimo wakwe.* = Moonde uses laziness in her work. Also butolo
'corridor' disease in cattle e.g. *nombe zinji zyakafwa kuno kumusanza akaambo kabulwazi bwadenkete.* = Many cattle died in the southern province be-cause of corridor disease.
a big bundle, e.g. *Bakatebba nkuni zinji, aumwi wakaanga deye lyankuni.* = They gathered a lot of firewood and each one tied up a big bundle.
a type of plant (*Trichodesma zeylanicum*) Leaves used for green relish, also boiled with small rodents as flavour-ing. *Ijilo twakalisya cisyu cadeyu.* = Yesterday we ate a vegetable relish.
a fall-trap, e.g. *Twakajana kakololo lyamulimba diba.* = We found that the fall-trap had fallen on a big rat.

thickness, consistency, e.g. *Naakali kusuka nsuwa wakali kwiimba. Eeci cakali kucita kuti mabisi libe dibbidila lyacibbobbe.* = When she was shaking the milk-gourd she was singing. This was done so that the sour milk would become of the right consistency or thickness for cheese.
a funeral, e.g. *Boonse wii baile*
kuli bali adila. = All were quiet, they seemed as if they were at a funeral. Also *dilwe*
a female polecat, e.g. *Diintengwe uyandisya kapati kuyandaula cakulya ciindi camasiku.* = The polecat likes to search for food especially at night. Also *diintingwe*.
a big hole, e.g. *Kamuya mukasowe zipepa mudindi.* = Go and throw the papers in the big hole.

a name for the Gwembe Valley, e.g. *Bana Munyumbwe nobakkomana balitembula kuti 'tobana baku Dindi.'* = When the people of Munyumbwe are happy they praise themselves by saying, "We people of *Dindi*".

a bladder infection whereby one passes urine frequently, e.g. *Ooyu mwana ncasuba abulo mazuba onse uciswa bulwazi bwadokaloka.* = The reason that this child urinates in bed every day is that it is suffering from the disease called *dokaloka*
lizard, e.g. *Mwana walikusobanya dolo.* = The child was playing with a lizard.
a drum used as a container, e.g. *Kamuya mukalete meenda mudolomu.* = Go and bring water in a drum.
a town or city, e.g. *Bantu banji balayanda kukkala mudolopo.* = Many people like to live in the city.
half-human, half-snake creature connected with witchcraft, e.g. *Bantu baamba kuti, kuti domba lyajayigwa aulaalyo ulafwa.* = People say that if the *domba* is killed the owner also dies.
one who idles, e.g. *Tababeleki pe, mbaadomolitopota buyo.* = They do not work, they are idlers.
a wound that does not heal, e.g. *Munene ujisi dondamwaka akuulu.* = The old man has a wound that does not heal on his leg.
a large pot, e.g *Nyama yajikwa mudongo.* = The meat has been cooked in a large pot. Also *inongo*
dirt, (ety. English), e.g. *Cibaki cangu cilaa dooti.* = My shirt is dirty. Also *itombe*
a giraffe, e.g. *Ndabona dudwa mumulundu wa Chisale.* = I have seen a giraffe on Chisale hill. Also *nndudwa*
30 cm. measure, e.g. *Wakatupa kooye kalampa madumpwa obilo.* = He gave us a string which was 60 cm. long.
a large hill, e.g. *Kuli basokwe banji mudundu omuya.* = There are many monkeys on that big hill. Also *mulundu*.
middle of the head, e.g. *Banyina bakabikka musamu aduntilo lyamwanaabo.* = The mother put medicine on the centre of her child's head.
a jumping mouse, e.g. *Babwa balikutanda dundwa cifwumo-fwumo.* = The dogs were chasing a jumping mouse in the morning
groups of different houses, e.g. *Mbookaindila biyo kaanda aka ubona dunge-lunge lyabwaandaanda.* = When you pass by this small house you see groups of different houses.
a big heap, e.g. *Mutumbu wakamulazika mwana kumbali adwi lyamatanga.* = The suckling mother laid the child beside a big heap of pumpkins. Also *cilwi*
the rainbow, pl. *bafwulicoongo*, e.g. *Imvwula niyakakkazikide, bafwulicoongo bobile bakalibonya.* = When the rain was about to start, two rainbows appeared.

a land-tortoise, e.g. *Bamwi bantu balalya fwulwe.* = Some people eat tortoise. *Uutapakamani ngofwulwe.* = The one who is not alert is a tortoise. Also *inondo, kabanda, cibinda, sicaanga* (red stripes, living in rocks). water tortoises = *nondo, ibbandwa*.
a civet, (a slender nocturnal cat with a barred and spotted coat) e.g. Nitwalikuweza masiku twajana nkaanga _fwungwe_ munsi amulonga. = When we were hunting at night we found a civet near a river.
a type of wild fruit tree. Its fruits are pink when ripe. e.g. Basankwa bobile balikucela _fwutwe_. = Two boys were gathering fruits from the _fwutwe_ tree

a tin, pl. magabba, e.g. Bama-daala bakali kuyobola mali mumagabba mapati. = The old men were keeping money in large tins. Eeli gabba lyakazwide mulwi wamapepa lyanzabili, lyomwe-lyomwe pepa elyo lyakajisi bulemu bwa-kkumi lyampondo. = This tin was full of a heap of green notes, each single note having the value of ten pounds.
an ant-bear, e.g. Twabona bwina _bwagalaba_. = We have seen the den of an ant-bear.
a large forehead, e.g. Munyati ulaa _ganza_ lipati. = The buffalo has a large forehead. Also _caanza_

dandruff, scales on skin, pl. maamba, e.g. Ndabaa _maamba_ kunsi amaulu. = I have hardened skin under my foot. Ooyu mwana ujisi _gamba_ pati kunsi acituta. = This child has a big patch of hardened skin under the foot.
careless speech, e.g. Ooyu mwana talomenye, ulaa _gamba-amba_. = This child is not upright, he speaks without respect.
a large house, e.g. Muleli wacisi ukkala muganda lipati. = The president of the country lives in a large house. Also _nanda_.
a bull frog, e.g. _Gande_ lyaka-bboloka nilyakatiisole kweelana amusune. = The bull-frog burst when it tried to make itself equal in size to an ox.
a wasp, e.g. Lyamuluma aliso ganko naali kugonka tusamu mumuunda. = A wasp stung him on the eye when he was cutting trees in the field.
insolence, e.g Ooyu musankwa ulaa _gayu_, ncatalemeki bapati. = This boy is insolent that is why he does not honour the elders
a constriction trap used in hunting, e.g. Mwami oyu wajaya muswi mupati _agoba_. = This chief has killed a big fish in a constriction trap. Also _tabalangwe_.

the claw protruding from a dog's hind leg, pl. magobanyama, e.g. Mubwa muniini uleelede kugonkwa mago-banyama natanakomena. = A small dog should have the claw protruding from the back leg cut off before it grows.

male place for meeting, e.g. Bamadaala bakaindi bakali kulaya bana babo basankwa _kugobelo_. = Long ago the old men used to instruct their young sons at the men's meeting place. Kujwe kwa-kali kalongo _katugobelo-gobelo_ twakali koona bana basankwa. = To the east there was a line of small male houses where the boys slept.
a children's game, e.g. Bana balasobana _gogoogo_, geege atandabaale. = Children play the traditional games, _gogoogo_, geege and tandabaale.
grandmother, (ety. Sindebele) e.g _Goko_ bana nebabungana amwi, ula-baita kunanda akubalaya. = When child-ren come together, the grandmother calls them to her house to instruct them. Also _baneene_
the time after sunset, e.g. Beembezi balazinjizya nombe muciba _kugoko_. = The herders enclose the cattle in the kraal after sunset.
the time of eating the first maize, e.g. Ciindi cibizwa zilyo mu-myuunda citegwa _goloka_. The time when the first maize is eaten is known as goloka.
the time when maize ripens, e.g. Bantu banji balakkomana nobasika *agolokelo*. = Many people rejoice when they reach the time when the maize ripens.
cloudy weather, e.g. Waboola *goma*. = Cloudy weather has started.
a type of bird, the shrike (esp. of genus Lanicus), the butcher bird, e.g. Ndiyoka *gombe-gofwu* lyajaya bataata. = I am roasting a shrike which my father killed.

a vast stretch of bush or forest, e.g. Basyuumbwa bakaakunjila mugonde pati bavwimi nobakali kubatanda. = The lions entered a vast stretch of bush when the hunters were chasing them. Lyakali *gonde* lisinkene kapati alimwi liyoosya. = It was forest which was very thick and fearful.

the sacred burial-place of the Batonga where the people pray for rain and celebrate the harvest festival, e.g. Batonga basekelela Iwiindi Iwabo ku *Gonde*. The Tonga people celebrate their harvest ritual at Gonde.
the knee, e.g. Moonde waalilwa kweenda nkaambo bamuuma nkoli *agondo*. Moonde was unable to walk because they struck her on the knee with a stick.
a ridge, e.g. Koboola undibi-kkile *gongola* ananda. Come and put a ridge on my house.
reflection, e.g. Wakali kwiide kubona *gubiibi* lyamumuni atunyenyeezi tuzwela-zwela. He was just seeing a reflection of light and stars moving up and down.
a monkey (generic), pl. bagudi, e.g. *Bagudi* baamana mapopwe mu-myuunda. The monkeys have finished off the maize in the fields. Also ceta
a fertile depression, e.g. Anona ace masuku *amugumba*. How sweet the masuku fruits of the fertile depression.

a waterless plain, e.g. Bana ba-sya balubende *mugundu*. The children are digging for rodents in the waterless plain. Muli cikwikwi cilya akunyonyoona zisyango zyagundu lyanu. You are the locusts that eat and destroy the plants of your waterless plain. Also *igundu*.
a type of grass, e.g. Buzuba bumwi Syaanasulwe wakajana mbizi yakali kucela *gungambizi* mu-cimvwule. One day a hare found a zebra grazing grass in the shade.

attention, focus, e.g. Tee kufwumbwa kuti muntu ulila mufwu, nokuba kuti waamba zicisizya kumoyo, takutegwa kwaba umucitila *qweqwetela*. = Is it not so that whenever a person weeps for a dead person, even though he says things which pierce the heart it does not follow that there will be someone whjo takes offence.
an immodest girl, e.g. Aaka kasimbi nkagwenu-gwenu takakakwatwi. This little girl is immodest and will not be married.

disturbance, e.g. Mukaindi kasyoonto kwakali *gwete* kapati, nkaambo bazovwuu, balubondwe, indudwa abacibize boonse bakali kubalikila mu-syokwe. In a short time there was great confusion, because the elephants, antelopes, giraffes and zebra were all running way into the bush.
a shoulder, e.g. Ndabwezede nkuni *agwezyo*. = I was carrying firewood on the shoulder.
the single-bag bellows of a Tonga Valley blacksmith Also *vwuba*
a wing, e.g. Inkuku yatyoka *ba-ba*. The chicken has her wing broken. Also *ibbaba*.
root smoked as a love charm.
open country, land, e.g. Twali kweembelela kwibanda kujwe. = We were grazing cattle in the plain to the east. Banyama balacela mwibanda. The animals are grazing in the plain. Also ibbanda.

a scar, pl. mabata, e.g. Muntu wabba ulaa bata ankumo. = The one who stole has a scar on his forehead. Cisamu candiyasa abata lilaa kuulu. = A stick pricked me on the scar on the leg. Also lubata, imbata.
a scorpion with red stripes, e.g. Mwana walumwa baubanze. = A scorpion stung the child. Also ibbalabanze.
a scab over a sore, e.g. Kogwisya bbaabbani acicisa. = Remove the scab from the sore. Kobbatulula ibbaabbani acilonda. = Remove the scab from the wound.
a loose cloth, e.g. Mucembele usamide bbaakani. = The old woman is dressed in a loose cloth.
type of big bird, e.g. Ibana ijilo bakajaya ibbaandwa musyokwe. = The children killed a big bird in the bush yesterday.
a wing, pl. mababa, e.g. Ibbaba lyankuku lilanona. = The wing of a chicken is tasty.
a coat, pl. mabbaki, e.g. Mwana wasama bbaki. A child is putting on a coat.
a wheel-barrow, (Ety. English) e.g. Kamususa zitina abbala. = Collect the bricks with a wheelbarrow. Also ingolovwani.
a letter of the alphabeth, e.g. Bbala litaanzi ngu A, licaalizya ngu Z. = The first letter of the alphabeth is A, the last is Z.
a stripe, a spot of colour, e.g. Musune wangu ulaa bbala mwida. = My ox has a spot of colour on the stomach.
colour, e.g. Mucisani eci kuli ibbala libundulala. In this cloth the colour is fading.
a circle of hunters, a general hunt, e.g. Bavwimi bandandama muibbalabala nobavwima. Hunters make a circle when hunting. cf. ibbalo,

flame, light, e.g. Naakazwa anze Syaakasondansima wakabona mucivwuka ca Munali kwakacili bbalabala lyamulilo. = When Syaakasondansima went out at night, he saw there was still the glow of a fire in Livingstone's tent. Ndazyiba kuti bwaca, nindabona bbalabala lyazuba. = I knew it was dawn when I saw the light of the sun.
scorpion, e.g. Mudaala walumwa bbalabanze. = The old man is stung by a scorpion.
a game drive, pl. mabalo, e.g. Bawezi bajisi bbalo kooba banyama. The hunters have a hunt to surround the animals.
steps or threshold of a house, e.g. Bana koomukaintu bakamujatika kubbalo lyananda acikotamino cananda ya Sicibende. The relatives of his wife encircled her at the steps of the house.
a rib, pl. mabambo, e.g. Musune watyoka bbambo. = The ox's rib is broken. Also impango
a banana, pl. mabbanana, (ety. Port, Sp.), e.g. Mweemba uyanda bbanana. Mweemba wants a banana.
plains, pl. of cibanda, e.g. Ibbanda lili kujwe amunzi ndipati. = The plains to the east of the village are extensive.
a bad spirit, e.g. Ibbanda lyanjila mwana ndikali. The bad spirit which has entered the child is fierce. (This, it is said, may occur in the case of a dead spouse seeking revenge.)
a dangerous spirit of one who has been killed unjustly and usually by witchcraft and seeks revenge on the living. Also ibbanda.
a water-tortoise, e.g. Nindakali kuloba jilo ndakaca *ibbandwa mukalobo*. = When I was fishing yesterday I caught a watertortoise on the hook.
a coffer, treasury, bank, (ety. English) e.g. *Bataata bajisi mali manji mubbanga*. = My father has plenty of money in the bank. *Ibbuku ndibbanga lyatwaambo*. = A book is a treasure of information.
gaps left in ploughing, pl. *mabbanga*, e.g. Bantu batacizyi kulimya jamba lyanombe, basiya *mabbanga* nobalima. = People who do not know how to use an ox plough, leave gaps when plouging.
flame, e.g. *Ibbangabanga lyamulilo lilalibonya kumbo*. = A flame of fire is seen in the west. Also ibbalabbala.
a cartridge belt, e.g. *Ibbanti lyamucibuno lyakomenesya*. = The cartridge belt is very big.
iron wheels, e.g. Cikkocci *camabbanti* tacizumizigwi mumugwagwa wataala. = A scotch-cart with iron wheels is not allowed on the tarred road.
a large scar, an ulcer on the buttock, e.g. Mutinta ulaa *bbata* kumeso. = Mutinta has a large scar on the face.
short-sightedness, e.g. Bataata balaa *bbayibayi*. My father is short-sighted. Musune ubona *bbayibayi*, talimi kabotu, = An ox which is shortsighted does not plough well. Also imbayimbayi.
a side, pl. *mabazu*, e.g. *Ibbazu lyangu lyomwe lilaa cicisa*. = I have a sore on one side. Walicisa *mabazu* obile. = He hurt himself on both sides.
a bucket, (ety. English) e.g. Ndali kukuula *bbekete lyandongwe*. = I went to buy a bucket of groundnuts.
an udder, pl. *mabele*, e.g. *Ibbele lyampongo lyakomena*. = The udder of the goat has become big.
a small large-headed lizard, e.g. Bana bakayoowa nibakabona *ibbelebenzya lisubila*. The children were afraid when they saw the small red largeheaded lizard. Also haakabelebele
a big thigh, pl. *mabelo*, e.g. Mudaala watyoka *bbelo*. The old man's big thigh is broken. Also cibelo.
a donkey, pl. *mabbema*, e.g. Kaindi bakali kubelesya kapati *mabbema*
Long ago they used to use donkeys as transport. Also mbongolo.
the castor-oil plant, e.g. *Ibbempengene lilijisi matu manji*. = The castor-oil plant has many leaves. Also ibono
a big edible rodent, e.g. Ijilo ndakajaya *bbende*. I killed a big edible rodent yesterday. Also mubende, lubende
a gap of missing teeth, e.g. Kwaloka limbi linyo kuzwa mukanwa aboobo *ibbende lyakomena*. Another tooth has fallen from the mouth yesterday and so the gap has grown.
a panga-like instrument, e.g. Mudaala ugonka minsale *abbenga*. = The old man is cutting sugar-cane with a panga.
a pile of branches in fields to be burnt, pl. *mabibi*, e.g. Amubikke mulilo *abbibi lili mumuunda*. = Set fire to the pile of branches which is in the field. Also cibibi.

a big fire, e.g. Muvwimi wakapya akufwa *mubbibi lyamulilo*. = The hunter was burnt and died in a big fire. Mbwindakasika nkwiile kufwusa amwi mapopwe *mubbibi lyamulilo*. = As soon as I arrived I just threw some maize cobs on the blazing fire.
a kiln for burning bricks, e.g. Tuya kukuyaka *bbila*. We are going to build a kiln for burning bricks. Also ibbile, ondo, ovoni.

abnormal body, e.g. Ulya najempa wamuntu inga watwala! Umubwene buyo bbili liya yebo wati nimbaanyina, nimbaanyina yakuli? = You are going to marry this prostitute! You only see a large body which you call a cowry shell, a cowry shell from where?
baby's craving for mother's breast, e.g. *Ibbimba* lyamwana oyu lipa kuti banyina kabatalyi kabotu. = This baby's craving for milk prevents the mother from eating well.
jealous suspicions as between husband and wife, jealousy of one who tells another to refuse giving to a third party, e.g. *Ibbimba* lyabamakaintu bamwi ndibi. = The jealousy of some women is evil.
a fish-basket trap, e.g. Bacembele bajata inswi zinji *abbinda*. = The old women caught many fish with a fishingbasket. Also *isiko*
longing, longing for what is another's, envy, e.g. Bantu banji bala *abbivwe* kubeenzinyina bavwubide. Many people are envious of their friends who are rich. Also *munyono*.
a horse, e.g. Ndatantide *bbiza* kuya kudolopo. = I was mounted on a horse going to the town. Also *ibiza*.
a bottle, e.g. Basimbi bajaya *bbodela* nibali kusobana. = The girls broke the bottle when they were playing.
a box, (ety. English), e.g. *Ibbokesi* lyazisani lyakaligwa mbeba. = The box of clothes was eaten by the rats.
a ball, e.g. Bana basimbi baya *kubbola*. = The young girls are going to the ball game.
a white lily, pl. mabolomombo, e.g. Eeli *ibbolomombo* ndibotu kapati. = This water-lily is very beautiful. Also ibbolombombo, cibolomombo
influenza epidemic, e.g. Bantu banji baciswa *bbolonkoto*. = Many people are sick with the flu.

propolis, a red/brown resinous substance got by bees from buds for use as constructing and varnishing honey-combs, e.g. *Ibbombo* lyanzuki ezi lilalula. = The propolis of these bees is bitter. Also *munsu*.
a large dove, a large type of wild pidgeon, e.g. Bataata bajaya *bbombo*. = My father has killed a pidgeon. Also Haanalimombo, *imombo*.
castor-oil plant, pl. mabbona, e.g. Katulima *mabbona* kutegwa katujana mafwuta. = Let us grow castor-oil plants so that we get oil. Also *ibbono*.
a pen for sheep or goats, e.g. Kamuyaka *bbondo*. = Build a pen for the sheep.
a type of relish, e.g. Twali kukucela *bbondwe*. = We went to collect relish. Also *cimowa*.

swarm of bees hanging from a branch, pl. mabooma, e.g. Inzuki zyabamba *bbooma* mumusamu. = The bees have made a swarm in the tree. Also cisaula mulengwa = a swarm that has already built combs; citanga canzuki = a moving swarm.
type of edible fruit leaf, flower, e.g. Bantu banji tabalilyi *bboonko*. = Many people do not eat *bboonko*. Also *ibonko*

goiter, Adam's apple, dewlap, e.g. Bina Cheelo baciswa *bbozu*. = The mother of Cheelo has goiter. Mutinta naakacili mwana *bbozu* lyakali lisyoonto, sunu lyakomena. = When Mutinta was young the goitre was small, but now it has grown. Also *ibozu*.
the dew-lap of a cow, pl. mabozu, e.g. Mucende wangu ulaa *bbozu* lipati. = My bull has a big dew-lap. Also malembwe-lembwe.
a big reed, e.g. Koya ukalete *bbu* kumulonga. = Go and bring a big reed from the river. Also *lubu*
a stretch of high grass, e.g. _Bana tabeelede kusobanina mubbubi nkaambo kukkala nzoka ziluma._ = Children should not play in the high grass because there are snakes there which bite.
a book, pl. mabuku, e.g. _Ibbuku lyangu lyapya._ = My book is burnt.

a large manufactured metal drum for carrying fuel, but used in village life for brewing beer, pl. mabbulo, e.g. _Makoko mazuba ano bajikila mumabbulo ngobati 'madolomu'._ = Beers are brewed nowadays in large metal drums which they call 'madolomu'
a clay seat, e.g. Nobeenzuma, amukkale abbumbili awo. = My friends sit on that clay seat. Also cibumbili
below the navel, e.g. Ncaakanetuka mwana, bakamuuma abbumbu. = They beat the child below the navel that is why it fainted.
a stout person, a giant, e.g. _Oyu muntu ndibbumbwa._ = This person is a giant.
an obese person, e.g. _Ibbumbwa-buuka lilikkede alusasa._ = The big-bodied person is sitting on a mat.
a weal, e.g. _Ndaba abbunda mpubanduuma bayi._ = I have the welts where the teacher beat me. Also muvwundu, pl. mivwundu.
groups, e.g. _Minzi yakali kuyakwa abbunga nkamu yabalombwana boonse bamumunzi omo._ = Villages were built by groups of all the strong men working together from within that village.
a mole or rat hill, pl. mabbunze, e.g. _Twajana mabbunze manji mumusena mufwumba basilufwukwe._ = We found many heaps in the vlei where the moles make holes.
wadding or cloth to pack a gun, e.g. _Ibbusha lilayandika kutatila muntobolo yamudinkilwa._ = Wadding is needed to pack a muzzel gun.
a shoe, pl. mabusu, e.g. _Ibbusu lyangu lyazimina musyokwe._ = My shoe is lost in the bush.
wadding, e.g. _Mbeba yakabamba bbusya pati niyakamana kuzyala kutegwa ibikke bana._ = After the mouse gave birth she made much wadding to put her young into. Also ibbusha, manswa.

open space in the bush, e.g. _Ndakabasiya bana ndati nkalete mapopwe akulya kubbuwa._ = I left the children and said let me bring maize and eat at the open space in the bush. _Kuti nombe zyakkuta zilayanda koona abbuwa._ = When the cattle are full they like to lie down in an open space.
a yard where cattle are milked, e.g. _Kamutola nombe kubbuwa zikakamwe._ = Take the cattle to the yard to be milked.
a baobab tree, a baobab fruit, pl. mabuyu, e.g. _Ibbuyu ndibotu kujika ceele._ = The baobab fruit is good for cooking porridge.
a mole hill, pl. mabuzye, heap of soil, e.g. _Imbeba zibamba mabbuzye mumusena._ = Rats make heaps of soil in the vlei. Also ibbunze.
an open place, e.g. _Bana bakali kuyasa ntinde abbwalo._ = The children were playing the game of piercing the tubers in an open place.
sweet-beer, e.g. _Kwa Mapanza balakumba bbwatu mazuba onse._ = The people of Mapanza brew sweet-beer daily.
protruding buttocks, pl. mabbwaya. e.g. _Basankwa mbubakkala nkwiide kulanga mabbwaya abasimbi._ = The boys as they sat were just watching the large buttocks of the girls.

a stone, pl. mabwe, e.g. _Bana baku Dindi balayanda kufwusana mabwe._ = Children from Dindi like to throw stones at each other. _Inzoka bakaijaya abbwe._ = They have killed the snake with a stone. (Ibbwe likwengela = a whetstone, also cikwengelo, pl. makwengelo)
very strong medicine, e.g. Wakamenede bbwe. = He had swallowed very strong medicine.

a flat stone, e.g. Nokwakasiya wakayandaula akoona mukasumbu atalaa bbwe-njale lyakali koona bayuni. = When it was dark she searched for a place to sleep on the island on top of a flat stone where the birds sleep.
half-cooked porridge. e.g. Ooyu mwana wajika bbyo. This child has half-cooked the nsima. Also mukonde, mubbyaanga.
jealousy in matrimonial matters, e.g. Basankwa bamwi bajisi bingu kwiinda bamakaintu. Some husbands are more jealous than wives. Also ibbimba, ibbivwe, buzuba.
a horse, e.g. Ndakaula ibiza jilo. = I bought a horse yesterday. Also ibbiza.
impurities left after skimming castor-oil, e.g. Koya ukasowe ibombo mudindi. Go and throw the impurities in a hole.
a large dove, e.g. Ibombo zilatula mayi muzyoonde. = The large doves lay their eggs in thick bushes. Also imombo.

a plant used as relish, e.g. Oomu muzikuta basimbi mobakali kujika tusyu-tusyu twamisyobo mbuli: lunkomba, ibondwe, cikombo cabbuyu alimwi anakafwulo, eeco ncobati 'lubanga'. = There in the grass huts is where the girls were cooking different types of relish such as, lunkomba, ibondwe, cikombo cabbuyu and nakafwulo, that one which they call lubanga.

a plant (Amaranthus thunbergii) A green relish whose diced leaves are cooked for at least 1 hr. (Dec.-May), e.g. Kamujika bonko lyaleta baama. = Cook the relish which mother has brought. Also ibboonko
castor-oil plant, pl. mabona, e.g. Munsi alubuwa kwakazwa bona lyomwe. = One castor-oil plant germinated near the front yard.
a type of relish, e.g. Tuyakukucela bondwe kumuunda. = We are going to gather relish in the field.
castor-oil plant, e.g. Ibono ndeekasyangide mumbewu lyakayuma. = The castor-oil plant which I had planted in the field has dried up.
mushroom used as relish Dec.March. e.g. Ibowa busibikidwe acikko bwaida. The mushroom relish which was put on the fire got burnt.
Adam's apple, skin at throat, dewlap, e.g. Bakaintu bangu bakasilikwa bozu ku Maamba. My wife was healed of a throat disease in Maamba. cf. ibbozu.
a plant, e.g. Kondicelela bozu elyo lipati. Collect that big plant for me.
a plant (Hyparrhenia sp.) used as thatching grass, e.g. Bakaleta ibubi akutalika kuvwumba kaluli. They brought the plant for thatching and began to thatch the little roof.
liquid honey, e.g. Kamutila bulolo munkomeki yamudaala. Pour the liquid honey into the old man's cup. Also mulolo wabuci.
iguana, e.g. Babwa bajaya bulu mumuunda. The dogs have killed an iguana in the field. Also nabulwe, ikwamba, sibbulu.
a mole-hill, e.g. Ndabona bunze lyasilufwukwe mucindongwe. = I have seen a mole-hill in the groundnut field. Also ibbuzye.
a clear or bare space in the bush, e.g. Basune balilede abuwa. = The oxen are lying in the clearing.
a smooth pebble, e.g. Kondipa bwebio eelyo. = Give me that smooth stone.

the afterbirth, e.g. *Icabacembele mbocakakaka kuzwa bakaya kumunanga*. *Okuya bakaakwaambilwa kuti bakamupiile maanzi mulwazi*. Nobakasika mucembele umwi wakabweza lufwulu akuteka maanzi munongo. Wakawubata mfwundo yomwe nkabela wakapaila mubusyu bwamulwazi. Nokwakainda kaindi kasyoonto buyo, *icabacembele cakazwa*. = When the afterbirth would not come out they went to the witchdoctor. There they were told to spit water on the patient. When they arrived back one elderly woman took a drinking gourd and drew water from a clay pot. She took one mouthful and sprayed it on the face of the patient. After a little time the afterbirth came out.
a shawl with a fringe, pl. *macali* Also *malesu, iccali*.
pith, what is chewed and spat out, e.g. *Mwana waswida canki lya-munsale*. = The child spat out the pith of the sugar cane. Also *cikanci*.
a workshop, e.g. *Kamuya mukafwule tweembe kucapu*. = Go and forge axes at the workshop. Also *insaka*.
a shawl with a fringe, pl. *maccali*, e.g. *Bacembele mukabaulile payi lyaccali*. = Buy the old woman a blanket with a fringe. Also *icali*
abusive language, e.g. *Ooyu musimbi ulaa ccapo ncobamuuma basankwa*. = This girl uses abusive language that is why boys beat her.
panga, machete, e.g. *Twakafwuma kuya kugonka mbalo amacceba*. = We set out early to cut roofing poles with machetes.
a type of bird, the wryneck, pl. *maceece*, e.g. *Musankwa wajaya cceece amalekani*. = The boy killed the wryneck bird with a catapult.
a testicle, pl. *macende*, e.g. *Eeyi ngulube ilaa ccende lyomwe*. = This pig has one testicle.
a big tail, e.g. *Sokwe ulaa ccila pati*. = The monkey has a big tail.
a big wild cat, e.g. *Kwaima matwi mboiti ndiccucu*. = The ears stood up like those of a big wild-cat.
sugar, e.g. *Kamundibikkila ccuka mucibwantu*. = Put sugar for me in the sweet-beer.
a machete, e.g. *Mulozi bamuyasa ceba mumutwe*. = They cut the witch's head with a sword. Also *icceba*
sand, e.g. *Tususa cebecebe lyakuyasya cijikila*. = We are drawing sand for building a kitchen. Also *musenga*.

overhanging or high bank of river, e.g. *Icenga nilyakakolomoka, sinombe waimvwi mpawo wanyikila mumulonga*. = When the overhanging bank of the river collapsed, the herder who was standing on top was drowned in the river. Also *ijeleele*.
placenta of animals, e.g. *nombe yalya cenzi niyamana kuzyala*. = The cow ate its placenta after calving. Also *iteezi*.
a curse, e.g. *Bantu balaa ceta mbabalozi*. = The ones who have a curse are the ones who are witches. Also *lusingo*.
a lathe, e.g. *Kokwenga keembe kako acezyo*. = Sharpen your axe on the lathe.

a type of bird, the seed-eater, pl. *maconco*, e.g. *Ndabwezela conco lyakatyoka bbaba musyokwe*. = I have picked up a seed-eating bird whose wing got broken in the bush. Also *kacwencwe*. ida womb, stomach, e.g. *Ulaa da* = She is pregnant, e.g. *Ooyu mubwa ulaa da

zyotatwe*. = The pregnancy of this dog is three weeks. Also *da* stomach = *cifwu, cikaka, igumba, cuumba* 2<sup>nd</sup> stomach = *ceembelo, cifwumbilizya* 3<sup>rd</sup> stomach = *mulomwe, cinyonkelo* 4th stomach= *intaba, impumbwe, imbwebwe*
a domestic duck, e.g. *Idada lya-ngu lyalumwa nzoka masiku.* = My duck was bitten by a snake during the night. Also *ikungubu*.
mud for making bricks, e.g. *Kamukanda bulongo kuti bube daka lyakubambya zitina.* = Mix the soil so that it becomes mud for making bricks. *Kamu-kanda daka lyakuyasya.* = Make mud for building.
a big tongue, e.g. *Musune mupati ulaa daka lipati.* = The big ox has a big tongue. Also *mulaka*
a tonsil, e.g. *Idakabiya lya-nswi lilanona kulya.* = The tonsil of a fish is very tasty. Also *idavwiya*, pl. *malakavwiya*.
a strip of palm, pl. *madala* or *malala*, e.g. *Cisuwo eci cakoombezegwa amadala mabotu.* = This basket has been edged with good strips of palm.
a spring of a gun, e.g. *Ndidala lya-ntobolo lyaleka kusebenza.* = It is the spring in the gun which has stopped working.
the womb, e.g. *Eeyi nkuku nciyafwa iji lyakafwida mudalilo.* = The hen died because an egg broke in its womb. Also *cizyalilo*.
placenta of animal, e.g. *Nibai-pandula nombe bajana mwana mudalo.* = When they opened up the animal they found an unborn calf attached to the placenta.

a plant which sometimes has long rows of small inverted thorns along each branch which easily become atta-ched to clothes, e.g. *Cisani cangu cana-matilwa damatila nindali kutebba nkuni.* = My cloth was stuck with thorns from a thorny plant when I was cutting firewood.
a pond/lake, e.g. *Tuya kudambwa kukuzela.* = We are going to the pond to fish.
a hole planted with mealies, pl. *mala-mbwa*, e.g. *Kusyanga mudambwa ncibotu mumyaka yadanga.* = To plant in a hole is good in years of drought
the halo around the moon or sun which forecasts rain, e.g. *Sunu kuzuba kuli dambwa lyameenda.* = Today there is a halo around the sun forecasting rain.
a dam, e.g. *Idamu lina Moomba lyakayuminina kale.* = The Moomba dam already dried up.
a braclet or leg bangle of wire and thread, pl. *malanda*, e.g. *Musankwa oyu ulasama danda kukuulu.* = This boy is wearing a bangle on the leg.
a dining room, e.g. *Basicikolo balida mudandula.* = The pupils eat at the dining hall. Also *cipala*
a large house, e.g. *Baacisya bakayaka dandulo.* = My uncle built a big house. *Basikalumamba baona mudandulo.* = The soldiers are sleeping in a large building.

a prolonged drought, e.g. *Mwaka wakamana kwakali danga.* = There was a drought last year. *Mumwaka wadanga umwi, zilyo zya Mweemba zyakamana mucimumbwa cakwe.* = During a certain year of drought, the food supplies in the grain-bins of Mweemba were exhausted. Also *ciyumayuma*
a cataract on the eye, e.g. *Musankwa oyu ulaa danga muliso.* = This boy has a cataract in the eye. Also *kabale, cilanga*.
the bright evening star (Venus), e.g. *Idangabalya nilyabbila ni-twaunka kukoona.* = We went to sleep when the evening star disappeared.

a flower, pl. *malanga-langa*, e.g. *Idangalanga eli ndibotu kapati.* = This flower is very beautiful. *Idanga-langa lyapusene ono nikwatontola lila-tondezya bubotu bwalyo, libaa kanunkilo kanyonokela nzuki.* = The flower is with-ered now, when it is cold it shows its beauty, its nice scent attracts the bees.
a big old cow, e.g. Bakajaya nombe *ddabbala* ankolola. = They killed a big old cow at an initiation ceremony. Also indabala.
type of plant, e.g. Twakatala kulisya *ddebelebe* lyoonse. = We are tired of always eating the *ddebelebe* plant. Also *muteezi*. *idduba lyamuwaama*. a violet
a line of people, e.g. Kwali *debelwa* lyabantu bali kuyanda kuula *ccuka*. = There was a line of people going to buy sugar. Also indebelwa.
a tomatoe, pl. *madeede*, e.g. *Ndakaula madeede manji ijilo*. = I bought many tomatoes yesterday.

used to describe a beautiful woman, e.g. Bumwi buzuba nkaanga sulwe kakaswaanganya *ideede* lyamwana musimbi, lino pesi lyakalisubilila balitala. = One day the rabbit met a tomatoe of a young woman, but she was only beautiful externally.
sharp side of sugar cane plant, e.g. Mwana lyamunenga *deenzya* lyamunsale. = The child was cut by the edge of a sugar stalk.
a ruler of people who attends to their needs, e.g. *Idelabantu* wakabamba muswaangano wakuyungizya luumuno mumunzi. = The ruler called a meeting to advance peace in the village.
dewlap, e.g. Kojata *dembwelembwe* lyanombe. = Catch the dewlap of the cow.
a type of cloth, felt, e.g. *Ndakaula mabbusu adenda*. = I bought felt shoes.
a big old man, rt. *munene*, e.g. *Ncinzi biya ncetajisi cijisi dene eli*. = What do I not have which this big old man has?
a large milking vessel for *cibwantu*, e.g. *Ideu* lyacibwantu lyavwula. = The large container of sweet-beer is full. Also mulewu, pl. milewu.
a coin, pl. *mali*, e.g. *Idi* lyangu lyazimina munzila nindazyila kumuunda. = My coin got lost on the way when I was coming from the field.

a fall-trap made of stone or hard clay, e.g. *Idiba* lyamudaala lyajaya kancele. = The fall-trap of the old man killed a young partridge. Bumwi buzuba wakaakujana kanyama kalimbwa mudiba. = One day he found an animal had been caught in the trap.
a penny (old coinage), pl. *madibilisi*, e.g. *Madibilisi taacilibonyi mazubaano*. = Pennies are never seen nowadays.
a ticket, (ety. English) e.g. *Idikiti* lyesu lyazimina mucitima aboobo twabbadela ambi mali. = Our ticket got lost on the train and so we had to pay more money.
the rites of death, e.g. Kuli ba Moonga kuli *dilwe*. = There is a funeral at Mr. Moonga's. (-vwumbula *dilwe*, *-vwunika* = postpone a funeral)
a big feather, e.g. Ndabwezela *dimba* lyasikube. = I took up the big feather of a vulture. Also ipepe, mapepe, munimba.
long and loose garment, e.g. Ndakamuulila musimbi *dimpwilimpwi* lituba lyakusama amuccado. = I bought a long, loose white dress for the girl to wear at the wedding.
a big hole with broad mouth, pl. *malindi*, e.g. Twali kusya *dindi lyakusowela tombe. = We were digging a big hole for throwing away the dirt.
a calf of the leg, e.g. *Mwiindi wamusune oyu mmupati. = The calf of the leg of this ox is big. Also ijindi, mwiindi.
the instep = *idindi lyakuulu*

unmarried elderly woman, e.g. Uyeeya kuti nguni musankwa unga wazumina kukwata *dindu* lyamukaintu lijisi amwana wamusyokwe? = What man do you think would agree to marry an elderly unmarried woman who has had an illegitimate child?
a very fertile piece of land, e.g. *Idinga lyangu lilakomezya kabotu mapopwe.* = The maize grows well in my fertile plot.
collar-bone, pl. *malinga*, e.g. *Nitwakali kusobana bbola umwi musankwa wakatyola dinga.* = When we were playing football one of the boys broke his collarbone.

a big wooden spoon, pl. *malisya-batumbu*, e.g. *Mulinga ulayandisya kulisya disya-batumbu.* = Mulinga likes eating with a big spoon. *Idisyabatumbu balityola bana.* = The children have broken the big spoon.

something very soft, e.g. *Mwana waciswa aboobo mubili waile kuba divwi-divwi.* = The child is sick and so the body has become soft. *Ndaula bulo bwaidivwi-divwi* = I bought a mattress. Also *cibonzu-bonzu*.
a big fish-hook, e.g. *Ndijisi dobo lyakulobya babondo.* = I have a big fishing-hook for fishing barbel.
a frequent need to urinate, e.g. *Ooyu mucembele uciswa dokaloka.* = The old woman suffers from a frequent need to urinate. Also *kasyunsyu*
a mapani bee, pl. *malola*, e.g. *Tuyakukulida malola.* = We are going to take out honey from the mapani bees.

a place to which bees continually return, e.g. *Mwakali twakalizitandide nzuki, pesi uno mwaka zyasika nkaambo ndidola lyazyo.* = Last year we drove out the bees, but this year they have arrived because it has become a permanent hive for them.
a waistcoat, e.g. *Nobakaintu, amundisumine dolobaki.* = Woman, sew me a waist-coat. Also *ndolobaki*
a metal drum, pl. *madolomu,* e.g. *Kunyina meenda mudolomu.* = There is no water in the big metal drum. Also *ibbulo*
a town, a city, e.g. *Idolopo lya Lusaka ndipati kapati.* = The city of Lusaka is very big.
the muscle of the upper arm, e.g. *Musimbi ulya ulaa cicisa adolwa.* = That girl has a sore on the muscle of the upper arm. Also *syaadolo*
a trap, e.g. *Munene uteya bakakololo adoma.* = The old man is trapping gerbils with an *idoma* trap. Also *idiba*.

said to be a creature, half human, half fish or snake, used by the witch as a medium to bewitch others, pl. *madomba*, e.g. *Ooyu mulozi uloozya domba.* = This witch bewitches through his/her medium. *Bantu balowa basanina madomba.* = People who bewitch feed mermaid-like creatures.
the muscle of the upper arm, e.g. *Idombela lyamwana lilizimbide.* = The muscle of the child's upper arm is swoolen. Also *idolwa*.
an incurable sore, e.g. *Bacembele balaa dondamwaka akuulu.* = The old woman has an incurable sore on her leg.
oedema (disease in which watery fluid collects in cavities or tissue of the body), e.g. *Bantu baciswa dondamwaka baleetezya.* = People suffering from oedema are to be sympathized with.
a great river, e.g. *Bwato bwanyikila mudonga.* = The boat sank in the great river. Also *mulonga*.
a channel for water, a furrow, overflowing path of a river, e.g. *Idongalonga lyamulonga Magoye lilaa nswi kapati.* = An overflow channel of the Magoye river is full of fish.
a big clay pot for beer, rt. inongo, e.g. *Basankwa bandijayila dongo lyabukoko.* = The boys have broken my
the edible fruit of a wild shrub, pl. maloolo, e.g. *Idoolo ndindakavwundikide lyakabizwa.* = The fruit of a wild plant which I had kept became ripe. Also muloolo.
dirt, (ety. Eng.) e.g. *Cisani cangu cilaa dooti.* = My dress is full of dirt. *Basicikolo balaa dooti balaumwa kucikolo.* = Dirty pupils are beaten at school. Also tombe.
a drop of liquid, e.g. *Ndalokelwa dosi lyameenda.* = A drop of water fell on me.

an embryo, a mixture of blood and water, e.g. *Mudaala uluka dowalowa.* = The old man is vomitting a mixture of thick blood and water. *Cintu cadowalowa civwelene amate ciide kuloloteka koonse-koonse.* = A mixture of clotted blood and spittle just poured out everywhere.
a flower, e.g. *Iduba lyamunanda yangu lyaneta.* = The flower in my house has withered. Also iluba.
a flower, pl. malubaluba, e.g. *Eeli dubaluba ndibotu.* = This flower is beautiful. Also iduba.
a two-yard measure, e.g. *Amunditendele dufwa lyamulembo.* = Cut me off a two-yard measure of cloth. Also idumpwa.

luggage, e.g. *Citima nicakaima bakaseluka amadukulu, bakkiti, babwa, madada a banyama bamwi.* = When the train stopped they got out with luggage, cats, dogs, ducks and other animals. Also dubulu, madubulu
a horse-fly, e.g. *Idumambizi lileetela bulwazi bwakusoomona kuti lyakkala ali cakulya.* = A horsefly causes diarrhoea when it lights on food. Also ibingambizi.
a mason wasp, pl. madumanombe, e.g. *Madumanombe alacisa naaluma bantu.* = When mason wasps sting people they hurt.
a type of bird, the martial eagle, e.g. *Idumatoongo mmuyuni mupati.* = The martial eagle is a great bird. Also haatoongo.

a length of calico, a two-yard measure, pl. madumpwa, e.g. *Mucembele wakaula madumpwa amulembo obilo kutegwa asuminwe cibaki.* = The old lady bought two yards of cloth so that she could make a blouse.
the queen termite or queen bee, e.g. *Ikuti inzuki zyafwidwa dunda wazyo, zilapola.* = If the bees loose their queen, they move to another place.
a big fruit (unidentified), e.g. *Musamu oyu uzyede dunda lyomwe.* = This tree is producing one big fruit.
a big mountain, e.g. *Tuya kukulanga dundu liinda kukomena mu Afulikka.* = We are going to see the highest mountain in Africa.
shallow water, e.g. *Basimbi bazela nswi mudungulungu.* = The girls are fishing in shallow water.
a verandah, e.g. *Bantu balayanda kukkala muduze lyananda ciindi nokupya.* = People like to sit on the verandah of the house when it is hot. Also ikkoce, ikkota.
a fertile plain, savannah, e.g. *Kuli zisamu zimwi muduzi.* = There are some of trees in the plain.
a heap, as of ears of sorghum, e.g. *Idwi lyamaila muceme lyakabumbwa.* = A heap of sorghum has been attacked by weevils. Also mulwi
a cannibal, pl. madyabantu, e.g. *Kaindi-kaindi kwakali madyabantu muzisi zinji.* = Long ago there were cannibals in many countries.
a lung, pl. malyabowa, e.g. *Ndiciswa dyabowa.* = I have a lung illness. Also ifwufwe, izumbwa
a mushroom eater/ tortoise, e.g. *Ndajaya dyabowa lyali kulya bowa bwangu.* = I have killed the tortoise which was eating my mushrooms.
the nail of the big toe or thumb, rt. *Iwala*, pl. *mala*, e.g. *Lyandipwaya bbwe adyala.* = A stone struck the nail of my big toe.
a big doorway, door or gate, pl. *malyango*, e.g. *Kojala dyango elyo.* = Close that big door.
a seed-eating bird, e.g. *Ndajaya dyamaila mumuunda.* = I killed a seed-eating bird in the field.
a hole in a river-bed in which fish gather, e.g. *Nitwali kuzela mumulonga, ndajana dyolwe.* = When we were fishing in the river, I found a hole in which the fish gather. Also *inkumbwi*.
a barbel, pl. *mafaci*, e.g. *Ndajaya faci lyomwe nindali kuloba.* = I killed one barbel when I was fishing. Also *mubondo*.
a glen *ifwibakumba* a bulb which is smoked as a love-charm, e.g. *Ifwibakumba lyakapya ciindi syokwe nilyakapya.* = The lovecharm root got burnt when the bush went on fire. Also *ibbakumba*
a type of bird, the barred owl, e.g. *Sunu kwali kulila fwimbampeyo.* = Today there was a barred owl hooting. Also *ifwulampeyo*.
soft matter, e.g. *Mapepe atumba ngafwindi-fwindi.* = The feathers of an owl are soft and wooly.
the downy feathers on a young bird, e.g. *Bana bankwilimba bazwide fwinti-fwinti amubili.* = The downy feathers started coming out on the body of the young pidgeons.
tow (flax, hemp, fibres) e.g. *Kamuleta fwinti-fwinti lyabuluba tubambe mulembo.* = Bring cotton tow so that we make a garment. Also *ivwindi-vwindi, insambwa*.
a glen, e.g. *Basikalumamba bakainda*
yamalundu.* = The soldiers passed through the glens of the hills. Also *mweenya*, pl. *myeenya*.
a shovel, (ety. Eng.) e.g. *Kamuleta fwosholo tufwumbulule cikala.* = Bring a shovel so that we take mud out of the well.

a stupid person, e.g. *Ifwubafwuba lyanyikila mumulindi nilyazyila kubukoko.* = A stupid person fell into a hole when he came from beer drinking *ifwufwe* a lung, e.g. *Ifwufwe lyampongo lyajanika lilibolede niyapandulwa.* = The lung was found to be rotten when the goat was cut open. Also *ipupwa, idyabowa, izumbwa*
post-natal pains, e.g. *Bamwi bamakaintu nobamana kutumbuka inga baciswa fwufwuti.* = Some women suffer from post-natal pains after giving birth.
antenna, e.g. *Wajata fwula lyacuuka.* = She caught the antenna of an insect.
a type of bird, the barred owl, e.g. *Ndajana fwulampeyo mumusamu uli kunze ananda.* = I found a barred owl in a tree behind the house. Also *ifwimbamepyo*

an orange, pl. *mafwuleenke*, e.g. *Kondicelela fwuleenke lyomwe.* = Take one orange down from the tree for me. *ifwulicoongo.* rainbow, e.g. *Kuti walibonya fwulicoongo inga mvwula taiwi.* = If you see the rainbow, the rain does not fall.
a tortoise, e.g. *Ndabona bowa bwali kuligwa fwulwe.* = I saw a mushroom which was eaten by a tortoise. Also *inondo*.
the fruit of the mafwumo tree, e.g. *Ifwumo lyacisamu ndiyumu kugonka.* = The fruit of the tree is hard to cut.
the core of a tree, e.g. *Cisamu eci cilaa cifwuno ciyumu.* = This tree has a hard core. *Ifwuno* yamubanga tiibumbwi. = The core of the mubanga tree cannot be eaten by white ants. Also *mutima*.

a big instrument for bailing out water, e.g. Ibwato nibwakadonkoka, twakafwambaana kubelesya *ifwunte* kutegwa bwato butabbili. = When the boat was holed, we quickly used a large ladle for bailing out the water so that the boat would not sink.

a type of tree (hexalobus monopetalus), reddish heartwood used for hut-poles, and tool-handles. The flesh of the fruit is edible. e.g. Ndifwala mwiini wamusamu *wafwuntwe*. = I am cutting a hoe-handle from an *ifwuntwe* tree. Also *mulukwa*.
a big bone, pl. mafwuwa, rt. cifwuwa, e.g. *Ifwuwa* lyanombe lyandiyasa mukanwa. = A big bone of a cow has pierced my mouth.
a big tin can, pl. magabba, e.g. Koleta *gabba* lyamukupa walusu. = Bring a tin of powdered milk. Also *cigabba, buleke*
a big orange-like wild fruit, pl. maabo, e.g. *Igabo* eli lyakabola. = This wild orange is rotten. Also *intamba*
the nail of the big toe or thumb, e.g. Kozwa awa nentanakukusyamba *gala!* = Get out of here before I pinch you with a big thumb-nail. Also *idyala*.
disrespect, inattention, sloth in obeying, e.g. Mwana ulaa gama usampuzya bazyali bakwe. = A disrespectful child brings shame to it's parents. Also *kamfwumfwu*.
a great frost, e.g. Muzisi zyamakuwa kulaba *ganda* ciindi camupeyo. = In Western countries there is a severe frost during the cold season. Also *caanda*.
a big house, e.g. Ndakayasya *ganda*. = I had a big house built. Bavwubi bayaka *maganda mapati*. = Rich people build big houses.
a forked collar used in the past as a slaves collar, pl. maganda, e.g. Bazike bakali kwaangwa *maganda* munsingo. = Slaves were bound about the neck with forked collars. Also *inkabo*.
the month of June, e.g. Mu Zambia impeyo yaanda mumwezi wa *Igandangali*. = In Zambia the cold becomes freezing in the month of June. Also Gandapati.
a bull frog, pl. magande or maande, e.g. Bamwi bantu balalya magande. = Some people eat bull-frogs.
mumulo= The bull frog is croaking in the river.
what is unripe or uncooked (fruit or vegetable), pl. maganga, e.g. Aaya mango mmaganga. These mangoes are unripe. Also ikkwange, pl. makwange.
an ear of sorghum with grain, e.g. Koleta *gangala* lyamaila lyomwe. = Bring one ear of sorgum. Also maangala, pl. myaangala.

a small hollow in the ground where seed has been sown, pl. maganka, e.g. Tweende tukasye *maganka* mu-muunda. = Let us go and make holes for sowing in the field. (when used as a verb, e.g. Tiimwali kulimina pe mwali kuya kugangaika buyo. = You were not weeding properly you were just making holes. (kugankila = kusyanga mumwezi wa Itwi)
a wasp, e.g. Mubwa walumwa *ganka* mubwina bwasulwe. = The dog was stung by a wasp in the burrow of the hare. Also iganko
a wasp, e.g. Ndalumwa *ganko* aliso. = I have been stung by a wasp on the eye.

a single inspiration, e.g. Cimwi ciindi ulajana muntu ujisi *ganu* lyomwe biyo nkokuti ulamuka kuyeeya. = Sometimes you find that a person has one idea only, which shows he is slow in thinking. Also gano.
a bad habit, e.g. *Ali nguwe mpaakali kujanwa gayu litasisiki pe.* = In him there was found a bad habit which could not be hidden. Also *kampenda*.
a male place for instruction, converse, eating and sleeping, e.g. *Ciluli cagobelo capya.* = The roof of the men's shelter has been burnt. Also *cipala*

time after sunset, e.g. *Ndajana muyuni ulya nkuku kugoko.* = I found a bird eating a chicken after sunset. *Mula-vwu wakasika kuti azikulume nombe ciindi cagoko.* = The lion arrived to attack the cattle at sunset. *Bana balainka mafwumo-fwumo musyokwe kukweembela anzala yabo, kukuboola ndigoko, nelitesuka zuba.* = The children go to the bush in the morning with hunger to herd, returning is at sunset when the sun is sinking.

the harvest, e.g. *Ciindi cagoloka bantu banji tiibakaoloka mapopwe akaambo kakumuka kwamvwula.* = At the time for eating the first maize many people did not eat it because of the lateness of the rains (when used as verb, *ciindi cakooloka*)
the time when the mealies ripen, e.g. *Ciindi cagoloko bantu balazyana masabe.* = At the time when mealies ripen people dance the masabe. Also *igoloka*.
a lily, e.g. *Mumulonga kuli golokoko libotu.* = There is a beautiful lily in the river.

Adam's apple (a projection at the front of the neck formed by the thyroid cartilage of the larynx.), e.g. *Igolyo-golyo lilacisa kumena cintu.* = The thyroid cartilage pains when swallowing something. Also *igoyooyo, ikkulumina*.
