back of neck, e.g. *Muntu naawa waakuumya golyoolyo ansi.* = When the person fell he banged the back of his head on the ground. Also *kagulumwe, kaleente*
a house for storing grain, e.g. *Kozwisya mapopwe mugombwa.* = Take the maize out of the grain store. also *butala*.
type of tree, soft wood, easily planted, e.g. *Bataata basimpa igombwa lyambewu.* = My father made a fence for the garden by planting *gombwa* trees. Also *moombwa*.
the knee, pl. *magondo*, e.g. *Ndafwuyuka gondo nindawa mubbola.* = I have sprained my knee when I fell playing football.

gum, gummy pulp, slime, e.g. *Ooyu mubondo ulijisi goni kapati.* = This barbel fish is very slippery. *Komukokolola goni mulwazi ayoye kabotu.* = Clear the gunk from the patient so that he can breathe properly.
a claw, pincer, antenna, e.g. *Inkala wakiikompola goonkonono lyomwe sulwe.* = The rabbit broke one claw of the crab.
first attempts of child to stand on it's own, e.g. *Mwana waima goonkonono.* = The child has learnt to stand up for the first time.
a very big anklet of metal, pl. *magoto*, e.g. *Igoto lyacibulo lyalokela a kuulu kwamwana watyoka.* = A big piece of metal fell on the leg of a child breaking it.
a bubble, pl. *magovwu*, e.g. *Mubwa ulya govwu lyansipa.* = The dog is eating bubbles of the soap. Also *iccovwu*.
one big hair, as of horse's tail, pl. *magoya*, e.g. *Igoya lyamucila wabbiza lyakosoka.* = A big hair of the horse fell off.
the human windpipe, gullet, e.g. *Igoyooyo ncecibeela mwiinda cakulya kuya mwida.* = The gullet is the part through which food passes to the stomach.
a big spider, e.g. Kuli gubi lipati munanda yabakaapa. = There is a big spider in the house of my grandmother.
a big web, e.g. Eeli gubi lyasiluubilili ndipati. = This web of the spider is big.
a mist, e.g. Meenda aya alaa gubi. = There is a mist over the water.
dim vision, e.g. Ndilaa gubi kumeso. = My eyes are misty.
mist, e.g. Taakali kubona kabotu pe wali kwiide kubona gubiibi lyamumuni. He could not see well but could only see a mist of light.
light attire, e.g. Ndasama gubi-gubi nkaambo kulapya. = I wear light attire because it is hot.
a spider with enlarged abdomen, e.g. Igubilili lyanyikila mumeenda. = A spider dropped into the water.

dimness, blurred vision, e.g. Basyaanene tabeendi kabotu nkaambo balaa gubilizi mumeso. My grandfather does not walk well because he has a thick cobweb (cataracts) in the eyes. Ncintu ciyumu kugusya gubilizi ligwitide mumitwe yabantu. It is a hard thing to take away the thick cobweb which clings to the minds of people. (igubilizi derives from lubilili, a cobweb)
a cause of haste, e.g. Lufwu Iwamuntu ndigubilizya bantu. = The death of a person makes people hurry.
a cavity in the ground igugusu a cockroach, pl. magugusu, e.g. Eeli gugusu lilaa mayi ayanda kukonkonwa. This cockroach has eggs that are about to be hatched. Also ipempya, mapempya, igukusu.
a large insect, e.g. Ndalumwa guka akuulu. = I was bitten on the leg by a big insect. Also cuuka
a cavity in the ground, e.g. Acibuye cacikuta kuli guku pati. = There is a big hole in the floor of the enclosure.
bleeding gums, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa gulamenyo. This child has bleeding gums. Also ulaa musyibu
a big mound of white termites, e.g. Tuya kukuteya nswa agulu lyesu. = We are going to trap termites at our big termite mound.
a big leg, e.g. Ooyu muntu mmulema, ulaa gulu lipati. This person is lame, she has a large leg. Also kuulu.
the back of the neck, e.g. Mwana wangu uzimbide gulyu-gulyu. = My child is swollen at the back of the neck. Also igolyo-golyo
an enlarged stomach, e.g. Mwana oyu ncalaa gumba lyabula, uciswa bulwazi bwanzala. = The reason why this child has a big stomach is that he is suffering from malnutrition.
type of tree, e.g. Inzuki zyakanjila mugumba lilaa mpako mpati. The bees entered a gumba tree which had a large hole.

a big blanket, e.g. Igumbezi lyabana lyaligwa mpongo mulyayanikidwe. The blanket of the children has been eaten by goats where it was hung up to dry. Wakasya cilindi, wakabweza gumbezi lyakali kuvwumba bana bakwe akuvwunga mutunta wamubwa akuvwumbila mu-cuumbwe. = He dug a hole, he took the big blanket that was covering his children and wrapped the dead body of the dog and buried it. Also ligumbesa, igumbeza, lipayi, ngubo.
a jigger/chigger (a tropical flea, a harvest bug), magundu, e.g. Kuli magundu mumapopwe. = There are jiggers in the maize.

a waterless plain, e.g. Tuya kukweembela basune mugundu. = We are going to herd the oxen on the waterless plain. Basimpongo baliitobela nsolo mumasamu. Bana-bana balacaala mugundu beembela mpongo. = The goatherds follow the honey birds among the trees. The smaller children remain in the water-less plain herding the goats.
type of tree, acacia with short straight thorns, e.g. Ndayaswa bumvwa bwagunga. = I have been pricked by a thorn from the *igunga* tree.
a type of grass, e.g. Bumwi buzuba Syaanasulwe wakajana mbizi yakali kucela *gungambizi* mucisaka. = One day a hare found a zebra grazing grass in the forest.
downy feathers, e.g. Bana bankwilimba bacitalika kuzwa *gungungu*. = The young pidgeons are producing their soft feathers. Also ifwintifwinti
big black ants which travel in pairs and do not bite, e.g. Mwana uyoowa *gungunyewu*. = The child is afraid of big black ants. (family of basimunyewu)
a fowl's ovary, e.g. Nitwakaijaya nkuku twajana *igungunyo* lilizimbide. = When we killed the hen we found the ovary swollen. Also cizyalilo cankuku.
the coconut of the kankomone palm-tree, e.g. Ndajana buyo *gunka* lyomwe ansi. = I only found one coconut on the ground. Also ivwuma, mankomona.
a large traditional stool, e.g. Mudaala ulaa *guno* ndyakkala lyoonse. = The old man has a big traditional stool upon which he always sits. Also *cuuno*
a big tumour, e.g. Uciswa *gute* mumutwe. = She has a big abcess on the head. Also *cuute*.
a hole in the ground made by termites, e.g. Basimunyewu bakabamba *guugu* munzila. = The black ants made a hole in the path. Cilaa *guugu* = It is hollow.
a strong wind, e.g. *Iquwo* lyausya samu pati. = The great wind made
guava fruit, pl. makwaba, e.g. Uuciswa walya buyo _gwaba_ lyomwe. = The sick one only ate one guava.
wide opening, e.g. Kuli _gwala_ (bukwazi) kumulyango. = The door is open.

a disturbance, e.g. Tee kufwumbwa kuti muntu ulila mufwu nokuba kuti waamba zicisizya kumoyo takutegwa kwaba umucitila _gwegwetela_. = Even when the mourner says something painful when he is mourning the dead, it does not mean that someone else should cause a disturbance against him. Also -gwegwetela
the leaf of maize, pl. magwelele, e.g. Komupa _gwelele_ musune. = Give the ox a leaf of maize. Also ikkweelele
shoulder, pl. magwezyo, e.g. Baalumi bavwula kubikka nkuni a_gwezyo_. = Men usually carry firewood on the shoulder.
the small wild orange, pl. mawi, e.g. Eeli _gwi_ lyakabizwa. = The small wild orange was ripe.
the European potatoe, pl. magwili, e.g. Njanda kusyanga _gwili_ mumbewu. = I want to plant potatoe in my garden
a shirt, e.g. Kondisumina nkopela _ahempe_. = Sew buttons for me on the shirt.
a good luck snake, e.g. Mutaijayi _hongoke_ nkaambo tailumi. = Do not kill a good-luck snake because it does not bite. Also ingogoce, ingokoce, inongoce.

a fish trap, e.g. Ncibatajana nswi muhyahya (syasya) nkaambo bakamuka kuteya. = The reason that they did not find fish in the trap is that they were late to trap. (While _moono_ is the normal term for these cone-shaped traps throughout central Africa, on the plateau it is sometimes replaced by the term mungwala, and in the escarpment by the term, *ihyahya*. see Barrie Reynolds, *The Material Culture of the Gwembe Valley*.)
the sea. e.g. Kuli mato manji a *jabayaba* sunu. = There are many boats on the sea today.
mist, e.g. *Ndilaa jabilisi* kumeso *ncetaboni kabotu*. = I have a mist before my eyes that is why I do not see well.
skin, e.g. *Koibulula jabilisi lili atalaa mukupa*. = Remove the skin from the milk.
fatty membrane round the bowels.
scum on top of water, e.g. *Meenda ali mucikala alaa jabilizi*. = There is scum on the water in the well. Also nyanzabili.

weir of grass and branches, a bank across a current of water for catching fish, e.g. *Bamakaintu balajaya nswi zinji mujalilo*. The women kill many fish using a weir. Also *lujalilo, mutulauma, mutuntuulu* (heap of soil), *impuo* (heap of stones)

a hoe, pl. *maamba*, e.g. *Mwiini wajamba watyoka*. The handle of the hoe is broken. *Jamba lyanombe* = a plough. *Jamba lyacilumbu* a prayer-hoe. *Jamba lyabunduwe (lyabulumbu)* = a prayer-hoe, e.g. *Kaindi bantu bakali kubelesya maamba abulumbu mulukwato*. = Long ago people were using prayer hoes in marriage.
a hand, e.g. *Ndiciswa janza Iyalulyo*. = My right hand is unwell.
hand-writing e.g. *Ulaa janza bbotu*. = He has good hand-writing.
a type of fish, pl. *mayanze*, cf. *Tacikatazyi kujaya mayanze mpaali manji*. = It is not difficult to kill *mayanze* fish where there are many. (*mayanze* can also refer to a type of song.)
an overcoat, e.g. *Ndaula jansi lyabataata*. I have bought an overcoat for my father. *Ijansi lyangu lyateta*. = My overcoat is soaked.

an unusually large head of the handle of an axe, e.g. *Igutwe lyakwe lyakali lipati alyalo lilamfwu-lamfwu - jembeembe lyamutwe*. = His large head was big and also long resembling the massive head of an axe handle.
an egg, pl. *mayi*, e.g. *Inkuku yatula ji lyomwe*. The hen has laid one egg.
a sorgum plant, pl. *maila*, e.g. *Musune walya jila*. An ox has eaten a sorgum plant.
a big shin, e.g. *Mweenzuma ulaa majindi mapati*. = My friend has big shins. Also *mwiindi*.
the base grinding stone, e.g. *Koleta jio tuziye busu*. = Bring the grinding stone so that we grind flour. Also *iziyo, izyiyo*. (Mwanankando is the stone for rubbing.)
a big cloud, pl. *mayoba*, e.g. *Indeke yavwumbwa mayoba*. = The aeroplane has been covered up in the clouds.
mayoba sunu*. = There are big clouds today.
a yoke, pl. *majoko*, e.g. *Ijoko lyesu ndipati*. = Our yoke is big. Also *ijogwe*
long rubber boots, gum-boots, pl. *majombo*, e.g. *Majombo mmabotu kubantu babeleka mumabwe nomuba mumamvwa*. = Gum-boots are good for people who work in rocky or thorny areas.
a heavy chisel-ended iron bar for drilling blast-holes, a crowbar, e.g. *Jombolo lyangu lyatyoka*. My crowbar got broken.

a long unbarbed heavy-headed spear used for hunting elephant, e.g. *Ijonga ndibotu kuwezya bazovwu*. = The *ijonga* spear is good for hunting elephants. *Mufwuzi wakafwula ijonga yakuvwimya bazovwu*. = The blacksmith forged a spear for hunting elephants.

a millipede, pl. mayongolwa, e.g. *Ijongolwa lilijisi maulu atabaliki.* = The millipede has uncountable legs. *Ijongolwa livwula kubonwa ciindi camainza.* A millipede is normally seen during the rainy season. Also moongolwa, ijongolo.
the sky, the firmament, e.g. *Ijulu lilasiya mbi.* = The sky is black.
pressure, influence for good or evil, e.g. *Kuti nilyatali jungwe lya Mutinta, nindatakamaninzya cikolo.* = If it had not been for the influence of Mutinta, I would not have finished school.
act of inciting people to do what you yourself would not do, e.g. *Ndime ndiya kuba jumbayumba lyamanyongwe utaambiki.* = I will become an instigator of indescribable disorder.
a giant bird, pl. mayuni, e.g. *Mutumbu wakalijana juni mumusamu.* = The suckling mother found a huge bird in a tree.
tomorrow, e.g. *Basankwa baya kuunka kukulima junza.* = The boys are going to plough tomorrow. Also juunza.
a wave, pl. mayuwe
a word, pl. majwi, e.g *Twakaateelela majwi ngaakali kwaamba munene naakali kutulaya.* We listened to many words which the old man was saying when he was advising us.

the voice, e.g. *Ndamvwa buyo ijwi, pesi wali kukanana tiindamubona.* = I just heard a voice, but I did not see the one who was speaking. *Ijwi tete likkazika moyo kumuntu onse.* A soft voice makes everyone feel at ease. *Ijwi ligogoma* = a guttural sound.
what remains of chest when ribs have been removed, e.g. *Ikaaba kankuku mukaabane abana mwalya.* = Share the chest of the hen with the children when you eat. Also nsando.
a short story, e.g. *Ndiyanda kumwaanina kaano.* = I want to tell you a short story. Also caano.
a beaded waist-band, pl. makaba, e.g. *Basimbi bakaindi bakali kuyanda kusama makaba muzibuno zyabo.* = The girls of long ago liked wearing beaded bands around their waists. Also ikkaba.
a blanket, e.g. *Mukamufwu bakamupa kaba lipati.* = They gave the widow a big blanket. Also ipayi, igumbezi.
a small kraal, e.g. *Kaba kaboombe kamwaika.* = The small kraal for the calves was destroyed. Also luba (see under makaba)
charcoal, pl. makala, e.g. *Bacembele bakali kuyandaula makala akufwebya ncelwa.* = The old woman was looking for embers to light a calabash-pipe. Also masizi.

a roofing-pole, pl. makalisyo, e.g. *Makalisyo amuumba-nkoli mmayumu kuyasya ciluli cananda.* Roofing-poles made from the muumba-nkoli tree are good for constructing a roof of a house. Also isomo, ikankala.
the pith, e.g. *Utalimeni kanci lyamunsale.* = Do not swallow the pith of sugar-cane. Also icanki, cikanci. elephant is tough. also cikanda, ikkanda.
a clot of blood ikani affair, matter pl. makani, e.g. *Koboola musa, ndijisi ikani anduwe.* = Come my friend, I have a matter to discuss with you. Also inkani.
a roofing-pole, pl. makankala, e.g. *Muyaki waunka kukugonka maka nkala.* = The builder went off to cut roofing poles. Also isomo, ikalisyo.
a piece of meat e.g. *Sibbuku wakatola ikanko lipati lyanyama.* = The headman took a big piece of meat from the back of the cow. Also cituli.
a small hollow in the ground for sowing seeds, e.g. Kamudokoola tukanko atusamu tusyange mapopwe. = Poke out small holes in the ground with sticks so that we plant the maize. Also iganko.
a large mouth, e.g. Syuumbwa ulaa kanwa pati. = A lion has a big mouth.
card-playing, e.g. Twali kusobana kasi. = We were playing cards. Also njuka, ikkasi.
a head-pad, coil, e.g. Kozinga kata lyaloozi. = Wind a coil of fibre. Also ikkata, inkata
a beaded waist-band, pl. makkaba, e.g. Sunu bamakaintu tabasami makkaba. = Today the women do not wear beaded waist bands. Also ikaba.
a portion, e.g. Amunditendele kkaba lyamafwuta nkabikke mucisyu. = Cut me out the thick portion of fat so that I put it in the vegetables.
a hot coal, e.g. Utalyati kkala lyamulilo lilapya. = Do not step on a hot coal, it burns. Also isizi.
a wide shallow well, e.g. Inombe zyakanjila mukkala. = The cattle entered the wide shallow well.
a shoal/collection of fish, e.g. Bacembele bandipa kkama lyanswi. = The old woman has given me a bundle of fish.
a large hide, e.g. Ikkanda lyamuzovwu ndiyumu. = The hide of an elephant is thick.
clot of blood, e.g. Mpubakali kujayila ngulube ndakajana kkandalowa. I found a clot of blood where they were killing a pig. Also bwaanga bulowa
a verandah, e.g. Atuyuse mvwula mukkoce. = Let us shelter from the rain in the verandah.
a big rope for catching big game like buffaloes, e.g. Amoose kkole tutambisye basune. = Make a big rope to tame the oxen. Also lukole.
a small hole for concealing noose for catching game, e.g. Insumba yamunyati yakajatwa mukkole. = The hoof of the buffalo was caught in a trap.
a cold in the chest, e.g. Ndiciswa kkolokolo, ijwi ncolisinkide. = I am suffering from a cold, that is why my voice is blocked. ikkolokolo lyakakweekwe = whooping cough.
a door on hinges, e.g. Mucembele wakayuba kusule akkoma. = The old woman hid behind the door. Wakakonkoozya akkoma akanteengezya kakwe. = She knocked on the door with her little finger.
a hole from which potteryclay is dug, e.g. Ikkomba lyabulongo lyakadilimuka. = The hole from which pottery clay is extracted has caved in.
the navel, e.g. Mutinta wakalumwa nzengene akkombo. = A tick bit Mutinta on the navel.
a verandah, eaves of house, e.g. Ikkota lyananda lilazwisya. = The verandah of the house is leaking. Also ikkoce, iduze.
any big expanse, e.g. Inga tandicikonzyi kutakubona mwanamakani aya kumanina kkotyo lyamwaka. = I am not able to miss seeing my friend for the duration of the whole year.
a cucumber, a small watermelon, pl. makowa, e.g. Ikkowa lyakujika lyakabola. = The cucumber to be cooked is rotten.
a weak, useless person, e.g. Naceta ndikkowa lyamuntu, cakabacisya nsoni kapati bazyali bakwe. = Naceta is a useless person, she brought great shame on her parents.
the shoulder, e.g. Masowe wakalumwa nzengene akkuko. = Masowe was bitten by ticks on the shoulder. Wakaboola umwi musilisi akundijata akkuko. = A certain doctor came and held
the wind-pipe, e.g. Mwana watingwa kafwuwa kanswi akkulumino. = The child was choked by a small fish bone in the wind-pipe.
a heap, a pile, e.g. Munene wakalijisi kkungo lyamali mukaanda kakwe. = The old man had a pile of money in his little house.
a cloud, pl. makumbi, e.g. Mujulu muli kkumbi pati lyamvwula. = There is a big rain-cloud in the sky.
warmth, heat, e.g. Kasise kakakasaalilwa mukaindi kaniini nkaambo muciteente mwakali kkutikuti. = The robin was warmed up in a short time because there was heat in the nest.
the skin of an animal, e.g. Babwa balya kkutu lyamoombe wakafwa jilo. = The dogs are eating the hide of a calf which died yesterday.

a piece of bark, the rind of soft fruit, the shell of an egg or ground-nut, the scab over a sore, the prepuce, pl. makwa, e.g. Kuli wabikka kkwa lyaji mucikko. = There is someone who has put the shell of an egg on the fire.
a leaf of the maize plant, pl. makweelele, e.g. Kamuumpa makweelele munsi abutala. = Burn the maize leaves near the bin.
a prostitute, e.g. Akabe buyo kkweelele uyandisisya buyo mali kuzwa kubasankwa. = Let her become a prostitute who just longs for money from men. Also kapenta.
a type of bird, the big white stork, pl. makobondo. e.g. *Makobondo* alya nzengene murnombe. = The big white storks eat the ticks on the cattle. Also inkobo
a gathering, e.g. Kumucado kuli koka lyabantu. = At the wedding feast there is a gathering of people. Also inkamu, imbunga.
a channel for water, e.g. Meenda amvwula akasya kololomba munzila. = The rain water dug a trench in the path. Also *idongalonga*
a pad of hay or straw, e.g. Ikombe lyakapya jilo bana nibakali kusobana mulilo. = The pad of hay was burnt yesterday when the children were playing with fire.
the navel, pl. makombo, e.g. Bana nobakali kutanta ncinga umwi wakalicisa akombo. = When the children were getting up on the bicycle, one of them hurt herself in the navel.
the prow or stern of a canoe, e.g. Ikombo lyabwato lilicengeme ncobuteendi kabotu. = The prow of the boat is bent that is why it does not move properly.

clod of earth, e.g. Bana nobakalede abulo, bakalokelwa ikomwe kuzwa atalaa bwaanda. = When the children were sleeping on the bed, a clod of earth from the top of the wall fell on them. Also igomwe, ivwunga.

tracks, paths, sing. mukondo, e.g. Beembezi balatanda mbelele zyabo kukalundu, balo balaima mukondo. = The shepherds drive their sheep to a hill, they stop in the tracks. Mukondo balasobana, balasotooka, balabumbuluka, balababama mbuli ndeke. = They play in the tracks, they jump about, they roll about, they glide like a plane.
cake made by ants under- ground, e.g. Kwajanika konga pati mutwali kusya nzuki. = A big ant-cake was found where we were digging out the bees.
scab over a sore, pl. makookonde, e.g. Zicisa nizyakayumya, kwakacaala makookonde. = When the sores healed, scabs remained.

an archway of poles, e.g. Basimbi nibakaunka bakainda munsi-munsi ikopano. = When the girls went ikosi-kosi a stern gaze, a severe look, e.g. Mweenzu talangwi kosi-kosi inga wayoowa. A visitor is not stared at as he might fear.
a lump, a knot, a hard swelling hard unripe fruit, e.g. Mwana walya koto lyalingo. The child has eaten a hard unripe mango.
a verandah, e.g. Atukkalile mukotye muli cimvwule. Let us sit on the verandah where it is shaded. Also ikkoce, iduze.
scum, foam, froth, e.g. Muzisani nzesanzya kuli kovvu linji. There is much lather in the clothes which I am washing. Also movwu, ifwulu
twine, string, e.g. Bana, amoose koyo tukateye nziba. Children, plait a string so that we trap a dove. Also kooye, kakole.
a small heart, e.g. Muntu ulya ulaa koyo kaniini. That person is shorttempered. (Ncibi kubaa koyo-koyo. It is bad to be short-tempered.)

a stalk of grain, a field with only stalks left standing, pl. makuba, e.g. Bacembele beenzya kuba lyamapopwe. The old woman is walking with a maize stalk as a walking stick. Mucembele wakali kukukula makuba mumuunda wakwe. The old woman was clearing the maize stalks from her field. Also ikkuba.
a type of bird, the vulture, e.g. Ikubi lilya nyama yakabola. The vulture eats rotten meat. Also sikube.
the shoulder-blade the shoulder, pl. makuko, e.g. Kondibikka nkuni akuko. Put the firewood on my shoulder. Also ikkuko.
a cloth big enough to cover the whole body, e.g. Mulwazi ulivwumbide kukubu mubili onse. The patient is covered with a cloth over the whole body.
faint spoor in grass, e.g. Nitwali kweenda twabona ikula munsaanzila. When we were going along we saw spoor beside the path.
the throat, the windpipe or trachea, e.g. Meenda anduumpa akulumina. The water has burnt my throat. Also ikulumino, ikulyukulyu, ikkulumina.
the windpipe, gullet, e.g. Ndatingwa kafwuwa kanswi akulumino. I was choked in the windpipe by a little bone of a little fish. Also ikulumina, igoyooyo
the throat, e.g. Nindali kulya nsima yaima akulyukulyu. When I was eating nsima it got blocked in my throat. Also ikulumina, ikkulumina.
a hole in the ground made by termites, e.g. Imbeba yanjila mukumbwi. A mouse has entered the termite-hole. also iguugu, nkumbwi.
a shoal/collection of fish, e.g. Ndaula kungo lyanswi. I have bought a bundle of fish.
a tame duck, a goose, e.g. Ikungubu lyalumwa babwa lyafwa kale. The tame duck which was bitten by the dogs has aleady died.
a place for sleeping for several people, e.g. Bantu adilwe boona kungubulo. At the funeral people lay together on the floor.
a big piece of wood or log, e.g. Kosikka kuni acikko. Put a log on the fire.
an incurable foot-ulcer, e.g. Basilisi tabauzyi musamu wakusilika ikuni. The doctors do not know of any medicine for curing the foot-ulcer. Also dondamwaka
an ear of sorghum with or without grain, e.g. Kotenda kunka lyanzembwe. Cut an ear of sorghum. Also ikkunka.
a small coconut, e.g. Kamuya mukandicelele tukunka tobilo nditolele bana. Go and gather for me two small coconuts so that I take them for the children.
a small palm tree, e.g. Bana bakagonka kakunka. = The children have cut down a small palm tree.
an incurable foot ulcer, e.g. Mwanaangu uciswa kunkalwizi, kunyina naya kupona. My child is sick with an incurable foot ulcer, he will never be cured. Also ikuni.
a fibre of aloe, e.g. Ndigonke kusa lyakuyasya cibalu. = Let me cut fibre for building a wind-screen.
a traditional stringed-dress worn by Gwembe Valley women in the past, pl. makusa. Also maaya
a very fertile piece of land, a garden, e.g. Ikuti lilaa munzi wangu lilakomenzya mapopwe kabotu. = The fertile piece of land in my village makes maize grow very well. Also idinga.

a salt-pan, e.g. a shallow depression in the ground in which salt water evaporates to leave a deposit of salt. e.g. Bamacembele baunka kukusya munyo kukuto. The old women went to dig salt at the salt-pan.
a fish thrown on the bank by swollen stream, e.g. Twakajana ikuwo lyanswi mumbali amulonga. = We found a fish left behind near the river by the swollen water.
a piece of bark, pl. makwa, e.g. Kopandula kwa elyo tusikke. = Split that bark so that we stoke the fire. Ikwa lyamuumba lilalula. The bark of the muumba tree is bitter/hot. Also ikkwa.
a thorny cucumber, pl. makwaambala, e.g. Bana bateya basimaankobbolyo amakwaambala. = The children are trapping blackbirds with thorny cucumbers.
an iguana living in a hole in the ground, e.g. Twakajaya kwaba mubwina bwagalaba. = We killed an iguana in an antbear's den.
species of fish, e.g. Ndalobola kwabankuyu mumulonga. = 1 have killed a kwabankuyu fish in the river
a skin gament, e.g. Bacembele bakasama kwakwabinda kumalende. The old lady wore a skin garment at the rain-shrine.
a scab e.g. Kolibbabbula kwakwabinda lili acicisa. Remove the scab from the sore.
an iguana, e.g. Ikwamba lyanjila mumpako yabbwe. An iguana entered a cave in the rock. Also ibulu, ikwaba, cikwaba.
a box with nailed lid, a box made of metal with a round lid, a coffin, pl. makwati, e.g. Ikwati lyazisani lyabbigwa. The box of clothes was stolen.

eco kwakanyina makwati. Bakaindi tiibakali kubikwa mukwati pesi cifwene cakali kubambwa cini-cini. = Long ago there were no coffins. The people of the past were not put in coffins but a real grave was made.
bride-wealth given by bridegroom to relatives of bride, e.g. Badaala batola mali akwato koo Mutinta. = The old man has taken bride-wealth at Mutinta's house.
sheath of maize-cob, e.g. Koleta kweelele lyapopwe tuyasye mulilo. = Bring the sheath of a maize cob so that we light the fire.
a whetstone for sharpening knives or spears, pl. makwengelo, e.g. Koya ukwenge cipeni akwengelo. = Go and sharpen the knife on the whetstone.

the name slaves inherited from their owners, e.g. Ba Mulembwe mbobakali Baloongo, abalo aba bazike bakabalilwa kwibbandilo lyabasimalelo babo. As Ba Mulembwe was of the Baloongo clan, all these slaves were identified with the name of their master. ikwibba kwibba lyaloozi. = one length of fibre string, pl. *makwibba*, e.g. *Bana bamucete beenda amaaya, takwe nebasama zisamo zibotu pe. Basama tupapa twabanyama amakwibba aloozi.* = Children of a poor person go about dressed in the traditional stringed garment, they never have good clothes. They wear shells of animals and strings of fibre.
a sling Also *ikwisyo*
a stone for crushing nuts, for mixing ochre with fat, etc. e.g. *Kamukwiya ndongwe akwiyo.* = Mash the groundnuts with the crushing stone.
a lamp, (ety. English) e.g. *Ila-mbe lyazima niwamana mungwimba.* = The light went off when the parrafin finished.
a hole in which seed is sown, pl. *malambo*, e.g. *Bataata basyanga mapopwe mumalambo mumbewu.* = My father sows seed in holes in the garden.
a piece of land, e.g. *Ndasyanga buyo lambo lyomwe.* = I have only planted one piece of land.
a bracelet of wire and thread, e.g. *Mwana usamide landa kukuboko.* = The child is wearing a wire-and-thread bangle on the arm. Also *idanda*
a flower, e.g. *Ilangalanga lyaneta.* = The flower got withered. Also *iduba*
a mat formed into a canoe, e.g. *Iliba ndyotwakabamba jilo, taliibuki kabotu mumeenda.* = The canoe made out of a mat which we made yesterday does not float properly on water. Also *ciliba*
a fall-trap, e.g. *Tiilyalebuka liba lya-mudaala.* = The fall-trap of the old man has not fallen. Also *idiba.*
a tooth, pl. *menyo*, e.g. *Ilinyo lyomwe lyazwa mukanwa lyamwana.* = One tooth came out of the child's mouth. Also *linyo*
a petticoat, e.g. *Ilokwe lyakaula baama lyakakomenesya.* = The petticoat which my mother bought was too long. Also *ilongwe.*
a stick planted for a hunting shrine, which grows into a tree on which are hung trophies and instruments of hunting. Also *muntiokela*
a petticoat Also *ilokwe.*
a species of wild fruit, e.g. *Tuya kukucela loolo.* = We are going to gather fruit from the *muloolo* tree. Also *mukonyombwa, mudyaki.*
a flower, e.g. *Iluba lili munanda lyalangazya.* = The flower which is in the house has blossomed. Also *iduba*
a big striped mason wasp which stings cattle, e.g. *Ndalumwa lumanombe mumutwe.* = I have been stung by a big mason wasp. Also *cumanombe, idumanombe.*
a big black mason wasp, e.g. *Ilumanyati lilacisa kuti lyakuluma.* = The mason wasp pains if it stings you.
a young girl, e.g. *Musimbi wakafwa jilo wakacili mandala.* = The girl who died yesterday was still a young girl. Also *ciliya*

a collection of cattle kraals, sing. *mumba*, e.g. *Kumazuba basinombe balayobolola nombe zyabo, balazijalila mu-mba.* = In the evening the herders gather the cattle together and enclose them in the kraals. Also *ziba, (sing. ciba.)*
a sign-post, marks on the ground, a target, e.g. *Mputwagolela kusyanga twabikka mbaakani.* = We have put a mark on the ground where we stopped planting. Also *impaakani*
a cowry shell, (cyprea moneta) e.g. *Bamacembele bakaindi bakali kuyandisya kusama mbaamba.* = The women of long ago were fond of wearing cowry shells. Also *mbaanyina.*
a large drop, e.g. *Kwaloka mbaamba lyameenda.* = A large drop of water fell down.
a duiker, e.g. Muvwimi have been affected by the mbala plant a wajaya mbaambi antobolo. = The hunter mother squirts breast milk on him. killed a duiker with a gun.

a bullet, e.g. Muvwimi naakali kupakila Also kasya, nakasya. ntobolo, wakaluba kubikka mbala mumuimbaanyina a cowry shell, (a mollusc luli. = When the hunter was loading his with a smooth, glossy domed shell with a gun, he forgot to put the bullet in the long, narrow opening) e.g. Basimbi ba- barrel. nsiku bakali kuyandisya kusama mbaa- imbalo roofing timber, e.g. Basankwa

In traditional life the girls were bagonka mbalo zyaciluli. = The boys are very fond of wearing cowry shells. Kaindi cutting roofing-poles. Also lubalo. musankwa wakali kulangilwa kuti asamike imbamba skin disease, e.g. Bantu bamusimbi wakwe zintu zibotu nzyobakali talyi kabotu baciswa mbamba. = People kusama, mbuli kumusukila kasalu ka- who do not eat well suffer from skin mpongo, kumuulila bulungu, kumujanina disease. Also mbanje.

mubul= imbambo the shortest rib, e.g. Naakali In the past a young man was sought who kunduuma, wakandityola mbambo. = would dress his wife with beautiful things, When he was beating me he broke my such as preparing the hide of a goat, shortest rib. buying beads for her and finding cowry imbanje dagga, e.g. Imbanje njiyashells for threading among the beads. sondosya muntu oyu. = It is dagga which Also imbaamba. has made this person mad.

ox with crumpled horns, e.g. imbasela a bonus, something addMusune wesu ujisi meja ambaba. = Our itional given freely, e.g. Nindaula mapoox has crumpled horns. pwe manji, bandibikkila ambasela. = imbabala a bushbuck, e.g. Babwa When I bought much maize they gave me baalilwa kujaya mbabala. The dogs some extra for free. Also impasela. (Ila)

column1: have failed to kill the bushbuck imbata
column2: sweet-potatoe, e.g. Tuya Also mubabala. kukusimpa mbata kumuunda. = We are

black spots on legs from going to plant sweet-potatoes in the field. sitting close to fire, e.g. Muntu uyotesya Imbata yanditinga amoyo. A sweet-pokapati mulilo, ulaba ambala mumaulu. = tatoe stuck in my throat. Also cimbwali.
scar, e.g. Mbata zyamapenzi zilali-toher/himself at the fire, develops black ndezya mumeso akwe. The scars of spots on the legs. Also imbale suffering showed themselves in his eyes.
a type of gourd, e.g. Kamuleta cinkuli Also ibata, lubata. cambala tubambe cipiililo. Bring an imbaya fences, pl. of lubaya, e.g.

gourd so that we make a ritual Imbaya zyamyuunda zyakapya lyakapya container. (A gourd containing beer which syokwe. The fences of the fields were is poured out or spit out at the doorway burnt down when there was a bush fire. when calling on the ancestors.) Bami tiibakajisi maanda akubetekela ali

a type of plant (Euphoria tirucalli) used mbuli sunu pe, baali kubetekela mumbaya as a hedge around a village, the laetex is zyamamwa. The chiefs did not have used as a fish poison. e.g. e.g. Muntu wa- houses in which to try cases as today, toogwa mbala bakamupiila mukupa wa- they were trying cases within fences of munkolo. For a person whose eyes thorns.
short-sightedness, e.g. *Ulaa mbayimbayi*. = He is short-sighted. Also *ibbayibayi*.
habit of hiding food for fear of being deprived of it, greed, e.g. *Mwana ulaa mbayo tayandi kulya antoomwe abeenizinyina*. = A greedy child does not want to eat with other children. Also *inzuno*.
cloth for carrying baby on back, e.g. *Mutumbu wakaanga imbazyo kuti abbale mwanaakwe*. = The suckling mother tied the cloth for carrying the baby. Also *ingubo*.
a mouse, a field rat, e.g. *Bana basya mbeba mucindongwe*. = The children are digging rats in the groundnut plot.
bribe, e.g. *Wakapa mbebekezyo kutegwa kaambo kakwe kabekwe abasibbuku*. = He gave him a bribe so that his case could be tried by the headman.

a simple round wooden bowl, e.g. *Imbede yakali yakunywida cibwantu a bukoko*. = The *imbede* bowl was for drinking sweet-beer or beer. *Musimbi usanzya mbede*. = The girl is washing the bowls. Also *indido*
the point of a spear, e.g. *Imbele yasumo ilifwumpide*. = The point of the spear is blunt.
a sheep, e.g. *Imbelele tazijisi mugutu*. = The sheep have no ram.

a razor-blade, e.g. *Mwana wanengwa mbeli amunwe*. = The child was cut on the finger with a razor-blade. *Chibbwalu wakali mukandu kulwana pesi amulomo yakali mbeli*. = Chibbwalu was a coward as regards fighting, but had a mouth like a knife.
a club or stick, e.g. *Bakamuuma mbesanu musankwa utamvwi*. = They beat the stubbourn boy with a stick. Also *nkoli*.
court-trial, e.g. *Sunu mbeta zilabeda kumwami*. = Today the trials will be at the chief's place.
a garden, e.g. *Imbewu yesu izwide cisyu*. = Our garden is full of vegetables. Also *mbeu*
an adze, e.g. *Imbezo yabataata ilabosya kapati*. = The adze of my father is very sharp. Also *imbezyo*.
a chisel, an adze Also *imbezo*

the finger beside the little finger on the left hand, e.g. *Mbiliimbili ujanika akati kakantengezya a munwe waakati*. = The finger beside the little finger on the left hand is found between the little finger and the middle finger.

sap or gum of tree, juice of fruit, e.g. *Basimpongo bakacela matobo ajisi mbilila*. = The goatherds gathered matobo fruits which had juice. Balsam = *Imbilila zyamisamu zinunkilila cinonono*. Other words for gum from trees: *masina, insakizi, igoni, mukupa, bulimbo, busaki*
a sty in the eye, e.g. *Liso lyangu lijisi mbilimbili akaambo kakaundu kakanditowede*. = My eye has a sty because of a tiny seed which entered it. Also insokweeda.
a float on a fishing line, e.g. *Kobikka mbilimbili akooye kakalobo*. = Put a float on the fishing line. Also *imbilibili*.
flying shreds of burnt grass, e.g. *Muwo waleta mbimbi mulubuwa*. = The wind blew flying shreds of burnt grass into the yard. Also *mimbi*.
one who instructs boys, e.g. *Kamusala mwaalumi uluzi kuba mbimbi wabasankwa*. = Select the right man to be instructor for the boys. (Also *-sinsa, -sinsimika*)
raw meat, e.g. *Eeyi nyama nimbisi kamwiijika alimwi*. = This meat is raw cook it again. Also *cikwangi, inkwange*.
an animal similar to a duiker, e.g. *Nyama yambizi ilanona kapati*. = The meat of the imbizi is delicious.
a zebra, e.g Mubala wambizi mmubotu. e.g. = The colour of the zebra is beautiful. Also cibíze.
the point where the throat begins, e.g. Ndayaswa kamvwa kanswi ambobelo. = I have been pierced by a fish-bone at the top of the throat. Also kameneno.

hair-balls vomited by cattle, e.g. Inombe zicela kabotu ziluka mbobelo. = Cattle who graze well vomit hair-balls. Also imbobela imbobo a kind of trap, e.g. Ndajaya bakwale botatwe mumbobo. = I killed three partridges in a trap. Also kantembo.

the stings of bees, sing. lubole, e.g. Mwana naakalumwa nzuki, mbole zyakasyaala mumutwe moonse. = When the child was stung by bees, the stings remained all over its head. Kamumujwa mbole mwana. = Remove the bee-stings from the child.
ripe masuku fruit, e.g. Basimbi bayumwide zisuwo zizwide mbole. = The girls carried baskets full of ripe masuku fruit.
humus, manure, rotten things, e.g. Mumbewu yangu kuli mbolezi kapati. = There is plenty of humus in my garden.
tender meat, e.g. Eeyi nyama yankuku nimbombebombe. = The chicken meat is tender.
a touniquet, e.g. Kamumwaanga mbombolokoto muntu oyu buleke kuzwa bulowa. = Tie that man with a tourniquet to stop the blood coming out.
a mirror, e.g. Mwana wapwaya mbonembone yabanyina. = The child has broken the mirror of it's mother. Also cimboni-mboni.
a donkey, a mule, e.g. Kwesu tulimya mbongolo. = At my home we use donkeys to plough.
the pupil of the eye, e.g. Munene ulaa katube amboni. = The old man has a cataract on the pupil of the eye.
the castor-oil bean, e.g. Bakamwale kaindi bakali kunana mafwuta ambono. The female initiates long ago used to smear themselves with castor-oil. Also ibbono.
riches, wealth, sing. lubono, e.g. Bataata balaa mbono zinji. = My father has much wealth.

the castor-oil bean, e.g. Bamwi bacela mbono-mbono kumbali alwizi a kumbali atulonga. = Some collect the castor-oil bean from lakes and near rivers. Insiku mafwuta ambono-mbono akali kunana bami abavwubi. = Long ago castor-oil was only applied by chiefs and the rich. Also ibbono.
a boa-constrictor, e.g. Mubwa wakajatwa mbooma jilo wakafwa. = The dog which was attacked by a boa-constrictor yesterday died. Also muceka
mead, (honey-beer) e.g. Kaindi bamakaintu bakali kukumba mbote. = Long ago the women used to brew mead.
the edible fruit of the mabubu bush, e.g. Imbubu nzibotu kujika ceele. = Mbubu fruit is good for cooking porridge.
the nut of the imbula tree, e.g. Imbula zitaningabizwa zilaa nkamba. = The unripe mbula fruit is bitter.
a type of bird, the short-tailed warbler, e.g. Imbulaceeye nkayuni kasyoonto kapati. = The short-tailed warbler is a tiny little bird. Also imbulamweeye.
See imbulaceeye.

variegated groundnuts, e.g. Bakamuletela musozya wakavwelene abupapa bwacimbwali, mbulukutu anyemu zyakanamudononga nzezyakali zinji, nseke zyamapopwe zyakalilobede buyo. = They brought him crushed groundnuts mixed with maize grains, mixed with dried and sliced sweet-potatoes, variegated ground nuts and the *kanamudononga* groundnuts which were plentiful, grains of maize which were very few.
an ear-ache, e.g. *Baama baciswa mbulukutwi.* = My mother has an ear-ache.
a cannibal, e.g. *Imbulu-matali lyakajata mwana jilo.* = A cannibal caught a child yesterday. Also *idyabantu.*
an iguana, e.g. *Imbulamatali watumanina nkuku zyesu.* = The iguana has finished off our chickens. Also *nabulwe.*
anything round, e.g. *Imbulumbumbe zyakuumya tuyuni zyamana.* = The pellets for hitting birds are finished.
a kind of cherry, e.g. *Imbumbu zyakeeta bana zilanona.* = The imbumbu fruit which the children brought are sweet. Also *imumbu, mubumbu.*
lead bullets, e.g. *Batutuma kukuula mbumbulu kudolopo.* = They have sent us to buy bullets to the town. Also *nkulu.*
a giant, e.g. *Bana bakayoowa nibakabona imbumbunga yamwaalumi mumugwagwa.* = The children were afraid when they saw a giant on the road.
a sugary plant, e.g. *Twajana bana batafwuna mbunje mumbali amuunda.* = We found the children chewing the sugary plant near the field. Also *munsale*
a small treacherous boy, e.g. *Basazinyina Dudulika abakali kweeba bakajana mbunkwenkwe bwakalombe.* = The relatives of Dudulika and the marriage negotiators found a small treacherous youth.
swarms of small ants, e.g. *Myootokala yakali kwiile kubee mbusilikuku kuvwula.* = The vehicles were just like swarms of small ants.
an empty place or den of an animal, e.g. *Bavwimi bakajana buyo mbuta akalede sulwe.* = The hunters found only an empty place where a rabbit had lain.

seed, e.g. *Tubamba mbuto zyamapopwe.* = We are preparing maizeseeds. (seeds sown in dry ground = *ikanka, iganka, ilambo*; pumpkin seed = *lunyungu*, pl. *nyungu* also *intanga*, if dry, malekete; a seed bed = *katampu*; seed of the small melon used as relish = *bukowa*, when pounded = *musukwindi*; grass seeds = *insoce, insinya*; black-jack = *syaazyipa*)
a type of fruit, e.g. *Bana bacela mbuukuma zyakulya.* = The children are collecting mbuukuma fruit to eat. Also *mbubu, ngayi.*
a blind fly, e.g. *Bana balalumwa mbuwo ciindi camainza nobeembela.* = Children are bitten by blind flies during the rainy season when they are herding.
*nsima* without relish, e.g. *Akaambo kakutalya nswi, sunu ndali kwiide kulya nsima mbuye.* = Because of not eating fish, I have been eating *nsima* without relish.
Also *imbuye*
a dog Also *mbwa*

musical instrument played by initiates in the house, e.g. *Kamwale wakavwungana kukkala ciindi cilamfwu munanda kagamine buyo kusobanya mbwale akulizya mantimbwa.* = The initiate squated for a long time in the house just amusing herself with the *mbwale* and playing the *mantimbwa.*
type of tree (*Adenium multiflorum*) root and stem chips used as fish poison. e.g. *Tacili cibotu kubelesya imbwayuma ciindi cakuzela nswi.* = It is not good to use poison when fishing.
a lion, e.g. *Imbwayuma* mmunyama mukali kapati. = The lion is a fierce animal. Also caanza, syaanza, syuumbwa.
hair-balls vomited by cattle, e.g. Iņombe zikkuta nzeziluka *mbwebwe*. = Well-fed cattle are the ones who vomit hair-balls.
the fourth stomach of ruminants, e.g. Muvwimi naakafwunda munyama wakajana *mbwebwe* zilibolede mukati. = When the hunter opened the animal he found that the fourth stomach was rotten.
slipperiness, e.g. Cigwinya ukozya mubondo, ulijisi *mbwebwebwetu* amubili. = The eel is like the barbel it has a slipperiness on the body. Also butezi.
a moustache, e.g. Basankwa bamwi bayandisya *imbwebwedo* kutegwa kabeebelwa abamakaintu. = Some men like wearing moustaches to be admired by women.
fear, e.g. Ijilo ndakamvwide *imbwembwe*. = Yesterday I felt fear. Also cintebwe.

type of sorgum which is eaten raw, e.g. Bantu banji bakafwutuka nibakatalika kulya *imbwende*. = Many people were saved when they began to eat a type of raw sorgum. Also mwende *imbwiila* groundpeas, e.g. Musozya wambwiila ulanona kapati. = Samp mixed with groundpeas is very tasty. Wakacita kuti ciindi camasiku wajika nyemu *mbwiila*. = At night-time he used to cook groundpeas. Also nyemu mbulukutu.
Alsoiila*
a healthy beast which is smooth-skinned and fat, e.g. Moombe unyonka kabotu uba *mbwindili*. = A calf that sucks well becomes fat and smooth. Also mbwilingi
a pocket-knife, e.g. Bataata bakaula *mesi* yakubelesya. = Father bought a pocket-knife for using.
a blow with the fist, e.g. Mukubusi wakauma mudaala *mfwaindi* nkali. = The youth beat the old man with a severe blow.
a traditional pipe, e.g. *Imfwebyo* yamudaala yakapya mu Nsondo. = The old man's smoking-pipe got burnt on Sunday. Also imfwuko, imfwesyo.

grey hair, e.g. Bamadaala bakaindi bakali kumuka kuzwa mfwi kumutwe. = Old men of long ago were slow to grow grey hair on the head. Also imvwi *imfwolokwe* a table-fork, (ety. English) e.g. Bamwi bantu bakazyibila kulisya *mfwolokwe*. = Some people are used to eating with a fork. Also imfwoloko.

a clay pipe, a pipe with a long reed stem, a calabash pipe for smoking hemp, e.g. Bamadaala abamacembele bakaindi bakali kuvwula kufwebela mumfwuko. = The old men and women of long ago frequently used clay pipes for smoking. Also incelwa, indombondo.
a type of insect, an ant-lion, when in larval stage digs holes in sand to trap ants, e.g. *Imfwuko-mfwuko* tailumi bantu. = The ant-lion does not attack people. Also imvwuku-vwuku

a flat piece of metal for transferring fire to a pipe, thongs, e.g. Nobana kamundiletela *mfwuko-mfwuko* yangu ndibikkile mulilo. Children bring my piece of metal so that I put fire in it. Also lumano.

a hole where the bull-frog stores its water, e.g. Meenda amumfwukula alatontola. = The water of a bull-frog's hole is cold. Mwaka umwi meenda gande ngilyakayobwede akamana, *imfwukula* yalyo yakayuma. = One year the water kept by a bull-frog finished, his pond dried up. Caande wakafwuka *mfwukula itontola yakulyookezezya. = The frog dug a hole for resting in.
temporary pimple, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ulaa mfwula kubusyu. = This boy has pimples on the face.
the gizzard, e.g. *Imfwuli* yankuku yaligwa mubwa. = The gizzard of the chicken has been eaten by a dog.
the rainbow, e.g. *Imvwula* niyali kuyanda kuwa twabona *mfwulicoongo* kujwe. = When it was about to rain we saw a rainbow in the east.
type of wild fruit, e.g. Bana baya kukucela *mfwulimuninga* kumyuunda. = The children have gone to collect *mfwulimuninga* fruit in the fields. Also inkoomwa, insipi.
the early rains, e.g. *Imfwumpaluya* yakawa mwakali yakali mpati kapati. = The early rains which fell last year were very heavy. Also *impumpaluya*.

a mouthful, e.g. Mucembele umwi wakabweza lufwulu akuteka meenda munongo. Wakavwubata *mfwundo* yomwe nkabela wakapaila mubusyu bwamulwazi. = One old woman took a long-stemmed calabash and drew water from the water-pot. She took a mouthful and thereupon sprayed it on the face of the patient.
the hard centre of a tree, e.g. *Imfwuno* yacisamu eci taipyi akaambo kakuyuma. = The hard part of this tree does not burn because it is very hard.
yam* zyamwaani. = He carved vernadah poles from the cores of mwaani trees. Also moyo wamusamu.
what is hidden from view, e.g. Nkuku yoonse njomwajika taata uliimana alikke. Kamundisisila *mfwunyungu*. = Father will finish off all the chicken you have cooked. Hide away a secret piece for me.

porridge left from the day before, food prepared the night before, e.g. Basicikolo nobafwumina kucikolo balya *mfwuta* nkaambo kakutayanda kujika. = School-children when they set out early in the morning eat food prepared the previous night because they do not want to cook. Also *ndala*.
a gun, e.g. Musooja bakamuyasa *mfwuti* akuulu. = They shot the soldier in the leg. Also *ntobolo*.
a type of shell, e.g. Tukalete *mfwuuma* kumulonga. = Let us go and bring shells from the river.
flying shreds of burnt grass, e.g. *Imimbi* ezi zyazyila kwali kupya syokwe. = These flying ashes of grass have come from where the bush was burning. Also *mbimbi*.
a bird, the large dove, e.g. Mwiinga wajaya *mombo* mumuunda. = Mwiinga killed a large dove in the field.
a clot of dried blood, e.g. Mulwazi naayanda kufwa walikuzwa *mondo* kumulomo. = When the patient was about to die a clot of blood came out of his mouth.
the barbel fish, e.g. Bamwi bantu tabalyi nswi *mondo*. = Some people do not eat barbel fish.
a striped tick, e.g. Aakandilumide *moola* mumutwe, masusu akamana. = My hair is gone where the striped tick bit me on the head. Also *inzengene*

a place of plenty of foods and entertainment like Lusaka or Livingstone. e.g. *Imoondyekaaka*, bumbuulu-mbuulu bulangwa buyo ameso. = A place of entertainment and variety of foods where you cannot even manage to finish them.
a notch, a mark, e.g. Bataata bakabikka *impa* mpobakali kuyanda kukkala. = My father put a mark where he wanted to live. *Koanga mpa zyobilo alooye olo.* = Tie two notches on that rope.
a target, indicator, e.g. Tuyanda kubikka *mpaakani* mpotwa-abanina myuunda. = We want to put a sign where we divide up the fields. Also *imbaakani
a bird's breast, e.g. *Inziba ndakayuuma ampaandwa.* = I struck the dove on the breast. Also impandwa, insando.
the mahogany bean, e.g. *Impaapa zilanona kuyoka.* = Mahogany beans are tasty to roast.

various gifts given by the boy's family to the girl's; e.g. *Ciindi musimbi nazumizigwa kuti atwalwe, bausyi baita zintu zimwi kutegwa mwana apailwe kabotu. Eezi zitegwa impaizyo. Kumpaizyo kulacitwa isumo lijisi bana banji, aabo mbobati bamwi 'mala'. Eeli sumo lyeelede kuti kalijisi bana baimpene, bamwi kabalanzya ansi, bamwi mujulu. Eeli sumo ndilyona kumwi litegwa 'isumo lya-mufwunko'. Lyajanika sumo eli, nkokuti aka wakamana, wasyaazya zimwi. Sikusindikila nguuya kuleta zintu ezyo zyampaizyo, zili mbuli 'jamba lyabulundwe', 'isumo Iwamufwunko' azimwi.* = At the time when it is agreed that the girl should be married, her father calls for certain gifts so that the marriage of his daughter should be carried out properly. These gifts are called '*impaizyo*'. The presentation of gifts should include a spear which has several barbs, what some call 'mala'. This spear ought to have different barbs, some looking downwards, some looking upwards. This same spear is sometimes called the mufwunko spear. When this spear is found, this part of the ritual is finished, there remains other gifts. The one who accompanies the gifts is the one who brings these other gifts, they may be hoes or spears or other things. *Bamukwasyi wamusankwa nibakazulizya mpaizyo, bakatuma bakwela musimbi.* = When the family of the boy had gathered together all the marriage gifts, they sent people to bring the girl. (*Impaizyo* refers to the taking of a spear and hoes to the father of the bride before he gives the traditional blessing. e.g. *Mpaizyo inga nkutola sumo lilaa mala, amaamba abulumbu. Eezi zinakuunka asikusindikila nabwiinga, aakujokela nkobazwa. Nzyakuti usyi amupiilile kabotu mwanaakwe.* = *Impaizyo* are the goods that allow the father of the bride to give his traditional blessing, these are a spear and hoes from the west which are taken by the companion of the groom on the day when the bride is brought.)
shoots from the stem, e.g. *Nomulimina kamulangisya mapopwe aakapanda mpakatwa kamuzizwisya.* = You who weed look carefully at the maize-stalks that have produced shoots and remove them.
a cave/hole/hollow in a tree a bee's hive, e.g. *Inzuki zyakanjila mumpako yacisamu.* = The bees entered a hole in the tree.

a dish for washing in, basin, e.g. *Mitiba koinyika mumpali.* = Soak the plates in a basin. *Mucuumbwe bakabikka mpali yakwe njaakali kubelesya kacipona.* = In the grave they placed his dish which he was using when still alive.

a water lily, pl. *mpana* = water-lily tubers, e.g. *Ndiyanda kujika mpana.* = I want to cook the water lily tuber. *Basimbi baunka kukusya mpana.* = Girls have gone to dig water lily tubers. Also inkubu; (it's stem = mulilima)
a wise person, e.g. *Impana yakati 'muzoka ulya kweendeenda'.* = The wise person said, "The big snake eats as it moves about."
big flying termites, e.g. Impanamana zilauluka mangolezya. = The big flying termites fly at evening time. Also inswa.
the fork of a tree, Konditemena mpanda yakubambya malekani. = Cut me a fork for making a catapult.
a parrot, e.g. Mpanda wakolwa naamana kulya nseke zyalubanje. = The parrot got drunk after eating dagga seeds.
the Christian cross, e.g. Munanda yangu ndijisi mpanda imweka. = I have a luminous cross in my house. Also ciingano.
a large white shell, e.g. Mpande zyakali kusamwa abantu balemenede. = Mpande shells were worn by important people. (The impande shell was once used as currency among the Batonga.)
a type of disease, e.g. Mukaintu wako taciswi mpande. = Your wife is not suffering from the mpande disease.
a bird's breast, e.g. Impandwa yakancele taili mpati. = The breast of the small partridge is not big. Also insando, impaandwa
crevice, cave, impangala yabbwe = a cave in the rocks, e.g. Inzoka yanjila mumpangala yabbwe. = A snake has entered the crevice.
a type of Ila song, e.g. Baila baimba ciimbo campango. = The Ila people sing a type of song called mpango.
a rib, e.g. Muntu watyoka mpango nibamuuma musako. = The man broke a rib when they beat him with a stick.
a verse of a hymn, e.g. Kondiimbila buyo mpango yomwe yaciimbo. = Sing me just one verse of the hymn.

a valley or low lying area between hills or mountains, e.g. Munene Mugolo amwanaangu Gulaya bakatozya yakumpango yamulundu. = The old man Mugolo and my son Gulaya went towards the vlei between the hills.

a precocious child, e.g. Ooyu mwana nimpanu-mpanu. = This child is very lively impanza high forehead, baldness, e.g. Mudaala wainda waawa ulaa mpanza. = The old man who just passsed by here is bald. Also lubuwa
something flat, as a steak of meat, e.g. Eeli bbwe ndipapali. = This stone is flat.
an extra little quantity given freely, e.g. Kuti waula cisyu cinji balapa ampasela. = If you buy a lot of vegetables they will give you extra free. Also imbasela, ibbasela.
a cow which refuses to give milk, e.g. Eeyi nombe nimpasi. = This cow refuses to yield milk. Also insasi.
a small bee which makes honey in trees, e.g. Tulida buci bwampasi. = We are foraging for the honey of small bees.
sparks, e.g. Musamu wamwaani ulijisi mpasi. = Wood from the mwaani tree produces sparks. Also nsasi.
the hip, e.g. Mulwazi ulaa zicisa ampaso. = The patient has sores on the hip. Kasolo = hip bone; ipaso = socket of hip joint

locust, e.g. Kuti Chitebenta azumanane kundikatazya uno mwaka takalimi, balamwiita balya mpaso. = If Chitebenta continues to trouble me this year he will not be able to plough, he will be called by those who eat locusts (i.e. the dead)
a problem difficult to solve, e.g. Aaka kaambo nkayumu kapati, nimpasulula-balozi. = This affair is very difficult, it is for the wise ones to solves.
a difficult problem or task, e.g. Aaka kaambo nimpasununabalozi. = This problem is a difficult one.

goods, riches, property, e.g. Babbi bandibbida mpasya yamurjanda. = The thieves stole the wealth of my house. ---|--impata a large flat fish, e.g. Nitwali kuzela ndajaya mpata mpati. = When we were fishing I killed a big flat fish.
a cartridge belt, e.g. Bama- silikani bakasamide mpatani muzibuno zyabo. = The policemen were wearing cartridge belts around their waists.
sandals, e.g. Basankwa ba- kali kubamba mpato zyakusambala. = The boys were making sandals to sell. Also indyasyo, inkwakwayile, insangu.
soles of feet, e.g. Mpato zyangu nzipati. = The soles of my feet are big.

receptacle for fat or oil, e.g. Impao yamafwuta yavwula. = The container of fat is full. Bagusya mafwuta aamunsuwa akwaabikka mucibiya kuti asi- bikwe amulilo. Amana kucocoma atililwa mucinkuli ciitwa kuti impao antela nzazi. = They take the fat from the gourd and put it in a pot so that it is put on the fire. When it has boiled it is poured into a gourd called impao or insazi. Also impau impawo receptacle for oil, e.g. Impawo zyakajisi mafwuta akunana. = The oil containers had oil for anointing the body. Also impau
a bee-comb, pl. mampeebu, e.g. Ulagwisya buci, ulagwisya mampeebu amulolo amampeebu amana. = She re- moves the honey, she removes the combs with nectar and the combs with larvae.
white paint, e.g. Inanda yangu yakasingululwa ampemba. = My house is painted with white paint.

the nose, a nostril, e.g. Impemo yoonse yamwana ilaa zicisa. = The whole nose of the child is full of sores. (The nose-plug (cisita) was used as an ornament in the past, The cisita was inserted in a hole in the septrum. It could be a piece of reed or sorgum or a short length of porcupine quill or ivory. The cisita could be bead-covered, this was a plug with a sleeve of beads. Occasionally small loops or strings of beads were added to the ends of sleeved nose plugs. The ivory nose-plug was called munko- nde.) Also cisita, Iwingwa, balumba-lumba
the prow of a canoe, e.g. Kamwaanga looye kumpemo yabwato. = Tie a rope to the prow of the canoe.

intransigence, e.g. Bapati bakacenjezya bana babo kuti mpempela antela nkazi nzibi ziletela mapenzi. = The elders warned their children saying that intransigence or stubbourness is bad and brings problems.
a type of fish (bream), e.g. Kumusyika baulisya mpende zitete. = They are selling fresh bream at the mar- ket.
a tale-bearer, e.g. Impe- pabami uleta kutamvwana muminzi. = A tale-bearer brings misunderstanding to the villages.
a moth, a butterfly, e.g. Mababa ampepelukwa mmabotu, ala- mweka-mweka. = The wings of a butterfly are beautiful, they shine. Also impepeligo, inkonkolekwa.

a velvet-bean whose pods cause intense itch, e.g. Ndababwa mpese mubili onse. I am itching from the velvet bean all over. Nyika yandibaba ilaa mpese. The world irritates me, it is as prickly as the velvet-bean.
prickly caterpillars which live on the castor-oil plant, e.g. Impese zilalya matu amabbona. = Prickly caterpillars eat lea- ves of the castor-oil plant.
a pencil, (ety. English) e.g. Mwana naatalika kwiiya mubbuku taanzi ubelesya mpesele. = When a child starts Grade 1, she uses a pencil.
a trumpet, e.g. Bamasooja nobafwoolwa balalizya ampeta. = When the soldiers are marching they sound the trumpet. Also kasibyo, kasibo, nyeele
a pea-beetle, e.g. Basimpongo balabotelwa kusiba impetamuuka. = The herders enjoy blowing the pea-beetle. Also mpiililyo.
a length of cloth (4 yards), e.g. Amunduulile mpeto yamulembo. = Buy me a length of cloth.
rolled up edge of cloth around the waist, e.g. *Impetu yamusinsi yakomenesya.* = The hem of the skirt is very big.
cold weather, cold season, e.g. Mazuba obile ayinda kwali *mpeyo kapati.* = For the last two days the cold has been intensive.
a band of warriors, an army, e.g. *Impi yamasooja iyakukulwana kumusanza acisi coonse.* = A battalion of soldiers is going to fight in the southern part of the country.
various items for making a dancing belt, e.g. Kamubungika *mpiililyo tubambe mayaamba.* = Gather together the different items so that we make a dancing-belt.
a beetle found in the vlei during the rainy season, e.g. Beembela balayanda kusobanya *mpiililyo.* = Herd boys like playing with the beetle which is found in vleis in the rainy season.
a short piece of wood, e.g. *Ooyu kwale ndamujaya ampika.* = I killed this partridge with a short piece of wood.
a hot condiment, pepper, chilli, e.g. *Impilibbili yavwulisya mucisyu aboobo calula.* = There is too much pepper in the relish and so it is bitter.
See impilibbili
a rite/ceremony, e.g. Kuli *mpimbiziko mumunzi mwa Cheelo.* = There is a ceremony at Cheelo's village.

an amulet, a small piece of stick worn on a necklace or around the waist. e.g. Basimasabe basama *mpimpi abulungu kumaanza amunsingo.* = Those who suffer from masabe possession put on bead amulets on their hands and neck.
a short piece of wood, e.g. Wakajaya nkanga zyobilo kumbali adambwa *ampinda.* = He killed two guineafowl with a short piece of wood near the dambo. Also *impika.*
difficulties, e.g. Nindakali kweenda masiku ndakajana *mpindaukwa mulweendo Iwangu.* = When I was travelling at night-time I found problems on the journey. Also impinduukwa.
profit, e.g. Mumakwebo angu kunyina *mpindu mpati njejana.* = I have found no great profit in my business.
Also impindaukwa.
traditional stool, e.g. Ooyu munene ulicizyi kufwala cuuno *campingili.* (musikili) = This old man knows how to make a traditional stool from the musikili tree.
a musikili tree, e.g. Wakasyobola nyeele zyakwe amafwuta *ampingili.* = He smeared his flutes with oil of the musikili tree. Also nsikili
the length between two joints, as in a reed, e.g. Kondityolela *mpingu yamunsale yomwe.* = Cut off one section of sugar-cane for me. Also impyungu, impingwa.

the length between two joints, a notch, e.g. Sicibende wakali kubazumizya kuti ibbwatu mucisasikilo kaliselela *mpingwa yomwe buyo yakabu.* = Sicibende permitted them that the sweetbeer in the container should go down only one notch of the reed.

a twirler, a thin stick with branchlets jutting out at end and rubbed between hands for stirring porridge or beer, e.g. Kobelesya *mpisio kujaya makoto munsima.* = Use the twirler-stick to break up the lumps of mealie-meal in the nsima. Also impusyo.
pl. of lupisyo, Also impisio, impusyo.
fibre skirt, e.g. Basimbi bakali kubamba *mpiye* zyaloozi Iwamiyanda yamubombo. = The girls used to make fibre skirts from the roots of the mubombo tree. Also *maaya*
type of bird which produces the sound 'mpwii', found in vleis, e.g. Kumazuba basimpongo balaya kukuteya *mpiye*. = In the afternoon the herders are going to trap birds.
a woman's apron, e.g. Mukaintu najika usama *mpizya*. = When a woman cooks she wears an apron.
an ostrich, e.g. Mayi ampo mmapati kapati. = The eggs of an ostrich are very big. cf. impowani, impye, impwii.
entrance to an animal's burrow, e.g. Impuukwe zilaa *mpo* zyabwina zyobile. = Rodents have two outlets in their burrows. Also *mpwido*
facial bone structure, a cheek bone, the temples, e.g. Wakanduuma mbayi *ampobe*. = She gave me a smack on the cheek-bone.
a plant used for making salt, e.g. Bacembele bakabamba munyo wa*mpoko*. = The old woman made salt from the *impoko* plant.
a plant which appears at the first rains and is eaten as relish, e.g. *Impoko* ilanona kusanganizya akalubabwaanga. = *Impoko* is tasty when it is mixed with kalubabwaanga.

bracelet of beads used in naming a child, e.g. Mwana naakaulikwa zina lyanguli, bakamusamika *mpola* ituba kukwaanza. = When the child was given a traditional name, they put a bracelet of white beads on its wrist. Baciswa masabe balasamikwa *mpola* zituba. = Those who are suffering from masabe wear white bracelets.

beads put around waist for certain traditional dances = *impola* zyabulungu impolwe hollow grass used for weaving and also for sucking liquids, e.g. Ndakabamba cuuno *campolwe*. = I made a bush-stool of grass. Also insambo.
desire to eat alone because of greed, e.g. Lyoonse uyanda kulya olikke. Ino iya kumana lili *mpomba* webo, Mooya? = You always want to eat alone. Now when will this greed end, Mooya? Also *impompa*.
fear of having to share food when hungry, e.g. Ndakabaa *impompa*. = I was full of fear in having to share the food.
the first rain, e.g. Uuno mwaka kwakawa *mpompaluya* mpati kapati. = This year the first rain was very heavy.
waterfall, e.g. *Impompo* yamulonga ili kumulundu. = The waterfall of the river is in the hill. Also impwampwa.
leaves of cow-beans, e.g. Atweende tukacele *mponde* mulunyabo. = Let us go and pick the leaves of the cow-bean plant.
dried leaves from beans, e.g. Matu *amponde* mmabotu kubamba *cisyu*. = The leaves of the the bean-plant are good for making relish.
a grey fruit, e.g. Ciindi canzala bantu balalila *mpondo*. = During the famine the people eat a grey fruit as supper.
a pound in British currency, (ety.Eng.) e.g. Bakaindi bakali kubelesya *mpondo* isalala. = People of long ago used to use gold coins.
an animal hoof, e.g. *Impondo* zyamusune oyu nzipati. = The hooves of this ox are big. Also insumba.
a goat, e.g. *Impongo* zyamana mapopwe mumbewu. = The goats have finished the maize in the garden.
hollow grass used for sucking liquids, e.g. Ingulube zilalya nkolokoti zyampoolwe mumusena. = The pigs are eating the tubers of hollowed grass in the vlei.

obstruction in a stream, a weir, or small waterfall, e.g. Bamakaintu nibakali kuyanda kujata nswi, bakapanga *mpoompo* kumulundu wamulonga. = When the women were fishing, they constructed a weir upstream. Also *impoopo*
a small waterfall, e.g. Basimbi nibakazwa kucikolo bakali kusobana *ampoopo*. = When the girls came out of school they were playing at the falls. Also impoompo.
first rains Also impumpa-luya
butterflies, e.g. Mwakali kwakali *mpopolofwa* zinji. = Last year there were plenty of butteflies. Also impopolokwa, inkonkolekwa.
hand-bag, purse, e.g. Wakajala *mpotomona* yakwe. = She closed her bag.
a crested crane an ostrich, e.g. Bamwi bantu balavwuba *mpowani*. = Some people keep ostriches.
a wart, mole, pimple, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa *mpu* mumaulu. = This child has pimples on the legs.
a cattle disease, e.g. *nombe zyamu-daala zyoonse ziciswa impu*. = The cattle of the old man are all suffering from a cattle-disease.
hair-oil, e.g. Chitebenta wakali kulizila masusu *ampuki*. = Chitebenta was smearing his hair with oil.
short-bladed spear, e.g. Wakafwusa sumo *lyaimpula* naakabona kanyama. = When he saw the small animal he threw a short-bladed spear.
a farm, e.g. *Impulasi* yabatata ili kumbo aa Monze. = My father's farm is west of Monze.

possessions, e.g. Wakafwumina kwaanga twakwe toonse akulonga *ampuli* yakwe. = Early in the morning she gathered all her things and moved away with her possessions. Suntwe wakatija akuyoonjila akulijalila munanda *ampuli* yakwe. = The hyena ran off and entered the house and shut himself in with his possessions.
a plate, e.g. Koleta *mpulilo* twaapwide nsima. = Bring the plate so that we put in the nsima. Also mutiba, nsangwa.
an ear ache, e.g. Akaambo kakuciswa *mpulukutwi*, matwi angu taamvwi kabotu. = I don't hear well because of suffering from an ear-ache.
a plant with edible leaves, e.g. *Impupulwa* ncisyu cibotu. = The *impupulwa* plant provides good relish.
a window, a loop hole, e.g. Sicikolo wajaya *mpulungwido* kucikolo. = A pupil has broken a window at the school.

a honey-comb with honey, e.g. Nobakali kulida nzuki basankwa bakajana *impuma* zyabuci. = When the boys were collecting honey, they found honey-combs filled with honey. Kwakaleleenga *mpuma* zyabuci kumutabi wacisamu. = A comb of honey hung from the branch of a tree.
a crowd of people, e.g. Ndajana *mpumba* yabantu mumugwagwa. = I found a crowd of people on the road. Lipakweenda wakagama *mpumba* yabasimukowa. = Lipakweende went over to the crowd of clan members.

a coil or mass of hair on top of, or at the back of, the head, e.g. Ooyu musimbi ulaa *mpumbe* yamasusu. = This girl has a cone of hair at the back of her head. Kaindi musankwa naakakubuka, wakeelede kusungwa *mpumbe*. = In the past when a boy matured, he had to wear the impumbe. Also insuku
an extended stomach, ---|--e.g. Muntu uneneede ulaa *mpumbwe* yada. = A fat person has a layer of flesh hanging below the normal stomach. Also imbwebwe, cibwembwe.
a small ball of feathers set in front of the hair, e.g. Mukombwe ulaa *mpumbwe* kumbele amalembwe-lembwe. = A cock has a small ball of feathers in front of its neck pouch.
the first rains, e.g. Kono *impumpaluya* tainingawa. = This year the first rains have not yet fallen. Also impampaluya, civwunanombe.
an armlet of grass, e.g. Musimbi wakalisamide *impumpu*. = The girl was wearing an armlet of grass. Also caaso, pl. zyaaso.

the thick end of a pestle, e.g. Kotwisya *mpumpu* yamunsi buntele. = Pound the groundnuts using the end of the pestle. *Impumpu* nimbotu kusyubuzya musozya. = The thick end of the pestle is good for pounding musozya. Also ibbumpu.
rice, e.g. Kamujika *mpu-nga* balye beenzu. = Cook the rice so that the visitors can eat. Also mupunga; laisi (ety. English)

an edible grass similar to finger-millet (*Urochloa mosambicensis*) whose seeds are boiled as a cereal in Feb. e.g. Masiku bakalalila nsima *yampunga* mubwaawo bwacisyuungwa. = At night they were making nsima from the seeds of *mpunga* grass with cisyuungwa relish.

a type of grass used by herd-boys in a game, e.g. Kaindi basankwa beembela bakali kusobanya *impunga*. = Long ago herd-boys used to play a game of whipp-ing one another with *impunga* grass. Also ncaaca
a rodent, e.g. Twajaya *mpungwe* zyosanwe. = We killed five rodents. Also impuukwe
a tuft of hair at the end of a cow's tail, e.g. Kotenda *mpusa* yamucila wagombe kutegwa ufwiimpe-fwiimpe. = Cut the tuft of hair from the cow's tail to shorten it.
a grey snake, e.g. *Impusi* yakali-sisa munkuni. = A grey snake was hiding itself in the firewood. (belts can be made from the skin of the grey snake) *impusyi*. Also *impusi*
a stick for stirring sour milk, e.g. Usaangune kwaapuka ampusyo ma-bisi kotaningateka. = Stir the sour milk with the stirring stick before you get some of it. Also impisyo

the ox-tail binding around a spear shaft, e.g. Amundibikkile *mputi* ku-sumo lyangu. = Put the ox-tail binding around my spear shaft. Luti Iwasumo Iwatyokela *mumputi*. = The ox-tail bind-ing of my spear got broken.
a rodent living in large communities, e.g. Nitwali kusya, twajana *mpuukwe* kkumi mubwina bomwe. = When we were digging, we found ten rodents in one hole. Also impugwe. *impuugwa* • See impuukwe.
breath, e.g. Taakaninga aku-yoya *mpuuma* zyamuya noziba zyotatwe wakafwa. = Before he took in a breath of air or maybe three, he died.
fame, glory, e.g. Munzi okwa sibbuku Mweemba ulaa *mpuwo* mpati. = The village of headman Mweemba has a great reputation.
waterfall, e.g. *Impwa-ampwa* yamulonga Lufwuwa ili ku Chi-yobola. = The waterfall of the river Lufwuwa is at Chiyobola. Also impompo.

exit from burrow. e.g. Syaa-nasulwe wakazwa *ampwaido*, mulavwu wakaata kuzwa *ampwaido*, wakapatila. = The hare came out of the exit hole of the burrow, but the lion was unable to, but got stuck coming out of the hole.

wrestling contests, e.g. Wakajana acisyanyina ulaangilwe akaambo kamilandu yampwazinga imwi njobayandisisya kucita bamwi bantu muminzi mobakkala. = He found his uncle arrested for offences of fighting which in some villages where people live they love to practice.
a borer beetle, e.g. Uuno mwaka *impwe* taziboneki pe nkaambo bantu tabalimide. = This year the borer beetles are not to be seen because the people did not plant.
the entrance to an animal's burrow, e.g. Galaba wazwida kumpwedo yabwina. = The ant-bear came out of the entrance of a burrow. Also impo, impwido.
a curse impending, for example due to homicide
abusive language, e.g. Kasimbi aka takakalomi, kalaa *mpwelempwele*. = This little girl will not grow to become good, she uses abusive language.

a hole going right through, an escape hole in a burrow, e.g. Tiitwabwene kuti bwina bujisi *mpwido* aboobo mbeba zyoonse zyazwida nkuko. = We did not see that the hole had an outlet and so all the rats escaped through it.
a bird, the large quail, pl. bampwii, e.g. Basankwa bavwima *bampwii*. = The boys are hunting large quails. Also mintwilili
a hole, e.g. Mwayaka caanda campongo, musiye *mpwiningido* zinji kutegwa muwo kawiinda. = When you build a house for goats, leave many holes so that the air can pass through. Also impulungwido.
a hole in cloth, wall or fence, e.g. Bwaanda bujikila bulaa *mpwiningizyo*. = The wall of the kitchen has an opening (for ventilation).
a weaned child, e.g. Ooyu mwana ucili *mpwitamamina*. = This child is still very young. (-pwita = sip, mamina = mucous from nose)
a heifer, e.g. Mazubaano bantu banji balimya *mpwizi*. = These days most people use heifers for ploughing.

deceit, e.g. Mebo ndabelesya *mpyata* kutegwa azwe murjanda mwasambalila bukoko. = I used trickery so that she would come out of the house where she was selling beer. Basankwa balaa *mpyata*, mbuli syaanamabumba. = Men are full of deceit like the hare. Also bumpelenge.
ostrich, e.g. *Impye* mmuyuni ujanwa kucimpayuma. = The ostrich is a bird which is found in the desert. Also impo, impowani.
the length between two joints, as in a reed, e.g. Munsale oyu ulaa *mpyungu* zyosanwe. = This sugar cane has five sections between joints. Also impingu.
a joint or articulation as in a finger, also a node or nodule as in a reed, e.g. Minwe yangu ilatonga *mumpyungu*. = My fingers are cracking at the nuckles.
blackberries, a kind of cherry, e.g. Bana bayakukucela *mumbu* mu syokwe. = The children have gone to collect blackberries in the bush. Also imbumbu, mubumbu
a glow-worm, fire-flies, e.g. Masiku ajilo *muni-muni* zyakali zinji kapati. = Last night there were many glowworms. Also mwini-mwini, inguunguni, mwini mwenge.
a sorgum plant disease, the plant becomes black, e.g. Maila angu taajisi *munje* pe. = My millet is free of disease. Also dyumba.
a sugary plant, e.g. Mumuunda ulya *munje* wakakomena kabotu. = In that field the sugary plant has grown well. Also imbunje.

grey hair, e.g. Eezi *mvwi* zyabanene zyaamba cintu cipati. Swebo tulakonzya kubainda kuluno, pele tatukonzyi kubainda maanu. = The grey hair of the elderly has deep meaning. We can surpass them in running, but we cannot better them in wisdom. *Waba amvwi* = He is grey-haired. *Wamena mvwi.* = She is going grey.
a blind fly, e.g. *Kolijaya mvwo elyo.* = Kill that blind fly.
an envelope, e.g. Lugwalo ndweetambula luli *mumvwolopo.* = The letter which I received is in an envelope.
a hat, e.g. Eeyi *imvwosi* yabaneene aba nimbotu kapati. = This hat belonging to my grandfather is very beautiful. Also *imvwuse.*
a black fish, pl. *bamvwube,* e.g. Wakamutondezya nzila naakamana kumukangila *bamvwube.* = She showed him the path having fried black fish for him. Also *mubondo.*
an antlion, e.g. *Imvwuku-mvwuku* zifwumba tulindi twakujatila tuuka mumusenga. = The ant-lion makes little holes for catching insects in the sand. Also *imfwuko-mfwuko.*

rain, e.g. Ijilo kwakawa *mvwula mpati.* = Yesterday there was a great fall of rain. (musingu, cipumpwe = dark and heavy; kalyobolyobo / kacabwacabwa cameenda = heavy but short; muyoba = lasting all day and night, tunyunyu-nyunyu = drizzle; imfwumpaluya, impumbaluya = early rains.)
a type of fruit, which grows on the banks of rivers, e.g. *Imvwuli* zili mumbali amulonga zyakabizwa. = The *imvwuli* fruits which are on the bank of the river have ripened.
hornless head of cattle, e.g. *nombe mvwuma* yapuna mulubaya Iwaciba. = The hornless cow passed under the fence of the krall.

the big coconut of the borassus palm, pl. mavwuma/mamvwuma, e.g. *Imvwuma* nseningalilide nkaambo nkotukkala kunyina masamu *amamvwuma.* = I have not yet eaten a big coconut because there are no trees of coconuts where we live.
mildew, scum on surface of water, e.g. Meenda ali mumpoto abaa *mvwundi.* = The water in the pot has become scum. Also inkubi
a maggot, grub, larvae, e.g. Koisowa nyama eyo nkaambo yaba *amvwunyu.* = Throw away that meat because it has maggots.
a hat, e.g. *Imvwuse* yamudaala nimbotu. = The hat of the old man is nice. Also *imvwosi.*
an animal's den, e.g. Nitwali kuvwima twajana *mvwuta* yasulwe. = When we were hunting we found the burrow of a hare.
a bellows, e.g. Mufwuzi nafwula tweembe amaamba ubelesya ma*vwuto.* = When the blacksmith is forging hoes he uses bellows. Also hwutio, mavwuba.

a hippopotamus, e.g. *Imvwuvwu* mmunyama mupati alimwi utajisi boya amubili. = The hippopotamus is a huge animal without hair on its body. Wakeenda wakasika kukasuwa, wakajana *imvwuvwu* yakajisi mwana mutete. = When he went and arrived at an island, he found a hippopotamus which had a young one. *Imvwuvwu* zyakamana mapopwe abantu munsi alwizi. = The hippos have finished off the maize of the people beside the lake. Also civwubwe.
a mosquito, e.g. *Imwe* likaintu ndelileta bulwazi bwantuntumaanzi kubantu. = The female mosquito is the one which brings the disease of malaria to people. Also insenya.
a glow worm/firefly, e.g. *Imwini-mwini* zilamweka masiku ciindi camainza. = The fireflies light up at night during the rainy season.
a needle, e.g. Ndali kukulomba naliti kuli bina Cheelo. = I went to ask for a needle from the mother of Cheelo. Also inyeleti.
prickly grass, e.g. Inama lilayasa bantu batasami mpato. = Prickly grass pierces people who do not wear shoes.
a graveyard, e.g. Mwana wabaacisya wakafwa wakazikkilwa ku namaumbwe yaku Monze. = The uncle's child who died was buried at the graveyard at Monze.
heavy clay, e.g. Kuti kwawa mvwula nciyumu kuccovwa ncinga mu inandobe. = If the rain falls it is difficult to pedal a bicycle in the heavy clay.
the evening star, the planet Venus, e.g. *Inangabalya* ilafwambaana kuzwa kujwe ciindi cacilimo. = The evening star rises early during the dry season. Also intanda
a nostril, e.g. Ndabaa zicisa munago. = I have sores in my nostril. Also inango.
an eland, e.g. Twajaya inansefwu nitwali kuvwima. = We killed an eland when we were hunting.
pl. of *Iwaanzi* (a crack), e.g. nanda eyi ilaa *inanzi* zipati. = This house has big cracks.
a shower of rain, e.g. Sunu kwawa *ncabwacabwa* lyamvwula. = Today a shower of rain fell.
noisy chewing, e.g. Mutinta utani kulizyi *ncanku* pe. = Mutinta do not be chewing noisely when you are eating.
food for journey e.g. Bavwimi bakabweza *nce* yakujika. = The hunters take food to cook on the expedition.
mental disorder, hysteria, e.g. Ooyu mubwa bukali bwakwe mbwa*nceetela*. = The agressiveness of this dog is a kind of mental disorder.
poison, particularly arsenic, e.g. Muneene bakamubikkila *ncefwu* mubukoko, ncaakafwa. = The put poison in Muneene's beer, that is why he died.
a wart, e.g. Nyama yamusefwu tiitengwi inga waciswa *ncefwu*. = One does not complain about the meat of an eland as one may become develop a wart. Also impu.
a boa, python, e.g. Bavwimi bajaya *nceka* musyokwe. = The hunters killed a python in the bush. Also *muceka*.
one who always stays at home, e.g. Ooyu mwana *nincelamunzi*. = This child always stays at home.
an alluvial garden beside the Zambezi.
a type of bird, the wattled starling, e.g. Kwali kulila *ncelelebula* kujwe oku. = A starling was chirping over to the east.
a selfish person, e.g. Ooyu mudaala *nguncelelebula*, tayeeyi bana kumunzi pe. = This old man is selfish, he does not think of the children in the village.
the spout or nozzle of a blacksmith's bellows Also *cihuba*

a calabash pipe for smoking hemp, an unbaked clay pipe, a bubble pipe, e.g. Ba Cheele bafwebya *ncelwa*. = Mr. Cheele is smoking a bubble-pipe. Also *ndobondo* (*mwanancelwa* = The small wooden container which fits into the calabash pipe into which is put tobacco, maize-grains and fire.)

fear of what might happen, e.g. Ndabaa *ncence* nkaambo kuti ndacaamba ncindabona munzila inga cilaleta mapenzi. = I feared what might happen because if I said what I saw on the way it might bring problems.
a small sweet wild fruit with seeds inside, e.g. Amukandicelele *ncenje* muloonde. = Go and collect for me the *incenje* wild fruit in the forest.
a thorny round fruit, e.g. AdiIwe mukamufwu umpilwa zincenya. = At the funeral the widow or widower she/he is fumigated by zincenya fruits. (to drive out the spirit of the spouse)
bad behaviour, e.g. Wakalijisi nceya. = He was a rude fellow.
a hunting area, e.g. Baalumi boonse baunka kuncila. = All the men have gone to the hunting area. Also cila
a mortar, a stamping block, e.g. Incili yakafwala mudaala ilaa Iwaanzi. = The mortar which was carved by the old man has a crack.
name of a place famous for a stone that resembles a mortar used for pounding, e.g. Ndasweene bazilawo bone ku Incilibbwe. = I met four kudus at Incilibbwe.
a filter, e.g. Inciliko yamusika yazimina. = The ash-filter is lost. Also ciceleko.
asbestos, e.g. Inanda yokwesu bakaivwumbya ncinda. = They roofed our house with asbestos. incinga
a bicycle, e.g. Ndiya ku Monze ancinga. = I am going to Monze by bicycle. Also namutendele.
the fruit of the mucinga tree, e.g. Cheelo tweende musyokwe tukacele incinga. = Cheelo, let's go into the bush and gather the fruit of the mucinga tree.
madness, e.g. Kufwepa lubanje cipa kuba ancinko. = Smoking dagga leads to madness. incoko
spiral-copper or brassanklets, also ndalila.
chalk, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Incoko zyabayi zyamana. = The chalk of the teacher is finished.
a type of bird, the shoveller duck, e.g. Twali kuuma ncowe mudamu amalekani. = We were killing a duck at the dam with a catapult.
See incowe.
locust, e.g. Incucula zyakai-
business, affair, matter, e.g. Kunyina *ndaba*. = It does not matter.
kuti bamujaya Mweemba akaambo kakubba nombe kunyina *ndaba* pe. = Even though they killed Mweemba for stealing cattle it does not matter. Also mulandu
big old cow, e.g. Inombe *indabala* yainda awa. = A big old cow just passed here. Also iddabbala.
*nsima* left from the previous day, e.g. Bana bafwuma kulya *ndala* ya*nsima*. = The children rose early eating the *nsima* left from the previous day.
bracelet of brass wire, anklet of metal, e.g. Mucembele bamusamika *ndalila* kukwaanza. = They put a bracelet of wire on the old womans wrist. Also mundalila, ndalila, incoko.
a small drum, e.g. Lyakafwa Mwami Mweemba bakali kulizya *ndandala* nibakali kuzemba. = When Chief Mweemba died they were beating the *indandala* drum when they were running to and fro.
a fishing-net, e.g. Nobana amweete *ndangala* tukazube nswi. = Children bring me the fishing-net so that we fish. Also intangala, lusabwi.
a dining-hall, e.g. Basicikolo balida *mundandula*. = The pupils eat in the dining-hall. Also idandula
aggression, e.g. Taakali kutondezya *ndavwu* kumacembele, wakaba *ndavwu* kubantu boonse. = He did only not show aggression to the older women but became aggressive to all people.
decrees, regulations, e.g. *Indazyo yabataata zyakagwasya mikwasyi minji muminzi.* = The rules of my father have helped many families in the village.
type of edible leaf, flower, e.g. Bantu balya matu *andebele* mulweendo. People eat edible leaves on a journey. Also *indebelebe*.
a member of the Matebele tribe of Zimbabwe, e.g. *Mundebele wakasika jilo.* = An Ndebele person arrived yesterday.
a procession, e.g. Kupobwe lyabwiinga bantu bali kweenda *ndebelwa*. At the marriage-feast the people were walking in a procession. Also *debelwa*
a pack of wild dogs, e.g. Baumpe balayanda kweenda *mundebelwa*. The wild dogs like to move in a pack.
