a bundle of spears, e.g. Kukaswi kacijikila kuyaamikidwe *ndee* yamasumo. = In the corner of the kitchen there is a bundle of spears leaning against the wall. Also *indeye*.

one who lacks money to pay tax, e.g. *Indeenya* bakamutanda munanda yamfwulumende akaambo kakutabbadela. The one who was unable to pay tax was evicted from the house owned by the government for failing to pay.
an aeroplane, e.g. *Indeke ilafwambaana kweenda kwiinda zyeenzya zyoonse.* The areoplane travels faster than any other means of transport.
bucket, e.g. Mufwuzi ulakonzya kufwula *ndelema*. The blacksmith can forge buckets.

a flag, e.g. Cisi acisi cilijisi *ndembela yaco.* Each country has it's own flag. Mubala usubila *andembela* ya Zambia wiiminina bulowa bwakatika lyakali kulwaninwa Iwaanguluko. The colour red of the Zambian flag stands for the blood which was spilt at the time of the fighting for independence.
a bundle of spears, e.g. Bakazyuuma *ndeye* zyamyuumba akubbabbu-ka antobo. They beat the bundles of spears and jumped with the shields.
a coin, e.g. *Indibilisi* lyangu lyazimina musyokwe neeli kuyandaula nkuku. My coin got lost in the bush when I was searching for the hen. Also *idibilisi*.
a wooden dish, plate, or bowl with projecting handle or spout, e.g. Kondisanzyila *ndido* mbikkile cakulya. Wash the wooden dish so that I put in the food.
manner of eating, e.g. *Ndido* yamulombwana oyu nimbi. This boys manner of eating is bad.

a type of traditional dance, e.g. Masiku ayinda, twali kuzyana *ndikiti*. Last night we were dancing the *indikiti* dance. e.g. *Indikiti* njeizyanwa camoombelela nkaambo yalo izyaninwa munanda. The *indikiti* dance is danced more gently as it is danced in the house.
prominent buttocks, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu wakalaa *ndilika* yamatako, ino sunu wakaide kusyelebala. This woman was fat-buttocked, now today she is flat.

one day's task, a hoeing feast at which beer is brewed and food provided by farmer with big fields for people who help him weeding, e.g. Ijilo bamakaintu banji bakaunkide kundima kwasibbuku Malawo. Many women went for one day's work to headman Malawo's village.
one day's task
a plot of land, e.g. *Indimo* yamuunda wangu ilaa mbolezi. My plot of land has plenty of humus. Also *indima*
a stunted and black head of sorgum, boiled and used as relish in Gwembe Valley, e.g. Bamakaintu ba Zambezi balaiyanda *indiololo* kapati. The women of the Zambezi river like *indiololo* very much.
an incurable ulcer on the foot, e.g. *Indola mbulwazi butundulula.* = A foot ulcer is a painful disease. Also indondamwaka.
drowsiness, e.g. *Chimuka ulaa ndolo nkaambo wabucesya kunkolola.* = Chimuka was drowsy because he was at the inititation until dawn.
a waistcoat.
toe, pl. *tulolomi*, e.g. *Indolomi yangu ilacisa mubbusu.* = My toe is paining in the shoe.
incurable ulcer in the foot Also ikuni, indola
type of insect, a lizard, e.g. *Ndabona ndolwa mulutantambeba.* = I saw a lizard on top of the wall under the roof of the house. Also dolwa, haadobeelela, tombela.
a big rock, e.g. *Ndali kubweza ndomba lyabbwe.* = I was moving a big rock.

a bubble-pipe, a calabash pipe for smoking e.g. *Bacembele bafwebya ndombondo.* = The old women smoke a bubble-pipe. *Munene wakapakila tombwe mundombondo yakwe akutalika kufweba.* = The old man packed his pipe with tobacco and began smoking. Also indobondo.
a sharp point, e.g. *Indomo yanyeleti ilabosya.* = The point of the needle is sharp.
a large drop, pl. *mandondo*, e.g. *Niyalikuwa mvwula mandondo ali mapati-pati.* = When the rain was falling the drops were big. (*lindondo* = a pearl) Also mabuula.
an injection, e.g. *Musilisi wakamuyasa mwana ndonga yomwe.* = The doctor gave the child one injection.
groundnut, e.g. *Ndakatebula ndongo zinji uno mwaka.* = I have harvested many groundnuts this year. Also indongwe
groundnut, e.g. *Indongwe zyabacembele zyakamana ngulube mumuunda.* = The pigs have finished off the groundnuts of the old woman in the field.
a creeper with big beans, pl. *mandowa*, e.g. *Mandowa akazyala kabotu nkaambo mvwula yakawa kabotu.* = The bean-creepers produced well because the rain fell in abundance.

a type of bird, the scarlet touraco or Livingstone's lourie, also used as pl. of *luluba*, the touraco or lourie, e.g. *Bana baniini baya kukulanga nduba.* = The little children went to see the lourie bird. Also inkulyu-nkulyu
a giraffe, e.g. *Kanji-kanji ndudwa ilya matuvwu azisamu akaambo kakulampa kapati.* = A giraffe mostly eats the leaves of trees because of it's great height. Also indyabuluba.
a bitter pumpkin, e.g. *Bakaintu bakasyanga nyungu zyandulu mukutazyiba.* = The women planted seeds of bitter pumpkins unknowingly.
a heap of earth coming from a hole, e.g. *Imbeba zyakalundika indululu nizyakafwumba.* = The rats heaped up a pile of earth when they were digging. Also ibbuzye
a plant, with green bitter leaves (used as relish) with small black fruits when ripe, e.g. *Indulwe kumbewu yakayuma.* = The plant with bitter green leaves got dried up in the garden.

a rug, a wollen blanket, pl. *mandumba*, e.g. *Bana basuba abulo mubayalile ndumba.* = Spread out a rug for the children who unrinate in the bed. *Bana tabayandi kulivwumba mandumba.* = The children do not want to cover themselves with blankets. *Basimbi bakaliputilila andumba.* = The girls covered themselves with a woolen blanket.
a heap of earth coming from a hole in the ground Also ibbuzye, indululu.
smartness, e.g. Basimbi bayanda basankwa bandungudungu. = Ladies like smart men. Also indwaandwa.
a building which is raised from the ground, a platform, indungu-dungu lyananda, e.g. Bataata bakayaka ndungudungu lyakuulisizya zintu. = Father built a raised construction for selling things through.

aggression, cruelty, e.g. Ncibi kucita ndutiluti kuli bamucaala. = It is bad to be aggressive to orphans. Bamalozi bakali kusaala minzi ya Batonga candutiluti. = The Balozi were raiding the villages of the Batonga with cruelty.
a type of nightingale, e.g. Induuntila yalikulila kabotu masiku. = The nightingale was singing beautifully at night. Also indwaantila.
a brown insect like a locust, pl. maduuntila, e.g. Nobana atukaakujate maduuntila sunu. = Children, let us go and catch the brown insects.
wits, intelligence, e.g. Mutinta nindwaandwa yamusimbi. = Mutinta has her wits about her. Also indungundungu.

intelligence, e.g. Sicikolo ulaa ndwaandwaandwa ulazwidilila mumisunko. = The pupil who has intelligence passes the examinations. Tazinaboola indwaandwaandwa zyakwe. = His intelligence is not yet developed.
type of bird, the nightingale, e.g. Indwaantila zikkala mumabuwa. = The nightingales live in the open country. Also induuntila.
a glutton, e.g. Ooyu mwana nindya. = This child is a glutton.
the fruit of the mulyabavwimi tree, e.g. Nitwali kunkuni twajana ndyabavwimi musyokwe. = When we went cutting firewood we found the fruit of the mulyabavwimi tree in the bush.
a shoe, e.g. Indyasyo zyangu zyazutuka katambo kaanzya. = My shoes have been cut on the thong which binds them.
the sole of the foot, e.g. Mutinta ujisi cilonda adyasyo. = Mutinta has a wound on the sole of her foot.

payment before the discussion of crime, e.g. Ciindi naakabbukilwa bulale bakamwaambila kuti koleta indyatalubuwa kutegwa tukanane kabotu. = When he committed adultery they told him to bring an opening payment so that they discuss properly.
the sole of a shoe, e.g. Indyato yabbusu lyangu yatyoka. = The sole of my shoe got broken.
an edible white mushroom, e.g. Bowa ndyu bulanona kapati. = The mushroom, indyu, is very tasty.
February, e.g. Mumwezi wandyu imvwula ilawa kapati. = In the month of the mushroom, (i.e. February), the rain falls heavily.
cheetah, e.g. Inemba izyala mbuli mangoye. = A cheetah gives birth like a cat. Also malama.
tattoes, cicatrices, e.g. Bakandiyasaula nembe munsingo nindakali kuciswa mutwe. = They made cicatrices on my neck when I had a headache.
a peg for stretching and drying the skin, e.g. Kamugagaila nembe tuyanike cisalu. = Hammer in the peg so that we dry the skin. Also inkanka.

sign, mark, seal, e.g. Inembo nzyajisi amubili zitondezya kuti mmusyomi mumisamu yacintu cisiya. = The marks which she has on her body shows that she is a believer in traditional medicines. inembo zyankwela = erotic cicatrices on women's backs and abdomens. e.g. Ndajana bamakaintu bayasaulana nembo zyaluyando. = I found the women tatooing one another with erotic cicatrices.
clay pot for beer, e.g. Bakaapa bakabumba *nembwa* zyobilo. = My grandmother moulded two clay beer pots. Also mbede
tonsil, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa *nenda* ncataambauli kabotu. = This child has tonsilitis that is why he does not speak well. Also idakabiya, kakoto, kameneno
antbear, e.g. Ndajana bwina *bwanengo* mucuulu kumusanza amunzi. = I found the den of an antbear in a termite hill south of our village. Also galaba.
the first rains, e.g. Mwaka wakamana tiiyakawa *nfwumpa-*
Last year the early rains did not fall. Also impumpaluya.

crest, mane, e.g. Wakabona ndiinga syuumbwa lipungunya *ngala* mucivwuna. He saw a big lion shaking its mane in the thicket (Tuft of feathers on a bird's head kaala; nakaala = crested crane); bacipuwa *ngala* = white people
tuft of long feathers, also magalagala, ingala zyamabungabunga.
head ornament, e.g. Bamami bamwi inga basama *ngala* kumitwe. = Some chiefs were head-dress.
*ingala* (*zyamabungabunga*) = a maize flower. e.g. Mapopwe esu akazwa kale *ngala*. Our maize has already flowered.
maize tassel, e.g. Mapopwe ali mumbewu yokwesu akazwa *ngalaala*. = The maize in our garden has produced tassels.
Also *ingalaala*.
sap, resin, exudation from tree, e.g. Misamu imwi taijisi *ingamwa*. = Some trees have no resin.

a fable with a song, e.g. *Ingano* zyakaindi zilakondelezya kapati. = Traditional fables with songs are very enjoyable. Ibbuku eli lilaa *ngano* zijisi masendelela asendelezya bukkale abweende bwabantu. This book has stories descriptions which convey the life and movement of people. Also caano.
a grey millet with long stem, e.g. *Ingaze* ilakomena kabotu mumasena mutakwe mvwula nyinji. Grey millet grows well in vleis which have not much water. Also inzembwe.
a hut built on props above ground, e.g. Bantu bensiku bakali kukkala *mungase*
ansiancestors used to live in elevated houses to escape from animals on the ground. Also ingasi, ingazi.
a hut on stilts, e.g. Basyaaneene bakalijisi *ngasi* mpati mobakali koonena. = My grandfather had a big hut on stilts where he used to sleep.

a platform on supports with roof, a look-out in a field for watching thieving animals, pl. *magazi*, e.g. Twakayaka *ngazi* yakuyaminina basokwe kumuunda. = We built a look-out platform in the field to scare off the monkeys. Mumyuunda bakali kunga nkuyaka *ngazi*. *Ngazi* iyakwa mbuli caanda cankwilimba, nkabela yalo kiili mpati akulampa. Kutanta inga kuli malele biya akutantila. Alimwi iyakilwa akati kamuunda kutegwa ijwi nosoola kalisika koonse-koonse. They used too build look-out platforms in the fields. The lookout platform was build like the hut of pidgeons but it was bigger and higher. There is a ladder for climbing into it. And it was build in the middle of the field so that when one called to scare away an animal, the voice reached everywhere.
a rabbit, e.g. *Ingelema* ulijisi twaano tunji. = A rabbit has many stories. Also sulwe.

a type of plant (*Corrigiola littoralis*), a green relish used in June and July, leaves are diced and cooked for 1 hr. e.g. Bamakaintu balaampa a kuyobola *ingima* yakubelesya ciindi cacilimo. = Women dry and store the *ingima* plant for use during the dry season.

the wrist, knuckle, ankle, kneecap, e.g. *Ndafwuyuka ngo yakumaulu.* = I have sprained my ankle. *Nzoka yamulumina ango kumbali amusisa oyu waakasindi.* = The snake has bitten him on the ankle near his Achilles tendon going to the heel.
a mango, pl. mango, e.g. *Jilo ndakalya ngo lisubila pyu!* = Yesterday I ate a very red mango!

a hooked stick used to hook and pull down fruit or firewood from a tree, e.g. *Cikuni canduuma mumutwe nindali koobola nkuni angoboobyo.* = A piece of wood struck my head when I was hooking branches for firewood. *Bakatyola ingoboobyo yakoobozya manego mumbali anzila.* = They cut down a hooked stick for bringing down *matobo* fruits beside the path. Also *ingobyo*
a mash of groundnuts and other relish, e.g. *Bacembele bajika ngogo.* = The old woman has cooked a mash of groundnuts. Also *ingoogo*
a harmless snake said to bring good luck, e.g. *Ingogoce yalinjide munanda sunu.* = A harmless snake entered the house today. Also *ingokoce*.
See *ingogoce*.
a type of disease, e.g. *Ulalabalika nkaambo nguuciswa bulwazi bwangokooko.* = He is raving because he is the one who is suffering from the mental disease.
a tendency to err, make mistakes, have accidents e.g. *Ulaa ingolomokwa* = He is prone to accidents. Also *sinunzuunzu*

the occurance of a taboo which demands a ritual of purification of a neighbourhood where someone has been killed or if a foreigner has died there. e.g. *Kuti muntu wafwida munanda yabantu, kweelede kujaigwa cintu nkaambo ningolomokwa.* If a person dies in the house of someone else, it is necessary to kill something ritually as it is special taboo. cf. *insotomokwa*

ululation, *kuuma/kulizya ngoloolo*, to beat the lips with tongue or fingers as one cries out, e.g. *Lyakanjila mooye, bamakaintu bakali kuuma ngoloolo.* When the girl went into seclusion. for initiation, the women ululated in joy. Also *inguluulu, mupululu*.
wheel-barrow, e.g. *Amususe museenga angolovwani.* = Draw the sand with a wheel-barrow.

a musical drum, e.g. *Ingoma yabukali yalila nikwazwa mulundo kudilwe.* The war-drum sounded on the second day of mourning to mark the end of the funeral. *Bakalibambila zisamo azizembyo zyangoma.* They were preparing their attire and mourning drums for ritual running up and down. (*kayanda* = a big drum; *mwaandu* = a drum made out of a large pot; *nakubili* = a drum beaten on both sides; *namalwa* = friction drum; *indandala* small drum, *namondonga* small drum; *budima* = main drums of Gwembe Valley)
a snuff box, e.g. *Basyaaneene balijisi kangoma nkobabikkila tombwe wamumpemo.* My grandfather has a box where he puts snuff.

a ritual Valley dance for rain preparatory to the pouring of beer over the graves and members of one's joking clan, e.g. *Bajwanyina bakali kuzyana ngoma ijilo kucuumbwe.* The joking clan members were dancing the *ngoma* dance at the grave yesterday. *Insete basimbi bakali kuzisama kungoma akuzipelu insiku.* = The girls used to wear stringed aprons at the rain-dance and at the *zipelu* long ago.
an impotent person, e.g. Chooka tayandi kukwata nkaambo ningomwa. = Chooka does not want to marry because he is impotent.
the sound of a bell ringing, e.g. Inombe zilizya ingondoongondo nozicela. = The cattle make the bells (around their necks) ring when they are grazing. cf. *mulangu waŋombe*
the joint of the knee, e.g. Ndalipwaya cisamu aŋgongozi. = I hit the tree with my knee-cap.

the core of a fruit similar in taste to groundnuts, a wild nut of the mubula tree, e.g. Ijilo baama bakabikka buntele bwangoogo mucisyu. = Yesterday mother put a mash of fruit-core in the relish. Twajana basankwa bobilo bapwaya ingoogo mucisiko camubula. = We found two boys crushing the *ngoogo* nut under the mubula tree.
a hat, e.g. Hikasenke usamide *ngowani* yamasilikani. = Hikasenke is wearing a policeman's hat. Also *imvwuse, imvwosi, intulu*

pl. of *loozi*, fibre, e.g. Amwaange *ngozi* zyakuvwumbya ciluli. = Tie fibres for thatching the roof. Mulembwe wakaanga *ngozi* kumbele aŋanda yakwe kuzyibya bantu kuti kwakali mutumbu. = Mulembwe tied fibres in front of his house to inform the people that there was a new mother. (Also to prevent a pregnant woman from entering the house because of the belief that this would bring sickness to the child.)
mist, light fog, haze, e.g. Sunu nibwaca kwali *ngubi*. = When it dawned today there was a mist. Also *nkubi, buuma.*.
mildew, e.g. Cisyu cili mucibiya cakaba angubi nkaambo kakukkala kaindi. = The relish which is in the dish has mildew because of lying there for a long time.

a blanket, e.g. Ndali kusanzya *ngubo* zyabana. = I was washing the childrens' blankets. Boonse bakali kulivwumba *ngubo* zyabanyama bakonze, bananja, basyaambololo abanaluvwi. = All were covering themselves with blankets of animal skin, hartebeestes, lechwe cobs, kudus and reedbucks.
the lining of an elephant's stomach, e.g. Muzovwu naazyala mwana wacivwumbidwe *ngubo*. = When the elephant gave birth, the baby elephant was still covered with the lining of the elephant's stomach.
firestones (Ila), e.g. Amubikke *ngulu* zyotatwe acikko. = Put three stones at the fireplace. Also *masuwa*

a pig, e.g. *Ngulube* yalikanda muntimba. = The pig wallowed in the mud. Bantu bakakotoka alya *mpolibonenwa ngulube*. = The people broke from work at that time when the pig was able to see the sun. (the pig does not raise its head and so can only see the sun when the sun is low in the sky).

ululation, e.g. Kamuuma *nguluulu* basika bakali kukuvwima. = Ululate because the hunters have arrived. Cabacembele nicakazwa, bakaintu mu munzi bakatalika kuuma *nguluulu*. = When the afterbirth came out, the women of the village began to ululate. Also *ingoloolo*
a small cattle-fly, e.g. Ino zyavwula *inguluzi* nkaambo nombe zyasika. = Now there are plenty of cattle-flies because the cattle have arrived. Also *imbuwo*
a type of bird, the ground seed-eater, e.g. *Ingulyu* yamana maila. = The ground seed-eating bird has finished the millet.
hornless cattle, e.g. Ooyu musune *ningumpu*. = This ox is hornless. Also *imvwuma*.
beast with horns cut, e.g. Musune wakagonkwa meja wakaba ngumpule. = The ox which had its horns cut became known as *ngumpule*. Also *ingumpu, igumpu*.
a head-dress of skins, e.g. *Ingundu yamucembele yayauka.* = The head-dress of the old woman is torn.

weight, burden, e.g. *Mukansondo wakakakilwa kuyumuka akaambo kakulema kwanongo alimwi angundumina lyamwana ngwaakabbede kusyule.* = Mukansondo was unable to get up because of the heaviness of the water-pot and the weight of the child which she was carrying on her back.
the yoke of an egg, e.g. *Ingunga yaji ilanona.* = The yoke of an egg is tasty. Also *mungunga*.

danger, e.g. *Zyakali ngunzuunzu zyatimba lyakaba joko lyambelele.* = What was danger for a small antelope became the yoke of a lamb. (After a person survives a dangerous situation there is peace) Also *inunzuunzu, ingunzuuzu*.
a firefly or glow worm, e.g. *Inguunguni zimweka masiku.* = The fireflies shine at night. Also *imwini-mwini, imuni-muni, mwini-mwenge*.
power, life force, e.g. *Inguzu zyakweenda nsejisi pe.* = I have no powers to walk.
a palm leaf, e.g. *Ndagonka ngwalala lyavwuuma.* = I have cut a palm from a palm tree. (used as fan)
a load, pl. *mangwanda*, e.g. *Ingwanda ndeyumwide lilalema.* = The load which I am carrying is heavy. Also *mukuli*.
a box with lid fixed, e.g. *Ibbokesi lyamusankwa ndingwanda, ligagaidwe mpikili.* = The box of the boy was fixed, nailed with nails.
a type of bird, a seed-eater, e.g. *Ingwence zyali kulya nseke zyabwizu mumusena.* = The seed-eating birds were eating the seeds of the grass in the vlei. Also *ingulyu*.
two furrow plough, two furrows, e.g. *Kwamana ngwenya, nkusyanga mweengwe wamapopwe.* = After two furrows you plant rows of maize.
a boxer, e.g. *Esther Phiri ningwenya yamusimbi mu Zambia.* = Esther Phiri is a female boxer in Zambia.
a hat, e.g. *Munene usamide inheta mpati.* = The old man is wearing a big hat. Also *inzyeete*.
a deep cavity, e.g. *Ulete mutiba ulaa nindi.* = Bring a soup plate. (which has a hollow in it.)
an anklet, a braclet, a ring (of bone, ivory, brass wire), e.g. *Ndasama ninga kukuulu.* = I am wearing an anklet on my leg.

a type of fish, pl. *baningu*, e.g. *Ndajaya ningu mumulonga mutwali kuzela.* = I have killed a *ningu* fish in the river where we were fishing. *Inkwazi iluma baningu, batuba bakwazi amapelepele.* = Vultures eat fish (known as) *ningu, ituba, kwazi and ipelepele. Mukaintu ooyo wakalijisi kalomo kaniini kamweelede mbuli kuti niningu.* = This woman had a small mouth which suited her resembling the mouth of a *ningu* fish. Also *muningu*.
the anus and rectum, e.g. *Mwana ulumidwe nzengene anio.* = The child has been bitten by a tick on the anus.

a beauty, e.g. *Salia wakali musimbi mubotu kaka. Mazuba ano mbabaniinga kabategwa ninjabi yamusimbi.* = Salia was indeed a beautiful woman. Nowadays she would be among those who would be called a beauty.
a method of building, e.g. *Injakilo yamwana ulya nimbi.* = The method of building of that one is bad.
dried meat, biltong, e.g. *Inyama injanike nimbotu kuyoka.* = Dried meat is good for roasting.

the railroad, e.g. Citima ceendela munjanji. The train runs on the railway line. (*Matobelanjanji* = followers of the railway, i.e. prostitutes. e.g. Mazubaano cijisi ntenda kuyanda matobelanjanji. Nowadays it is dangerous to seek prostitutes.)
a hunter's bracelet of skin, e.g. Muvwimi usama *njasilo* naya kukuvwima. = When a hunter goes hunting he wears a bracelet of skin.
a waterfly, e.g. Kuli *njebeebe* zinji mudamu lyesu. = There are many waterflies on our dam.
a support to raise one side of the pot on the fire, e.g. Atubikke *njela* kutegwa mpoto ikkale kabotu. = Let us put a support so that the pot sits properly.
precipice, cliff, e.g. Bana tabeelede kusobanina *anjeleele*. = Children should not play on a cliff. Also *ijeleele*
a fig, e.g. Ndali kuula *nji* zyakulya. = I had gone to buy figs for eating.

pl. of /wiili, a shell-fish, e.g. Nibakalanduka mulonga bakajana zipapa zya*njili*. When they crossed the river they found the shells of many shell-fish. Mpoto tukwalizya *njili*. We use shells to clean the pots.
a louse, e.g. Mumapayi kuli *njina*
There are many lice in the blankets.

the teaching, a lesson, e.g. Yakamwiinda *injiisyo* aboobo wakati, "Kunyina ncondizyi, kamundigwasya." Ndakakilwa. He missed the lesson and said, "There is nothig that I know. Can you pleas help me, I am unable."

noise made by flight of flock of birds, e.g. Nobwakaca mafwumofwumo yakamubusya *njobelo* yabayuni bakali kudilimuka kuuluka. When it was dawn early in the morning she was awakened by the noise of a flock of birds flying past.
an amusing conversation, e.g. Twali kuyooma *njoomo*. We had an amusing conversation. Ulaa *njoomo*. = He is amusing.
leprosy, e.g. Bulwazi bwa*njovwela* bulayoosya. The disease of leprosy is fearsome. Also busicinanta.
a pestilence, measels, e.g. Mumunzi mwabbuka *njowela*, bantu tabeelede kweendeenda. In a village where a pestilence breaks out, the people should not move about. Also kalwalo

card-playing, e.g. Ndayanda kuuma *njuka*. I want to play cards. Twabucesya kusobana *njuka*. We were playing cards until dawn. *Njuka* tacili cisobano cibotu kubana baiya cikolo abataiyi nkaambo kakuti tacisobanwi katakwe mali, ciyiisya kubba. = Card-playing is not a good past-time for pupils or for those who are not learning because one cannot play without money, it teaches stealing.
a collection of big birds, e.g. Kwainda *njuni* mujulu kugama kumbo. = A flock of big birds passed overhead going westwards.
a forked stick which was used as a slave's collar, e.g. Bazike bakali kupenga kubikkwa *nkabo* munsingo. = Slaves were suffering by having a forked stick around the neck. Also iganda.

a turtle, e.g. *Inkaka* ilya buci bwanzuki abwampasi mumasamu adyaamene. Ijisi kalaka kalamfwu nkiidyomeka mumpako yabuci. = The turtle eats bee honey and the honey of the small mpasi bee in the bent trees. It has a long tongue which it sticks into the hives. (It cannot descend when it is full in the trees, it just throws itself down onto the ground.)

one who does not want to be seen, e.g. Munene ooyu mmubi. Nkokuti nkalombwana kakalya musizya, nkalombwana ncobeni kakasama cikumba cankakakubonwa. = This old man is evil. That is to say he is a strong man who has taken medicine to discourage those who are trying to take away his power of witchcraft, he is a truly powerful man who wears the skin of an invisible magic animal. Also inkakatwaambwa
a bunch of feathers worn at a funeral ceremony, e.g. Bamadaala bansiku bakali kuyandisya kusama nkakalale mumadilwe. = The old men of long ago used to like wearing a bunch of feathers at a funeral.

dice, kuwaala/kuuma nkakata = to throw/beat the dice, e.g. Murjanga wali kuuma nkakata. = The witchdoctor was throwing the dice. (The four dice thrown in divination are: cinokozi, sikwme, kalume, intuba.)
the crested guinea-fowl, Also inkangatole.

the scaly ant-eater, e.g. Ndajana nkakatwaambwa musyokwe nindali kweembela mpongo. = I found a scaly ant-eater in the bush when I was herding goats. Aaka kakutu kakali kamunyama utegwa nkakatwaambwa, munyama wamaamba manji kapati. = This skin was of a scaly ant-eater, an animal which has very many scales.
a crab, e.g. Ndajata nkala mpati munsi abbwe. = I found a big crab beside a stone. Bakasika akalambwa kankala. = They arrived at the little pool of a crab.
a breed of dog, e.g. Luzubo Iwankala olu ndupati. = This breed of dog is big.
lime, e.g. Akaambo kakubula mali, ndakakonzya biyo kuula kasaka komwe kankalaga. = Because of a shortage of money I was only able to buy one bag of lime.

an energetic and zealous person or group, e.g. Masowe wakali nkalakata yamulombwana kumakani akuumana nyindi. = Masowe was an energetic person as regards boxing. Nkalakata zyabalombwana amacembele zyakakkala kubamba twaambo. = An energetic group of old men and women sat down to deal with the problems.
a waggon, a cart, e.g. Inkalaki yokwesu izwide mapopwe. = Our waggon is full of maize. Also inola.
my grandnephew by my sister, e.g. Inkalamabelo yabaama yakafwa. = The grandnephew of my mother died.
Zulu-styled hat, e.g. Mumootokala kwakali nkalamazulu yokwa Haabeenzu. = In the car there was a Zulu hat belonging to Haabeenzu.
a lion, e.g. Inkalamu tiilizyali. = A lion does not give birth to itself.
a species of tree, e.g. Mukagonke masomo ankalanga. = Cut down poles of the nkalanga tree.
a type of tree, e.g. Musamu wankalangu mmuyumu kugonka. = The nkalangu tree is hard to cut. Also inkalanga.
rust, e.g. Cibulo cameenda cakaba ankalaya. = The water-bucket has become rusty.
beast given to parents of girl after her initiation by parents of boy.
pl. of lukalo, a fibre rope, e.g. Koosa nkalo zyakwaanzya boombe. = Plait fibre ropes for tying the calves.
a small bundle (of fibres, herbs, spears), e.g. Kondipa nkama yamuliwa. = Give me a bundle of vegetables.
a bitter unripe taste, e.g. Masuku ataningabizwa kabotu alaa nkamba. = The masuku fruits which are not yet ripe are bitter.
a wild bitter plant, e.g. Nkamba a zisyu zimwi nzibakayanikide zyakamana. = The wild bitter plant and other relish which they had dried had all finished.

a magistrate's or chief's court, e.g. Tuya kukubetekelwa kunkambe yamwami. = We are going to be tried at the court of the chief. Bantu bamwami bakali kubbadela mali manji bamana kubetekwa munkambe yakwe. = The people of the chief were made to pay high fines after they had been judged at his court.
an amount, e.g. Inkamo zyacisyu ezi nzipati. = The amounts of this relish are great. Also inkamu, inkama.
useless person, e.g. Eci cana ncendela ninkampule, taciteyi pe. = This brat I am looking after is useless, he does not even trap birds nor animals
a crowd, great number or size, e.g. Kuli nkamu yabaimbi yali kwiimba. = There was a choir of singers singing.
a hair-comb, e.g. Inkamu yamasusu yapya mucikko. = The hair-comb was burnt in the fire.

the way of talking, e.g. Inkananino yamuntu ulya yali yakuyoosya. = The way of talking of that person was frightening. Bananyina bakali kukondwa alimwi akumuseka akaambo kankananino yakwe. = His mates were happy and were laughing at him because of the way he talked. (kubaa nkananino = to exaggerate)
desert, hard black ground, e.g. Inkanda ili kujwe amulundu Musise taijisi zisamu. = The desert to the east of Musise mountain has no trees.
skins, e.g. Inkanda zyabantu bamwi taziyandi kubalwa kapati zuba. = The skins of some people do not need to have much sunshine.
a clot of blood, e.g. Ndajana nkandamalowa munzila mbuli kuti kuli ncibajaya. = I found a clot of blood on the path as if they had killed something.
the colour red, e.g. Moonga wasamide cibbudula cankandamalowa. Moonga was clad in a red shorts.

the ritual celebrations for one who has returned from afar, e.g. Kuli ba Simoonga kuli pobwe lyankandamaulu Moonga wakali kubukuwa. = At Simoonga's home there is a feast to welcome back Moonga who has returned from abroad.
dry land, e.g. Inkandambwe yakapya alo mani akaliwo akapidilizya. = The dry land went on fire and so the grass which was there was burnt.
a candle, e.g. Kodomeka nkandela munanda musalale. = Light a candle so that there is light in the house.

the upper grinding-stone, e.g. Nkando yabacembele yakomoka. = The upper grinding-stone of the old woman has been chipped. Eci ciindi coonse muka Sicibende wakali kusiminine ankando, wakali kuswiilila. = All this time the wife of Sicibende was pressing on the upper grinding stone, she was listening. Also mwanaankando.
a wooden bowl, e.g. Ijilo ndakaula inkandwi yakubwezela bulilu. = Yesterday I bought a bowl for carrying food for the journey. Also nkwandi
a guinea-fowl, e.g. Inkanga zyakatalika kutula mayi. = The guinea fowls have started laying eggs.
the crested guinea-fowl, e.g. Bavwimi bajaya nkangatole. = The hunters have killed a crested guinea-fowl. Also inkakatole.

a peg for the idiba trap or for a tent, e.g. Kamusimpa nkanka zyakubikka diba. = Insert the pegs for the idiba trap. Aaka kadaala kakasimpide nkanka zyamusamu nzila zyoonse zyakali kuboola kumusamu wakwe. = This old man planted pegs of wood all along the paths which led to his tree.
stubbourness, e.g. *Ncibi kubaa nkanka nokanana kaambo nkotazyi.* = It is bad to be persistent in a matter about which you are ignorant. Also *inkazi.*
a group, e.g. *Nkanka zyabalombwana ezi zyakakanana twaambo tunji.* = The group of powerful men talked about many topics.
most distinguished people, e.g. *Caambilizya kuti ntotuswe nkankaala mubbanki.* = It means that we are the most distinguished people in the bank.
a handful, e.g. *Ndakabweza nkankamaanza lyandongwe.* = I took a handful of groundnuts. Also *mukanya, munsuma.*

matter, business, e.g. *Inkani yabantu basimakwebo tiiyapasululwa, nkaambo wakabba talibonyi akati kabo.* = The problem among the businessmen is unresolved, because the one who stole is not to be seen among them.

the hips, e.g. *Ooyu mwana ngwakaandula nkanya.* = This child is the first born. (lit. to cut the hips) *Citenge mbucakaangidwe munkanya mbuli kuti kuli wazyila kukulima.* = The citenge was tied around the hips like someone coming from ploughing.
bundle, e.g. *nkapi zyaloozi.* = bundles of fibres. Also *nkata zyaloozi*
perspiration, e.g. *Masiku onse ndali kuzwa nkasaalo nkaambo kakuciswa.* = I was sweating all through the night due to illness. Also *mitukuta, itukuta, mibe*
an oar, e.g. *Basibwato babelesya nkasi kukwasula bwato.* = The boat people use an oar to row the boat. Also *insoke.*
a cow which refuses to give milk, e.g. *Eeyi nombe ninkasi, tiiyandi kukamwa.* = This cow is a non-milker, she refuses to be milked.
meat left after fat has been removed, e.g. *Mujike nyama nkasu iyanikidwe aciluli.* = Cook the lean meat which is drying on the roof.

a headpad or coil of grass or cloth, e.g. *Kondizingila nkata nkabweze nkuni.* = Make a headpad for me so that I can carry the firewood. Wakasika kuli nguwe *ankata* yasibbolonzya wakamutwikka. = She came to him with a headpad of grass and he helped her to lift the load on to her head.
divining bones, e.g. *Munanga oyu ubelesya nkata mukusonda kwakwe.* = This diviner uses divining bones in his divination.
a vest or singlet, e.g. *Mwana tanasama nkausu pe.* = The child has not yet put on a vest.
a bangle of bone/ivory/copper, e.g. *Ndisamide nkaya zyosanwe kukuboko.* = I wear five bangles on my arm. cf. *inyinga.* (*Ijinga* = a big ivory bangle.)

broken pot e.g. *Basimpongo bakali kukamina mpongo munkaye.* The herd boys were milking the goats into broken pots. *inkazi* stubbourness, e.g. *Mweemba ulaa nkazi, tayandi kunyonwa.* = Mweemba is stubbourn, she does not want to be changed.
dwelling place of refuge, e.g. *Wakajokela kunkazo yabo.* = He returned to their dwelling place of safety.

a chain, e.g. *Inketani yancinga yazutuka.* = The bicycle chain is broken. *inketele* (ety. Eng.) a kettle, e.g. *Kosibika meenda akujisya nsima munketele.* = Put water in the kettle on the fire for cooking nsima.

a mason wasp, pl. *manko,* e.g. *Lyandiluma nko aliso.* = A mason wasp has stung me on the eye. Also ivwo, pl. mavwo; (Mason wasp building in houses = loma, simuzinzimwa; big black mason wasps = kanyati, ilumanyati; large, striped, stinging cattle = ilumanombe)
a knot tied in grass, e.g. Bana baanga *nkoka* amani. = The children tie knots in the grass.
the elbow, e.g. Ijanza lyangu lyatontola nkaambo *nkokola* yapwaya acisamu. = My hand is numb because the elbow struck a tree.
a butterfly, e.g. Uuno mwaka twabona *nkokolekwa* zyamisyobomisyobo. This year we saw butterflies of different varieties.
a pigmy, e.g. Nseningabwene muntu mufwaafwi mbuli *nkola*. = I have not yet seen a man as short as a pigmy. (an old pygmy = inkulukulu, inkuludu.)
a type of bird, the plover, e.g. Ndabona mayi *ankolekole* musyokwe. = I saw the eggs of a plover in the bush.
a beast with loose horns, e.g. Musune wesu *mmukolekole*, meja alazungaana. = Our ox has loose horns, the horns are shaking.
a knobkerrie, a club, a walking stick, e.g. Basyaanene beenzya *nkoli*. = My grandfather walks with a walking stick.
a rope, e.g. Ulasunga tubwa tutayandi kutobela *ankole*. He ties the puppies who do not wish to follow with a rope.

pl. of lukolo, a woman's breast, e.g. Baama balaa cicisa kunkolo. = My mother has a sore on her breast. Bazyali bakali kulanga kukomena kwankolo nkaambo tiibakacizyi kubala mezi yakuzyalwa kwabana. Parents were looking at how the breasts developed because they did not know how to count the months until the birth of children.
female initiation ritual, e.g. *Inkolola* ili kwa Simoonga izwa mu Mujibelo. The initiation which is going on at Simoonga's will be concluded in the 'coming out' ceremony on Saturday.
the crust of porridge, pl. makololo, e.g. Babwa kobapa *nkololo*. = Give the dogs the porridge crust.
the fruit of the mufwulimuninga tree, e.g. Twali kukucela nkoloondo. We were gathering the fruits of the mufwulimuninga tree.
a waggon, e.g. Basankwa bakwela *nkolowi* nkaambo basune basungidwe batija. The boys are pulling the waggon because the oxen which had been yoked ran away. Also nkalaki.
a variety of sorgum, e.g. Uuno mwaka tuyakusyanga *nkolwe*. = This year we will plant sorgum.

a type of tree, e.g. *Inkomba* a sibbololonzya njemisamu imwi mibotu kukucita nsipa muminzi. *Inkomba* and sibbololonzya are some of the trees for making soap in the villages. Sibbololonzya ulamena mumbali alwizi amutulonga: *inkomba* lilamena mumyuunda abamwi balalicita telele. = Sibbololonzya grows near the lake and streams: *inkomba* grows in the fields and some use it for relish. Also cinkomba, citeezi, mudelele.
a verandah, e.g. Mucembele wakakkazika nongo *munkombe*. = The old woman placed an earthen pot on the verandah. Also ikkoce, iduze
the navel, e.g: Ndakalumwa nzengene *ankombo*. = I was bitten by a tick on the navel.
the stern of a canoe, e.g. Kamwaanga lukole *ankombo* lyabwato. = Tie a rope to the stern of the boat. Also inkomboombo.

spitting cobra, ringhals, e.g. *Inkombola* yandipilla mate mumeso. = The spitting cobra sprayed my eyes with spittle. *simakoma* head-erect cobra; *kasambwe* = short spitting cobra (greenish, readiest to fight and bite)
the stern of a canoe, e.g. *Inkomboombo* yabwato yatyoka. = The stern of the boat is broken. Also inkombo, impemo, impunu.
a cup, e.g. Koleta *nkomeki* tunywisye meenda. = Bring a cup for us to drink water.
See *inkomeki*.
a pocket, a small pouch, e.g. *Inkomo* yabuluke yazauka. = The pocket of the trousers is torn.

a type of small coconut, e.g. Njanda kubweza *nkomone* mumutiba. = I want to take a small coconut out of the plate. inkomponi (ety. Eng.) a compound, e.g. Baacisya bakkala munkomponi kwa Kanyama. My uncle lives in Kanyama compound.
bowlegs, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa *nkomvwa*. This child is bowlegged.
a type of tree, (Ziziphus sp.) whose fruit is eaten in March. e.g. *Inkomwa* tazinabizwa mazubaano. = The fruits of the *inkomwa* tree are not yet ripe these days. Also inkoomwa, imfwulimuninga.
an overhanging high bank of a river, e.g. Ndaimvwi *ankomwe* yamulonga nindabona ciwena mumeenda. = I was standing on the bank of the river when I saw a crocodile in the water.
a cloth bag, a pocket, e.g. Mali ngindabikkide munkomwe asoweka. = The money which I put in the bag is lost.
a clod of earth, e.g. Bana baumana mankomwe amalongo. = The children are beating one another with clods of earth. Also ivwunga, igomwe.

a pit, an extensive game-pit for several head of game, e.g. Basankwa balikusya *nkona* mumukondo wabanyama. = The boys were digging a pit in the path of the animals. *Nkona* mbuzyakali kuteegwa, banyama tabaindi akwiinda. = The animals were not going past the pittraps which had been set.
a tuber used in famine times, e.g. Mumwaka wanzala twakafwutuka *ankona*. = In a year of famine we are saved by bush-tubers.
war, e.g. Muzisi mumwi kuli *nkondo*. In some countries there is war.
an insipid water melon, e.g. Ooyu namunyo *ninkondole* buyo, tanoni. This water melon is a tasteless one, it is not sweet.
a honey-comb formed in the ground by black ants, e.g. Nitwali kusya cuulu twajana *nkonga* ansi. = When we were digging an anthill we found a honeycomb of black ants.
an ox with horns curving inwards, e.g. Musune wankonko ulacela mumusena. An ox with horns curving inwards is grazing in the vlei.
a butterfly, e.g. Uuno mwaka twabona *nkonkolekwa* zyamisyobo-misyobo. = This year we saw many different varieties of butterflies.
a butterfly, e.g. Bana basobanya *nkonkolwa*. The children are playing with a butterfly.
a roof which touches the ground, e.g. Inkuku ilakumba munkonkolwa. = A hen sits on its eggs on a roof which touches the ground. Also citumba.
arm-bangles e.g. Kumweelede *nkonokono* kumikono. = The armbangles on her forearms suit her.
leavings or scrapings of food, e.g. Bana bakwangulula *nkonono*
The children are eating the scrapings of the pot. Also makololo.
a fist, e.g. Sicikolo bamuuma *nkonye* mumutwe bayi. The teacher has beaten the pupil on the head with his fist.
the triangle of bones forming the back of the pelvis (the sacrum), e.g. Cibulo nicakaloka cakandu- uma _ankonyokonyo_. = When the bucket fell it struck me on the pelvis. Also bukome, inkanya.
a butterfly Also inkonkolekwa, inkonkolwa
a button, e.g. _Inkopela_ aci- sani cangu zyakakosoka. = The buttons have come off my dress.
a cap, e.g. Mudaala usamide _nkopesi_. = The man is wearing a cap. Also _nkepesi, nkwepesi, cisoli, cisoti_.
bunda= a fez.
the nape of the neck, e.g. Kuli wakanduuma bbwe _ankosi_. = Someone has struck me on the back of the neck with a stone.
a government official, e.g. Sunu ku- mazuba tulaswaigwa _inkosi_. = This even- ing we will be visited by a government official.
ripeness, e.g. Nzembwe mu- muunda zyasika _ankosoko_. = The sorgum in the field has reached the stage of ripeness. (_kuinkosoko_ = the time of ripeness)
a red ox or cow with a stripe along it's back, e.g. Eeyi mpwizi _ninkosole_. = This red heifer has a stripe along it's back.
a head of cattle with notched ear = _inkosole kutwi_, e.g. Inombe yangu _nko- sole yasoweka_. = My cow with the notched ear is missing.
the end of the rains, e.g. _Inkosole niyakamana, kwakaboola mpeyo_. = When the rains finished, there came the cold.

a longing to satisfy ones desire, for such things as meat or toba- cco, e.g. Suntwe wakali kunywa wakabaa _nkosya_ kapati. When the hyena drank he had a longing for meat. _Nkosya yato- mbwe yakali kwiinda_. = The desire for tobacco was getting worse. Also buusa, busa.
a shelled mealie-cob, e.g. _Ndeelyo nkoti_, komusansamuna kumaa- nza mwana. = Here is a shelled mealie- cob, clean the child's hands with it. Also cinkonti.
occipital bone, at back of brain
a knot, a knot made in grass as a sign, e.g. _Inketani koyaanga nkoto kutegwa ifwiimpe_. = Tie a knot on the chain to make it shorter.
a goggle-eyed person, e.g. Aawa kwa- inda muntu _wankoto zyameso_. = A goggle-eyed person passed by there.
a hornless head of cattle, a tuskless elephant, e.g. Inombe _inkotoolo ilayanda kulwana lyoonse_. = The hornless cow always likes to fight.
a stone suitable for sharp- ening, a grinding stone, e.g. Koya uka- yandaule _nkotozyo_. = Go and search for a stone which can be used for sharpening.
an eyelash, (an eyelid = _cikoye_), e.g. Bamwi bantu bajisi _nkoye zilamfwu_. = Some people have long eye- lashes.

sense, character, e.g. Kumubuzya _nkwaabede, kuvwuwa wakali kwiide kuso- tauka kakunyina kaambo kalaa nkoye nkaamba_. = Asking her where she had been, in answering she was just evasive without giving any reason which made sense. Ooyu mukaintu wakasala kusowa _nzila zyakwe zyabumpelenge akuccilila bulemu bwabantu balaa nkoye_. = This woman chose to get rid of her ways of deceit and to follow the dignity of people who had good character.
a water-lily, e.g Nitwakamana kuzela, twakatalika kufwumba _inkuba_. = When we were finished fishing, we started to dig out waterlilies. Also impana
mildew, e.g. Insima ili mu- caambikwa yakabaa _nkubi_. = The nsima in the pot has mildew. Also imvwundi
a hen, e.g. Kamujata nkuku tujaile beenzu. = Catch the chicken so that we kill it for the visitor. *Inkuku yabutwa* = a wild hen.
pl. of lukukubwi, a type of bird, a snipe, e.g. Tuya kukuvwima nkukubwi mumusena. = We are going to hunt snipe in the vlei.

a special group of people, e.g. *Inkunkunyenze zyabalombwana abamakaintu zyakayeeya kuti lubono lucaale bana babelesye nkaambo bakali bapati kale.* A special group of men and women thought that the inheritance should remain with the children as they were already adults.
dry, fallen leaves, e.g. Kamukukula alubuwa, kuli *nkukwani*. = Sweep the courtyard, there are dry fallen leaves. Also *inkwakwani*.
rust, e.g. Cipeni caceede anze cabaa *nkula*. = The knife which was left outside has rust. Also *inkalaya*.

a round bullet, e.g. Munyati bakamuyasa *nkulu* amubili. = They pierced the buffalo's body with a bullet. Walijatilila mpoyakanjila *nkulu*. = He held himself at the place where the bullet had entered.
an elderly pigmy, e.g. Twakajana *inkuludu* iyota mulilo. = We found an old pigmy heating himself at the fire.
a type of bird, the emerald starling, e.g. Twaunka kukuleta bana bankulukuze. = We are going to bring the young of the emerald starling.
an elderly pigmy, e.g. Tujana busongo bunji *munkululu*. = We find much wisdom in an elderly pigmy. Also *inkuludu*.
a type of bird, the touracco, e.g. Wakasekka munimba wankulyukuku acingowani cakwe. = He stuck a feather of the touracco in his hat. Also *inkulyukulyu*.
a type of bird, the touracco with scarlet feathers, e.g. Mweene wajayila baneene *nkulyukulyu*. = Mweene killed a scarlet touracco for my grandfather. Also *inkulyukuku*.
a snail, e.g. *Inkumba yeendeenda ciindi camainza*. = The snail moves about during the rains.
the chief's messenger, e.g. *Mwami watuma nkumba yakwe kutamba bantu bakwe muswaangano*. = The chief send his messenger to invite his people to a meeting.
bank of river, e.g. *Munkumba yamulonga kwakali butinti mbobatakali kubwene*. = Near the river there was a swamp which they did not see. Also *nkumbwi*
a cowry-shell, e.g. Aka kana kakasamide zintu zyobile amubili: *inkumba alimwi akampakatwa*. = This child was dressed with two things on the body: a cowry-shell and a shoulder-band.

sympathy, pity, tender love, e.g. Aaba bacembele balaa *nkumbu* kubazyukulu babo. = This old women has a special love for her grandchildren. Teletete wakamufwida *nkumbu* Kasise. = Teletete felt pity on Kasise.
hole in the ground made by termites, the inside of an animal's den, e.g. Mumbali-mbali abutala kuli *nkumbwi*. = There is a termite-hole beside the grain-bin.

the depths of a pool, e.g. Kana kabbila muzyiba kaunka *munkumbwi*. = The child drowned and went into the depths of the pool. Kuti kwatontola kapati inswi zinji zikkalila *munkumbwi* mudyolwe. = If it is very cold many fish go into the deep parts of the pool in a hole.
side compartment in a grave, e.g. Nobakasika acuumbwe mutunta bakaubikka mucuumbwe *kunkumbwi*. = When they reached the grave they put the body in the side compartment down in the grave.

an important person, VIP, e.g. Ndakanyandwa mbobanga basala ndime kuunka kumuswaangano kakuli zyakaliko nkumekume zyakali zipatipati kuli ndime amulimo. = I was surprised in that they chose me to go to the meeting while there were more important people than me at work.
a very wealthy person, e.g. Simunzyaabo a Mudyaka wakalivwubide kapati, mbabakali kutegwa ninkumenkume. = The uncle of Mudyaka was very rich, he was among those who were known as wealthy people.
the forehead, e.g. Mwana wanduuma bbwe ankumo. = The child hit me with a stone on the forehead.
(idiomatic) luck, Ndakabaa nkumo. = I was fortunate.
a slope, e.g. Muunda okwesu ulaa nkunamwa. Our field has a slope.
a bunch of mealie cobs, e.g. Mubbi wakajatwa ankungo lyamapopwe mumaanza. = The thief was caught with a bundle of mealie-cobs in his hands. Also ikkungo.
a bull-elephant, e.g. Beembezi bayoowa nibabona inkungulu mu musena. The herders feared when they saw a bull-elephant in the vlei.
a childless or wifeless man, e.g. Lubuwa Iwankungulume lulaa tombe lyoonse. = The courtyard of an unmarried man is always dirty. Also insumbalume.
a haze over water, e.g. Cifwumofwumo kwali nkungwe atalaa meenda. In the morning there was a haze over the water.
a person who is always travelling about, e.g. Musimbi oyu ninkunkalwizi. This girl likes travelling about (i.e. she is a prostitute) Also najempa.

respected people e.g. Inkunkunyenze zyabalombwana abamakaintu zyakayeeya kuti lubono lucaale bana babelesye nkaambo bakali bapati kale. A gathering of respected men and women thought that the inherited wealth should remain for the children to use as they were already grown up.
a type of bird, the hoopoe, e.g. Ndajana nkunkuunku atalaa ciluli cananda. = I found a hoopoe on top of the roof of the house.
firewood, e.g. Kosikka nkuni acikko, mulilo waceya. Put firewood into the fire, the flame has gone down.

a bush pig, pl. bankuntula, e.g. Babwa bajaya nkuntula. = The dogs have killed a bush-pig. Banyama bali mbuli bankuntula abasokwe, babula cakulya musyokwe, batalika kulya zisyango zili mumyuunda. = Animals who are like wild boars and baboons, lacking food in the bush, begin to eat the plants in the fields. Also muuma, sicipongo, mungundu.
a button, e.g. Yaloka inkunupu nitwali kutingaana mumusenga. = A button fell off when we were wrestling in the sand. Also inkopela.
a type of wild fruit, e.g. Mwana mumucelele nkunyukunyu awalo. = Collect nkunyukunyu fruit for the child also.
a cow with long horns bending backwards, e.g. Inkupi mwiizandule itanjili muciba. = Separate the cow with the long horns bending backwards so that it does not enter the kraal.

wrinkles on forehead, frown, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ulayanda kubikka nkusa ankumo. = This boy likes putting wrinkles on the forehead. Also inkusita, pl. mankusita, minya; wrinkles between the eyebrows = kaimba, pl. twimba; -zinga tunkusa / zinga minya / zinga mayimba = *make wrinkles.*
tampan, lice on fowl, e.g. *Inkuku zyamana kufwa akaambo kanku- swi.* = The chickens have all died off be- cause of lice. Kampotyo, kankotyo, inta- ntabwa = a very small kind infesting poultry.
a chief's court, e.g. *Twazwida kunkuta kumabeta.* = We have come out of the court from the trials.
type of bird, the African spoonbill, e.g. *Inkutakuta-kaya- mba ilalila mumeenda.* = The African spoon-bill cries in the water.
a skin-apron, e.g. *Bamadaala basama nkute nobabeleka.* = The old men wear skin-aprons when they work.

a fig tree, e.g. *Uuno mwaka nkuyu zilizyede kapati.* = This year the fig tree bears much fruit. (bukuyu = common big fig tree; mulembela = with figs growing in clusters on the trunk; mutumbi = bearing very small figs; mwiyi = bearing small elongated figs)
the armpit, e.g. *Inkwa yangu ilacisa.* = My armpit is sore.

a rounded section of bark detached from a tree, e.g. *Simpande ulabeza inkwa, ulikwenkweza kuti buci butaka- caalili baakulya bazyali kumunzi.* = Simpande carves out a section of bark, he levels it off so that the honey does not remain when the parents eat it at home. *Ntyungila ulagwisya buci akububikka mu- nkwa.* = Ntyungila takes out the honey and puts it in a rounded piece of bark.
an ox with horns extending sideways, e.g. *Musune okwa taata ni- nkwaali, meja alikwaalele.* The ox of my father is called 'inkwaali', it has horns extending sideways.
a peg of the idiba trap, e.g. *Kobikka nkwabyo adiba.* = Set the peg of the idiba trap.
an edible vegetable bulb, boiled with wood ashes until bitterness goes, e.g. *Inkwakwa ilabota kuti yajikwa kabotu.* = The inkwakwa vegetable is nice if cooked well.
a fence, e.g. *Tuya kukuyaka nkwakwa zyambewu.* = We are going to build fences for the garden.
dry fallen leaves, e.g. *Muswi oyo ukkala munsi amabwe, mu- matope amunkwakwani.* = The big fish lives under stones, in the mud and in dead fallen leaves.
a sound of rustling, e.g. *Ba- na bamvwa inkwalani kunsi abulo.* = The children heard a rustling sound under the bed.
a head of cattle with horns growing horizontally, e.g. *Eeyi nombe ninkwali.* = This cow has horizontal horns. Also inkwaali

a traditional wooden plate or bowl, e.g. *Bataata bafwala nkwandi.* = My father is carving a bowl. *Nkwandi mmitiba yacisamu njobakali kulida bensiku.* = The nkwandi were wooden dishes which our ancestors used for eating. Also mugano
raw or underdone meat, e.g. *Mwana ulya nyama nkwange.* = The child is eating undercooked meat.
a green vegetable plant *(Commelina diffusa)*, e.g. *Inkwasia ncisyu cikonda bamakaintu.* = The green vege- table is a relish which delights women.
dry fallen leaves, Also inkwakwani.
sores in the groin, e.g. *Bantu bane- neede babaa nkwaya nokupya.* = Fat people develop sores in the groin when it is hot. Also inkwiya.

a fish-eagle, e.g. *Inkwazi ya- jaya inswi mudamu.* = The fish-eagle is killing fish in the dam. *(Iluma nswi mbuli baningu, batuba, bakwazi amapelepele.* = It eats fish like baningu, batuba, bakwazi and mapelepele.) Also sikwaze
the middle part of a coconut, part of a coconut shell, e.g. *Inkwebe yakabola ileelede kusoogwa.* = The inside of the coconut which has rotted should be thrown away.
a type of bird, the redwinged partridge, e.g. *Basankwa basobelela inkwecece.* = The boys are stalking a red-winged partridge.
the colour yellow, e.g. *Mubala wainkweeqwe taukondi bantu banji.* The colour yellow does not please many people.
type of bird, partridge species, e.g. *Ijilo ndakajana kwacegwa nkwekeke mukooye kangu.* = Yesterday I found a partridge caught in my trap.
sexual desire or activity, *kulya nkwela* = to have sexual intercourse, e.g. *Ncibi kubaa nkwela amucizi wako.* = It is wrong to act sexually with your sister.

edible heart of a palm **inkwepesi yamasusu** a wig **inkwido** the bolt or handle of a door, e.g. Mazuba, kojata *nkwido.* Mazuba, hold the handle of the door. Kobikka *nkwido* = Bolt the door. Also mwinzyo
entrance, e.g. *Mucembele wakanjila munanda akuwida ankwidizyo.* = The old woman entered the house and fell down there at the entrance.
a large type of locust, e.g. *Mumbewu yangu muli nkwigwi zinji.* = In my garden there are many large locusts. Also *cikwikwi*

a type of bird, the pidgeon, e.g. *Inkwilimba zilakatazya kuvwuba.* = It is hard to rear pidgeons. *Nkwilimba nciyakaceela moyo, mmapenzi ngiibona lyoonse-lyoonse.* = What makes a pidgeon to have a small heart is because of the problems that it always faces.
a type of bird, the African green pidgeon, e.g. *Balwazi balombozya kuyoka nkwilinti.* = The patient desires to roast a green pidgeon.
an ear-ring, pl. *mankwinta-nkwinta,* e.g. *Mankwinta-nkwinta aya mmabotu.* = These ear-rings are beautiful.

a wooden hoe, e.g. *Wakacilima cilili candongwe ankwisyo.* = She dug a groundnut-patch with a wooden hoe. *Bakasika mucisaka kukusya Iwidi ankwisyo akululongela munsangwa zyabo.* = They entered the bush and dug a tuber with a wooden hoe and put it in their baskets.
a type of bird, a starling, e.g. *Inkwizi-nkwzi nkayuni keebeka.* = The male plumb-coloured starling is a beautiful bird.

*kusiya cankwizi-kwizi* = to be of the dark colour of blue **inndenya** one who lacks money to pay tax, e.g. *Inndenya zyakali kujatwa cibbalo kaindi.* People who were without money to pay tax were taken for forced labour long ago.
a giraffe, e.g. *Inndudwa ilaa mukosi mulamfwu.* The giraffe has a long neck.
a type of bird, the wagtail, e.g. *Innduuntila ilayanda kulunduka ansi kwiinda kuuluka.* = The wagtail prefers to run on the ground rather than fly.
a footprint, pl. *mano*
a water-tortoise, e.g. *Ndajana nondo ilya bowa.* I found a tortoise eating mushrooms. Also *ibbandwa
a land-tortoise, also kabinda, cibinda, sicaanga (with red stripes living in rocks.)

a large clay pot for storing water, beer, general use, e.g. *Inongo yacibwantu yapwaika.* The large clay pot for storing sweet-beer is broken. *Ansanza yananda kwakali cibwantu munongo camulalansana. = To the south-end of the house there was sweet-beer, made from the root of a short shrub, in a pot. (cibiya, cilongo = for cooking any kind of food; impoto, intolomani = a metal pot; citentu, cilongo, caambikwa = for cooking porridge; cinkomba = a large pot for cooking vegetables; cuumbu, cibizilo, cipempe, kafwuko = for carrying and keeping water or milk; italo, citalo = a narrow-necked pot for brewing beer; namatimba, cibuya = a broad pot for cooling and keeping beer; cinkuntu = for keeping solids; cibimbili = for keeping a portion of meal; luntanza = used as a dish; insambilo, cisambilo = for washing baby; muleu = for washing oneself; kasambi = for carrying things, such as salt. Cicelwa = a newly made pot but not yet burnt; mwaandu = a big pot covered with skin and used as a drum at certain dances.)
the nipple of the breast, e.g. Ooyu musimbi uzimbide inonso yakwe. = This girl has a swelling on her nipple.
vegetable bulbs eaten in November, e.g. *Inquaqua ilasyuuka ciindi cakumwaka.* = The *inquaqua* bulb germinates in the dry season.
vegetable bulbs eaten raw or cooked in March, e.g. *Inquibu lilanona.* = The *inquibu* bulb is tasty.
a kidney, e.g. Bacembele bayanda kuyoka *nsa yaņombe.* = The old woman wants to roast the kidney of a cow.
a vine, wild grapes, e.g. Amunzi twakasyanga *nsaansa.* = We planted vines in the village. Also musansa
a locust, a grasshopper, e.g. Bamwi bantu balalya *nsabaandwa.* = Some people like to eat grasshoppers. Also nsozi, insaabandwa, inswabanda, cenze.
the sabbath, (ety. Heb.) e.g. *Mu Nsabata tuyakukukombela baciswa.* = On the sabbath we are going to pray for the sick.

a fishing-net, e.g. *Insabwe antela tunyandi zyakasika ciindi cakasangana misyobo yabantu minji mucisi.* = The *insabwe* or *tunyandi* fishing nets arrived when many different tribes of people entered the territory. Also *insabwi*
a fishing-net, e.g. *Insabwi zyangu ziyandika kusumwa.* = My fishing nets need to be stitched.

the calf of the leg, e.g. *Ooyu musune ulaa nsafwu zipati.* = The calves of this ox's leg are big. *Kumweelede malanda kunsafu ankonokono kumikono.* = The fibre-leggings on the calves of her legs and the arm-bangles on her forearms suit her.
resin, sticky sap, e.g. *Insagazi ilalamatila kuzisani.* = Resin sticks to the clothes. Also insakazi.
size, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Nibakatalika kulwana bantu bakati, "Atubaleke aba, *ninsaizi baleelene*". When they began to fight the people said, "Let us allow these, they are of equal size. Also misela
forge, smithy, e.g. *Bataata bafwulila munsaka.* = My father forges at the smithy.
an open structure in a field, e.g. Niyakaboola mvwula, twakayusa *munsaka.* = When the rain came, we took shelter in an open structure in a field.

a tin or musical rattle beaten as an accompaniment to music or carried by a traveller to ward off evil spirits or to accompany his/her singing. e.g. Muka Moonga ulicizyi kuuma *nsaka.* = The wife of Moonga knows how to beat the musical rattle. Also nsakalala, muyuwa.
a musical rattle, e.g. Baimbi balauma ansakalala nobaimba. = Singers shake rattles when singing. Also insaka.
a cheerful person, e.g. Mainza ninsa*kalala*. = Mainza is cheerful.
bees which make honey outside the bark of a tree, e.g. *Tuyakukulida nsakayuni mucisamu*. = We are going to harvest honey from the bees in the tree. Also *insakakayuni*
the gum of the mubwabwa tree, e.g. *Insakazi nimbotu kuvwelenganya musili wamuntobolo*. The gum of the mubwabwa tree is good for mixing with gunpowder. Also *insagazi*

weeds, e.g. *Mumapopwe muyandika kulimina nkaambo nsaku zyavwula*. It is necessary to weed among the maize because the weeds are proliferating. Some kind of weeds: mulungwe, kampububu, kampubu, lubalukila.
a finger-ring, e.g. *Ndisamide nsale zyobile kuminwe*. I am wearing two rings on my fingers. Also *ntasa*
tattoo incisions, e.g. *Mubili wamulwazi ulijisi nsalunsalu nkobamuyasaula lyoonse*. The body of the patient has many tattoo marks where they were always making incisions.

a branding-iron, e.g. *Koleta insama tuumpe boombe bataningaumpwa*. = Bring the branding-iron so that we brand the calves who have not yet been branded. *Moyo wangu wakali kuyaka mbuli cisisi cansama*. My heart was on fire like the ember of a burning-iron.
a pot for washing the baby, e.g. *Insambilo yamwana yapwaika*. = The basin for washing the baby has been broken.

a pot for washing with traditional medicine, e.g. *Insambilo ncibiya nociba cipapa cibikkila micelo iisamba mwana kacili muvwanda kumukwabilila kumalwazi aasiyene-siyene mbuli masoto, cibele, camainza antela cabana, ntenga-ntenga aamwi manjaanji*. The *insambilo* is a pot or part of a calabash into which is put medicines to wash the child when still an infant to protect it from different diseases such as masoto, cibele, of the rain, of children, ntenga-ntenga and other many diseases.

a bracelet of grass, e.g. Komulukila *nsambo* mwana. = Weave a grass bracelet for the child. *Kulungula nsambo* to weave a braclet of grass; *insambo zyamalala* plaited rings of palm leaves *insambwa* strands of material, like flax or hemp, e.g. *Mudaala uyumwide nsambwa lyalubanje*. The old man was carrying strands of hemp.
calf of the leg, e.g. Musune wakayaswa keembe *ansamfwu*. = The ox was cut by an axe on the calf of the leg. Also *insafwu*
thin pieces of stick used in weaving fishing-baskets, e.g. *Ndiluka cisuwo cansamu*. = I am weaving a fishingbasket with thin pieces of sticks. Also *insongoono*
a round bullet, e.g. Muvwimi wakabelesya *insamvwu* kujaya muzovwu. = The hunter used a round bullet to kill the elephant. Also *inkulu*.
a rodent which digs perpendicular holes, e.g. *Tuyakukusya nsana mucindongwe*. We are going to dig rodents in the groundnut patch. Also *insangamuni*.

ability, e.g. Bantu banyina *nsana* abusongo bapenga omuno munyika. = People without ability and wisdom suffer in this world. Bantu zyakabamana *nsana* nkaambo eeci caano camapenzi cakabeenzya bulowa. These things dried up the energy of the people, because this story of suffering drained the blood.
a hammer, e.g. *Insando yandipwaya amunwe*. = The hammer struck my finger.

a bird's breast, e.g. Bataata bayanda kulya *nsando* yankuku. = My father wants insanga insangaazi insangamuni insangano insangayoka insangu insangwa insanka insansa insanse insanza insasi to eat the breast of a chicken. Also impaandwa salt, when it was used in the past for trade, e.g. Basambazi bakali kuulisya nsanga kaindi. = The traders were selling salt in the past. good grazing-grass, e.g. Insangaazi yakali kucela basune yakapya. = The good grazing-grass where the oxen were feeding got burnt. a rodent which digs in river beds, e.g. Tuya kukusya nsangamuni mumbali amulonga. We are going to dig rodents near the river. Also itaba, pl. mataba pl. of lusangano, an assembly, e.g. Bantu bansangano balaa muswaangano mupati kumwami mu Mujibelo. The churches are having a big meeting on Saturday at the chief's palace. a snake with a succession of white and black rings. (alleged to bring bad luck if you do not kill it on seeing it.) e.g. Beembela bakajaya nsangayoka ijilo. The herders killed a black and white ringed snake yesterday.
seeds of the musangu tree, e.g. nombe zilalya nsangu kapati. = The cattle eat the seeds of the musangu tree very much.
seeds, e.g. Ndakaula nsangu zyatantaacuulu kuli Haandulwe jilo. = I took rape seeds to Haandulwe yesterday.

persistence, (a riddle) Ndakajana kasimbi mumalundu: kukauma ndakauma pesi kukabweza kakankakila....Ninsangu. = I found a young girl in the hills; to beat her, I beat her, but to take her away I was unable (answer) rape seeds. (once rape seeds are planted they will always continue to grow on that spot.)

a flat basket, e.g. Ndali kukusambala nsangwa kudolopo. = I went to sell flat baskets to the town. Basimbi bakali kuyiisigwa kuluka nsangwa. = The girls were taught to weave flat baskets. Naakali kuciswa muntu kaindi twakali kubweza nsangwa yamaila twakali kuunka kumunanga kuya kumusonda. In the past when a person became ill we took a flat basket of millet, we went to the witchdoctor to divine the cause of the illness. Insangwa ntutumba tusyoonto ntobakali kupulila nsima bantu bakaindi lyakanyina mitiba. Insangwa are small baskets with which the people of the past used to distribute nsima.
a strainer made of long flexible shoots, e.g. Baama baluka nsangwa yakuminunuzya cibwantu. Mother is weaving a strainer for straining sweet-beer. Also lukwi

animal placenta, e.g. Niyakapandulwa mpongo, kwakajanika bulwazi mu nsangwa. When they cut open the goat, a disease in the placenta was found. a small basket of palm leaves, e.g. Mutinta wakaluka nsanka zyobilo. = Mutinta has woven two palm-leaf baskets. the back between the shoulder-blades, e.g. Chimuka ulizimbide ansansa. Chimuka is swollen between the shoulder-blades in the back. Also isansa. a spark, e.g. Cisani cangu cakadonkoolwa nsanse. My dress has been holed by sparks. Also insasi.
the south = kunsanza = kumusanza, e.g. Inombe zyali kuya kunsanza. The cattle were going southwards.

the part of the house furthest from the door = kunsanza, e.g. Mutumba wamuntu ubikkwa kunsanza. The corpse of a person is put in the part of the house furthest from the door. a spark, pl. insasi or masasi, e.g. Insasi zyamulilo zilakonzya kuumpa bwizu. Sparks of fire can burn the grass. Also insanse, insasamwenje.
a woman's scarf, e.g. Saliya wakalisamide *insasiko* mbotu ijilo. = Saliya wore a beautiful scarf yesterday.
decorations, e.g. Munanda omu muli *nsasiko*. = In this house there are decorations.
a boa-constrictor Also muceka
a striped rodent, Also simasaulu, insuulu

a narrow-mouthed calabash for oil, e.g. *Insazi* yavwula mafwuta ambono. = The narrow-necked calabash is full of castor-oil. *Insazi* ezi zyakajisi mafwuta akusambazya. = These calabashes had oils for washing with. Also impau
a grain of maize, e.g. Kondipa *nsece* yomwe yampopwe. = Give me one grain from the maize-cob. Also inseke
a hen, e.g. Ndijisi *nsece* zyobilo amukombwe omwe. = I have two hens and one cock.
a waterfly, e.g. Bana tabayoowi *insee*. = Children do not fear the waterfly.
flying ants, e.g. *Inseele* zilayanda kuulukila kumumuni wamagesi. = Flying ants like to fly towards the electric light. Also inswa.
a bracelet of grass, e.g. Kaindi basimbi bakali kusama *inseete* mumaboko. = Long ago girls were wearing grass bracelets on the arms. Also insambo.
a sieve, e.g. Buntele kobuseba *ansefwa*. = Sift the pounded groundnuts with a sieve. Also cisebyo
a cyst, e.g. Ooyu munene ulaa *nsefwu* agondo. = This old man has a cyst on his knee.

elands, pl. of musefwu, e.g. Nyama ya-*nsefwu* taitengwi, inga wabaa *nsefwu*. = One does not complain about elands meat, you may develop a cyst. Utume buyo mwana ambeyo andiletele *nsefwa* yakasina ndisebye busu. = Just send me
weeds
a non-laying hen, e.g. Ijilo *twakajaya nkuku nseke.* = Yesterday we killed a non-laying hen.
a seed, grain, pip, coarse grain left after pounding, e.g. *Inseke zyamapopwe twakazisyanga jilo.* = We planted maize seeds yesterday.
a water-snake, e.g. *Muziba motusamba twajana nsekela-meenda.* = We found a water-snake in the pool where we swim.
an iron part of a plough, e.g. *Insembi yajamba yamana kusenseluka.* = The plough is worn out by friction. Also *insimbi*
a bank or barrier of mud or clay in a river forming a small dam.
scent sold in shops, e.g. *Mukaule nsende yakununkilizya.* = Buy perfume.
a bank of mud or sand, e.g. *Ijeleele lyansende lyadilimuka.* = The cliff of mud and sand collapsed.
the verse of a hymn, e.g. *Nitwakamana kupaila twakaimba biyo insendu zyobilo.* = When we had finished praying, we sang just two verses of a hymn.
a large soft stick, e.g. *Sulwe wakatema insengele akukwabbaula suntwe.* = The hare cut a pliable stick and beat the hyena.

a good-luck charm of hollow sticks fastened on arm or waist, e.g. *Babbi mbubajata sunu basamide nsengo mu-zibuno.* = The thieves they caught today were wearing good-luck charms on their waists. Also *nsengo*
*kuya ansengwe* = to defecate, e.g. *Mutinta wakaleede a nsengwe nibakamubbida ncinga.* = When Mutinta went aside to relieve herself, they stole her bicycle.
corrugated iron sheeting, pl. masenke, e.g. Caanda campongo cakawumbwa ansenke. The goats shelter has been roofed with corrugated iron sheeting.
a mosquito, pl. mansenya, e.g. Kuli nsenya litukatazya muņanda notoona masiku. There is a mosquito which troubles us in the house when we are sleeping at night.
a cane-rat, e.g. Insenzi zyanjila mubwina. The cane-rats entered a hole. Also insezi, mukoswe.

an apron or skirt of strings used in dancing, e.g. Basimbi bakasyobola nsete zyabo amwido wansikili. = The girls oiled their dancing aprons with oil of insikili. Insete basimbi bakali kuzisama kungoma akuzipelu insiku. Long ago the girls were wearing skin-skirts in dancing the ngoma and zipelu. Insete azyalo zyakali kunanikwa cinkanda. The dancingskirts were also oiled with black traditional cream. Also maaya, cikanda.

an eland, e.g. Muvwimi wakajaya nsetu zyobilo. The hunter killed two elands. Also musefwu. insetukwa maanu ansetukwa = insight, e.g. Moomba wakabelesya nsetukwa. Moomba used intelligence to solve this problem.
a white head of cattle with red spots, e.g. Ndajana butanga bwarjombe zinseu. I found a herd of red-spotted cattle.
a species of wild cat, e.g. Ijilo twakajaya nsezi zyobile. Yesterday we killed two wild cats.
the ground, earth, e.g. Insi itakwe mudumu taizwisyi mapopwe. Land without moisture does not cause the maize to germinte.
clay for pottery mixed with powdered shards, what leavens clay for pottery, e.g. Kobikka insibo mukasuwo utole kumubumbi. Put the prepared clay in a basket and take it to the potter.
bed-bugs, e.g. Nsiinsini zindiluma nzindipa cilabila masiku onse. = The bed-bugs which bite me always give me sleepless nights. Also insinsini.

an eagle, e.g. Insika yazimana nkuku. The eagle has finished off the chickens. Nkuku ilalaya bana bayo mbubeelede kuyuba nsika niyasika. = The hen teaches her chicks how to hide when the eagle comes. Bana bansika abasyapipilyo balalya nyama yabana bankuku. = The young of an eagle and of black-shouldered kites eat the meat of chicks. Also musika
hiccups, e.g. Ndakali kuciswa nsikila. I was suffering from the hiccups. Also intiko.
the fruit of the musikili tree, e.g. Musikili uzyede nsikili zinji. The musikili tree bears much fruit.
deep purplish-red colour of an ox, e.g. Katowa uyandaula musune wainsikili-sikili.
is looking for the red ox. Also cisikili.
the past, e.g. Insiku bantu bakali kutolwa mubuzike. Long ago people were taken into slavery.
a big black warrior ant, (Megaponera Foetens) e.g. Mputwalede anze kuli nsilibi. = There were black ants where we were sleeping outside.

the stable food of cooked mealie meal, e.g. Insima yakwasa kale. = The nsima is already bubbling. (insima yandala = the nsima left over from the previous day; mukonde, ibyo = half-cooked nsima, cinkalantu, cikalanto, cigalananda = too dry, too stiff; Iwele, lucese thin; ceele = kneaded with relish; cuungabusu = too much meal in it; imbuye, imbuye-mbuye = without relish; mukangabisi = already minced but not yet cooked; *bukololo* = hard burnt parts.)
grass seed, e.g. *Inseke zyansima zyakasimpa nkabela zyakamena niyakawa mvwula.* = The grass-seeds were planted therefore they germinated when the rain fell.
the musk-cat or genet, a spotted wild cat, e.g. *Insimba nkanyama kaluma nkuku zipati.* The genet is a small animal which eats big chickens.
a piece of iron, e.g. *Insimbi yajamba yatyoka mumuunda.* = The blade of the plough broke in the field.
a clothes iron, e.g. Koya ukalombe *nsimbi* yakuccisizya zisani. Go and ask for an iron tp kiron the clothes.
a gong, e.g. Yalila kale *nsimbi* yakuti basicikolo banjile mucikolo. = The gong has already sounded so that the pupils enter the school. Also *mulangu*

incisions on skin for bloodletting, cicatrices, e.g. Mwana bakamuyasa *nsimbo* zyakumukwabilila bulwazi bwa-kasuntu. = They made incisions on the child's body to protect her from epilepsy. Ndayanda kukugoma-goma amubili wako nkuteme *tunsimbo* twacoolwe cakujana zilyo. = I want to prick your body to make small incisions for good-luck in finding food. Kumeso wakaligalangene kajisi *nsimbo* zinji kapati. = His face was ugly having many cicatrices. (*Inembo zyankwela* = sex tattoes) Also *inembo*, sing. *lulembo, insalusalu.*
poisonous prickly seed of low grass, e.g. *Cisani cangu cayaswa nsina.*
has adhered to my dress. Beembela bayaswa *nsina* musyokwe. = The herders are pricked by sharp grassseeds in the bush.
a common black active and biting ant, pl. *tusindabene*, e.g. *Insindabeene ntuuka tuluma.* = The black ants are insects which bite.
a tool for making barbs on spears, e.g. Basyaanene babamba masumo *ansindo.* = My grandfather is making barbs with an instrument.
pl. of *lusinga*, a nerve pain, e.g. Mukaintu uciswa *nsinga* mumenyo. = The woman is suffering from a pain in her teeth.
the neck, e.g. *Insingo yangu ilacisa.* My neck is sore.
a common cold, e.g. Mwanaangu uciswa *nsini.* My child is suffering from a cold. Also *isyini.* (When used as adverb it means 'different': Ooyu muntu uzyana cizyano
This person dances the dance in a different way.)

a bribe, hush-money, e.g. Mwana wakali kamboni wababbi bakamupa *nsinkamulomo* kutegwa ataambi camasimpe. = The thieves gave the child a bribe who was a witness against them so that she would not tell the truth.
the neck, e.g. *Insinko yangu ilacisa ncetacebi kabotu.* My neck is sore that is why I cannot look around easily. Also *insingo.*
a stalk dipped in milk and sucked, e.g. Bacembele banywa mukupa *ansinsa.* The old woman drinks milk with a straw.
a bed-bug, e.g. Munanda motoona kuli *nsinsini.* There are bedbugs in the house where we sleep. Also *insiinsini.*
grey grass-seeds which adhere to the clothes, e.g. *Insinya zyacilamatila cisani nindali kutebula.* When I was harvesting, grass-seeds stuck to my clothes. (blackjack) Also *insini, insina.*
a chisel for cutting iron, e.g. Koleta *nsinzo* tukosole luwaile. = Bring a chisel for cutting the wire. Also *insindo*
distances, pl. of *musinzo*, e.g. *Insinzo nzindakeenda kuyandaula basune nzilamfwu.* The distances were great over which I was searching for the oxen.
rays, e.g. Bantu bakali kusalama muzimvwule kuyusa *nsinzo zyazuba*. = People were just lying on their backs in the shade sheltering from the rays of the sun.
soap, e.g. Ndalomba *nsipa* yakusambya. = I am asking for soap to wash.

a hidden lover, e.g. *Insise* caamba 'musankwa wakunze' kuti mukaintu utumbuka kali kajisi musankwa ngubali kweenda limwi ciindi naalaa da, mukaintu ukonzya kumuka kutumbuka. = *Insise* refers to a hidden lover - if the pregnant woman has a lover, it may cause a delay at the time of delivery.
bed-bug, e.g. *Insisini* zilaluma ciindi camasiku. = Bed-bugs bite at night time. Also *insiinsini, insinsini*.
a traditional clay plate, e.g. Kamuzisanzya *nsiya* ezyo tulide. = Wash those plates so that we eat.
small fish, e.g. Bazeli bajaya *nsiya* zinji. = Those fishing killed many small fish.
crushed charcoal, a charcoal stain, e.g. Ndasiya *nsizi* mumaanza nindali kusanzya mpoto. = I left a charcoal stain on my hands when I was washing the pot.
a sharp grass-seed, e.g. Ndatoogwa *nsoce* muliso. = I was blinded in the eye with a sharp grass-seed. Also *insinya, insina*.
sharp, grey/black grassseeds, e.g. *Insoke* zyalamatila acisani cangu. = Sharp grass-seeds have stuck to my dress. Also *insinya, insina, insoce*
an oar, e.g. Mainza wakali kwasula ansoke mpati. Mainza was rowing with a big oar. Also *inkasi*
a stye in the eye, e.g. Mutinta ulaa *nsokweda* aliso. Mutinta has a stye in her eye. Also *insokweeda*.

a honey-bird, e.g. *Insolo* mmuyuni ukonzya kukutondezya kuli *nzuki* zyabuci. = The honey-bird is a bird which can show you where the honey-bees are. Bakamvwa *nsolo* kiilila. They heard a honey-bird chirping.
dewclaws, i.e. the inner claw which some dogs have, the false hoof of deer etc.
blueberries, the fruit of the *musombo* tree, e.g. *Insombo zyabizwa*. = The blueberries are ripe.
a mother who has given birth to her first child, a cow which has calved for the first time, e.g. *Inombe nsomona ilakatazya kukama*. = A cow which has calved for the first time is difficult to milk.
a big needle, e.g. Masaka waasumye *nsonde*. = Use a big needle for sewing the sacks.

a sharp point or edge, the top of grass, *insonga yamulaka* = the tip of the tongue. e.g. Ndazwa mate kunsonga yamulaka nindabona cakulya cibotu. = I saliviated on the tip of the tongue when I saw good food. Tokonzyi kukkala ansongaa masumo. = You cannot sit on the points of spears. Also *bucesi*
peak of the roof, e.g. *Insonge yaciluli yavwumbulwa kambizi*. = The peak of the roof was taken off by the whirlwind. Also *insonje*.
a descriptive name for sharp grass-seeds, e.g. Ndayaswa *nsongolwa-bayasenye*. = I have been pricked by sharp grass-seeds. Also *nsongolwa-bayanzene*.
thin sticks used in weaving fish-baskets, e.g. Tutema *nsongoono zyakulusya moono*. = Let us cut thin sticks for weaving fish-baskets.
a non-poisonous type of snake, (seeing one is said to bring good luck), e.g. Bana bajana *insongoyoka* kunsi abulo. The children saw a good-luck snake under the bed. Also *ingokoce*.
shame, embarrassment, e.g. Mudenda ulaa *nsoni kwaamba ncaatumwa.* = Mudenda is embarrassed to say what she was sent for.
the peak or apex of a traditional house or of a mountain, e.g. *Inanda izwizya ansonje.* = The house is leaking at the apex.

a mistake, an offence made by dying in a another's village for which a fine has to be paid, e.g. *Chigamba wakacita insontomokwa nkaambo wakaakufwida kumunzi wabantu.* = Chigamba was guilty of an offence because he died in the village of other people (i.e. he defiled the village by bringing death there.) Also *ingolomokwa*
a long line of people as in a procession. Also *milongo-milongo.*

the common locust, e.g. *Cisyu mumbewu camanwa nsozi.* = The relish in the garden has been finished by locusts. (*cigwigwi* = a swarm of locusts; *munamupezani* = jumps, doesn't fly; *insabaandwa* = has long thin legs)
air from anus, e.g. *Kuli wasula nsozi inunka.* = Some one has expelled stinking air from the anus.
the bladder, e.g. *Mucembele bakamupandula nsubilo.* = They operated on the old woman's bladder.
a percussion cap, the nipple of a gun, e.g. *Yakamucisa ntobolo nkaambo yakadubukila ansuka.* = The gun hurt him because it exploded at the nipple.
hair smeared with red ochre, e.g. *Masusu akamwale ngansuki.* = The hair of the female initiate is smeared with red ochre.

hair gathered into a cone, e.g. *Balombe abaalumi bakalibambila nsuku zyakusama amitwe amakaano akusama amakuko.* = The boys and men prepared hair-cones to wear on their heads and ornamental wooden axes to wear on their shoulders.
a calabash used as a churn, e.g. *Insuma bakayaanzika aciluli.* = They hung up the churn on the roof.
hooves, pl. of *lusumbwa*, e.g. *Musune wakalicisa nsumba.* = The ox hurt its hooves.
a childless man, an unmarried man, e.g. *Bunsumbalume bulapenzya kuti waciswa.* = A childless or wifeless man makes others suffer if he is sick. Also *inkungulume.*
an island, e.g. *Bwato bwesu buyakukwiimina munsi ansumbu.* = Our boat will stop beside the island. cf. *kaluzi*
a less destructive kind of white-termite, e.g. *Insumbwa tazinyonyooni mapopwe mumyuunda pe.* = The white-ant does not destroy maize in the field.
a spear Also *isumo*

a type of wild fruit, e.g. *Ziindi zyoonse basiņombe balalya micelo yamisyobo-syobo. Balalya nsumo, nsombo, nsibbi, mawi anundu.* = The herd boys eat fruits of different kinds. They eat *nsumo*, blueberries, *insibbi, mawi and nundu.*

a top-knot of hair, e.g. *Bamwi basankwa balayanda kusuwa insumpa.* = Some boys like to leave the top-knot growing. *Basankwa bakali kulekelwa kasusu amutwe kakali kutegwa insumpa antela inzumba, tiibakali kusakulwa mbuli bakaintu.* = Boys had some hair on the head left called a top-knot, they were not shaven completely like women.
a high or commanding tone, e.g. *Insumukilo yakasinsimuna bantu bakali koona.* = The high-pitched voice awoke the people who were sleeping.
a small needle, e.g. *Cisani camwana kocisuma ansunda.* = Stitch the baby's dress with a small needle.
a barren animal, e.g. *Ooyu mubwa ninsundi.* = This bitch is barren.
impudence, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa *nsundila*, ncaumwa lyoonse. = This child has an impudent manner, that is why it is always beaten.
a red variety of sorgum, e.g. Uuno mwaka mbanji bayanda kuyoolima *nsundwe*. = This year there are many who want to plant a red variety of sorgum.
a large loose head-dress or hood made of warm material, e.g. Ncibotu kusama *nsungale* ciindi campeyo. = It is good to wear a hood in time of coldness.
a hair-style, e.g. *Insunkununu* yamusankwa nimbotu kwiinda yamusimbi. = The hair-style of the boy is more beautiful than that of the girl.
apoplexy, a fainting-fit, e.g. Mucembele oyu uwa *nsuntu*. = The old woman has a fainting-fit. *kufwa ansuntu* = to die suddenly Also *cisuntu*.
a crowd, e.g. Ndakabona *nsuse* yabantu *ananda*. = I saw a crowd of people at the house. Also *impumba*
a calabash for milk or for churning, e.g. *Mabisi ali munsuwa alalula*. = The sour milk in the calabash is bitter.
amniotic fluid, (the fluid surrounding the innermost membrane that encloses the embryo)
big flying-ants, e.g. *Aabo bantu badinkila nswa*. = Those people have blocked the flying-ants from coming out.
grasshopper/locust with long thin legs, e.g. *Kuli bantu balya nswaabanda*. = There are people who eat grasshoppers. Also *insabaandwa*.
a file, e.g. *Kondikwengela*
answaile*. = Sharpen the axe for me with a file. Also *inswaili*

fish, e.g. *Tuya kukuzela nswi*. = We are going to net fish. *(-loba* = fish with a hook; *luswiswi* = small fish; *mubondo* = barbel, *impende* = bream; *isiko* = fish-trap; *moono* or *mungwala* = fishing-basket; *cizongo* = fishing-basket of wicker-work, plaited meshwire; *isyuta* = a reed fishing-basket; *lusabwi* = fishing-net; *nabuyuwa* or *munzenze* = fishing-net made of grass)
