a type of wild fruit, e.g. *Basimbi baya kukucela inswibba*. = The girls are going off to gather wild fruit.
a duiker, e.g. *Inyabo zyamanwa nsya*. = The beans have been finished off by a duiker. Also *nsya*
a diminutive seed like tobacco, e.g. *Insyangu zyatombwe zyatika*. = The tobacco seeds have spilt out.

seeds, e.g. *Mvwula yacivwunajombe yakamenezya nsyangwa zyakagankwa civwu ciyumu asyokwe lyakavwuna nombe, mpongo ambelele*. = The first rains caused the seeds which were preserved in the hard soil of the bush to germinate, which saved the cattle, goats and sheep.
the cartilage of the nose, e.g. *Insyono yangu ilizimbide*. = The cartilage of my nose is swollen. Also *moononono*.

a fruit used as a charm in hunting, e.g. *Wakabweza jamba wakaya kucibaka nkwaakabwene insyu. Wakasya mulindi. Wakalosya nsyu mumbali kuti mwiingile atazoocenjeli*. = He took a hoe and went to the place where he saw the magic fruit. He dug a hole. He dropped the magic fruit nearby so that the bushpig would become stupid.
the concluding marriage custom involving the drinking of beer and the reception of spears by the married couple, e.g. *Insyungu inga ibaanga njiigozya tupaapa toonse twakukwata kwa-*
aende*. = The *insyungu* ritual is the one which brought all the marriage traditions to completion for the people of Sicibende's day.
an edible root found in vleis, e.g. Bana basya nsyute mumusena. = The children are digging edible roots in the vlei. Also insyuto.
a bundle of spears, e.g. Kukaswi kananda kuli ntaala. = There is a bundle of spears in the corner of the house. Ntaala yamasumo mudaala wakaisowa. The old man lost the bundle of spears. Also intaama
a bundle of spears, e.g. Kazemba wakalijisi ntaama yamasumo naakali kulwana syuumbwa. = Kazemba had a collection of spears when he was fighting the lion. Also intaala.
a stride, step or pace, e.g. Ndaenda buyo ntaamo zisyoonto kuzwa munanda, mpoona nzoka yandiluma. = I went only a few steps from the house, thereupon a snake bit me.
a stride; kubikka ntaamu = to place on the ground between legs. Also intaamo, intambiko.
the fourth stomach of ruminants, e.g. Naakamana kufwunda munyama wakayoka ntaba. = When he had finished skinning the animal he roasted the fourth stomach.
a glut, abundance intabi branches, pl. of mutabi, e.g. Mukagonke buyo ntabi zyobile zyamutumbi. = Only cut two branches from the mutumbi tree.
a flea, e.g. Ooyu mubwa camukosya nintabwa. = It is fleas which has made this dog thin. Also intatabwa, intantabwa.
a crocodile, e.g. Umwi muzeli walumwa ntale mumulonga. = One fisherman was attacked by a crocodile in the river. Also ciwena
a pipe with a long reed stem, e.g. Bamacembele bamu Zambezi bafwebela muntale. The older women of the Zambezi smoke the long reed stemmed pipe.
the iron binding at the end of a spear shaft, e.g. Intale iizambidwe asumo yakosoka. The binding on the shaft of the spear broke.
cotton thread, e.g. Ndilomba ntali zyakusumya. I am asking for cotton thread for sewing.
bees-wax, e.g. Intalo ilayaaya kuti zuba lyabala. = Bees-wax melts if the sun shines. Also bunzuka.
a big wild orange, e.g. Ndawa nindali kucela ntamba mujulu. = I fell down when I was collecting big wild oranges.
a stride, e.g. Intambiko zyako nzifwaafwi. = Your strides are short. Also intaamu.
a strap, belt, or thong, e.g. Mudaala usuka ntambo zyakwaanzya basune. The old man is softening thongs for tying oxen.
a twig which holds the kabulindi trap in place. Also intano.

the morning star, e.g. Intanda niyazwa ndabukide kale. When the morning star appeared I had already arisen. Meso akwe akaile kusalala mbuli ntanda yakubucedo. His eyes were shining like the morning star.
a peg releasing a trap, e.g. Kooye kalebuka niyalekezya ntanda. = The trap springs when the peg is released.
the name of a Tonga newspaper, e.g. Makani aya ndakaabala mupepa lya Intanda. I read about that matter in the Intanda newspaper.
the foot of the bed, e.g. Intandabilo yabulo yadenuka. The foot of the bed has become detached.
a herd, e.g. Chooka ubinga intanga yampongo. Chooka is driving a herd of goats. Also itanga.
a pumpkin seed, e.g. Mukasyange nta nga mumuunda wanu. You should sow pumpkin seeds in your field.
a boy's dormitory, e.g. *Muntanga* yabasankwa kuli tombe. = There is dirt in the boys dormitory.
the most open and cleanest place in the open courtyard, e.g. Sunu ndalede *antangalala*. = Today I was lying in the open courtyard.
an interval, a distance between two, e.g. Imwi minzi iyakidwe *muntantaano*. = Some villages are built with a space between them.

space between objects, e.g. Kwakali mwaalumi wakakwete bakaintu bobile, nkabela bakakkede *ntantaanwa*. Long ago there was a man who had two wives, however they lived a distance apart. Baalumi bakalya abana babo basankwa acipala cabo, bakaintu babo a bana babo basimbi bakalya *ntantaanwa*. Men ate with their sons at the male place; their wives and daughters ate a distance apart.
a tiny tampan which infests poultry, e.g. Inkuku zyakanjililwa *ntantabwa*. = The chickens are infested by tampans. Also *intabwa*.
a hereditary disease, e.g. Bulwazi *bwantanta-mukowa tabumani mumukowa*. = The hereditary disease does not end in the clan.
a twig which holds the kabulindi trap in place. e.g. Koleta *ntano* tuteye banyama. Bring a twig so that we trap animals. Also *intanano*.
a small stick tied to a string in the indiba trap, e.g. *Intanyotyanyo* yatyoka nilyalebuka idiba. = The small stick broke when the trap was sprung.
dregs of liquid, e.g. Inkuku amuzipe *ntapitapi* zyazwa mubukoko. = Give the chickens the dregs of the beer. Also *busiwa*.
a finger ring, e.g. *Banabukwetene bali kusamikana ntasa*. = The married couple were putting rings on each others fingers. Also *inwenwe*

a flea, e.g. Inkuku zilaciswa nkaambo zyakalumwa *ntatabwa*. = The chickens are sick because they have been bitten by fleas. Also *intabwa*. *intaule* (ety. Eng.) a towel or scarf, e.g. Kosama *ntaule* kumutwe utabiji
Put a towel on your head so that you are not made dirty with dust.
persistence, intransigence, e.g. *Intaze* iletela mapenzi. = Intransigence brings problems. Also *nkazi*.

pl. of lutebe, a bag made of bark or bundle of grass for carrying food, e.g. Beenzuma bakaunka kuli nguwe zona bakaleta *ntebe* yazyakulya = Our friends who went to him the day before yesterday brought a bag of assorted foods. (note. *ntebe* as adverb meaning underneath, e.g. Sinzala naakabona beenzu, wakasisa nsima *muntebe*. = When the hungry one saw visitors, she hid the nsima underneath.)
a bracelet of grass, e.g. Basimbi basunu tabacizyi kubamba *intebya*. = Girls of today do not know how to make bracelets of grass.
clay sticks used in the traditional kwaama game, e.g. Basimbi babelesya *intela* mucisobano cakwaama. = Girls use clay sticks in the traditional game called kwaama.
upper part of legs, thighs, e.g. Akaambo kakuciswa wakaakwiide kusyaazya *ntelebalo* kukoka. = She just remained with very thin thighs because of the sickness.
a metal mould for bullets, e.g. Bataata bayaayizya *ntelo* yakubambya nkulu. My father is melting iron to make a mould for bullets.
a clearing made in the forest for a new field, e.g. Sunu tuya kukulima *ntema*. = Today we are going to plough a new field. Also inteme
a woman's apron, e.g. *Intembe njasamide taisalali pe.* = The apron which she is wearing is not clean.
a clearing made for a new field, e.g. *Basankwa baya kukugonkolola nteme.* = The boys are going to cut trees down to clear a place for a new field. Also intema.
danger, accident, e.g. *Intenda zyamumugwagwa zyavwulisya mazubaano.* = Traffic accidents are very frequent nowadays.
a footprint, pl. matende, e.g. *Ndabona ntende zyamuntu mumuunda wangu.* = I saw the footprints of a person in my field.
a type of fruit, e.g. *Intendele ilakola, tailigwi.* The intendele fruit is poisonous, and is not eaten.

a type of fruit, (unidentified) e.g. *Basimbi bacela ntenge, nsamba mantambwa amanego cilimo, mupeyo bacela ntumbulwa a micelo imwi. Kumwaka balya masuku naabizwa.* = In the dry season the girls harvest the fruits, *ntenge,*
andgo,* in the cold season they gather *ntumbulwa* and other fruits. In the growing season they eat *masuku* fruit when it is ripe. Also *ncenje*
a haircut style, e.g. *Wakafwuma kuyundwa akunyoolwa ntengu alunyoolo.* = He set off early for a haircut and to be shaved with a razor in a special style.

a type of bird, the small white-breasted starling, e.g. *Mwana weenena muyuni ntengwa.* = The child spied a bird, the white-breasted starling. '*Intengwa mubili, busungu buli mucamba.*' = As small in body as a starling, but there is determination in the heart.
fresh meat, e.g. *Munene wakali kwiide kumweta-mweta mbuli muntu wabona ntente.* = The old man was just smiling like a person who has seen fresh meat. Also *intete*

intesy = to placate by offering a gift; *mali aantesyamoyo* = a subsidy or grant, e.g. *Baama bakaleka kunyema nibakapegwa ntesyamoyo.* = My mother ceased being angry when she was given something to placate her.
a short stick in a trap, e.g. *Koleta ntezyo tuteye bayuni.* = Bring a short stick so that we trap birds.
a type of bird, the small flycatcher, e.g. *Mwana wajaya kantiinga mumusamu.* = The child killed a small bird in a tree. Also *intiiti.*
the robin or waxbill, also *intiinga.*
plaits of hair, braids, tufts, e.g. *Basimbi bayanda kubambwa intiki.* = Girls like to have their hair plaited.
hiccups, e.g. *Intiku mbulwazi bupenzya.* = Hiccups is a disease which can cause distress. Also *insikila.*

strings of beads, e.g. *Basimbi bakali kuyanda intilani kaindi.* = Long ago girls liked strings of beads. (*Basimbi bakalongela tukuze, makwambe, ntilani, makwaza, buswani, makobekobe, zisita zyabulungu, basimbilu, basyaacikwaakwa azisamo zyacipaale zimwi muzitwida.*)
strips of palm used for sewing, e.g. *Intima yamalala nzibotu kuluka zisuwo.* = Strips of palm are good for weaving baskets.
heart or innermost centre of the wood of a tree, e.g. *Intima yamubanga ninjumu nta.* = The heart of a *mubanga* tree is very hard.
mire/mud, e.g. *Loozi ndalunyika muntimba.* = I have soaked the fibre in the mud. *Wakajana kalonga kakajisi ntimba inji.* = He found a stream which had a lot of mud.
a quiver of arrows, e.g. _Basankwa basunu tabacizyi kubamba intimbwa._ = The boys of today do not know how to make a quiver.
a tuber, pl. bantinde, e.g. Basankwa basobana tinde mumusena. = Boys are playing with a tuber in the vlei. Also intindi.
the bulb of a plant, e.g. Basankwa basya ntindi mumulundu. = Boys are digging tubers on the hill. Also intinde.
a traditional game in which sharp sticks are thrown at a tuber, e.g. Basankwa basobana _ntindi_ mumusena. = The boys are playing a game of _intindi_ in the vlei.

a root used as famine food (when the bark is removed and the roots are soaked for 5 days, then pounded and cooked with pod pulp of Tamaindus indica. Root chips are used as fish poison. The wood is cut by children into footballs. (Neorautanenia sp.) e.g. Miyanda yantindili yakali kuligwa myaka yanzala. = The roots of the _intindili_ plant were eaten in years of famine.
a creeper whose root is used to subdue bees. = Inzuki zyakolwa _ntindili_ tazilumi pe. = Bees sated with the _intindili_ creeper do not sting.
the narrow waist of a hornet, e.g. Iganko lilinengetede _antingi_ yalyo. = The hornet is narrow at its waist.
sound made when water is hit with hollowed palm of the hand, e.g. Basimbi bamwi basunu cilaala koonse akuuma _ntinta._ = Some girls of today are unable even to clap the water.
a lynx, (any of various wild members of the cat family), e.g. Babwa bangu bajata _intobelaceye._ = My dogs have caught a lynx. Also kanga lubuwo, intobelabauya.
a shield, e.g. Bantu balwana a-masumo balikwabilizya _ntobo._ = People fighting with spears protect themselves with shields.

a gun, e.g. Ndijisi _ntobolo_ yakuvwimya. = I have a gun for hunting with. (Buta = trigger guard; moola = trigger; mululi = barrel; cipani = hammer; insuka = nipple; idala = spring; itako = stock. Intobolo lyacifwefwe = shot gun; intopesi = gun-cap; buunga = gunpowder)
a railway repair-waggon, e.g. Muntu weendela _antololi_ munjanji inga kali mubotu wiinda Mazuba kwaciindi eci. = A man working on a railway repair-waggon is better off than Mazuba during this time.
a cylindrical cooking pot, e.g. Tumbuwa mutubambile _muntolomani._ = Make buns in the pot. Bakajika _muntolomani_ musozya wakulya munzila. = They cooked the samp in a pot for eating on the way.
jail, e.g. Bantu bakabba moombe waba Mweemba bali _muntolongo._ = The people who stole Mr. Mweemba's calf are in prison.

smallpox, e.g. Kwakasika bu-Iwazi _bwantomba._ = There came the disease of smallpox. Syantongole wakabatabukizya _ntomba_ beenzinyina bakaceede mumunzi mwa Nanjina. = Syantongole infected his friends who remained in the village of Nanjina with smallpox.
a lizard, e.g. _Intombela_ uyotela zuba mukkota. = The lizard is warming itself on the verandah.
a bin made of bark, e.g. Bacembele bagusya maila _muntombo._ = The old women have taken maize from the bin. Also cikooko, ikkooko.
tail of a lion.
penis, (taboo word) e.g. Muntu wakazimbide _ntoni_ wakafwa jilo. = The man with a swollen penis died yesterday.
nipple of a gun, e.g. Intoni yantobolo taili kabotu pe. = the nipple of the gun is not correct. Also moola wantobolo.
a toy village, e.g. Bana basobana kuntoombwa. Children play in the toy village.
a long pointed stick used as a spear in games. e.g. Kamuleta intoomwa tutalike kusobana. Bring a long stick so that we begin to play. Also kazonde, munzonde, munzoogwa, intuntulwa.
a percussion cap, explosive material, e.g. Kujaya nswi antopesi cipa mulandu. Killing fish with explosives makes one guilty of an offence.
the sound made by clicking, cracking the fingers, e.g. Mwiinga naali koolola minwe kwali kulimvwisya ntosi. = When Mwiinga was clicking his fingers the sound could be heard clearly.
vagina, (taboo word) e.g. Musimbi wakaumwa uzimbide ntoto. = The vagina of the girl who was beaten is swollen.

saliva after exertion or during sleep, e.g. Mwana wali kuzwa ntovwolomo naali koona. Saliva was coming from the child's mouth when it was sleeping. Aa ino nkali kaambo awa kazwisilwa ntovwolomu? = What was the matter which brought forth the froth? (What made you so angry?) Also intovwulomo, intovwolomu.
froth from mouth, e.g. Naali kubetekwa walikuzwa ntovwulomo kumulomo. When he was being tried froth was coming out of his mouth. Also intovwolomo.
the fourth dice thrown during divination, e.g. Munanga wakabelesya intuba. The witchdoctor used the forth dice. Also inkakata.

dried, dust-covered or whitened skin, e.g. Bamwi bantu balijisi intuba itamani nobanana mafwuta. = Some people have dried up skin even though they apply oil. Bana basobana mutwe balaa ntuba kusikila basanzigwa abamanyina. Children who play in ash become white until their mothers wash them. intube white blotches on skin left from work or play, e.g. Bamwi bana bakali kunanikwa mafwuta mubili onse kubombya ntube. Some children were smeared with oil all over the body to soften the hard patches on the skin.
death in childbirth, e.g. Bamuka Chiyaba bakafwa ntubukila. = The wife of Chiyaba died in childbirth. Also intumbukila.
the fist, e.g. Kovwunga ntuku. = Make a fist. Kolwanya ntuku = Fight with the fists. "Also inkonye.
steak of meat without bone; cikantizi = steak of meat with the bone.
white-faced owl, e.g. Kuti ntuku-ntuku yalilila aciluli cananda, mmalweza. If a white-faced owl cries on the roof of a house, it is an evil omen.
a fillet of steak, a joint of boneless meat, e.g. Amunditendele ntuli yanyama. Cut me a fillet of steak

a feeling of sudden fright, emotion, panic, e.g. Ndamvwa ntulu nindamvwa kufwa kwa Namoonga. = I got a shock when I heard about the death of Namoonga. Ndakaba antulu naandikonga syuumbwa. I was in panic when the lion frightened me. Zyaakabona masiku alya zyakamupa ntulu. The things he saw that night gave him a fright. Ntulu zyakali kulibonya kumeso akwe. = Signs of shock were to be seen in his eyes.
a hat, e.g. Sincinko usamide ntulu iizapukide mumutwe. The mad person is wearing a torn hat on the head.
sudden stimulation of the heart, e.g. Nintulusya moyo buyo. It just makes the heart beat fast.
a dish of osier work, a small basket, e.g. Kondinyamuzya ntumba yabusu. = Help me lift the basket of meal.

dishes, e.g. Bina Chaalama bakasyibingana kuyobolola ntumba ooyu mukaintu atababoni kuti bakaliuside. The mother of Chaalama kept herself busy collecting dishes so that this other woman did not notice that she was sad.
the fruit of the mutumbi tree, e.g. Tuyuni tulya ntumbi. The little birds are eating ntumbi fruit.
a suckling female animal, e.g. Ngulube ntumbu yafwa nzala. = The sow died from hunger. Or The sow is hungry.)
the death of a woman or female animal in giving birth, e.g. Mukwaale wakafwa ntumbukila. = Mukwaale died giving birth. Also intubukila

a plumb, e.g. Bayuni balaziyanda ntuumbulwa zibizwide. Birds love ripe plumbs. Milomo nkujana yaakwiide kutuba buu unakuti kuli wali kulya ntuumbulwa zikwange. = His mouth was very white as if he had been eating unripe plumbs. =
the hump on a beast, e.g. Mucende ulaa ntunda mpati. = The bull has a big hump. Also inunu.

pride, (in positive sense) e.g. Ndakabaa ntunda mwanaangu naakapasa Giledi 1. = I was proud when my child passed Grade 1. Naakabona kuti bana bakwe bakakkede kabotu mumaanda abo, mudaala wakabaa ntunda. = When he saw that his children were living well in their homes, the old man was proud. Also matunta.
pride, (in negative sense) e.g. Wakabaa ntunda. He became full of himself. Kwakaba kumupa ntunda. = It only gave him pride.
languages, e.g. Ndicizyi kwaambaula ntundu zinji. I know how to speak many languages. Also milaka
heavy loads, e.g. Zyandilemena ntundu zyabacembele. I found the luggage of the old woman very heavy.
nakedness, e.g. Kulala intundubwi to sleep uncovered. e.g. Atubaulile payi bacembele boona antundubwi. Let us buy a blanket for the old woman who sleeps uncovered. Also cinswe, mutundulu.

a biting maggot, red fly, e.g. Ansi mpotoona kuli ntunga. = There are maggots on the ground where we sleep. Intunga zyali kubaluma akubasipa malowa abo. The insects were biting them and sucking their blood. Also cuumba.

a poisonous tuber which can be eaten when it is washed and boiled, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kuzisungulula ntungulu kutegwa zitabakoli. The people of long ago used to prepare the ntungulu tuber so that it would not poison them.
a structure without a roof, e.g. Kumantoombwa nkwaali matungu, nintuntu. At the mantoombwa (training period for children) there are many structures, they are roofless. Also intuuntu
a bitter kind of fruit, e.g. Amuleke kunyeela ntuntulwa. = Stop chewing the bitter fruits.
a stomach swollen with water, e.g. Ndanywa meenda manji aboobo ndabaa ntuntumeenda. = I drank much water and so I had a swollen stomach.
trembling from shock, e.g. Chilonde naakamvwa kuti bausyi balumwa syuumbwa, wakabaa intuntwa. When Chilonde heard that his father was attacked by a lion, he trembled. Also ntulu
a banded mongoose, e.g. Nitwali kuweza twajana intununu ilalwana anzoka mpati. = When we were hunting we found a banded mongoose fighting with a big snake.
a small needle, e.g. Mukanduulile ntunzyo. Buy me a small needle.
luggage, e.g. *Intuta* yakali kulema. = The luggage was heavy. Also cibbutu, cindundi, cindinduli.
a giraffe, e.g. *Intutwa* ilya buluba mumisamu milamfwu. = The giraffe eats flowers from tall trees.
a wild fruit, e.g. Milomo nkujana yaakwiide kutuba buu unakuti kuli wali kulya *ntuumbulwa* zikwange. = His lips were found to be just white as if he had being eating unripe wild fruits.
a roofless structure, e.g. Basankwa bakayaka *ntuuntu* kumantoombwa. = Boys build roofless structures at the mantoombwa training game. Also intuntu, mantoombwa.
long pointed sticks used by children as spears when playing, e.g. Basankwa bayasa ntinde *antuuntula*. = Boys pierce the tuber with long pointed sticks. Also intoomwa, inzonde.
a cultivated edible root, e.g. Bataata bakamana kale kulimina *intwanga. = My father has finished weeding the *intwanga* root crop.
grinding of the teeth = kulya *intwakubili*, e.g. Muntu uli mumapenzi uluma *ntwakubili*. = A person in affliction grinds the teeth. Also intwino.
a trouble-maker, e.g. Ooyu muntu ni*ntwakubili*. = This person is a troublemaker.
a precocious child, e.g. Ooyu mwana *nintwantwaantwa, uyookomena kabotu. = This child shows signs of exceptional qualities, it will develop well. Also mpana, mpanu-mpanu.

smartness, elegance, e.g. Akaambo kantwantwaantwa Chimuka wakali kuyandwa basimbi. = Because of elegance Chimuka was loved by women. Nabulongo yakali *ntwantwaantwa* yamukaintu. = Nabulongo was an elegant lady. Also intwaantwa, indwaandwa
a rumour, e.g. Ndakamvwa *intwiintwi* akuti mwami uyakuswaya munzi wesu juunza. = I heard a rumour that the chief will visit our village tomorrow. Also intwiitwi, mavwambukila
rumour, whisper, talk, e.g. Banyina bakaimwa *ntwiitwi* kuti mwanaabo musankwa wakasika ku Mutanda. = His mother heard it said that her son had reached Mutanda. Also intwiintwi
grinding the teeth, e.g. Jesu akuboola, babi bayooluma *ntwino*. = When Jesus comes, evil-doers will grind their teeth. Also intwakubili.
See intwino.
a giraffe, e.g. *Intwiza* icela buluba. A giraffe grazes on flowers. Also intutwa.
a poison (arsenic, introduced by Europeans), e.g. Mwida mwangu mucisa mbuli kuti ndalya *ntyefwu*. = I have stomach pains as if I have eaten arsenic. Also ncefwu.
a young tender shoot, e.g. Minsonje yamapopwe icili *ntyubuka*. = The shoots of the maize are still tender.
the back, e.g. *Inuma* yamwana ilizimbide. = The back of the child is swollen. Also musana.
a type of fruit, e.g. Tuya kukucela *nunda* kumuunda. = We are going to gather wild fruit in the field. Also *inundu*
a small round wild fruit, dark in colour when ripe, sweet to taste, with seeds. e.g. Twakajana *nundu* musyokwe zyaliiba kupya. We found *nundu* fruit in the bush which were ripe.
a joint or knuckle of a finger, e.g. Kuli kalonda *anunga* yamunwe. = There is a little sore on the knuckle of the finger. (joint of knee = ingo, ingongozu)
a porcupine, e.g.: *Inungu* ninkali kapati kubabwa. A porcupine is very fierce towards dogs. cf. cinungwe, caminungwe. (a quill = munungu)
a bead, e.g. Balwazi amubatungile nungu. = Thread the beads for the patients.
the hump, e.g. *Inunu* yamucende warjombe nimpati. = The hump of a bull is big. Also ntunda.
a finger-ring, e.g. *Inweenwe* yamukaintu wangu yazimina. = The ring of my wife is lost. Also intasa, insale.
beans, e.g. Sunu tulajika *nyabo* zyakulisya. = Today we are going to cook beans as relish.
crushed beans prepared as relish, e.g. Bacembele bajika *nyabo-nyabo*. = The old woman is cooking crushed beans for relish.
a giant edible mushroom (appears in December), e.g. Mumwezi wa Nalupale notulya *nyabo-nyabo*. In the month of December we eat big mushrooms. Also bowananda.
meat, e.g. Bamwi tabalyi nyama yampongo nkaambo babaa cigwenyembe mumutwe. = Some people do not eat goats meat because they develop a head skin-disease.
frowns, wrinkles on the forehead, e.g. Ndaswaanganya bamadaala balaa *nyandingene*. = I met with old men who had wrinkles on their foreheads. Also minya.
beans, e.g. Inkuku zyazimana *nyangu mubutala*. = The chickens have finished off the beans in the grain-bin.
a whale, e.g. *Inyangumi*
mulwaanje. = The whale lives in the sea.
onions, e.g. Mubikke *nyanisi* mucisyu. = Put onions in the relish.
the green scum on stagnant water, e.g. Meenda ali mucikala alaa *nyanzabili*. = There is scum on the water in the well.
the colour green, e.g. Cisani cangu *ncanyanzabili*. = My dress is green.
a buffalo, e.g. Kuweza *nyati* iiyasidwe nkucenjela. = One needs to take care when hunting a wounded buffalo.
a musical horn/flute used in budima dancing, e.g. Bazyana budima bali kulizya *nyeele*. = The budima dancers were playing flutes.
a needle, an injection, e.g. Ndayaswa *nyeleti* amunwe. = I was pricked by a needle on the finger.
a precocious child, e.g. Musankwa oyu *ninyembe-nyembe*. = This boy is quick to develop in ability. Also intwantwaantwa.
groundnuts, e.g. Kotwa *nyemu* zyabuntele. = Pound groundnuts into a mash.

beans or peas, e.g. Ku Dindi mbanji bantu balima *nyemu-mbwiila*. = In the Gwembe Valley there are many people who plant groundpeas. *inyemumbwiila* groundpeas, e.g. Musozya oyu ngwanyemumbwiila. = This samp is mixed with groundpeas.
a manner of walking, e.g. *Inyendelo* yamwana ulya nimbi. = The way that child walks is bad.
a type of bird, the cattleegret, e.g. *Inyengeene* ziyanda kukkala munsi arjombe. = Cattle-egrets like to live near cattle. Also lukobo, inkobo.
a furnace for smelting, e.g. Muzibikke *munyengelezi* kutegwa ziyaaye. = Put them in a furnace so that they melt.
a star, e.g. *Inyenyezi* tazilibonyi akaambo kamakumbi. = The stars are not seen because of the clouds.

a cicada, e.g. Cilimo *nyenze* zilalila kapati sikati. = In the dry season the cicadas make a lot of noise during the daytime. Imvwula ilawa, *nyenze* zilalila kumasamu. = When the rain falls the cicadas chirp in the trees. *Inyenze* zyakalila cakusinka matwi. = The cicadas were crying so as to deafen the ears. Also inzenze.
the earth/land/ground, e.g. *Inyika* yoonse bantu balafwa. = Throughout the world people die.
*kunyika* = to the north, e.g. Basune bako bagama *kunyika*. Your oxen are heading northwards.
pl. of Iwiimbo, a song, e.g. Eezi *nyimbo* zya Leza nzibotu. = These hymns are good.
mother of an animal, e.g. Ooyu moombe *nyina* yakafwa. The mother of this calf has died.

pl. of Iwiindi, a fist, blow with fist, e.g. Basankwa kurjombe bali kuumana *nyindi*. = The boys were beating one another with fists when herding cattle. Baumana *nyindi* ziyoosya. They beat one another with fierce blows.
a bangle of bone or ivory, e.g. Kaindi basimbi bakali kusama *inyinga*. = In the past women wore bangles of ivory. Also inkaya.
a type of bird, the black dove, e.g. Nangulu wakaca *inyingu* mukooye kakwe. Nangulu caught a black dove in his snare.
an electric eel, e.g. Utajati *inyinsi* nkaambo ulalebuka maboko. = Do not catch an electric eel because you will be paralysed in the arms.

a leather strap for fixing assegai, the iron binding at the end of a spear shaft, e.g. Wakamujana muvwimi kakankamina *nyinza* asumo lyakwe. = He found the hunter fixing the leather strap to his spear.
the anus and rectum, e.g. Mwana ulalila nkaambo ulaa cicisa *anyo*. = The child is crying because it has a sore at the rectum. Also inio, muzindo.
the nipple of the breast, e.g. *Inyonso* yabaama ilaa cicisa. = The nipple of my mother's breast has a sore.
kuti nkolo zyakwe zyakali kusiya kapati kutunyonso. = She found that her breasts were very dark at the little nipples. Also inonso.
clay rolled into the shape of a stick by children, used in the traditional kwaama game. e.g. Bana babumba *nyonga*. Children mould clay sticks.
the queen of a species of termite, e.g. *Inyoola* ikkala muguku. = The queen termite lives in a big hole under the termite hill.
thirst, e.g. Ndamvwa/ndafwa *nyota*, amundaabile meenda. = I feel thirsty / I am dying of the thirst, give me water.
the sting of a bee, e.g. Inzuki nzikali zilaluma cakufwa *anyudu* zyazyo. = Bees are fierce, they sting to the death with their stings. Also lubole.
black burnt grass, e.g. Suntwe wayuba *munyumbi* yasyokwe lyapya. = The hyena is hiding in the black burnt grass.
a hammer, sledge hammer, a hammer used as an anvil, e.g. Ndalipwaya *nyundo* amunwe. = I have smashed my finger with a hammer.
pumpkin seed, e.g. Njandaula *nyungu* zyakusyanga. I am looking for pumpkin seeds to plant.
a lion's or zebra's mane, e.g. *Inzagala* yasyuumbwa ilayoosya. = The mane of a lion is frightening. Also inzangala, ingala.

hunger, e.g. Uuno mwaka kuli *nzala* mucisi. = There is hunger in the country this year. Muziindi zyanzala njina yamunanga yakali kumutondezya mabazu akajisi zyakulya. During famine times the louse of the witch-doctor showed him the places where there was food.
a long piece of wire coiled around the wrist, e.g. Kuli bakandibbida *nzambe* yakukwaanza. Someone has stolen my wire-bangle.
a lion's mane, e.g. Kuti syuumbwa wanyema, _nzangala yaimikila._ = When a lion is angry, his mane stands up. Also _inzagala, ingala._
hollow grass, used for sucking liquids, e.g. _Ndakabelesya inzeka kusyuunta buci mukankuli._ = I used a straw of hollow grass to suck up the honey in the gourd. Also _impoolwe_
wandering, e.g. _Inzelengo yamusimbi oyu imutola kubuvwuule._ = The wandering of this girl leads her into prostitution. Also _izeleembo_
grey millet with a long stem, finger-millet, e.g. _Imwi misyobo ilalima nzembwe kapati._ = Some tribes are fond of sowing grey millet.
a large soft tick, e.g. _Mubwa ulaa nzengele zinji mumatwi._ = A dog has many ticks in it's ear. Also _inzengene_
a tick, e.g. _Inzengene zileta bulwazi bwadenkete kunombe._ = Ticks bring 'corridor disease' to cattle. Also _inzengele, insengele, imoola_ (striped); _bandama_ (small)
cicada, e.g. _Inzenze zilila nokupya kapati._ = The cicadas sing when it is very hot.

a fly, pl. _inzi_ and _inzinini,_ e.g. _Ciindi camainza kuli nzi zinji._ = During the rains the flies abound. (_Imbuwo_ = blind fly; _inguluzi_ = small cattle fly; _izimbwa_ = big cattle fly; _idumambizi, pl. malumambizi_ = hippo fly; _luuka or siluuka_ = tsetse fly; _kasusuli_ = sand fly)

a dove, a small pidgeon, e.g. _Insiyalukosi ninziba isika mainza._ = The insiyalukosi dove is a dove which comes in the rainy season. e.g. _Tuteya nziba kumuunda._ = We are trapping doves in the field. _Inziba kunyina niiya kulila mbuli nkanga._ = A pidgeon will never cry like a guinea-fowl. **inziba lungu/bulungu** = a small dove (There are three types of dove: sibulale, insiyalukosi and imombo.)
an edible grass, e.g. Edible grass-seeds are boiled as a cereal in Feb. e.g. _Inzibaiba ilaligwa abantu mumwezi wa Mulumi._ = The inzibaiba grass is eaten by people in the month of February.
path, way, e.g. _Inzila iiya kumulonga nindamfwu._ = The way to the river is long.
sugar-cane, e.g. _Eezi nzimbe ziyandika kwaangwa kutegwa zinyamunike._ = These sugar canes need to be tied so that they become transportable.
a big cattle-fly, e.g. _Kwanyikila nzimbwa mumeenda._ = A big cattlefly dropped in the water.
a heavy fall, e.g. _Walo nkulipwaila nzinga ansi._ = He himself jumped and smashed himself with a heavy fall.
cock, e.g. _Inzingini yangu yafwa._ = My cock died. Also _mukombwe._
a game with spinning tops, e.g. _Basimbi basobana inzingulukata._ = The girls are playing with spinning tops. Also _inzungulukata._
a fly, e.g. _Inzinini nzinji amunzi mpobakama._ = There are many flies at the village where they are milking. cf. _inzi._
a part of the body, e.g. _Inzo zyakwe zyoonse zilacisa._ = All the members of his body were sore.

unmatured young branches, e.g. _Abalo bamakaintu eci ciindi batema nsamu, noziba nzoboti, kuti baluke mazyiko aabo._ = Also it was the time when the women were cutting sticks or young branches for making fishing-baskets. Also _ntenga-ntenga._
a snake, e.g. _Misyobo yanzoka mminji._ = There are many different type of snakes. _Ijilo mwana wakaswidwa mate kunzoka._ = Yesterday a child was spat upon by a snake.
sharp sticks thrown at tuber in game, e.g. Bana basobana *nzonde*. = The children are playing the *nzonde* game.
an elephant, e.g. Mumunzi wesu kwainda tanga *lyanzovvu*. = A herd of elephants passed through our village.
a grasshopper, e.g. Izimwi *nzosi* zijisi mubala mubotu. = Some grass hoppers have beautiful colouring. Also *insozi*.
relations, clans, e.g. Muno munyika ya Batonga kuli *nzubo* zyabantu zyaandeene. = Here in Tongaland there are different clans.
very large baboon, e.g. Nitwalikweenda mumugwagwa, twajana *banzuka banji*. = When we were walking along the road, we found many big baboons.

a bee, e.g. *Nzuki* zyakanjila jilo mumpako tazinabikka *buci*. = The bees which entered the hole yesterday have not yet put in honey. (other names for bees = kampakala, impasi, kaandi, kadonta, intolola, sisamu, ciboza, sicipansi, sikaulu, kanga-silyombo)
a puzzle, e.g. Toonse yakatwaalila *inzukuunzuku* yakatupa bacembele. = We all failed to solve the puzzle which the old woman gave us. Also *impasulula balozi*
edible heart of a young palm, used as a ball in childrens games.
the lung, e.g. *Inzumbwa lyanombe lilanona*. The lung of a cow is tasty. Also *ipupwa, ifwufwe*.
the tuft of hair at the end of a cow's tail, e.g. *Inzunde yamusune oyu nindamfwu*. = The bushy end of this ox's tail is long. (Non-bushy part = *lugwizo*) Also *ntunda*.
a bruise, e.g. *Ndabaa inzungu mumutwe*. = I have a bruise on the head. Also *cicuzu*.
spinning tops, e.g. Bana basobana *inzungulukata*. Also *inzingulukata*.
greediness, kubaa *nzuno* = to hide food for fear of having to share it, e.g. Chaaba wakakwata musimbi ulaa *nzuno*. = Chaaba married a wife who has the habit of hiding food. Also *imbayo*.
a swelling on the head, e.g. Mwana ngubauma amutwe bayi wabaa *nzunzu*. The child who was beaten by the teacher has developed a swelling on the head.
with all one's energy, e.g. Mweemba wakacizwida *nzunzu* kwiimba *ijilo*. = Mweemba was singing with all her energy yesterday
hiding food for fear of having to share it. e.g. Kofwambaana undibikkile *nzuwo* kunze a citendele. = Be quick and put the food behind the door.
a species of wild cat, the tiger cat, e.g. Chaampa wakajana kwacegwa *nzuzi mukooye*. = Chaampa found that a wild cat had been caught in the snare. Also *nsezi*

a cow, e.g. *Inombe nzyazyi ilasungwa*. = The cow is being yoked. Also *impwizi*. (cow refusing milk = *impasi, nombe nkasi*; cow which has no milk = *coombeboya*; cow with horns bending backwards = *inkupi*; cow without horns = *inkotolo*, cow which has calved for the first time = *insomona*.)
a maggot which lives in the ground in traditional houses and becomes the red fly, e.g. Acibuye cananda yokwesu kuli *nzyondondo*. = There are maggots on the floor of our house.
a grub found in rotten fish, e.g. Kuli *nzyundu munswi*. = There is larvae of insects found in the fish.
a manner of speaking, e.g. *Inambilo yamwana oyu njabumpelenge*. = The speech of this child is treacherous.
a house, e.g. *Inanda yatoombe yakadilimuka*. The shelter of the calves collapsed.
a household or family, e.g. *Inanda ya Haatombwe njakuciswa-ciswa ziindi zinji.* = The family of Haatombwe was frequently experiencing sickness.
a forked stick which was used as a slaves collar, e.g. *Kaindi bazike bakali kwaangwa nanda munsingo.* = In the past slaves were held by the neck with a forked stick. Also *inkabo*.

*inanda yamizimo* = a ritual house or house of the spirits **inandamaambo** a spring, a fountain, e.g. *Meenda taamani mumasena mujanwa inandamaambo.* = The water does not dry up in vleis where a spring is found.
many trees in the courtyard grown from cuttings of the *mubwabwa* tree, e.g. *Amusimpe nanga mumbali alubuwa.* = Plant the cluster of trees beside the courtyard.
a witchdoctor, e.g. *Nobantu atweende kunanga tukasonde cajaya muntu.* = People, let us go to the witchdoctor and divine what killed the person.
aof bird, the small kingfisher, e.g. *Inanga yabayuni zilya nswi mudambwa.* = The small kingfisher eats fish in the dam.

pl. of *Iwaanzi*, a crack, e.g. *Kacumbika kosyingulula kutegwa bauka batazyalili munanzi zyabulambo.* = *Kacumbika*, replaster the walls so that the insects cannot breed in the cracks of the wall. *Zifwuwa zyamaboko azyamaulu zyoonse zyakajsisi nanzi.* = All the bones of his arms and legs had cracks.
a cart, waggon, e.g. *Basune bakwela nola.* = The oxen are pulling the cart. Also *cikkocci*.
a kind of wild plum, pl. *manomba*, e.g. *Ijilo twakacela manomba asubila pyu.* = Yesterday we gathered *manomba* fruits which were very red.

cattle, e.g. *Inombe zyokwesu zyakabbigwa jilo.* = Our cattle were stolen yesterday. (*mukumbakumba* or *inkolekole* = beast with loose horns; *inkotolo* or *imvwuma* or *ingumpu* = beast without horns; *ikwalete* or *inkwali* = a cow with horns growing out horizontally; *namundindi* or *nandima* = a very big beast; *yamasekwe* = black and white coloured beast; *yabubalabubala* = black and white, black spots; *yacisikili* = a deep purple-red colour; *yamakombola* = light red colour; *inkosole* = red with white stripe around the body; *yamulala* = beast with white on the back; *inseu* = white with red spots)
a type of bird, the fly-catcher, e.g. *Ndajana tanga lyanombemabala.* = I found a flock of fly-catchers.

a cane or flexible rod used as a whip, e.g. *Cibelesyo cipati casimpongo nkeembe. Utema nkoli, nondo, tusako antindi ankako.* = The great tool of the goatherd is the axe. He cuts knobkerries, canes, sticks and little wooden spears with it. *Baama, Syaankolo wanduuma anondo.* = Mother, Syaankolo beat me with a cane.
the core of a nut which contains oil, pl. *manongo*, e.g. *Twakali kucela nongo nitwakali kweembela.* = We were collecting nuts when we were herding. Also *inoongo*.
a non-venomous snake, said to bring luck to the person who sees it. e.g. *Inongoke taijisi busaki bukali.* = The *inongoke* snake does not have a poisonous bite.
a gong, e.g. *Bayi bauma kale inonji kucikolo kutegwa bana banjile.* = The teacher has already struck the gong at the school so that the pupils enter.

a type of wild fruit, e.g. *Basimbi balafwuma munsaka kukubweza mpingili anoongo zyakweenga mafwuta.* = Girls go off early in the morning to collect seeds of the *impingili* and *inoongo* fruits to extract oil from them by heating. Also mbula

a species of grass, e.g. Mbelele, mpongo a nombe zilalya *nunga* amunyengele. = Sheep, goats and cattle eat a *nunga* and *munyengele* grasses. *Zuba lyapya ulazitola nombe kumbali a Zambezi zikalye nunga.* = When the sun gets hot, he takes the cattle near the Zambezi so that they eat the *inunga* grass.

something which gives you the strength to do that which is good or bad which you normally could not do, e.g. *Ninunzuunzu zyamupa kutanda syuumbwa alikke.* = It was abnormal power which made her, by herself, chase the lion away.
a word, pl. *manwadi*, (ety. Eng.) a letter, e.g. *Mwanaangu wandilembela nwadi ijisi makani mabotu.* = My child wrote me a letter which had good news. Also *lugwalo*
a sword, machete, e.g. *Mudeene wakajaya musune wangu apago lipati.* = Mudeene killed my ox with a big machete. Also *ipanga*.
a hole in river-bed in which fish is gathered, e.g. *Ipago lizwide nswi ziyubide.* = A hole in the river is full of fish which are hiding.
a stripe, e.g. *Bataata bapambaila butala apambe liniini.* = My father decorated the maize-bin with a small stripe.
clan groupings, pl. *mipampo*, e.g. *Mumazyalane muli mipampo-mipampo yamikowa minji.* = In all generations there are many different clan-groups.
a wide-bladed sword or knife or machete, e.g. *Ipanga eli ndali kugonsya cisyu.* = I was using this machete for cutting relish.
a big knife, machete or a sword, pl. *mapango*, e.g. *Bataata bagonka minsale apango.* = My father cuts sugar-cane with a machete. Also *ipanga*.
uninhabited bush, e.g. Kanchele nkayuni kakonzya kupona mupangwa. = The smaller partridge is a bird which can survive in a desert. Also isyokwe buyo, isaka.

the hard rind of fruit, an eggshell or groundnut shell, a scab, scales, pl. *mapapa*, e.g. *Konywisya buyo papa lyagabo meenda.* = Just use the shell for drinking water. Intale yakati, "*Amundipale mapapa amusana.*" = The crocodile said, "Scratch the scales on my back." *Iji litasimpide lijisi ipapa bonzu.* = An egg not fully developed has an unformed shell.
the socket of the hip, e.g. *Ipaso yamusankwa yagejuka naali kusobana bbola.* = The boy's hip was dislocated from the socket when he was playing football.
an African identity document in colonial days, e.g. *Citupa ncicakali paso lyabakale.* = The *citupa* was the African identity card in the past.
a satchel, pl. *mapatani*, e.g. *Basicikolo bapakata mapatani aamabbuku nobaya kucikolo.* = Pupils pack their satchels with books when they go to school.
a blanket, pl. *mapayi*, e.g. *Ipayi lyabacembele ndibotu.* = The blanket of the old woman is a good one.
a honey-comb without honey, pl. *mape*, e.g. *Kosowa pe elyo mucikko.* = Throw that empty comb on the fire.
the dew-lap of cattle, pl. *mapebwelebwe*, e.g. *Mapebwelebwe anombe zya Chikuwa mmalamfwu.* = The dew-laps of European cattle are long. Also malembwe-lembwe.
the page of a book, (ety. English) e.g. *Ipeeji lyabbuku lyakazauka.* = The page of the book was torn.
feather, pl. *mapeepe*, e.g. *Mapeepe abayuni mmauba-uba.* = The feathers of birds are soft and light. Also ipepe.
honey-combs without honey, e.g. Twakajana nzuki zyabikka kale _mapeepe_. = We found the bees had already put combs.
a big clay pot, pl. _zipempa_, e.g. Kaindi bukoko bwakali kujikilwa _mu-zipempa_. = Long ago they used to brew beer in big clay pots. Also citalo
the mouth, e.g. Caambikwa cijisi _ipempe lipati_. = The pot has a large mouth.
a moth, e.g. _Mapempe_ anyikila mucibwantu. Moths dropped into the sweet-beer.
paper, pl. _mapepa_, e.g. Basicikolo balemba _mapepa manji_. = The pupils are writing many papers.
a feather, e.g. Ndabwezela _pepe lyacungwe_. I have picked up the feather of a vulture. (sign of luck)

a turkey, (Ety. _piru_, Portugese) e.g. Aawa ampulasi kuli mukuwa uuvwubide _pilu zinji_. There at the farm there is a white-man who owns many turkeys. Also kalukuni _ipo_ a groundnut without kernel, pl. _mapo_, e.g. Indongwe zyangu tazijisi, _mmapo alo_. = The groundnuts have nothing inside, they are empty shells. Also _ipoopo_
a feast, e.g. _Ipobwe lyabwiinga lilinda sunu masiku_. = The vigil of the marriage-feast is being celebrated to-night.

a traditional knife, e.g. Bumwi buzuba Malambo wakabweza _poko libosya kuya kubba nkuku_. Wakasomona _poko lyakwe kuti aikosole mukosi ileke kubbubba_. One day Malambo took a sharp knife to go and steal a chicken. He took the knife out of the sheath so that he would cut the neck and it would stop flapping. Also _cipoko, cibezyo, cipanga, impoko, cipeni_.
a type of bird, the crowned hornbill or toucan, e.g. _Pokooko_ wali kulila kubucedo. A crowned hornbill was crying at dawn. Also _poko-poko_
big male baboon, pl. _bapombo_, e.g. Nindakali kulya cinkwa, bakandinyanga _bapombo_. When I was eating bread, male baboons snatched it from me.
a skull, e.g. Ndeeli _pompo lyasokwe_. Here is the skull of a monkey.
a big whip, pl. _mapondo_, e.g. Basimpongo bakavwimbula mwingile a-_maponda mapati_. The goatherds beat the warthog with big whips.
a type of bird, the skylark, e.g. _Poopololo ulalila mujulu_. = The skylark is singing above in the sky.
a pawpaw, e.g. Kondicelela _popo lyakabizwa_. Pick me a pawpaw which has ripened.
a type of bird, the wagtail, e.g. _Popololo wafwa mumabuwa_. = The wagtail has died in the open country.
a maize-cob in its sheath, pl. _mapopwe_, e.g. Eeli _popwe tiilyabizwa pe_. = This maize-cob is not cooked enough.

a pestle used by the Zambezi Batonga for pounding millet. It is long and heavy and has wide splaying at end. e.g. Bamakaintu batwa mabele akubelesya _pubila_. The women pound a red millet with short stem using a long heavy pestle splayed at the end. Also _munsi_,
a plank, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Undibambile cijazyo cabutala _apulanga_. = Make me a door for the grain-bin with a plank.
a high-spirited child, e.g. Mainza _ngupulipwipwi_. Mainza is a high-spirited child.
a knot, as on a tree, a lump, a cluster, e.g. Kuli _pumba lyanzuki mumango_. There is a swarm of bees in the mango tree.
a baboon, pl. bapumpulika. e.g. *Bapumpulika balayanda kunyanga zinkwa kubeendanzila.* = Baboons like to steal bread from travellers.
a spear for hunting elephant or lion, e.g. *Mukaule punda kutegwa tukavwime bazovwu.* = Buy a spear so that we hunt elephants. Also *kale*
a lung, e.g. *Ipunga lyankuku lyabola.* = The lung of the chicken is rotten. Also *ipupwa, ifwufwe*
a lung, pl. mapupwa, e.g. *Bantu bamwi bayandisya kulya mapupwa abanyama.* = Some people like eating animal lungs. Also *ipunga, ifwufwe*
a pumpkin, e.g. *Mumuunda muli pusi pati.* = There is a big pumpkin in the field.
pumpkin, pl. mapusyi, e.g. *Nguni wajisi mapusyi aya?* = Who had these pumpkins? Also *ipusi.*
a useless child, e.g. *Mwana utacebi bazyali bakwe ndipwekepweke lyamwana.* = A child who does not remember to help his parents is a useless child.
a forest, e.g. *Isaka lya Moomba lilivwuukide.* = The forest of Moomba is dense.
a sack, (ety. English) e.g. *Baama babikka mapopwe musaka.* = My mother has put the maize in a sack.
a saddle, e.g. *Mwana ulalela kukkala asale yancinga naccovwa.* = The child is unable to sit on the saddle of the bike when she peddles.

a large hide, a garment of skin, e.g. *Isalu lyacibize ndibotu.* = The hide of the zebra is beautiful. *Mwami mupati usama salu lyasiluwe.* = The great chief wears the skin of a leopard. *Ndakali muntu limwi ndaide kuba salu.* = I was a well-off person but I have become a hide. (i.e. totally worn out)

an armlet or necklace made of strips of animal hide or grass, e.g. *Cisambo antela isambo lyajanwa mu-nombe lyeelede kubambwa kabotu. Eeli isambo ndyakusamika bakamwale munsingo. (Bakamwale balasamikwa zikonde ezi zyasambo kuteeti kabalibonya kuti bakajailwa nombe zineneede zilaa mafwuta.)* = The strips found from animals ought to be kept well. The strips are for initiates to wear around their necks. (These strips are worn by initiates afterwards so that they are seen to be the ones for whom fat cattle were slaughtered.)
a big tree or log, e.g. *Isamu lyamubanga lyawa amuwo.* = The big mubanga tree fell with the wind.
a cluster of fruit, e.g. *Kondipa sankinya lyamafwulenke.* = Give me a heap of oranges.
a very small weaved dish for porridge.
the back between the shoulderblades, e.g. *Inzengene yandiluma asansa.* = The tick bit me on the back between the shoulder-blades. Also *insansa.*
a cut off branch, e.g. *Mwajala sanzu amulyango wambewu.* = You have closed the garden gate with a branch.
a pad, coil of straw, reed-mat, e.g. *Basimbi balalyookezya asasa.* = The girls are resting on a reed-mat.
a fountain, e.g. *Bantu balalima zisyu munsi-munsi asau.* = The people are planting vegetables beside the fountain. Also *inandu-maambo*
a hive of bees, e.g. *Mumusamu ulya kuli saula lyanzuki.* There is a hive of bees in that tree.
a cheek, pl. masaya, e.g. *Mwana uzimbide saya.* = The child's cheek is swollen.
a cluster of bees, e.g. *Isayila lyanzuki lyawida amwana walikoona.* = A cluster of bees fell on the child when it was sleeping.
pit-sand, e.g. Basankwa basusa see lyakuyasya. = The boys are drawing sand for building. (musenga = river sand.)
grit, a stretch of sand, e.g. Baciwena balayotela atalaa seele. = Crocodiles are basking in the sun on top of a stretch of sand.
a big burrow or den of an animal, e.g. Kakololo uyobola zilyo zyakwe museenengo. = A large rodent keeps its food in a big burrow.

a wonderful happening, a miracle, e.g. Sunu ndabona seese lyamuntu usondokede uzyana akwiimba. = Today I saw an amazing performance of a mad man dancing and singing. Also cilengwalengwa, cimpanganiko.

a bangle, bracelet, ear-ring, of wound thin wire, pl. maseka, e.g. Basimbi bayanda kusama maseka mabotu mumatwi. Girls like to wear beautiful earrings in the ears. Also idanda, pl. malanda, inkwinta-nkwinta.
a roof pole, pl. masekete, e.g. Masekete aananda taaningazulila. = The roof-poles of the house are not yet enough. Also ikkapulosi, pl. makkapulosi.
a generation, e.g. Isela lyamudaala oyu lyakamana, pesi walo nkwacili. = The generation of this old man has passed away, but he is still present.

a burrow, pl. masempo, e.g. Cucu wanjila musempo lyanengo masiku. = A mouse entered the burrow of an antbear at night. Nengo lyakati, "Sena tozyi kuti ndime mwami wabanyama boonse boona mumasempo onse?" = The antbear said, "Don't you know that I am the king of all animals who sleep in burrows?"
a large edible grub found in trees or on the ground, e.g. Inkuku yalya senda. The chicken ate a grub.
a sheet of corrugated iron, pl. masenke, e.g. Mainga wabba senke lyokwabo. Mainga stole the corrugated iron sheet from their village.
a mosquito, pl. masenya, e.g. Isenya lyali kulila masiku lyatukatazya. = The mosquito which was buzzing at night disturbed us. Also insenya.
cheek, e.g. Iseya lyamuvwanda lyazimba nkaambo lyalumwa nzuki. = The cheek of the infant is swollen because it was bitten by bees. Also isaya.
day time, midday, e.g. Isikati nciindi cakulyookezya. Midday is the time to rest.
a sickle, pl. masikela, e.g. Basimbi babweza masikela baunka kukujwa bwizu. = The girls have taken sickles and gone off to cut grass.
a big musikili tree, e.g. Kuli bayuni banji musikili lipati. There are many birds in the big musikili tree.
the large stem of a plant or trunk of a tree, e.g. Ndigonka siko lyamusamu. = I am cutting the trunk of a tree.

a fish-trap, pl. masiko, e.g. Isiko lyamana kulukwa. = The fish-trap has been weaved. Baneene, kamundilukila siko lyakuzezya. = Grandmother, weave me a fishing-basket. Mainza wakabweza siko lyakwe akuya kumulonga kuya kuzela. = Mainza took her fishing-basket and went to the river to fish. Masiko ngabakaintu kutegwa kabaibula kabotu tutaka. = Fishing-baskets are used by women so that they can skim off the small fish easily. Also moono.
a type of cloth, pl. misila, e.g. Booye bakaindi bakali kulizamba misila yandeketela. The young girls of long ago used to wrap themselves in ndeketela cloth.
a heap of grass or rubbish, e.g. Basinombe bakasisa ndongwe zyakubba musilibi. The herders hid the groundnuts they had stolen in a heap of grass.
A large portion of newly ploughed land, e.g. *Isinde liyakufwunkululwa juunza.* = The new land will be reploughed tomorrow. Also *businde.*
the sweet part of the stalk of a green mealie or of sorgum, pl. *zisende,* e.g. *Basankwa bayanda kulya zisinde.* = Boys like to eat the sweet parts of green mealie-stalks. Also *cimbololo.*
a curse, e.g. *Isingo lyakandisinga baneene lilayoosya.* = The curse by which my grandmother cursed me is a terrible one.
the common cold, e.g. *Muwo uletelezya kuciswa sini, kapati kubana basyoonto.* = The wind brings along the sickeness of the common cold, especially to little children. Also *isyini.*
a long skirt, a gown, e.g. *Isinsi lyabaama ndipati.* = The skirt of my mother is long.
a piece of charcoal, e.g. *Kobapa sizi lyamulilo bataata.* = Give my father a piece of charcoal.
a sock, pl. *masokesi,* (ety. English) e.g. *Ndaula masokesi aamwana.* = I have bought socks for the child. Also *isookesi.*
the bush, e.g. *Isokwe mumuunda lyapya.* = The bush in the field has been burnt. Also *isyokwe*
a big monkey, e.g. *Isokwe lyatanta atalaa ciluli.* = The big monkey has climbed on top of the roof.
a roofing pole, e.g. *Isomo lyaciluli lyatyoka.* = The roofing pole is broken.

a big sharp stick, e.g. *Mukaintu uutumbusya weelede kuti kajisi cibenga antela somo libosya ndyakusisya kalindi kakuzikkila camacembele.* = The midwife ought to have a machete or a big sharp stick for digging a hole for burying the afterbirth.
a canine tooth, e.g. *Mwana wazwa songanyama.* = The canine tooth of the child developed.
a descriptive name for sharp grass-seeds, e.g. *Ndayaswa songolwa-bayanzenye nindali kutanda kwale.* I was pierced by sharp grass when I was chasing the partridge.
a thorny plant with blue flowers, e.g. *Ndayaswa sonso munzila.* = I was pricked by a thorny bush on the way. *Ulayaswa mancenya naa masonso.* = You will be pricked by a thorny bush or thorny fruit.
socks, (ety. Eng.) pl. *masookesi,* e.g. *Ncibotu kusama masookesi malemu ciindi camupeyo.* = It is good to wear heavy socks during the cold season. Also *isokesi.*
stone used in fire to support pot, pl. *masuwa,* e.g. *Acikko kuli masua otatwe.* = In the fireplace there are three stones (used as supports for the cooking vessel.) Also *isuwa.*
bladder, e.g. *Isubilo lyamulwazi lyayauka.* = The bladder of the patient is torn. (*isubilo lyamululwe* = a large gall bladder)
a dust, e.g. *Oomu munanda muli suko.* = There is dust in the house. Also *kasuko.*
the fruit of the mahobohobo tree, pl. *masuku,* e.g. *Ndajana buyo suku lyomwe.* = I found only one fruit.
the back, e.g. *Isule lyangu lilacisa.* = My back is paining.
body-odour, e.g. *Bamwi bantu bajisi isumbaswe libi.* = Some people have a bad body-odour. Also *kanunko.*

a spear, e.g. *Musune wakalya mapopwe bakamuyasa sumo.* = They speared the ox which ate the maize. *Sicibende wakamwiinda kumbele mwinakwe akusimpa sumo, wakati, "Utakalali abili,* ukalale bumwi." Nabwiinga bwakasimpula sumo akulitoleela kwabo. Eli lyakali sumo *lyamufwunko*. Nabwiinga naakasika kwabo bakamutambula sumo. = Sicibende went ahead of his wife and stuck the spear in the ground and said, "You do not sleep two days at your parents home, you sleep one day." The bride took out the spear and took it to her parents home. This was the "*mufwunkd'* spear. When the bride reached home the parents received the spear. (ipunda, a large spear for hunting lion or elephant; muumba, a fishing spear, may be barbed or barbless; musamba waluswi = a fishing spear; *isumo lyacinkosi* = a barbed spear; caanza campongo or isumo *lyamaala* = barbed spears; sinkombo or isumo *lyakakombo* = a spear with one long barb; ijongo or muyonga = a longbladed spear; kayonga = a thin and short-shanked spear; isumo *lyamugwaza* or isumo *lyamulinga* = a big bladed spear used at close-quarters; *isumo lyasikamembya* = a light spear.)
a type of tree (*baphia massiensis*), pl. *misunde*, e.g. Mucoonde omu kuli *misunde minji*. = In this thicket there are many trees of the *misunde* type. Also muntembwe, musenezika.

an evergreen shrub, with pink-white pea-like flower and dark brown hanging pods. It is used for spear-shafts, hut building and firewood. Pounded roots in water give a soap. Roots and leaves are used for sores and rashes. e.g. Basimbi batajisi nsipa, bawaccizya *musunde*. = Women who have no soap wash with pounded roots of the *isunde* plant.

a type of plant (*gynandropsis gynandra*), a green relish, leaves and stems are diced and boiled for several hours. May be planted around villages. e.g. Cisyu *casungwa* tacizyizyilwe abana basunu. = The vegetable relish called *sungwa* is unknown by the youth of today. Also ciyuni-yuni, luyuni.

a type of plant, (*Celosia trigyna*), a green relish, leaves cooked for 1 hr. with pounded cucurbit seed. *Isunku ncisyu cakali kuligwa kaindi*. = *Isunku* was a bitter vegetable relish which was eaten long ago.
a fishing-basket made of reeds, e.g. Bataata bakaluka *sunta lipati lyanswi*. = My father wove a big fishingbasket.
a bundle of grass, pl. *misunta*, e.g. Bamaama bayumwide *sunta lipati lyabwizu*. = My mother is carrying a big bundle of grass.
hair, pl. *masusu*, e.g. Mwana mumugele *susu*. = Cut the child's hair. Bavwimi bakaindi bakali koosa *susu*. = Hunters of the past used to plait their hair into a long tapering cone.
a sixpence, in colonial times, e.g. Kaindi *susu* wakali kuulwa cibbudula. = In the past a pair of shorts was bought for sixpence.
one of the three stones which supports pot on fire, pl. *masuwa*, e.g. Kondiletela *suwa lyomwe*. = Bring me one stone for the fire-place. Also *isua, isyuwa*
a door made of reeds, e.g. Kobikka *iswaaswa* amulyango. = Put a reed-door at the entrance. Also citendele camabu.
a large fish, e.g. Bacembele bakajaya *iswi*. = The old woman killed a big fish. Also *inswi*.
a sack, pl. *masyaka*, e.g. Bakaintu baaka mapopwe mumasyaka mapati. = The women are packing the maize in big sacks. Also *isaka*.
a large hide, e.g. Musune wangu bakamujaya bantu, ndaakuzyiba *syalu*. = People killed my ox, I recognized the large hide. Also *isalu*.
a big tree, e.g. *Musyamu lipati* omuya mukkala mulala. = In that big tree over there, there lives a black mamba. Also isamu.
cheek, e.g. *Isyaya lyabacembele lilizimbide akaambo kalusinga.* = The cheek of the old lady is swollen because of a nerve-pain. Also isaya.
a wonderous event, e.g. Mu*nanga wakacita syeesye lyakagambya bantu boonse.* = The witchdoctor performed a wonder which astounded all the pople. Also iseese.
a grub or insect, pl. *masyenda*, e.g. *Ingulube zilayanda kulya masyenda mumuunda.* = Pigs like to eat grubs in the field. Also isenda.
a barred-owl, e.g. *Mu musikili omu kulila syibampeyo.* = In this musikili tree an owl is hooting.

non-poisonous green snake, e.g. *Mudaala walitija syibamulosi nolitajayi.* = The old man fled from the non-poisonous snake even though it does not kill. (It moves through the grass like the sound of a whistle.)
midday, during the day, e.g. *Beenzu bakasika syikati jilo.* = The visitors arrived at midday yesterday. Also isikati.
a type of tree with dark green foliage, e.g. *Musyikili omuya momukkala bayuni banji.* = Over in that big musikili tree there are plenty of birds. Also isikili, musikili.
a fishing basket, e.g. *Baama babweza syiko baunka kukuzela.* = My mother has taken a fishing basket and has gone to fish. Also isiko.
a heap of grass or rubbish, e.g. *Ndalikuvwumbulula ndongwe zyasisidwe musyilibi.* = I was uncovering groundnuts which were hidden in a heap of grass. Also isilibi.
the common cold, e.g. *Bantu banji baciswa isyina ciindi campeyo.* = Many people suffer from the common cold during the cold season. Also isini.
a tree-mouse, e.g. *Syokobeba zyatanta mumusamu.* = The tree mice have gone up the tree.
the bush, e.g. *Inombe zili kukucela musyokwe.* = The cattle are grazing in the bush. Also isokwe.
non-poisonous snake, e.g. *Isyubusyubu lyanjila munanda.* = A non-poisonous snake has entered the house. Also isyibamulosi.
a spear, e.g. *Muzeli wanswi wayasa mweenzinyina isyumo.* = A fisherman has wounded his friend with a spear. Also isumo.
a bitter edible relish, e.g. *Isyungwa ncisyu cilula-lula.* = Isyungwa is a relish which is slightly bitter. Also isungwa.
a big reed fishing-basket, e.g. *Ba Ila bazezya syuta.* = The Ila people fish with the big reed fishing-basket.
a mat shaped into a canoe, e.g. *Basankwa bakwasula syuta.* = Men row the mat-shaped canoe.
an edible root, e.g. *Bana basya syutu mumusena.* = The children are digging an edible root in the vlei. Also nsyuto
a stone used in the fireplace to support the pot, e.g. *Cibiya catika nilyapanduka syuwa.* = The pot spilled over when the firestone was split. Also isuwa.
a rodent which digs holes and lives in vleis, pl. *mataba*, e.g. *Mutinta ulayanda kusya mataba.* = Mutinta likes digging for rodents.
a table, e.g. *Kobikka cakulya atafwule.* = Put the food on the table. Also itebule.
a buttock, pl. *matako*, e.g. *Ndaa cuute atako.* = I have an abcess on the buttock.
the bottom of a dish or well, e.g. Meenda amana mucikala, kulibonya tako. = The water is finished in the well, the bottom can be seen.
the butt-end of a gun, e.g. *Itako* lyantobolo lyakabumbwa. = The butt of the gun has been eaten by ants. Also musyoti.

a river bank, e.g. *Itala* lyamulonga ndidamfwu. = The bank of the river is steep. Also inkomwe *italabalanga* the firmament, the heavens, e.g. *Italabalanga* lilaa nyenyezi zinji. = The sky has many stars. Also buuma
different ways, e.g. *Ndabaa* talitali. I am pulled in different ways.
a wide-necked pot for brewing beer, e.g. *Italo* lyabukoko lyazula cibwantu. = The wide-necked pot is full of sweet-beer.
the cheek, pl. matama, e.g. Musankwa oyu ujisi *matama* mapati. = This boy has big cheeks. Also isaya.

a log of wood, e.g. Koya kaulete mulilo nguulya kutanda lisunta busi okuya. = Go and bring fire from that smoking log over there. Batombela bakatandaana akuyoonjizyanya mumpako yatanda. = The lizards chased one another and followed one another into a hole in a log. Namusya ndamufwunda akusisa nyama mutanda lyamukamba. = I skinned the duiker and hid the meat in the wood of a mukamba tree.
the gizzard, e.g. *Itandali* lyamuyuni mupati lilafwambaana kuseta cakulya. = The gizzard of the big bird is quick to break down food finely.
a herd, a pack, group, e.g. *Itanga* lyabasokwe lili mumuunda. = There are a pack of monkeys in the field.
open space in front of a house, e.g. Lubeta Iwakali *atanga* lyananda. = The court-case was (held) in the open space in front of the house. Also lubuwa.
a market place, e.g. Basimbi baunka *kukuula nswi kutanga.* = The girls have gone to buy fish at the market.
a cattle-melon, pl. matanga, e.g. Bana bapandaula matanga akusanizya ngulube. = The children are splitting open the cattle-melons to feed the pigs.
the most open and elevated place in the courtyard, e.g. Bantu bayanika zisani zyabo *atangatanga.* = The people have hung up their clothes at the highest place in the coutyard.
a pool, pond, e.g. Eeli *tangazyiba* momusobanina ngulube. = This pond is where the pigs play.
a big hole in the ground around which grass grows, e.g. Bwizu bwamuitangazyiba tabuyumi. = The grass around the depression does not wither.
the highest area of the courtyard, e.g. Bana balasobana *atangaila.* = The children are playing on the high patch of the courtyard. Also *itangatanga*
a gun, e.g. Munyati uyasidwe *tangula* mmukali. = The buffalo who is wounded by a gun is fierce. Also intobolo.
an ash-heap, e.g. Munene wakasisa munkuli wabukoko *mutantala.* = The old man hid the gourd of beer in an ash-heap.
the hand, the palm of the hand, e.g. *Itansyi* lyalulyo lilaa matwiza. = The right hand has blisters.
a finger ring, e.g. Mugutu wakamusamika tasa musimbi wakwe. = Mugutu gave his girl-friend a ring to wear. Also intasa, insale, ininga.
a table, e.g. Mufwazi undi-bambila *tebule.* = The carpenter is making a table for me. Also itafwule.
a blanket made from the inside bark of the mubombo tree. pl. matebwe. = Matebwe taabonwi sunu. = Blankets made from bark are not seen today.
clay for pottery or the hole from which the clay is dug. = Amukalete bulongo kuteelengo. = Bring clay from the pit for pottery-making. Also nkomba
relish, e.g. Bana baya kukuyandaula telele. = The children have gone to look for relish. Also lunkomba, delele, cinkomba.
a length of cloth, e.g. Koyaula itembe lilamfwu lyamulembo. = Cut off a long length of cloth.
a pliable young shoot or sucker, e.g. Kunyona-nyona tempetempe ncuuba-uba. = To twist the shoot is easy.

a footprint, a foot, pl. matende, e.g. Mvwundyanga naakazinguluka kunze, kunyina atende ndyaakabona akali kuzyana syaazyana. = When Mvwundyanga encircled the house outside, he did not see any footprint where the witchdancer was dancing. Muzyamba wakali kutobela matende abakaintu. = Muzyamba was following the footprints of the woman.

a pumpkin, e.g. Sunu ndajika tende. = Today I will cook pumpkin. Mbelele nozicela tende kusule akalundu, bana balasobana mumukondo. = When the sheep are grazing pumpkin-leaves behind the hill, the children are playing in the track.

a wild vegetable (Cocculus hirsutus), leaves are used as green relish, fibre is used for basketry. e.g. Bacembele bacela tende wakulusya zisuwo. = The old women are gathering fibres for weaving baskets.
a reed, pl. matete, e.g. Nditemene tete lyomwe buyo. = Cut me just one reed. Also lutete.
an edible starchy tuber, wild yam, e.g. Basimpongo basya tetebalo mumusena. = The goatherds are digging a wild yam in the vlei.
the slough of a snake, e.g. Inzoka yalikwama isiya timbatimba. = The snake has sloughed leaving its skin.
a type of beetle, e.g. Mwana wakalumwa tingila amulomo. = The child was bitten on the mouth by a beetle.

a spring, a garden with permanent moisture, a permanently swampy place, e.g. Haasyipa ulakomena mutinti cakuzinguluka mwaka. = Blackjack grows in a permanently swampy area the whole year round. Kutinti nkotuteka meenda aide kukunka. = It is from the spring that we draw water which is just flowing.
the cast-off skin of a snake, e.g. Ndajana itipatipa lyanzoka yakalikwama mumusamu. = I found the skin of a snake which had sloughed in a tree. Also itimbatimba
a monkey-apple, pl. matobo, e.g. Bana balya matobo musyokwe. = The children are eating monkey-apples in the bush.
a hide not yet softened, e.g. Bakanangamika tutobo twabasiluwe a masanzu. Kutegwa tuyume.= They had put the untreated leopard skins on the branches to dry. Also cikutu
dirt, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa tombe amubili. = This child has dirt on the body.
valley, e.g. Imbelele zicela mutombolo. = The sheep are grazing in the valley.
a bridle, pl. matomu, e.g. Basune baangwa matomu notukolobeka. = The oxen are tied with bridles when we are cultivating.
white foam from mouth, e.g. Sikasuntu uzwa tomu kumulomo. = The epileptic is frothing from the mouth. Also intovwolomu, ncovwu.
a very small type of wild orange, e.g. Mwana wacela tondo likwange. = The child is gathering a wild unripe orange.
an old site of a village, a ruin, pl. matongo, e.g. Tuya kukulya mango kutongo lyabataata. = We are going to eat mangoes at the deserted homestead of my father.
a type of bird, the whitebellied stork, e.g. *Kwainda itongola ligama kujwe.* A white-bellied stork has passed heading eastwards.

complaint, greviance, e.g. *Itongoosi ndejisi amweenzuma oyu Kaumba, nobami, ndyaminyinza yamyuunda yesu njotulima.* The complaint which I have against my friend Kaumba, O Chief, concerns the boundaries of our fields which we plough.
a temporary marshy place, e.g. *Mugwagwa uya kucibbadela lyakaba tope-tope.* The road going to the hospital has become a marsh.
an insipid water-melon, e.g. *Itopi lyanamunyo akaba meenda alo.* = An insipid water-melon became just tasteless water.
a snake in a fable, said to carry people away, e.g. *Kuli caano ca Haakacite atosi.* There is a story about Haakacite and a mythical snake.
a leaf, pl. *matu*, e.g. *Kwanyikila tu mucibulo cameenda.* A leaf dropped into a bucket of water.
light, e.g. *Ituba lyazuba lyagwasya kuti tubone cili munanda.* = The sunlight helps us to see what is in the house.
a big cataract in the eye, e.g. *Bakandigwisya tube muliso kucibbadela.* = They removed a big cataract from my eye in the hospital.
a drop of sweat, pl. *mitukuta*, e.g. *Muliso ndanjilwa tukuta.* = A drop of sweat entered my eye. Also *inkasaalo*.
a piece of meat, e.g. *Mubwa wazubula tuli mumutiba ulida bana.* = A dog took a slice of meat out of the children's plate.
a type of bird, the large vulture, e.g. *Basankwa babona tulula-nzovwu mucisaka ca Haankombo.* = The boys have seen a large vulture in the forest of Haankombo. Also *sikube*.
a type of bird, the big white stork, pl. *matululanzuzu*, e.g. *Matululanzuzu alya nzengene mumweezi.* = The big white storks eat ticks in the valley. Also *inkobo, lukobo*

a hut, pl. *matumba*, e.g. *Kumantoombwa balombe bakali kuyaka matumba akwaavwumba amazembwe abwizu. Zilongo, ncili, minsi amaziyo zyoonse zyakali kubambwa mumatumba.* = At the *mantoombwa* training tradition the boys used to build huts and roof them with grass. Cooking pots, mortars, pestles and grinding stones were made at their huts.
a type of bird, the owl, e.g. *Meso akwe akali kulanga mbubona bulanga tumba masiku.* His eyes could see as an owl sees at night.
nakedness, pl. *mitundulu*, e.g. *Ndeenda buti atundulu?* How can I walk naked?
a high piece of land, e.g. *Ituntaulu lyadamu lyakakolomoka.* = The dam-wall collapsed.
a clot of milk or blood, e.g. *Mukupa wakakamwa jilo lyaba tupwata.* = The milk which was milked yesterday has become coagulated.

a foul expression, an expletive, pl. *matusi*, e.g. *Bamwi bantu balatukila matusi anunka nsu.* Some people curse with foul expressions that stink terribly. *Nibakali kuumwa boobu Bina Mainza kunyina anibakajosya noliba tusi pe.* = When she was been beaten like that the mother of Mainza did not react, not even a single bad word.
a leaf, e.g. *Unditemene tuvwu lyomwe lyamango.* = Cut one mango leaf for me.
a blister, e.g. *Ndazwa tuzya andi-pwaya cibulo.* I blistered where the iron struck me. Also *itwizya*.
a cheetah, e.g. *Muvwimi wakalumwa twaluwe.* = The hunter was attacked by a cheetah.
ashes, e.g. *Koyola twe acikko.* = Remove the ashes from the fireplace. Also *idyota*
August, (when new leaves shoot and look like the ears of animals) e.g. *Mumwezi wa Twi twakaula masaka amapopwe osanwe.* = In the month of August we bought five bags of maize.
a blister, e.g. *Bantu batazyibide kugonka, balafwambaana kubaa twia.* = People who are not used to cutting, quickly develop blisters. Also *ituzya, itwiza*
a blister, e.g. *Ikuti twiza lyadonkolwa lizwa cili mbulimeenda.* = If a blister is pierced a water-like substance comes out. Also *ituzya, itwia, itwizya.*
okra, e.g. *Bantu banji basilika kulumwa kwanzoka tabalyi tyezi.* = Many people who treat snake-bite do not eat okra. Also *iteezi, muteezi, idelele, cinkomba, citeezi, lunkomba.*
a lazy inactive person, e.g. *Chimuka wakakwata tyola lyamukaintu.* = Chimuka married a lazy inactive wife. Also *litolo, ityolo.*
marriage negotiation by proxy, e.g. *Haanyimbo nguwakali ityombo kumukaintu wangu.* = Haanyimbo represented me in the marriage arrangements with my wife. Also *sityombo.*
malaria, e.g. *Bantu banji baciswa vwaamwa.* = Many people are sick with malaria. Also *intuntumaanzi.*
a great number, e.g. *Kwakali vwamani lyabantu kumuswaangano wakali jilo.* = There was a great number of people at the meeting which was yesterday.
a large new hoe, e.g. *Ivweta lyakaula bataata lilima kabotu.* = The large new hoe which my father bought digs well.
soft and fluffy hair or feathers, e.g. *Mapepe atumba ngavwindivwindi.* = The feathers of an owl are soft and fluffy.
July, e.g. *Matuvwu amisamu akunkumuka mumwezi wa Vwilili.* = The leaves fall during the month of July. Also *Kunkumuna-masamu.*
a clod of earth, e.g. *Mwana wazimba mpaawumwa vwinga.* = The child is swollen where he was struck by a clod of earth. Also *ivwunga.*

September, e.g. *Mwezi oyu upandulula kuteeti masamu onse asyuuka, mateo avwumba masamu wititii. Nkokuzwa zina eli Ivwivwi.* = This month refers to the time when all the trees begin to bud, the bush has covered the land completely. That's where the name *Ivwivwi* comes from.
tow, the downy feathers of a young bird, e.g. *Mwana wamuyuni ulatalika kuuluka naazwa vwivwindi.* = The young of a bird begins to fly when the downy feathers appear. Also *ivwindivwindi.*
loose soil, pl. *mavwu*, e.g. *Ivwu elyo liyandika kutolwa mumuunda.* = That soil should be taken to the field. *Ivwu lyalungutuka.* = dry earth
a bellows, pl. *mavwuba*, e.g. *Bafwula zibulo babelesya mavwuba kubbe-bbya mulilo.* = The forgers of iron use a bellows to increase the fire.
stalks of corn, e.g. *Vwuba lyakalivwunikidwe, mukati mwakali nzembwe.* = The stalks of corn were covered and inside there were grains of corn.
a scarf, malesu or insasiko = a woman's scarf.
the covered sky, e.g. *Sunu kunakutontola nkaambo kuli vwumbanyika.* = It will be cold today because the sky is covered with clouds.
cloud cover, e.g. Komusamika cikasaala mwana nkaambo kuli _vwumbansi._ = Clothe the child in something warm because there is a cloud cover. Also ivwumbanyika.
November, (time of quick growth in vegetation), e.g. Mumwezi wa _Vwumbapati_ mvwula inga ilawa kapati. = During November the rain usually falls heavily. Also Zyumbipati
a clod of earth, e.g. Ooyu musune komuuma _vwunga._ = Beat that ox with a clod of earth. Also ivwinga, ikomwe.
ground well broken up, e.g. Bulimo bwakalimwa jilo bwakaba _vwunku-vwunku._ = The ground which was ploughed yesterday was well broken up.
a maggot, pl. mavwunyu, e.g. Eeyi nyama yabaa _vwunyu._ = This meat has maggots.
a white slug found in manure or wood, e.g. Ndababwa _vwuya_ wazyila mumakwa acitanda. = I am itching from a white slug which came from the bark of a log. Also ivwiya
a small wild orange, pl. mawi /magwi, e.g. Eeli _wi_ ndyakuvwundika. = This wild orange is to be kept until ripe.
verse of a hymn, pl. mayanza, e.g. _Kayanza_ kaciimbo eci kalakatazya kuzyiba. = The verse of this hymn is hard to memorize. Also insendu, impango
a rain cloud, e.g. _Iyoba_ lisyoonto lyawisya mvwula sunu. = A small raincloud produced a fall of rain today. Also joba, ikkumbi.

a type of insect, a millipede, pl. mayongolo, e.g. Munanda Kacumbika tayandi nzinini, ntunga, tubanze, tuubi, basimunyewo, bunyenyene, basicoomboIwa, _mayongolo amulanzi._ = In the house Kacumbika does not like common flies, red flies, scorpions, spiders, black stinging ants, small black ants, big red ants, millipedes and the termites which build large mounds.
a wave, e.g. Bwato bwatontwa _ayuwe kkali._ = The boat was driven along by a fierce gale.
the mane of a lion or zebra, e.g. _Izangala_ yasyuumbwa ilaimikila naanyema. = The mane of a lion stands up when he is angry. Also ingala.
a big fly, e.g. Mumukupa kwanyikila _zi._ = A big fly dropped into the milk. Also inzi
a pool, e.g. Basimpongo basambila muziba linywida mpongo. = The goatherds are bathing in the pool where the goats drink. Also izyiba.
a big cattle-fly, e.g. Kolijaya _zimbwa lyuuluka elyo._ = Kill that big fly flying over there.

a clan name, e.g. _Izina lyaakalo_ ndizina mwana ndyaulikwa amucembele wakwe wakamutumbusya. = The name lyaakalo (which refers to the bed on which the baby is born) is the name which the baby is given by the midwife who assisted at his birth. (The words for nicknames are: _izina lyacimpampi, izina lyacaali, izina buyobuyo._)
a ring around the sun or moon, e.g. Sunu kuzuba kuli _izingu_ litondezya kuti kulakonzya kuboola mvwula. = There is a halo around the sun today showing that rain is expected.
the bottom millstone, e.g. Kaindi busu bakali kubuziya _aziyo._ = In the past they were grinding mealie-meal on a grinding-stone. (inkando = the upper stone)

the day before yesterday, the day after tomorrow, e.g. Njakuunka _zona_ kudolopo. = I will go to town the day after tomorrow. Baama bakasika _zona kuzyila kudilwe._ = My mother arrived from the funeral the day before yesterday. Also izoona, izyoona.

The day after tomorrow, the day before yesterday, e.g. *Ndakamubona munyama izoona.* = I saw the animal the day before yesterday. *Ndiyakumubona muntu izoona.* = I will see the person the day after tomorrow. Also izona, izyoona.

the sun, e.g. *Sunu zuba lilabala kapati.* = The sun is shining fiercely today. (Minsi yazuba or miyanda yazuba = rays of the setting sun; at sunrise = *izuba lyapompa, izuba lyapasuka, izuba lyapata*; at sunset = *izuba nolibbila*; after sunset = *kuluubeube, kumangolezya, kugolezya, kulubundu-bundu*; sunlight = *lumwi*.)
a day, e.g. *Bataata bakaakukkala izuba lyomwe buyo ku Lusaka.* = My father stayed only one day in Lusaka. cf. buzuba
a scoop fishing-basket, e.g. *Izubo lyanswi lyayauka.* = The fishingbasket is ripped up. Also moono, isyiko

a hiding place, e.g. *Wakabweza jamba wakaya kuzuka nkwaakabwene nsya. Mbwaakasikila muzuka, wakasya mulindi mulamfwu.* = She took her hoe and went to the duiker's hiding place which she saw. As soon as she arrived at the hiding place, she dug a deep hole.
what is complex, e.g. *Kulabulula zumbabaya nciyumu.* = To unravel what is complex is difficult. Also inzukuunzuku.
an evil spirit, e.g. *Munanga wakagusya izwa mumulwazi.* = The witchdoctor drove out the evil spirit from the patient.
the knee, pl. mazwi, e.g. *Izwi lyamusune lilaa cicisa.* = The knee of the ox has a sore. Also igondo
a word, a voice, e.g. *Izwi lyomwe lilabeleka kumuntu musongo.* = One word has its effect on a wise man. *Syaansima wakalizyiba izwi* = Syaansima knew the voice. Also ijwi.
a generation, e.g. *Eeli zyalane liyakumana akaambo kalufwu Iwavwula.* = This generation will be wiped out because of the frequency of death.
the uterus, e.g. *Mwana oyu wakazyalwa kufwambaana nkaambo zyalilo ndisyoonto.* = This child was prematurely born because the uterus is small. Also cizyalilo.
a shirt (ety. Dutch), e.g. *Matongo usamide zyempe lituba.* = Matongo is wearing a white shirt.
a stupid person, e.g. *Lyainda zyengo lyamuntu kaliya kubukoko.* = A stupid person passed by, going for beer.
kutiisya muntu, ani ndizyengo.* = I thought I was teaching a human being, instead of that she is a stupid person. Also ciyanga, izyinya, mufwubafwuba.
a pool or lake, e.g. *Muntu ngubakajaya bakamunyika muzyiba.* = The person whom they killed they dropped into a pond. Also iziba.
name, e.g. *Nduwe ni zyina lyako?* = What is your name? Also izina.
a ring around the moon or sun, e.g. *Kuti kwaba zyingu kumwezi, inga mvwula nkwiicili.* = If there is a ring around the moon, there will still be rain. Also izingu.
what is uselss or untalented, e.g. *Izyinya lyajaya twana twankuku.* = A stupid person killed the chicks. Also muzyinya, cizyinya, zinya.
an upper grinding-stone, pl. mazyinyo, e.g. *Bacizi besu bakujwe bacaabelesya mazyinyo.* = Our sisters from the east still use grinding-stones. Also iziyo.
a big snake, e.g. *Aawo kwainda izyoka.* = A big snake passed here.

the day after tomorrow, the day before yesterday, e.g. *Cikolo ciyakujalwa izyoona akaambo kakubula meenda.* = The school will be closed the day afer tomorrow because of the lack of water. Also izona.
a bedroom, inner room, a partition. e.g. Swebo toona kuzyuli. = We sleep in the bedroom.
a female bee, e.g. Izyungabuluba nzezileta munsu kubuci. = It is the female bees which bring beebread to the hive.
dizziness, e.g. Ndabaa zyuungwe aboobo nsekonzyi kweenda endikke. = I am feeling dizzy and so I cannot walk alone. Also izyuungu, cizunguboombe.
a big root, e.g. Ndadadula janda lyamusamu. = I have uprooted a big root of a tree. Ijamba lyakagaba ajanda lipati nilyakatyoka. = The plough got stuck in a big root when it broke. cf. muyanda.
a cliff, e.g. Nkujana mootokala nkuukunkulika ajeleele mbuli kuti ulapinda-muka. = It was to find that the car was running towards the cliff as if it was about to go over it.
a stick for marking, e.g. Munene wakabikka jiligasi kutaminina akuyakila munzi. = The old man marked with a stick, claiming as his own possession the place to build a village.

large tail of a wildebeest. e.g. Masiku nibakamana kulalila, munanga wakamuzyanya mulwazi, wakauminwa ngoma akukambilwa akwiimbilwa nyimbo. Wakagantwa amutwe akuvwupuulwa a mubili ajingo, mucila mupati wamunyumbwe. = At night time after supper, the witchdoctor made the patient dance. Drums were being beaten to the kukambilwa dance and songs were sung. She was pressed on the head and the body was sprinkled with the big tail of a wildebeest.
a millipede, e.g. Wakamulisya nciinga nkoma cakasanganizigwa atubyaabyi twasuntwe ajongola. = She made him eat a horrible tortoise mixed with the dirt of a hyena and a millipede.

the secretary-bird, e.g. Jule mmuyuni utaalukila nzila kubantu bajisi malweza. = The secretary-bird is a bird which crosses the path in front of people on whom fall an evil omen. Also nakansakwe, namandweza.
agitation, confusion, e.g. Nywebo bana ndijungwe elyo ndyomucita alimwi muleta mapenzi kubazyali banu. = You young ones, you bring about confusion and you bring suffering to your parents.
breast of an animal or chicken, pl. twaaba, e.g. Kaaba kalanona. = The breast of a beast is tasty. Also katiti
a tuft of feathers on bird's head, or crest, e.g. Nakaala ujisi kaala kalamfwu. = The crested crane has a long crest. Also kasumpa, lucilimba = the crest, as of hoopoe
a mark, e.g. Inombe yokwesu ndiliizyi nkaambo ijisi kaama ankumo. = I know my cow because it has a mark on the forehead.
something to be told or answered, e.g. Ino ujisi kaambo nzi kakundaambila? = What is it that you have to tell me?
a small house, e.g. Kuli mulilo mukaanda kangu. = There is a fire in my little house. Also nanda.
a big trap with two compartments, one for bait, the other to trap game, like a leopard, a trap for guinea-fowl, e.g. Ndakajaya nkanga zyobilo mukaanda kangu. = I killed two guinea-fowl in my trap.
