beer brewed at the end of the funeral wake, e.g. Bantu kabakola kaandaano. = The beer at the end of the funeral made the people drunk. Kaandaano mbukoko bukumbwa ciindi lyamana kuzwa dilwe basimukowa kabatanamwaika. = Kaandaano is the beer brewed at the conclusion of the funeral before the relatives disperse.

midnight, e.g. Bavwimi bazwa akaandabwe kuya kucila. = The hunters go out to the group-hunting at midnight. Wakali kunga anjila kumazuba kusambala bukoko kuya kuzwa mpaakaandabwe kabusiku. = She used to enter to sell beer in the evening and leave at midnight.
the month of May, e.g. Mumwezi wa Kaandakaniini noitalika mpeyo. = The cold season starts in May.
a little frog, e.g. Aaka kaande bantu tabakalyi. = People do not eat this little frog.
a small type of bee making honey in trees, pl. twaandi, = Bana balya buci bwatwaandi. = The children are eating honey of small bees. Also kadoonte
first-born, e.g. Mwana wakusaanguna kuzyalwa wiitwa kuti nkaandulankanya. = The child to be born first is called 'kaandulankanya." (lit. the one who splits the hips)
the breast of an animal, e.g. Yakafwa nombe yakajisi cilonda akaango. = The cow which had a sore on it's breast died. (kaaba mweendo wakaango = the foreleg of a beast)
sugar, e.g. Ino nguni wakupa kaania-bbakala aka yawe? = Who has given you this sugar?

a violet tree-snake (type of boomslang), does not run away but pretends to be dead, has highly venomous bite, e.g. Kaankuni wajanika munkuni zyajisi bacembele. = A violet tree-snake was found in the firewood of the old woman. Also kakuni, siboninsonje, siboninduli.
an axe, e.g. Kondiletela kaankuni. = Bring me an axe. cf. keembe.
a short story, e.g. Bakaapa bakatwaanina kaano kabotu ijilo. = Our grand-mother told us a nice short story yesterday.

brew beer for the purpose of greeting the in-laws or a wife's husband, e.g. Baama bakumba kaanzyo kakwaanzya mukwe wabo. = My mother is brewing a special beer to greet her inlaw. Mukaintu naayanda kwaanzya mwaalumi wakwe azwa nkwaazwa wakeelede kukondola bukoko. Oobu bukoko butegwa 'kaanzyo'. Bukoko obu bwakali kukondwelwa kumunzi kwabo mukaintu. = When a wife wants to greet her husband from where he comes she ought to brew beer. This beer is called 'kaanzyd. The beer was brewed at the wife's original home.
small fibre for tying something, e.g. Koleta kaanzyo twaange bwizu. = Bring a fibre to tie the grass.
my grandmother (vocative) pl. bakaapa, e.g. "Chaalama" bakamwiita bakaapanyina. "Kaapa," wakavwiila Chaalama. = "Chaalama" called the grandmother. "Grandmother", answered Chaalama.
Also kaataati . . .

bullying behaviour, e.g. Banyina musankwa bakali kunga kufwumbwa baboola kuswaya bana babo bakali kuleta kaataati munanda yabo. = The mother of the boy whenever she came to visit her married sons and daughters used to adopt a commanding type of behaviour. Also kaasyaasyi
hiatus, pause, gap, e.g. Uleelede kulipa kaatu ciindi noimba nokuba kwaambaula. = You should allow yourself a pause when you sing or speak.
a cat, e.g. Kaaze ulalya mbeba. = The cat eats mice. Also mangoye.
a small enclosure, e.g. Kuli toombe tobilo buyo mukaba aka. = There are only two calves in this small enclosure. Also ciba.
talkativeness, e.g. Mukaintu sibunjaka ulaa kababa. A quarrelsome woman is talkative.
a small wing of a bird, e.g Kanene ulya kababa kakatiiti. Kanene is eating the wing of a robin. Also ibaba.

descriptive name for a gecko in a traditional fable (a nocturnal lizard with adhesive pads on the feet) (Used in cursing, e.g. Balowa kubota kabafwa kabafwidilila. It would be good if witches died forever.) Also kabafwa-kabayindilila.)
descriptive name for gecko in a traditional fable, Also haamakanka, haasyikulukulu, kabafwa-kabafwidilila.
a letter of the alphabet, e.g. Kabala komwe kumwaalila kubala. She has failed to read one letter of the alphabet.
mark, e.g. Ulasumbula, ulatuba buu mbuli lukobo tacikwe akabala kabyaabi pe. He is clean, he is as white as an egret which is without a spot.
a cataract or blockage in the eye, e.g. Koboola musa undigusye kabale muliso. Come friend and remove the speck in my eye.
a small head-pad, e.g. Kobikka kabale amutwe uyumune nongo yameenda. Put on a small head-pad so that you carry the pot of water. Also nkata.
a spitting cobra, e.g. Ndapiilwa kabambakuku muliso. I was spat in the eye by a spitting cobra. Also inkombola.
a grave, e.g. Usyi mufwu nguuyenga kabanda. The father of the dead man is the one who measures the grave. Wakaambila muntu kuti acite kabanda. He told the man to make a grave. Also cuumbwe.
an ornamental axe, e.g. Mudaala ujisi kabanga kabosya kapati. The old man has a very sharp ornamental axe.
the sharp point at the end of a fowl's tail-feathers, e.g. Koitenda kabanga nkuku, utakajikilizyi. Cut off the tail-end of the chicken, do not cook it. Also. kakungu
a scorpion, e.g. Kabanze kalacisa kuti kakuluma. A scorpion pains if it bites you. Also ibalabanze (has red stripes wth more severe sting)
the shortest rib, e.g. Munene bamutyola kabatuzi nibamuuma nkoli. They broke the old man's shortest rib when they beat him with a club.
a small enclosure, e.g. Kuli cisyu cibotu mukabaya aka. There is nice relish in the enclosed patch. Also lubaya.
a type of bird, the button-quail, runs swiftly through grass. e.g. Kabaya uladuntila mubwizu cakufwambaana. The button-quail runs swiftly through the grass.
undercoat, e.g. Wausomona mwaanda wamakkwacca ngwaakabikkide mukabbamba nkaakasamide kunsi akumutambika nguwe. He took out a hundred kwacha which he had put in his inside coat and gave it to him.
a type of edible mushroom, pl. bakabbanza. e.g. Bakabbanza mbowa bunona kapati. The kabbanza is a mushroom which is tasty.
drainage hole or furrow, e.g. Ucimana kulebula boobu nkumukwelela mukabbolovwu. When he shot her he dragged her into a drainage hole.
overcoat, e.g. Wacinca zisani zyaakasamide, wasama kabbomba kasiya. He changed his clothes and put on a black overcoat.
shorts, e.g. Kabbudula kamwana kaligwa mbeba. The shorts of the child has been eaten by rats.
container, e.g. Mukaintu wakali kwiiyobola nyama mukabbule kandongwe. One woman kept the meat in a container of groundnuts.

a heap of ashes, e.g. Walo nkulipwaila nzinga ansi, sa mbwaanga akali kabbunta, nkujana caakwiide kutuba mubili onse buu. He also was just throwing himself down, since he was doing so on the ash-heap, his whole body became white with ash.
heap of soil, e.g. Kamuboola muzikulange zisani zyali akabbunte mbozisubila. Come and see how brown the clothes are which were on the heap of soil.
a small parcel, e.g. Kwakali mulwi wazipepa wakalumikidwe amwi akupanga kabbutu. There was a heap of papers stuck together and made into a small parcel.
a small piece, e.g. Nacilomo bakamupa buyo kabeela kaniini. They gave Nacilomo only a small piece. Also cibeela.

a spatula or tool which has a broad flat, blunt blade, used especially for mixing or spreading, a snuff spoon, e.g. Mwana wakaletela mudaala mulilo akabego. The child brought the old man fire on a flat instrument. Also lubeko, lumano.
upright frame for drying maize, e.g. Kamuyanika mapopwe akabeko. Dry the maize on the standing frame.
a small lizard with large head, e.g. Kabelebele takaligwi, kalakola. The kabelebele lizard is inedible, it is poisonous.
a small job, e.g. Sena ujisi kabeleko kamwi juunza? Do you have another small job tomorrow.
thick beer poured on the grave of the deceased by the leading clan elder on the last night of the funeral.

beer which is drunk the day before the main mweesyo or final funeral ritual, e.g. Ndaboola buyo kukuzyibya makani ngindakakwaambide eliya kukabelelezi kamunene. I have just come to let you know about the matter I had told you on the day of drinking beer before the main beer is drunk at the mweesyo after the old man's funeral.
gap between teeth, either natural or made, e.g. Kabende kamusimbi ulya nkabotu. The gap in that girl's teeth is attractive. Also cibende, kapozya musozya.
a type of axe or mattock, e.g. Ubelesye kabeula kupandaula nkuni. Use the mattock to split the firewood. Also ibbeula.
a small grey bird with black spots which sits on the ground not on branches, e.g. Wakali kwiide kutweta abe nkabeya. He was panting like a small bird. Also kazyingi

a plant (Fimbristylis dichotoma), the stalks are used for ash filtration as a source of salt. e.g. Basikale bakali kubelesya musamu wakabimbi kubamba munyo. The ancestors were using the kabimbi plant for making salt.

a small flat land-tortoise (skin and shell used for love-potion), e.g. Lusu Iwacikwa cakabinda lubikkwa mumusamu waluyando. The powdered shell of the flat land-tortoise is put in traditional lovemedicine.
a small clay pot, e.g. Kobikka kabiya kacinkomba acikko. Put the clay pot of relish on the fireplace.
a small washing-pot, e.g. Batumbu babelesya kabiya munsambilo yarnwana. A mother uses a special pot for washing her child.
a rain-shrine pot, e.g. Kabiya kamumalende kalavwuntamikwa. The rainshrine pot is turned upside down.
small frog, e.g. *Kabombwe ngwamumeenda.* = The small frog lives in water.
measles, e.g. *Bana banji bakafwa abulwazi bwakabombwe.* = Many children died from measles. Also *cifwumu.*
a small barbel, e.g. *Ndajaya kabondo komwe nindali kuloba.* = I caught one small barbel when I was fishing. Also *moondo, mondo*

Adam's apple, a lump, goitre, e.g. *Muntu oyu ujisi kabozu kapati.* = This person has a large Adam's apple. *Kabozu kacili kaniini kalasilikika.* = When a goitre is still small it is curable Also *kagoyooyo, kankulumino, igolyo-golyo.*
type of edible mushroom, = *kabozu kamoomba*
the shaft of an arrow.
small reed, e.g. *Kaindi kabu kakali kakufwepela.* = Long ago a small reed was used for smoking. Also *lubu*
a whim, a passing mood, e.g. *Kabuko nkabi.* = Moodiness is bad. *Ulaa tubuko.* = He has moody spells. Also *kabundi*
a small *mubula* tree. e.g. *Aaka kabula kakazyala mbula zinji.* = This small *mubula* tree has many fruits.
a small storage bin for ground-nuts, a pole and dagga granary, e.g. *Bikka ndongwe mukabule.* = Put the groundnuts in the small storage bin. Also *kabbule, katala.*
a trap for catching every variety of game, e.g. *Basyaneene bakajaya banyama banji muli kabulindi.* = My grandfather killed many animals in a trap. Also *nkona.*
a bit of iron, e.g. *Kakamuyasa kabulo muliso.* = The piece of iron pierced him in the eye.
any spherical object, pl. *tubulunge*, e.g. *Basankwa babumba tubulunge twakuumya tuyuni abulongo.* = The boys mould round objects using clay for hitting little birds. Also *lubumbulu.*
a round object, pl. *tubumbulu*, e.g. *Tubumbulu twamalekani twamana.* = The pellets for the catapult are finished. Also *lubumbulu.*
a very small cake of tobacco, e.g. *Mudaala ulomba kabumbuluzana.* = The old man is asking for a little cut of tobacco.

a type of tree (strychnos potatorum), the fruit makes a soapy lather with water, but seems to be poisonous. Roots and fruit used to stupefy fish. e.g. *Bazeli bakajaya nswi zinji akabumbwi.* = The fishers killed many fish with poison. Also *mulombe, musisi.*
fickleness, e.g. *Ulaa kabundi.* = He/she is fickle, changeable Also *kabuko*
inquisitiveness, e.g. *Bana balaa kabusizya nkaambo bayanda kuzyiba.* = The children are inquisitive because they want to know. cf. *kabuzisya*
a borer-beetle, e.g. *Mapopwe angu amana bakabusumpe.* = My maize is destroyed by borer-beetles. Also *musunse.*
a little dog, a pup, e.g. *Kabwa kaniini takayandi kulya.* = The little pup does not want to eat.
a pebble, e.g. *Kabwe kaniini kabelesegwa mumalekani.* = A small stone is used for catapults.
a pearl, a diamond, e.g. *Basankwa baulisya tubwe twakakumweka.* = The boys are selling diamonds.
grumbling, e.g. *Bantu bamwi bacembaala balaa kabwekela.* = Some old people are fond of grumbling.
a hyena, e.g. *Kabwenga uyandisya kulya mpongo zyabantu.* = The hyena likes eating the goats of people. Also suntwe.
a poor and useless person, e.g. Uyeeya kuti mebo inga ndakupa mwanaangu, webo *okabwindi*? = Do you think I can allow you to marry my daughter, you who are just a poor and useless person?
a rat with a long mouth, e.g. Wakali kulaba-laba abee ngutumba wajata ka *bwindi*. = He was blinking like an owl which had caught a rat.
an abcess, e.g. Munene uciswa *kabyaabi*. = The old man is suffering from a very powerful wound. Also kanamalumbe
heavy rainfall, enough water to wade in, e.g. Ijilo kwakawa mvwula *yakacabwacabwa*. = Yesterday there was heavy rain.
impudence, e.g. Musimbi ulya ulaa *kacapicapi*. That girl is impudent. Also kanyemvwu-nyemvwu, kasapu-sapu, kacapo-capo.

a type of small dress, e.g. Muciindi eco wakazikwiide kubbukizya *kaccaccaacca* kakasamikidwe kucidooli camukuwa. At that time there appeared a type of dress which the doll of the white woman was wearing.
a rodent, e.g. *Kacecetula* kambeba takamvwugwi kufwambaana. = A rodent which gnaws is not noticed quickly.
a hag, a little old woman, e.g. *Kacembele kalatukila*. = The little old woman is insulting. (*kacembele kalwaano*, a praying mantis Also *kacembele gondo*)
a steer not yet castrated, e.g. *Kacende* aka kayakukomena akuba mucende mupati. This steer will grow and become a big bull.
an unidentified shrub with edible fruits, e.g. Bana balalya *kacende* musyokwe. = The children are eating wild fruit in the bush.

milk-porridge, e.g. Mwaunka kucigayo mukanantisye busu kutegwa bumwi tuzyoobujisye *kacese*. = When you go to the mill see that the meal is ground fine so that we can use some of it to make milk-porridge.
a little tail, e.g. Imbeba ijisi *kacila kasyoonto*. The mouse has a small tail. (*kacila kanombyo* = a dormouse, an agile mouse-like rodent with a bushy tail)
a small sore, e.g *Kacisa* kako kazwa busina. There is pus coming from your small sore. Also *cicisa*.

heavy falling of rain, e.g. Majwi aaciimbo comwe camalende ngaaya: "*Kacobocobo* kameenda nomuli kwa Moonze." The words of a certain rainshrine song are as follows: "The heavy falling of water, you who are there at Moonze's village."
an ear ornament, pl. *macoco*, e.g. Musimbi wangu ujisi *tucoco tubotu*
My girl-friend has beautiful ear-ornaments. Also inkwinta-nkwinta
a type of bird, a finch, e.g. Ijilo twakali kujaya *tuconco tunji* muzyoonde. Yesterday we were killing many little finches in the woods.
a small spoon, e.g. Kobelesya *kaconco* kusanina mwana. = Use a small spoon to feed the child. Also muungo, conco
bruise, e.g. Wakanyina *kacuzu*
kutii muntenda. = She had no bruise to help her realize that she was in an accident.
a bracelet of beads, e.g. Ndijisi *kadanda* kabulungu komwe. = I have one bracelet of beads. cf. *katenta*
a malnourished person, e.g. Kuti kana kamuntu kabula malili mabotu takakuli kabotu pe, kalaba *kadandala*. = If a child lacks healthy mother's milk, it becomes undernourished.
a little fish, pl. *tudiika*, e.g. Sunu tiitwajaya nswi zipati, twajaya buyo *tudiika*. = Today we did not catch big fish, we only caught little ones.
a mark left by scratching, e.g. Nguni wabamba *kadokwi* mumafwuta angu? = Who left a mark on my cream?

a drop, a spot, pl. *tudo-mbwi*, e.g. Amulyango wakabona *tudo-mbwi twabulowa*. = At the entrance she saw drops of blood. Mubili woonse waasamide deleensi lyakalaa *tudombwi-dombwi tutuba tukoya twankanga*. = Her whole body was clothed with a dress which had white spots like that of a guinea-fowl. Also kadonsi
a type of rodent, e.g. *Kadongolongo katijila mubwina nika-bona kaaze*. = The rodent ran into a hole when it saw a cat.
a small narrow line, e.g. *Ndabona kadongolongo kabasimunyewu*. = I have seen a small narrow line of black ants.
a drop, pl. *tudonsi*, e.g. *Wakabona tudonsi twabulowa munanda*. = She saw drops of blood in the house.
a small type of insect making honey in trees, e.g. *Ndaenena kadoonta acuulu*. = I spotted a small insect which makes honey on the termite hill. Also kadoonti
a small buck-goat, e.g. *Kadoonta nkinda-kaula jilo kaloboka*. = The small buck-goat I bought yesterday has escaped.
a little grass house or enclosure, pl. *tudumba*, e.g. *Wakabayakila kadumba bamakwaakwe*. = He built his in-laws a small grass house. Also cidumba.
self-will, impetuosity, e.g. Mulumaangu ulaa *kadwaadwa*, tasitikizyi kulima. = My husband is impetuous, he ploughs carelessly.

e.g. Bana balatwangila bazyali babo kuti tabayiide alimwi buumi bwabo *mbwakadyoli-dyoli antela kaminzi-minzi*. Children insult their parents saying that they are not educated and their lives are out-of date or of the village.
a small mushroom, pl. *bakadyumbwi*, e.g. *Ndalikujwa bakadyumbwi*. = I was plucking mushrooms.
early maize, e.g. *Kamusyanga mbuto yakafwamba njiibizwa kufwambaana*. = Plant the early maturing seed which is quick to ripen.
unsettled stomach, e.g. *Ndabaa kafwelufwelu ndiza ndiyanda kusoomona*. = I have an unsettled stomach, perhaps I will soon have diarrhoea.
a small young animal, e.g. *Ndatola kafwembe kuciko*. = I took a small calf for the marriage-payment.
the anus or rectum, e.g. *Kafwiti kamwana kazimba ncataambuki*. = The anus of the child is swollen that is why it does not defecate.
a type of bird, the snipe, e.g. *Kafwiti kalaa mulomo mulamfwu akukkala munsaa tulonga*. = The snipe has a long beak and lives near streams. Also lukukubwi, kafwitikabili.
a type of bird, the snipe, Also kafwiti, kafwitibili.

a moveable disguised grain-bin made of bark which could be hidden, pl. *tufwuba*, e.g. *Kaindi bakali kusisa maila mutufwuba*. = Long ago they used to hide the millet in a grain-bin. *Ifwuba liyobweda maila*. = A useless thing can contain millet. (Though a person looks foolish he can have what is valuable)
a water-pot, e.g. *Nkuku zinywa meenda mukafwuko*. = The chickens are drinking water in the water pot.
a small pipe for smoking, e.g. *Kafwuko kamunene kapwaika*. = The old man's small pipe is broken. Also mfwuko.
a blade, e.g. *Nkanone tufwulo akaleba*. = Let me go and sharpen the blades with an axe. Also cifwulo.

a type of tree *(ochna pulchra)*, fragrant yellow flowers, an important source of nectar, flesh of fruit is edible, light brown wood, can crack when drying, can be used for toolhandles, ash from bark gives a crude salt. e.g. *Kondibezela mwiini wakafwulwefwulwe.* = Carve me a handle from the *kafwulwe-fwulwe* tree. Also *mukanga, munyele, musengamenu, muswe, muzota-balozi.*
a sable-antelope, e.g. *Matwi akafwumba ali mbuli ambongolo.* = The ears of a sable-antelope are like those of a donkey. Also *Iweengu.*
a little dung, e.g. *Katuumpa kafwumba kanombe nkakatakwe kuzima.* = Let us burn a small lump of cattle-dung, it is the one which will not quench.
a sable-antelope, also *Iwengu.* A sable-bull = *kantanta, sikadinga*; a sable-cow = *lucinga*
a mark, a scar, a streak, e.g. *Kwacaala kafwundu-fwundu mpaawumwa cimboko.* = The mark remains where he was beaten by a sjambok.

a type of tree, *(dalbergia nitidula)*, fragrant white/cream flowers and pods. Exudes dark brown gum, used for turnery, tool-handles and fence posts. Is durable and termite resistant. Roots used for pleurisy, gonorrhoea and other complaints. Bark used for wound dressing and the treatment of pneumonia. Witchdoctor uses roots to extract 'missiles' fired from magic gun. e.g. *Balozi babelesya miyanda yakafwundula kulowa bantunyina.* = Witches use the roots of the *kafwundula* tree to bewitch other people. Also *mukonkoto, mukandanjase, mutatambeba, ndelele, mufwundansofwu, mukanga-nzovwu, mulya-nombe, mwamba.*
a charm in a snake skin or piece of cloth, e.g. *Kaindi basimafwaindi bakali kusama *tufwungo* mumaboko. = In the past boxers used to wear charms around their arms.

a disease difficult to cure, e.g. Bulwazi *bwakafwungo* tabusilikiki. = The disease of *kafwungo* cannot be cured. Cilatondwa koona amukaintu wakasowa inga waba *akafwungo*. = It is taboo to sleep with a woman who has had a miscarriage or has aborted because you may contract the disease of *kafwungo*. Mubili wakwe wakalipupungene mbubuli muntu wakali kuciswa *kafwungo*. = Her body became wasted like a person who was ill with 'kafwungo'.
a staff, a walking stick, e.g. Munene uligankizya *kafwunko* naenda. = The old man uses a walking-stick when he is walking.
type of tree (sweet fruit like fig), pl. *mafwuntwa*, e.g. Bana baya kukucela *mafwuntwa*. = Children have gone to gather *mafwuntwa* fruits. Also kasyuuntwa, kafwumu.

a grass-hut or temporary dwelling, pl. *mafwutu, tufwutu*, e.g. Basimbi bakali kuyaka *tufwutu* kumbo amunzi. = The girls were building grasshuts to the west of the village. Bukoko bwamantoombwa bwakali kukondwedwa kumunzi akaambo kakuti *mafwutu* ayo taakali *mafwutu* mayumu akonzya kusinkila zintu zimwi zyakali kunga zilakonzya kunyonyoona bukoko. = The mantoombwa beer was brewed at the village because these grass-huts were not strong enough to block certain things which could destroy the beer. Also cikuta, civwuka.
the Kafue river, e.g. Kuya ku Lusaka nkulanduka mulonga wa *Kafwuwe*. = When going to Lusaka you have to cross the river Kafue.
nickname for a lion, e.g. *Kagampu* ulalila muzyoonde. = The lion is roaring in the woods.
stench, e.g. *Inanda yoonse yakali kwiide kununka kaganko kaminsyu.* = The whole house was smelling with the stench of urine.

base of the spine, e.g. *Naaka-tiikkale a kauno kangu, mebo ndakakakwempa. Mpoona wakaakwiide kukkazya kagata ansi.* = When he was about to sit on my stool, I pulled it away. Thereupon he was just made to sit on the base of his spine on the ground.
A small grinding-mill, e.g. *Kagayo kamaanza amuncini wazisani ndakabaulila bataata.* = I bought a hand-mill and a sewing-machine for my father.
a scissors, e.g. *Kamundiletela kagele ndigele bauso.* = Bring me the scissors so that I cut your father's hair.
a water-channel, e.g. *Ndajana mondo zinji mukagolo kazwida ku-mulonga.* = I found many barbel in the water channel coming from the river.
a wooden-trough, e.g. *Bakali kubeza kagolo kaniini kubee mbwato omu mwakali kwiimikwa masumo.* = They were carving a small wooden-trough like a boat in which spears were stood up.
a ditch e.g. *Masiku wakoona anze buyo mukagololindi.* = At night he just slept outside in a ditch.
the long feather of a cock's tail, e.g. *Wakamusamika musimbi kagolyo kamukombwe.* = He dressed the girl with a long feather of a cock's tail. Also munimba.

a long tapering head-dress worn by hunters in long grass, e.g. *Bavwimi mubwizu bulamfwu balasama tugolyo kutegwa kabalibonya.* = Hunters in long grass wear long tapering head-dress so as to be seen (by other hunters). Also kaholyo
a disturbance, as of people, e.g. *Bamwi bantu tababeleki kabotu, balaa kagulukulu.* = Some people do not work well, they are a source of disturbance.

back of head, e.g. *Chiimbo naawa waakuumya kagulumwe abbwe.* = When Chiimbo fell, he struck himself on the back of his head on a stone. *Lumwemwe nkujana Iwaakwiide kusika kukaqulumwe!* = The smile was found just to reach to the back of the head!
a plastic container, e.g. *Sicikolo ujisi meenda mukagumbuli.* = The pupil has water in a plastic container.
a hole, e.g. *Inzoka yanjila mukaguugu mmulala.* = The snake which has entered the hole is a black mamba. Also kakumbwi.
habit of travelling about, e.g. *Musimbi oyu ulaa kaguwe ncatakwatilwi.* = This girl is a wanderer that is why she does not get married.
a type of bird, the skylark, e.g. *Kagwigwi kalalila mumubanga.* = A skylark is chirping in a mubanga tree.
a shirt, e.g. *Wakasamide kabbudula akahembe katuba.* = He wore shorts and a white shirt. Also izyempe.

hair gathered into a long cone, pl. tuholyo, e.g. *Bavwiimi bakajisi tuholyo amitwe kutegwa kababonana mubwizu bulamfwu.* = Hunters had their hair gathered into a tall cone so that they see one another in the long grass. Also kagolyo
a type of bird, the namaqua dove, e.g. *Kaiba ulalila mumusamu.* = The namaqua dove is chirping in the tree. Also katundulu.
a wrinkle between the eyebrows pl. twimba, Also kankusa, minya.
an eagle, falcon, e.g. *Kainga katola kana kankuku.* = The falcon has taken a chick.
stamen of flower, e.g. *Kajamya-jamya kaduba nkakapa bana kucisyango.* = It is the stamen of the flower which makes the plant fruitful.
abnormal sound of voice, e.g. Wakatalika kukanana, *jwi lyakwe lyakanyina akakaamo-kaamo*. = He began to speak, his voice was normal.
a tendon, e.g. *Mucembele wakasiya mutendu wanyama omwe wakali akakanda*. = The old woman left one piece of meat which was tendinous.

a little brewed beer or sweet-beer, e.g. *Nsima yabwiinga tiili nsima yamukusu yakubwenga pe; njakakandi, alimwi kasapwi*. = The lump of nsima at a wedding is not to be eaten but the wedded couple have to spit it out and allow other people to eat first.
a lock of hair, e.g. *Mwanalumi wakatenda kakama kamasusu amukaintu wakwe akali malamfwu*. = The husband cut a lock of hair from his wife which was long.
a bunch of vegetables, e.g. *Ndakaula kakama komwe kacisyu*. = I bought one bunch of vegetables.
a small bundle, e.g. *Baama bakandipa kakata kamunkoyo*. = Mother gave me a small bundle of munkoyo roots.
a headpad (sometimes of cowry shell), e.g. *Koleta kakata kaloozi ako*. = Bring that fibre headpad.
a snare or noose hung from a branch used to trap birds and small animals
a type of tree, with dark bark, straight thorns, good fibres, e.g. *Ndakajaya nziba mukakoka jilo*. = I killed a dove in a tree yesterday. Also *muunga-siya*:

an elbow, e.g. *Lumamba ulaa kacisa akakokola, ncatatandabiki kuboko*. = Lumamba has a sore on his elbow, that is why he cannot stretch out his arm. *Utamudonti kakokola mweenzinyoko*. = Do not nudge your friend with the elbow. *Wakalyuuma kukakokola*. = She beat herself on the elbow. i.e. If you have avoided some danger you spit on your elbow showing how lucky you are and will take care to avoid such a thing in the future.

an elbow, pl. *tukokozwi*, e.g. *Amane kulya, nguzu zyakajokela mu maboko akwe, waligankizya atukokozwi, wabuka, wakkala*. = When she had finished eating, power returned to her arms, she helped herself up by the elbows, she rose, she sat.
an elbow, e.g. *Basibukoko banduuma mabwe akakola*. The beer drinkers hit me with stones on the elbow. Also *kakokola, kakokozwi*.
the teat of a man, e.g. *Mainza wayaswa kamvwa munsaa kakole*. = Mainza was wounded by a thorn beside his teat.
string used as a girdle, e.g. *Moonga wakali koosa kakole kakusama mucibuno*. Moonga was plaiting a girdle for wearing around the waist.
a spring-trap, e.g. *Koleta kakole tukateye nziba*. Bring the spring-trap so that we trap doves. A variation of this trap is *kakole akwansimba*.
a type of bird, the plover, e.g. *Ndakajaya kakolekole kakajisi bana*. = I killed a plover who had young.
a little string, a snare, e.g. *Kamoosa kakole kakutezya*. = Plait a snare for trapping with. Also *kooze, kooye*.
a groove, a trench, e.g. *Meenda ainda mukakololindi*. = The water passes through a trench.

a gerbil, (a large burrowing mouse-like rodent found in arid regions). e.g. *Nyama yakakololo nimbotu ilaligwa abantu banji*. = The meat of the gerbil is good and is eaten by many people. *Kakololo a nsezi babalilwa kuciinga cambeba*. = The gerbil and the wild cat belong to the species of rodents. *Wabija oyu kakololo wamuntu!* = How bad this rat of a man is!
a frog, e.g. *Kakolo-lombwe kakazwa mudambwa.* = A frog came out of the dam.
type of tree (gives long straight poles) e.g. *Ciluli eci cijisi masomo akakolondumi.* = This roof has poles of the *kakolondumi* tree. Also *kakololondumi*
a small hammer rounded at one end, e.g. *Muyaki ugagaizya kakoma ananda.* = The builder hammers the house with a small hammer rounded at the end.
a small calabash, e.g. *Kondipa meenda akunywa mukakoma.* = Give me drinking water in a small calabash. Also *afwulu*
a spear with one long barb, e.g. *Isumo lyakakombe lilabosya kapati.* = The spear with one barb is extremely sharp. Also *kakombo.*
a spear with one long barb, e.g. *Kondipa sumo lyakakombo.* = Give me a spear with one long barb. Also *sinkombo.*
umbilical cord, e.g. *Wakalokelwa kakombokombo naakacili muvwanda.* = The umbilical cord was dropped on him when he was an infant (thereby causing impotence)

a thin and bony person, pl. *tukomfwu*, e.g. *Basimbi basunu boonse ntukomfwu.* = All the girls of today are thin and bony. *Nguni mucembelenyina muno mucisi umubaala? Tee kwiina. Boonse ntukomfwu twalo.* = Which of her old women companions can compare with her. There is no one. They are all just skinny.
meal ground and boiled for beer, e.g. *Kamujika kakonde tulobe bukoko.* = Prepare the meal for beer making.
porridge, e.g. *Basicikolo tabaciyandi kulya kakondo.* = The pupils do not want to eat porridge. *Ooyu musamu ngwakulya mukakondo.* = This medicine is for eating in porridge. Also *ceele.*
a small path, a narrow track, e.g. *Injombe zileenda mukakondo.* = The cattle are moving along a narrow track.
soil which has white lumps. pl. *tukonga*, e.g. *Bulongo bujisi tukonga tabuumpwi zitina.* = Soil which has white lumps is not good for burning bricks.

type of tree/plant (*Maerua variifolia*) smoke from burning roots said to help fever, e.g. *Mwana uciswa tuntumaanzi komusilisya busi bwakakonka.* = Treat a child with malaria with the smoke from *kakonka* roots.
a vegetable relish (*Corchorus tridens*) Also *telele.*
a small basket, a weaved plate, e.g. *Kobweza kakopa ukaulile madeede.* = Take a small basket and go and buy tomatoes. Also *insangwa*
a small container for cream or milk, e.g. *Amundipe mukupa mukakopo ndinywe.* = Give me milk in a small container for me to drink.
small swelling, e.g. *Kakoto kalacisa muliso lyangu.* = A small swelling in my eye is sore.
one eyelash hair, e.g. *Kuli kakoye kandinjila muliso.* = An eyelash hair has entered my eye.
a hair of the eyebrow, pl. *tukoye*, e.g. *Bamadaala banji balijisi tukoye tutuba.* = Many old people have white eyebrows.
a small stalk or cob of maize, e.g. *Kakuba kaniini aka kajisi popwe lipati.* = That small stalk of maize has a big cob.
a pot for conserving or carrying water, e.g. *Meenda azwa mukakuko mmabotu kunywa nkaambo alatontola.* = Water coming from a pot is good to drink because it is cold.
a small shoulder, e.g. *Kakuko kamwana kalacisa.* = The small shoulder of the child is hurting.
a snare, e.g. Ulati ngu-kwale wajatwa *mukakukubila*. = He was like a partridge caught in a trap. Also *kakkukka*
a running-knot, e.g. *Kamu-bamba kakulila alooye Iwampongo*. = Make a running-knot on the goat string.
bald head, e.g. Lyoonse wakali kugelwa *kakulu* kayi taakali kuyanda *mvwi* kuti kazilibonya. = He was always shaven bald as he did not want the grey hairs to be seen.
a small hole in the ground, e.g. Inzoka yakalilizingaide *mukakumbwi*. = A snake had coiled itself up in a hole in the ground.
a cap, e.g. Twakajana mudaala kumutwe usamide *kakundanyina*. = We found an old man wearing a cap. Also *kakepesi*
a group e.g. Uyakujana mpobabede *nkakungo*. = You will find where they are in a group.
the base of the back, e.g. *Kakungu kamwana kalacisa nkaambo wawa*. = The base of the child's back is sore because she fell.

a violet tree-snake, a variety of boomslang, slightly venemous, feigns death and is like a piece of wood, e.g. *Kakuni talumi ccita wamutalika*. = The violet tree-snake will not bite unless you provoke it. Also *kaankuni, siboninsonje*
a small piece of firewood, e.g. *Koleta kakuni kasyoonto tuyoosye ndongwe*. = Bring a small piece of firewood so that we roast groundnuts with it.
a borassus palm-tree, e.g. *Bamacembele bakaunka kukucela mavwuma kukakunka*. = The old women have gone to gather palms from the borassus palm-tree. Also *kamvwuma*.
a small valley, e.g. *Inombe zilacela mukakunka*. = The cattle are grazing in a small valley.

a very small worn hoe, e.g. *Kamubweza kakuta tukeenge cuumbwe*. = Take a small hoe so that we mark the grave. (This hoe is taken away by the father when he has marked the grave, that is why they usually use an old hoe rather than a new one)
small grass-screen, e.g. *Bakayaka kakuta kaniini kukwabilila muwo*. = They built a small grass-screen to shelter from the wind.
a fig tree (it's fruit = *inkuyu*), e.g. *Kakuyu akaya kalizyede kapati*. = That fig tree is very prolific.
a string of beads, a crown of beads, a necklace, pl. *tukuze*, e.g. *Bamakaintu bakali kusama tukuze mucibuno*. = The women were wearing strings of beads around the waist.
a scratch, e.g. *Ndakapuluka muntenda yamumugwagwa kakunyina kakwambu*. = I was saved frpm a road accident without the least scratch. Also *kankwambu, kankwamu, mukwambululu*.
small loose particles on the bark of a tree, e.g. *Kakwamu kazyila amusamu ulya katapukila ansi*. = The particle has fallen down which has come from the bark of that tree. Also *kafwapu*
a flaw, e.g. *Cilaa kakwamu*. = It has a flaw.
a young mealie-cob, pl. *tukwapa*, e.g. *Zipoka zijisi tukwapa*. = The stalks have produced young cobs.

animal-skin, e.g. *Mutinta wakabweza mwanaakwe wamubbala a kakwapili nkaakali kusama*. = Mutinta took her child and carried it in the animal-skin she was wearing. *Wakayala kakwapili nkaakajisi walivwunga*. = She spread out an animal-skin which she had and covered herself up in it.
whooping cough, tuberculosis, e.g. *Tubambo twakali kulibonya*
muntu mulwazi uutabukili bulo uuciswa *kakweekwe*. = The little ribs were to be seen like those of a sick bed-ridden man who is suffering from tuberculosis.
a small maize-cob cover, e.g. *Kakweelele kapepukila mucikko*. = The small maize-cob cover fell into the fire.
the upper-stone for pulverizing red ochre or snuff, e.g. *Bacembele basila tombwe akakwizyo*. = The old lady is grinding tobacco with a grindingstone.
a knot, e.g. *Kobamba kakwizyo akooye*. = Make a running-knot on the small rope.
hide and seek game played by children, e.g. *Bana basobana kalaambe mangolezya*. Children play hide and seek in the evening.
a riddle, conundrum, e.g. Mutinta ulatupa *kalabi komwe*. = Mutinta will give us one riddle.
conundrum, riddle, tale without song. Also *kalabi*.
a fish-trap, fish-string, e.g. *Baalumi bajaya nswi akalabwi*. = The men have killed fish with a trap.
the appendix, a wormlike appendage (of the caecum) within the stomach, e.g. *Kuli tulonda mukala-kasyoonto*. = There are sores on the appendix.

a small palm-leaf, a strip of palm, e.g. Mudaala ubamba cisebe cansuwa *atulala*. The old man is making a funnel for the milk gourd from small palm leaves. Amulete *kalala* toombele cisuwo. = Bring us a strip of palm so that we weave the edge of the basket.
a patch of unburnt grass left after bush is burnt, pl. *tulala*, e.g. *Muluya kuli tulala tunji*. In the stretch of burnt bush there are many unburnt patches.
short-tempered, lunacy, e.g. *Kuti bantu bamwi bacembaala balaa kalalu*. = If some people grow old they can fly into a fury.
a white frog which lives in the water, e.g. *Mwana wakkalwa kalamatilabbende*. The white frog is sitting on the child.
a small white frog Also *kanamatila-bele*.
a children's game (hide and seek), e.g. *Mweenzuma yamuluma nzoka notwali kusobana kalambe*. My friend has been bitten by a snake when we were playing a game.

a large hole in the ground made by water, e.g. *Wakalanga kubusena kwakali kalambo kalamfwu kapati bamwi nkobati kasyaleza (ifwumbwaleza)*. Aaka kasyaleza cakali cilindi cilamfwu kapati, tiicakali kubonwa ankocigolela. = He saw a place where there was very deep hole which was said to be dug by God. This divine creation was a big hole, it was not possible to see the bottom of it.
a pool of water, e.g. *Naakavwumbulwa ngubo, wakabaanga muntu wakazwa mukalambwa*. = When he was uncovered from the blanket, he seemed like a person who had come out of a pool of water.
eternal fire, e.g. *Bayakuloba mukalambwe kamulilo*. = They will perish in eternal fire.

noon, 12.00 hrs. e.g. *Moota wakasika akalanga-bwaaseme*. The car arrived at noon. Bakaya kumunzi kukususula zilyo akalangabwaaseme akukotoka alundindiwana. = They went home to have their lunch at noon and knocked off in the afternoon.

a piece of cloth covering the genitals, e.g. *Izyuubo-ubo zyoonse kacembele kakasamununwa kwasyaala buyo kalapi abusyu*. = The little old woman was stripped of all the ragged pieces of blanket with which she covered herself,
a tobacco-plant (pink flower), e.g. *Tusiko twakalazyalazanga twasyuuka kabotu.* = The stems of the tobacco-plant are growing well.

a traditional axe, e.g. *Wakamu-gonka kaleba ncaakafwa.* = He struck her with an axe that is why she died. *Wakaide kudenketa nkata yaloozi, wasowa akaleba akulubikka luno luyumu nta.* = He threw down the bundle of fibres and threw away the axe and started to run very fast.

a tin container, with handle, e.g. *Simpongo ulalibambila keembe, nkoli, myuumba, kankuli, cisumo, a kaleke kakujikila musozya wanyabo.* = The goatherd prepares for himself an axe, a club, barbed spears, a gourd, a small spear, and a container for cooking bean stew. *Amundipe bukoko mukaleke.* = Give me beer in a container.
an arrow with a short head, pl. *tulembe*, e.g. *Kaindi twakali kujaya bayuni abanyama atulembe.* = Long ago we were killing birds and animals with small-headed arrows.
a fig tree, e.g. *Buyuni bunji bulya nkuyu mukalembela.* = Many birds eat figs in the fig tree.
potatoe or cassava leaves, e.g. *Cisyu cakalembula cilababotela bamatumbu.* = Cassava leaves are liked by suckling mothers.

type of plant (Ammocharis tinneana), the pounded heated root is applied after cooling to relieve swelling from sprains. e.g. *Amumucumbe kalemukoko mpaafwuyuka mwana.* = Rub the child where it has a sprain with the powdered root of the *kalemukoko* tree.
the Creator, e.g. *Bantu a zintu zyoonse zyakalengwa a Kalenga.* = People and all things were created by the Creator.
a type of bird, the sparrow, e.g. _Kaleze katyoka kababa takauluki._ = The sparrow's wing is broken, it does not fly.
a type of bird, the linnet, e.g. _Kalezekaimbi kalaimba kabotu._ = The linnet sings beautifully.

a small beard, pl. _tulezu_, e.g. _Bantu bamwi bayanda kulekela kalezu._ = Some people like to let their beard grow. _Bamadaala bakali kwiile kulijata tulezu nibakamvwa lufwu Iwamwami._ = The old men just held themselves by the beards when they heard of the death of the chief. _Kalezu kalamfwu kakooswa mbuli mukkwilo._ = The long beard was plaited like a cattle-whip.
a small amount of money, e.g. _Kaswi aka kaulwa kali kaniini buyo._ = This little fish costs only a little money. Also _mali_.
disturbance, e.g. _Kunyina ni-kwakazyibidwe kuti buzuba oobu kulaba kalikiliki kali boobu._ = It was not known that on this day there would be such a disturbance.
a sensitive bush-insect, e.g. _Kalikumbate nkauka kamvwa kapati._ = The _kalikumbate_ is a bush-insect which is very alert.
sensitive plant, like the insect it folds up when toched.
a slender kind of locust, pl. _bakalila-musyolo_, e.g. _Bamwi bantu balalya tusozi tuunga bakalila-musyolo._ = Some people eat a slender species of locusts.
an inedible mushroom, e.g. _Kalima-beenda mbowa bukola, tabu-ligwi._ = _Kalima-beenda_ is a poisonous mushroom, it is inedible.
an edible mushroom, e.g. _Kalima-bweenda mbowa bunona kapati._ = _Kalima-bweenda_ is a very delicious mushroom.
a small feather, e.g. Cheelo wakamusomona *kalimba* nkabela Mwiinga wakaba musamu. = Cheelo removed a feather and so Mwiinga became a tree.
a hand-piano, e.g. *Kalimba* kako kalila kabotu. = Your hand-piano has a lovely sound. Also kankobela.
small ligament checking the motion of the tongue (fraenum), e.g. Ndazwa mate kukalimilimi nindamvwa kununkila kwanyama. = My mouth watered at the back of my tongue when I smelt the aroma of the meat.
proud feeling of a succesful farmer, e.g. Ncibi kulipa *kalimilimi* inga bakulowa bantu. = It is bad to boast as a successful farmer because people may bewitch you.
a light job, e.g. Mumupe *kalimo* kaniini mwana oyu. = Give this child a light job.
measurement of land, e.g. Amuka-tebule *kalimo* kanyemu. = Go and harvest a patch of groundnuts.
a small hole, e.g. Tulabikka mpopwe yomwe mukalindi komwe. = We put one maize-seed in one hole.
a small washing pot, e.g. Kobikka meenda asalala *mukalisukulido* usukulule zisani. = Put clean water in the small washing-pot to rinse out the clothes. Also kabiya, kakata.
a tooth-brush *kaliyoliyo* a type of bird, the small kingfisher, e.g. *Kaliyoliyo* kalaguna-guna mutwe. = The small kingfisher nods its head.
behaviour, e.g. *Kalizyo* kasyuu-mbwa kalayoosya. = The behaviour of a lion is frightening.

name given by midwife to newly born child, e.g. Mazina manji ngaakalo antela ngaabusasa. Ino ndizina nzi litegwa ndyaakalo? Eli ndizina mwana ndyaulikwa amucembele wakwe wakamutumbusya; ulaulikwa zina eli buzuba lyaloka lulila antela lukombo-bombo. = Many names are called akalo or busasa. This is the name of the child given by his midwife when s/he is delivered; s/he is given this name on the day that the umbilical cord drops off.

a little bed, e.g. Simpongo tajisi lubono lunji munanda yakwe, pele muli *kalo* kamatete kakalukwa aloozi Iwamubuyu. = A goatherd has not much possessions in his house, he only has a small bed made from reeds tied together with mubuyu fibre.
a fish-hook and line, e.g. Amukanduulile *kalobo* nselobya nswi. = Buy me a fish-hook so that I can hook fish with it.

a gynacological problem, e.g. Mukaintu uciswa *kalobola* usilisigwa mujola-bafwu. = A woman who has a gynacological problem is healed by the use of certain roots. Munzya wakatalika kuciswa bulwazi mbobaamba kuti *kalo-bola*. Eeci cakaletelezya kuti ooyu muka-intu katamiti pe. Munzya began to be ill with the sickenss they call *kalobola*. This caused this woman not to conceive.
a fishing-rod Also *kalobo*.
a fish-hook Also *kalobo*.

a toe, e.g. Mwana wayaswa kaunsyakwale *akalolomi*. = The child has been pierced by a small thorn on the toe. (When you chase after a partridge you can be pierced by such a small thorn, then when you stop to remove it the partridge escapes, kaunsya-kwale = that which allows the partridge to fly away) Cilacisa mumoyo, nkuyaswa *akalolomi*.
a young boy, a lad, e.g. Akaya *kalombe* kalayabila kabotu. = That young boy sings the kuyabila song well.

a small sore, e.g. Aaka *kalonda* takaponi kufwambaana. = This sore does not heal quickly. *kalonde* alchohol, distilled liquor or spirits, e.g. Sunu bantu banywa bukoko *bwakalonde.* = Today the people are drinking spirits.
a stream, e.g. Kunyina meenda mukalonga omu. = There is no water in this little stream.
a water-furrow, irrigation channel, e.g. Ku Nakambala balabelesya tulongo tunji kwiida minsale. = At Nakambala they use many irrigation channels to water the sugar-cane.
a small earthen pot, a small cooking pot for vegetables, e.g. Tujikila muka*longo.* = We cook in a small earthen pot.
akali kubila *mukalongo* kakali acikko. = The water in the small earthen pot on the fire was boiling.
a small line, e.g. Tuuka tuleenda *mukalongo* kunjila mubwina. = Insects go in a line to enter the burrow.
a trace of blood, e.g. Musankwa walikusoomona kalowa. The boy had a trace of blood in the stool.
cooked offals mixed with blood, e.g. *Kalowa kampongo kalanona.* = Cooked goat-offals mixed with blood are tasty.
a type of edible mushroom, e.g. *Kalowaboombe* mbowa busubila pyu. = The *kalowaboombe* mushroom is very red.
a type of fish, e.g. *Kalubale* ninswi italigwi baminsyi. = Kalubale is a fish which is not eaten by pregnant women. Also syaamwaama.
intensive heat of the sun, e.g. Eeci cakali ciindi zuba nolyuumpa ansi kapati cakalubulubu. = This was the time when the sun was burning the land with intensive heat.
a type of green relish, plants diced and cooked 30 min. e.g. Sunu twalikulisya cisyu cakalubabwanga. = Today we were eating a green relish. Also *kalubya-bwanga*

a plant, root heated in water, sips of the liquid said to relieve upset stomach. e.g. Kuti kamucisa mwida, konywa miyanda yakalubaluba. = If you have stomach pains, drink the root juice of the kalubaluba plant.
wild vegetable which has flowers, e.g. Bacembele baya kukucela cisyu cakalubyabwanga. = The old lady is going to collect a flowering relish.

a type of bird, a turkey, pl. bakalukuni, e.g. Kumitwe bakasamide musyini wamapepe abayuni basiyenesiyene mbuli basikakonze, batumba, bacuungwe, *bakalukuni,* bajule aimwi misyobo yabayuni. On their heads they wore a crown of different birds feathers like jackal-buzzards, owls, vultures, turkeys, secretary-birds and other types of birds. Also *ipilu*
umbrella, e.g. Kamubweza *kaluli,* ndiza mvwula ikamujane munzila. = Take an umbrella, perhaps the rain will find you on the way.
a small roof, e.g. Bapati bayaka *kaluli*
kandongwe. = The elders are building a small roof for the little groundnut granary.
madness, e.g. Sincinko ujisi *kalulu,* tacizyi ncacita. = The insane person who is crazy does not know what he is doing. Also *kalalu.*
a rabbit, e.g. *Kalulu* nkanyama kajisi matwi malamfwu alimwi kamaanu. = The hare is an animal with long ears and is intelligent.
a type of tree, e.g. Kamuya kumuunda *wakalulu* mukacele myuungu. = Go to the field of the *kalulu* tree and gather pumpkins.

a leech, e.g. Amukasonde kumunanga ubelesya *kalumabazela, tumvwe wamulowa mwana. = Let us go to the withchdoctor who uses a leech so that we understand who has bewitched the child. (the leech can be used in the process of divination) Also munsyundu, musyundu, kaluma-babuzi.
a traditional one-stringed musical-bow, e.g. Musankwa wakajaya *kalumbu kakwe*. = The boy broke his one-stringed musical-bow.
the third dice thrown in divination, e.g. *Inkakata yakalume taiko pe*. = The third dice is missing.
a small (detached) hill, e.g. *Kamutanta akalundu awo*. = Climb up on that hill.

a type of tree (*Strychnos innocua*), monkey orange, wild orange: wood is hard, inclined to split, leaves eaten by livestock, flowers frequented by hornets, seeds yield a reddish fixed oil and have emetic properties, the fruit pulp is good to eat raw or make marmalade and can be dried and used many months later. Also used as a remedy for dysentry or to make ear-drops. The oil from seeds and pulp can be used for soap-making. e.g. *Basimbi babamba nsipa zyakalungi*. = The girls are making soap from the seedoil of the *kalungi* tree. Also muteme, mutu.
a small bead, pl. tulungu, e.g. *Milemba ibambwa atutenta twatulungu*. = Face-veils are made from strings of small beads.
a pool of water, e.g. *Basimbi bakanjila mukalungu kameenda*. = The girls went into a pool of water. Also kazyiba
the favourite, e.g. *Ooyu mwana musimbi kaali kalungu kaamoyo kuli banyina*. = This daughter was the little bead of her mother's heart. i.e. the favourite.
a flexible rod, a switch, e.g. *Bacembele bakauma basimbi akaluso*. = The old woman beat the girls with a switch.
an islet, e.g. *Inombe zyajanika akaluzi*. = The cattle were found on a small island. Also insumbu, kasumbu, kasuwa
an epidemic, pestilence, infectious disease, e.g. Sikalileke nkalwalo kajaya. = AIDS is a disease which kills.
kamaa= He had epilepsy. Also injowela
the grave of a respected chief, used as place of prayer, e.g. Bana baku*kalya balalemekwa*. = The people who belong to the chief's grave are respected.

a flight in panic, e.g. *Basankwa nibakatalika kulwana, bakaintu abana boonse kakaide kuba kalyalyalya musyokwe*. = When the men started to fight, the women and children ran away into the bush in panic.
a traditional dance, e.g. *Bamacembele balicizyi kuzyana kalyaba*. = The elderely women know how to dance the *kalyaba*.
small entrance to a mouse hole or other small animal's burrow. e.g. *Kamusinka kukalyango*. = Block the burrow at the entrance.
intense short-lived rain, e.g. Kaindi kasyoonto kwaba kalyobolyobo kameenda. = In a short space of time there was a heavy but brief rainfall.
a swing, e.g. Bana balalyuumbwa akalyuumbo. = The children are swinging themselves on a swing.
a type of bird, the flycatcher, e.g. Kayuni kamabala kalya buuka. = The fly-catcher eats insects.

beer brewed for sale, e.g. *Banyina Mutinta bakaunza kamando kutegwa basambale mwana ajokele kucikolo*. = The mother of Mutinta began to brew beer for sale so that she could sell it and so that her daughter could return to school.
a boys' wrestling game, e.g. Musankwa watyokela mukamando. = The boy broke a bone in wrestling.
neuralgia, pleurisy, e.g. Bamaama bakafwa kamanu mucamba. = My mother died of pleurisy in the chest.

name of a tree, e.g. Mumwezi wa Mulumi bapati balatalika kubikka matuvwu aamusamu wiitwa kuti kamaumba munsuwa zyabo. Oyu musamu ujisi nguzu zyakubunganya mafwuta aamunsuwa. = In the month of February the elders begin to put the leaves of a tree called kamaumba in their gourds. This medicine has the power to bind the oil in their gourds.
grey sweet-potatoe, e.g. Twakasya kapati kambala. = We dug mostly grey sweet-potatoes.
a bullet, e.g. Muntobolo kuli buyo kambala komwe. = There is only a single bullet in the gun.
a whirlwind, gust of wind, storm, e.g. nanda yakavwumbulwa akambizyi. The house was unroofed by the whirlwind. Also kapepele
a witness, e.g. Bantu balayoowa kuba kamboni kukujaigwa kwamuntu. People are afraid of being a witness to the murder of a person.
pupil of the eye, e.g. Kamboni katoogwa muliso lyamwana. The pupil of the child's eye has been blinded.

the medicine or charm which makes one rich, e.g. Kambuma tacili cintu cipati pe alimwi tacipenzyi pe. = The medicine (kambuma) is not difficult or troublesome to acquire. Ulaa nanda ujisi kambuma kamali. The owner of the house has a charm for making himself rich. kambumbulu a small round object made of clay used as a projectile to kill birds, pl. tumbumbulu, e.g. Bana babumba tumbumbulu twakujazya tuyuni. = Children mould small round clay objects to kill birds.
cock-crow, early in the morning, e.g. Kacili kambundu nitwasika mumuunda. = It was early in the morning when we reached the field.
a cake of mbula fruit, e.g. Bacembele bandipa kambuumbu kasyoonto. = The old lady gave me a small mbula cake.
a bun, pl. tumbuwa, e.g. Bana bayanda kulya tumbuwa. = Children like eating buns.
a swallow, pl. tumebezya, e.g. Tumebezya tulauluka kakunyina kulyookezya. The swallows fly without resting. Also kamembya.
a wooden milk-bucket, e.g. Kamutila mukupa mukamelo. = Pour the milk into the wooden milk-bucket. Also cibisilo.
a type of bird, the swallow, pl. tumembya, e.g. Tumembya tubonwa mainza. = Swallows are seen during the rainy season. Also kamebezya

the oesophagus, the gullet, e.g. Mwana waingwa kafwuwa kanswi akameneno. = The child has been choked by a small fish-bone in the gullet. Kabacilya buci umwi mulombwana wakalidikizya anzuki mpoonya yakamuluma akameneno. = When they were still eating the honey, one boy ate a bee as well and thereupon it stung him inside the throat.
laziness in obeying, e.g. Mwana uulaa kamfwumfwu, tagwasyi bazyali bakwe. A child who is slow to obey, does not help it's parents.
a type of bird, the bulbul, e.g. Kayuni nkaanga kaminkwengwe kalakumba. The little bulbul is hatching.
a back bent inwards, e.g. Mainza ulaa kamini mubulema bwakwe. = Mainza is handicapped by a back which is bent inwards.
a smaller kind of bat, e.g. Kampaafwa kaleta nsinsini munanda. = The small bat brings bedbugs into the house.
a small type of bee, e.g. Kampakala takajisi buci. = The small bee does not produce honey. Also kampamakala.

a protective charm worn around the armpit, e.g. Sicibende ciindi naakatalika kukkala bakamucitila kampakatwa nkaambo wakaba alucisilwa. = At the tine when Sicibende started sitting by himself they made him a protective charm because he became sickly.
a head-band of 1", e.g. Mwami usamide kampalaba kabotu amutwe. = The chief is dressed in a beautiful head-band.
a bead-ornament about 1" broad, e.g. Bamuka mwami balasama kampalimba. = The chief's wife is wearing a bead-ornament.
mopani bee making honey in trees, pl. tumpamakala, e.g. Tumpamakala tujisi buci bunji. = Mopani bees produce a lot of honey. Also kampakala.
a canine tooth, pl. tumpanga, e.g. Mucembele uzutuzya tumpanga cituli canyama. = The old lady is cutting the piece of meat with her canine teeth as she eats. Also isonga-nyama.
a rib, e.g. Chimuka watyoka kampango nibamuuma ankoli. = Chimuka has broken a rib when they beat him with a club.
a chapter of a book, e.g. Ncinzi caambwa mukampango omu? = What is said in this chapter?

a little porridge sprinkled with powdered medicine, e.g. Munakaundu-ngana wakaunka kumunene kuya kumuzyibya kuti kampayu kamwana kakali kunga kazikunyugwa nokwakali kunga kulainda mazuba one, mwana wapona. = Munakaundungana went to the old man to tell him that it used to happen that if the little porridge for the sick child was sprinkled with powdered medicine, within four days the child would be healed.
top branches of a tree, e.g. Ncibi kulekela bana kuti kabasika kukampeleemfwa nobatanta mumisamu. It is bad to allow children to reach the higher branches when they climb trees.
small early kind of maize, e.g. Bana Haacizongo bakaoloka kale mu kampelya. = The people of Haacizongo have already started to eat the early maize. Also kafwamba, kayile
a habit, e.g. Musankwa oyu ulaa kampenda kabi kapati. = This boy has a very bad habit.
bead-ornaments for the head, a band of beads, pl. tumpinda, e.g. Bazyana masabe balasama tumpinda. = Those who dance the masabe wear headbands of beads. Also musinini, kansinini, milemba.
bead-ornaments for the head Also kampinda.
a beaded chest-cord worn by girls at puberty, e.g. Mooye usama kampombwe naakula. = A young girl wears a beaded chest-cord at puberty. Also kampombwa

a type of tree (Julbernardia globiflora), used for firewood, heavy constructional work, difficult to work. A good tree for bees with high quality nectar. Resin from bark used for dyeing and as a laxative. Rope is made from bark. e.g. Musamu wakamponi mmubotu kunkuni. = The kamponi tree is good for firewood. Also mumba, sandwe.

column2: light beer, e.g. Amundipe kampuuma bundle, e.g. Wakaide ku- kanamala, ndinywe. Give me light beer gomena kampuuma kamvwulupu kaba- so that I drink.
a traditional hand-piano, e.g. Bantu balizya kanamala adilwe. = People play the hand-piano at a funeral. Also kankobela, kanombyo.

anthrax, a contagious disease of cattle, which may be transmitted to humans by inoculation, inhalation and ingestion. e.g. 'Mwana uciswa kanamalumbe. The child is suffering from anthrax. Wakali ankazi anga nkanamalumbe. = He was as persistent as if it was the anthrax disease. Also namalumbe.
an animal, like a cow, e.g. Nokaba kanamani kaboya komwe kumunzi takako. = There is not even a single cow in the village.

a stick or straw dipped in milk to be sucked, pl. tunamatila, e.g. Basinombe bakali kunywa cibbobbe atunamatila. = The herds were drinking the frothy mixture of fresh and sour milk through straws. Also sinsa.
a small frog, e.g. Kamukkala kalamatilabbende mwana. = A small frog sat on the child.
a small frog Also kanamatila-bbende.
a small axe with handle covered with copper wire, pl. tunamifwundi, e.g. Tunamifwundu tatulibonyi mazubaano. = The copper-wired handled axes are not seen nowadays.
carbuncle, abcess, e.g. Caano eci Mainza cakamucisa kwiinda bucisa kanamalumbe. (bamwi nkobati kabyaabi naa kataambwi) = This story pained Mainza more than a carbuncle.
a root for making sweet beer, e.g. Eeci cibwantu cakakumbizigwa akanamugoonko. = This sweet-beer had been brewed with the kanamugoonko root.
a chicken disease, e.g. Wakeenda cakutombaila mbuli nkuku iciswa kanamulonzola. = He walked unsteadily as a diseased chicken.
a cur, wretched dog, e.g. Aaka kabwa kakaile kuba kanamunamu nkokatalyi. = This dog has become very thin because of not eating.
reddish millipede, e.g. Kanditantalika kanani akuulu. = A reddish millipede has climbed on to my leg.
a type of bird, the swimpi or smaller partridge, e.g. Kancele tanywi meenda manji. = The smaller partridge does not drink much water.
a small strip of cloth, e.g. Swebo toonse Leza utujisilizyi akancinda. = We are all supported by God with a small strip of cloth.
craziness, e.g. Muntu oyu tanoneenzyi, ulaa kancinko-ncinko. = This person is not pleasant, she is insane.
a long narrow stretch, e.g. Kabukomena bulimo, mutalimi kancololo. = Extend the piece of land, do not plough a narrow section.
Also kancololo.
a grey kind of sweet-potatoe, e.g. Ingulube yali kudadaula kandolo. = The pig was rooting up the sweet-potatoe.
abnormally small in structure, e.g. Musune wabelesegwa cakwiindilila inga kaba kandondoyo. = The ox which has been used most frequently has become reduced in size.
a type of bird, a fisheater, e.g. Bana baniini bakali kwiimba Iwiimbo kumulonga kabaiya muyuni kandondwe. = The children were singing at the river imitating the fish-eating bird.
a kind of creeper, e.g. Kandongwe ulasilisya malwazi amwi. = The kandongwe creeper heals some diseases.
a cigarette, e.g. Bacembele bafweba kanduundu. = The old woman is smoking a cigarette. Also kasanga.
an abnormally smallsized thing Also kandondoyo.
aggressiveness, e.g. Baila mbambabo, bantu bakandwane-ndwane. = The Baila, that is how they are, an aggressive people.
a pool of water, e.g. Basimbi bazela nswi mukanembwa. = The girls are fishing in a pool of water.
a green relish, the diced buds are boiled for approximately 30 min. e.g. Twali kulya cisyu cakanembe. = We were eating a green vegetable relish.

ligament under the tongue, e.g. Mwana akagonkwe kanenda kali amulaka. = The ligament under the child's tongue should be cut. Lili kuli deenzya tutende nenda? = Where is the blade for cutting the ligament? Ulaa kanenda = He is a stammerer.
small pieces of iron, e.g. Mukanduulile kangengema kancinga, basa. = Buy me the rim of a bicycle, my friend.
a fez, e.g. Babbi nibakabona musilikani usamide kangundu, bakatija boonse. = When the robbers saw the policeman wearing a fez, they all fled. Also ingundu.
drowsiness, e.g. Musankwa waba tungungu mpoonaawo mpakkede. = The boy became drowsy right there where he was sitting.
anything long or high, e.g Kakali kangwala kamulombe. = He was a tall youth.
a bar for digging holes, e.g. Koleta kangwala tusisye zilindi zyakasanza. = Bring a bar so that we can dig holes for the platform.
a blade of grass, pl. mani, e.g. Nkaaka kani kamunenga mwana. = Here is the blade of grass which cut the child.
sugar, e.g. Cibwantu ncibakasaanguna kunywa mbucakali cakaniabbakala, bakalikkutide kale. = As the first sweet-beer had sugar in it, they were already satisfied.
a youth, e.g. Koleka kutukila kanikenike kutegwa kakulemeke. = Stop scolding the child so that it will respect you.
a small insect which make honey in trees, pl. tunjilamantongwe, e.g. Tunjila-mantongwe tulatowa. = Small insects blind one.
type of tree, e.g. Tuyuni tuyaka zinteente muli kanjuyu. = Little birds have built their nests in the kanjuyu tree.

a traditional hand-piano with iron prongs, wooden base and gourd resonator with hole covered by cocoon (nenda) of the paper spider (kijubi) which causes a buzzing sound, e.g. Nsyecizyi kusobanya kankobela. = I don't know how to play a hand-piano. Also silimba, likembe, karŋombyo, kanamala.

depression or hollow place, pl. tunkolola, e.g. Batalika kuyandaula musyokwe mutunkolola amumilonga. = They began to search in the bush in hollow places and in the rivers. Moonse mutulundu a mutunkolola wakali kuccovwa kapati. = He was riding hard all through the hills and valleys. Also kakololindi
a trench, e.g. Meenda alakunka mukankololomba. = The water is flowing in a trench.
rinderpest, (a cattle disease with fever and dysentery) e.g. Inombe ziciswa kankolomwena. = The cattle are sick with rinderpest.
bone at back of head (occipital), e.g. Musimbi wakanokola twe acikko akulilamba kukankolyo-nkolyo *kakwe.* = A girl took a little ash and smeared herself on the back of her head.

type of tree (*hyphaene ventricosa*), pl. *tunkomona*, doum palm, vegetable ivory, fan-palm. (The wood is good and takes a beautiful polish and is borer-proof. The palm has many uses such as for making rafters. Fruits, seedlings and leading shoots are edible, the sap can be drunk as palm wine or distilled as a spirit. Leaves used for mats, baskets. Fibres can be extracted to make string and grain bags.) e.g. *Tunkomone tula-janika kapati ku Maala.* = Palm-trees are found especially at Maala. Also *kalala, kankunka mapokwe, mulala.*
a small kind of palm or coconut tree (smaller than the borassus), pl. *mankomone*, e.g. *Kankomone kazyala mankomone.* = A coconut tree produces coconuts. Also *kakunka*
a small piece of tobacco cake, e.g. *Amundigwasye kankomwa mbiike.* = Give me a small piece of tobacco so that I make a cigarette.

a small calabash adorned with beads used in divining, e.g. *Munanga wakaboola kumwi mumaanza katumbete kankuli kasyoonto kakasamikilwe bulungu bwakali kulengelela mokali munsingo walo nkaakali kwiita kuti 'kankonko'.* = The witchdoctor came while clasping a small calabash which was decorated with beads which were hanging from its neck, which he called 'kankonko'.
necklace of beads Also *munkonde, kasambo.*

empty cob of maize, e.g. *Nafwa usoogwa buyo aakankosyi nkaambo inga tali muntu, ngusikalalu.* = When he died he was thrown away like an empty maize cob, because he was no longer a human being but was insane.
a necklace of beads, pl. *tunkota*, e.g. *Bamakaintu bakali kusama*
munsingo.* = The women were wearing bead-necklaces.

chicken excrement, pl. *mankotyo*, e.g. *Inkuku yalosya kankontyo munsima yabana.* = The chicken has defecated in the children's food. *Kamu-gwisya mankotyo ankuku bakkale beenzu.* = Remove the droppings of the chicken so that the visitor can sit down.
excrement, as of fowl Also *kankontyo.*
a very small kind of tampan infesting poultry Also *kampotyo*
a small water-calabash with stem, e.g. *Meenda amukankuli alatontola.* = The water in the small calabash is cold.
a shaven head, e.g. *Ciindi campeyo ncibi kubaa kankulu inga yaku-jaya mpeyo.* = During the cold season it is not good to shave the head because you will feel the cold.

a type of tree (*albizia amara*) Dark brown, heavy and strong wood used for furniture, turnery and general building. Fruit used for malaria, coughs and as an emetic. e.g. *Kuti waciswa tuntumaanzi, konywa bana ba-kankumbwila.* = If you are suffering from malaria, drink the medicine of the fruit of the *kankumbwila* tree.
a grass headpad or crown, e.g. *Mukaintu ubikkide kankungwa kunsi anongo amutwe.* = The woman had placed a headpad of grass between the water-pot and her head. Also *nkata, kasambo.*
type of tree, pl. *tunkunka*, e.g. *Bamadaala bacela bana batunkunka lyanzala.* = The old men gather the fruit of the *tunkunka* trees during a time of famine. Also *kankomona.*
a small pot for holding solids, pl. *tunkuntu*, e.g. *Basikale bakali kuyobola mbuto mutunkuntu.* = The ancestors were preserving seeds in a small pot.
a frown, furrow one's brows in an expression indicating disapproval, displeasure or concentration, e.g. Wakaangide buyo kankusa. He just tightened his forehead in a frown.
a scratch, e.g. Mutinta ulaa kankwambu akamukwamba kaluwe. = Mutinta bears the scratch where the leopard clawed her.
a scratch Also kankwambu
a mask, e.g. Bana balayoowa akutija kuti babona kankwamu. = Children are frightened and run away if they see a mask.
a slice, pl. tunkwamu kankwenene a faint stripe, e.g. Kamweenga kankwenene mpotutiisimpile. = Make a mark where we will end.
an ear-ornament, pl. tunkwintankwinta, e.g. Bamakaintu banji balayanda kusama tunkwintankwinta mumatwi. Many women like to wear ear-rings.
a hatchet carried when walking out, e.g. Munene uyenzya kanomba mmukali. The old man who is carrying a hatchet is aggressive.
a blade of grass, e.g. Ngooyu nkusyomeka kansanga kabwizu mumutwe kati nkacoolwe. = There he is putting a blade of grass in his head saying it is for luck. Also kasanga

a type of fish-trap, pl. tunseenga, e.g. Mumilonga balateya tunseenga mumpati-pati zyamabwe, inswi muziinda. In the rivers they set fish-traps in the gaps among the stones where the fish pass. Balabikka tunseenga cifwumofwumo. Inswi noziboola kutala amulonga zilanjila mutunseenga. Zilanjila kabotu, pele zilakakilwa kuzwa. Kumazuba balanuna tunseenga, balajana nswi zilatapata mukati, elyo balazisukumwida anze. = They set the traps in the morning. When fish come they enter the fish traps. They enter easily but fail to get out. In the evening they check the fish traps and find the fish struggling inside, then they unload them onto the ground.
raffia-palm, e.g. Mutaanga oyu wakalukwa amatuvwu akansene. = This basket was woven with the raffiapalms.
a catapult, e.g. Basankwa bauma tuyuni kwiinda mukubelesya kansipu-nsipu. = The boys hit the birds by using a catapult. Also malekani.

a type of mental sickness, e.g. Muntu ulaa kansondo watijaana kale. = The one who has a mental disease is already running about. kanswende venereal disease, e.g. Banabukwetene banjililwa kanswende tabeelede kusisa pe nkaambo kuti basisa inga tabasilikwi kabotu. = Married people who have been infected by venereal disease should not hide it, because of they hide it, they may not be healed easily.

bilharzia, urination with blood, e.g. Bana banji baciswa kansyuunsyu. = Many children suffer from bilharzia. Kusamba mucizyiba cameenda ateendi, cipa kansyuunsyu. = To wash in a pool of water which does not flow, causes bilharzia.
bilharzia, cf. kansyuunsyu kanta a bow, pl. tunta, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kulwanya tunta. = Long ago people were fighting with small bows. Also kata.
private parts, pl. tuntanda, e.g. Bana tabasisi tuntanda twabo. = Children do not hide their private parts. Also cintanda.
a small open hut in field, e.g. Munene ukkede mukantangali uyamina buyuni. = The old man seated in the open hut in the field is scaring away the birds.
a sable-bull, e.g. Muciba omu kuli mucende *wakantanta*. = There is a sable-bull in the kraal.
a kind of game, e.g. Bana basobana *kantayile*. = The children are playing a game.
a small store, e.g. Bana nda-batuma kukuula nsipa *kukantemba*. = I sent the children to buy soap at a small store.
a neck fetter, a kind of trap for small game, e.g. *Kantembo* kako kaja-ya *sulwe*. = Your trap has caught a rabbit.
soft branches, e.g. Loo-zi *lwakantembwani ndubotu kutafwuna*. = Fibre from tender branches is good to chew.

the little finger of the right hand, e.g. Ooyu musimbi wakakon-koozya citendele *akantengezya kakwe*. = This girl knocked on the door with her little finger. Mutinta usamide ntasa aka-*ntengezya*. = Mutinta is puting on a ring on the small finger of the right hand.

the name of a tree which is said to make people forget, e.g. Musimbi oyu uluba mbuli kuti waka-lya *kantengwa-kaniini*. = This girl forgets as if she had eaten from the *kantengwa-kaniini* tree. Also *kazungula-kaniini*.

a type of traditional string-ed musical instrument used by a girl in the seclusion of initiation, pl. *tuntimbwa*, e.g. Mooye usobana *kantimbwa muna-nda*. = The female initiate is playing a traditional stringed musical instrument in the house.
a small kind of wild orange, pl. *tuntondo*, e.g. Basimaasikili balya *tuntondo mumavwuli*. = Swifts (a type of bird) eat matondo fruit from mavwuli trees.
a flute, e.g. *Kantoolilo kasi-bwa amulomo*. = A flute is played with the mouth.
a small insect making honey in trees, e.g. Kanditowa *kantowe nindali kuccovwa namutendele*. = A small insect got in my eye when I was riding a bicycle.

luggage, e.g. Mainza wakacitaila *akantuunya* kakwe alwezo kutozya kucitisyini ca Kalomo. = Mainza moved slowly with his luggage on his shoulder going to Kalomo railway station. Wakabbalula *kantuunya* kakwe katuubo akupa mweenzinyina kati bafwambaane kweendesya akalyookezye. = He took down his luggage from his back and gave it to his friend saying that they should hurry up so that he could rest.
a type of fruit which turns black when ripe, e.g. Kumaulu wa-kasamide mabbusu asiya akoya *tunka-jolezya*. On her feet she wore shoes whose colour resembled ripe black fruit.

a plant (Croton sp.), dried shredded leaves used as a tobacco substitute. Used in ritual as an incense from roots inhaled by dying person. e.g. Mubili wamufwu baunanika musinza wa-*kanunkila kutegwa utaboli*. = They anoint the body of a dead person with oil from the *kanunkila* plant so that it does not decompose.
scent, smell, e.g. Luwo lutontola lwakalijisi *akanunkilizi kabulo-ngo*. = The cool breeze had a smell of the clay.
faint smell, e.g. Munyama ooyu wakalikulya kufwumbwa cintu cinu-nka *kanunko kabuntu*. = This animal was eating whatever had the whiff of human-kind.

a green relish (*Tetratelia tenuifolia*), diced stem, leaves and flowers boiled in three changes of water Dec.-Feb. e.g. Baama bajika cisyu *cakanunu-bwi*. = Mother has cooked a green vegetable relish. Also *kayunubwi* ---|---
a little finger, a toe, e.g. *Mwana walinontola akanwe.* = The child hit it's toe against something.
the crown of the head, e.g. *Mukaintu oyu uciswa kanyampwido, ncatayumuni nongo.* = The crown of this woman's head is sore. That is why she does not carry a pot on her head.
a fishing-net, pl. *tunyandi*, e.g. *Kanyandi kamudaala kalajaya atutaka.* = The fishing-net of the old man also traps small fish. Also *insabwi*
a child's bracelet of palm-leaves, e.g. *Mwana bamusamika kanyanga akuboko.* = They have dressed the child with a palm-leafed bracelet on the arm.
the large black mason wasp, pl. *tunyati*, e.g. *Tunyati ntwaanko ntukali kapati.* = The black mason wasps are fierce.
impudence, e.g. *Musimbi utalomene ulaa kanyemvwu-nyemvwu.* = A girl who is not respectful is impudent.
piece of land, e.g. *Balimi balayanda kuti aumwi kalaa kanyika kakwe.* = Farmers wish that each one has his own piece of land.

an edible grass (*Craspedor-hachis*), seeds boiled as cereal in Feb. e.g. *Ciindi canzala bamacembele bakali kuunga nseke zyakanzie-nzie.* = At a time of famine the old women were collecting the seeds of edible grass.

foolishness, e.g. *Lubanje lupa zintu zyaandene kubantu baandene: bamwi lubapa luseko, bamwi kanziimwa.* = Cannabis gives different things to different people; it gives some laughter; others foolishness. *Naakamana kufweba lubanje, meso akakkalikila, wakaba akanziimwa, mate akasakamuka mukanwa.* = When he had smoked dagga his eyes settled, he became stupid, the saliva

a dried pumpkin used for carrying things, e.g. *Ngooyu upakete tuubo twakwe, kanzuma, ntolomani akapika ujisi nzila iya kumantoolo.* = There he is with his packed blankets, his little pump-kin bag, cooking pots making his way to the stores.
perseverance, a quarrelsome disposition, e.g. *Ncibi kubaa kanzumananwa.* = It is bad to be intransigent.

a short time, e.g. *Kuli ziimo zyakulyaaba kumafwunze, limwi tazilangi penzi lili kumbele. Zilanga buyo kulikkomanisya kwatunzuzumina tusyoonto.* = There is a behaviour which gives itself to useless things and which does not look to the future suffering. It just looks to the pleasure of a few minutes.

a sleeping-mat, e.g. *Mutinta kunyina majwi ngaakaingula, wakaindilila buyo kunsanza kwakaanda kwakavwunteme kanongo kabacembele, walala, watalika koona.* = Mutinta did not answer a word, but went straight to the back of the old woman's house, she lay down on a mat, she began to sleep.
a defect, e.g. *Uulaa kapa tazimini akubweenzu.* = One who has a defect cannot conceal it, even as a visitor to a new place.

a stage or element in the performance of a traditional custom, pl. *tupaapa*, e.g. *Nkokuti tupaapa toonse awa mpotugola.* = Thereupon at that point we had finished all the stages of the tradition. + limbs of the body, e.g. *Nobakamana kumusundaukila, bakamoolola-olola mutupaapa toonse.* = When they had finished training him, they stretched all the limbs of his body.
a small clay drinking-cup, e.g. *Ulakasaazya tukeza kumbali amulilo mukapali.* = She warms the beer near the fire in a small drinking-cup. Also *kalewu*
a baby, e.g. *Mwana ucili kapamba ulabambwa kabotu.* = A child who is still an infant is well looked after. Also *kavwanda*.
a small shell, e.g. *Mudaala usamide kapande kankumba acamba.* = The old man is wearing the shell of a snail on his chest.
a small gourd (*mumbale* = a big gourd)
a share or portion, e.g. *Koba-abanya namunyo bana, aumwi umupe kapanzi.* = Divide the mellon among the children, so that you give each one a portion. Also *kapaanzi, kabeela*
a vessel used for milking goats, e.g. *Kuli mukupa musyoonto buyo mukapapa.* = There is only a little milk in the container.
hide, pl. *tupapa*, e.g. *Kaindi bana bacete bakali kusama tupapa twabanyama amakwibba aloozi.* = Long ago poor children were dressed in animal-skins and long bark-fibres. Also *kapaya, kakutu*

a pill, tabloid shape, e.g. *Kantu kapapali kaleela akalyango nokaceya.* = A flat thing can be fitted into a small entrance no matter how narrow. (*kabumbulu* = round pill, *katuntuli* = regardless of shape.)
spark from red-hot iron or wood, pl. *tupasi*, e.g. *Kuti lubulo Iwapya kapati lulapasauka akutapuka tupasi.* = If iron is very hot the sparks are crackle and are thrown off. Also *nsasi*
a chief's bodyguard and messenger, e.g. *Mwami watuma kale kapaso kukuleta muntu.* = The chief has already sent a *kapaso* to bring the man.
skirt, e.g. *Wakakkala ansi akutalika koosa looye Iwakwaanzya kapaya kakwe nkaakalikusama.* = She sat down and began to stitch the skirt which she had been wearing.
relish, e.g. *Cisyu cakapaya-kamulamu cilanona.* = Relish of *kapaya-kamulamu* is tasty.
a bit of, e.g. *Nkaambo nzi ncondipa keele kapela buyo?* = Why do you only give me a small portion of porridge?
a safety pin, e.g. *Komukopela kapenete mwana acibaki cakwe.* = Put a safety pin on the blouse of the child.

a prostitute, e.g. *Mutinta naakakomena wakaba kapenta.* = When Mutinta grew up she became a prostitute. Also *najempa, najompa, nakeempa, nacinzulu, nanzulu, nakeempwenene, kampuwe, mwaamu, muvwuule, kapwenupwenu, mutangazu kubasankwa, kaguwe, nanzalu, muzembela njanji.*
small fish, e.g. *Koya ukanduulile tupenta.* = Go and buy me small fish.
a notched piece of gourd, e.g. *Kamubabikkila tukoko tuniini bataata mukapepa.* = Put a tiny amount of beer in the piece of calabash for my father. Also *kapempa*
a small piece of paper, e.g. *Ndajana kapepa kaniini atebule.* = I found a small piece of paper on the table.
a small feather, e.g. *Kapepe komwe kalapeepuka mujulu.* = One small feather has been blown up into the air.
a calabash, e.g. *Kapepe kako kazwide zigwete-gwete. Nkanwa amenyo ako.* (a riddle) = Your calabash is full of different things. It is the mouth and it's teeth.
a whirlwind, e.g. *Kaluli kabutala kakavwununwa akapepele.* = The roof of the grain-store was blown off by a whirlwind. Also *kambizyi*.
the coldness corresponding roughly to the month of May, e.g. *Mumwezi wa Kaandakaniini nokatalika kapeyo.* = The cold season starts in the month of May.
a criminal, e.g. *Kapika wapegwa mulandu. = The criminal was given a case to answer.
a small cooking-pot, e.g. Kofwambaana umujikile keele mulwazi mukapika. = Be quick to cook some porridge for the patient in a small cooking-pot.
a small nail, a tack, e.g. Koleta kapikili tubambuluzye nsefwa. = Bring a small nail so that we repair the sieve. Also neele
a beetle found in the hard bark of a tree, pl. tupile, e.g. Tupile tujanika mumakwa tulaluma. = Beetles found in the barks of trees bite.
type of snake (the night-adder) poisonous, e.g. Bana baka-tija nibakabona kapilebunyangu. = The children fled when they saw a night-adder.
a short piece, e.g. Kondi-letela kooye nokaba kapimpila buyo, nkanji. Bring me a string, even a short piece, it is enough.
a stick used to light fire by friction, e.g. Bantu balabamba mulilo akapisyo. People make fire by making friction with a stick.
a captain, foreman, e.g. Babelesi tababeleki kabotu nkaambo kapi-tawu tako. The workers do not work well because the supervisor is not pre-sent.
a walking-stick, e.g. Muntu mukali wakauma mwana amutwe a kaponda. The cruel man beat the child on the head with a walking-stick. Also kafwunko.
a bandage, e.g. Mulwazi upambaidwe kaponda acilonda. The patient's wound is wrapped with a bandage.
a brush of tail, e.g. Kamusansamuna kasuko akaponda kamucila wajombe. = Wipe off the dust with the brush of a cattle-tail.
moulded tobacco, e.g. Kaponda wazilundu wakali kulula kapati. = Moulded tobacco was very strong.
a kid (young goat), e.g. Kapongo kakazyalwa jilo, kafwa sunu. = The young goat which was born yes-terday, died today.
(idiomatic usage) Musimbi ciindi eci wakali kulila mbuli muntu utayandi ani kuti mumoyo nkapongo. = At that time the girl was crying like a person who resisted, but in her heart she wanted it.
the pupil of the eye, e.g. Mwana watoogwa kaundu akapopwe kaliso. = The child was blinded by a sharp blade of grass-seed in the pupil of the eye. Also kamboni
mealie-seed, e.g. Mwana wapatilwa kapopwe mukutwi. The child's ear is stuffed with a mealie-seed.
small early kind of maize, pl. tupopwe-popwe, e.g. Oomu mumuunda kuli tupopwe-popwe tunji. = Here in the field there is a lot of the small early kind of maize. Also kampelya, kafwamba.
an ostrich, e.g. Mucisi cesu takubonwi kapowani. In our territory the ostrich is not to be seen.

a natural gap between front teeth, e.g. Musimbi uujisi kapozya-musozya ulandikonda. = The girl with a gap in her teeth delights me. Also kabende. kapuka a young palm, e.g. Kapuka aka kalafwambaana kukomena. = This young palm grows quickly. Also kupuku, kapuko.
a small hole, e.g. Konjizya bunweba mukapulo kanyeleti usume. = Thread the needle so that you can sew.

stump, round head of axe, e.g. Kapumpu kamwiini wakeembe ka-panduka. The round head of the axe is broken. Wakanyina malezu manji, twakali tupumpu-pumpu buyo kucilezu. = He had not much of a beard, there was just stubble.
a running-knot, e.g. Kosuma kabotu kutegwa kapunepune kakaluzi. Sew well so that the running knot is alright.
bag, e.g. Baliyumwide tupuntumende tuzwide mpasya zyakaulilidwe bali mumunzi. They were carrying bags of goods bought for the people back home.
shorts, e.g. Kaputula kamwana kaligwa mbeba. The pair of shorts of the child has been eaten by mice. Also kabbudula.
a suitcase, e.g. Kobikka tupayi twako mukaputumende weende. = Put your blankets in a suitcase and go. Also coola.
an inquisitive gaze, e.g. Imubbi ulijisi kapwenu-pwenu kakulanga oko akooku. The thief has an inquisitive look in looking here and there.
a type of edible mushroom, pl. bakapyupyu, e.g. Bakapyupyu mbowa bunona kapati. Kapyupyu mushrooms are delicious. Also kapyuupyu
a crack around finger-nail, e.g. Munyo wandinjila akasa ulacisa kapati. = Salt which entered the crack on my finger-nail is painful.
strong appetite for meat, e.g. Kasa kandipa kuyandisya kulya nyama. = The craving for meat made me long to eat it.
early morning warmth from the sun, e.g. Bakajana banyina bayotela kasaansa kunze ananda yabo. They found their mother warming herself in the morning sunshine.
bad language, e.g. Bamwi bakali kulilila mukasaaza. Some were mourning using bad language.

a space cleared after cutting trees for firewood, e.g. Nindakamana kugonka nkuni zyamasaba, ndakalima akasaba kangu. When I had finished cutting down firewood for storage, I ploughed my own cleared space.
a small tree cut down for firewood, pl. tusaba, e.g. Nguni walikutebba nkuni mutusaba twangu? = Who was collecting firewood from the small trees I had cut down?
cultivate things already growing = *-limina kasaba.*
a small thick forest, e.g. Ndakajana nzoka zinji mukasaka omuya. = I found many snakes in that thick forest.
a rod, a staff or walking stick, e.g. Munene wakauma musankwa akasako. The old man beat the boy with a stick.
a sleeping platform with roof but without walls, e.g. Sikuyamina uwona akasalo. The one watching sleeps on the platform. Also ngazi
a small hide, e.g. Bacembele basamide kasalu mucibuno. The old woman is putting on a small hide around her waist.
