an iguana, e.g. Kafwuwa kakasamba takapwaigwi kalakola. The bone of an iguana is never crushed for eating because it is poisonous. Also nabulwe.
the back-bone, e.g. Kasamba kakapongo kalafwambaana kubizwa. The backbone of a goat gets cooked quickly.

a bracelet or crown of grass, a necklace of beads, pl. tusambo, e.g. Musimbi wangu usamide kasambo. My girlfriend is wearing a necklace of beads. Sicibende naakabutuka, banyina bakatalika kumulukila tusambo. When Sicibende had grown, his mother wove armlets of grass for him. Bakaintu bakaindi bakali kuluka zimwi zintu nzyobakali kusama mumaanza zitegwa tusambo. Pesi tiizyakali zibotu nkaambo zyakali kunga caba ciindi kwanjila njina muli nzyizyo. = The women of long ago used to weave certain objects which they wore on their arms called 'tusambo'. But they were not good because after a while lice would get into them.
the shorter spitting cobra, e.g. Mwana wapiilwa kasambwe mumeso. = The child was spat in the eyes by the shorter spitting cobra.
propensity to insult, e.g. Uulaa kasampu-sampu, unyemya bantu banji. The one who continually insults, angers many people.
an upright plant, small shrub, slender shoot, stick, e.g. Amulete kasamu tujaye nzoka. Bring a stick so that we kill the snake.
a small common type of hammer, e.g. Kasando kazimina, twabula mbotugagaila. The small hammer is lost, we have no way of hammering.
chest, e.g. Kamembya kajisi kasando kaniini. = The sparrow has a small chest.
a cigarette, a small reed used as cigarette, e.g. Mwana tayelede kufweba kasanga. A child should not smoke a cigarette.
a small blade of grass, e.g. Koleta kasanga twiibuluzye inziniini mumukupa. = Bring a small blade of grass so that we remove the fly in the milk.
August, e.g. Mumwezi wa Kasangabimbe notulya nkolola zinji. = We celebrate many initiation ceremonies during the month of August.
a small bunch, as of mealie cobs, e.g. Baama bajisi kasankala kamapopwe matete. My mother has a bunch of fresh maize.
a young boy, a lad, a tall but slender man, e.g. Kasankwa kapaale kalayandwa abasimbi banji. A tall, wellgroomed man is loved by many women.
a small bottle-shaped granary, e.g. Mapopwe abuulwidwe abikkwa mukasantulu. = Shelled maize is put in the bottle-granary.
a twig, e.g. Muntu utandwa kumunzi usinkilwa kasanzu kasikomwa. = A twig or branch of a curved thorn-tree is placed at the door of the one who is driven from a village to stop him returning.
habit of insulting people, e.g. Kubaa kasapu-sapu cipa kusulaikwa abantu. To have a habit of insulting makes one hated by people. Also kasampu-sampu.
a round weaved flattish tray, e.g. Kotola cakulya kubeenzu mukasabyo. = Take the food to the visitors on a tray. Also kasebyo
a crown of grass, e.g. Mutinta wakali kuluka kasambo. = Mutinta was sewing a grass head-pad. Also kankungwa
a flattish round tray, Also kasabyo.
a bandage for broken limbs, e.g. Muntu ngubakatyola mabambo babbi, basilisi bakamwaanga kasengele. = The doctors bound with a bandage the person whose ribs the thieves broke.
an old torn basket, e.g. Tatukonzyi kubikka ndongwe mukasengele ako. = We cannot put the groundnuts in that old torn basket.
a whistle made from horn or the leaf of the munkowa tree used to decoy duikers.
a small horn used as a charm or ornament, e.g. Kasengo kamulozi kakabuluka. = The small horn of the witchdoctor has lost power.

a spring of water, e.g. Ooyu mulundu wakajisi kasensa kameenda katakali kuyuminina. This hill had a spring of water which did not dry up. kasesi naseau, e.g. Mukaintu naamita inga watalika kubaa kasesi. When a woman is pregnant she begins to become nauseated.
a small type of bat, e.g. *Kaseseko nkakaleta sinsini murŋanda*. The bat brings bed-bugs into the house. Also kaseeseko
abnormal sixth digit, e.g. *Mwana wakatumbukwa ijilo wakatendwa kaseza*. They removed the sixth finger of the child who was born yesterday. Also kalenda
a small hole of a musical horn, e.g. *Kasibi kamweembo kacili kaniini*. = (In making a musical horn) The small hole of the horn is still too small.
a whistle made from horn, e.g. *Amusibe kasibo banyama baboole*. = Blow the whistle so that the animals come. Also kasengo.
See kasibo.
the spirit of opposition, e.g. *Musankwa oyu ulaa kasiimwe, ulayanda kukazyanya*. This boy has a rebellious nature, he wants to argue.
an early type of sorgum with short stem, pl. tusili, e.g. *Tusili tulabinda kubizwa*. Early sorgums are quick to ripen.
small grey mungoose, e.g. *Kasilili kalanyenuna menyo kukonga nzoka*. = The small grey mungoose opens it's mouth and shows its teeth to frighten snakes.
a shrew, (a small insectiverous mammal), e.g. *Kasilibwindi kafwa nikasotoka nzila*. The insect-eating mammal died when it crossed the path. Dundwa = the jumping shrew.
very early in the morning, e.g. *Eelyo wazwide akasimbula, oosika kale!* = Well you must have started very early, seeing that you have arrived already!
a knot, e.g. *Beembezi bakamwaanga kasinanto mweenzinyina aku*musiya*. = The herders tied their friend with a knot and left him. Also kanio-kaamujaya.
a type of black ant, e.g. *Mwana walumwa kasindabeene*. = The child was bitten by a black ant.
the heel, e.g. *Musankwa ulyatya tunwempela nkaambo kasindi kalacisa*. = The boy is walking on tip-toes because his heel is sore.
neuralgia, illness of the chest, pleurisy, pneumonia, e.g. *Mudaala kakamujaya kasinga kamucamba*. = The old man died from chest-pains.
a small band, e.g. *Mooye usamide kasini kabulungu mumutwe*. = The female initiate is wearing a small band of beads on her head.
a readiness to reprimand, e.g. *Mudaala oyu ulaa kasinsyo lyoonse*. = This old man is always ready to reprimand.
a bottle top, e.g. *Bbodela lijisi kasinsyo kasubila*. The bottle has a red cap.
a short distance, e.g. *Mbutwakeenda kasinzo kasyoonto twakasika kwabo*. = We only travelled a short distance when we reached his home.
a type of bird, the blue-breasted tit, e.g. *Basankwa bakaenena kasise mumusamu*. = The boys spied a blue-breasted tit in the tree.
a fault, e.g. *Mainza wakali kuyanda mukaintu wakwe, pesi wakabwene kasiya muli nguwe*. = Mainza loved his wife, but he saw a fault in her. Also kampenda
an unploughed ridge between furrows, a balk, e.g *Kosiya kasokwe mumuunda ube mugelo*. = Leave an unploughed ridge between the furrows in the field.
a small monkey, e.g. *Kasokwe kakandilida nyabo mumuunda*. = A small monkey ate the beans in the field.

the hip, e.g. Bbabuka wakagwejuka kasolo naakali kuuma bbola. = Bbabuka's hip-joint got dislocated when he was playing football. *Ndalumba ndemubwa, ndemuzike, ndemucele, ndakambila akasolo ndemupenzi.* = I thank you, I am a dog, I am a four-footed quadruped animal, I am a slave, I slap myself on the hip, (a sign of gratitude), I am one who suffers.
a large arrow-head without barbs, e.g. *Kasonde nkubakayasya ngulube yangu, ndakajana munzila.* = I found on the path the large arrow-head with which they pierced my pig.

a needle, e.g. *Koleta kasonde tusumye masaka.* = Bring a needle so that we sew the sacks. kasonga kakulembya a nib, pl. tusonga, e.g. *Basicikolo bakali kulembya tusonga mumabbuku kaindi.* = Pupils were using nibs when writing in books long ago.
one who speaks before his/her turn, e.g. *Kasongo-songo mumuswaangano takayandiki.* One who speaks out of turn is not wanted at the meeting.
cap, e.g. *Nakalindu wakasamide dimpwilimpwi lituba akasoti katuba.* = The young woman wore a long loose white frock and a white cap on her head
a still-born child, e.g. *Bazikka kasowe mbaamacembele bakaleka kale kuzyala.* = The ones who bury a stillborn child are the older women who have ceased to give birth.

a disease (when a woman aborts or miscarries, and then practices forbidden rituals, she may then cause other people to contract this disease whose symptoms are sores, continuous coughing, backache, etc,) e.g. *Bulwazi bwakasowe bulakatazya kusilika.* = The disease of kasowe is difficult to cure.
locust, elongated with longitudinal stripes, pl. tusozibuzuba, e.g. *Tusozibuzuba tatuceli masiku.* = The long type of locusts do not feed during the night.
a type of edible mushroom, pl. bakasozya, e.g. *Basimbi baya kukucela bakasozya.* The girls are going to collect mushrooms.
a swelling or abrasion from a bite, pinch or blow, pl. tusuke, e.g. *Mubbi wakacaalilwa tusuke mubakali kumusyamba.* = The thief was left with bruises where they were pinching him.
dust, e.g. *Moota ulundumuna kasuko nuuyenda.* The car raises the dust when it travels.
a female disease, e.g. *Musimbi oyu uciswa kasukulwa.* = This girl has the disease of kasukulwa.
frequent stomach upset, e.g. *Kufwumbwa kuti ndalunduka inga ndaa kasukusuku.* Whenever I run I have stomach upset.
a small island, e.g. *Bwato bwakasowekede bwakaakujanika akasumbu kamwi.* = The boat which was lost was found on one of the islands.
castrated steer, e.g. *Kasune kabataata kakatolwa kuciko.* = The castrated steer of my father was paid as the bride-wealth.
a clay bowl, e.g. *Amubikke cisyu cabadaala mukasunsilo.* = Put the relish of the old man in a clay bowl.
grey jackal, e.g. *Impongo zyobilo zyakalumwa kasuntula.* = Two goats were attacked by a grey jackal.
the brown hyena, e.g. *Kasuntwe-malenda nkakali kwiinda suntwe mupati.* The brown hyena is more fierce than the larger hyena.
the sand-fly, pl. tususubwi, e.g. *Tususubwi tulayanda kunjila mumeso.* Sand-flies like to enter the eyes. Also kampotwa.
a quarrelsome disposition, e.g. Ncibi kuba akasusyo akati kabeenzinyoko. It is bad to be quarrelsome among your friends.
one hair of the head, hair beginning to grow, e.g. Kasusu komwe katalika kutuba. One hair has started to go white.
the sand-fly, e.g. Kasusuli kandinjila muliso. = A sandfly has entered my eye. Also kasusubwi.

a small black ant-hill, pl. tusuumbwa, e.g. Naakakatala wakakkala atalaa kasuumbwa. When he was tired he sat on top of a small ant-hill. Tusuumbwa tujanwa mumisena. = Small black anthills are found in the vleis.
sexual partner, mwana kasuwa = partner in sexual love.
engagement of marriage, e.g. Musimbi wangu wakalesya kasuwa. My girlfriend ended the marriage engagement.
an island, e.g. Ciwena wakamulela musimbi mukasuwa. = The crocodile reared the girl on the island.
a small basket, e.g. Koleta busu mukasuwo kasyoonto. Bring the mealie- meal in a small basket.
inside corner, e.g. Mubbi wakayubide mukaswi kananda. = The thief hid in a corner within the house.
a small fish, e.g. Mutinta wajaya kaswi naali kuloba. = Mutinta killed a small fish when she was fishing.
a small brush, e.g. Masowe, koleta kaswi tuyaile nsefwa. Masowe bring a small brush so that we clean the sieve.

a bit of tobacco kasyaleza a large or gigantic natural depression or cave, e.g. Bantu banji bakali kukayoowa aka kasyaleza kwategwa mpaamalende. = Many people feared this ravine as it was regarded as a rainshrine. Also kalambo.
a handfull or small piece of tobacco cake, e.g. Mundigwasye kasyamu katombwe, ambeyo ndifwepe. = Please my friends give me a pinch of tobacco so that I also smoke. Also kankomwa, kasyaamu.
a bad reputation, e.g. Kokkazika moyo, inzala ilainda, utabaa kasyimo. = Cool your heart, the hunger will pass, don't get yourself a bad reputation.
a saying or proverb, e.g. Sena toningakamvwa kasyimyo kakuti, 'Uusunda uzyala mwana'. Have you not yet heard the proverb which says, "The one who tries, produces a child."
very small red ant which feeds on dead insects, pl. tusyulanyama.
frequent urination with blood, bilharzia, haematuria, e.g. Kamutola bana baciswa kasyuunsyu kucibbadela. You should take the children who suffer from bilharzia to the hospital. Also kansyuunsyu.

an arrow, pl. tuta, e.g. Kaindi bakubusi bakali kujaya tuyuni atuta. = Long ago youths used to kill little birds with arrows. Kata kabunete kalakonzya kujaya munyama mupati. = A poisoned arrow can kill a large animal. Also kalembe
a little bow, e.g. Basankwa bacili baniini babelesya tuta tuniini. = Boys who are still small use small little bows.
a painful wound, e.g. Chinkuli wakacisidwe kataambi amunwe. = Chinkuli had a painful wound in his finger. Also kanamalumbe.
a tiny fish, pl. tutaka, e.g. Muzeli ulobya kataka kujaya nswi zipati. = The fisherman fishes with a small fish to catch big fishes. Mweemba uyoka kataka. = Mweemba is roasting a tiny fish.
a single bead on a string, e.g. Munsingo nzoka yakajisi malembo-lembo asubila ulati ntutaka twabulungu. = The snake had red spots on the neck, you would say they are beads of a necklace. Also katenta
a small wide-necked pot for brewing beer, e.g. Bukoko buli mukatalo mbobubi. = The beer which is in the small wide-necked pot is the one which is bad.

a head-scarf, e.g. Mutinta wakaula katambala katuba kazekaudwe maluba asalala kakusama kumutwe. = Mutinta bought a white head-scarf decorated with red flowers to wear on the head. katambula-nsimauvwula pendent flesh-part of palate, e.g. Katambulansimauvwula kangu kapiila tute nindabona cisyu cibotu. = The back of my palate watered when I saw the nice relish. Also kameneno katampu a seed-bed, e.g. Aaka katampu kajisi cisyu cibotu alimwi cinona. = This seed-bed has good vegetables and they are tasty.
a small dry log used as firewood at a social event, e.g. Bana abakandikwelele katanda ndiyote. = Let the children go and bring me a small log so that I warm myself.
stamen of flower, pl. tutanga-tanga, e.g. Tutanga-tanga twamaluba aya ntulamfwu. = The stamens of these flowers are long. Also kajamya-jamya.
sable-antelope, pl. bakatanta, e.g. Mumabanda a Kafwuwe momujanika bakatanta banji. On the Kafue Flats is where you find many sable-antelopes. Also Iweengu.
a sapling, a flexible stick, e.g. Ndakabaumya katembwani bana bakalisya. I used a flexible stick to beat the children who had allowed the cattle to graze in the maize-field. Also kantembwani
an infectious disease, an epidemic, e.g. Katenda kabulwazi bwasikalileke nkakali. The infectious disease of AIDS is virulent.

piece of meat, e.g. Kwiina buzuba nobuba bomwe muvwimi naakabapa katendu kanyama nokaceya bazyali bakwe kuti balisamune. = There was not even a single day when the hunter gave his parents a piece of meat to feed themselves.

complaints, murmurings, e.g. Bantu bamwi kuti bacembaala balaa katengailwa. = When some people grow old they become full of complaints. katengamalilo ambulance, e.g. Kufwumbwa kuti babelesi bamucibbadela bamumvwa katengamalilo kazya bukwemba, balaingana kubamba zibelesyo zyakugwasya mulwazi uuletwa akatengamalilo. = Whenever the hospital staff hear the ambulance blow it's siren they go around preparing the untensils for helping the patient brought in by the ambulance.

a spiny shrub with blackbrown twisted pods. (dichrostachys cinera) It is very hard wood and durable. Good for firewood and charcoal. Leaves are high in protein and mineral content. Bark yields strong fibre. Pods eaten by animals, roots for basket-making. Leaves and roots used as treatment for snakebites, poulticing of burns etc. e.g. Loozi Iwakatenge ndubotu kuvwumbya maanda. = The fibre of the katenge shrub is good for thatching houses.
the little finger, e.g. Kuli cilonda akatengezya kamwana. = There is a sore on the small finger of the child. Also kantengezya.
a string of beads, pl. tutenta, e.g. Bakaintu bamwi bayanda kusama tutenta twabulungu. Some women like to wear strings of beads.
a reed, e.g. Babelesya katete kupima mutumba. = They use a reed to measure the corpse.
tobacco-packed reed for smoking, e.g. Basyaneene bafwebela mukatete. = My grandfather smokes using a tobacco-packed reed.
a baby, e.g. *Katete* takatolwi mumadilwe. = A baby is not to be taken to funerals.
a little dish, a saucer, e.g. Mwana ulida mukatiba kasyoonto. = The child eats from a small dish.
a small robin-like bird, e.g. *Katiiti komwe takakkutwi ccita tunji.* = You cannot satisfy hunger with one robin but perhaps with many.
the breast-bone, e.g. Alacisa akatiti nkaambo ndatikuka bwakaindi. = The breast-bone is sore because I had a hiccup for a long time. Also kaango

small dried skin or hide, e.g. Ulayala katobo kamwana wajombe katelemuka. = He spreads out the dried skin of a calf which is slippery. Also citobo Mwana uloona akatobo. = The baby is sleeping on a small dried skin.
a small tree, e.g. Kamuya mundicelele matobo mukatobo kali mumuunda. = Go and bring me fruit from the katobo tree which is in the field.
a small tin used as a lamp, e.g. Bana badomeka kale katolitoli munanda. = The children have already lit the small lamp in the house.
still-born child, e.g. Bamacembele mbabazikka katombe. = The old women are the ones who bury a still-born child, Also kasowe
a house or bed on a raised platform, e.g. Wakatanta mukatombo a koona. = He climbed up into the bed and fell asleep.
a container made of bark, e.g. Inzuki zilanjila mukatomboa. = The bees are entering the bark-container.
a small ruin, e.g. Aaka katongo nkabataata. = That small ruin is my father's.

the brew which is finally ready for consumption, e.g. Baama bandituma kuya kwiita acisya kuti bazikunywe katongola. = My mother has sent me to call my uncle so that he might drink the beer which is ready for consumption.
a type of bird which moves with the rains, e.g. Bana bajaya kantongola kaniini mumusamu. = The children killed a small tongola bird in a tree.

a type of tree (*syzygium guineense ssp. afromontanum*), wood used for furniture, house building, canoes, carving. Vinegar is produced from the fruits. A good honey tree. e.g. Mukatope kaya kuli buci bunji. = In the katope tree there is plenty of honey.
a kind of medicinal root, e.g. Kuti mwida kamumyonga, uleelede kunywa katoze. = If your stomach is upset you should drink medicine of the katoze root.
a young duiker, e.g. Katukaula wazimana ndongwe zyangu mumuunda. = The young duiker finished my groundnuts in the field.
a small basket, e.g. Bamacembele batola busu mukatumba. = The old women are taking the flour in a small basket.
a fig tree, pl. intumbi, e.g. Ndajana nkwilinti zinji mukatumbi muya. = I found many pidgeons in that fig tree.
a small mammal when suckling, e.g. Aaka katumbu kajisi mwana mupati. = This small suckling-mammal has a big offspring.
a type of bird, the namaqua dove, pl. tutundulu, e.g. Basankwa bateya tutundulu muziteente. = The boys are trapping namaqua doves in nests.
a beam or ray of light, e.g. Ndabona _katungazuba_ mumakumbi. = I have seen a ray of light through the clouds.
a small open hut in a field, e.g. Bataata bakkala _mukatungu_ noba-yamina baceta. = My father stays in a small open hut, when he is scaring the monkeys.

a village with a few people, pl. _tutungu_, e.g. Muntu ukkala _katungu_, ulalendelelwa. = A person who stays in an isolated house is lonely. Minzi ya Batonga yoonse yakaleka kuba minzi: twakaba _tutungu_ buyo. = All the villages of the Batonga have stopped being villages: they have just become small family homes. (Long ago larger numbers of people lived in the villages. With the advent of farming every family wanted to live near their field. As a result the villages diminished in size.)

a round object, a pill, e.g. Ulacapa munzila zyobile, agilazi akantu _katuntuli_. = He divined in two ways, by using a glass and by using a round object. Mulwazi akanywe _katuntuli_ komwe abuzuba. = A patient should drink one pill daily.
a basket used as a bowl or plate, e.g. Kobikka buntele _mukatwida_. = Put the groundnut-mash in the basket-bowl.

a small spider with long legs which spins a broad white web in houses, pl. _tuubi_, e.g. Munanda Kacumbika tayandi nzinini, _ntunga, tubanze atuubi_. = Kacumbika does not like flies, maggots, scorpions and small spiders in the house.
a web, e.g. Inzinini zilajatwa _mukaubilili_. = The flies are caught in the web.

small insect or reptile, pl. _tuuka_, e.g. Mwana walumwa _kauka_. = The child has been bitten by an insect. Munanda uloona kabotu nkaambo tamukwe _tuuka_ mbuli njina, nkuswi, nsinsini, nsengele, _ntunga, ndolwa, inzinini, tubanze, basimunyweu, bunyenyene, basicoombolwa, mayongolo, mulanzi amvwunyu_. = You will sleep well in the house because there are no insects or reptiles, like lice, tampans, bedbugs, ticks, biting maggots, lizards, flies, scorpions, black maching ants, small ants, large red ants, millipedes, termites and maggots.
an ant-hill, e.g. Sulwe wakaambila suntwe kuti akalibikke jamba _akaulumbi_. = The hare told the hyena to put the large hoe on the ant-hill. Also _kaulunzuma_.
heap, a bunch, e.g. Mukabbokesi omu kwakajanika _kaulunzuma kamakkwacca_. = In this box there was found a pile of kwachas. Also _cilwi, kaulu_
small pointed ant-hill, e.g. Kaceta kakalikkede _akaulunzuma_. = The small monkey was perched on a narrow and pointed small ant-hill. Also _kaulumbi_.
a barbed arrow, e.g. Ngulube yokwesu yakayaswa _kaumba_. = Our pig was pierced by a barbed arrow. Also _koomba_
a water-pot, e.g. _Kaumbu kazwide meenda_. = The pot is full of water.
a small grave, e.g. _Kaumbwe kamwana muvwanda takalampi kapati_. = The grave of the child should not be too deep. Also _cuumbwe_.
a flexible stick, e.g. Banene bakwabbaula bana _akaumpa_. = The old man beat the children with a flexible stick.
a tiny seed, e.g. Mwana wayaswa _kaundu_ mumboni. = The child was pierced by a tiny seed in the pupil of the eye.
a bad smell, e.g. Omuno munanda kuli _kaundwe_ kabi. = There is a bad smell here in the house. Naakanjila buyo wakamvwa _kaundwe_. = Just when he entered he got a bad smell. Also kanunko.

sloth in responding or obeying, lack of concentration, not focused on what you are doing, e.g. Ulaa kaungu nkaambo wakabbukilwa jilo. He is confused because he was caught committing adultery yesterday. Chimuka nasebenza ulaa kaungu, twaambo twa Tyaila twamunjila. = As Chimuka worked his mind was occupied elsewhere, what Tyaila had said had pierced him.
a three-cornered thorn usually found in fields, e.g. Ndayaswa kaunsya-kwale nindali kulimina mumuunda. I have been pierced by a three-cornered thorn when I was weeding in the field.
a boil, abcess, e.g. Wakalijisi kaute mumatako. He had a boil on his buttock. Also cuute
clapper of a bell, e.g. Wakaleta mulangu kakunyina akavwalu. = He brought a bell without it's clapper.
a small scratch, e.g. Bumvwa nibwandikwamba bwandisiila kavwalu. = When the thorn grazed me it left a small scratch.
a recently born child, e.g. Idilwe lyakavwanda talyoonwi anze. = The funeral of a recently born child does not call for people to sleep outside.
light porridge, e.g. Mbubwakaceda buyo, Mainza bakamujikila kavwipa. As soon as it was dawn, they cooked light porridge for Mainza. Also keele, kakondwi
a type of tree, e.g. Buyuni bulayobezyanya mukavwulindingwa. The birds are chattering in the kavwulindingwa tree.

a type of tree (borassus aethiopum), the fan-palm, borassus-palm, the wood is very resistant to insects, termites and fungi. Leaves used for plaiting into mats, etc. Midribs make brooms, fish-traps and nets. Leaf-stalk fibres make brushes. Flower-spikes can be tapped for palm wine and the roots are used for various medicines, e.g. Kavwuma nkasamu kalamfwu kapati. = The borassus palm is a tree which is exceedingly tall. Also kahuma, kalala, kankunka, mapokwe, muhuma.
a small cow without horns, e.g. Koombe kavwuma kalaciswa. = The small cow without horns is sick.
October, e.g. Izuba lilapya kapati mumwezi wa Kawumbi-kaniini. The sun is very hot during the month of October.
the season of slow growth, same as Kavwumbi-kaniini.
a species of frog, e.g. Ijamba lyakabbosyola kavwumbulabalimi. The plough has torn a frog open.

bundle of money, e.g. Mudaala wakali kutola kavvuvwu ku Lusaka kutegwa akaulilizye zyamukantoolo kakwe. The old man was taking a bundle of money to Lusaka so that he could buy things for his store. Also kafwuufwu.

a small wild orange tree, pl. tuwi, (the fruit = iwi, pl. mawi), e.g. Kakololo watanta mukawi nkaambo uyanda kulya mawi. Kakololo climbed a wild orange tree because she wants to eat wild oranges. Also itu, igwi

unsafe driving, e.g. Ooyu wakajisi citima wakali mulombwana winiwini. Cakali kubalika mbuli kuti awalo wakali kulibilililizya kuya kubonana anjabi yakwe. Kakali kawiliwili mwanaa mudaala. = This one who had a train was a real man. He was travelling quickly as if he was hurrying to see his girl-friend. He was driving recklessly that young man.

a type of tree resembles mukwa. Timber is fairly heavy, strong and heart-wood durable. Difficult to work and splits on nailing, but very good for furniture if properly handled. Good honey flow. Bark, roots and leaves used for medicines for sores, ulcers coughs, colds. e.g. Cuuno _cakawizi_ nciyumu kapati. = A stool made from the _kawizi_ tree is very strong.
a breeze, e.g. Kuli _kawo kabotu anze_. = There is a fresh breeze outside.

a big drum used in the Gwembe Valley. The kayanda drums, are played in sets of three. They are sometimes played together with other instruments at beer parties and other ceremonies. The kayanda membranes are either goat or cattle skin. Light wood is used for the drum itself and so the drums can be easily carried from place to place. These drums are also found in Western and North Western Provinces where they are known as _mukupelo, jitumba_ and _kibichiko_. e.g. Ingoma yakayanda tiilemi _kubweza_. = The kayanda drum is not heavy to carry.
a small root, e.g. _Kayanda kamusamu oyu kalakola_. = The small root of this tree is poisonous.
a little egg, pl. _tuyi_, e.g. _Tutiiti tutula tuyi tuniini-niini_. = The robins lay very small eggs.
a type of bird, the namaqua dove, pl. _bakayiba_, e.g. _Bakayiba balayanda kucelela mumugwagwa_. = The namaqua doves like to eat food from the road. Also _katundulu, kaiba_.
an early kind of small maize, e.g. Kamusyanga _kayile tukafwambaane kooloka_. Plant early growing maize so that we eat it soon. Also _kampelya, kafwamba_
a prisoner, pl. _bakayili_, e.g. _Kayili waloboka kuzwa muntolongo_. = The prisoner escaped from prison. cf. _mwange or mwaange_
the small locust bird, e.g. Insozi _zilaligwa kapati akayimbile_. = Locusts are eaten a lot by the small locust bird.
an eagle, e.g. Kamukasoola _kayinga, kalakwempa twana twankuku_. = Chase away the eagle, it will snatch the chicks. Also _kainga_.
a highly excited quarrel, e.g. Kwakaba _kayobe kakatazizye akati kabantu_. A very heated argument arose among the people.

groundnut extract, e.g. _Ikayobe nindongwe izyakangwa asautu, nkabela zyatwigwa muncili, mane zyeemuka. Zicimana kwiibaiba mafwuta, bazibumba caba mukusu wacoondoonde_. = Ikayobe are grounduts fried with salt, then pounded in a mortar until it is broken up. When the oil drains off it is made into a porridge.

a little spirit which chirps, pl. _tuyobela_, e.g. Munanda muli _tuyobela bana tabakkuti kabotu_. = In the house where there are _tuyobela_ spirits, the children are not satisfied when they eat. (these spirits are unseen but believed to eat much). Also _kayowela_.
diarrhoea, with debility in children, e.g. Mwana ulaa _kayokezi, taponi kabotu_. = A child who has diarrhoea does not live well.

a thin and short-shanked spear, e.g. Basankwa bakaindi bakalijisi masumo amisyobo yaandeene, mbuli isumo lyacinkosi, muumba, isumo lyampula a _kayonga_. = The men of the past had many different types of spears, like the barbed-spear, the fishing-spear, the shorter bladed-spear and the thin and short-shanked spear.

small dwarf-like spirits, pl. _tuyowela_, e.g. Mwana uligwa _tuyowela mwida_. The stomach of the child is being eaten by dwarf-like spirits. WanjiIwa _tuyowela_. = The _tuyowela_ spirits have entered her. Ulaa masabe atuyowela. = She has been possessed by the pigmy spirits. Mubili wakatalika kumana mbuli kuti kuli tuyowela twakali kumunywa bulowa. The body began to be finished as if little spirits were drinking the blood. Also tuyobela
the fontenella, the crown of the head, e.g. Mwana waleka kudunta akayumwido. = The child has stopped pulsating at the fontenella. Also kanyampwido
a small bird, e.g. Ndaakujaya kayuni komwe buyo. = I have only killed one small bird.
a type of relish, e.g. Basimbi baunka kukucela kayunubwi. = The girls have gone off to gather kayunubwi relish.
a shelf or platform for keeping plates, e.g. Sibbuku wakafwumuna cisako cakuumya akazalo kamitiba. = The headman pulled a stick for beating from the plate-shelf. Also kasakabale
an evil spirit which protects the evil-doer. e.g. Ulaa kazelo kamwi. = He has a special evil spirit which protects him from punishment.
a secret, e.g. Kaambo aka utaambili umbi muntu, abe kazimoyo wako. Do not talk about this matter to anyone, let it become your secret.
sorrow, e.g. Kazinza katamani kalakonsya. makes one thin. = Endless sorrow
a small blade of couch-grass, e.g. Kuti wasimpa kazinza kaniini kalakomena nokaceya buti. If you plant a small blade of couch-grass it will grow no matter how small it is.

anything done in secret, e.g. Bapati banywa bukoko bwakaziye munanda. The elders drink beer secretly in the house. Mudyaka wakacili kuyanda kwiiya, balo bamayi bakamulya kaziye mu muswaangano wabo. = Mudyaka still wanted to learn, but the teachers talked about him in private at their meeting.
kwaamb luyando Iwabo lube Iwakaziye. = The girl agreed saying that their love should be hidden.

beer brewed which is not for sale, e.g. Kuli kaziye kuli baneene. There is beer at my grandmother's home which is not for sale. Bakafwambaana kumusisa munanda kunze adolomu lyakaziye. = They quickly hid him in the house behind a drum of private beer.
bantu ndimba-ndimba babungana kale mbuli kuti kwakali kaziye kubukoko.
a long pointed stick used as spear in a children's game, e.g. Syaatinde uyaswa akazonde. The tuber is pierced by a long pointed stick.
before sunset, e.g. Uleelede kusika akazuba-kabala. = You should arrive when the sun is still shining.
a nesting-coop, e.g. Mpimpa wakabamba kazumbo kakuyobweda tuyuni. Mpimpa has made a nestingcoop to keep little birds.

a germ, e.g. Kazunda kakakweekwe kalamuka kufwa. = The tuberculosis germ is slow to die. kazungula-kaniini type of tree ("the German sausage") In traditional lore some say it makes people forget; others say it makes them fight. Muyuni ulikkede mukazungula-kaniini. A bird is sitting in the kazungula tree. Also kantengwa-kaniini.
dissension, e.g. Amunzi awa kuli kazwanga ciindi coonse. = At the village here there is disorder all the time. Also kayobe.
a tobacco plant, smaller than cisuku. It is pink-flowered with pointed leaves, e.g. Tombwe wakazyalazanga ulalula kapati. = Tobacco of the kazyala-zanga plant is very bitter.

parenthood, (illegal use of), e.g. Kubelesya *kazyale-zyale* muganda yabana, nobazyali, muleelede kucileka, nkaambo inga nkunyonganya ganda yabana bali kumvwana bobile. = You parents ought not to use the authority of parenthood in your childrens home (to take their money or property from them) because it is only destroying the home of the children who have been understanding one another.

a ritual ceremony in which beer is brewed which permits a married man to greet his in-laws, e.g. Twaunka tukanywe kakoko *kakazyibyo*. = We are going to drink the ritual-beer for greeting the in-laws. Sicibende ncaakayandisisya kuti kucitwe *kazyibyo* nkuti aanzigwe katacitiji makwe. = What Sicibende wanted very much was that the ritual greeting ceremony should take place so that he would be greeted (in the future by any in-law) and that he would not have to run away from his in-laws.

small jawbone, e.g. Mwana ulakukozya, busyu boonse, insingo mane *akeebo* koonse. = The child resembles you, the whole face, the neck, the little jaw-bone. Wakali kukanana kumwi kalikwezya-kwezya *kukeebo*. = He was talking while scratching his chin. Also mweebo.
the last-born, e.g. Bantu baya babula coolwe kufwidwa *keela*. = Those people are very unlucky they have lost their last-born child.
a light porridge, e.g. Amumusanine *keele* mulesi akkute. = Feed the weaned child with light porridge so that it is satisfied.

an axe, pl. *tweembe*, e.g. Kamubweza *tweembe* tukagonke masanzu aciba. = Take the axes so that we cut poles for the kraal. (There has been a variety of axes: *cikwese*, broad-blade, straight-edged working axe for cutting reeds and light shrubs; *bukanu*, a crescent-bladed dancing axe (formerly used as a fighting weapon); *kaleba*, a very small headed working axe often carried by men when walking; *munomba*, very long thin-bladed dancing axe; *cikwelebe*, a dancing/walking axe.)
leaves smoked by people as a love-charm, e.g. Waungula musimbi akaambo *kakeempula*. = You have confused the girl because of the love-potion. Also *namusekelwa*.
a type of snake, the boom-slang or common tree-snake, highly venomous, grass-coloured, e.g. Keemvwe ulajaya kufwambaana. = The boomslang kills quickly. Also *simufwula-keemvwe*, *sikafwula-mwemvwe*.
a non-poisonous mushroom, e.g. Bowa bwakeenda-bulima mbunji mumuunda omu. = There are a lot of non-poisonous mushrooms in this field.
a small strip, e.g. Cakabatolela ciindi kuubona mwezi, nkaambo kakali buyo *keengu* kasyoonto kakasendekede. = It took them time to see the moon, because it was just a small crescent declining.

small portion, e.g. Mu-muswaangano basololi bakalomba bama-sibbuku boonse kuti baumune zii kwa *keengwe* komwe kaciindi mukuyeeya lufwu Iwa Mwami Siamaundu. = At the meeting the leaders asked all the head-men to keep silence for one minute to remember the death of Chief Siamaundu.
small amount of sperm, e.g. Musankwa ucili mwana ugusya *keenze* kasyoonto buyo. = A young boy ejaculates only a small amount of sperm.
a morsel, e.g. Komupa *keeya*
wafwa. = Give the visitor a bite to eat, she is hungry. Also munsuma
a swampy area, e.g. Mukeezi omu bana bakajaya nkukubwi zinji ijilo. = Yesterday the children killed many snipes in the vlei.
a small animal-horn, (which may be used as charm or ornament) e.g. Keja kampongo nkaniini. = The horn of a goat is small.

faint smell, whiff, e.g. Wamuswena munsi-munsi wakajisi kemya kabi mbuli kajembwe kampongo nkaambo katulya-bayuni ntwaakali kusisikizya kufweba. When you came near him he had an unpleasant smell like a buck-goat because of the dagga which he smoked in secret. Also kaganko
small burrow, e.g. Imbeba zyanjila mukena omu. = The rats have entered into that small burrow. Also bwina.
lunation corresponding to August, e.g. Kaindi izikolo zyakali kujalwa mumwezi wa Kezabimbe. = In the past the schools were closing in the month of August. Also Kasangabimbe
a secret, e.g. Aaka kaambo akabe kezimoyo kuli nduwe. = Let this matter be a secret to you. Also kazimoyo.

a straw, a blade of grass, (bwizu is collective) e.g. Koleta kezyu tudomeke lambe. Bring a straw so that we light the lamp. Musimbi wakapokoola ansi akezu kumwi kavwuwa. = The girl was scratching the ground with a blade of grass while answering.
the rain-bird, the grey lourie, the 'go-away' bird, e.g. Kiiwa ulalila kakuyanda kuboola mvwula. The rain-bird cries when the rain is about to come. Also kkowa.
paper-spider, pl. bakijubi, e.g. Munanda omu muli bakijubi banji. In the house there are many paper-spiders.
a vegetable relish (Dicliptera micranthes), e.g. Bacembele bajika cisyu cakiulu. The old women are cooking vegetable relish.
a vegetable relish (Corrigiola littoralis).

cabbage, e.g. Atweende tukaule kkabicci kumbewu. = Let us go and buy cabbage at the garden. kkiccinipati (ety. Eng.) kitchen-party, e.g. Nkolola yabana basunu ngu kkiccinipati! Inititation for modern children is the kitchen-party!
a coin, e.g. Tulange lubazu lumbi Iwakkobeli. = Let us look at the other side of the coin. Also kkobili
a coin, e.g. Bantususu bali mbuli kkobili bali amabazu obilo, lubazu Iwabasimbi a lubazu Iwabasankwa. = Humanity is like a coin, it has two sides, the side of women and the side of men.
a solid wooden door carved in one piece from a tree trunk. Timbers used are from the trees are munga or mukula, e.g. Amulete kkoma lyananda. = Bring a solid wooden door for the house.

a hole in which pots are fired. e.g. Zyayuma zibiya balasya kkomba. Eeli kkomba ndyakusumikila zibiya. When the pots are dry they dig a hole. This hole is for firing the pots. kkopa Namboard, e.g. Cimwi ciindi wisi naakamana kuvwola mali akkopa, bana bakwe wakabaulila zyakusama. = Sometimes when the father was receiving money from Namboard, he bought his children clothes.

the rain-bird, the grey and black cuckoo, e.g. Kkowa ulalila mumusamu. = The rain-bird is chirping in the tree. e.g. Kkowa ulatwaambila kuti mvwula kiiyanda kuboola. The kkowa bird tells us when the rain is coming. Ooyo musimbi ndikkowa lyamuntu. Cakabacisya nsoni kapati bazyali bakwe. This girl is a cuckoo. She brings great shame on her parents.
the shoulder, e.g. Wakajata mulongwaakwe *akkuko*. He caught his friend by the shoulder.
a big sore which usually starts by itself and does not heal quickly, e.g. Wakati, "Makaye, ulaa *kkulenge kusyule*." = He said "Makaye, you have a slow healing ulcer behind." Also dondamwaka.
a strip of cloth which holds the stomach of the mother in place after childbirth Also mumya, mukaku.
a cave, e.g. Syuumbwa wanjila *mukkumbwi*. = The lion entered a cave.

the lunation which corresponds to the fall of leaves, e.g. Mumwezi wa *Kkunkumuna-masamu* kuli mpeyo kapati akaambo kamuwo. = During the month of July there is severe cold because of the wind. Wakali mwezi wa *Kkunkumuna-masamu*, muwo wakali kubbubbula citaambiki. = It was the month of July the wind was blowing terribly.

misfortune, e.g. Bakali kuyeeya kuti cimwi ciindi wakajisi *kkuswe* lyakutayandwa basankwa. = They were thinking that perhaps she had the misfortune of not been loved by men. Mukansondo mpaapengela muno mucisi, naa nkutakwatwa kwakwe *akkuswe* eli ndyobamwaamba bantu, ccita. = That is where Mukansondo suffers in this land, whether it is because of her not being married due to the misfortune of not being attractive to men which people say of her, I don't know. Also bbamba.
the back of a house, e.g. Mweemba ukkede *kukkuti*. = Mweemba is seated at the back of the house.
a valley, e.g. Idamu lya Kaliba lili *mukkuti*. = Kariba Dam is in a valley.
warmth, e.g. Kasise wakakasaalilwa mukaindi kaniini nkaambo muciteente mwakali *kkutikuti*. = The bluebreasted tit was heated up in a little time because there was warmth in the nest.

a prostitute, e.g. Nywebo nobantu babi muyanda kuti musimbi ooyu akabe *kkweelele* uuyandisisya buyo makkwacca kuzwa kubasankwa. = You evil people want this girl to become a prostitute who only craves for money from boys. Also kapenta

a sling, pl. makwisyo, e.g. Musankwa wauma munyama abbwe *lyakkwisyo*. = The boy has struck the animal with a stone from a sling. David wakajaya Goliyati *akkwisyo*. = David killed Goliath with a sling.
a grinding-stone, pl. makkwiyo, e.g. Mukkuti bamakaintu baciziya mu *makkwiyo*. = In the Valley the women still grind on grinding-stones. Also iziyo.
a hartebeeste, pl. bakonkone, e.g. Bakonkone balacela mucibanda. = The hartebeestes are grazing in the plain. Also konze, kotombwe.

a hartebeeste, (large antelope with long head and sloping back) pl. bakonze, e.g. Bakonze bazyala ciindi cacilimo eliya nelitalika kuumpa kapati zuba. = The hartebeeste gives birth during the dry season when the sun really begins to burn. Also kotombwe, konkone.
a type of plant, e.g. Cisyango cakoolotwe tacibonwi-bonwi. = The *koolotwe* plant is not commonly seen.
a barbed arrow, e.g. Koleta *koomba* tukayase nzoka mubwina. = Bring a barbed arrow so that we pierce the snake in the den.
a dense thicket, e.g. Syuumbwa wanjila *mukoonde* kali kunze ananda. A lion entered a dense thicket at the back of the house.
crushed groundnut meal, e.g. Nikwabula cisyu, twabwenga *koondeonde. = When there was no relish, we used crushed groundnut meal.
a castrated goat, e.g. Twakalya koongo lyakakwatwa musimbi. = When the girl married we ate a castrated goat. Also coongo.
a noose-trap, a snare, e.g. Inziba yacegwa mukooye. = The dove has been caught in the snare. Also kooze, cintembo, bukulila.
a snare, for birds especially, e.g. Kosungulula kayuni mukooze. = Remove the bird from the snare. Also kooye, akole
a hartebeeste, also konze.
a single hair of an animal's coat, e.g. Koya kakkiti kapa kufwundilila. = A single hair of a cat can make breathing difficult.
the running-noose of a bent poletrap, e.g. Mweeto wakoze watyoka. = The bent stick attached to the runningnoose and which acts as a spring in the idiba trap has broken.
an arm, e.g. Mutinta wazimba akuboko. = Mutinta's arm is swollen.
a game, e.g. Naakamana kwaanzika civwulumuto, wakaya mukucilika alimwi abeenzinyina. = After putting the utensils away, he went back again to the game with his friends.
the east, e.g. Inombe zyakali kugama kujwe. = The cattle were heading eastwards.
a hole in the ground made by termites e.g. Nzoka yakanjila mukumbwi. = The snake entered into the hole. Also nkumbwi
a bead-fringe used on top of the skirt e.g. Mukaintu wangu wasamide musinsi uusumidwe kunamunkana. = My wife was dressed in a skirt which was stitched with a beaded fringe. Also sikomoka.
July, e.g. Muwo mmunji kapati mumwezi wa Kunkumuna-masamu. = The wind blows a lot in the month of July.
sable-bull, e.g. Mucende wakunikusiya ulasandula kapati. = The sable-bull greatly improves the breed.
ebony, e.g. Musamu wakunikusiya ulasiya mbi. = The wood of ebony is pure black.
one place, e.g. Bantu aaba bakali kweembelela kuntu komwe. = These people were herding in one place.
a polecat, e.g. Nyimbaasalama nkanyama kaitwa kuti kununkangubo. = The polecat is a little animal which is called "the hide stinks." Also diintingwe
very early in the morning, e.g. Mwana wasika nikwacili kuseeni. = The child arrived when it was still early in the morning.
genuine and real, e.g. Ndakabona syuumbwa wini wakwaanza. = I saw a real genuine lion.

the greater partridge or rednecked pheasant, pl. bakwale, e.g. Bakwale bakamana mapopwe mumuunda mutwakasyanga mvwiki yakamana. = The partridges finished the maize in the field which we planted last week.

a cap or hat, e.g. Syaanasulwe wakasama nsuku, kwambe, munkonde, masangusangu munsafwu, tubbensu abukaano. = The hare was dressed in a head-dress, a cap, a bead and wire collar, dry globular seed-pods tied around the legs above the ankles, rags, and a traditional dancing axe. Also inkopesi, imvwuse, cisoti, inzyeete.
bark, e.g. Kwamu lyamusamu lisilisya babwa. = The bark of a tree heals dogs.
the armpit, pl. maapa, e.g. Wakasisa cisani mukwapa. = She hid the cloth in her arm-pit.
fish-eagle, pl. bakwaze, e.g. Bakwaze bazimana nswi mucizyiba. = The fish-eagles have finished the fish in the pond. Also sikwaze.
south-pole, e.g Kukweela-kumusanza kulatontola siko. = At the south pole it is extremely cold.
north-pole, e.g. Ku kweela-kunyika mulajana caanda calo. = At the north-pole you just find ice.

an antbear, e.g. Kwibba ujisi mala mayumu ngasisya zyuulu noziyuma buti, kuyandaula bunyenyene amumoma. = The antbear has strong nails with which it digs anthills no matter how hard they are, searching for small black ants and white ants. Also galaba, namunkwize, cinengwe.
a worm, pl. malaala, e.g. Bakubusi balobya malaala nobaloba nswi. = Young men fish with worms when hooking fish. Also namula, pl. banamula.
a type of edible mushroom, pl. balambalamba, e.g. Balamba lamba balanona kapati. The lambalamba mushrooms are quite delicious.
the large intestine, e.g. Kuti muleba mwanjila mayoka, mulacisa kapati. If worms enter the large intestine, it is extremely painful.
an axe, e.g. Kaindi baalumi tiibakali kweenda katajisi leba. In the past men did not travel without an axe.
Also leembweleembwe
a game played with hands joined in a circle, e.g. Bana baso-bana leembwe-leembwe. = The children are playing the leembweleembwe game.
a good singer, a song composer, pl. balengwe, e.g. Balengwe tacibakatazi kwaanza Iwiimbo. = It is not difficult for composers to start a song.
name for God, other names for God are: Lubumba-bantu (Sikabumba) = Moulder of people; Kalenganzubo (Namalengwa) Creator of all the tribes;
the Creator;

Bringer of rain, Merciful One; Munamazuba = The owner of the days; Haabusiwa = the provider of dregs (i.e. food); Nalubomba = the Kind One; Haatwakwe (Ushatwakwe) = God will do as he wishes (apart from us); Muninde (You wait for me) = The giver of thunder and much rain Mangwe (Ila) = The sender of so much water that there is no place left dry: Mutalabala = the one who does what no other can (or) the one who is infinite and eternal; Namese (Ila) = the rain giver; Shakemba (Ila) = The Rain-Giver. (Note: The names for God are connected with nature, especially the rain); Syaateelwi = The Immesurable One; Nacuumunye = the One who acts silently; Mukanzubo = the Mother of the peoples; Namakolokolo = the one who suckles us and provides for us as a mother; Namakungwe Mutalabala = The One who governs and provides for all living things; Chilomba-muyoba = the one prayed to for good rains; Leza-Nacoombe = The God of the Tonga rainmaker (Nacoombe was one of the names of a rainmaker of old.); Mukamwini-mazuba = The owner of days.

action of God; Bantu theology considers God as active in natural phenomenon: Leza ulawa. It is raining. Leza ulazuma. It is thundering. Leza ulalaba. = God is flashing in lightning. Waseluka Leza. God has come down (in a stroke of lightning) Leza ulaunga. = God is the wind blowing.
ety. English library, e.g. Atuunke kuliebbulali tukalombe mabbuku aakubala. Let us go to the library and ask for books to read.
a protuberance formed on some trees, e.g. Musamu oyu ujisi likoto lipati. = This tree has a big protuberance.
a blanket, e.g Bayi bajisi *likumbeza lipati kapati.* = The teacher has a very large blanket. Also igumbeza, ikumbeza.
a willow-tree, e.g. Musamu *lilongwe wakayuma.* = The willow-tree has dried up. Also cibumbya.
a vegetable relish (Cerato-theca sesamoides), e.g. Mumbeu mwesu *tatujisi lilumina.* = In our garden we do not have the vegetable *lilumina.*
the bishop-bird, seed-eater, pl. mancwe, e.g. *Mancwe alaalya kapati maila-muceme.* = The bishop-bird eats red millet a lot. Also *incwe*
traditional skirt of hanging strings, pl. manda, mostly used in past by Gwembe Valley women. Also *maaya*
hornet, pl. manko, e.g. *Linko lya-luma mwana lilacisa kapati.* = The hornet which stung the child is very painful.
a skin-bag for tobacco, e.g. *Kamubikka tombwe mulinkomo lyangu.* = Put the tobacco in my skin-bag. Also inkomo
a tooth, pl. meno, e.g. *Lino lya-mwana lilacisa.* = The child's tooth is paining. Also *linyo*, pl. *menyo.*
an eye, pl. menso, e.g. *Lusinga lunjila mulinso lulacisa kapati.* The nerve-pain which has come into the eye is very sore. Also *liso*, pl. *meso.*
a tooth, pl. menyo, e.g. *Mwana wakalukuka linyo lyomwe jilo.* = The child lost one tooth yesterday. Also *lino.*
ball-bearing, pl. malisau, e.g. *Nci-nga tayendi kabotu nkaambo malisau akamana.* = The bicycle does not go well because the ball-bearings are worn out.
an eye, pl. meso, e.g. *Liso lya-mpongo ndipati.* = The eye of a goat is big. *Mubetesi wakamulanga meso acika-yikayi Mwiinga.* = The judge with terrifying eyes looked at Mwiinga
an eye, pl. mesyo, e.g. *Inzoka ijisi* mesyo masyoonto-syoonto.* = A snake has small eyes.
thread of nut, pl. maliya, e.g. *Inoti tiijati nkaambo maliya akamana.* = The nut is not catching because the threads are finished.
the mason wasp, pl. baloma, e.g *Baloma bayanda kubumbilila munanda.* = Mason wasps like to build their nests in a house.
a discussion, e.g. *Aaba bantu bajisi lombololo lutamani.* These people are involved in an endless discussion. Also *musalo*
a discussion Also *lombololo*
weak sight, e.g. *Nsyeboni kabotu mabala nkaambo ndaa loofwe kumeso.* = I don't see the words clearly because I have weak eye-sight. Also *igubilili*
a tree which once planted grows well, e.g. *Bawezi babikka zyaanza zyabanyama aloombwa.* = The hunters put the horned-heads of the animals on the tree.
a type of relish, e.g. *Cisyu caloomooma ciligwa yatanga mvwula.* = The vegetable *loomooma* is eaten at the first rains.
a dense forest, a stretch of thick bush, e.g. *Suntwe wanjila muloonde.* = The hyena has entered a dense forest. *Loonde olu lulayoosya kumuntu buyo.* = This forest is frightening to a mere human.
a strip of animal-skin used to carry babies, pl. myoondo, e.g. *Loondo Iwamusune ndulamfwu kwiinda Iwasulwe.* = A strip of ox-hide is longer than that of a rabbit.
a spike, pl. maloonga, e.g. *Basikulunduka babikka maloonga kunsi lya mabbusu abo.* = Those who run put spikes under their shoes.

fibre of bark, pl. ingozi, e.g. Kamuleta loozi tuvwumbye nanda. = Bring fibres so that we thatch the house. loto lead, e.g. Ooyu conco wiile kudivwuka nkaambo wakabambwa aloto. This spoon just bends because it is made of lead. Also lotwe.
lead, e.g. Lotwe ndubulo luteteete. Lead is a light metal. Also loto. luba a cattle-enclosure, pl. imba, e.g. Inombe zili muluba. The cattle are in the kraal. Also ciba, cimpati, lubaya.
a loud crying, e.g. Kwakalimvwinsya lubaba akati kabana nibakaumwa. = There was heard a loud crying among the children when they were beaten.

a plant which itches, e.g. Bana bababwa lubabangwe mucoonde. = The children are itching because of a plant which is in the forest. Imwi misamu isigwa miyanda akukasaazigwa akunywisya mwana kukobelela luvwumwe njeeyi: lubabangwe, ntendele zipati azinza. = The roots of certain plants which are dug up and heated and given to the child to drink to protect it from the disease of luvwumwe are as follows: lubabangwe, mutendele and couch-grass.
baldness, e.g. Wakajana muntu iwalubala lupati mumutwe lubee ndubuwa Iwandeke. = He found a man with a great bald patch on his head like the runaway for an aeroplane.
wattle as used for building, pl. imbalo, e.g. Koleta lubalo tubangile ciluli. = Bring a wattle so that we bind the roof. The trees from which wattles are mostly taken are, mubombo, mucinga, mungunya.
a type of weed, e.g. Lubalukila Iwakamena mumuunda onse. = The whole field is covered with the lubalukila weed.
drum-head, a membrane or skin used for covering a musical drum, e.g. *Lubambo* Iwangoma eyi nduyumu. = The drum skin is hard. Yakabbwaluka *lubambo*. = The drum-head burst.

the custom of lending one's wife to another man for sexual intercourse, e.g. *Lubambo ndubi*. = The custom of lending one's wife to another man for sexual intercourse is bad. Kusalwa *lubambo*, wakutwala tasalwi. (proverb) = A sexual lover can be picked at will, but a wife is not chosen in this way.
a wild plant which can be used as relish, e.g. Cisyu *calubanga* tacinoni. = Relish made from the *lubanga* wild plant is not tasty. Also nakafwulo.
See lubanje.
medicine added to dog's food to make it fierce, e.g. Babwa balaa lubangu mbakali. Dogs who eat *lubangu* medicine are fierce.
a type of bird, the crestedhornbill or toucan, e.g. *Lubangwa* wazimana ndongwe. = The crested-hornbill has finished the groundnuts.

hemp, dagga, a drug used for smoking, (*Cannabis sativa*) e.g. Bantu bafweba *lubanje* bamwi lulabakola. = Cannabis confuses some people who smoke it. Wakasondoka nkaambo wakali kufweba *lubanje* naakali simpongo. = He went mad because he was smoking cannabis when he was a goatherd.
dagga, Indian hemp, e.g. Bana baniini tabeelede kufweba *lubanji*. = Young people should not smoke cannabis. Also lubanje, lubange.
courtyard, runaway of airport, e.g. Basankwa bauma bbola *mulubanza*
The boys are playing football at the football-ground. Also lubuwa.
a bird, the crested-eagle, hawk, falcon, e.g. *Lubanze* ulya nombe yakabola. The crested-eagle is eating the rotten carcass of a cow.
cicatrice, mark left after tatooing, an old scar, e.g. Mwana walicisa alu*bata.* = The child hurt itself on an old scar.
a fence, e.g. Impongo zyaloola lubaya Iwambewu zyacilya cisyu. = The goats broke the fence of the garden and ate the vegetables.

a slap with the palm of the hand, e.g. Mwanalumi wakauma mukaintu *alubayi.* = The man slapped his wife with the palm of the hand. Toonse twakatalika kuseka akuumana *tubayi* twaluyando mumasaya. = We both began to laugh and stroke each other's cheeks in love.
side, e.g. Kolanga lukaye Iwatombwe kulubazu Iwananda. = Look for the potsherd of tobacco at the side of the house.

a patch of low bush, e.g. Sulwe ulakonzya kuyuba *mulubbubuti.* = The hare is able to hide in a low patch of bush. *Mulubbubuti* moonse wakali kwiide kuzwela-zwela ancinga yakwe mbojene kuli utija munyama. = He was swerving in and out through by all the low bushes like one who was running from an animal.

the preying mantis, e.g. Ndabona *lubbungu* ampulungwido. = I saw a preying mantis on the window. Akaambo kakasuko bayoowa kutuba mbuli *lubbungu.* = Because of the dust, they fear to become white as a preying mantis.
a snuff spoon
an instrument used for holding hot embers. pl. *imbeko,* e.g. Ndoolu *lubeko,* undipe mulilo. = Here is a thongs, give me fire.
a spatula, (an implement with a broad, flat, blunt blade, used especially for mixing or spreading)
flatness, as of a tool or weapon, e.g. *Lubemba* Iwasumo eli ndupati. = The flatness of this blade is wide.
grass for making small baskets, e.g. Cisuwo eeci cakabambwa alu*bembe lubotu.* = This basket was made of good weaving grass.
a large edible bush rodent, pl. *balubende,* e.g. Bana basya *balubende* mugundu. = The children are digging for rodents in a waterless plain. Also siluumba, mubende
the hammer-headed stork, e.g. *Lubengelele* wazimana nswi mu mulonga. = The hammer-headed stork has finished the fish in the river.
judicial proceedings, a court of justice, e.g. Bajisi *lubeta* Iwababbi mbaasibbuku. = The one who had a court-case with the thieves was the headman.
a halo around the sun or moon, e.g. Kuli *lubeta* Iwajulu kuzuba citondezya kuti nkwiicili mvwula. = There is a halo around the sun showing that there is still rain. Also izyingu
a dispute in court, e.g. Lu*beteko* Iwabulale bwangu tiilwakeenda kabotu. = The court-case of my adultery has not gone well.

speed, agility e.g. Sicikolo ulaa *lubilo* nguuyinda beenzinyina mumuzundano. = The pupil who has speed is the one who passes out his friends in the competition. Wakalubikka *lubilo* kulunduka kuya kwiita munene. = He took off quickly running to call the old man. (-tola *lubilo* go quickly; -leta *lubilo* = come quickly.) Also luno

circumference, boundary, outer edge, e.g. Basimpongo bakamusida mucembele milindi *mulubimbi* Iwamuunda. = The herd-boys are digging holes around the circumference of the field for old woman. Wakateya tukole *kulubimbi* Iwamuunda kutegwa bayuni batazimani zilyo. = He set traps around the circumference of the field so that the birds would not finish the food.

a sting, pl. *imbole,* e.g. Inzuki isiya lubole mpuyaluma. = The bee leaves its sting where it stings. Lubole talukonzyi koonse akunjila mucikanda cabbule. = A sting cannot enter anywhere through the skin of a honey-badger. Also lumoola
compassion, e.g. Mwami oyu ulaa lubomba kubantu babisya. = This chief has compassion on people who err.

propolis, a red and brown resinous substance collected by honey bees from tree buds for constructing and varnishing honeycombs. e.g. Inzuki zyuunga lubombe mumaluba. = The bees are collecting propolis from the flowers. Also ibbombo
a goat-hut, e.g. Impongo zyoona mulubondo. = The goats sleep in the goat hut.
impala, pl. balubondwe, e.g. Mucibanda ca Kafwuwe kuli balubondwe banji. There are many impala on the Kafue Flats.
good luck in finding things, e.g. Coolwe ciletela lubonena Iwamali munzila. = Good luck brings the good fortune of finding money in the path.

bride wealth, riches, goods, e.g. Muntu mukutausi ujisi lubono lunji. = An industrious person has much wealth. Muntu uvwubide lubono lunji, kanji-kanji ulalela bantu banji. A person with abundant wealth very often looks after many dependants. Nokwakamana kuselana, bana koomulombwana bakapa lubono Iwamasyobe. = When the marriage negotiations were finished, the relatives of the boy gave a wife-payment of hoes.
a lynx, e.g. Luboye ngusimweenda alikke alimwi uvwima masiku, tabonwi-bonwi. The lynx travels alone and it hunts at night, it is rarely seen. Also lubuwo.
a reed, pl. mabu, e.g. Bamacembele bakaindi bakali kufwepela mulubu. The old women of the past used to smoke through reeds. (mutete = a reed packed with tobacco for smoking)
a patch of low bush, e.g. Inombe zicelela mulububute tazikkuti. = Cattle which graze in a patch of low bush are not satisfied. Also lubbubuti, luvwuna.
any piece of iron or metal, e.g. Lubulo lujisi milimo minji. Metal has many uses.
Moulder of people (a name for God), e.g. Lubumbabantu nguutupa zyoonse. It is the Moulder of people who gives us all things. cf. Leza.

a slap, (Ila) e.g. Wakauma mwana kapati nkujana naakawaala lubumbaizyi wakaakulivwunga buya mbuli kuti uuma mupatinyina. She beat the child very much in that when she was throwing punches she used force as if she was beating another adult. Also lukumbaizyi, lubayi. lubumbulu a round object, e.g. Bana balayanda kubelesya lubumbulu kujaya tuyuni. Children use round objects for killing little birds.
the main road, e.g. Myoota mminji yiinda muli lubumbulu. = There are many vehicles which pass along the main road.
dusk, twilight, e.g. Inombe zyakasika alubundu-bundu. = The cattle arrived at twilight.
early morning before sunrise, e.g. Muntu undisesa ulasika alubundu-bundu lyoonse. The person who demands payment from me always arrives before sunrise.
worms, e.g. Zilyo zyabo zyakaligwa lubungululu kazitanakuzyala. = All their crops were infested by worms before producing.
a type of bird, the dikkop, (there are two types: the water-dikkop and the spotted-dikkop), e.g. Mababa alu*butwi alaa mabala atuba.* = The wings of the spotted-dikkop have white spots.)
courtyard, e.g. *Bantu ba-zyana masabe alubuwa.* = People are doing a possession dance in the court-yard.
baldness, e.g. *Mutwe wabasyaanene ulaa lubuwa.* = The head of my grandfather is bald.
a caracal, long legged lynx-like cat with black tufted ears, e.g. *Lubuwo ulalya mbeba a twana twansya.* = The carcal eats rats and young duikers. Also luboye, kanga-lubuwo.

habit of asking many questions, e.g. *Mwana ulaa lubuzila mucikolo ulazimvwa kabotu ziiyo zyakwe.* = The child who asks many questions in class understands his/her lessons well. *Ndatalika kubuzisya bapati ncobasamina mpande abakaintu mbaanyina, pesi bandaambila kuti ndilaa lubuzila.* = I began to ask the elders why they wore the mpande shell and the women cowry shells, but they said I was too inquisitive.
crown of the head, e.g. *Inzoka yakamugoma alubwebwe, aciwezo amunsingo.* = The snake bit him on the crown of the head, on the shoulder and on the neck.
laterite, e.g. *Bulongo bwalubwebwele tabubambyi zitina.* = Laterite soil is not for making bricks with.
a quarrelsome disposition, talkativeness, e.g. *Muntu ulaa lubweko ngusibunjaka.* = The one who has a quarrel-some disposition with others is a bringer of conflict. Also kabwekela, kababa.
small stones, gravel, e.g. *Muntu ulaa zinowe taendi kabotu mu-lubwe-lubwe.* = A person who has corns does not walk easily on gravel. Also lubwebwele.
thin porridge, e.g. *Beembezi balya lucese Iwamukupa muciba.* = The herders are eating thin porridge in the kraal.
a troupe of small monkeys, e.g. *Muunda wakavwumpwa aluceta nguwako.* = The field which was invaded by a troupe of monkeys is yours.
a type of bird, the starling, e.g. *Bakazingulusya bwizu acikala kukobelela luceu.* = They surrounded the well with grass to prevent the starling from dirtying the water.
a snake's tail, e.g. *Lucila Iwamuceka ndupati.* = A python's tail is big.
the crest of the hoopoe bird, e.g. *Lucililimba Iwankunkuunku lujisi mabala mabotu.* = The crest of the hoopoe has beautiful colours. Also cizonzoolo, cinyonzololo, cisunka, ciimba.
the secretary-bird, e.g. *Lweendo ndubi sunu ndainjilwa lucimbanyendo.* = My journey today is bad because a secretary-bird crossed my path. Also Iwiinga-nyendo, jule.
sable-antelope (female), e.g. *Tamweelede kujaya lucinga wakazyala ino.* = You ought not to kill a sable-antelope which has given birth recently.
a patch of mucinga trees, e.g. *Balala balayanda kukkala mulucinga.* = Black mamba snakes like to live among the mucinga trees.
malice, mischievous jealousy, e.g. *Banji bakajaigwa akaambo kaluciso a munyono.* = Many were killed because of hatred and envy.
evil propensity to commit crimes, e.g. *Muntu ulaa lucondo uyakufwambaana kunjila muntolongo.* = A person with a strong inclination to criminal acts will quickly go into jail.
a whistle, e.g. *Bantu bazyana cinande balabelesya ludweba.* = People who dance cinande use a whistle.

a place of death, e.g. *Lufwido* Iwasyaambololo mpaakasamu naaba acuulu. = The death place of a kudu is by a tree or an anthill lufwu death, e.g. Mazubaano lufwu Iwavwula akaambo kasikalileke. = These days are filled with death from AIDS. Lufwu talutijigwi. Death cannot be escaped.
a calabash with a long stem, pl. imfwulu, e.g. Amundigwasye meenda mulufwulu. Give me water in a longstemmed calabash.
a type of bird, the painted-snipe, e.g. Ndakaenena lufwulu akati kamatete munsi amulonga. = I spotted a paintedsnipe among the reeds beside the river.
hot ash, as used to bake potatoes, e.g. Baama bayoka cimbwali mulufwuse. My mother is roasting sweetpotatoes in hot ash.
salvation, e.g. Lufwutuko Iwakwe mbana bakasika, nibakamujaya bantu. His salvation was the arrival of his children, otherwise the people would have killed him.
a spoon, e.g. Amundipe lugo ndilisye musozya. Give me a spoon to eat the mash of whole-grain maize, beans and groundnuts. Also muungo, conco.
a wide open space, e.g. Bananja bakali kulunduka alugwagwa lupati. The lechwe-cobs were running in a big wide open space.
a letter, writing, pl. magwalo, ingwalo, e.g. Kwakasika lugwalo lubotu izoona. A very good letter arrived the day before yesterday.
help, e.g Mwami uyanda lugwasyo kuzwa kubantu. = The chief wants help from the people.
clean oil, e.g. Kamutila lugwimba mumoota tweende. Pour the oil in the car and let us go. Also mungwimba.
the non-bushy part of a cow's tail, e.g. Inombe yalumwa nzengene alugwizo. The cow was bitten on the tail by ticks.

an animal horn, pl. meja, e.g. Luja Iwamunyati ndupati. The horn of a buffalo is great. (mukotolo = without horns; inkonko = with horns curved in; inkwali with straight horizontal horns; mukupi with horns curved back; imbaba = with crumpled horns.)

a diaphragm (muscular partition separating thorax and abdomen in humans or animals), e.g. Bakaintu bacizyala tabeelede kulya lujalila. = A woman who is still child-bearing should not eat the diaphram of an animal.
a weir or water-fence of reed and sorgums stalks, e.g. Ndayanda kuzela nswi alujalilo. = I want to fish at the weir.
a tongs, e.g. Komupa lujatio mwana alete mulilo. = Give the child a tongs to bring fire. Also lumano, lupasyi.
a cockscomb (crest of a cock), e.g. Mukombwe ulaa cilonda alujililimba. The cock has a sore on it's cockscomb. Also Iwiimba, ciimba, ciimbi
a field of stalks after harvest, e.g. Inombe zilacela mulukaba. = The cattle are feeding in the stalks of maize. Also lukuba.

a highly excited quarrel, e.g. Lukaka Iwabasibulale Iwaya ambele. = The highy excited quarrel of those involved in adultery grew worse. lukakatilo reverence, e.g. Tuleelede ku-baa lukakatilo kumuleli ulela kabotu. = We should have respect for a leader who rules well.
a letter, e.g. Koleta lukalata Iwakazwida kumwana wangu. = Bring the letter which has come from my child. Also lugwalo.
a twisted fibre of bark, a fibre rope, pl. inkalo, e.g. Impongo yaangidwe *lukalo.* = A goat is tied with a fibre rope. *mukalo* = a big rope.

a serious matter, e.g. *Kwakaba lukalo lupati niyakapya nanda.* = It became a serious matter when the house was burnt. *lukamantano* = unity, cooperation, e.g. *Munzi ujisi lukamantano ulasumpuka kufwambaana.* = A village which has harmony quickly develops.
skin on the body, e.g. *Masowe ulaa zibika alukanda.* = Masowe has rashes on the skin.
sloughed snake-skin, e.g. *Utalulyati lukanda Iwanzoka yakalikwama.* = Do not step on the skin of the snake which has sloughed.
an appearance, e.g. *Sunu musimbi wangu ulaa lukanda lubi.* = Today my girl-friend has an unhealthy appearance.
an eyelid, e.g. *Kondijwa nkoye yaindilila kulampa kuzwaa lukanda Iwankoye.* = Pluck for me the eye-lash which is protruding from the eyelid.

a very strong traditional medicine given to a woman to prevent her from having sexual relations with other men, e.g. *Ooyu mukaintu wakateegwa lukanko aboobo tayelede kuyandwa abasankwa bambi.* = This woman has been given *lukanko* medicine and so she should not be loved by other men.

a type of snake *lukano* half-moon shaped axe, e.g. *Bamwi bantu baalilwa kufwula tweembe, lukano, lupasyi, sumo a muumba.* = Some people are unable to forge little axes, a half-moon shaped axe, a tongs, a spear and a fishing-spear. Also *bukano*
a plan, e.g. *Mumoyo wakwe wakabaa lukanzo lupati Iwakuti Nacintu teelede kulekwa buyo.* = In his heart grew a great plan that he should not just leave Nacintu.
good grazing-grass, e.g. *Inombe zilayanda kulya lukata.* = Cattle like grazing good grass.
a potsherd, pl. *nkaye*, e.g. *Baneene bakwiya tombwe mulukaye.* = My grandmother is grinding tobacco in a potsherd.
a cucumber plant, e.g. *Lukoa olu luzyede makowa manji.* = This cucumber plant produces many cucumbers. Also *lukowa*.

a bird, the cattle egret, or a flock of such birds, e.g. *Lukobo lulya nzen-gene.* = The cattle-egret eats ticks. *Inswaanganino njiifwa lukobo.* = It is in a gathering of people that the cattle-egret dies.
a ferret or weasel, grey-mongoose (muishond), pl. *balukobo*, e.g. *Balukobo bazimana nkuku.* = The weasels have finished off the chickens.
a disease characterized by extreme emaciation, e.g. *Bulwazi bwasikalileke ndukobo lunyenaanzya kapati.* = AIDS is a disease of extreme emaciation which causes fearful emotions.
a cattle-egret, e.g. *Mumaanza wakajisi nkwilimba ituba buu mbuli lukobokobo.* = In his hands he had a pidgeon which was very white like an egret. Also *lukobo*
eves, verandah, e.g. *Basibukoko balikkede mulukoce.* = The beer-drinkers are seated on the verandah.
an area of *mukoka* trees, e.g. *Basankwa baleembela nombe mulukoka.* = The herders are herding cattle among the *mikoka* trees.
eye-lash, e.g. *Nseboni kabotu nkaambo lukoka muliso lyangu Iwalampa.* = I cannot see well because my eyelash is too long.
string, e.g. *Amukaange lukole koombe kataunkilili musyokwe.* = Tie the calf with string so that it does not go into the bush as well.
the nipple of breast, the breast itself, pl. inkolo, e.g. Mwana uyanda *lukolo*. = The child wants the breast.
teat of quadruped animal, e.g. *Lukolo Iwanombe eyi lulizimbide*. = The teat of the cow is swollen.
a furrow, rut, ditch, e.g. Bayaki basya *lukololindi* Iwarnanda. = The builders are digging the foundation trench of the house. Also *lulindi*
Also *lukololindi*
a large bead, e.g. Munene ujisi *lukolwe lulamfwu*. = The old man has a large long bead.

a calabash with curved stem, used as a cup, e.g. Kaindi twakali kunywida *mulukoma* meenda. Long ago we were drinking water from a calabash with a curved stem. Wakateka bukoko mulu*koma* akubutilaila ansi ziindi zyotatwe kumwi kalomba mizimo kuti kiiciba-langanya kabotu kubatilila cilyo cinji myaka yoonse. He drew up beer in a calabash and poured it three times on the ground while praying to the spirits asking them to continue looking after them well and bestowing on them plenty of food through all the years. Also *lufwulu*.

navel, umbilicus, e.g. Mukaintu uminsyi tayelede kuzutula nyama yamutendu amaanza inga *lukombo* luya kuzutuka akucaalila kuli camacembele kuciindi cakutumbuka. = A pregnant woman ought not to tear off a strip of meat with her hands as perhaps the umbilicus will be torn off and remain attached to the afterbirth at the time she gives birth. Also *ikkombo*.
umbilical-cord, e.g. *Lukombokombo Iwamwana Iwakaloka kale*. The umbilical-cord of the child has already dropped off.
a little mud-wall built to enclose pool in receding river, e.g Basibbuku bakayaka *lukome* Iwameenda. = The headman built a mud-wall to trap the water in the receding river.

arrogance, bullying, e.g. Kubaa *lukomo* tacipi kukkala kabotu. = Arrogance does not give peaceful living. Kugobelo kwakali *lukomo* lupati. Basankwa bapati bakali kukoma akutundulula basankwa bakacili baniini. In the boys quarters there was much bullying. The older boys would dominate and punish the boys who were still small.
discipline, e.g. Beembezi bakajisi lu*komo* kaindi. Long ago the herders were disciplined. *Lukomo* cakali cikolo cipati ciindi cesu. = Discipline was the great school in our time.
happiness, e.g. Bakajana *lukondezyo* kumilimo njobakacita. = They found joy in the work which they did.
a type of bird, the beeeater, pl. balukonga, e.g. Ntuunga balu*kongo* tulaleya mabwe. = The bee-eating birds avoid stones (thrown at them) in flight.
female genitals, vagina (taboo word), e.g. Cilatondwa kubelesya *lukongo* kutukila muntu. It is taboo to insult a person by using the word 'lukongo'.

a verandah, e.g. Mudaala wakali kufweba tombwe mumfwuko mu-*lukonkono*. The old man was smoking tobacco in his pipe on the verandah. Bazoka wakabayalide mbuli mitanda mu-*lukonkono*. He has spread the big snakes in the verandah like pieces of wood. Also iduze, ikkoce.
dryness, hardnss, e.g. Insima yayuma *lukonko-nondo*. = The nsima is as hard as the shell of a tortoise. Also mugalanganga.

inheritance, e.g. *Lukono* ndubono Iwamufwu ndwaasiya naafwa. Oolu lubono lulaabanwa abasimukowa wamufwu oyo. Ooku kwaabana *lubono* olu nkokukona. *Lukono* is the wealth which a dead person leaves when s/he dies. This wealth is distributed by the clan of that dead person. This distribution of this wealth is called lukono. Bana ba Mutinta tiibakabweza cintu alukono Iwausyi. = The children of Mutinta did not take a thing from the inheritance of the father.
confusion, e.g. Tiibakamaninzya mulimo akaambo kalukopano. = They did not finish the work because of the confusion.
judgement, e.g. Lukosolo Iwamulandu tiilwakaba kabotu. = The verdict was not just.
headache, e.g. Wakatalika kuungumana anga ninkuku yaciswa lukotwe. = He began to look down like a hen who had a headache.
a verandah, e.g. Kosekka mapepe mulukotye. = Insert the feathers in the verandah. Also iduze, koce, lukonkono

cucumber-seeds, e.g. Mu muunda omu kwakasyangwa lukowa lunji. = A lot of cucumber-seeds have been planted in this field. lukoye one eye-lash, pl. inkoye, e.g. Kogusya kasanga alukoye, kalakutowa. = Remove the fragment of wood from the eye-lash, it will enter the eye.
a field with only stalks left standing, e.g. Impongo zilacela mulukuba. The goats are grazing among the empty maize stalks. Also lukaba, makuti.
a bird, the snipe, pl. inkubwi, e.g. Basankwa baakujaya lukubwi lunji. = The boys are off to kill a lot of snipe. cf. lukukukwi
a fibrous plant in fields, grass for making ropes, e.g. Lukuku lulayasa. = The grass for making ropes pierces. Also -lukukwa
Indian hemp, e.g. Muntu wakaangwa akaambo kakusambala lukuku. = The person was arrested because of selling hemp.
a bird, the snipe, e.g. Basankwa bakajaya buyo lukukubwi lomwe. The boys killed only one snipe. Also lukubwi.

jute, a rough fibre made from the stems of a tropical plant, used for making rope or sacking, and also hemp, e.g. Amoose looye Iwalukukwa, ndoluyumu. = Weave a rope of jute, it is the one which is strong.
a common fibrous plant found in the fields. Also lukuku
the track, as of rat, e.g. Imbeba ziinda mulukula Iwazyo. The rats pass within their track. Also migula.
a type of plant or tuber sucked for water, also eaten during famine. e.g. Ciindi canzala bantu balalya lukuli. = During time of famine people eat the lukuli tuber.
a type of bird, the nightjar, e.g. Lukumba tayaki cinteente. = The night-jar does not build a nest.
leather waist-belt, e.g. Musankwa usamide lutambo Iwalukumba mucibuno. = The boy is wearing a leather belt around his waist.
a slap with palm of hand, e.g. Musankwa Iwamuusya lukumbaizi. = The slap caused the boy to fall down. Also lubayi.
a log of wood, a piece of firewood, pl. inkuni, e.g. Kamuleta lukuni lomwe. Bring one piece of firewood.
one time, one occasion, e.g. Ndainda lukupu lomwe kumuuma. = I have just beaten him once.
a clump of bushes, also lutewo-tewo lukuuku small maize, e.g. Lukuuku mmapopwe maniini alimwi aatajisi amakweelele manji. = Lukuuku is small maize and it does not have many leaves.
a stockade, as around a kraal, a stockade of growing trees around a place for meetings, e.g. Bantu balasyanga zisyu zyabo mulukwakwa. = People plant their relish within a fenced-off area.
type of tree, e.g. _Mulukwamba-nzuba tamunjili banyama._ = Animals do not enter under the _lukwambanzuba_ tree.
plant (_Corchorus_ sp.), pounded leaves cooked for green relish, e.g. _Baama batwa lukwankwa kuti bajike cisyu._ = Mother pounds the _lukwankwa_ plant to cook relish.
multiple marrying, e.g. _Muntu muvwuule ulaa lukwata-kwata._ = A promiscuous person goes through many marriages.
marriage, e.g. _Lukwato Iwabana baya luli kabotu._ = The marriage of those young people is good.
a big basket used as a measure for grain, a strainer-basket, pl. _imkwi._ e.g. _Kamupima mapopwe mulukwi._ = Measure the grain in the strainer-basket.
a flash of lightning, e.g. _Ndalu-yoowa lulabo nkaambo lulajaya._ = I fear lightning because it kills.
drought in the rainy season. e.g. _Lulanga talukomenzyi zisyango._ = A period of drought during the rains does not help the crops to grow.
expectant waiting, e.g. _Wandijazya lulangilo mweenzuma utasiki ino._ = My friend who has not arrived has punished me in waiting for him.

the season when growth begins, e.g. _Oobu bwakali buzuba bubotu, bukasaala kabotu ciindi calulelema._ = It was a beautiful day, nice and warm at that time of the year when growth begins. _Kwakali kululelema mumwezi wa Kavwumbi-kaniini._ = It was the season of growth in the month of October. Also _lulema_
a young new leaf, e.g. _Inyenze zilalila mululema._ = The cicadas are making noise in the new leaves. Also _lulelema_
the forest when trees are well in bud, e.g. _Ncibotu kuvwima tuyuni mululema._ = It is good to hunt little birds in the forest when the trees are in bud.
a design, e.g. _Citenge eci cijisi lulembo (bulembo) lubotu._ = This citenge has a beautiful design.
an incision for tattooing
Also _lukombokombo_
the tongue, pl. _indimi,_ e.g. _Tuleelede kucenjela kubelesya lulimi, lulaumya._ = We ought to be careful in using the tongue, it can bring a beating. Also _mulaka._
the run of foundations, a ditch around a field, e.g. _Basya lulindi Iwananda._ = They are digging the foundation trench of the house. Also _lukololindi_

part of marriage payment, e.g. _Cuumakkoma, luselo, luliyo, mafwenezya alubono lumwi lukwatya musimbi lulayandwa._ The marriage instalments for marrying a girl, _cuumakkoma, luselo, luliyo and mafwenezya,_ are necessary.
habit of begging, e.g. _Lulombela Iwanyama luletela cikoolo._ = The habit of begging for meat causes illness.
a flower, pl. _induba,_ e.g. _Luluba Iwabunkululu ncisyu._ = The flower of the _bunkululu_ plant is used for relish.
a chain of hills, e.g. _Muli banyama banji mululundu Iwa Nazyaando._ = There are many animals in the hills of Nazyaando. Also _tulundu_
a source of problems, e.g. _Ooyo musimbi wamwami tatukakonzyi kukuzumizya kumukwata, uyootupa lulyananga amoyo._ = We cannot permit you to marry that daughter of the chief, she will give us problems.
the right hand, e.g _Tubelesya janza lyalulyo notulya._ = We use the right hand when eating.
war, pl. _imamba,_ e.g. _Kwakabuka lumamba lupati akati kabasibbola._ = A big fight broke out among the footballers.
a tongs, e.g. Mwana wandiletela mulilo alumana. The child brought me fire with a tongs. Also lujatilo
a tongs or pincers, pl. imano, e.g. Ndoolu lumano, undiletele sizi lyamulilo. Here are the tongs, bring me an ember.
a place full of animal-burrows, e.g. Mucuulu omu muzwide lumbo Iwansezi. This anthill is full of the burrows of wild cats.
an unploughed field where plants have grown over the last year, e.g. Mutinta wakali kuyanga-yanga makuti atumbwali twamakoko akulya minsale yamakoko mulumbuumbe.
was uprooting tubers of sweetpotatoes and eating sugar-cane growing in an unploughed field.
small sweet-potatoe, e.g. Twali kulya lumbwali Iwini-Iwini. = We were eating real tasty small sweet-potatoes. Also cimbwali

a group of young children, e.g. Balupati-pati bakalekezya lumbwiila-mbwiila kubinga nombe balo bakali kutobela buyo munsi. = The older boys allowed the group of small children to drive the cattle while they just followed behind. Also lumbwili-mbwili.
a collection of very small children (lit. a swarm of little flying ants). e.g. Ndakajana lumbwiili-mbwiili lulasobana munzila. = I found a group of children playing on the way.
dew, e.g. Ndali kuya bukupa lume nindali kuya kwa Haajwakasako. = I was shaking off the dew as I walked to Haajwakasako's village. Also mume.
pride in one's ability, e.g. Akaambo kakucizyiba kabotu kuuma bbola, Mapande ulaa lumeko. Because of being expert in playing football, Mapande is full of pride.
a smile which attracts somebody in love affairs, e.g. Musimbi muvwuule ulaa lumeko kubasankwa banji. A prostitute smiles to attract many boys.

hot ashes, e.g. Milomo yakwe yakatalika kuba mbuli yamuntu wali kulya nyemu zyayokelwe mulumfwukuse. His lips began to look like a person who had been eating groundnuts roasted in hot ashes. Also lufwuse

a kind of termite building large hills, the soil of ant-hills, e.g. Cisani cangu cakaligwa lumoma. = My frock has been eaten by termites. Mutinta wakatalika kulya lumoma akusala zyakulya kutondezya kuti wamita. = Mutinta began to eat ant-hill soil and choose food, showing that she was pregnant. Also mumoma, mucenje, mulanzyi, munanze. (Before they drop their wings, they are called inswa. When flying they are called bwiliili. Termites who build small heaps, mostly in the vleis, are insumbwa, tuumbusu, manyenya. Their heap is
pl. masumbwa or cipumuulu, cuumbusu or cuumbuswa.) A proverb says, Mulandu tuubumbwa lumoma. = A crime is not eaten away by termites. (cuulu = ant-hill; nyoola = queen of ants;

or bamajenya = soldier ants; cintuluntumba = nest; mutende, sing. katende, a blackish kind living in the same anthills as the lumoma, coming out in large swarms during the second half of the rainy season, eaten only by children. Matingatila = large kind who fly out of the anthills and are fat and delicious, also called matingi-tingi; banacisinza or basicinzi = grey, cutting grass and storing it underground in big hole called inkubwi;

or tusilakuku or cinanabasimbi = whitish ants which make a cake of food, cikonga, pl. makonga, which the anteaters eat together with the termites lumomba a type of relish, e.g. Twalikulisya *lumomba* sunu. = We were eating *lumomba* relish today.

a sting, pl. imoola, e.g. Inzuki zisiya *lumoola* moziluma. = Bees leave the sting embedded when they sting. Balasamba ameenda akasaala mumaanza akumeso kuti batazimbi *alumoola* Iwanzuki. = They wash their hands and face with warm water so that they don't swell with the stings of the bees. Mulizyi anywebo *lumoola* mbolucisa. = And you, you know how a bee-sting hurts. Also lubole, lumole.
the state of gasping and dehydration after running. e.g. Mwanaakwe wakatijaana kapati. Kumamanino wakafwa *lumpamba*. = His child was running hard. In the end he was gasping for breath.
a roan-antelope, e.g. Bantu baweza *lumpelembe* mulwaani. = People hunt the roan-antelope among the mopani trees.
an uncultivated edible root, e.g. Beembezi balya *lumpobo* mumilundu. = The herders eat the *lumpobo* root among the hills.
density, e.g. Cilakatazya kuvwima *mulumpote*. = It is difficult to hunt in thick bush. (cisaka *calumpote* = a dense forest.)
