bush remaining in deserted fields, e.g. Ooyu ngomwaka ngobakalonga bana Bimbe, eelyo mumyuunda yabo kwaacaala tumwi twakulyaalya mbuli tumbwali *mulumpuumbe*. = This was the year when the people of Bimbe moved, therefore there remained in their fields some little things to eat like sweet potatoes among the bushes.
a cluster of thorny bushes, e.g. Bantu tabalunduki kabotu *mulumvwa-lumvwa*. = People do not run easily in thorny bushes. Also *Iwamvwa-Iwamvwa, bujabuya.*
a dispersal, e.g. Yakabuka nkondo, mpoona munzi onse Iwakaba *lumwayu kutija.* = War arose, thereupon the whole village scattered in running away.

a smile, e.g. Musankwa wakabaa *lumwemwe* naakazumina musimbi. = The boy had a smiling face when the girl agreed to his proposal. Camba cakwe catalika kukkalikila, *lumwemwe Iwasika kumeso.* = His chest began to be at peace, a smile came to his face. Nacintu wakalanga kumbi pesi nkujana busyu *lumwemwe mbwe.* = Nacintu turned the other way but one could find there was a wide smile on her face. Ino walo kumvwa boobo *lumwemwe Iwakali kusika kumakosi.* = Now when she heard that, the smile spread to the back of her head.
the left hand, or left side, e.g. Kamujatila *kulumwensyi* zituli zyanyama. = Hold the pieces of meat in your left hand.

the heat and light of the sun day-time when the sun is shining, e.g. Kamuyanika zisani *mulumwi.* = Dry the clothes in the sun-shine. Ciindi cakubeleka ncibi kutandabala mbuli nzoka iiyotela *lumwi.* = During work hours it is bad to stretch yourself out like a snake warming itself in the sunshine. (if the sun is not shining = *mamfwumfwu*)
rumours, e.g. *Lumya-lumya ndakatiilumvwe.* = I heard some rumours. Also mavwambukila, intwiintwi, lumyaamya
a muddy place, e.g. Inombe taziyandiki kucelela *muluncaan-nkwiza.* = Cattle should not be allowed to graze in a muddy place.

dusk, e.g. Ndapiluka kumunzi *alundindiwana.* = I return to the village at dusk. Bakaya kumunzi kukususula zilyo akalangabwaaseme akukotoka alundindiwana. = They went home for lunch at noon and knocked off at dusk. Also lubundu-bundu, ludimadima.
tomatoes, e.g. Cisyu cabikkwa lundombasi cilanona. Relish to which tomatoes are added is tasty. Also madeede.
something spotted black and white like a leopard, e.g. Mwami usamide kakutu kalundwanga-ndwanga. = The chief is wearing a spotted hide.
frivolity in dress, e.g. Musankwa munzanzi usama lundwanga-ndwanga. = A naughty boy dresses in a ridiculous way. Also lundwele-ndwele
life style or mannerisms of the old, e.g. Ncibi kulipa lunenenene inga wacembaalila lyo. = It is bad to pretend to be old as it might really make you old.
obesity, e.g. Muntu walunene-nene talunduki kabotu, ulakatala kufwambaana. = An obese person does not run well, s/he tires quickly.
the waist, e.g. Bantu nibakali kutingaana kaindi, bakali kujatana mulunengu. When people were wrestling long ago, they caught each other around the waist.
cream, e.g. Mabisi ajisi lungabi-ngabi ngamabotu. = Sour milk with cream is delicious.
iron rims, e.g. Lungengema Iwancinga Iwakapanduka. = The rims of the bicycle are split.

a pumpkin plant, e.g. Mwaka uno lungu tiilwakazyala kabotu nkaambo kadanga. The pumpkins did not grow well this year due to the drought. Also luungu, muungu, ipusi, muntemba, namundalanga, muzuma, kapande, mumbale.
collective for very small children or babies when they are troublesome, e.g. Kamulutanda Junjimizimo Iwabakatazya beenzu. Drive away the bunch of kids they will trouble the visitors. Also banjimizimo
the trigger of a gun, e.g. Muvwimi yakalamba ntobolo naakakwela lunkalaba. When the hunter pulled the trigger the gun jammed.
a plant, okra, Feb.- Aug., the leaves are cooked for 30 min., e.g. Bana balayanda kusunsa lunkomba. = Children like eating the okra.
a shaven head, e.g. Amulange mwaalumi ugeledwe lunkulu. = Look at the man who has been shaven bald.
speed, e.g. Muzovwu ulijisi luno lunji kapati. The elephant has very great speed. Also lubilo.
relish of crushed groundnuts, e.g. Kwabula cisyu sunu twasunsa luntele. = As there was no relish today we dipped into crushed groundnuts.
a clump of bushes, e.g. Sulwe wayuba muluntuuntumba. The rabbit hid in a clump of bushes.
cruelty, e.g. Mudaala oyu ulaa lunya kubana beembela. This old man is cruel to the children who are herding.
kuti banji balamunyansya alimwi balamuseka, wakatalika kubelesya lunya. When the headman saw that many people were despising and laughing at him, he began to use cruelty.
bean plant, cow-pea, e.g. Atweende tukacele mponde mulunyabo. = Let us go and gather the leaves of the bean plant. Also lunyangu
a vein which appears on a woman's stomach during pregnancy, e.g. Kuti mukaintu wamita, kulatalika kukomena kasinga kazyila abbumbu kakatobelezya da akuya kusimpila akatiti lyasimpa.

aka kaitwa kuti lunyabo. = When a woman conceives, a vein begins to grow from the below the navel and proceeds upwards along the stomach as far as the breast bone, towards the end of the pregnancy. This vein is called lunyabo.
light fine rain, drizzle, e.g. *Imvwula yalunyaanywa ilatesya.* = Light fine rain makes one wet. Also lunywaanywa.

a clay dish, e.g. *Lunyanda mmutiba wakali kubumbwa kuzwa kubulongo. Wakali kupulila cilisyo, kapati nyama.* = The lunyanda was a dish which was moulded from clay. It was for dishing out food especially meat.
cow-peas, e.g. *Lunyangu ndubotu kusanina nombe.* = Cow-peas are good for feeding cattle.

beans, e.g. *Musimbi wakalimide muunda wanyangu. Nkabela lunyangu nolwakazyala, zyakatalika kululya insya. Wakayoowa kulinda lunyangu alikke masiku.* = The girl planted a field of beans. When it started producing, a duiker began to eat the beans. She feared to guard the beans alone at night.

contempt, derision, e.g. *Bana batalomene balaa lunyansyo kapati.* = Children who are badly behaved are full of contempt. *Lunyansyo talujanyi bulemu.* Contempt does not earn respect. Mainza taakali mulombe wakajisi lunyansyo antela lunya kubeenzinyina. Mainza was a young man who had no contempt or hatred for his friends.

envy of one who lacks something which others have, e.g. *Ndabaa lunyaunya kulanga bantu balya kakuli ndifwide nzala.* = I become envious looking at those who are eating while I am dying with the hunger. Aabo balaa lunyaunya, abaabo basikuyanda maali beelede kucenjela nkaambo kazunda ka HIV kaboolede bubi. Those who are lustfully envious and those who favour polygamy need to take care because the disease of HIV has come in a terrible way.

a charm used for protection, e.g. *Bakaambaula atwaambo tujatikizya misamu mbuli yabulozi, yalunyoka aimwi misamu mikali yakulisita.* They talked about matters connected with charms such as for witchcraft, for punishment of unfaithful men, and other powerful medicines for protection. Also lukanko
a razor, e.g. *Lwaande lutendezegwa alunyoolo.* The big abcess was cut by a razor. *Bazike bakali kunyoozegwa lunyoolo.* Slaves used to be shaved by a razor. Also lusakulo

a generation, a line of descent, e.g. *Muleli wamumunzi omu ngwalunyungu Iwangu.* The leader of this village is of my generation. Wakacisalazya mwami kwaamba kuti tayandi lunyungu Iwakwe kutundululwa aciinga cabazike pe. The chief clearly stated that he does not want his line of descent afflicted by the offspring of slaves.
light rain, e.g. *Mwana wafwa mpeyo akaambo kakuugwa mvwula yalunyunyu-nyunyu.* = The child feels the cold because of being drenched with the fine rain. Also lunyaanywa, luvwulavwula.
light fine rain or drizzle, e.g. *Bantu balalima noiwa mvwula yalunywaanywa.* People continue to plough when a fine light rain falls. Also nyaanywa.
spittle, e.g. *Kumulomo kwakwe kwakali kwiide kuloka lunzenge.* = From his mouth, spittle was just dropping.

complaints e.g. *Mukaintu wangu ulaa lunuņu.* = My wife is full of complaints. *Sikulizeeza wakali walununu, moyo wakwe wakali kufwambaana kukwisuka.* Sikulizeeza was full of complaints, his heart was quick to vent anger. Comwe biyo ncaakali kukatazya, wakali walununu. = In one thing she was difficult, she complained.

the palm of the hand, e.g. Naakali kuyandaula mpongo wakaliswida mate alupaka mpoona wakauma mate. = When he was searching for the goats,he spat on the palm of his hand, therupon he beat the spittle. (Where the spittle is thrown off is the direction in which he should look for the animals.)
baldness, e.g. Bamakuwa banji bajisi lupala amutwe. Many white people have bald heads.
exhaustion and thirst after running, e.g. Mukaintu oyu wafwa lupampa naali kutandwa. = This woman is dead with exhaustion having been chased away. Also lumpamba.
a receptacle for spears, e.g. Mudaala ujisi lupango Iwamasumo munanda. The old man has a holder for spears in his house. Also intaala.
a forest of mopani trees, e.g. Basyaambololo balacela mulupani. = The kudus are grazing in the mopani forest.
a very long span of oxen, e.g. Inola ikwelwa alupani Iwabasune. = The waggon is pulled by a very long span of oxen.
a tongs, e.g. Lupasi Iwangu Iwatyoka. My tongs broke. Also lumano, lupasyi.
a stick for producing fire by friction, e.g. Koleta lupasyi tupike mulilo. = Bring a stick so that we produce fire by friction. Also lupika
a payment, e.g. Musankwa wakalikupa lupeta buce-buce kusikila mulandu wakamana. = The boy was gradually making payments until the whole fine was finished.

a stick to make fire by friction, e.g. Wakatyola kasamu kayumu kamutobolo akukagonkolola kabotu-kabotu kupanga lupika. He broke off a dry branch from the carrot-tree and broke it up carefully to make a friction-stick. Also lupasyi
a stick for stirring, e.g. Insima iikopezegwa lupisyo, tiijisi makoto. = Nsima which is stirred by a stirring stick, does not have lumps. Also lupusyo.
a thicket with a rich variety of wild fruits. e.g. Basankwa baali mulupumbu. = The boys were in the thicket of wild fruits.

a gong made of a buffalo-horn and beaten with a stick lupusi a pumpkin, e.g. Oolu lupusi taluzyede. This pumpkin does not produce. (a riddle, Noenda uyoogolela kuli? Ndupusi. = When you walk where are you going to end. It is the pumpkin and its runners.) Also lungu
a stick with projections at the base for stiring, pl. impusyo, e.g. Kobelesya lupusyo kupwaya makoto munsima. = Use a stick for breaking the lumps in the nsima. Also lupisyo
dim sight, disease of eyelids when eye-lashes fall out with tears flowing, e.g. Muntu ulaa lupwe taboni kabotu. The person who has a disease of the eye-lids does not see well.
a large scoop-net used for fishing, e.g. Bazeli banji babelesya lusabwe. Many fishermen use a net. Also lusabwi
a fishing net, pl. insabwi, e.g. Kaumba wajaya nswi zinji alusabwi lusyoonto buyo. = Kaumba caught many fish with just a small net. Also lusabwe.
a mosquito net, e.g. Mazubaano babikka musamu alusabwi Iwamansenya kutegwa afwe mansenya. Nowadays they put medicine on the mosquito net so that the mosquitoes die.
a dense forest, e.g. Inzoka zilayanda kukkala mulusaka. Snakes like to live in thick forests.
a stick, the shaft of spear or arrow, e.g. *Lusako Iwasumo Iwatyoka.* = The shaft of the spear is broken.
a razor, e.g. *Lwafwumpa lusakulo, nsyekonzyi kugela kabotu.* = The razor is blunt, I cannot cut hair properly.
a comb, e.g. Kamundipa *lusakulo ndi-kamunzye masusu.* = Give me a comb to comb my hair with.
an edible tuber, (roots cooked as relish) e.g. *Ndaula lusala Iwabbekete.* = I bought *lusala* tubers costing one tin of maize. Also *Iwidi, busala.*
cleanliness, e.g. *Basilisi ba-layanda kuti kakuli lusalalo miminzi.* = The health-inspectors wish that there is cleanliness in the villages.
holiness, purity, e.g. *Ncibotu kuti kakuli lusalalo mumiya yabantu boonse.* = It is good if there is holiness in the souls of all people.
a preference in choosing among many things, e.g. *Mukaintu ulaa da ulaa lusalululo kukulya.* = When a woman is pregnant she becomes choosy as regards food.
discrimination, e.g. *Lusalululo ndubi luleta mazwanga mumisyobo yabantu.* = Discrimination is evil it brings discord among the different groupings of people.
the spine of a fish, e.g. *Lusambo Iwanswi lujisi mamvwa manji.* = The spine of the fish has many sharp bones.
an assembly, the church, pl. insangano, e.g. *Lusangano Iwesu ndo-lupati kwiinda.* = Our church is the biggest of all.
a mat of reeds, e.g. *Koona alusasa.* = Sleep on the reed-mat. Also munseme.
the grass for mat-making, e.g. *Amulete lusasa tuluke munseme.* = Bring grass for making a mat. Also masanga, mpoolwe
mercy, e.g. *Bantu banji tabajisi luse kubantu babba.* = Many people have no mercy on thieves.
laughter, e.g. *Basilubanje bajisi luseko lunyina mpolutalikila.* = People who smoke cannabis have a laughter which comes from nowhere.

payment involved in marriage, e.g. *Cuumangoma, luselo, luliyo, ama-fwenezya alubono lumwi lukwatya musimbi lulayandwa* = The marriage payments of *cuumangoma, luselo, luliyo and mafwenezya* and other payments in marrying a girl with, are needed.
a stretch of sand, e.g. *Cilakatazya kweenda mulusenga.* = It is difficult to travel over sand. Also *luti*
the horn of a small animal used as a charm or ornament, e.g. *Lusengo Iwangu Iwapya.* = My horn-charm got burnt.
sandy soil keeping moisture, e.g. *Kulima mulusensa ncibotu mudanga.* = It is good to plough in sandy soil which retains moisture during a year of drought.
an edible tuber, resembling a potatoe, e.g. *Bantu banji balalya luseza.* = Many people eat the *luseza* tuber.
an edible tuber Also *luseza*
a bulb eaten raw or cooked after pounding in October-November, e.g. *Tuyuni tumwi tulayandisya kulya lushu.* = Some little birds love to eat the bulb, *lushu.*
soot, e.g. *nanda iijikila ilijisi lusi lunji.* = The kitchen is full of soot. *Cipopwe cilaa lusi cilalula-lula.* = Maize made brown (by soot?) is somewhat bitter.
smoke, e.g. *Muntu wakkala kulusi uzwa misozi bwamutowa busi.* = A person who sits where there is smoke sheds tears when blinded by the smoke.
a stick which when rubbed produces fire, e.g. *Kobamba mulilo alusika.* = Produce fire by rubbing the friction-stick.
early short-stemed sorgum, e.g. Buuka bwalumana lusili mumuunda. = The insects have destroyed the early sorgum in the field. Also maila.
sign, indentifying mark, e.g. Ncobeni nombe ndusimbo Iwa Batonga boonse. = Cattle-ownership is the identifying mark of all Tonga people.
history, e.g. Kamwiiya lusimo kumadaala. = Learn the history from the old men.

a blood vessel or vein or artery, a swollen vein, rhumatism, nueralgia, e.g. Baneene bakaciswa lusinga mucamba. My grandfather is suffering from chest pains. (lusinga Iwalinyo = toothache; lusinga Iwakaango/ lusinga Iwamucamba = pleurisy.)
truth, e.g. Tuleelede kubaa lusinizyo muli zyoonse nzyotucita. = We ought to be truthful in all that we do.
a narrow thong or lace for fastening a shoe or sandal, e.g. Koleta lusiya tusumye mabbusu. Bring a thong so that we sow the shoes with it. lusiu See lushu.
a heaped load, e.g. Cilayi cizwide lusongwa Iwamapopwe. = The sledge is filled with a load of maize.
emission of wind from bowels, e.g. Lusozi Iwamubwa lulanunka kapati. = The wind from the dog's bowels stinks very much.
powder, e.g. Kamubikka lusu Iwamusamu acilonda. Put medical powder on the wound.
hatred, e.g. Ncibi kubaa lusulo. = It is bad to have hatred.
crumbs, fragments, powdered wood as produced by borers, e.g. Walikunyunya lusu-lusu Iwamusamu muli cakulya. She was sprinkling powdered medicine in the food.
a hoof, pl. insumba, e.g. Lusumba Iwanombe lulanona. = The hoof of a cow is delicious. Also lufwumba, pl. ifwumba.
twisted bark-fibre, rope, e.g. Kamuleta lusungo, twaange boombe. = Bring the rope so that we tie the calves. Also lukole, lutambo, looye, lukalo.
the way of yoking, e.g. Lusungo Iwabasune olu ndubi. The way these oxen have been yoked is not good.
drizzle, e.g. Bana balasobana mulusunsu Iwamvwula. The children are playing in the drizzling rain. Also lunyaanywa.
a big basket used as a receptacle for grain, or as measure for grain, a strong receptacle for carrying stones. pl. insuwo, e.g. Ndiyanda lusuwo luzwide mapopwe. I want a big basket full of maize.
menstrual flow, e.g. Mukaintu oyu ulaa luswa mbuli kuti ujisi cipalamwida. This woman has a menstrual flow as if she had period pains.
propensity to insult, e.g. Muntu siluswenyo ngusibunjaka. = A person who had a habit of insulting is one who brings dissension.
a small fish/fry, e.g. Ndaluca luswiswi lunji-lunji. = I caught a whole lot of little fish.

weeds, e.g. Mukaintu muyumu ulaumana muunda nuujisi lusyanga lunji. A strong woman will finish the field even though it be full of weeds. Mpka zimwi zyakawida mulusyanga. = Some seeds fell among the weeds. Also mbuto
trust, faith, hope, e.g. Tuleelede kubikka lusyomo muli Leza. = We should put trust in God.

insolence, arrogance, bullying attitude, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ulaa luta kubana baniini. = This boy has a bullying attitude towards the little children. Cintu civwubwa tacicitilwa luta. That which is owned (like cattle, dogs etc.) is not despised.
misfortune, e.g. Nkalisonde *lutaka*. = I should go and divine the reasons for my misfortune.
a belt, e.g. Kamulyaanga *lutambo mucibuno*. = Tie a belt around your waist.
a log of wood or firewood, e.g. Basidilwe bayanda buyo *lutanda lomwe*. = The mourners only want one log.
a tender pumpkin (leaves used as relish), pl. *intanga*, a type of edible flower or leaf, e.g. Milibo yalutanga yakatalika kuluba. = The runners of the pumpkin began to flower.
a cattle out-post, e.g. Ndazyila kukuula mabisi *kulutanga*. = I have come from buying milk at the cattle out-post.
hunting ground, e.g. Bantu bakali *kulutanga*. = The people were at the hunting- ground.
joy, e.g. Bajisi *lutangalo nkaambo bakazwidilila mumisunko yabo*. = They are happy because they passed their exams.
a bundle of grass for carrying nuts, a small bag of bark, pl. *intebe*. e.g. Mainza wakalusekka Iwija *mulutebe Iwakwe*. = Mainza stuck the horn inside the small bag of bark.
a platform for drying meat, e.g. Kamuyanuna nyama *aluteme*, yaboola mvwula. = Remove the meat from the platform, the rain is coming.
a creeping plant used for weaving, (root is used to heal wounds), e.g. Bacembele baluka cisuwo *alutende*. = The old lady weaves a basket using the *lutende* plant.
a clump of shrubs, e.g. Muntu wayuba *mulutewo*. = A person is hidding in the clump of shrubs.
a stretch of bush, e.g. Muunda oyu uzwide *lutewo-tewo*. = This field is full of patches of bush.
a reed, e.g. Ndaakujana *lutete lomwe mumulonga*. I found one reed in the river. Also *lubu*.
a spear-shaft, e.g. *Luti Iwasumo Iwatyokela mumputi*. The shaft of the spear was broken where it was bound by ox-tail.
a curse, e.g. *Lutuko Iwamulozi luletela ntenda*. The curse of a witch brings along danger.
harshness, propensity to insult, impatience, rudeness on the part of a master, e.g. Nsemuyandi muntu ulaa *lutuzi kuli bamucaala*. = I do not like a person who insults orphans. Also luswenyo.

clusters of animal ear- shaped objects, e.g. Mumasamu moonse mwakali *lutwi-lutwi Iwamatuvwu akali kusyuuka, inzya wakali mwezi wa Itwi ncobeni*. = Among all the trees there were clusters of animal ear-shaped leaves which were budding, yes it was truly the month of the leaf. (August)
dusk, *kuluubeube* = after sunset, e.g. Mubbi wakazeluluka *muluubeube*. The thief sneaked away in the darkness. Wakasika kumunzi ciindi *caluubeube*. = He reached home at twilight.
a cobweb made by the *sicuu- bilili* spider, e.g. Inzinini zilajatwa *muluubi*. = The flies are caught in the cobweb.
light mist, e.g. Nsekonzyi kubona kabotu, kuli *luubi Iwasikuunku*. = I cannot see properly, there is a light mist.
a cobweb made by the *sicuu- bilili* spider, e.g. *Luubilili lujata nzinini zinji*. The cobweb catches many flies. Also *luubi*.

a swarm of flying-insects, e.g. Lumwi *luuka lulajaya nombe*. = Some insects kill cattle. Inombe zyakaceya akaambo kabulwazi mbuzyakalwala nozyakalumwa *aluuka ndulonya luleta nyati abazovwu*. The cattle have been reduced because of the sickness which they suffered from being bitten by the same tsetse-flies which buffaloes and elephants bring.

a mark from beating, e.g. Nokuba kuti musankwa omwe bamubunganina kumuuma, kunyina akumutulula luuma mumutwe pe. = Even though they gathered around to beat one boy, they did not leave a mark on his head. Bbwe luuma taliligwa lumoma. A hard rock is not eaten by termites. (Proverb)

a clump of muumba trees, e.g. Bana bakalya mucendecende muluumba. = The children ate mucendecende fruit among the muumba trees. Nolyakalangwa kumbo zuba muluumba-umba lunji, wakateelela nsolo ilalila. When the sun was being looked at to the west among a forest of muumba trees, he heard a honey bird chirping. luumbo burrow, e.g. Cibila naakatandwa babwa, wakaakunjila muluumbo Iwakwe. When the rock-rabbit was chased by the dogs, it entered into its burrow.
fibres taken from the bark of trees, pl. zyuumpute. e.g. Isumo lyangu lizambidwe loozi luumpute. = My spear is wrapped around with fibres taken from tree roots.
very small seeds blown into the eyes of humans and cattle and causing inflamation, e.g. Ndatoogwa luundu. = Very small seeds have entered my eyes.
a type of bird, the quail, e.g. Luunga amukombwe bakali kuvwima antoomwe. A quail and a cock were hunting together.
a type of bird, the quail, Also luunga.
pumpkin leaves or plant, e.g. Matuvwu aluungu ncisyu cibotu. = Pumpkin-leaves make a tasty relish.
deceit, e.g. Ulaa luuni Iwanzoka = He has the malice of a snake. Basiluuni tabajisi lubomba. Envious people are merciless.

uncontrolled desire for sex; e.g. Aabo balaa luunya-unya, abaabo basikuyanda maali beelede kucenjela nkaambo kazunda ka HIV kaboolede bubi. = Those who have an uncontrolled desire for sex and those who are polygamists ought to take care because the virus HIV has come bringing evil.
a cockroach, pl. mausu, baluusu, e.g. Munanda mwindalede ndalumwa baluusu. In the house where I was sleeping I was bitten by coakroaches. Also igugusu, pl. magugusu.
shyness, e.g. Ulijisi luusu Iwakulomba ncapengede. = She is shy to ask for what she needs.
hypocrisy, deceit, simaano aaluusweuswe a crafty or sly person, Muntu siluuswe-uswe tasyomeki. = A deceitful person is not trusted.
drizzle, e.g. Sunu kusunsumuna luvwulu-vwulu lutontola siko. = Today there fell a very cold drizzle. Also lunyaanywa, luvwula-vwula, lunywanywa
fatty membrane around bowels, the lining of an elephant's stomach, e.g. Luvwumbula Iwabazovwu talulibonyi-bonyi. The lining of an elephants stomach is not usually seen.
kwashiorkor, e.g. Mwana uutalyi kabotu ubaa luvwumbula. The child who does not eat properly develops kwashiorkor.

a disease which can afflict a new-born baby, non-closure of the fontanelle, e.g. Kuli. nzila zinjaanji zyakusilika mwana waciswa luvwumwe. = There are many ways of healing a baby who is sick because of luvwumwe.

a patch of low bush, e.g. Insezi ili muluvwuna. A wild cat is in a patch of low bush. Mukaintu wakali kukokola luvwuna kulubazu lwamuunda. = The woman was clearing a low patch of bush on the side of the field.
an illegitimate child e.g. Mwana watazyalilwa munanda, ngwamuluvwuna. = The child not born in the house, is of the bush. Also mwana wamusyokwe.
grass formed in swamps, e.g. Ciwena uliyubide luvwundu. = A crocodile is hiding in the grass of the swamps.
the earth/land, e.g. Mazuba ano manjaka azwide luwa loonse. = These days dissension fills the whole world.

wire, a telephone call, e.g. Ndakaumya luwaile kubana kubazyibya makani alufwu. = I telephoned the children informing them about the death. Ndakatambula luwaile kuzwa kubana. = I received a telephone call from the children.

a shoulder, e.g. Munene uyumwide nkuni aluwezo. = The old man is carrying firewood on the shoulder. Also Iwezyo, gwezyo. (shoulder-blade = ikuko; shoulder-blade of an animal = ijekete, ibebete; space between the shoulders = andelo.)
wind, e.g. Sunu kuli luwo lunji, bantu tabazeli kabotu. = Today there is much wind, the people do not fish well.

bad spirits, e.g. Wakanjila syokwe kuyandaula musamu waluwo. Wakaleta musamu wakusamba akuumpilila. = He went into the bush to search for medicine against the evil spirits. He brought medicine for washing in and for smoking out the bad spirits.
the burnt bush or field, e.g. Sulwe walilede muluya mutuba bu. = The rabbit was lying in the burnt bush which had been cleared.
luya Iwamuzovwu = ivory, Also luja lwanzovwu
cream, e.g. Mukupa wakakamwa jilo ujisi luyabilizi. = The milk which was milked yesterday is full of cream.
love, e.g. Ndayanda bantu balaa luyando mumicito yabo. I want people who have love in their actions.
idea, vision, discernment, e.g. Kobaa luyeeyo lubotu nokanana abantu. = Think well when you are talking to people.
a vegetable plant with a white flower, e.g. Cisyu caluyuni ncibotu kapati mubuntele. The luyuni plant is good when mixed with pounded groundnuts.
a swarm of small birds, e.g. Luyuni lwamumusena lulya nsangaaze. = A swarm of small birds of the vlei eat grass for grazing. Also buyuni
flowing spittle, e.g. Mweemba uzwa luzenge kumulomo. = A stream of spittle comes from the moouth of Mweemba.
phlegm, e.g Munene uciswa cisini, wiide kuzwa luzingo kumulomo. = There was just phlegm coming out of the mouth of the old man who had a cold. Also lute.
all one's relatives taken together, e.g. Luzobo lokwesu lwakamana kufwa. All our relatives have died. Also luzubo
hatred, e.g. Luzondo kubantu luleta mapenzi. = Hatred towards people brings suffering.
passing hunger, e.g. Utabi a kasyimo, inzala nduzu buyo. = Don't get a bad name, the hunger is merely transient.
clan, e.g. Luzubo lumwi talukwatiki. = Certain clans are not good to marry into.
dusk, e.g. Muluzubu-zubu kwakalibonya kootokala kaleya amunzi okwa Muchindu. At dusk we saw a small car diverting to the home of Muchindu.
the envelope of the foetus, the caul portion of this found on child's head at birth, e.g. Luzyalilo Iwamusimbi oyu lulipandukide. = The uterus of this girl is torn.
fertility, e.g. Mucembele ooyu ucilaa luzyalo. = This old woman is still fertile.
tenderness, compassion, e.g. Mwami ulaa luzyalo. = The chief is kind.
the inner room, e.g. Bana tabeelede koona kuluzyuli moona bapati. = Children should not sleep in the bed-room where the elders sleep. Also izyuli.
a crevice in a rock, e.g. Izikwaba zikkala mulwaakwe. = Lizards live in the crevices of the rocks.
severe treatment of family, e.g. Ulaa Iwaambwe. = He is severe with his family. Also lununu, luta

hostility, e.g. Kutamvwana kuletela Iwaandaano. = Misunderstanding leads to hostility. Bantu boonse bakali munkuta bakatyompwa nibakabona Iwaa-ndaano Iwaciimo camusimbi oyu. = All the people who were in the court were disappointed when they saw the look of hostility of this girl.
an abcess in the armpit, e.g. Lwaande lutendezegwa alunyoolo. = The abcess can be cut by a razor-blade. Also Iwande.
a stockade for catching fish, e.g. Nsiku ba Zambezi bakajaya nswi munzila itegwa Iwaando. = Long ago Zambezi people caught fish by building a weir.
a hunting-shrine which usually takes the form of a spear-rack, and is made from a shoot of the muntiokela tree which takes root. Also loombwa, madiose.
repeated journeys to a place, e.g. Bakazumanana kubaa Iwaanga kusikila bakamujana. They continued to make repeated journeys to the place until they found him.
a type of tree, e.g. Bakayaka munzi munsi alwaanga. They built a house beside a Iwaanga tree.
Also Iwaangunuko
freedom, e.g. Mu Zambia bantu bakajana waangunuko mumwaka wa 1964. In Zambia the people obtained freedom in 1964. Also Iwaanguluko
a forest of mopani trees, e.g. Basyuumbwa bajanwa kapati mulwaani. = Lions are found especially in a mopani forest.
the sea, a large lake, e.g. Mato mapati ayenda kabotu mulwaanje. = Big ships travel well on the sea. Also luvwubu.

a crack, pl. nanzi, e.g. Inanda ilaa Iwaanzi lupati yadilika sunu. = The house with a big crack collapsed today. Kwakaba Iwaanzi lupati mumikwasyi yabo yakakkede kabotu katanasika munanga. = There arose a big division among the families whom before had lived in harmony before the witchdoctor had arrived.
finger-nail or toe-nail, e.g. Kolutenda Iwala olo lulamfwu. = Cut that long finger-nail. Igala big toe-nail
the barb of a spear, e.g. Isumo lilaa Iwala lilakatazya kujwa. The spear which has a barb is difficult to extract.
a patch of thorny bush, e.g. Maanko ayakila mulwamvwaamvwa. The mason wasps built in a clump of thorny bush.
abcess in upper arm or upper leg. Also Iwaande.
a reed fence across stream to catch fish, e.g. Batwa bazezya Iwando. = The Twa people use a reed-barrier to fish.
the general hunt when the veld is set on fire e.g. Baya kulwando. They have gone to the hunt. Also cila.

curiosity, e.g. Bavwimi batobezya Iwandwano. = Hunters follow Iwano-Iwano. their curiosity. Also *Iwanga* a spirit-gate, (forked branches of the *mubwabwa* tree when planted in the yard) e.g. *Bataata bayaka cilyango ca Iwanga.* = My father is building a spiritgate. Also *Iwaanga.*
trading, e.g. *Basambazi babelesya Iwangaana Iwanombe.* = Traders use cattle in their trading.
a long story, a song, e.g. *Bacembele balijisi Iwano lunji.* = The old woman has many stories.
curiosity e.g. *Kana aka nkalwano-Iwano.* = This child is very curious. Also *Iwandwano*
a chasm, a chink, a crack, e.g. *Meenda amanina kuya ansi mulwansi.* = The water finished going down through a crack. Also *Iwaanzi.*
Also *Iwanje.*
thin porridge, e.g. *Amumunywinsye Iweele mwana wanetuka nzala.* = Give the child who fainted with hunger thin porridge to take. Also *ceele.*

dreadful happening, e.g. *Lwayuma Iweembe lutola bana bavwanda balo-balo, lutatoli ndiswe notwakamana kale mulimo.* = What a dreadful happening which kills only infants, not taking us who have already finished work.
wandering about, e.g. *Lweendeendela luleetela mapenzi.* = Wandering around brings problems. Proverb: *Inzoka njenzeenzi iletela mutumba wacucu.*
a journey, e.g. *Mweenzu uli mulweendo lulamfwu.* = The visitor is on a long journey.
a prawn fishing-net, e.g. *Lusabwi IwaIweendo talubonwi kabotu kunswi.* = A prawn fishing-net is not easily seen by fish.
mercy, e.g. *Katubaa Iweengelelo kuli bamucaala.* = Let us be kind towards orphans.
the sable-antelope, pl. ba*Iweengu*, e.g. *Balweengu bajisi meja mabotu*. = Sable-antelopes have beautiful horns.

deception, e.g. Bantu basi-*Iweeno baleta ntenda mucisi*. = People who spy bring danger to the country. *Mutinta ulaa Iweeno nkaambo wanditolela nombe yangu*. = Mutinta is deceitful because he took my cow from me. Also *luuni*.
a walk, pl. *nyendo*, e.g. Ndiya-kubaa *Iwendo Nsondo iboola*. = I will journey next Sunday. Also *Iweendo*
the sea, e.g. *Mulwenje kuli mato mapati sunu*. = There are big ships in the sea today. Also *Iwaanje*.
the large-headed barbel, e.g. *Inswi yaunka nkaambo kalobo kajata alwenta*. = The fish got away because the hook caught a large-headed barbel.
small species of cicada, e.g. *Kwandikambila Iwenza nindali kunjila munanda*. = A cicada clapped its wings at me when I was entering the house. (a bad omen) Also *lubbungu*.
a type of tree, e.g. *Mbelele ampongo zilatantaana mulukoka amu-Iweye*. = Sheep and goats wander far away to the *lukoka* and *Iweye* forests. Also *mweeye*.

a type of bird, the bustard, knorhaan, lesser paaw, e.g. *Lwibbe ujisi maulu malamfwu*. = A bustard has long legs. *Masusu aa Munali akali mbuli mapepe alwibbe*. = The hair of Dr. Livingstone was like the feathers of a bustard bird.
a type of tuber, e.g. Namwiinga abanyina bakafwuma kukusya *Iwidi musaka*. = Namwiinga and her mother went out early to dig tubers in the forest. Also *lusala*.

a shell, molusc, mussel, pl. *njilli*, e.g. *Mulwaanje momujanika Iwiill*. = Shells are found in lakes. *Wakaakazya* makani kuyuma buya _mulwiili_ nta. = He denied the affair vehemently as strong as a closed shell-fish.

a song, pl. nyimbo, e.g. _Baimbi bakaimba Iwiimbo lubotu._ = The singers sang a nice song. e.g. _Nyimbo zyakwe zyakalaa majwi anyendo, zyaku-sunza zilyo, nzala, buunyu, kusomba, kulima, bulyo buli mbuli bwabacimvwinye acinkumwe amajwi amwi aswaangene anzala acewo._ = Her songs contained words about journeys, searching for food, stinginess, generosity, farming, foods of insects and other words connected with famine and plenty.

traditional agricultural rituals celebrated before planting, (_Iwiindi Iwa-kumwaka_) and harvest (_Iwiindi Iwaku-tebula_) pl. inyindi, e.g. _Munzi wesu waka-alilwa kukumba Iwiindi._ Our village failed to brew the beer for the _Iwiindi_ celebrations. Bakali kuya kwa Chibwe kumukaintu wakali musinsimi kumuzyibya kuti _Iwiindi Iwakali afwiifwi kunyikwa._ = They were going to Chibwe to a woman who was a prophetess to inform her that the _Iwiindi_ ritual was about to be pre-pared. (i.e. the maize was being soaked to make beer for it.)
a potsherd, as used to cover a pot, e.g. _Kwakacaala buyo Iwiinga mpu-bakali kubumbila zibiya baneene._ = There only remained a potsherd where my grandma was making pots. Also _lukaye_
the secretary-bird, e.g. _Wakasuma mulomo walwiinga-nyendo antoomwe akalezu kasijembwe wa-mpongo._ She sewed the beak of a secretary-bird together with the beard of a male goat.
the cord or stick which passes through the nose of a cow, e.g. _Kamumubikka Iwiingwa moombe oyo aleke kunyonka._ = Put a cord through the nose of the calf to stop it sucking.
a nose-ornament, e.g. _Bamacembele baku Dindi balibikka Iwiingwa mumpemo._ = The women of the Gwembe Valley wear nose- ornaments. Also _Iwingwa, bulumbalumba, cisita._

the hole made in the cartilage of the nose **Iwiiyo** learning, education, e.g. _Lwiiyo ndobaiya mazubaano mwati baiya zyamaano biya?_ = In the education which they receive today are they learning real wisdom?
an animal horn, e.g. _Ndiya kukusunza zilyo kumwaalumi uujisi Iwija luzwa zilyo nalusiba._ I am going to ask for food from a man who has a horn which produces food after he blows into it.
the shell of a snail, pl. njili, e.g. _Lwili ndolupazya zibiya._ = You scrape with a shell to make the pots smooth. cf. _Iwiili._
a cockscomb, e.g. _Mukombwe ujisi Iwimbilila lulamfwu._ = The cock has a long cockscomb.
a song, e.g. _Lwimbo lubota kulwiimba kabotu._ A song becomes good when sung properly. Also _Iwiimbo._
the Tonga agricultural thanks-giving rituals, e.g. _Kuyakuba Iwindi Iwacisi coonse ku Gonde._ There will be a traditional ritual for the whole country at Gonde. Also _Iwiindi._
a nose-ring, e.g. _Lwinga Iwakabikkidwe amoombe Iwakaloka._ = The nose-ring which had been put on the calf dropped off. Also _Iwiinga, bulumbalumba_
Also _Iwiingwa_
a big river, a lake, e.g. _Mulwizi momujanwa nswi zipati._ In the sea is where is found big fish. Also _Iwizyi_
passing hunger, e.g. _Utabaa kaambyo nkobanakukwaamba bantu, inzala ndwizu._ Do not pay attention to what people say, the hunger ia passing. Also _luzu._
the Zambezi river, Lake Kariba, the sea, any large stretch of water, e.g. *Cimwi ciindi mayuwe mapati alajanika mulwizyi.* = Sometimes big waves are found at sea. Also *Iwizi.*
scale of fish or crocodile, pl. maamba, e.g. *Ciwena wabbabbuka lyaamba lipati.* = A big scale has been detached from a crocodile.
a big mopani tree, e.g. *Muyuni ulikkede mulyaani.* = A bird is resting in a big mopani tree.
a larva, as of a bee, pl. mana, e.g. *Lyana lipati lyakazwa mukkwa lyabuci.* = A big larva came out of the honey-comb.
a bird, the vlei-lourie, e.g. *Ndakajaya lyobolo amalekani.* = I killed a lourie with a catapult. Also *lyabola*
a flea, pl. maundu, e.g. *Baama balumwa lyuundu nobali kuzela mucizyiba.* = My mother was bitten by a flea when fishing in a pool. Also *munsyundu*
a plot of land which has remained un- ploughed for a long time. e.g. *Basankwa bavwima babeya mulyuundu.* = The boys were hunting birds in the unused field. Also *igundu.*

a big round edible bitter hard- shelled wild fruit which ripens turning from green to yellow at the beginning of the hot season, referred to as the big wild orange. pl. of *igabo*, e.g. *Bakakololo balayanda kapati kulya maabo.* = Gerbilles like very much to eat big wild oranges.
epilepsy, e.g. *Bunji bwabantu baciswa maafwa balabaa kasuntu ciindi cakkala-kkala mwezi.* = Many people who suffer from epilepsy have a fit at the new moon.
plenty, e.g. *Ulajana maala-maala abana.* = You will find plenty of children.
polygamy, e.g. *Maali alalunguzya.* = Polygamy causes hardship. Chinkonti ngusimaali, ujisi bakaintu botatwe. = Chinkonti is a polygamist, he has three wives.
a special axe, e.g. *Mwami uyenzya keembe kamaalila.* = The chief walks with a maalila axe. Also *keembe kamalengwa.*
pl. of *igamba*, a crack on feet, e.g. *Kolicumba abbwe kugusya maamba kutusindi.* = Rub yourself with a stone to remove the cracks on the ankles.
pl. of *ijamba*, a hoe or a plough, e.g. *Kamuleta maamba tukalime.* = Bring ploughs so that we go and plough.
gossip, e.g. *Ulalitaya kuti kolaa maambaamba.* = You will involve yourself in serious problems if you gossip.

what is spoken in a concealed way, e.g. *Kukanazya maamba-mbali inga bana tabamvwi ncowamba.* = It is not likely that children will understand what you say if you talk with deep hidden meanings. Also *maambila-mbali.*
insinuations, allusions, secret or deeper hidden meaning, Also *maamba-mbali.*

an illness affecting babies been suckled (arising from immoral sexual actions of a parent), e.g. *Kwategwa akali maambizyi ngaakali kuciswa.* = They said the baby was suffering from an illness (caused by parental sexual immorality).
excrement of baby, e.g. *Mutinta uyola maambukwa amwana.* = Mutinta is taking away the excrement of the baby. *Uleelede kusinda maambukwa.* = You should wipe away the baby's excrement.
'*maambukwa abana*'is used to describe the colour yellow. e.g. *mapopwe a maambukwa-abana* = yellow mealies, Also *nkweegwe*
the uncut leaves of pump- kin cooked with fish as a relish, pl. of igambwa, e.g. Maambwa ajikwa munswi alanona. = Pumpkin leaves cooked with fish are delicious.
epilepsy, e.g. Chikandi uciswa maafwa ncataunki kucikolo. = Chikandi has epilepsy that is why he does not go to school.
a honeycomb full of larvae, e.g. Bamwi bantu bayandisya kulya maana abuci. = Some like to eat the honeycombs full of larvae. Also mana.
pl. of nanda (a house), e.g. Bantu basunu bayaka maanda mabotu. = People of the present generation build good houses.
a pollard (animal that has cast or lost horns), e.g. Musune oyu ngwamaando ulaluma. = This hornless ox bites. Also muvwuma
coarse meal left after stamping which is given to fowl, e.g. Insima eyo mmaando alo. = That nsima is just coarse meal. Also masembe-sembe.
twins, e.g. Bana bamaanga baulilwa zikozyenye. = Twins are bought similar goods. Also mayanga

multiple births at same time and in same place, e.g. Kuti bana basimbi bakkala antoomwe munanda yomwe batumbukila antoomwe ciitwa kuti maangansi. = If young girls who live together in the same house give birth at the same time it is called maangansi.
pl. of mango/inango, the nostril, e.g. Mwana ujisi mamina mumaango. = The child has mucous in the nostrils.
main poles of the roof of a round house, usually fastened together before being hoisted on the roof. Also mabompwa.
grass for cattle, e.g. Inombe zilacela mumaani mateteete. = The cattle are grazing on soft grass. Also mani.
be busily occupied doing different type of work, e.g. Mwiinga wajata maanka-maanka. = Mwiinga is caught up in many jobs.

the human reason, intellect, wisdom, sense, prudence. pl. of igano/iganu, e.g. Ooyu mwana igano/u limwi lyakazwa. = This child lost one of its faculties. Ooyu mwana ulaa maanu. = This child is intelligent. Tojisi noliba lyomwe iganu. = You have not a single drop of wisdom.
hidden food e.g. Mumpotomona omu ndijisi mwaangwa-loozi. = In this bag I have hidden food.
pl. of caanza (a horned head of game or cattle), e.g. Maanza abanyati alayoosya. = The horned heads of buffaloes are frightening.
pl. of ijanza (the hand), e.g. Musimbi ujisi mali manji mumaanza. = The girl is holding a lot of money in her hands.
water, e.g. Ndayanda kusamba maanzi aatontola. = I want to wash with cold water. (Some say that meenda means running water, while maanzi means still water.)
a map, e.g. Mweenzu ujisi maapu nayenda munyika mpya. = The visitor takes a map when going about in a new country.
a boundary, e.g. Mulonga wa Zambezi ngamaapu aa cisi ca Zambia a Zimbabwe. = The Zambezi river is the boundary between Zambia and Zimbabwe. Also munyinza
a big male baboon, e.g. Maapwe ulalila mumulundu. = The big male baboon is crying out in the hill.
a grey kind of millet with long stem, pl. of ngase, e.g. Bantu banji balalila maase. = Many people are eating grey long-stemmed millet.
pl. of buta, a bow (weapon), e.g. Kaindi ndakali kujaya tuyuni amaata. = Long ago I used to kill little birds with a bow and arrow.
boats, pl. of _bwaato_, e.g. Bazeli babelesya _maato_ nobazela. = Fishermen use boats when fishing. Also _bwato/bbwato_.

dress of hanging strings, e.g. Kaindi basimbi bakalisamide _maaya_. = Long ago girls wore the half-skirt of hanging strings. Bamwi basimbi bakaunkide kuya kusya loozi Iwamubombo Iwakoosa toozi twakubambya _maaya_. = Some girls had gone to dig fibres from the mubombo tree for twisting fibres into strings for making the _maaya_ skirts. _Maaya_ ayo akali kulukwa aloozi Iwamubbuyu, alimwi alwamiyanda yasikalubumbu. Loozi Iwamisamu eyi tiilwakali kutyoka, Iwakali luteteete. Alimwi aya _maaya_ akali kunanikwa mafwuta amukula kutegwa lyoonse kalufwununuka, kalutayumi. = Those _maaya_ skirts were woven from baobab fibres and from the roots of the sikalubumbu. These fibres did not break and they were soft. Again these skirts were smeared with ochre so that they remained soft and fresh and did not dry out. Basimasabe basama _maaya_. = Those who are possessed with masabe spirits wear the _maaya_ skirt. Also _manda_ (sing. _linda_), makusa, ntebwe, mansani, syaacimwanyu.
food, e.g. Bamwi bakaidizya _maawo_ akaambo kakweebelezya Syaanasulwe. = Some people burnt the food because of admiring Syaanasulwe.
leavings of food in pot, or hidden food, e.g. Ijilo kwakacaala _mabaaba_ mucaambikwa. = Yesterday the leavings remained in the pot. Also imbaakwa.
unpredictable or ungovernable utterances, e.g. Bantu nibakanyema, kwaambaula kwakaba _kwamabaaba_. = When people were angry, the talk became unpredictable.
pl. of _ibbaba_, a wing, e.g. Inkwilimba zijisi _mababa_ mayumu kapati. = Pidgeons have very strong wings.
meat remaining in pot for husband, Also makalanongo.
pl. of _ibbala_ (a word or a letter of the alphabeth), e.g. Kamulemba _mabala_ mapati-pati. = Write in capital letters.
spots; small spots = _bubala_; very small spots = _buseese, bunsensele_; spots like a bush-buck's or guinea fowl's. = _bubalabubala, bundondo_; ill-defined, as hyaena's = _zibika_.
stripes, spots, a mixture of colours, e.g. Cibize mmunyama _wamabala-mabala_. = The zebra is an animal with stripes.
sides, pl. of _mbali_, e.g. Bambi bakali kwiiyenda _mumabali_ inzila. = Some were walking on the edges of the path.
pl. of _cibalo_ (a reading lesson/ a chapter of a book), e.g. Ibbuku eli lilijisi _mabalo_ manji. = This book has many chapters.
pl. of _ibbambo_, a rib, e.g. Mubbi bakamutyola _mabambo_ obilo. = They broke two ribs of the thief. Also mitwe, _zibalo_
flats or flood-plain, e.g. Banyama banji bali _mumabanda_. = There are many animals on the flood-plain.
a track where animals pass, e.g. Mu_mabanda_ abanyama muli magatagata. = There are bumps in the track where animals pass.
open space, e.g. Basinombe balayota mulilo _mumabbakasa_. = The herd boys were warming themselves at the fire in the clearing.
chipped wood, used as stoppers for childrens toy-guns, pl. of _ibbala_, e.g. Bana basobana _mabbala_. = Children play with the plugs of their toyguns.
wheel-barrows, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kubelesya mabbala kususya bulongo bwakuyasya damu. = The people of the past were using wheel-barrows to transport clay for building a dam.
carriers, e.g. Bantu bakali kuyandisya kubelekela mumadolopo bakali kubaita kuti mabbala-mpoto. = People who like to work in the towns were called carriers of pots.

court-clerk, e.g. Ndali kuyanda kuula saimoni, pesi ndajana mabbalani tako. I wanted to buy a summons, but I found the court-clerk was not there. Mulimo umwi wakali mumoyo wakwe, mulimo wabumabbalani. = In his heart he desired one job, the work of a court-clerk.
washing-tubs, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Basicikolo basambila mumabbavwa. = The pupils bathe in baths.
velvet beans, e.g. Bantu bakali kucela makoto amabbeenkenene akwaatola kukwaalya. = People were collecting unripe velvet beans and taking them to eat.
loin-cloth, e.g. Wakalisamide mabbensu atukutu twabasaazwe. = He was wearing a loin-cloth made from the skins of a small white animal with a bushy tail.
rags, e.g. Ooyu mwana ngumucaala ncasama mabbesu. = This child is an orphan, that is why it is wearing rags.
the sunset, e.g. Mukaintu wangu wakasika kumabbililo aazuba. = My wife arrived at sunset.
velvet-beans, e.g. Kamulima mabbingabinga kubikka mbolezi mumuunda. Plant the velvet-beans to put humus in the field.
pl. of ibbiza, a horse, e.g. Basikalumamba bakatantide amabbiza. = The soldiers were riding horses.
empty groundnuts, pl. of ibbobo, e.g. Indongwe ezi mmabbobo alo, tazibikkide pe. The groundnuts are just empty shells and have nothing inside. Also mapoopo

badly roasted maize, e.g. Amwi mapopwe akaliyokedwe kabotu-kabotu, pele amwi akabizwide mabbolo-mabbolo akaambo kakuti bakali kubindila kuzya kukukomba kucikolo. = Some cobs of green maize were well roasted, but some were badly done because those who were roasting were hurrying for prayers at school.

pl. of ibboli, a receding eye, or dried mucous from eye, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa mabboli. This child's eyes are filled with mucous. Wakacili kulisyobola mabboli kumeso. He was still wiping the mucous from his eyes. Also mantongwe.
primary rafters tied together before hoisting, pl. of ibbompwa, e.g. Amuboole basa mundigwasye kwaanzika mabbompwa. Come friends and help me to put up the rafters. Also masomo.
castor-oil beans, e.g. Masusu akali kutalikwa kupumbwa, eci cakali kucitwa amafwuta amabbonantelemba. The hair had begun to be plaited, this was done with oil from the castor oil beans. Also mabbono
pl. of ibbono, a castor-oil bean, e.g. Mafwuta amabbono alagwasya kapati. The oil of the castor-oil bean is of a great help.

bundles, heaps, e.g. Wakaliulide mabbudu-mabbudu aa salalula omu mwakali madulesi, malukwe, masyaati a zimwi zisamo zyabapati. He was selling bundles of second-hand clothes in which were dresses, trousers, shirts and other clothes for adults.
pl. ibbumbu, lower part of stomach, e.g. Muntu uciswa mubbumbu tasubi. = A person whose lower abdomen is infected does not pass urine.
bundles, e.g. Bakaleta mabbundu-mabbundu azisani. = They brought bundles of clothes. Also mabbudu
careless talk, e.g. Ndilekelele ndasubuka mabbwaabbwa. = Forgive me, I repent for my careless talk.
bad cooking, pl. of ibbyo, e.g. Nabwiinga wakagunwa naakajika mabbyo. = The newly-married woman was ashamed when she cooked badly. Also mukonde, mubyaanga, mubbyaanga.
castor-oil beans, e.g. Bantu babamba mafwuta amabeempengene. = The people are making oil from castor-oil beans. Also mabbono

a red kind of millet with a short stem, pl. ibele, e.g. Kaindi bakali kulima mabele. = Long ago they used to plant red millet. Mabele akakunuka kale. = The red millet seeds are already out of their shells.
pl. of cibelo, a thigh, e.g. Musimbi oyu ujisi mabelo mapati. = This girl has big thighs.
galvanized iron sheets, e.g. nanda yangu ilazwisya nkaambo mabenkele alidonkookede. = My house is leaking because the galvanized iron sheets have been holed. Also masenke.

pl. of ibbibi, a heap of chopped wood, e.g. Mabibi akakomena nkaambo misamu yakali mipati. = The heaps of chopped wood became large because the trees were big. Mulimi umpa mabibi mumapande. = The farmer is burning the heap of cut wood in the cleared field.
growls, e.g. Mabibo asyuumbwa alayoosya. = The growls of a lion are terrifying. Also mabobelo.
a kind of dance, e.g. Bamwi bantu bazyana cizyano ciitwa kuti mabibo. = Some people dance a dance known as mabibo.
marks, pl. of ibbika, e.g. MuIwazi oyu ujisi mabika amubili. = This sick person has marks on the body. Also malambwa.
velvet-beans, e.g. Bana, amweende mukatebule mabingabinga. = Children, go and harvest the velvet-beans. Also mabbinga-binga.

sour milk, e.g. Bana balayanda mabisi. = Children like sour milk. Nziniini mumabisi ziliibe. = Flies are free to enjoy themselves on the sour milk. (metaphor used if people want to do whatever they want when alone.) Also mandili, malili, malula, cipwaza, when solidified = masase; mixed with fresh milk = bwanda or mwaanda.
something unripe or raw, pl. of libisi e.g. Ukandiletele mango mabisi. (naa makwange). = Bring me unripe mangos.
testicles, pl. of ibobo, e.g. Mucende okwesu acibeleka mabobo nkaambo taakazibwa kabotu. = The testicles of our bull still work because it was not properly castrated. Also macende.
a lily, pl. of ibbolomombo, pl. of cibolomombo, e.g. Mabolomombo ayelezya musena. = Water-lilies beautify the vlei.
the primary rafters Also makazyo
a plant, oil is extracted from the seeds for body use, e.g. Basimbi baunka kukuleta mabona akubambya mafwuta. = The girls have gone to bring an oil plant for making skin-lotion.
spectacles, e.g. Nsekonzyi kubala kuti nsetajisi mabonebone. = I cannot read if I have no spectacles.
pl. of lubu, a reed, e.g. Mumulonga omu muli mabu manji. = There are many reeds in this river.
a wild shrub Also bulanwa
something to be shared, e.g. Maano mmabulanwa. = Wisdom is something to be shared.
pl. of cibumbu, low blackberry bush, e.g. *Mabumbu* abizwa kumwaka. = Blackberries ripen in the dry season (Oct.-Nov.)
pl. of *cibumbu*, a roofless structure, e.g. Basincinko bayaka *zibumbu* zizazangene. = Mad people build rough roofless shelters.
pl. of *ibbumbwa*, a giant, e.g. Ndajana *mabumbwa* obilo alikkede munzila. = I found two giants sitting on the path.
pl. of *bbumbwa-meenzyi* hollows, depressions, a depression in the land which gathers water, e.g. Ndaile kuba *bbumbwa-meenzyi*
anditeen= I just have become like a depression which gathers water because of the troubles which surround me.
rain-drops falling from trees, big heavy scattered rain-drops, e.g. Anditombweeda *mabuula*. = Big heavy raindrops fell on me.
pl. of *libuulule*, shelled maize, e.g. Ukalete mapopwe *mabuulule* kale. = Bring the maize which has been already shelled.
pl. of *ibbuwa*, open country with few trees, a space free of grass, also pl. of *cibuwa*, e.g. Irnombe zilede muma*buwa*. = Cattle are lying in the bare spaces.

pl. of *ibbuyu*, fruit of baobab tree, e.g. *Mabuyu* alanona mumukupa. = Baobab fruit is delicious in milk. Amulyookezye nkamulangile *mabuyu* mumubuyu ulya. = Rest so that I check that baobab tree for fruit for you. *mabbwatu-bbwatu* statements which should not be said publicly, uncontrolled speech, e.g. Chipwetenge naakacili mwana wakali wamabbwatu-bbwatu. = When Chipwetenge was young he was uncontrolled in his speech.
stones, pl. of *ibbwe*, e.g. Basi*bbuku bakajaya mubwa wangu amabwe*. = The headman killed my dog with stones.
machete, e.g. *Macceba* atenda nkomwe zyawo. = Machetes cut their pouches.
a place of refuge, e.g. Muzike wakabona *maccijilo* lyakasika beenzu. = When visitors arrived, a slave found the opportunity to escape to freedom.
a spoilt or selfish character, e.g. Utamupi *macece* mwana oyu. = Do not spoil this child.

grazing lands, e.g. *nombe zyokwesu tazijisi macelelo mabotu*. = Our cattle do not have good grazing land. Moonga wakali kubinga *nombe* kutola *kumacelelo*. = Moonga was driving the cattle to the grazing lands.
placentas, pl. of *ccembele*, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu *ccembele tiilyamaninina kuzwa naamana kutumbuka*. = The placenta did not come out completely when this woman gave birth.
pl. of *mucembele*, a midwife, e.g. Bina Mutinta mbabakali *bacembele* ba Masowe naakatumbuka. = The mother of Mutinta was the midwife for Masowe when she gave birth.
scrotum/testicles, pl. of *iccende*, e.g. Mudaala usilikwa *macende kucibbadela*. = The old man is having his testicles treated at the hospital. Also zisamwa, mabolo.
grazing fields, e.g. Bana, amuzitole *kumacezezyo* mabotu inombe ezyo. = Children take those cattle to good pastures. Also macelelo.

a type of bird, the eagle-owl, pl. *bamaciciti*. e.g. Kuti *maciciti* kalila lyoonse amunzi utondezya malweza. = If an eagle-owl is always crying in the village, it is a sign of an evil omen. Also macincizya.

a stretcher, a portable ham---|--mock, e.g. Muntu walicisa ubwezelwa a- *macila.* = The one who injured himself is carried on a stretcher. Bantu bakajisi mubili wamwami mumacila, bakalyookezya nkaambo kakulampa kwakasinzo. = The people who were carrying the body of the chief on a stretcher rested as it was some distance. ession-dance, e.g. Ingoma zyamadaansi zilalila sunu masiku. = The masabe drums are beating the *madaansi* rhythm tonight.
amusing conversation, e.g. Basimbi bajisi *madaanta* munanda. = The girls had an amusing conversation in the house. Also *madanta*.
rhythm of two or more pounding, e.g. Bamakaintu batwa *macilicili* muncili yomwe. The women are pounding rhythmically in the one mortar. Also majiji, majiiji.

comical conversation, e.g. Kanji-kanji bantu bakali kukkala anga tabali basikulila akaambo kakuti kwakali *madani*, kusabuzyanya akuseka. = Many times people were staying there as if they were not mourners because there was entertaining talk, the mocking of joking relationships and laughter.
the sound of footsteps, e.g. Ndamvwa *macilicili* amunyama, nsetanamubona. = I heard the sound of the feet of an animal, I did not yet see it. Also majiti-jiti
tomatoes, also ludombasi.
a type of bird, the eagle-owl, pl. bamacincizya, e.g. *Macincizya* ulila masiku. The eagle-owl hoots at night. Also maciciti.
pl. of idiba, a fall-trap, e.g. Bakakololo bajaigwa amadiba balafwunzuka. The big rats which are killed in the fall-traps get smashed open.
bicycles, pl. of incinga, e.g. Bantu bazundana kubalika amacinga. = The people are competing in a bicycle race.
stealing as a way of life, e.g. Ulamvwa buyo twana nkotuti kumunene, "Mazuba ano ngamadibba-dibba." You will hear children saying to an old person, "Nowadays one lives by stealing."
ear-ornaments, pl. of icoco/kacoco, e.g. Bamakaintu mbabasama macoco. The women are the ones who wear ear-ornaments.
bronze (brown alloy of copper and tin), pl. of *idibilisi* = a bronze coin, e.g. Kondipa *dibilisi* lomwe. Give me one copper coin.
bruises, e.g. Wakakkala akulibbabbanuna *macuzu-cuzu* mwaakali kubbabbuka kuumwa. He sat down to detach the skin on the bruise that became loose where they were beating him.
pl. of idinga, a fertile piece of land, e.g. Bataata balima *mudinga* libotu. = My father ploughs in a good fertile piece of land.
pl. of ida, womb, stomach, e.g. nombe zilaa *mada* mapati. The cattle have big stomachs.
destructive people, e.g. Imunga amasiku kwiide kwiingaila, *madintyu* aakalipenda kale-kale. At night there are dangerous people wandering about. Also *mantyu*
pl. of idada, a duck, e.g. *Madada* atula mayi mapati-pati. = Ducks lay fairly large eggs.

a hunting-shrine, created by planting a muntiokela stick, which taking root, grows into a tree. On the growing tree are hung objects associated with hunting-traps, weapons, etc. e.g. Kuli zyaanza zinji *amadiose*. There are *madala* pl. of idala, a palm-leaf, e.g. Cisuwo eci cakoombezegwa *amadala* mabotu. This basket was edged with good palm-leaves *madaansi* a type of masabe possmany trophies at the hunting-shrine. Also Iwaanga.

dynamite, an explosion, e.g. _Basinombe bakali kuuma mikkwilo unakuti mmadobbi._ = The cattle-herders were beating their whips as if it was dynamite going off. _Akalizyanya madobbi kujulu, ngunduu-u-u!_ = The thunder clapped above, ngunduu-u-u!
pl. of idola, a mapani bee, e.g. _Tulagusya buci bunji mumadola aya._ = We extract much honey from these mapani bees. Also malola.
sores, e.g. Mukaintu wakafwa wakajisi madonda mubili onse. = The women who died had sores all over the body.
sore throat, e.g. Ooyu mwana tameni kabotu cakulya nkaambo ulaa madunya amoyo. = This child does not swallow well because he has a sore throat. Also mandunya.
luggage, e.g. Tatuyandi kweenzya madukulu abana kusyule. = We do not want to travel about carrying luggage and babies on our backs. Also madubulu
unpleasant relish, e.g. _Cisyu eci mmadulyu, nseyandi kucilya._ = This relish is unpleasant, I don't want to eat it.
the froth of sour and fresh milk mixed, e.g. Ndayanda kulya musozya wamadyobu. = I want to eat musozya with a mixture of sour and fresh milk. Also madyovwu
a dangerous place, e.g. Tacigwasyi kukkala kumafwa nkaambo banji inga bafwa. = It does not help to live in a dangerous place because many people may die.

a child which escapes death which came to the other children of the same mother, e.g. Mwana oyu nguwakacaala alikke lyakamana bakali kufwa mafwaafwa. = This child is the only one who remained when all the others had died.
epilepsy, e.g. Muntu oyu uciswa mafwaafwa. = This person suffers from epilepsy. Also masuntu

distress, pl. of ifwabi, e.g. Mazuba amwi bantu bajisi mafwabi manji. = On some days the people have much distress. Kuyaka amwi nkubotu nkaambo kakuti mafwabi naamusikila mulagwasyanya. = To build near one another is good because when problems come you can help one another. Also mapenzi.
fists, e.g. Kaindi twakali kucikonzya kukona kakwiina akuvwungilana mafwaindi mbuli mazuba ano. = Long ago we were able to inherit without fisticuffs like nowadays.
a sale/auction, e.g. Kuya kuba mafwandisyo azisani ku Chisekesi juunza. = There will be a sale of clothes at Chisekesi tomorrow.
poorly-cooked food, e.g. Mukaintu mubaya ujika mafwasa. = A carelss woman cooks the food poorly. Also mavwunze, masafwa.
akwardness e.g. Ulaa mafwasa. = He is clumsy. Also buyamba
fits, e.g. Bulwazi bwamafwe-mabi bulakatazya kusilika. = The disease of bad fits is difficult to cure.

the marriage-payment installment paid to the relatives of the bride, e.g. Musankwa uyanda kukwata wakapa kale mafwenezya. = A man who intends to marry has already paid the mafwenezya contribution to the relatives of the girl.
protruding bones, e.g. Sikalileke uletelezya mafwenya. = AIDS causes the bones to protrude. Also mafwinya.
small ducks, pl. of ifwililyo, e.g. Idada lyakakonkona mafwililyo manji. = The duck hatched many little ducks.
creases in the skin in fat people, or creases in cloth, e.g. _Cisani catafwunwa ngulube cibaa mafwinya-fwinya._ = The cloth which was chewed by the pig is full of creases. Also makoba

repeated opening and closing of eyes, e.g. _Mafwinya-fwinya amusimbi oyu ngabuvwuule._ = The winking of the eyes of this girl is sexual. (As verb: _Kofwinyafwinya utatoogwi._ = Open and close your eyelids so that the speck does not become an obstacle in your eye.)
rubbish, e.g. Kamubikka _mafwisi-fwisi mumulindi._ = Put the rubbish in the pit. Also mankwisyi, makwisilili, makwisi-kwisi.
a hissing sound, e.g. Kaaze _ujisi mafwooto ayoosya mbeba._ = The cat has a hissing sound that scares the mice.
pl. of ifwufwe, a lung, e.g. _Bulwazi bwakakweekwe bucisya mafwufwe._ = The disease of tuberculosis affects the lungs.
pimples, e.g. Mwaalumi ooyu _ujisi mafwula mapati-pati kumeso._ = This man has big pimples on his face.
coldest period of year with cold breeze, June-July (-fwula = blow), e.g. _Mwezi wa Gandapati a Kkunkumuna-masamu njamafwulampeyo._ = The months of June and July are the coldest months of the year.
orange fruits, pl. of ifwuleenke, e.g. _Musinza wamafwuleenke ulanona._ = Orange-juice is sweet.
gourds, pl. of ifwulu, e.g. _Meenda alatontola kwaanywida mumafwulu._ = Water is cold when you drink it from gourds.
heaps of dung, pl. of bufwumba, e.g. _Mafwumba anombe apa mbolezi._ = Cattle-dung makes the soil fertile.
the early morning, e.g. _Bantu basesa mulandu basika mafwumina._ = The people who demand payments arrive early in the morning.

the grey fruit of the mafwumo tree, pl. of ifwumo. (may come from cifwumofwumo, the morning, as it is collected early in the morning,) e.g. _Musinza wamafwumo ulanonzya ceele._ = The juice of the grey fruit sweetens the porridge.
lines, marks, pl. of mufwundundu, e.g. Bantu beelede kubikka _mafwundundu kutondezya musimpila myuunda yabo._ = People should put indicators to show where their fields terminate.
welts left by whip lashes, e.g. Kwacaala _mafwundundu mubalikumuuma miluso Mainza._ = Welts remained where they were whipping Mainza.
a frown or wrinkles on the forehead, e.g. Kapapa wanyema nca_jisi mafwunya ankumo._ = Kapapa is angry that is why he has wrinkles on his forehead.
pleats in a dress, e.g. Kondisumina _musinsi wamafwunya mapati-pati._ = Sew me a skirt with fairly large pleats. Also minganja, minya
connivance, agreement by a look, e.g. _Mafwunyino amusimbi oyu ngakuzumina._ = The look of the girl conveyed her assent.
carelessness, e.g. Kubeleka _camafwunze ncibi._ = It is bad to work carelessly. Also mafwasa.
the inside of a pumpkin, e.g. Basankwa nobakali kulya myungu, _mafwunzu bakali kupa babwa babo._ = When the boys were eating the pumpkins, they gave the insides to their dogs.

oil, butter, e.g. Insiku ma_fwuta ambonombono akali kunana bana a bavwubi._ Bantu biyo bakali kunana ma_fwuta ansikili, anoongo, ampingili, abweengo, abukowa *amafwuta abanyama*. = Long ago castor-oil was used to anoint the skins of children and the rich. The common people were smearing them-selves with the oils of the *nsikili, noongo, bweengo* and *bukowa* plants and with the fat of animals. Kaindi bakamwale bakali kukkala kabatasambi, alimwi kabanana cisila *(mukula)* *amafwuta* mazenge amumpawo. = Long ago the initiates stayed without washing while smearing themselves with ochre and oil from milk butter. Masusu akali kutalikwa kupum-bwa. Eeci cakali kucitwa a *mafwuta* amabbona-ntelemba, naaba anyemu, an-tela inyungu zyamapusi. = The hair was coiled. This was done with oil from the castor-oil bean, or from groundnuts and from pumpkin seeds. Muli ziyuni zifwa *amafwuta*. = You are birds who die with plenty of fat. (said of those who die while still young and prosperous)
the back areas of the house, pl. of *ifwutila*, e.g. Mukaintu wa-sowa ukkala *kufwutila* lyananda. = A woman who had a miscarriage sits at the back of the house. Also makkuti, pl. of kkuti.

grass-huts, e.g. Bukoko bwamantoombwa bwakali kukondwedwa kumunzi akaambo kakuti *mafwutu* ayo taakali *mafwutu* mayumu akonzya ku-sinkila zintu zimwi zyakali kunga zila-konzya kunyonyoona bukoko. The mantoombwa beer was brewed at the village because those grass-huts were not strong ones which could block some things which could destroy the beer.
pl. of *ifwuuntwa*, a type of fruit, e.g. Bana banji bayanda kulya *mafwuuntwa*. Many children like to eat *mafwuuntwa* fruit. Also mafwumo.
beers, e.g. *Magaankata* bakali kwaindilizya kwaanywa. They were drinking beers to excess.
feathers worn at a funeral feast, e.g. Bamacembele bakalisamide *magaga* nibakali kuzemba kudilwe. = The old women were dressed in feathers when they were ritually walking to and fro at the funeral.
a bunch of feathers made into a head ornament for funeral feasts, e.g. Aya *magala-gala* ngakuya kusama kudilwe. This bunch of feathers are for wearing at a funeral. Also injakalale.
gloves, e.g. Wasama *maga-nza* asiya. = He wore black gloves.
any bumpy surface, e.g. Incinga yangu yafwa *mumagatagata*. = My bicycle got broken on the corr-ugations.
valleys, e.g. Basinombe ma-tanga ajombe baayumbila *mumagezi* kukucela. The cattle-herders take the herds to the valleys to graze.
glasses (ety. Eng.) pl. of *igilazi*, e.g. Babbi bakajaya *magilazi* a-nanda. The thieves broke the window-panes of the house.
guitars (ety. English), pl. of *igitaali*, e.g. Bantu bakazyana *magitaali* busiku boonse. The people danced to guitar-music through the night.
a collection of big trees, e.g. Basankwa beembela nombe *mumagoba*. = The boys are herding the cattle among the big trees. Also mafwinyafwinya.
protruding loose claws at back of hind leg in dogs, e.g. Mubwa wakatyoka *magobanyama* naakali ku-tanda sulwe. The dog broke the hind leg-claw when it was chasing a rabbit.
an edge, termination, e.g. *Magolelo* abuumi buno ndufwu. = The end of this life is death.
caves, e.g. Ngooyu lino wanjila *magolo-golo* amilundu mumabwe. = Here he is now entering the caves of mountains among the rocks.
edible white tubers, pl. of
or cigilokoko (a lily) e.g. Magolokoko asilika malwazi manji. = Edible white tubers cure many diseases.
clods of earth, pl. igomwe, e.g. Magomwe abulongo alaumputika kwiinda magomwe abufwumba bwakaindi. = Clods of earth can be more easily broken up than clods of old manure.
thick forests, e.g. Wakagama nzila yamagonde-magonde. = We took the path through thick forests.
the knees, pl. of igondo, e.g. Mutinta wakatyompwa, wamvwa mumagondo sikoo. = Mutinta was disappointed, she felt her knees go cold.
an edible root found in vleis, e.g. Beembela balalya magonte musyokwe. = The shepherds are eating the magonte root in the bush.
big metal anklets, sing. igoto, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kusama magoto amundalila mutungo. = People of long ago used to wear big metal rings on their ankles.
lumps, e.g. Insima eyi njamagoto. = This nsima has lumps. Also makoto.
pl. of igoya, body hair. e.g. Magoya amubwa oyu mmalamfu. = The hair of this dog is long.
hairy, e.g. Mubili wakwe woonse wakali wamagoyooya. = His whole body was hairy.
pl. of igovwu, froth, e.g. Insipa eyi ilijisi magovwu manji. = This soap has plenty of froth.
bumps at back of head, rolls of flesh between neck and head of a fat person, e.g. Kulya kabotu cipa kubaa magudu. = Eating luxuriously give one rolls of fat at the back of one's neck.
pl. of igukusu, a cockroach, e.g. Munanda ya Jolezya kuli magukusu manji. = In Jolezya's house there are many cockroaches.
pl. of *iguka*, an insect, e.g. *Mumuunda kuli maguka alya minsonje.* = There are insects in the field which eat the shoots.
pl. of *iguku*, a fat chicken, e.g. *Mutinta ujisi maguku mapati-pati.* = Mutinta has fine big chickens.
pl. of *igulu*, a big ant hill, e.g. *Ndajana basyaambololo banji mumagulu.* = I have found many kudus among the big ant-hills.
pl. of *igulu*, a huge leg, e.g. Haamakumo wakajisi gulu lipati akaambo kabulwazi. = Haamakumo had a huge swoIlen leg because of the sickness.
objects which protrude, e.g. *Bulo bulaa magunya-gunya.* = The bed is uncomfortable.
goods-trains, pl. of *cigusu*, e.g. *Tiitwakaningaakucitanta citima, aalo magusu ngutwakali kubona.* = We had not yet boarded a passenger-train, it was only goods-trains that we had seen.
pl. of *igute*, a big boil, e.g. *Magute amwana taanabomba.* = The boils of the child have not yet softened. Also *zyuute*, sing. *cuute*.

pl. of *igwa*, piece pf bark, e.g. *Muumba ujisi magwa mapati.* = The muumba tree has thick bark. Also *ikwa*, pl. *makwa*, (e.g. *Makwa akayuma alasikkwa.* = Barks which are dry are used for firewood.)
loud uncontrolled laughter, e.g. *Bakatalika kupiluka kumunzi kumwi bayaakuseka magwagwaagwa.* = They began to return to the vilage while laughing uncontrolably. Also *magwegweegwe*
letters, pl. of *lugwalo*, e.g. *Basicikolo balalembelana magwalo.* = The pupils are writing letters to one another.
the rough parts of skin, e.g. *Musimbi ujisi magwala-ngubo, tasambi.* = The girl who has rough patches of skin, does not wash.
pl. of igwanda, a bundle of assorted things, e.g. Mucintoolo omu kuli magwanda. In the store there is an assortment of many things. Also mangwanda
an empty honey-comb, e.g. Inzuki zyakaunka, zyakasiya magwanda alo. = The bees went off, they only left the empty comb behind. Also mape.

whole-grain cooked maize, e.g. *Magwaza* alanona kuti komvwide nzala. Whole maize-grain when cooked is delicious to eat when you are hungry. Moyo wakwe mukati wakali kubila cabukali mbuli mpoto yamaqwaza. = His heart inside was boiling with anger like a pot of cooking maize-grains. Also mangamwe
things for sale, e.g. Mumadolopo magwebo ayenda kabotu. = In the towns business goes well. Also makwebo.

maize-leaves, e.g. Inombe zilya magweelele muciba. = Cattle are eating maize-leaves in the kraal. Also makweelele. magwegweegwe careless laughing (can connote impropriety), e.g. Basimbi balaseka magwegweegwe. = The girls are laughing in an undignified manner.
be unsteady, e.g. Kaindi bamacembele bakanyina magwenugwenu. = Long ago the old women were steadfast.
potatoes, pl. of igwili, e.g. Bamakuwa balaayanda kapati magwili. = White people like eating potatoes very much.
wild fruit, e.g. Nobakasika mumuunda, bakajana mulwi wamagwilinti ulilundene kale. = When they reached the filed they found a pile of wild fruit already heaped.
a cereal (generic), a slow-growing sorgum (5 months), e.g. Maila alamuka kubizwa. Sorghum is slow in growing.
quick-growing white sorgum (3 months), e.g. *Maila-muceme* alafwambaana kubizwa. White sorgum is quick in growing.
refusal to accept advice, e.g. Aaya mailiili eenu ngaamumana. = Your refusal to accept advice has finished you.
claws, e.g. Bakombwe bajisi maimba malamfwu. = Cocks have big claws. Also mayimba
furrows, wrinkles, e.g. Ankumo maimba aangana. On the forehead furrows were knitted. Also mayimba

a cord worn by girls in the past. It was put over the left shoulder and under the right armpit. e.g. Kaindi musimbi wakali kusamikwa maingankwa. = Long ago a girl was made to wear a cord. Nkujana kumweelede maingankwa, kutitima boya mumikono yakwe nabuntu. = You find that the cord suits her, the hair that grows on her arms adds to her beauty.

what delights the heart, e.g. Aayo makani mmainu ncobeni, ndakkomana kwaateelela. That report is indeed sweet. I am glad to hear it. Chitonga mwaambo ujisi majwi, mainu, ayo ateelede kuloba. = The language of Chitonga has words and a sweetness, those things should not disappear.
the rainy season, e.g. Izisyu zitete nzinji kapati mainza. = There are plenty of fresh vegetables during the rainy season.

levers, lifters, e.g. Magwaza mmajamuna-mpemo nkaambo naatafwunwa aputausya mpemo. = Whole cooked-grains when being chewed move the nose up and down (ie. they are hard to chew) because when they are chewed they move the nose. Also manyamuna
half-ground maize grains, e.g. Busu obu mbwamajandaulwa. = This flour is not fully ground. Also maando.
hands, pl. of ijanze, e.g. Basankwa bajisi mikkwilo mumajanze. = The boys have cattle-whips in their hands. Also maanza, pl. of janza.
a respect for other people's rights, e.g. Ncibotu kubaa majeezya mumaumi abantu. = It is good to have respect for the lives of people.
lots of honey, pl. of buci, e.g. Ku Bulubale kuli maji manji nkaambo nzuki ziteegwa buya. = In Luvale territory there is much honey because the bees are just trapped. Also maci
eggs, pl. of iji, e.g. Kamupa maji kubana kutegwa bakomene kabotu. = Give the children eggs so that they grow well.
the rhythm of three or four pounding together, e.g. Basimbi batwa majiji. The girls are pounding a compounded rhythm. Also macilicili, majijiiji, magaga.
pounding of three or four in one mortar, e.g. Bakaintu batwa majijiiji. = The women are pounding a compounded rhythm. Also majiji.
any food connected with masabe possession, e.g. Nyama yamasabe acakulya coonse citegwa majiko. = The masabe meat and all food (connected with masabe) is called majiko.
a mirage, illusion, e.g. Naakali kweenda mucimpayuma mazuba manji, wakabona majilikitwa. = When he had been walking in the desert for many days, he saw a mirage.
protruding teeth, pl. injilikitwa e.g. Menyo amajilikitwa abisya mukanwa. = Protruding teeth disfigure the mouth.
footsteps, e.g. Wakamvwa majindiindi anze. = He heard footsteps outside.
clouds, e.g. Buno buzuba kunyina majobo manji mujulu. Today there are not many clouds in the sky. Also mayoba.
yokes, pl. of ijoko, e.g. Ndaula majoko otatwe kwa Haakacoma. = I bought three yokes at Haakacoma's.
boots, pl. of ijombo, e.g. Basinombe baleelede kusama majombo musyokwe. Cattle-herders ought to wear boots in the bush.
millipedes, e.g. Bantu bakaide kugogomana unakuti majongolwa akumalende. = The people began to bow their heads like millipedes at the rainshrine.
a field of stalks after harvest, e.g. Kozitola mumajuti nombe zikacele. = Take the cattle to the empty stalks so that they feed.
words, pl. of ijwi, e.g. Sena ucijisi majwi akundaambila? = Do you still have something to tell me.
pl. of bukaano, a ceremonial axe, e.g. Balombe bakalibambila makaano akusama amakuko. The boys made themselves ceremonial-axes to carry on their shoulders.

pl. of ikaba, liquid fat, e.g. Makaba amafwuta akavwuzya mabbodela obilo. The melted fat filled two bottles. Makaba amafwuta angulube = lard (i.e. fat from abdomen of pig, rendered and clarified for use in cooking.)
drinking anything that you come across, drinking like a dog, e.g. Ncibi kubaa makaba-kaba, inga koya kukaba cikola. It is bad to drink carelessly, you might drink poison.
amphibians, water-creatures, e.g. Imvwula ilawa, maande a makaci alalila mumaziba. = The rain falls and frogs and other amphibians make noise in the ponds.
rough surface on the body, excrescences, scales, e.g. Mwana ulaa makakala mumaanza. = The child's hands are rough-skinned. Also maamba.
pl. of inkakata, diviningobjects, dice, e.g. Munanga ubelesya makakata, taboni. = The witchdoctor who is using divining-objects does not see the real cause of the problem.
footprints, e.g. Babwa batobela makakata abanyama. = The dogs follow the imprints of the animals.
pl. of inkakilo, an objection, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa makakilo akutumwa ncalengaula kwaamba. = This child has irrelevant reasons for refusing to be sent that is why he is always making excuses.
pl. of ikala, hot coal, e.g. Kamubikka makala manji munsimbi tuccise zisani. = Put many embers in the iron so that we iron the clothes.
pl. of cikala, a waterhole, a well, e.g. Bamakaintu bateka meenda mumakala. = The women are drawing water from the wells.
meat remaining in the pot for husband, e.g. Mukaintu mubotu usiila mulumaakwe makala-nongo. = A good wife leaves some meat remaining in the pot for her husband. Also mababa
passenger-train, ety. Eng. carriages, e.g. Kamubweza zibbutu, wasika makalajisi. Take your luggage the passenger-train has arrived.

cassava/manioc, e.g. Bamalozi balya nsima yamakamba. = The Balozi people eat nsima from cassava. makambo-kambo dewlap (fold of loose skin hanging from throat of cattle) e.g. Musune okwesu ngwamakambokambo. = Our ox has a dewlap. Also malembo-lembo, malembwelembwe.

place for milking, e.g. Cibisilo cikkala kumakamino. = The milk container is kept at the place for milking makamu a crowd, pl. of inkamu (a group), e.g. Kwakasika makamu manji. = Many groups arrived. makamu-makamu different groups, e.g. Makamu-makamu abantu akali koompana. Various groups of people were crowding together.

pl. of cikanci, a medicinal root, root for bathing wounds, a pad of hay or straw applied to wound, a poultice, e.g. Kamukanda makanci amusamu acilonda camwana. Apply the poultice to the wound of the child.

food or pith spat out after chewing, e.g. Lubuwa luzwide makanci aminsale. = The courtyard is full of the remains of sugar-cane which had been chewed and spat out. Bantu nibakali kulya minsale bakali kuwaala makanci mucingungulu. = When the people were eating sugar-cane, they threw the pith in the dustbin. Also mankansyi
skin, bark, e.g. Cilonda ciyanda kuyumya cikwakwamuka makanda. The wound that is about to heal casts off the skin. Wakali kusama makanda. = He was wearing skins.
what is worn out, e.g. Iswe aba kale makandaa nyemu. As for ourselves we are already worn out like the shells of groundnuts. Mulumbe oyu wakamumana makanda. This news made him weak. Also makwa.
the health of a person, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa makanda mabotu/mabi. = This child had good/bad health.
skins used as clothes, e.g. Wakali kusama makandakanda kumaboko. He was wearing animal skins on his arms.
sayings, conversation, news, affairs, e.g. Utasiki munsi, tujisi makani amaseseke. Do not come near, we are having a private conversation. (mwanamakani = a friend)
pl. of ikankala, protruding kulya nkuku. = Jackal-buzzards like eating front teeth, e.g. Oyu musankwa ulaa chickens. makankala amenyo. = This boy has protruding teeth.

a type of grass like finger-millet which between the places where we live. grows in tufts, e.g. Inombe zilayanda kucela makata. Cattle like to graze on makkasi pl. of ikkasi, a playing-card, (this type of) grass. Also lukata. e.g. Bantu basobana makkasi balayanda

Make planks for crossing the Bakubusi bakaindi bakali kuyanda kuAlso mabompwa. zyana makkwaya munkolola. = Young river. people like to dance the makkwaya dance
refusals, e.g. Aayo mmakazyo ankazi. at the female initiation ceremony. = These are the refusals of stubbourness.
creases or dimples in the makkishi type of Luvale dance, Luvale skin Also mafwinya-fwinya.

column1: traditional ritual masked figures, eg Ba
column2: the bank of a river, e.g. Mulonga wataLubale mbabazyana cizyano camakkishi. kazyolwa wakabula makoba. (a proverb) = It is the Luvale people who dance the = A river which does not meander has no dance of makkishi. banks.

the jackal-buzzard, pl. ba- Makobbokobbo name given to the makkalila, e.g. Makkalila wanditolela nkuku mpati. A jackal-buzzard has taken my big chicken. Bamakkalila balayanda Indebele invaders, e.g. Oyu musankwa wakali sikutija Makobbokobbo. = *This man was fleeing from the Matebele.*

delaying tactics in marriage arrangements, e.g. Nkaambo *kamakobekobe* basankwa banji cibapa kuti bacince mizeezo yakukwata. = *Many boys change their minds about getting married because of the delaying tactics in marriage arrangements.*

hanging ear bead-ornaments, pl. of ikobekobe, e.g. Basimbi bakali kusama *makobekobe*. = *The girls were wearing ear-rings. (ear-rings of wound copper and iron wire = tukakao or cikobwela)* Also bucaca, mankwita-nkwita, macoco, bulumba-lumba.
clothes, pl. of ikobelo, e.g. Muntu mucete tajisi *makobela* manji. = *A poor person hasn't many clothes.*
Also buboli
a type of bird, e.g. Kumazuba basimpongo balaya kukuteya *makoce*. = *In the evening the herds go off to trap birds.*
verandahs, pl. ikkoce, e.g. Bamadaala balikkede mumakoce amaanda. = *The old men are seated in the varandahs of the houses.*
clothes hanging loosely, e.g. Bapaizi basama *makobo* mu Misa. = *Priests wear loose-hanging garments at Mass.*
eyes in deep cavities (con- genital), e.g. Basokwe bajisi *makobwa mapati*. = *Monkeys have eyes in large receding cavities.* Also makobbe.
crops growing from the previous year's residue, e.g. Ndongwe *zyamakoko* zilataanguna kubizwa. = *Groundnuts which grow from last year's crop are first to ripen.*
pl. of bukoko (beer), e.g. Bana basunu balabinda kutalika kunywa *makoko*. = *The present generation hurry to begin* drinking beers.
a weed, flower of which is sucked by children for sugar, e.g. Bakubusi balayanda kusyuunta *mako- komwamomba*. = *Young people like to suck the makokomwamomba flower.* Also bukoko bwamoomba
traps, e.g Wakateya *makole* abasyaambololo abanyama bamwi. = *He set traps for kudus and other animals.*

a simple form of xylo- phone, which used to be used by Valley Tonga herdboys, e.g. Mooye usobana *makolekole* munanda. = *The girl being initiated plays a simple xylophone in the house of initiation.*
big male baboons, pl. of likolo, e.g. Masokwe *makolo* aleenda alikke-alikke. = *The big male baboons move about on their own.*
a boar, e.g. Menyo *amakolo* alabosya kapati. = *The teeth of a boar are very sharp.*
big breasts, pl. of lukolo, e.g. Musimbi oyu ujisi *makolo mapati*. = *This girl has large breasts.*
