a place for hanging things, e.g. Inyama ilaanzikidwe *amakolo*. = *The meat is hanging up at the hanging place.*
eyes under protruding fore- head, e.g. Sokwe ulaa *makolya mapati*. = *A monkey has sunken eyes under a protruding forehead.* Also mankolyo
a greedy person in eating relish, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngu *mako- mbola*. = *This person is greedy in eating relish.* Also mulyato.
a gloomy face, e.g. Muntu *wamako- mbola* mmukali ciindi coonse. = *The person with a gloomy face is ever angry.*

spots on the head of cattle, e.g. Inombe yokwesu njamakombola. = *Our cow has a spotted head. Kwakali kunga kwaba buyo kumazuba kwiinda nombe yamakombola lyoonse mulubuwa Iwacikolo. = It happened that every evening a cow with a spotted head passed through the school courtyard.
light red-haired cattle = *nombe yamakombola*
brownish-white cakes (made of grass and soil) of the *tukonga* termites, e.g. *Cuulu camakonga ncibi kubambya zitina.* = The mound used by the *tukonga* termites is bad for making bricks.
ankle to knee or wrist to elbow, e.g. *Masambo mumakono-kono akavwulisya.* = The grass-bracelets were many from ankle to knee.
oaths, e.g. *Mutinta wakalilumbila amakonsyo mapati naakali kwaamba kaambo aka.* = Mutinta swore with mighty oaths when he was relating the affair.

beaten bark used for storage container, a drum of bark used as a bin /bag/vessel, pl. of *cikooko, ikkooko*, e.g. *Bamacembele balayobola mbuto zyabo mumakooko.* = The old women keep their seeds in drums of bark.
the nape of the neck, e.g. *Muntu taliboni kumakosi pe.* = A person cannot see the back of his/her (own) neck at all.
bring shame to a person, e.g. Makani aya akamulemya *kumakosi* Mutinta. = This affair brought shame to Muntinta.
(idiomatic) Kanji-kanji bantu batulanga *kumakosi.* Very often people look at the back of our necks. (they mock us as we walk away)
Kwabija ace *kumakosi* nkwetakonzyi kulibona. = It is bad that I cannot see the future.
the time when sorgum ripens, e.g. *Buyuni bulaneneya kumakosokelo amaila.* = Birds fatten during the period when the sorgum ripens.
pl. of *ikkoto/cikoto*, a lump, knot, hard swelling, navel-hernia, e.g. *Insima yatakopwa kabotu ilaa makoto.* = Insima which is not stirred well has lumps.
hard unripe fruit, e.g. Mutani kulyi mango acili *makoto.* Do not eat mangoes which are still unripe.
pl. of *ikkowa*, a cucumber, e.g. *Amwi makowa alalula, amwi alatontola.* Some cucumbers are bitter, some are alright.
a fruit with thorns, e.g. *Bakamujikila kasima kacisyu camakowambala.* They cooked him a little nsima with the relish of a vegetable. Also *makwaambala*
sorgum, maize stalks, e.g. *Makuba amapopwe ngaasaninwa nombe.* = The stalks of maize are for feeding cattle.
ear-plugs, e.g. *Makuba amumatwi alamweelela musimbi ulya.* = The ear-plugs suit that girl.

pl. of *ikubi*, a vulture, e.g. *Makubi alya mutunta wamunyama.* = The vultures are eating the carcass of an animal. *Juunza cifwumofwumo nzyoobatola musaka nkabasiye bakasweeke akuligwa basuntwe amakubi.* = Tomorrow morning I will take them into the bush and leave them so that they be lost and be eaten by hyenas and vultures.
waves in the lake, e.g. *Bwato bwakabbindamunwa amakubi alaa nguzu.* = The boat was overturned by powerful waves. Also *mayuwe*
shoulder-blades, pl. of *ikuko*, e.g. *Balombe bakali kulibambila makaano akusama amakuko.* The boys were making ceremonial-axes for themselves to carry over their shoulders.
dry shelled-maize, e.g. *Kabbule kazwide makukulule amapopwe.* = The grain-bin is full of dry shelledmaize. Also *mabuulule, muwa*
roots, e.g. *Makuli amusamu oyu* alaligwa. = The roots of this tree are edible. Also miyanda
pl. of ikkumbi, a cloud, e.g. Sunu ijulu lizwide makumbi. = Today the sky is full of clouds.
brown edible fruit with hard shell, when unripe green, size of small orange, when dried used as leg-rattles, e.g. *Makumbuzu alanona kulya.* = Makumbuzu fruit are sweet to eat. Also masebelele
pl. of ikkumi, ten, e.g. Kwakasika bantu bali *makumi* otatwe ku-muswaangano. = Thirty people had arrived at the meeting.
tuskless elephants, pl. of ikumpu, mukumpu e.g. Kwakainda muzowu *mukumpu* kunze ananda yangu. = A tuskless elephant passed behind my house.
large pieces of firewood, e.g. Adilwe kwakali *makuni* manji. = There were large pieces of firewood at the funeral.
pl. of cikunka/likunka, an ear of sorghum after it has been beaten, e.g. Kamuya mukagonke *makunka* amaila. = Go and cut the ears of sorgum.
(Valley Tonga) a type of masabe dance which is mixed with the beat of the buntibe drum from various villages.

antagonism, enmity, e.g. Chibbwalu a Chitebente *makupa* abo kunyina naakamana kusikila kubucembele bwabo. = The antagonism between Chibbwalu and Chitebente continued up to their old age. *Makupa* aya akaindilila wakaba munyono. = The disagreement developed to become envy.

pl. of *ikusa*, sisal, a fibre of aloes, (which has erect spikes of flowers and leaves yielding bitter juice and can be used as a purgative,) e.g. Kamuya mukalete *makusa* tukunte bukusa bwakuteezya nziba. = Go and bring fibres so that we make cords for trapping pidgeons.
strings of beads, e.g. Kwa Mukanzubo balayanda *makusa* amalungu akubambya milemba. = At Mukanzubo they want strings of beads for making face veils.
pl. of *ikkuti*, a field of potatoe rows, e.g. Baama babamba *makuti* aku-simpa cimbwali. = My mother has made rows for planting sweet-potatoes. Also mabundu
rows of plaited-hair, e.g. Basimbi basunu babamba *makuti* amasusu. = The girls of today make rows of plaited-hair.
pl. of *mukuwa*, a white person, e.g. Bamakuwa bakasika kaindi. = The white people arrived long ago.

tree or rubbish drifting with the current, e.g. Bana tabeelede kusobanina mumulonga mainza inga batolwa *makuwe*. = Children ought not to play in the river during the rainy season as they might be taken away by the floating rubbish. Also malabisi, mankuce, mankufwi -nkufwi, masifwi-sifwi.
pl. of *mukuyu*, a fig tree, e.g. Kujanika bayuni banji *mumakuyu*. = Many birds are found in fig trees. ikkuyu = a very big *mukuyu* tree.
pl. of *ikkwa*, piece of bark, e.g. Bana baciswa cifwumu bakwaminwa *makwa* amululwe. = They remove the bark of the *mululwe* tree to treat children who suffer from measles

prepuce, rind of soft fruit, shell of egg, monkey-nut, scab over sore, *makwa* anzoka = slough of a snake, e.g. Inzoka yaanywa maji, yasiya *makwa* alo. = The snake has sucked the eggs, it has only left the shells.
scratches, e.g. Kaluwe kamuluma, kamusiila *makwambe* mubili onse. = The leopard attacked him leaving scratches all over his body. Also mivwalu
beaded waist-cords, e.g. Basimbi bakalisamide *makwambe*. = The girls wore beaded waist-cords.
pl. of *ikkwati*, a metal box with lid nailed, two metal lids forming a round box, e.g. *Mudaala uyobola mali akwe mukkwati*. = The old man keeps his money in a metal box.
dry unbaked leaves of tobacco, e.g. *Makwaya alicipide kwiinda misanga*. = Unbaked tobacco-leaves are cheaper than cigarettes

portions of work to be done before payment is made. e.g. Babelesi bakavwola mali manji nkaambo bakamaninzya *makwaza* manji. = The workers earned much money because they finished many portions of work. Also mugwazo, zikwaankwani.
type of womens ornaments, e.g. Basimbi bakalongela *makwaza*. = The girls packed the ornaments.

trade, business, e.g. Kuli *makwebo* asiyene-siyene mumadolopo. = There are different businesses in the town. = *Mumakwebo* angu kunyina mpindu mpati njejana. = I find no great profit from my business.
leaves of any cereal, e.g. Kamubikka *makweelele* amapopwe muciba. = Put the maize-leaves in the kraal.
places or stones for sharpening, pl. of cikwengelo or ikkwengelo = a whetstone or grindstone, e.g. Bantu bakwenga tweembe twabo ama*kwengelo*. = People sharpen their axes on whetstones.

pl. of *ikkwibba*, a long bark fibre, e.g. *Makwibba* aloozi avwumbya maanda. = The long fibre barks are used for thatching houses. Bana bacete basama *makwibba* aloozi. = Poor childen wear bark fibre.
pl. of *ikkwibba*, a sling, e.g. David wakajaya Goliyati *akkwibba*. = David killed Goliath with a sling. Also *makwiso*.
pl. of *ikwiso/ikwisyo*, a sling, e.g. Ncibi kuwaalana mabwe *amakwiso* inga mwacisana. = It is bad to throw stones at one another with a sling, perhaps you might hurt one another. Also *makwibba*.
dry grass put on a fire of cattle-dung to make it blaze, e.g. Mulilo *wamakwisi-kwisi* tauzimi kufwambaana. = A fire of grass and dung does not go out quickly.
rubbish, sweepings, e.g. Kamubikka tombe ndyomukukula mumulindi wa*makwisi-kwisi*. = Put the dirt which you are sweeping in the rubbish pit. Also mankwisyi-nkwisyi, *makwisilili*.
sweepings, groundnutleaves. e.g. Amuumpe *makwisilili* andongwe kutegwa kusalale mulubuwa. = Burn the groundnut-leaves so that the place is clean. Also mankwisyi-nkwisyi.
entrails (of several people or animals) pl. of bula, pl. of ida, e.g. Bantu balayanda *mala* arjombe nkaambo alafwambaana kubizwa. = People like the entrails of cows because they are quickly cooked.
pregnancies, e.g. Mucembele ulayanda banakazi balaa bana batete abanakazi balaa *mala*. = The old woman likes women with tender young children and women with pregnancies. Also mada.
barbs, e.g. Luwaile *Iwamala* lulayasa. = Barbed wire cuts.
unfermented beer without sugar, e.g. Bamakaintu banji bayanda cibwantu*mala*. = Many women like unfermented beer without sugar. Also cinamala.
pl. of *Iwala*, finger or toe-nail, e.g. Ndalipwaya nsando *alwala*. = I smashed myself on the nail with a hammer.
the area below the navel, e.g. Mulwazi ujisi cilonda *amalaangilo*. = The patient has a wound below the navel.

nonsense, loss of senses, e.g. *Webo kozwa awa, ulaa malabali.* = Go away, you are full of nonsense. Akaambo kakulila lyoonse basimunzinyina bakamwaambila kuti ujisi *malabali.* = Because of her continuous crying her co-villagers said she had lost her senses.
temporary camp of official, e.g. *Basikalumamba bakayaka malabba mumulundu.* = The soldiers have built a camp on the hill
rubbers (ety. Eng.), e.g. Ku Monze nkokuulwa *malabba ancinga.* = It is at Monze where rubbers for a bicycle are bought.
pl. of *cilabba/ ilabba* = a rough grasshut, e.g. Basicikombelo bali ku*malabba.* = The church goers are at the temporary grass-huts.
rags, e.g. Basincinko tabakombeleli kusama *malabulaba.* = Mad people do not mind wearing rags. Also *milapi, mazaapila*
careless talk, e.g. *Malabulabu taayandiki, inga koya kulitaya.* = Careless talk is not wanted, you might say something which can put you into trouble. Also *malabbulabbu, mabbwaabbwa*
instructions, e.g. *Komupa malailile mabotu mwana, atakasoweki.* = Give the child good instructions, so that she is not lost.
gills, e.g. *Inswi ijisi malakavwiya.* A fish has gills. Also *malaka-vwuya.*
tonsils, pl. of *ilakabiya,* e.g. *Malakabiya kumwana muniini apa kuti akabe abbozu kumbele amazuba.* = Tonsils in a little child can cause it to have a problem with the thyroid gland later.
gills of fish, e.g. *Inswi ziyoyela mumalakabiya.* Fish breathe through the gills. Also *malaka-vwiya*
palm-leaves, pl. of *ilala,* e.g. *Zisuwo zilusigwa amalala.* = Baskets are weaved with palm-leaves. Big palm leaves = *mangwabale or mangwalala*

fibrous flesh of fruit eaten in June. Fronds used on basket construction with frond-fibre used as twine, also a salt source through ash-filtration. e.g. *Bensiku bakali kubamba munyo wamalala.* = The ancestors were making salt from palm leaves.

a place to sleep, e.g. Wakalibindide mulombwana cakuti nikwakamusiila munzila tanaakayanda kulomba *malalo.* The man was rushing so that when it became dark on the way he did not wish to ask for a place to sleep.
a cheetah, pl. *bamalama,* e.g. *Ngumalama.* It is a cheetah. e.g. *Malama mmunyama mukali kapati.* = The cheetah is a fierce animal. Also *masekese, inemba, simabala, itwaluwe.*
little pits, as for maize planted out of season, e.g. *Kumwaka tulasyanga mapopwe mumalambo.* = We plant maize in the dry season in little pits.
seed sown in dry ground, *ilambo,* e.g. *Mapopwe amumalambo alafwambaana kubizwa.* Maize seed sown in dry ground is quick to ripen.
coloured mark, e.g. *Inombe yabataata ilaa cilambo cilizyibya.* My father's cow has a coloured mark by which it is known.
January, e.g. *Mumwezi wa Malambwa kuli miyoba minji.* In the month of January there are many cloudcovered skies.
places with plenty of water, e.g. *Bacula balalila mumalambwa.* = Frogs croak in watery places.
spots of leprosy, pl. of *idambwa,* e.g. *Muntu uciswa cinsenda ulaa malambwa mubili oonse.* A person suffering from leprosy has spots over the whole body. Also *mabala.*

fictitious stories, e.g. *Bana* bakasıwiılızya hvaario, tulabi, malamina amasendelezya kumwaka, masiku acikko camulila = Children were listening to stories, riddles, fictitious tales and hidden indirect talk during the dry season, at nightime at the fireplace.
pl. of *idanda*, a fibre cloth used in the past, e.g. Booye bakaindi bakali kusama ***malanda*** mumaulu. = Long ago the female initiates wore fibre leggings.
sunflower, e.g. Kono ***malangazuba*** taakakomena kabotu. = This year the sunflower did not grow well.
palate, e.g. Masuku alatumpya ***malangilo***. = Masuku fruit blisters the roof of the mouth. Also cilakula.
expectation, e.g. Cino ciindi ncamalangilo amvwula inji. = This is the time when there is expectation of much rain.
coal/charcoal, e.g. Malasa manji azyila ku Maamba. = Much coal comes from Maamba.
fun in conversation, e.g. Akaambo kamalasila akwe bantu tiibakamuteelela ncaakali kwaamba. = Because of his jocular way of talking the people did not take him seriously.
portents, e.g. *Malayila*
taaluu= The amazing wonders of God can never be told. Also malayilile

wonders, miracles, e.g. *Jesu* wakacita ***maleele*** manji. = Jesus worked many miracles. Muntu usondokede wakacita ***maleele***. = The mad person did astounding things. Yakatalika kuwa mvwula ***yamaleele***. = The rain started to fall in an extraordinary way.
the trigger of a gun, e.g. Muvwimi wakadubula ntobolo naakajata ***malebwido***. = The hunter fired the gun when he caught the trigger.
a catapult, e.g. Basankwa balajaya tuyuni ***amalekani***. = The boys kılled little birds with catapults.
dry seeds of pumpkin, e.g. Baama bakanga _malekete_ mulukaye. = Mother is frying dry pumpkin-seeds in a potsherd. Also nyungu
a ladder, e.g. Kamubelesya _malele_ kutanta musamu. = Use the ladder to climb the tree.
clothes hanging loose, e.g. Musimbi usama _malelela_ ujisi bulemu. = A girl who wears loose hanging clothes shows respect.
administration, governance, e.g. Tujisi _malelo_ mabotu aluumuno mu Zambia. = We have peaceful governance in Zambia.
headwife, e.g. Simaali sunu walede _kumalelo_. = The polygamist slept with the head-wife to-day.
fig trees, pl. of cilembela, e.g. Bayuni banji bajanwa _mumalembela_. = Many birds are found in fig-trees.

rain-shrine, e.g. Katuya tukakambile mvwula _mumalende_. = Let us go and ask for rain at the rain-shrine. (Nzi-lengwa-lengwa mbuli misamu, zitangaziba zyakulibeda amilonga zibelesegwa mukukambila mvwula.)
wit, creativity, e.g. _Malengelezi_ akwe amupa mapuwo. = His creative ability made him proud.
genesis, origin, e.g. Kuzwa _kumalengelo_ muntu nguwakali mupati kuzilenge zyoonse. = From the beginning the human being was the highest of all creation.
something mysterious, something to do with witchcraft, e.g. Ndabona _malengwa_ ayoosya sunu. = Today I have seen a fearful and mysterious thing.
pl. of _cilengwa-lengwa_ = marvels, unusual event, prodigy, e.g. Aaya _mmalengwalengwa_. = These are marvels.
labia, lips of female pudendum or genitals, (taboo word) e.g. Bamwi basimbi tabajisi *malepe*. = Some girls have no labia.
a woman's scarf, a shawl with fringe, e.g. Bakaintu bamwi bajisi *malesu*. = Some women have scarf's.
the trigger of a gun, e.g Koguma *maleswido*, ntobolo ilile. = Press the trigger of the gun so that it fires. Also malebwido, moola
public, a crowd of people, e.g. Utani kuciti zintu zyuusisya *amaleya*. = Do not do shameful things in public. Also buleya
erratic ways, inconsistency, e.g. Kogeme mpogeme, utabi *simaleyaleya*. = Go where you are going, do not be indecisive in where you go.
a beard, pl. of *idezu* or *kalezu*, malezu akujulu = moustache. e.g. *Malezu acisyuuka alababa*. = The beard when it begins to grow is itchy. *Malezu ndakalaalekede*. = I had left the beard to grow.
money, pl. of *idi*, a coin, *mali amuwayawaya/ amuweccewecce* = small change, e.g. Bantu banji tabajisi *mali mazubaano*. = Many people have no money these days.

pl. of *idiba*, a fall-trap of stone or hard clay, pl. also *madiba*, e.g. Koteya mbeba *amaliba*. = Trap the rats with stone or clay fall-traps. Wakayunza *maliba ngaakali kuteya*. = He inspected the traps which he had set.
a borehole-machine, e.g. Acibaka eci kuyandika *malibbolela* kweenzya meenda. = At this place there is needed a borehole-machine to bore for water.
boastfulness, e.g. Musankwa ulya *mmalibeja* buyo, kunyina ncacita. = That boy is just a boaster, he does nothing.
delusions, e.g. Muntu uwamba kuti uponya bantu ulaa *malibejwa*
a bufwubafwuba. Leza nguuponya. The one who says he heals people is just full of delusions and foolishness. It is God who heals.

humility - from *kulibonzya* = to humble oneself (Ila), e.g. *Malibonzya mmabotu kuti koyanda kujana zibotu*. = It is good to behave humbly if you want to find good things. Also (kuli)-tesya, (kuli)-bombya
a pretense for getting something else, e.g. Utaboni bantu nkobaunka kuya kulomba kulaigwa, *mmalido onse ngobacita*. = Don't just look at how people go there to seek advice, it is just a pretense.
common sense; muntu utakwe *maligi* = a foolish person
heavy footsteps, e.g. Ndamvwa *malikiti abantu batijaana*. = I hear the heavy footsteps of people running.
the funeral feast, e.g. Bakaapa bakaunka *kumalila* ijilo. = My grandmother went to a funeral yesterday.
gum from fig or rubber tree, e.g. *Malili amusamu oyu abambya malabba*. = The gum from this tree produces rubber.

milk, e.g. Basimpongo mukupa balawiita kuti *mmalili*. = The goatherds call milk *malili*. Mulongwaangu ulalya *malili aajombe*. = My friend eats cow's milk. Kobavwunikila *malili azilyo zyabo kutegwa zitalokelwi nzinini*. = Cover their milk and other food so that flies don't drop into it.
funeral-beer, e.g. *Malilila takwe naakasibikwa mane bantu nobakamana kulimuna maila*. = The funeral-beer was never brewed until people finished harvesting millet. Also *mweesyo*
mourning for several dead, pl. of *idilwe*, e.g. Kuli *malilwe manji mucisi coonse*. = There are many funerals throughout the whole country. ciimbo camalilwe = a dirge
many, e.g. Iminzi munsaa cikolo cesu mmalimba-limba. = The villages near our school are many.
instruments for playing or dancing, e.g. Kuli malimba ali kulila busiku boonse. = There were musical instruments playing all night.
pl. of idimba, a big feather, e.g. Bakombwe bajisi malimba malamfwu. = Cocks have long tail feathers. Also minimba, inimba.
pl. of idindi, a big hole with broad mouth, e.g. Kamusyanga mapopwe mumalindi. Plant the maize in large holes.
foresight, ability to predict, make a reasonable estimate of future events, e.g. Nseboni ciyakucitika, malingaano angu taali kabotu. = I cannot foretell what will happen, by foresight is not good.
lack of appreciation, e.g. Kuti wamuletela cakulya cibotu, walo ulaa malingunya. If you bring him good food, he does not appreciate it. Also malinguya.
wasps, pl. of ilinko, wasp, Akandiluma malinko aliso. = Wasps have stung me on the eye. Also maanko
ball-bearings, pl. of lisawo, (ety. Port. lead-shot), e.g. Malisawo ajanwa muncinga. Ball-bearings are found on bicycles.
threads of a screw, e.g. Insimbi iyenda mumaliya niikkiigwa. = A screw moves on threads when it is being tightened.

turns, pl. of bulizi, e.g. Basankwa beembela bapana malizi. = Boys who herd take turns. Sunu mbulizi bwako bwakweembela nombe. Today it is your turn to herd the cattle. malo pl. of bulo, a bed, e.g. Munanda yangu kuli malo otatwe. In my house there are three beds.

refers to the ritual of purification called 'ngolomokwa in which a village is cleansed from blood shed in homocide. e.g. Aafwida mweenzu, kujaigwa nombe yamaloa kusalazya munzi. = When a visitor dies, a cow is killed to cleanse the village.
floods, e.g. Mumwaka wa malobe mapopwe taakomeni kabotu. Maize does not grow well in a year of flooding.
pl. of idola, permanent hive of bees, (pl. also madola) e.g. Muvwubi wanzuki ujisi malola manji. = The owner of the bees has many hives.

pl. of idomba, a half human and half fish-like creature used by the witch when bewitching. A female form, like a mermaid, was sent to bewitch a man and a male form of it was sent to bewitch a woman, e.g. Balozi mbabavwuba malomba. The witches are the ones who own these half-fish, half-human creatures.
the boundary, e.g. Muunda wa Kaumba ncowakali mufwaafwi nkuti kumalomoneno kwakali cilundu cipati cakaciinkene. The reason why Kaumba's field was short is that there was a big hill at the boundary.
end of the field, e.g. Nobakasika kumalomu bakanyandwa kubona nkuku ziingaila musyokwe. When they reaches the end of the field they were surprised to see chickens wandering about in the bush.
big clay pots, e.g. Bamanyina balabajikila bana musozya wanyangu mumalongo. = The mothers cooked samp for their children in clay pots.

an edible fruit of a wild tree, pl. of iloolo, a species of wild fruit yellow when ripe, green when unripe, size of kawi fruit, brown seeds, very sweet, e.g. Bana balya *maloolo* musyokwe ciindi caku-mwaka. = Children eat the *maloolo* wild fruit in the bush during the dry season. Also *maloyoloyo*.
pl. of ciloto, dream, e.g. Sunu ndajisi *maloto* mabi. = Today I had bad dreams.
blood, pl. of bulowa, e.g. *Malowa* abantu bamwi mmabi. = Some people have bad blood.
witchcraft, e.g. *Malweza amalowe* aabantu akasangana. = An evil omen and the witchcraft of people had mixed.
a yellow wild fruit, e.g. *Maloyoloyo* alabanonena bana. = The *maloyoloyo* wild fruit is sweet to the children. Also *maloolo*.

pl. of iduba, a flower, e.g. Mazubaano bamakaintu bayandisya kubi-kka *maluba* mumaanda. = Nowadays women like putting flowers in their houses. Kwakali lukwakwa Iwamaluba Iwakazingulukide munzi. = There was a fence of flowers surrounding the village.
pl. of idubambizi, a horse-fly, e.g. Musune uciswa ukkalwa *maluba-mbizi*. = On a sick ox is where the horse-fly alights. Also *malumambizi*
pl. of buluke, a pair of trousers, e.g. Basankwa basama *maluke*. = Boys wear trousers.
sour-milk, e.g. *Malula* alanona mumusozya. = Sour-milk is tasty in samp. Kuti waciswa mwida, ncibotu kunywa *malula*. = If you have stomach-pains, it is good to drink sour-milk. Also *mabisi*
groups of people e.g. Kumuzundano *maluluulu* aabantu akacili kuzwaa kusika. = At the contest groups of people were still coming and going. Also *maunda-maunda*

anything bitter, e.g. Bulwazi bwatuntumaanzi busilisigwa *amalulwa*. = The disease of malaria is cured by what is bitter. Bantu bamwi balayandisya kunywa *malulwa-lulwa*. Some people like to drink what is bitter.
a grass poisonous for the cattle, e.g. Inombe zilya *malulwe* zilafwa. = Cattle which eat poisonous-grass die.
a bitter plant used to cure malaria, e.g. Bantu balabelesya *malulwe* kusilika bulwazi bwantuntumaanzi. = People use the *malulwe* plant to heal the disease of malaria.
type of wasps, e.g. Naakali kutijaana boobu mubili wakwe wakali kukankama mbuli *malumanombe*. = When he was running in that way his body was shaking like angry wasps.
those who are not Batonga, (also idumbu), e.g. *Bamalumbu* mbanji mucisi mazubaano. = There are many non-Tongas in the land these days.
pl. of mulumbu, a husked, unshelled, cob of maize, pl. also milumbu, e.g. Kamundipa mulumbu wapopwe omwe. = Give me one cob of maize.
nails, e.g. Bakagagaila *malunda* ananda yokwesu. They hammered nails on our house.

a heap of beads, pl. of bulungu, beads, necklace of beads: *bulungu bwamulilo* = small red beads; *bulungu bwacikambwe* = small blue beads, e.g. Sunu bamakaintu bakaleka kusama *malungu* mucibuno. = Nowadays women have stopped wearing strings of beads around the waist.
pl. of bulwazi, disease, e.g. *Malwazi* ajaya bantu arjombe avwula mucisi. = The diseases which kill people and cattle are abundant in the land.
rags, e.g. Ooyu mwana ngumucaala ncasama *malwendu-Iwendu*. = This child is an orphan that is why she wears rags.

an evil omen, e.g. Mweenzuma wandibona *malweza*, mwati nkunditukila = By insulting me unexpectedly my friend has become a sign of oncoming disaster. "Utandilambi _malweza ime!" = "Do not smear me with an evil omen." (_Malweza_ can also refer specifically to the evil of incest.)
below the navel
pl. of _idyabantu_, a canni- bal, e.g. _Balowa bamwi ngamalyabantu_. = Some witches are cannibals.
pl. of _idyabowa_, an eater of mushrooms, e.g. _Malyabowa ninondo_. = Tortoises are eaters of mushrooms.
in the evening, e.g. _Nda- zileta nombe kumalyakumbo_. = I will bring back the cattle in the evening.
pl. of _idyamaila_, a seed- eater bird, e.g. _Malyamaila amana maila muceme mumuunda_. = The seed-eating birds have finished off the sorgum in the field.
holes, burrows, e.g. _Nengo yakamuyiisya cucu kusya malyango_. = The antbear taught the mouse how to dig holes.

a beast given to the father of the girl, who is given in marr- iage, for him to hold for her, e.g. _Kuli nombe imwi njoceenda limwi amusune wamuyumusyo: eyi nombe itegwa nino- mbe yamalyansima. Inombe eyi taipegwi muntu umbi, njamusimbi sikutwalwa. Eeyi nombe ilategwa njamalyansima akaambo kakuti kuti kunyina nombe eyi, nobamupa musimbi nsima abo bamutwala inga tailyi akwiilya pe_. = There is another beast which goes together with the beast given to the father of the girl. This beast is called _nombe yamalyansima_. This beast is not given to another person, it is the property of the girl who is married. This beast is called _malyansima_ because if it is not there when the ones who marry her give her _nsima_ to eat, she can completely refuse to eat it. (Ila)

ventilation, e.g. _Netoona masiku tweelede kusoleka kusiya mama- nga kumaanda esu kuti muya mubotu kuunjila_. = When we are sleeping at night we ought to leave ventilation in our houses so that the fresh air can come in. _Intolongo tiikwe mamanga pe, amulyango ilakkiigwa lubbe_. = A prison has no ventilation and the gate is tightly closed. Also _mpulungwido_
our mothers, e.g. _Bamama- ma bakalicizyi kutulaya kaindi_. = In the past our mothers knew how to advise us.
the last/end, e.g. _Mama- nino abuumi buno ndufwu_. = The end of this life is death.
bullets, e.g. _Eeyi ntobolo taijisi mambala_. = This gun has no bullets.
a troublesome person, e.g. _Musankwa mambala ulaumwa ziindi zinji_. = A troublesome boy is beaten many times.

arrogance, impudence, e.g. _Mwana ulaa mambeke nsemuyandi_. = I don't like an impudent child. _Aba bana bakomenena mumakuwa balaa mambeke_. = These children who have grown up under the whites are full of arrogance. Also _macece_.
snuff spoons, e.g. _Bama- cembele banji babelesya mambeko kuto- mbwe wamumpemo_. = Many old women use snuff spoons for their snuff. Also _lubeko_, pl. _imbeko_
sweat-scrapers, e.g. _Kosansamuna nkasaala amambeko_. = Wipe off the sweat with the scrapers.
having many things to do at the same time, e.g. _Wabula mbwacita, wajata mambile_. = He did not know what to do, he had many things to do at the same time. Also _-jata bubi_
mumps, e.g. _Mwaalumi uciswa mambolomu_. = The man is suff- ering from the mumps. mambone-mbone spectacles, e.g. *Koleta mambone-mbone njanda kubala.* = Bring the spectacles I want to read.
pride, show off, e.g. *Mambonwa akaliko.* Pride was there.

pretense in disliking what you really like, e.g. *Musankwa tanaakaleka kwaambauzya musimbi nokuba kuti wakali kukaka-kaka. Akwalo naa kwaali kukaka kwini tee ndiza akali mambumbu.* = The boy did not stop proposing to the girl even though she was refusing. And as for her was it real refusal or perhaps a kind of pretense. *Basankwa bamazuba ano balayanda kukombelezya musimbi kuti kalipa mambumbu.* = Boys of these days like to coax a girl who pretends to refuse their advances.
venereal disease, e.g. *Mambunga alakonzya kusilikwa.* = Venereal disease can be treated. Also kanswende
canine teeth, with no teeth between, pl. of kambwili, e.g. *Ujisi mambwili atantene.* He has canine teeth which are growing on top of one another.
a small hole, pl. tumbwili, e.g. *Cacula kalalila mumambwili.* = The frog is croaking in a small hole.
idle tales, mostly lies, e.g. *Utani kwiile kumvwa mambyaambya.* = Do not just listen to rumours. Also mavwambukila.
pl. of bumena (yeast of sprouted grain, leaven, meal of malt). Kamukumba bukoko, *mamena akayuma kale.* Brew the beer, the yeast of the sprouted maize is already dry. Also mimena.
fits, e.g. *Muntu oyu uciswa mamfwa.* This person suffers from fits. Also maamfwa.
nasal-cartilage, e.g. *Bakamuuma nyindi amamfwonyo.* = He was beaten with a fist on the nostrils. Also mansyonyo.
cold or misty weather, weather without sunshine, e.g. *Sunu kuli mamfwumfwu takweendeki.* Today the weather is misty and not for moving about.
Also mafwunze
inner contents, e.g. *Muntu ulidunda tali muntu mubotu pe.
calona mamfwunzu abujula.* A person who is proud is not a good person. He is like the shell of a pumpkin without anything visible inside.
nasal mucous, pl. of ibbina, mucous from one nostril, e.g. *Kosinda mamina, mwana.* Remove the mucous, child.

a medicinal plant *(Combretus mossambicense)* given to dogs as a hunting medicine: the roots are dried, pounded and mixed with food to instil bravery. e.g. *Lubangu Iwamaminambelele ndukali kapati.* = The medicine of the *mamina-mbelele* plant is very potent.
an ill-mannered person, e.g. *Ndayoowa kuti kayakundikatazya ulya ngumampala wamuntu.* I fear that that one might trouble me as he is a badly behaved person.
butter-milk, e.g. *Mampamba amukupa abambya nsipa.* = Butter from milk is used for making soap. Also munkungwe, mungwele
fat left after meat is removed, e.g. *Bakazenga mampampa akacaala nibakagusya nyama.* They melted the fat which was left when they removed the meat.
fried boiled maize, e.g. *Mampandu aciwaya twakali kuzilida buyo.* = We were just eating boiled and fried maize.
coarse rough meal, e.g. *Bakakumba cibwantu cinji amampandwida.* They brew a lot of sweet-beer from coarse rough meal. Also mampaandwa, maando-maando, masembe.
crossed legs or crossed branches, e.g. Basankwa bayaka ciba amampangi amisamu. = The boys build kraals with crossed branches from trees.
top, highest point, e.g. Ndakatanta musamu akuunka biya kumampeleemfwa kwini. = I climbed the tree and went to the very top.

empty honey-comb, e.g. Kunyina simpako ulumwa nzuki nazyi kuti kunyina buci, *mampemfwa* alo. = No forager is willing to be stung by bees if he knows that there is no honey, just empty combs. Also mape
windings, e.g. Bakali kuyubaila mumampetu-mampetu. = They were hiding in the maze. Also mpetu-mpetu.
delaying tactics in marriage, e.g. Kaambo kali kafwiifwi kaletelwa mampindamangobe, kamuka kukosoka. The matter was simple but delaying tactics were brought which delayed the decision.
a house with many rooms, e.g. Eeyi nanda njamampindamangobe. This house has many rooms.
an intricate language, e.g. Mulaka wako ngwamampindamangobe, taumvwugwi. = Your language is complicated, it is unintelligible.
a labyrinth, e.g. Aayo mampindiņombe, kunyina cimwugwa pe. Those things are too complex, nothing is understood.
windings, e.g. Kaambo kaala kukosola, nkamampiti-mampiti. = The case cannot be solved. It has many twists and turns. Also mampetu-mampetu
a hollow grass used for weaving, pl. of impoolwe, e.g. Bana basiba *mampoolwe*. The children are using the hollow grass to whistle through.
an energetic person, e.g. Icilombwana cimwi cisinkimene alimwi icamampuba cakaima akutalika kulibanda. = One sturdy and energetic man stood up and began calling out his praise-names.
reverence when approaching superior, e.g. Bantu beelede kubaa *mampuka* munsi lyamuleli. People ought to have respect when near a leader. Also mulemyo, bulemu.
roughness, e.g. Ooyu mwiini wakeembe ulaa mampumpunya. = The handle of the axe is rough.
rumours, e.g. Utani kutobeli twaambo twamampya. Do not follow rumours. Also mambyaambya.
thorns, pl. of bumvwa, e.g. Mwana wakayaswa *mamvwa* tayendi. = The child who was pierced by thorns does not walk.
different opinions, e.g. Akaba *mamvwaamvwa*. There arose different opinions.
pl. of imvwo, e.g. a blind-fly, e.g. Basimbi bakali kusya lusala bakalumwa *mamvwo*. = The girls who were digging edible tubers were bitten by flies. Also mazyimbwa
large wasps, pl. of imvwu, e.g. Mwana wanetuka naalumwa ma*mvwu* obilo. The child fainted when stung by two large wasps.
soil, pl. of ivwu, soil, e.g. *Mamvwu*
mapopwe soils makes the maize grow.
big cones of borassuspalm, pl. of imvwuma, e.g. *Mamvwuma* azyalilwa mujulu. = The fruit of the borassus-palm is produced high up on the tree.
carelessness, e.g. Muntu ulaa *mamvwunze* tabambi zintu mubulondo. A person full of carelessness does not care for things in a neat way.
a holocaust, e.g. *Kwakaba mamwiko manji lyankondo yama Natzi.* = There were many holocausts at the time of the Nazi war.
larvae of bees still in comb, e.g. *Bamwi bantu bayandisya kapati mana.* = Many people love the larvae of bees in the comb.
pl. of *lyana*, a comb, e.g. *Kuli mana otatwe mupe lyabuci.* = There are three combs in the honey-nest.

useless children, pl. of *lyana*, e.g. *Nkwaali mana amwi ali mbuli masebelele anga mmabotu buyo atala, koya nkooko apwaye, ncinzi njojana? Alibolede mukati!* = There are some useless children who are like *masebelele* fruits, which seem to be beautiful on the outside, but if you squash them what do you find? They are rotten inside!
our mothers, e.g. *Manakuliswe bajisi lulayo lubotu.* = Our mothers have good advice. Also bakuliswe.
pineapples, e.g. *Kulubazu Iwakumbo kuli mananashi manji.* = On the western area there are many pine-apples.
a small scented root used as a charm or ornament, e.g. *Munanga ubelesya mananda kuvwuma munzi wakwe.* = The witchdoctor uses a charm to protect his village.
the horn of an antelope used as a musical instrument, a harp-like bow, e.g. *Mananda ngwalwija Iwalweengu.* = This musical instrument is from the horn of an antelope.
pipe made from branch of cacytus tree, e.g. *Mananda alabambwa akakutusu.* = The pipe is made from a cactus tree.

ochre, e.g. *Onaawa naakazwa munanda, mananda onse taanaakubuluka, nkukwatwa kale!* = Just recently when she came out of the house (after initiation) before all the ochre had worn away, she already gets married!
a children's game. e.g. *Basimpongo tabakkali buyo nobamana kulya, balasobana mananga.* = Goatherds do not just sit after eating, they play the *mananga* game.
syphilis, e.g. *Manansa mbu-Iwazi bupenzya bantu kwiinda mubu-mambe.* = Syphilis is a disease which troubles people because of promiscuity.

sudden appearance of a person when spoken about, e.g. *Webo ulaa manca, wasika mbutwamana kukwaamba.* = You appear when spoken about, you arrived as soon as we had finished talking about you. Also mazumbu.
tufts of burnt grass left by fire, e.g. *Ndakajaya sulwe mumancaalizya.* = I killed a rabbit among the tufts of burnt grass left by the fire. Also luya.
a squint-eyed person, e.g. *Ndakasyaba musimbi wamancenga.* = I proposed to a squint-eyed girl.
thorny round nuts, e.g. *Simpongo ulayaswa mancenya amasonso.* = The goatsherd is pricked by thorny round nuts.
a rough surface, e.g. *Zinowe taziyandi kweenda mumancinya.* = Corns do not like travelling over rough ground. Also magunyu-gunyu.
matches, pl. of *kanchisi*, a match, e.g. *Kokkwenyuna mancisi tudomeke lambe.* = Strike a match so that we light the lamp. (*cikwama camancisi* = a box of matches)
froth, suds, e.g. *Insipa zimwi tazijisi mancomvwa manji.* = Certain types of soaps do not produce sufficient suds. Also *iccovwu*, pl. *maccovwu*.
pl. of *incwe*, the bishop bird, seedeater, e.g. *Mancwe azyala cilimo.* = The seed-eaters propagate during the dry season.
pl. of *incwencwe*, the bishop bird Also *mancwe*.
a skirt of cowhide and strips, a dress of hanging strings, pl. of *ilyanda*, e.g. *Booye bakaindi bakali kusama manda*. = The young girls of long ago used to wear the *manda* dress. Also *maaya*.
binoculars, e.g. *Undipe mandaala ndayanda kubona munyama ulya uli kule*. = Give me the binoculars I want to see that animal which is far away.
an initiated girl, e.g. *Munanda muli mandala tamunjilwi basankwa*. = The house where a girl is being initiated should not be entered by boys.

fluid from the womb, e.g. *Inombe ilafwumbwa mboyamanina kumuzyaala mwana, mbwaawida ansi ucili amandeka aakuzwa angawo mwida amubili yatalika kumumyankuta*. = It happens that when a cow calves, as soon as it falls to the ground and is still covered with fluid from the womb, it starts licking the whole body of the calf.
sour-milk, e.g. *Kamubikka mandili mumusozya musyubu*. = Put sour-milk in the samp.
snores, e.g. *Mapulanga ulaa mandonono nawona*. = Mapulanga emits snores as he sleeps. Also *magonono*
stilts, pl. of *ndoombe*, a stilt, e.g. *Kweenda amandoombe nkucenjela*. = You should be careful when walking on stilts.
slipperiness e.g. *Cigwinya ukozya mubondo, ulijisi mbwebwebwetu amandoondo amubili*. = The *cigwinya* fish is similar to the barbel, it has spikes and slipperiness on its body.
blankets, e.g. *Bataata bakatuulila mandumba mapya*. = Father bought new blankets for us. Also *mapayi*
commodities in large quantities, e.g. *Mutala a Zambezi zitima zilazubula mandunduli malemu ajanika kumigodi*. = The trains carry heavy loads across the Zambezi from the Copperbelt.

beer drunk on the third day after the beer was fully brewed, e.g. *Alo cini cakamukkazide ncakuti wakali kunywa kanongo kamandungwa*. = What really made him content was that he was drinking a pot of *mandungwa* beer.
take pride in something which is not your own, e.g. *Ma! Nciindi taata kuli yooyo ulimvwa mandunya acntu camuntu*. = It is his problem to feel proud of something which is not his own. Also *matunta*.
monkey-apples, pl. of *inego*, e.g. *Kwa Chipembele kuli manego manji kapati*. = There are plenty of monkey-apples at Chipembele. Also *itobo*, pl. *matobo*.
power, vitality, courage, e.g. *Manga amubwa ali kumucila*. = The vitality of a dog is shown in its tail. *Wakabaa manga akwaambaula*. = He got the courage to speak.
*bana bamanga* = twins, also *mayanga*
head decorations for men attending funerals, e.g. *Ba-Ila basama mangalangala mumadilwe*. = The Ba-Ila wear head-dress during funerals.
cooked unhusked grain, e.g. *Mangamwe alanona kuti komvwide nzala*. = Cooked whole-grains of maize are tasty when you are hungry. Also *magwaza*
decorations, designs, e.g. *Cuuno cakwe cali cabwami cijisi mangele-ngele atuba mumbazu zyoonse*. = His chair was majestic having white designs on all sides.
mangoes, pl. of *ingo*, e.g. *Mango makwange alasyakamuka*. = Unripe mangoes are bitter.

evening after sunset, e.g. Bakaintu bakasika *mangolezya* kuzwa kudilwe. = The women arrived back in the evening from the funeral. Kamwale utolwa kusyokwe *mangolezya* bantu boonse nobanjila mumaanda. = The female initiate is taken in the evening to the bush (to the toilet) after all the people have entered their houses.
mumps, e.g. Mainza ulaa bulwazi bwamangolomu, masaya akwe alizimbide. = Mainza has the mumps, his cheeks are swollen.
a charm said to generate power, e.g. Kanoma wakalide *mangolomu* anyindi. = Kanoma used the charm which generated aggressiveness when fighting with the fists.
drums, pl. of ingoma, e.g. Ino nkuli kwali kulila *mangoma* sunu? = Where were the drums beating today?
a cat, pl. bamangowe, e.g. Mangowe wangu wakazyala jilo. = My cat gave birth yesterday. Also *mangoye*.
a cat, e.g. *Mangoye* ulaluma tuzoka anze mulukonkono Iwananda. = A cat kills the young snakes outside behind the house.
solitary dancing, e.g. Ulaa *mangulwe*. = She dances alone.

a type of masabe possession, e.g. Bamaama bakanjilwa *mangulwe*. = My mother is possessed by the *mangulwe* spirit. *mangulwe-ngulwe* interference with other peoples affairs, e.g. Mujibelo akamuumya *mangulwe-ngulwe*. = Interference with other people's affairs gained Mujibelo a beating.
the principle poles of a roof usually fastened together before hoisting, pl. of iganguzyo, e.g. Kamwaagagaila kabotu *manguzyo*. Nail the main roofpoles together properly. Also mabompwa.
big palm leaves, e.g. Basimbi baya kukuleta *mangwalala* atuvwuma. = The girls are going to bring big palm-tree leaves.
a term referring to the Lozi people when they raided the Tonga for cattle, e.g. Ninsilamatongo yakacaala liya lyakainda *bamangwalu-ngwa-*
caga. = The remains of village were left when the Lozi passed through the land of the Batonga.
pl. of ingwanda, luggage, load, box with lid nailed, e.g. Silweendo uyumwide *mangwanda*. = The traveller is carrying luggage.
butter-milk, whey (watery part of milk that remains liquid when the rest forms curds), e.g. Kamutusanina *mangwele* tubwa. = Feed the pups with buttermilk. Also mulaza
one who interferes with what does not concern him, e.g. Chiwele ngusimangwemba = Chiwele is a person who meddles in other people's affairs. Also *mangulwe-ngulwe*.

comic actions, e.g. Aumwi utamikizya umwi kuti wakamubona ucita nzila zyabulozi, mbuli kusanina domba, kusanina zyeelo, kuba abuyowela munanda, kuyobola nsengo, kulyaambauzya, *mangweengwe* akuzyana. = One slanders the other that she saw him practicing witchcraft, such as feeding a creature of witchcraft, feeding spirits, having spirits in the house, keeping a horn for witchcraft, talking to himself, doing amusing actions and dancing the witch's dance.
whey, e.g. Mabisi atali malemu mmangwele biyo. = Sour-milk which is not thick is just whey

amusing behaviour, e.g. Mwiinga wakakolwa akutalika kutukkoma-nisya kwiinda *mumangwinini* akwe akuswiilizya mantyaantya. Mwiinga was drunk and began to delight us with his amusing behaviour and in listening to his jokes.
nonsense, e.g. Mebo obuno buzuba tandiyandi *mangwinini*. = As regards myself on this day I do not want any nonsense.
green grass, grass as fit for cattle, sing. *lyani* or *kani* (a blade of grass) e.g. *Impongo zilacela mumani mabotu.* = The goats are grazing on good grass. Also *maani*.
traditional medicine, e.g. *Muntu wakalya mani akulikwabilila, tafwi kufwa-mbaana.* = A person who ate protective medicine, does not die early.
a musical-instrument used by girl in the seclusion of initiation, e.g. *Mooye usobanya manimbwa.* = The young girl is playing a musical-instrument (used during initiation).
end of line/series, e.g. *Koya ukaime kumaninino amulongo.* = Go and stand at the end of the line.
oil, e.g. *Basicikolo banana manjanja.* = The pupils smear themselves with oil. Also *mafwuta, manconco*.
uncertainties, e.g. *Kuli manjeezya akuti Joojo uli ku Lusaka.* = There is uncertainty whether Joojo is in Lusaka.
intrigue (underhand plotting), e.g. *Basankwa babi balaa manjelayisya akujaya Jolezya.* = Evil men have a plot to kill Jolezya.
respect for other people's rights, e.g. *Ncibotu kubaa manje-zeezya mumicito yabantu bambi.* = It is good to have respect as regards other people's actions.

doubtfulness, confusion, uncertainties, e.g. *Wakacaala wanyongana kale mumi-zeezo akaambo kamanjezeezya akamu-vwulila.* He remained confused in his thoughts because of the uncertainties which filled him. *Cakamupa manjezeezya mmukaintu wakwe ngwaatakabwene ka-botu.* = What made him uncertain was his wife whose behaviour was not trans-parent to him. e.g. *Utabi a manjezeezya, uunke ncobeni nkoya.* = Don't be irresolute, you should go where you are going. Also *manjezyeezya, manjeezezya*.
moral attitude, conscience, e.g. *Manjezya amusankwa oyu mmabotu.* = The conscience of this boy is good.
mirage, also *masilikiti* + overlapping-teeth, e.g. *Tatafwuni kabotu nkaambo menyo akwe ngamanjiliki-twa.* = He does not chew well because his teeth are overlapping.
to be accepted in many places, bne given the right of freedom of movement, be approachable, e.g. *Muntu mubotu ulijisi manjilo manji.* = A good person is very welcome in many places.
entrances, e.g. *Bakali bantu banji mumanjililo aamubbuwa lyabbola.* = There were many people at the entrances of the football-ground.
manager, paymaster, (ety. Eng.), e.g. *Kubeleka kabotu cikkoman-isya manjimela.* = To work well makes the manager happy.
ice, e.g. *Kobikka mankaakamba acaanda, inswi zitatunti.* = Put ice in the fridge so that the fish do not rot. Also *caanda*

hair in the armpits, e.g. *Ncibotu kusanzya mankwaakwa nkaambo kuti tociti oobo inga munkwa mwamu-nkwa.* = It is good to wash hair in the arm-pits because if you do not do this the armpits will smell. Also *mankwaankwa*
talkativeness, e.g. *Ncibi kuba simankanana.* = It is bad to be talkative. Also *munkanwe*. Also *mankonono*
mud, e.g. *Mwana wali-kanda mumankandya.* = The child has smeared herself with mud. Also mankanda, butope butyopo

remins of food, e.g. Zilyo nozyali kundiceela, ndali kuzisanina nombe *amankansyi* aandongo alimwi ndali kuvwuzya akuzipa busu bwamalangazuba. = The food which they were gathering for me, I was feeding the cattle with the remains of the groundnuts and I frequently gave them sunflower-flour.
pl. of *cinkanza*, a clot of dried blood, e.g. Mufwu walikuzwa ma*nkanza* amalowa. = Clots of blood were coming out from the dead person.

a wide spread, e.g. Musune wangu ujisi *mankapa* aboya. = My ox has a wide spread of hair. Kankuli kamunanga kakali kuyoosya kulanga akaambo *kamankapa* abulungu ngokakasamikidwe. = The small calabash of the witchdoctor was fearful to look at because of the wide mat of beads with which it was dressed.
pl. of *inko*, a mason wasp, e.g. Mwana walumwa *manko*. = The child has been stung by mason-wasps.
receding eyes, e.g. Musankwa oyu ngwa*mankobwa*. = This boy has receding eyes. Also mabboli.
poles for closing entrance, e.g. Kamwiinganya *mankolo* amulyango waciba. = Close the entrance to the krall with poles. Also minkulwa, micinjili
pl. of *inkolo* (breast, udder) e.g. Eeyi nombe ijisi *mankolo* mapati. = This cow has big udders.
eyes under protruding forehead, e.g. Basokwe balaa *mankolyo*. = Monkeys have eyes under a protruding forehead. Also *makope*.
scales caused by not washing, e.g. Nciinga Syaavwaki cakalijisi *mankomba* kumaulu akumaboko. = Useless Syaavwaki had scales both on his legs and arms.
badly cooked food, e.g. Nabwiinga wajika *mankombole* kumakwe. = The newly-wed woman cooked badly at her in-laws.
dried pumpkin cooked with mashed groundnuts, e.g. Wajika ma-*nkomboli*. = She cooked dried pumpkin with mashed groundnuts.
pl. of *inkomone*, a small coconut, e.g. Twakali kulya *mankomone* ku Namwala. = We were eating small coconuts at Namwala.
pieces of a cake of tobacco/hemp (sometimes buried in kraal to make extra strong), e.g. Bacembele babwezelela *mankomo-nkomo* atombwe. = The old woman is gathering up pieces of tobacco.
food without relish, e.g. Tulye biyo *mankondole* nkaambo twabula cisyu. = Let us just eat the food without relish.

saliva from mouth during sleep, spittle coming out of sides of mouth, e.g. Kosamba kumeso ujisi ma-*nkonono*. = Wash your face, you have spittle on it. Jolezya wakali kwiide koona, wakali kwiide kulizya *mankonono*. = Jolezya was just sleeping, he was just dribbling saliva. Also *mankanana*.
pl. of *cinkonti*, a shelled mealie-cob, pl. also *zinkonti*, e.g. Kamusikka *mankonti* acikko. = Put the shelled mealie-cobs in the fire. Also *mankosyi*.
shelled mealie-cobs, e.g. Kamuleta *mankosyi* tusikke nkaambo nkuni nzitete. = Bring the empty cobs so that we stick them in the fire because the firewood is wet. Also *mankonti*
droppings of birds, e.g. Mutinta naakabuka wakakkala akulilanga amubili, wakajana ulatuba buu *mankotyo*

muntu walede mukaanda koona nkuku. = When Mutinta woke up, she sat and looked at her body, she found she was completely white with bird droppings, like a person who had been sleeping in a hen-house. Wakalikunga ateelela kulyatauka kwabayuni antoomwe akukasaala kwama-baba alimwi amankotyo wayeeya kuti antela mizimo yakwe yamuleta mwana. = When she heard the tramping of the birds together with the warmth of the wings and the droppings, she thought that perhaps her helping spirits had brought her child.
silt, debris, detritus, e.g. Kwakacaala mankuke mumuunda lyakazula mulonga. = Only silt remained in the field when the river had overflowed. Also mankuwe
pl. of cinkuli, a calabash, e.g. Mumuunda oyu kuli mankuli manji. = There are many calabashes in this field.

traditional medicine which makes one strong or aggressive, e.g. Bantu banji bakali kwaamba kuti wakayasidwe mankuma anguzu. = Many people said that he had been tatooed with traditional medicine for making one strong. Wakatalika kuvwitima cabukali nokuba kuti taakanywide mankuma. = He began to pant with anger even though he had not taken mankuma medicine.
vitality, e.g. Aino kubandika bobuya inga nkutegwa buyo mwaacili mankumwa akubwana. = To talk like this means you have still the vitality of youth.
the ordinary cylindrical drum as distinguished from the budima drums among the Valley Tonga, e.g. Mwaampazisamu ulafwala mankuntu asiyene-siyene. = Mwaampazisamu carves drums of different kinds.
containers for storing food, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kuyobweda mumankuntu maila. = The people of the past used to store millet in containers.
wrinkles, pl. of kankusa, (a single wrinkle), e.g. Ncibi kutondezya bantu mankusa. = It is bad to show people a wrinkled up face. Also minya
trees drifting when river is in flood, e.g. Kamuzwa mumulonga alamucisa mankutye. = Come out of the river the drifting trees will hurt you.
insects, e.g. Kwa*kaba nzala mpati. Zilyo zyabo zyakaligwa mankuunkumbuli. = There was great famine. Their food was eaten by insects.

many loaves of bread, e.g. Musimbi wakatalika kuula mabbaanzi kuzwa kunanda ijikilwa, mankwa akusambala ananda. = She began to buy buns from the bakery and many loaves of bread to sell them at her home.
hair in the armpit, pl. of inkwaankwa, e.g. Amundipe mbeli ndinyoole mankwaankwa. = Give me a razor-blade so that I remove hair from the armpit. Also makwaankwa
loud laughter e.g. Bamakaintu bakauma mankwalala. = The women laughed loudly. Also magweegwe
many big pieces of bread, e.g. Bantu bakalya mankwa-mankwa kumucado. = People ate many big pieces of bread at the wedding.

hallucination, an abnormal experience of something which is not really present or happening, e.g. Ndabaa mankwela akuti Mutinta nkwali kuno. = I had an hallucination that Mutinta was present. Also mankwelu

loud laughter, e.g. Wakamvwa bakaintu anze baseka mankweleele: "He! He! He! He! Heeewuuu! = She heard the women outside laughing loudly, He! He! He! He! Heeewuuu! Mpoona awo boonse kwakabboloka mankweleele kuseka. = Thereupon all burst out laughing. Also magwegweegwe
foolish laughing, e.g. Silubanje ulaa mankwelu akuseka nokunyina cacitika. = A drug-addict laughs foolishly when nothing is happening.
sweepings, e.g. Basicikolo bakali kuyola mankwisilili mulubuwa. = The pupils were gathering up the sweepings from the courtyard.
ear ornaments **mankwita-nkwita** ear-ornaments, pl. of inkwitankwita, e.g. Muka Maumbi usamide *mankwita-nkwita*. The wife of Maumbi is wearing ear-rings.

footprints, pl. of lino, e.g. Joojo ujisi *mano mapati*. Joojo has big footprints. Wakabona *mano* abantu baali kwiinda mazuba ali mbwaabede nobakali kuvwima. She saw the fooprints of people who were passing by some days past when they were hunting.
a brown fruit of musangu tree eaten by animals, e.g Inombe zilya *mansangu-sangu*. = The cattle are eating the fruits of the musangu tree.
bruises, pl. of insangwa, e.g. Bana mbaali kuuma Kagele bazwa *mansangwa* amibili. The children who were beaten by Kagele have bruises on their bodies
special plates used for nsima made out of grass or reeds, e.g. *Mansangwa* alida nsima. = Special plates are used for eating *nsima*.
a garment worn by the Zambezi people, e.g. Bacembele basanzya *mansani* mumulonga. = The old women are washing clothes in the river.
colostrum (first milk of mammal after parturition), e.g. Beembezi bakali kuumwa ciindi nibakali kulya ma*nsema*. The herders were beaten when they drank the first milk of the cattle.
a disease which child contracts from sucking breast after mothers milk has finished and takes in wind instead of milk, e.g. Mwana oyu uciswa *mansema*. = The child suffers from bad breast-feeding.
sediment as in beer, e.g. Bamwi bantu basanina ngulube zyabo *amansiwa*. Some people feed their pigs with beer-sediment. Also masiwa.
pl. of cinswa, a rat's nest, e.g. Imbeba zibikka *manswa* mubwina. = Rats place nests in a hole.
pl. of cinswanswa, a rat's nest. Also *manswa*.
nasal cartilage and bones, e.g. Muntu uciswa syini, *mansyonyo* alacisa. = When a person is suffering from a common cold, the nostrils also are sore. Also mamfwonyo.
a dilema, e.g. Ndabaa *mantaanta* = I am in a dilema. Zyavwula nzyecita, ndaajata *mantaanta*. = I have a lot to do, I am caught in a dilema. Also maanka-maanka.

a mixture of boiled fermented and non-fermented meal in water but not yet made into beer; the day before the beer is ready when it is still strong and bitter, e.g. Katuya tukanywe *mantabe*. = Let us go and drink *mantabe* beer. Also matimba
a horsefly, pl. *bamantaka*, e.g. Inyama yabola, ilaa *bamantaka*. = The meat is rotten, it is full of horse-flies. Also idubambizi.

dolls with which girls play at *mantoombwa*, e.g. Basimbi bakabbala bana *bamantamba* nibakali kusobana ku-*mantoombwa*. Girls carried dolls on their backs when they were playing at the children's *mantoombwa* training.
a bow-legged person, e.g. Maulu okwa Haakagoli *mmanteeka*.
is bow-legged.
scruples/doubts, e.g. Kuvwuzya *mantelayisya* mucamba cilakosya. To be obsessed with scruples makes one grow thin.
a collar, e.g. *Mantemba* akwabilila mazyempe kutombe. = The collar protects the shirt from dirt.

a stringed musical-instrument played by the girl undergoing. initiation, e.g. *Mooye usobana mantim-bwa* *munanda naalendelelwa*. = The girl plays the *mantimbwa* in the house when she is feeling lonely.

roofless huts built by boys for girls at harvest festival in which they imitate adult behaviour, rough construction for young girls playing at house-keeping. *Mantoombwa ninzi? Ma-ntoombwa mmatungu, nintuntu*. = What is *mantoombwa*? *Mantoombwa* are roof-less huts or rough constructions.

training at housekeeping, e.g. *Bana ba-sobana kujikilila kumantoombwa*. = The children are practising cooking at the *mantoombwa*. *Ncisobano cabasimbi a ba-lombe ncibasobana kumantoombwa ba-zyali babo nobamana kulimina nzembwe azilyo zimwi*. = It is a game for girls and boys which they play after their parents have harvested *nzembwe* and other crops. *Basimbi baniini bakali kujikila mantoombwa mutugabba-gabba kumbo amunzi*. = Small girls were playing at housekeeping and cooking in small tins to the west of the village.

rheum, a discharge from the eyes, tears, mucous, e.g. *Kogusya mantongwe kumeso yawe*. = Please remove the mucous from your eyes. *Uta-balekeli kulya amantongwe kumeso bana*. = Do not let the children eat with rheum in their eyes.
pl. of *cintoolo*, a store, e.g. *Ndaunka kumantoolo*. = I have gone to the stores.
pl. of *intoolwani*, tufts of burnt grass left by fire, e.g. *Sulwe wa-yuba mumantoolwani*. = The hare is hiding in the tufts of burnt grass.
a surprise, e.g. *Syaana-sulwe naakamvwa boobo wakaba ama-ntukwe agambya*. = When the hare heard this he got a surprise.
pride, e.g. *Simapuwo ulaa mantumbwaambwa*. = A proud person is full of arrogance.
insight as to cause of the problem, e.g. *Kumucita boobo walo mucape kwakaba kumupa mantunamina*. = By doing this the witchdoctor was giving him the insight to see clearly the cause of the problem.
hummocks, something protruding. Also *tuntuntaulu*
pride, e.g. *Kuba amantuntwa-ntuntwa inga bantu baku-sulaika*. = To become full of pride, will make people hate you.
talk that causes laughter, e.g. *Bantu bakaseka kapati nkaambo kamantyaantya ngubakamvwa kuli Mu-ntyai*. = People laughed very much because of the amusing talk which they heard from Muntyai.

large-bodied people, e.g. *Mantyu aatakombeleli akoona koonse*. = Powerfully built people do not mind sleeping anywhere *manuka-mucamba* a chest-complaint, e.g. *Bantu baciswa manuka-mucamba, ta-bayoyi kabotu*. = People who have chest problems, do not breathe well. Also *manukilwa, kamanu*.
a traditional disease where patient is obsessed with the aroma of cooked-meat, e.g. *Ulwala manunki-nunki*. = She is obsessed with the desire to eat meat.

boiling maize, e.g. *Munanga naakali kusonda, kankuli kakali kwiide kugunauka ulati manya-munampemo ali mucibiya*. = When the witchdoctor was divining, the gourd was moving up and down like the grains of maize being boiled in the pot. Also *magwaza, mangamwe*.
rudeness, carelessness, e.g. *Kubaa manyanga inga wabula balo-ngwe*. = Being rude will prevent you having friends.
caterpillars, e.g. Mapopwe taakakomena kabotu nkaambo akaligwa manyanga. = The maize did not grow well because it was eaten by caterpillars.

a combination of beads of different colours woven into a necklace and worn by elders in the Gwembe valley, e.g. Bamacembele bakujwe basama manyanga munsingo. = The old women of the Gwembe Valley wear a coloured beadednecklace.
most precious gifts e.g. Buzumi bwesu mmanyanga a Leza. = Our life is the inestimable gifts of God. Inngolide mmanyanga abavwubi. = Gold is the most prized gift of the rich.

crinkles, wrinkles, bends in line or surface, e.g. Mwana uciswa masoto ulaa manyanina muntebe. = A baby who suffers from a disease attributed to the extra-marital sexual life of a parent has wrinkled thighs. Also minya
a type of grass, e.g. Inombe zilacela mumanyanja. = The cattle are grazing in the manyanja grass.
grass from which salt is made, grass growing in swampy areas, e.g. Kamuleta manyanje, tubambe munyo. Bring the grass which contains sodium chloride, so that we make salt.
mumany= Snipes live in grassy swamps.

strong sexual feelings, e.g. Imisamu yamuzyondo yakali kukatazya kujana. Tuntu twakali kuvwelenganyizigwa twakali tunji. Tuntu tatukwe abwaambe, tweenzya manyeele. = Love charms were difficult to come by. The little things mixed in with them are many. The little things are unmentionable, they arouse sexual feelings.

fun, a friendly look while showing teeth, sympathetic smiles, pleasant looks, amusing speech or actions, what is comical, e.g. Musobani ulaa manyeena ulakondelezya. = A comedian entertains people. (Simanyeena ulakondelezya kukkala limwi. = It is delighful to live with a humourous person.) Bantu balaa manyeena balasesya. = People who are funny make one laugh.
foolish play, e.g. Manyeenwa ayakukumana sunu. = You are going to do away with your foolish play today.
a molar tooth, e.g. Ndanjilwa lusinga mumanyelelwa. = I have a nerve-pain in the molar tooth,
unripe grain, e.g. Mango acili manyeleIwa alasyakamuka. = Mangoes which are still unripe are acidic.
grimaces, unpleasant looks, e.g. Musimbi naakamita, bazyali bakatondezya manyemwe. = When the girl became pregnant the parents showed disapproval.
smile showing the teeth, e.g. Milambo wakalaa manyena ncobakali kumuyanda bantu. = Milambo always had a smile that is why people liked him.
a kind of long grass, elephant-grass, pl. of inyengele, e.g. nombe zilalya manyengele. The cattle are eating elephant-grass.
designs, e.g. Kalembo katebule kasumidwe manyengwe mabotu. = The table cloth is nicely designed.
sandals, e.g. Manyetelo azutuka nindali kutanda nombe. = The sandals were ripped when I was chasing the cattle.
big black ants marching in columns, crowds, pl. of inyewu, pl. of munyewu, e.g. Bantu wakali munyewu kumuswaangano. People were packed like ants at the meeting.
lands, e.g. Mwaka wakamana kwakali nzala mpati mumanyika manji. = Last year there was a great famine in many countries.
sensitive to touch, e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa manyili. This child is sensitive when touched. Also bunyeele
his/her mothers, also cows, e.g. Kamutola boombe kumanyina. = Take the calves to their mothers.
crinkles (wrinkles or bends in line or surface) Also manyanina, minya.
your mothers, e.g. Ino Joni, bamanyoko mbakowa nzi? = John, what is the clan of your mothers?
skimmed milk, e.g. Mukupa manyomu taijisi cakulya cizulide. = Skimmed milk does not have full food content.

edible caterpillar much relished by the Bene Mukkuni manyongwe conflicts, e.g. Mumunzi omu kuli manyongwe, bantu tabakkali kabotu. Within this village there are conflicts, the people do not live at ease.
kutianjizya mu manyongwe. = They began to fear that it would get them into trouble.
jam, e.g. Ncindakali kuyanda kulya ndakacizila manyonsi. = I smeared the jam on what I wanted to eat.

unsafe, precarious, e.g. Oonse acuuno kukkala wakakkazya manyonyomanwa. Even the way he sat on a chair was unsafe. manyonyoonyo roughness (as of stone or wood), e.g. Ipulanga eli lijisi manyo-nyoonyo. = This plank is rough.
milk separated from cream, e.g. Mukupa oyu mmanyovwu. This milk is separated from the cream.
pl. of inyumbi, milk separated from cream. Also manyovwu.
smelting furnaces (always two together, as it were male and female.)
a place where paths divide up. e.g. Bakasika amanzaanina anzila zyabazovwu. = They arrived where the elephant-trail splits up.

house built for in-laws by son-in-law. e.g. Mulombe umwi aumwi naakayanda kukwela musimbi wakwe, wakayaka nanda yabanyinazyala itegwa nanda yamanzaanino. = Whenever a boy wanted to marry, he built a special house for his in-laws as a sign of his departure with the girl to his own home. Also maandanino
crossroads, e.g. Wiime aano ambali amanzaanino aanzila zyabazovwu. Stand here near where the road of the elephants divide. Also maandanino
a great famine, e.g. Mazubaano manzala aile kutobelana. = These days one famine just follows another.

confusion, e.g. Kacumbika ulayasya muzenge wamulilo ampako mpuzizwida nzuki. Alaba manzinzili nzuki, zilafwubaala. Kacumbika is lighting a grass-torch at the exit hole of the bees. There is confusion among the bees, they become stupid. mana cracks in a surface, rough surface, pl. of ina, a crack, e.g. Eeyi nanda ilaa mana, ilakonzya kuwa kufwumbwa ciindi. This house has cracks, it can fall at any time. Basicikolo beelede kusamba kutegwa batabi amana.
should wash so that they do not have cracks under their feet. Also maamba
a rough surface, e.g. Kuti kotasambi inga wabaa manangaala. = If you do not wash you will have rough-skin. Also maamba

a wild red plums, sing. nomba, e.g. Tuya kukucela manomba. = We are going to gather wild plums. Also mancomvwa, wild red plums (can also mean 'froth') Musimbi wakali mubotu, usubila pyu mbuli maņomba. = The girl was beautiful, as attractive as plums.
a yellowish fruit, e.g. Twali kuulisya manombyo kucipangahodi. = We were selling wild fruits at the waiting room.
a yellowish fruit, a wild fruit yielding oil, the yellow fruit from a kind of rubber tree, edible e.g. Ku Pemba nkokuli *manono manji*. = At Pemba there are yellow fruits. Also *manombyo, manono*.

rumours, e.g. Bana Syaacibangula bakamvwa *manunununu* akuti kwakanjila ntomba mucisi. = The people of Syaacibangula heard rumours that smallpox had entered the territory. Ndakamvwa buyo *manunununu* alufwu Iwa Jolezya. = I only heard rumours about Jolezya's death.
stupidity, e.g. *Mmanunzu aa mulombwana akazumine kupa luba loonse mbolubede*. = It is the foolishness of the man to agree to give away the whole kraal as it is.
letters, e.g. Mainza wakali kukonzya kubala akulilembela *manwadi*. = Mainza was able to read and write letters by himself.
a generous person, e.g. *Muntu mwaabi ngwamapaapa*. = A generous person is one who gives freely.

naievety in giving, e.g. Kaindi bazyali tiibakali kuyanda kukwasya mwanaabo kumusankwa mutolo. Sunu bacita *mapaa-pa*. Kufwumbwa natali similimo balamu-tambula. = In the past parents did not want to have their daughter married to a lazy man. Today they give her away easily. Anyone, even if not a hard worker, is accepted by them.
holes pl. of impako-mpako, e.g. *Musamu oyu ngwamapako-pako*. = The tree has holes.
the skin removed, as from a potatoe, e.g. Kosanina ngulube *mapale* azwa kuzitende. = Feed the pigs with pumpkin skins.

clay plates, e.g. Manyina alabajikila bana musozya wanyangu mumalongo. Basika biyo balazuzya *mapali*. The mothers cook samp mixed with beans in clay pots for the children. As soon as they arrive they fill the clay plates.
edible water-lily tubers, pl. of impana, e.g. Muzyiba omu kuli *mapana manji*. In this pool there are a lot of edible water-lily tubers.
the clearing or field where trees have been cut, e.g. Kono tuyaku-syanga ndongwe zyesu *mumapande*. = This year we are going to plant ground-nuts in the field which has been cleared of trees.
the distinctive white patch on the forehead of an animal, e.g. Musune wangu ulaa *mapande*. = My ox has a distinctive white patch on the forehead. Also *cipande, kaama*
planks, split wattles, e.g. Muyaki uula *mapandula* aciluli cananda. = The builder is buying planks for the roof of the house.
pl. of ipanga/cipanga (a panga or machete), e.g. Bantu bagonka minsale ku Mazabuka babelesya *mapanga*. = The sugar-cane cutters at Mazabuka use pangas.
skin, shell, slough, a snake's cast skin e.g. Imbooma yakaliyupula *mapapa*. = A boa-constrictor has sloughed it's skin. *Mapapa amaji* = egg shells. Also *mapopo*
pawpaws, e.g. Mukuwa ujisi misamu *yamapapaya* minji mumbewu yakwe. = The white man has many paw-paw trees in his garden.
pl. of ipaso, an entry permit, Bantu bamucisi cimbi tabakonzyi kunjila mucisi cesu kakunyina *mapaso*. = Foreigners cannot enter our country without entry-permits.
socket of hip-joint, *Mapaso* alacisa, nsekonzyi kweenda kabotu. = My hip-joint is painful, I cannot walk properly. Also impaso.
an edible grasshopper, e.g. Bantu bamwi balalya mpaso. = Some people eat grasshoppers.

blankets, pl. of ipayi, e.g. Ciindi camupeyo mapayi alayandika kapati. = During the cold season blankets are greatly needed. Bantu baabi bapa mapayi kubacete. Generous people give blankets to the poor.
pl. of ipe, an empty bee-comb, e.g. Inzuki zyakabunywa buci, kwakacaala mape alo. The bees finished the honey, only the empty combs remain.
leprosy, itch, e.g Bantu baciswa mapele balasilikwa kabotu mazubaano. People who have leprosy these days are well treated. Also cinanta, cinsenda

imprint, sign, e.g. Baleli besu ubabone sunu ameso aako aayo obile. Uleke kubabonena atalaa mapeni aa galaba. May you see our leader today with those two eyes of yours. May you stop only looking at him above the imprint of an ant-bear (on a Zambian coin)
pl. of ipenzi, suffering, e.g. Mazubaano boonse bantu bajisi mapenzi anzala. These days all the people feel the sufferings of hunger.
papers, pl. of ipepa (ety.Eng.), e.g. Mapepa akulembela akamana. = The papers for writing on are finished.
pl. of ipepe, a feather or quill, e.g. Bamwi bayuni bajisi mapepe mabotu. = Some birds have beautiful feathers.
ears of sorgum with little grain, e.g. Maila muceme taali kabotu, mmapese alo. = Sorgum is not good, the ears have little grain.
a rope made out of fibre or sisal, e.g. Kamubaanga boombe amapese. = Tie the calves with fibre ropes.

fake money, also mali akulibambila mapesi ears of sorgum with little grain, e.g. Buyuni bwakaamana maila, bwakasiya mapesi alo. The birds finished off the sorgum, they left only ears with little grain. Also mapese, masenga.
tributes, pl. of lupeto, e.g. Bantu bakali kupa mapeto kumwami kutondezya bulemu. The people were paying tributes to the chief to show respect.
pills, pl. of ipiilusi (ety.Eng.), e.g. Bamwi bapegwa mapiilusi mucibbadela. Some are given pills at the hospital.
spots, e.g. Chidaala ujisi mapika mubili onse, antela wabaa cinanta. = Chidaala has spots all over the body, perhaps he has become leperous.

the temples, (the flat part either side of the head between the forehead and ears.) e.g. Akaambo kamapenzi, mukaintu wakwe wakacaazya mapobe. Bacause of problems, his wife became thin in the temples. Also mpobe
a borassus palm-tree, e.g. Basokwe bakkala mumapokwe. = The monkeys live in a borassus palm-tree. Also cipamba.
pawpaws Also mupapaya.

a commotion, riots, e.g. Kwakacitika mapiliipili ataambiki, kasuko taakwe nikakamana kusikila buzuba bwakainda dilwe. There arose a great commotion, the dust did not settle until the day the funeral ended.
pl. of iponda, a big stick, e.g. Basimpongo bakavwimbuula mwingile amaponda mapati. The goatherds whipped a warthog with big sticks. =
British bank mapondo-mapondo notes of £1. e.g. Nobaimba boobu kumwi ku milomo bakalumide camapondo-mapondo. As they were singing like this they were biting many pound notes in their mouths.
pl. of ipoopo, fresh shells of groundnuts, e.g. Balya ndongwe zya*mapoopo*. = They are eating the fresh shells of ground nuts.
pl. of ipopo, a pawpaw, e.g. *Mapopo alanona kapati*. = Pawpaws are delicious.

pl. of ipopwe/cipopwe, mealie-cob in sheath unhusked, e.g. *Mapopwe ncecakulya cipati ca Batonga*. = Maize is the staple food of the Batonga. *mapopwe matete* = corn on the cob still fresh; *mapopwe amuwa* = shelled maize
pl. of ipulanga, a plank, e.g. *Mudeene wakaula mapulanga mabotu*. = Mudeene bought good planks.
pl. of ipunga, a lung, e.g. *Ingulube yafwa yajisi bukoto mumapunga*. = The pig which died has spots on the lungs.
pl. of ipupwa, a lung, e.g. *Mapupwa anombe mmauba-uba*. = The lungs of a cow are light. Also *mapunga*
vanity, conceit, e.g. *Muntu ulaa mapuwo tajisi balongwe*. = A proud person has no friends. Also *kulilumbaizya, kulilumbilizya, kulidunda*.
pl. of ipusi, a pumpkin, e.g. *Bamaama bajika kale mapusi*. = My mother has already cooked the pumpkins.

the second stage of the funeral ritual among the Valley Tonga, which takes place a few weeks later. Relatives of the deceased pour ritual-beer on the grave as an offering to the ancestral spirits. Afterwards the beer is shared among the mourners. e.g. *Bantu banywa bukoko bwamapwaila*. = The people are drinking the ritual-beer a few weeks after first stage of the funeral. Also *mweesyo*
frivolity, e.g. *Tiikwakali kwiide kucita mapwapwaapwa ku malende*. = There was no playing around at the rain shrine. Also *masesya*
big drops of rain, e.g. *Nicakamana cikulamabwe, wakatalika mapwatapwata amvwula*. = When the hailstones finished, there started big drops of rain.
cut firewood left to dry, heaps of felled trees, e.g. *Masaba abacembele abbigwa*. = The cut firewood left by my grandmother got stolen. Also *matoba*

the second return of the wife to her parents home, e.g. *Koomulombwana nabwiinga wakazikwaawona mazuba one nkabela alimwi wakabweeda kwabo. Oku kubweeda kwiitwa kuti masaba*. = The bride slept at the boy's place for four days and then returned to her parents. This return is called *masaba*.

an unfriendly spirit which enters people making them ill. There are many different types of *masabe*. Each can be driven out by the relevant drumrhythm, song and dance, which is the remedy to the particular type of possession. e.g. *Ino nkuli kulila ngoma zyamasabe*? = Where are the *masabe* drums being beaten?

a set of three drums which were used on the north bank of the Zambezi by the Goba and Korekore: 1. *Musindo*, *miningilo*, 2. *Nyaluo*, *ngoma hulu*, 3. *Mpanje*, *mubandalikwa*. *Musindo* is a pedestal drum similar to the smaller *badima* drum and was beaten with a stick; *mpanje* was a long straight-sided cylinder-drum or pole-drum, and *nyaluo* is a smaller type of *mpanje*.
pl. of *isaka*, a sack,a bag, e.g. *Masaka azwide mapopwe akapya*. = The bags full of maize got burnt.
a dense forest, e.g. *Syuumbwa ulalila mumasaka*. = The lion is growling in the thick forest.
charms or medicines used by witches, magic, e.g. *Ikucapa* kwakwe teesyi kwamasimpe, nkwamasalamuzi. = His witch-finding is not genuine, it has to do with magic.
a magician, e.g. Ijilo kwakaswaide simasalamuzi acikolo cesu. = Yesterday there arrived a magician at our school.
light showers preceeding fine weather or when the rain is easing off, e.g. Bantu batalika kweenda amasalazyizyo amvwula. = The people have started to walk when the rain was just finishing.
supports, e.g. Koleta masalazyizyo tutabye ciluli cabutala. = Bring supports so that we can prop up the roof of the maize-bin.
tender mealie-cobs, e.g. Mapopwe taaningabizwa acili masalesale. = The maize had not fully ripened, it is still at the tender stage (and one has to choose with care to select a suitable one.)
a ticklish spot under ribs, e.g. Muntu taumwi mumasa-masa inga wafwa. = A person is not beaten on the ticklish spot under the ribs as s/he may die. Also mumasa, mumateku or munategu, citeku
tea-leaves, e.g. Kamuleta masamba tubambe tiyi. = Bring the tealeaves so that we make tea.
grass-bracelets, e.g. Masambo mumakonokono avwulisya. = The grass-bracelets from ankle to knee (or wrist to elbow) were plentiful.
biltong, (nyama yakayanikwa; mitendu miyumu)
disgrace, e.g. Ncibi kulicenjezya akati kabeenzinyoko nkaambo ciletela masampu. = It is bad to make oneself clever in all things among friends because it brings disgrace.
insolence, e.g. Musimbi ulaa masampusi takwatwi pe. = A girl full of insolence does not get married.
what brings disgrace, rt. masampu, e.g Kweenda aukolwa mmasampuzyo buyo. = To go about with a drunkard causes disgrace.
changes in life style, e.g. Muntu wamasandu-masandu tasyomeki. = A person who changes life style frequently is untrustworthy.

a type of grass for matmaking, e.g. Kamuleta masanga tuluke munseme. = Bring grass so that we weave a mat. Munanga wakaambila Chikupu kuti bayandaule cuulu cijisi masangasanga mayumu. = The witchdoctor told Chikupu that they should search for an ant-hill which had a certain type of grass.
big cigarettes, e.g. Muntu ulya ufweba masanga mapati. = That man smokes big cigarettes.

globular seed-pods tied to legs when dancing, e.g. Wakatamba abasimbi basikwiimba akucaca bakalibambila amasangu-sangu, nsakalala amuunde. = She invited girls for singing and rattling who prepared themselves globular seed-pods tied to the legs, handrattles and perfume. Also masebelele.
fruit from musangu tree, eaten by cattle, e.g. Inombe zilacela mumasangusangu. = Cattle eat fruits from the musangu tree.

last ceremonies of marriage, e.g. Nabwiinga ukkalikila lyamana masansa. = The bride takes up permanent residence after the last ceremonies of the marriage. 'Kusowa masansa' bamwi balati 'nkuzyola matende' antela 'nkupilula matende' amusimbi kuya kwabo. = 'Kusowa masansa' some say means the retracing of the footsteps of the bride to her original family home. (after three days staying with her new husband).
protruding cheeks, e.g. Bamwi bantu balijisi masanta mbuli kuti baciswa cimbolomu. = Some people have protruding cheeks as if they were suffering from the mumps.

the custom of killing many beasts at the funeral of a rich man, e.g. *Kubaanga obu buzuba bwamasantu mbobuzuba basidilwe mbobakali kuyandisisya.* = It seems that for the mourners, this day of the killing of beasts was the one they liked most.
platforms made of timber, e.g. *Mapopwe abikkwa mumasanza twamana kutebula.* = The maize is put on the wooden platforms when we have finished harvesting.
branches, e.g. *Wakaciyakila kabotu alubaya Iwamasanzo amoomfwenene.* = She fenced it well with branches of the *moofwenene* tree.
pl. of *isanzu*, a cut-off branch, e.g. *Kamusinka masanzu ainda nombe.* = Close (the place) where cattle pass with cut-off branches.

a disease which afflicts an unborn baby, alleged to be contracted when the mother walks through a crossroads where other parents have enacted a ritual to deliver their child from a disease which is said to remain at the crossroads and can affect the pregnant mother's baby whom she carries. e.g. *Mwana uciswa masanzya ulakatazya kusilika.* = The unborn baby suffering from the disease (known as *masanzya*) is difficult to cure.
pl. of *lusasa*, a mat, e.g. *Baama bayanika mimena amasasa.* = My mother is drying the yeast on mats.
a puff-adder, pl. of *cisasa*, e.g. *Cisasa ninzoka ilaa bunete bunji.* = The puffadder is a snake which has a lot of poison.
sour milk, e.g. *Ooyu mukupa aba kale masase.* = This milk has already become sour.
sparks, pl. of *insasi*, e.g. *Makwa*
masasi manji.* = The barks contain many sparks.

fruit of the Tamarind tree, e.g. *Bakali kutwa masau mpoona bavwela meenda caba citobolo banywa.* = They were pounding the fruit of the Tamarind tree and then mixing it with water to become *citobolo* for drinking.
pl. of *isaya*, the cheek, e.g. *Mwana uneneede ujisi masaya mapati.* = A fat child has big cheeks.
husks, e.g. *Mase abukoko alalula.* = The husks of beer are bitter.
leg rattles
pl. of *iseese*, a marvel, miracle, e.g. *Jesu wakali kucita maseese manji.* = Jesus worked many miracles.
lies, e.g. *Mutamumvwi oyo, ulaa maseese.* = Don't believe that one, he tells lies. (Valley Tonga)
pl. of *iseka*, wire ornaments for the legs, e.g. *Mooye oyu usamide maseka mumaulu.* = This girl wears wireornaments on the legs.
coarse meal left after pounding, e.g. *Busu obu bujisi maseke.* = This meal is coarse. Also *inseke, maando*
a cheetah, e.g. *Masekese uvwula kapati muzibaka mugwetukide.* = The cheetah likes the wide open spaces. Also *malama*.
a type of tree, pl. of *musekese*, e.g. *Loozi Iwamusekese taluli luyumu.* = Fibre from the *musekese* tree is not strong enough.
things that cause laughter, e.g. *Eeyi nkamu ilaa masekesyo ataambiki.* = This group is full of unimaginable amusement. Also. *masesya*

poles inserted between others already fixed, pl. *isekete* (roof pole), e.g. *Kamuleta maseketi tusekkelele ciluli.* = Bring poles so that we insert them in the roof. *Wisi naya musyokwe kukutema maseketi, mwana wakwe mulo-*
ulatobela. = When the father goes into the bush to cut poles, his son follows.
black and white-haired cattle, e.g. *Sena nombe yako njama-sekwe?* = Is your cow black and white-haired?
milk of new mother, e.g. *Kamwiikama masema nombe yazyala ino.* = Milk off the new milk from the cow which has just given birth.
crushed grains of maize, e.g. *Ndakakkala munsi-munsi ampubakali kuseba masembe bamaama.* = I sat near where my mother was sifting the crushed maize-grains.
burrows, lairs, dens, e.g. *Babwa balalumwa mumasempo amazoka.* = Dogs are bitten in burrows by snakes.
a vlei, swampy ground, marsh, e.g. *Inombe zicelela mumasena.* = The cattle graze in the vleis.
places, e.g. *Masena acikolo amana, pesi bambi bacinjila.* = The places at the school are finished, but some are still being accepted.

pl. of isenda, a large grub found in the ground and in trees and eat-en by the Valley Tonga (variation lisenda,) e.g. *Ingulube zilaayanda masenda.* = Pigs like large grubs. *Bakapona kulya masenda, abauka bamwi.* = They survived on insects known as *masenda* (large white maggots found in cow manure) and grubs and other insects.

speech to one person which is meant for another who is present, indirect or hidden way of conveying a message to another, e.g. *Kwaamba cigaminina, ncibotu kwiinda masendelela.* = It is better to speak directly instead of through hidden talk. *Masendelela mma-ambi-lambali, ntusimpi, mmafwiinsya-makani. Mmilongo yamajwi mifwiifwi, iipandulula makani manji.* = Masendelela are: maambila-mbali, tusimpi, mafwiinsya-makani. The lists of words are short, they convey much information.
indirect way of speaking Also masendelela.
Also masendelela.
