old baskets, pl. of isengele/cisengele, e.g. *Mabango angu naakaajosya akaba masengele.* = When my baskets were returned they were worn out.
kicks, pl. of musengele, e.g. *Inombe yanduuma masengele akuulu.* = The cow gave me a kick using the leg. Also misembele, milazyi.
galvanized iron-sheets, e.g. *Bavwubi baona mumaanda amasenke.* = Rich people sleep in houses with iron roofing.
pl. of cisenketi, a shelled mealie-cob, e.g. *Bantu bajisya masenketi.* = People cook using shelled mealie-cobs for the fire. Also cinkonti
a secret, e.g. *Kulibambila kwabo kwakali kwamaseseke.* = Their preparation was done in secret. *Akali maseseke akwe alikke.* = It was his secret alone.
laughter, mirth, e.g. *Musimbi oyu ngwamaseya.* = This girl is amusing.
jokes, antics, e.g. *Muntu ulaa masesyo ulakondelezya.* = A comical person amuses.
pl. of cisi, land, country, region, e.g. *Masi aa Bukuwa alatontola kapati.* = The lands of white people are cold.
rubbish, e.g. *Mwana wawa mumulindi wamasifwi-sifwi.* = The child fell into a rubbish-pit.
late morning, day-time, e.g. *Mweenzu wangu wakasika masikati.* = My visitor came during the daytime.
mosquito-net, e.g. *Mwana walumwa mansenya nkaambo kunyina masiketa.* = The child is bitten by mosquitoes because there is no mosquitonet. Also lusabwi Iwamansenya
refuse of winnowed sorgum, e.g. Kamutola masiki muciba zilye nombe. = Take the refuse of winnowed sorgum for the cattle to eat in the kraal
diseases e.g Malwazi asunu alajaya. = The diseases of nowadays kill.
night-time, e.g. Impongo zyesu zyabbigwa masiku. Our goats were stolen at night.
heaps of burnt ashes in a field. e.g. Mapopwe angu akakomena kabotu mumasilibi. My maize has grown well in the heaps of burnt ashes.
the remains in a pipe after smoking, e.g. Ifwuko yangu izwide masilila. My pipe is full of the remains of tobacco. Also mulende
a mirage, e.g. Masilikiti alibonya mumigwagwa alagambya. = The mirage which is seen on the roads is amazing.
heaps of burnt ashes in a field, e.g. Kamuya mukamwaye masilisi mumuunda. = Go and scatter the heaps of burnt ashes in the field. Also masilibi
charcoal for forge, e.g. Komupa masimbi mufwuzi akufwulile jamba. = Give the blacksmith charcoal so that he forges a hoe for you.
the end, e.g. Masimpilo abuzumi buno ndufwu. = The end of this life is death.
sticky sap, gum of tree, pl. of busina (pus), e.g. Cilonda eci cizwa masina. There is a lot of pus coming from this wound.
a necklass of beads, roots or grass worn by suckling mother.
a coarse kind of grass near rivers, e.g. Kuli masinde manji mumbembelekwa amulonga. There is a lot of coarse grass along the bank of the river.
newly tilled land, e.g. Tuyakusaanguna kusyanga mapopwe mumasinde. We are first going to plant maize in the newly tilled land.

pl. of cisinka mulomo, a bribe, e.g. Mubetesi upegwa masinka-mulomo ncatabeteki kabotu. = The judge is given bribes that is why he does not work properly. Kupa cisinkamulomo nkuzyiba kaambo. = To bribe somebody is to admit you are guilty.
pl. of isinsi, a skirt, e.g. Amwi mafwumofwumo kwaimpana masinsi kuzya kwangu. One morning there was a swishing of skirt coming to my house.
dregs, pl. of busiwa, e.g. Amundipe masiwa nkasanine ngulube.
kutia masiwa abukoko. Give me the dregs so that I feed the pigs. The goats will die if they eat the dregs of the beer. Also mansiwa
pl. of isizi, an ember, e.g. Kobikka masizi kumitwe abulo kuti kolota bubi. Put (dead) embers at the head of your bed if you have nightmares.
pl. of cisobano, a play, e.g. Kuli masobano manji sunu kucikolo. = There are many games today at the school. (pl. also zisobano, misobano)
roofing poles, pl. of isomo, e.g. Basankwa bakaleta masomo mabotu. = The boys have brought good roofing poles.
wild fruit yielding oil, e.g. Basikale bakali kubamba mafwuta a masomvwa. The ancestors were making oil from wild fruits.
redness, e.g. Wakaula cisani camasomvwa. = She bought a red dress.
canine teeth, pl. of isongonyama, e.g. Chimuka tatafwuni kabotu nkaambo masongonyama alacisa. = Chimuka does not chew well because the canine teeth are hurting him.
thorny fruits, e.g. Mumuunda omu kuli masonso tamweendwi kabotu. = In this field there are thorny fruits which make it difficult to pass through.
socks, pl. of isookesi (ety. Eng.), e.g. *Baiyi bajisi masookesi mayumu.* = The teacher has strong socks.

A sickness in the baby due to a parent's extra-marital sexual relationships, e.g. *Mwana wakwe wakafwa masoto akaambo kakweenda.* = His child died from a disease attributed to the promiscuity of one of the parents.

a traditional medicine used in pregnancy, e.g. *Mukaintu uli mumwezi wa Namulela ulabelesya antela kunywa musamu wamasoto kutegwa mwana uli mwida atanyani. (Mwana ucili mwida ulakonzya kuciswa masoto nokuba kuti bazyali bakwe kunyina bumpelenge mbubeendana.)* = A pregnant woman in her seventh month uses or drinks the traditional medicine for *masoto* to prevent the baby within her from shriveling up. (The child in the womb can suffer from the *masoto* disease even though the parents have not been cheating one another by having other illicit sexual relationships.)

wild loquat fruit, e.g. *Basimbi bacela masuku mulusukwe.* = The girls are collecting wild loquat fruit among the *masuku* trees. *Masuku mmanono, pele mbula zilanunkilila.* *Masuku* fruit is sweet, but *mbula* fruit has a pleasant smell. *Basimbi bakafwunka zibunge zyambula zyakulya nobalima. Masuku balakanda mumukupa, amwi balatafwuna.* = The girls make cakes of *mbula* fruit which they eat while ploughing. They knead the *masuku* into the milk, while they chew some. *Masuku alaloka ansi naabizwa, basinombe balatanta mumisuku ciindi canzala kukucela masuku* = Wild loquat fruits fall off when ripe, the cattle herders climb into the loquat trees during the time of hunger to gather the fruit.
coagulated lumps, e.g. *Kamundiletela masuma abulongo.* = Bring me coagulated lumps of clay.
pl. of *isumo*, a spear, e.g. *Kamuleta masumo tujaye munyama.* = Bring the spears so that we kill the animal.
bamboos, pl. of *musumpo*, e.g. *Wakaide kuya murjanda wasalama abulo bwamasumpo.* He just went into the house and lay down on a bed of bamboos.
spears, e.g. *Masumu amudaala mmabotu.* = The spears of the old man are good. Also *masumo*.
wild fruits Also *mafwumu*
a type of wild fruit, e.g. *Bana balya masunka munzila.* = Children eat wild fruit on the way.

cattle killed at a funeral, e.g. *Muntu muvwubi ujailwa nombe zinji zyamasuntu.* = Many cattle are killed at the funeral of a rich person. *Bamwi bantu ambweni balayeeya kuti eyo nyama nciitegwa masuntu nkaambo bantu balaisuntula akwiitola muminzi yabo.* = The reason why some people think that this meat is called *masuntu* is that some of this meat is taken away by the mourners. (*kusuntuka* = fall down from fits. It refers to animals being slaugtered in great number - falling down as if they were having fits) The skin of the first beast killed was used to wrap the corpse for burial.
fits, e.g. *Muntu ulaa masuntu tayelede kuloba alikke.* = A person who gets fits ought not to fish alone.

hair on the head, pl. of *isusu*, a hair, e.g. *Masusu abakaintu mmalamfwu.* = The hair of women is long. *Cikuba camasusu* = plaited hair; *insuki* = hair as smeared with red ochre; *cisumpa* = a tuft of hair; *civwuma or insuku* = hair gathered into a cone, *lukuka* = hair around the base of the cone.
a lock or curl of hair Also muntiki
the heaps which whiteants make, pl. of cisuumbwa, e.g. Kuli masuumbwa mumusena. There are mounds made by white-ants in the vlei. Also -cuumbusu, pl. zyuumbusu
the three stones which make up the fire-place, pl. of isuwa, e.g. Cikko cijisi masuwa otatwe. = The fireplace has three stones (for holding the pot.)
lumps at back of head, e.g. Masowe akomena masuwa kumakosi akwe. = The lumps behind Masowe's head are growing.
a type of caterpillar, found on mopane trees in November.
cross-roads, bifurcation, e.g. Ndabasiya amaswaangano anzila. = I left them at the crossroads.
roots for making sweetbeer, e.g. Cibwantu camasyaabe cilanona. = Sweet-beer made from the masyaabe roots is delicious. Also masyabe.

roots from which sweet-beer is made, e.g. Bamwi basimbi bakaunkide musyokwe kuya kusya masyabe a munkoyo a mulalansana wakukumbila kamwale cibwantu. = Some girls had gone into the bush to dig out masyabe, munkoyo and mulalansana roots for brewing sweet-beer for the initiated girl. Also masyaabe.

dress for dancing. e.g. Wakaaanga masyamba, pesi kuzyana takacizyi. Mmagwaza. (a riddle) = She dressed herself in dancing costumes, but does not know how to dance. It is the whole grains of cooked-maize. Also mayaamba
big boys, e.g. Kwakali kunga bana nobatalika kwiiya nkujana masyankwa alindilila kubanyonganya. = It happened that when the children began to learn there were big boys waiting to disturb them.
fishing-baskets, pl. of isyiko, e.g. Bakaintu bazezya masyiko. = Women fish with fishing-baskets. Also moono.
inside cavities of nose, e.g. Kalinda ulaa masyono asiya. Kalinda has black nostrils.
nasal cartilages and bones, e.g. Muntu uciswa syini masyonyo alacisa. = The interior of the nose of a person with a cold is sore.
excrement, e.g. Masyu ankuku alanunka kapati. Chicken-excrement stinks a lot. Also maziu.
last rain, e.g. Mvwula yamamanino mumwaka itegwa masyulampeyo. The last rain at the end of the year is called masyulampeyo.
fruit of the masyuuntwa tree, e.g. Bamwi bantu balakumba bukoko bwamasyuuntwa. = Some people brew beer from the fruits of the masyuuntwa tree. Also masumo, mafwumu

scattered in speech or endless mobility, e.g. Ucita matabanta-tabanta kukanana. Akaaka waamba, akaaka waamba. Kunyina acomwe ncindamvwa cilaa matwi. = You are too scattered in your talking. You say this, you say that. There is not a single thing I hear which has sense.
foul language, e.g. Muntu ujisi mulaka wamatabweyabwe ulalwanisya. A person who uses foul language causes fights.
the buttocks, pl. of itako, e.g. Mukaintu ulya ujisi matako mapati. = That woman has big buttocks.
the beginning, e.g. Matalikilo abuumi buno nkumitwa. = The beginning of this life is being conceived.
large clay containers for brewing beer, e.g. Bukoko buli mumatalo bubila kabotu. = The beer in the big clay containers is fermenting well.
pl. of intamba, a big wild orange, e.g. Basokwe balya *matamba* mumulundu. = The monkeys eat the big wild oranges on the hill.
a ladder or stairs, e.g. Kamundipa *matambikilo* twaanzike nyama. = Give me the ladder to hang up the meat. Also malele.
harness for horse or donkey. e.g. Twakajana mbongolo zyaangidwe *matambotambo*. = We found the ass harnessed.
pl. of lutanda, a log of wood, firewood, e.g. Adilwe bantu bakkala a *matanda*. = At a funeral people sit on logs of wood.
pl. of butanga, a herd of cattle, e.g. Kuli *matanga* manji aņombe mumusena. = There are many herds of cattle in the vlei.
water-melons which are less watery, pl. of itanga, e.g. Mumuunda wangu kwakazyalwa *matanga* alo. = In my field only water-melons which aren't so watery have been produced. Also *matanga* syokoli
mud with high water content, e.g. Akali *matapya*. = There was watery mud. Also mankandya
our forefathers, e.g. Anu ndiswe bani kukonzya kucinca malailile a *matatakulu*? = And who are we to be able to change the directives of our forefathers?
tires, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Namutekenya wakaula *matayila* mapya. = The driver bought new tires.

saliva, spittle, e.g. Koleka kuswida *mate* munanda, watusesemya. = Stop spitting in the house, you disgust us. Mate aali mujanza aumwa akanwe inga lyoonse atapukila kulubazu lwatozya nombe zisweekede. = When the spittle in the palm of your hand is struck by the little finger it will always jump out on the side to where the cattle have gone.
bantu bakaile kubula *mate* mukanwa. = All the people had no spittle in the mouth, i.e. they were astounded or dumbfounded.

blankets, pl. of itebwe, e.g. Bazyali nibamana kubbadela mali kumuzuluzi wacikolo, bana balapegwa mab buku akubala akulembela, zisamo, mbede *amatebwe* azintu zili boobo zyakubelesya mucikolo. = When the parent have finished paying money to the administrator of the school, the children are given books to read and to write in, uniforms, dishes and blankets and things like that for using at school. Also mapayi
a special kind of grass, e.g. ņombe zilaayanda *matebe*. = The cattle like a special grass called *matebe*.

the side of an animal's or person's body, the flank, e.g. Mwiiyi naakakolwa, bakamuuma nkoli *mumateku*. = When the teacher got drunk, they beat him with sticks on the sides of the body. Also ziteku, masa-masa
ticklish spot under the ribs, swelling in right side of abdomen, flanks, e.g Utandijati *mumategu*, ndilaa bunyeele. = Don't catch me under the ribs, I am ticklish.
plans, e.g. *Matelaisi* akavwula mumoyo wakwe akuyandaula nzila mbotu yakufwutula mukaintu oyu. = His heart was full of plans of finding a good way of saving this woman.
relish, (sing. itelele) e.g. Mupweepwe *amatelele* amwi akayuma mumyuunda yabo. = Mupweepwe and other types of relish had withered in their fields.

pl. of intema, a clearing in forest for new field, a private field, e.g. Kamuumpa *matema* mumuunda. = Burn off the clearings that has been made in the field. Ndakausyanga kale muunda wa-*matema* angu. = I have already planted a field which I own personally.
unmarried women, e.g. Mumunzi mwa Choombe kuli matema manji. = In Choombe's village there are many unmarried women.
See matema.
pl. of citeo, a thicket, bush, e.g. Katubweza maamba tukagonke *mateo*. = Take the hoes so that we go and hack out the bushes. Also matewo, mavwuna.
pl. of lutete/itete, a reed, e.g. *Matete* ngotulusya zisuwo aminseme. = We use reeds in weaving baskets and mats.
pl. of itende, a footprint, a foot, e.g. Ndabona *matende* amuntu wabba. = I have seen the footprints of the one who has stolen.
cutlery, (what is used for cutting up, rt. -tenda.) e.g. Kamubikka *matenzyo* balisye bamakuwa. = Put out the cutlery for the white people to eat with.
front teeth, e.g. Syuumbwa ujisi ma*tenzyo* mapati ngatyoloozya zifwuwa. = A lion has massive front teeth with which he breaks up the bones.
bushes, e.g. *Matewo* mumuunda akasyuuka. = The bushes in the field have sprouted. Also *mateo*.
a refuge, e.g. Kucikolo cilakonzya kuba *matijilo* abana batolo. = The school can be a refuge for lazy children.
tricks, (Eng. ety.) e.g. Mutinta wakali kucita buyo *matilikisi*. = Mutinta was just playing tricks. Also mampyaampya

a mixture of boiled fermented and non-fermented mealies but not yet made into beer, e.g. *Matimba* abukoko alanona. = A mixture of fermented and non-fermented meal is delicious. Buzuba bwakali kunyugwa *matimba* bamwi banabokwabo bakafwuma kubuka. = The day when this mixture was drunk, some of the family got up early.
large juicy fat termites, e.g. Kumwaka notujata *matingatiila*. = In November we catch large juicy 'flying ants.' Also matingi-tingi.
large juicy fat termites, e.g. Bamwi bantu tabaalyi *matingitingi*. = Some people do not eat the large juicy fat termites. Also *matingatiila*.
pl. of itinti, a spring forming a morass, e.g. *Mumatinti* tucela syaasyipa mutete. = We collect the fresh blackjack plant in the swampy ground.
mud, mire, e.g. Mwakandizwisya *mumatipa*. = You took me out of the mud. Also mankandya.
pl. of bwato, a boat, e.g. Bazeli babelesya *mato* nobazela bakapenta. = Fishermen use boats when they are netting kapenta fish.
heaps of firewood left for drying, e.g. Bantu bakabba *matoba* angu jilo. = Some people stole my heaps of firewood yesterday. Also masaba
'monkey apples', fruit of *mutobo* tree, e.g. Amwi *matobo* taanoni pe. = Some monkey apples are not sweet.

a fruit which unfolds revealing all that is inside, e.g. Mebo ndi mbuli *matobo*, mbubona busyinyukide *matobo* mbwembede, kunyina ncesisa pe. = Myself I am like a *matobo* fruit, just as a *matobo* fruit unfolds revealing what is inside, that is how I am, I hide nothing.
waggons e.g. Umwi musyobo wamalasha nguyuuya uukonzya kubonwa *mumatoloko* aacitima kutobelezya njanji. = One type of coal is the one you can see in the trucks of a train which follows the railway.
carriages, e.g. Mutwe wacitima ulakwela *matolokesi* aajisi bantu antela mpasya. = The locomotive pulls the carriages which have people or goods.

shelters, e.g. Mumazuba ayo balombe bakasaanguna kubabelekela basimbi nobayakubakwata. Bakayaka magazi, *matombo*, amilimo imwi. = In those days the boys first worked for the women before they married them. They build look-out huts on supports, shelters, and other works.
drops, e.g. Imvwula yaleta *matombo-tombo* buyo, tiiyawa. = The rain only brought isolated drops, it did not rain. Also mandoondo.
maize planted late, e.g. Mapopwe *amatompo* alalweela kuyoka. = The late maize is sweet to roast. Also namutompo, mutompo.
pl. of *itomu*, a bridle, e.g. Amubabikke *matomu* basune baleke kucela. Put bridles on the oxen so that they stop grazing.

a type of wild fruit, e.g. Mu Zambezi balasakwida mapopwe a mbuto zimwi nzibalima mainza. Ciindi eci balalya *matondo*. In the Zambezi valley they weed the maize and other crops which they plant during the rains. At that time they eat *matondo* wild fruit.
ruins, deserted village, pl. *itongo*, e.g. Kamukkala awa kuleka ku-*matongo*. Stay here instead of in a deserted village.
complaints, pl. of *itongoosi*, e.g. Muntu oyu ujisi *matongoosi*
This person has the complaints of a child.
rheum, e.g. Bana batalyi *amatongwe* kumeso antovolomu kumilomo yabo. Do not let the children eat with rheum in their eyes and froth on their mouths.
a white variety of sorgum, e.g. Okuno tulima *matuba* kuleka maila asubila. Here we plant white sorgum not the red variety.
a swollen head, e.g. Kalwalo ujisi *matukukutu* mumutwe, bakamuuma. Kalwalo has a swollen head, they beat him. Also inzunzu
old stored maize, e.g. Ndiyandaula mapopwe *matumba* abukoko. = I am searching for old stored maize for beer.
a type of grass for matmaking or for making salt from ashes, e.g. Amukalete *matumbu* tulusye zizongo. = Bring the kind of grass so that we can make baskets with hooking handles.
suckling mothers, e.g. *Bamatumbu* banjila ino mukunyonsya bana. = The suckling mothers have just come in to suckle their babies.

good luck charms, bones, roots etc. found in a witch-doctor's house. e.g. Mukaanda kamusilisi mwakali nsengo, *matumwa*, miyanda minji atufwuwa. = In the house of the healer there were horns, charms, many roots and bones.

pl. of *citungu*, a temporary hut in a field, e.g. Bayamina bayaka ma-*tungu*. The ones chasing away birds build temporary huts. Mantoombwa ncinzi? Mantoombwa *mmatungu*, nintuntu. = What is mantoombwa? Matoombwa are temporary huts, they are walless shelters. Bakali kwiiya kuyaka maanda antela *matungu* aakuyusila mvwula kuti yatalika kuwa kabali musyokwe. They were learning to build houses or shelters to shelter from the rain if it begins to fall when they are in the bush. matunka-matunka scattered heaps of big pumpkins, stones etc. e.g. Mumuunda kuli *matunka-matunka* amabwe. = In this field there are scattered heaps of large stones.

pride, e.g. Nkubona onse ma-*tunta* ngubakajisi ciindi nobakali kukanana amana. All the pride which they had when they were talking was finished. Ooyu musankwa ulaa *matunta* nkaambo bausyi mbabainda buvwubi mumunzi. = *This boy is proud because his father is the richest in the village.*
pl. of *itusi*, a profane or insolent word, e.g. *Ncibi kubelesya matusi.* = It is bad to use foul language. *Balatukila matusi anunka nsu.* = They used foul stinking language.
pl. of *intuuntu*, simple houses build for girls playing at housekeeping, e.g. *Bakubusi bayaka matuuntu kumantoombwa.* = The youth build simple houses at the mantoombwa.
pl. of *ituvwu*, a leaf, e.g. *Matuvwu amisamu alakunkumuka.* = The leaves of the trees are falling off.
pl. of *lutwalo*, marriage, e.g. *Matwalo asunu taakkali ciindi.* = The marriages of today do not last long.
marriage, e.g. *Muntu mupati ulizyi tulengwa twamatwazi toonse mbotweelede kweenda.* = An elder knows all the marriage-customs as to how they should be performed.
ears, pl. of *kutwi*, e.g. *Muzovwu ujisi matwi mapati.* = The elephant has big ears.
barbs, arrows, e.g. *Matwi atulembe ajatila mukati kakayuni.* = The barbed arrows hook inside the bird.
pl. of *itwizya*, a blister, e.g. *Mwana ulaa matwizya akupya.* = The child has blisters from being burnt. Also buya.
pl. of *ityuntya*, a dead thing already swollen, e.g. *Inswi zyaba kale matyuntya tazikwe kuulwa.* = Fish which have already become swollen will not be sold. Also matunta
stripes, e.g. *Kaluwe kalaa maubi-maubi.* = A leopard has stripes.
pl. of *iguka*, a very large insect, e.g. *Kogusya mauka mumukupa.* = Take the insects out of the milk.
pl. of *kuulu*, a leg, e.g. *Maulu amunene alacisa.* = The legs of the old man are sore.
pl. of *cuumba*, a grub or red fly, e.g. *Munanda muli maumba, tamoonwi kabotu.* = In a house where there are grubs, there is no sleeping well.
butter, e.g. *Eeyi nsuwa ijisi maumba alula.* = This gourd has bitter butter.

akali kwiibululwa kabotu-kabotu akuyobolwa mumabbodela amuzigabba.* = The butter was carefully skimmed off and preserved in bottles and tins. *Mafwuta ajombe bakali kusuka kuti abe maumba.* = They used to shake the cream from the cattle so that it would become butter.
harvest-bug/jigger, pl. also bamaundu, e.g. *Maundu alacisa.* = The jiggers hurt. Also magundu, pl. of igundu,
pl. of muunda, a field, e.g. *Kamutola nombe kumaundu zikacele.* = Take the cattle to the fields to graze. cf. myuunda.
grazing-lands, e.g. *Mbelele ampongo zilatantaana nozisika mumaunga.* = The sheep and the goats scatter when they reach the grazing lands.
evening, e.g. *Izuba lyakali kale kumaungilo.* = It was already evening time.
an empty comb of bees, e.g. *Inzuki zyakaunka, zyakasiya buyo mauwe-uwe.* = The bees have gone, they have just left an empty comb of bees. Also mape.
a caterpillar, e.g. *Bantu bayoowa zyuuka balaatija amauwu.* = People who fear insects run also from caterpillars.
scratches, marks, e.g. *Aile kuba mavwalu-vwalu alo mucipepa.* = The paper just became scratched.

rumours, sensation, e.g. *Ncibi kubweza ntaamu akaambo* nkoomvwa buyo *mavwambukila*. = It is bad to take a step because you have just heard rumours. Kwakali *mavwambukila* akuti bamayi bamwi bakali bana kuli nguwe. = There were rumours that some of the teachers were younger than him. Haamwaandwe wakabona kuti *mavwam-bukila* akali mupepa libalwa, makani tanaakamutilimuna naaba aniini Lwando. = Haamwaandwe saw that the rumours which were in the newspaper did not make Lwando shiver in the slightest.

long garments, e.g. Bapaizi basama *mavweleende* malamfwu. = The priests wear long robes. Zikobela zyabwami nzyobasama bami ciindi nobaya kukubamba twaambo, *mmavweelende*. = The robes of power which the chiefs wear when they are settling affairs are long garments.
a cemetery, e.g. Bafwa ba-zikkilwa mumavwikko. = The dead are buried at the cemetery. Also namaumbwe
wheels, pl. of *ivwili*, e.g *Mavwili* ancinga taazinguluki. = The wheels of the bicycle do not rotate.

a layer of thick hair, e.g. Cida cakwe *camavwinda-mavwi-nda* aboya cakali kwiide kuyuna mucika-usu cakazapaukide ncaakasamide. = The big stomach with layers of thick hair was just visible through the torn vest which he was wearing.
peas, e.g. Bamakuwa bayanda kapati kulya *mavwinga*. = The whites like very much to eat peas.
pellets, small rounded objects, e.g. Mutani kuumani *mavwinga* abulongo mu-latowana. = It is bad to beat one another with pellets of clay, you will blind one another. Also *mavwunga*
pl. of *ivwo/imvwo*, wasp, e.g Andiluma *mavwo* ampemo. The wasps have stung me on the nose.

pl. of *ivwu*, soil, earth, e.g. Aaya *mavwu* alasubila. = This soil is red. *Ivwu lyalungutuka* = dry earth; *ivwu lya-bumbuluka* = loose earth *mavwuba* a bellows, e.g. Bafwuzi ba-vwukuta *mavwuba* nobafwula. = The blacksmiths blow the bellows when they are heating metals.
camping-site, e.g. Uulya mu-kambausi ngusimamambi, natukambau-kila bobuya *kumavwuka*. = That preacher is an adulterer, although he preaches to us at the camping site.
store-houses, silos, e.g. Mapopwe akamana mumavwulo aku Monze. The maize has finished in the silos at Monze.
growling, e.g. Syuumbwa ulaa *mavwulumo* ayoosya. = The lion has a terrible growl.
pl. of *imvwuma*, a big coconut borassus-palm, e.g. *Mavwuma* mmabotu kulya. = Big borassus-palm tree coconuts are good to eat. Also *muvwuma*

a cluster, e.g. Bakabona *mavwuna* amumbu, mpoona bakaleya batalika kulya mumbu. They saw a cluster of fruit-shrubs, thereupon they went aside and started eating the fruit. (they are like black cherries, close to the ground.)

hiding places for animals, e.g. *Mumavwumbuli* muli mazoka aluma mbelele, mpongo, nombe, mbo-ngolo ababwa. = In the animal dens there are snakes which bite sheep, goats, cattle, donkeys and dogs. Mubwa ulatu-yubununa tunyama *mumavwumbuli* mo-tujanwa. The dog reveals where ani-mals are to be found in their dens.
maggots, pl. of *imvwunyo*, e.g. Inyama yabola ijisi *mavwunyo* manji. = Meat which is rotten has plenty of maggots. Also *mavwunyu*
negligence, carelessness, e.g. Mukaintu mubaya ujika camavwunze. = A careless woman cooks poorly.

prostitution, prostitutes, e.g. Mazubaano bamavwuule balafwa kapati abulwazi bwasikalileke. = Nowadays prostitutes die very frequently from the disease of AIDS. Kaindi tiikwakali ma*vwuule*, ngomuti nywe 'matobela-njanji'. Kaindi basimbi tiibakali kuya munjanji akuyabuvwuula. = In the past there were no prostitutes, whom you call 'followers of the railway'. In the past girls did not go to the railway to become prostitutes. Also buvwuule.
waterfalls, e.g. Wakalikkede munsi *amavwuumina* aa KusyunguNamutitima. = She was sitting beside the waterfalls at Livingstone.
hair on lower part of abdomen or pubes, public hair, (taboo word) e.g. Bana tabajisi *mavwuzi*. = Children have no public hair.
fish-hooks, pl. of *iwezi*, e.g. Kalobo kangu kajisi *mawezi* mayumu. = My fishing-line has strong hooks.
pl. of *iwi*, small wild orange, e.g. Kaceta nkanyama kalya *mawi*. = The small monkey eats small wild oranges.
groundnuts without kernel, e.g. Ndakalima buyo ma*wowo andongwe*. = I have harvested empty groundnuts. Also *mapoopo*.
upper-class residential area, e.g. Bavwubi mbabakkala mumayaadi. = The rich people are the ones who live in upper-class residential areas.
a dancing belt made up of objects which jangle as one dances. e.g. Kamubungika mpiililyo tubambe *mayaamba*. = Gather together all the objects so that we make a dancing belt.
child born before eight-months pregnancy, pl. *bamayaba*, e.g. Ooyu mwana ngumayaba, ncatajisi nguzu. = This child was born prematurely that is why it is weak.

bad dreams, e.g. Ino nkaambo nzi ncolibonya mbuli muntu walaa *mayabwa-yabwa*. = Why is it that you seem to be like a person who has had nightmares. Tiindoona kabotu akaambo *kamayabwa-yabwa*. = I did not sleep well because of nightmares.
See *mayabwayabwa*.
buildings, e.g. Tatujisi *mayake* ayandika acikolo cesu. = We don't have the necessary buildings at our school.

a gynacological problem in women where the male sperm is said to be blocked from reaching the uterus, e.g. *Mayale* asinkila bulowa bwamusankwa kusika kucizyalilo. = *Mayale* blocks the sperm from reaching the uterus.
twins, e.g. Cimwi ciindi bana *bamayanga* balaa mambeke. = Sometimes twins are troublesome.
a type of dance, e.g. Bamacembele mbabacizyana *mayanze*. = The old women are the ones who still dance the *mayanze*.
means of doing something, e.g. Wakabulide *mayanzyo* akukonzya kutija. = He had no means of running away. Also *nguzu*
pl. of *ciyasauzyo*, instrument for making incisions, as on forehead, e.g. Kamuleta *mayasauzyo* tuyasaule bana. = Bring the razor-blades so that we make incisions on the children.
pl. of *ijeya*, a honey-comb without honey, e.g. Bana baasowa ma*yeya* nkaambo kunyina buci mukati. = The children have thrown away the honey-combs as there is no honey inside. Also *mape*
a good moral conscience, e.g. Ncibotu kubaa *mayeeyesya Leza* ciindi coonse. = It is good to have a conscience which refers to God all the time.
corn of any kind, esp. sorgum, e.g. Buyuni bwamana mayila. = The birds have finished the sorgum. Also maila.
pl. of kayimba, a furrow between eyes
claws, e.g. Mukombwe ujisi mayimba mapati. A cock has big claws. Also maimba.
helpless person, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngumayingaila, tajisi munzi. = This person drifts from one place to another, s/he is homeless.
rainy season, e.g. Mayinza asika, atubambe maamba. = The rainy season has come, let us repair the ploughs. Also mainza.
pl. of ciyoba, a rain cloud, e.g. Mu Mukazimaziba notujisi mayoba. = In the month of January we have rainclouds.
rain-clouds, e.g. Aboola mayobo, kamuleta nombe amunzi. = Rainclouds have come, bring the cattle home. Indeke ilauluka kunze amayobo. = The aeroplane flies beyond the clouds.
extreme emaciation from old age, e.g. Mubili wacembaala ulaa mayoka. When the body grows old it becomes emaciated.
small bones of a snake (harmful), e.g. Utalyati akafwide nzoka, kuli mayoka. = Do not tread on the place where the snake died, there are harmful bones.
millipedes e.g. Utani kubakongezyi bana nkumba, mayongolo abauka bamwi. Don't be frightening the children with snails, milipedes and other insects.
bubbles, foam, pl. of igovwu, e.g. Kamubikka zisani zyanu mumayovwu. Put your clothes in the suds.
musical rattles, also miyuwa, pl. of muyuwa, e.g. Bamacembele balizya mayuwa. The old women are shaking the rattles.
waves, pl. of ijuwe, e.g. Tatulobi kabotu sunu nkaambo kamayuwe. = We are not fishing well today because of the waves.
rags, e.g. Musimbi wakaboola usamine mazaapila mbuli kuti uyakukuzela. The girl came wearing rags like one going to fish. Also mazapu-zapu.
rags, e.g. Bana babacete balayoowa kuunka kucikolo nkaambo basama zisani zyamazakala. The children of the poor fear to go to school because they wear rags.

mane of an animal, e.g. Ooyu mubwa ulayoosya nkaambo mazakala akwe ali mbuli asyuumbwa. = This dog is terrifying because its mane is like that of a lion. Ndecibwa camazakala kuluma cilatobola. = I am a dog whose bite is not felt outside.
frayed edges, e.g. Cisani cangu camana, cabaa mazangala. = My garment is finished, it has become frayed.
rags, e.g. Basincinko basama mazapu-zapu. The insane wear rags. Also malwendu-lwendu, malabu-labu
rough speech, e.g. Muntu simangwemba zyoonse nzyaamba nzyamazazawu. = Everything a badly reared person talks about is done in an agresssive way.
rags, e.g. Wakati sunu tabucili bulukwe, akaba mazazawu. = He said today they are no longer trousers, they have become rags. Also mazapu-zapu
meat, e.g. Kwategwa ndikamutambe kubwiinga bwesu kuya kulya mazazu. It was said that I should invite him to our wedding to come and eat meat.
supernatural, e.g. Zintu zyamaze-maze zyakajanika kumalende. = Supernatural occurances were found at the rain-shrine.
caterpillar **mazi** unclean dung, pig, dog or human excrement, e.g. *Mazi alanunka.* = Excrement stinks. Also *maziu.*
pl. of *inzimbwa*, a big cattle-fly, e.g. *Mazimbwa alaluma.* = The big cattle-flies bite.
a person with big lips, e.g. *Milomo ya-muntu ulya yakaile kuba mazimbwa.* = The lips of that person have just become very big.

names, pl. of *izina*, e.g. *Amwi mazina alakatazya kwiita.* = Some names are difficult to pronounce. (*Mwendalubi* = born when relative dies; *Mutinta* = born from the same mother between several children of the opposite sex; *Bubala* = born when a kraal was being built; *Mayaba* = born after 8 months pregnancy)
pl. of *inzinini*, a big fly, e.g. *Mazinini ajanika muzimbuzi zimwi.* = Big flies are found in some toilets.
faeces, e.g. *Maziu alanunka kapati.* = Faeces stink a lot.
a type of flowering plant, (herders play with them as guns by removing the inside) e.g. *Amundiletele miyanda yamaziula.* = Bring me the roots of the plant *maziula.* Also *mafwufwe.*
white spots on the loins of red and black cattle.
loquacious, chattering, fond of talking, e.g. *Mukaintu ulaa mazoontwa ngusibunjaka.* = A talkative woman is a troublemaker. Also *bukanazi*
a fruit drink, e.g. *Bantu banji balayanda kunywa Mazowe.* = Many people like to drink Mazowe.
pl. of *buzuba*, a day, e.g. *Insondo ijisi mazuba ali ciloba.* = The week has seven days.
A large basket put in the water to catch fish.
the Zulu people, e.g. *Bama Zulu bamwi bakkala mu Zimbabwe.* = Some Zulu people live in Zimbabwe.
lungs, e.g. *Zintu zibimbya mazumbwa ndazipenga kale.* = I am already suffering from things which shake the lungs.

front teeth, incisors, e.g. *Bamwi bantu bajisi mazutuzyo malamfwu.* = Some people have long front teeth. Also *matenzyo.* (*Mazutuzyo aakutala* = upper incisors) *Mazutuzyo aakunsi* = lower incisors.)
conflicts, pl. of *inzwanga*, e.g. *Nseyandi kukkala mumunzi wamzwanga.* = I do not want to live in a village of conflicts.
knees, e.g. *Kamulijata mumazwi tusotoke cina syaamacula.* = Hold yourself by the knees so that we do the frog-jump. Proverb *Mazwi aliimpene.* Also *magondo*

outlets, e.g. *Bakatandaana akuyoonjizyanya mumpako yakakwazamukide kumanjililo akumanikila kumazwido.* = They chased each other until they made each other enter a hole which had a wide entrance and a narrow outlet.

self-importance, pride, stupid or careless behaviour, e.g. *Sunu ulabona, alakuzwa mazwipu, ndakupwaila abbwe.* = Today you will see, all the pride will leave you, I will crush you on a stone. *Muntu muyanga ulaa mazwipu mabi.* = A stupid person is full of pride. *Wakoona acitisyini nkaambo mu Lusaka takulipwi mazwipu.* = She slept at the railyway-station because in Lusaka there can be no careless behaviour.
generations, e.g. *Mazyalano abantu azyila kule.* = The generations of people extend far into the past.
strange activities, e.g. *Basimasalamuzi balaa mazyelembwembwe akatazya kumvwa. = Practioners in black magic have very strange activities which are hard to understand.
footprints, e.g. Bantu bakajana mazyoto-zyoto nkobakali ku Iwanina banyati. = The people found the marks where the buffaloes were fighting. Also mazyozyoozyo
footprints, e.g. Ulaa muunda wakajana mazyozyoozyo aamuntu mwaali kubbolyooka kucela myungu. = The owner of the field found the tracks of someone where she had been searching about to pick pumpkins.
excrement, e.g. Mazyu ambeba taanunki. = The faeces of a rat do not smell. Also maziu, mazi.

a target, a sign-post, marks on ground, e.g. Utaleki kusya notanasika ambaakani. = Do not stop digging before you reach the point indicated. Mulimi lyoonse uleelede kubaa mbaakani yamapopwe ngatiikalime. = A farmer should always have a target as to how much maize he intends to harvest.
a cowry-shell, e.g. Kamuleta mbaamba tukwizinge cibiya. = Bring a cowry-shell so that we polish the pot. Also mbaanyina
a large drop, as of water, like a pearl, e.g. Nindakalanga kujulu, mbaamba yakawa abusyu bwangu. = When I looked up, a large drop of water fell on my face. Also indondo, idosi
a duiker, e.g. Mubwa wangu ulazijata mbaambi. = My dog catches duikers. Also insya, namusya, kanamusya

A single cowry-shell or a woman's head-dress made of cowry-shells or a necklace worn by important men, often made of cowry-shells, beads and fibre, e.g. Mwami usamide mbaanyina munsingo. = The chief is wearing a cowry-shell on the neck. Kaindi musankwa wakali kulangilwa kuti asamike musimbi wakwe zintu zibotu nzyobakali kusama mbuli kumusukila kasalu kampongo, kumuulila bulungu, kumujanina mbaanyina zyakutungilizya mubulungu. = Long ago a boy was looked upon to dress his wife with beautiful things which they wore, such as dressing a goat's skin for her, buying her beads, and finding a cowry-shell for stringing onto beads.
ox with crumpled horns, e.g. Musune wambaba wapatila mumasanzu. = The ox with the crumpled horns got stuck in the fence.
a bushbuck, e.g. Inyama yambabala ilanona. = The meat of a bushbuck is tasty. Also mubabala
name of tree with pencil-like stems (cuttings used to heal syphilis and leprosy) also used for fences at graves, e.g. Mukupa wambala ulacisa mumeso. = Sap from the mbala tree stings the eyes.

a medicine for fighting, e.g. Basingoma nobakali kuyanda kuya kukulwana bakalya cakulya cakajikilizigwa mbala. = When the drummers were about to go to fight they ate food cooked with the medicine for fighting called mbala.
sunshine, e.g. Cifwumofwumo mucembele wakayotela mbalala yazuba abbwe. = In the morning the old woman warmed herself on a stone in the rays of the sun. Also kabalala
strips of pliable wood used for roofing, e.g. Kamuleta mbalo tubangile butala. = Bring roofing-strips so that we bind up the grainstore.
dagga, e.g. Muntu ufweba mbamba uli mbuli sincinko. = A person who smokes dagga is like a mad person. Also lubanje, tulya-bayuni.
a type of disease, e.g. Muntu utalyi kabotu uciswa mbamba. = A person who does not eat well suffers from the mbamba disease. (rashes on the body from lack of food)
the shortest rib, e.g. *Imba-mbo yamunene ilacisa.* = The small rib of the old man is sore. Also *bbambo*
medicinal root used for cibongozi/cuufwa disease in adults, e.g. *Mbanda-zikali ulanunka.* = *Mbandazikali* smells. Also *mandazikali.*
a present, something extra given freely when you buy something, e.g. *Lyoonse muntu ubeleka kabotu ule-elede kupegwa mbasela.* = A person who works well should always be given a bonus.

scars, e.g. *Mubbi ulaa mbata zyakuumwa mubili onse.* = A thief has scars all over the body from been beaten. *Mbata zyamapenzi zilalitondezya mume-saakwe.* = The marks of suffering show themselves in her eyes. *Mbata zyazyuumo zyabo tiizyakali kwaambwa.* = The scars of their beatings were indescribable.
a heater, a brazier, a charcoal stove, e.g. *Kamuleta mulilo mumbaula tuyote.* = Bring the stove so that we warm ourselves.
pl. of lubaya, a fence, e.g. *Bantu bakali kuyaka mbaya ziyumu ku-cingilila minzi yabo.* = The people were building strong fences encircling their villages.
short-sightedness, e.g. *Bacembele balaa mbayibayi, tababoni kabotu.* = The old woman is short-sighted she does not see well. Also *bbayi-bayi*
a mouse or house-rat, e.g. *Ba-kaaze balayanda kulya mbeba.* = The cats want to eat the mice.

wealth used to secure the right to a woman in future marriage, e.g. *Babindika musimbi babikka mbebe-kezyo.* = Those who want to secure a young girl for a future marriage give wealth to the parents of the girl as a bond. Also *cijalilizyo.*
earthenware container for drinking sweet-beer or beer, e.g. *Kamu-leta cibwantu mumbede ndinywe.* = Bring sweet-beer in an earthen vessel so that I drink.
point of spear, pencil, e.g. *Imbele yasumo yafwumpa.* = The point of the spear is blunt.

type of plant, (*Sesbania sesban*), the whole plant or flowers are used for relish, e.g. *Maluba ambelebele aligwa cisyu.* = The flowers of the *mbele-bele* plant are eaten for relish. Also *musebebe.*
employment, work, e.g. *Musankwa uyandaula mbeleku.* = The boy seeks employment.
a sheep, e.g. *Ndiyandaula mbelele zyakasoweka.* = I am searching for the sheep which got lost.
razor-blade, e.g. *Ndiyakukuula mbeli yakulinyoozya malezu.* = I am going to buy a razor for cutting my beard.
edge of the river, e.g. *Munyati ulalunduka mumbembelekwa amulonga.* = The buffalo is running along the edge of the river.
a garden, e.g. *Muli cisyu cibotu mumbewu oomu.* = There is good relish in this garden. Also *mbeu*
adze, (a tool similar to an axe, with an arched blade at right angles to the handle,) e.g. *Amulete mbezo tufwale joko.* = Bring an adze so that we carve a yoke.

anything which blocks or veils the eye such as a cataract or a stye, e.g. *Meso amulozi ngambilibili, alimwi alasubila.* = The eyes of a witch are veiled and they are red. *Mwana ulalila nkaambo ulaa mbilibili muliso.* = The child is crying because he has a stye in the eye. Also *insokweda*

float on fishing-line, e.g. *Kokwisula ka-lobo yabbila mbilibili.* = Pull the hook, the float has dipped. ---|--**mbilikana** rivals, e.g. Basibbola baku Chikuni *nembilikana* yabasibbola baku Chiyobola. = The footballers of Chikuni are the rivals of the footballers of Chiyobola.
resin, gum or sap of tree, juice of fruit, e.g. Kozila *mbilila* akasamu tunamatile tuyuni. = Rub resin on the tree so that the birds get stuck.
float on fishing line, e.g. Utakwisuli kalobo niitaningabbila *mbilimbili*. = Do not pull the fishing-line until the float dips down. Also *mbilibili*.
flying shreds of grass, e.g. Kamuvwunika cibwantu, cilazula *mbimbi*. = Cover the sweet-beer, it will be filled with flying shreds. Also *mimbi*
raw (meat), e.g. Eeyi nyama tainingajikwa, *nimbisi*. = This meat is not yet cooked, it is raw.
zebra, e.g. *Imbizi* mmunyama weebelwa akaambo kamubala wakwe. = The zebra is an admired animal due to it's stripes.
the point where throat begins, e.g. Munene uciswa *mbobelo*. = The old man has a sore throat.

hair-balls vomited by cattle, e.g. *Imbobelo* zyasyuumbwa bantu balaziyanda nkaambo zilabelesegwa munzila zyaandeene. = People like the hairballs of lions because they are used in different ways. (e.g. for feeding cattle who then are said to become more aggressive towards people who try to steal them.)
a kind of trap, e.g. Muvwimi ute-ya banyama *ambobo*. The hunter is trapping animals with an *mbobo* trap. Also *nkona*
manure, humus, rotten things, e.g. Muunda utajisi *mbolezi* upa nzala. = A field without humus brings hunger. Eeci cilili cilijisi *mbolezi*. This garden is fertile.
tender meat, e.g. Bamacembele balya nyama *mbombebombe*. = The old women eat tender meat.
a tourniquet, e.g. Amumwaange *mbombolokolo* mwana, buleke kuzwa bulowa. = Tie the child with a tourniquet so that the blood stops flowing.
a mirror, e.g. Muntu ulee-lede kulilanga *mumbonebone* kuti abone mbwabede. = A person should look at herself in a mirror to see how s/he is. Also *cimbonembone, cimbonimboni*
a donkey, e.g. *Mbongolo* mmunyama ubweza mukuli mulemu. = A donkey is an animal who can carry a heavy load.
the pupil of the eye, e.g. Mwana wayaswa kaundu *mumboni*. = A small seed pierced the pupil of the child's eye.
castor oil plant, pl. *mambono*, e.g. Koleta mafwuta *amambono*. = Bring the oil of the castor plant.
collection of wealth, pl. of *lubono*
mead, e.g. Bantu bakakolwa *mbote* bakaponena kucibbadela. = The people who were drunk with mead recovered in hospital.
edible fruit of the mabubu shrub, e.g. Bukoko bwambubu bulakola kapati. = The beer from *mbubu* fruit is very potent.
nut of the mabula tree, e.g. Bamwaaba balaziyanda kapati *mbula*. = Grey jackals like *mbula* fruit very much.
a plant (Painari sp.), fruit eaten in August-Sept. e.g. Muzibaka zinji *mbula* tazijaniki. In many places the *mbula* plant is not found.
a type of bird, the short-tailed warbler, e.g. Tacigwasyi kujaya *mbulaceeye* nkaambo nkayuni kaniini. = It does not help to kill a short-tailed warbler because it is a tiny bird. Also *mbulamweeye*.
a type of bird, the short-tailed warbler, e.g. Mutinta wajaya buyo kambulamweeye komwe. = Mutinta killed only one short-tailed warbler. Also mbulaceeye.
a variety of groundnuts, e.g. Mbulukutu ziide kulibbosyokela mukanwa tanaakutafwuna. The groundnuts were just bursting in the mouth before you chewed them.
ear disease, e.g. Macila uzwa masina mumatwi akaambo ka mbulukutwi. Macila has pus flowing from her ears because of an ear problem.
anything round, e.g. Basankwa babumba tumbulumbumbe twamalekani. = The boys are making round pellets for catapults.
a cannibal, e.g. Muwezi wakalumwa mbulumatali. = The hunter was attacked by a cannibal.
lead bullet, e.g. Intobolo yamudinkilwa ijisi mbumbulu zyosanwe. = The loaded gun has five bullets.
a corpulent person, e.g. Bbalanombe ndakamuyoowa nkaambo nimbumbunga yamusankwa. = I fear Bbalajombe because he is a giant of a man.

unexpected occurance, e.g. Wakabaambila bantu kuti bamujatile kubaitila acibukila mbuta. = He asked the people to excuse him for calling them unexpectedly. Kaambo kakaba kaacibukila mbuta. = The case arose unexpectedly.
Buka ulajana basinkondonyokwe bakujaila ambuta. = Get up or else you will find your enemies will kill you on the spot.
burrow, e.g. Kasulwe kakabamba mbuta mpokoona lyoonse. The hare made a burrow where it always sleeps.
seed, e.g. Katusyanga mbuto zifwambaana kubizwa. = Let us plant early growing seed.
a fruit, e.g. Imbuukuma zilasyakamuka. The imbuukuma fruit has a bitter taste. Also mbuku
pl. of lubuwa, a courtyard, e.g. Bakaintu balondo balakukula mumbuwa zyabo. Tidy women sweep their courtyards.
a blind fly, e.g. Ciindi cakumwaka noziluma mbuwo. = Blind flies bite in the dry season before the rains.
withouth, e.g. Kamuleta buyo, niiba mbuye, tulalya. = Just bring nsima, even without relish, we will eat it.
Also mbuye. mbuyu-mbuyu the leaves of the young mubuyu tree used as a relish, e.g. Mbuyu-mbuyu zijikwa cisyu. = The leaves of the mbuyu-mbuyu tree are cooked for relish.
traditional Tonga round wooden or eliptical stool, e.g. Wakaiya kufwala zyuuno zyambwalakasa. = He learnt to carve traditional stools.
hairballs vomitted by cattle, e.g. Inombe ziswa mbwebwe. = The cattle are spitting out hairballs. Also mbobelo
fourth stomach of ruminants, e.g. Cakulya casika mumbwebwe cilisetede kapati. The food which reaches to the fourth stomach is finely ground.
moustache, e.g. Kolinyoola mbwebwedo, zinakunjila munywidwa. Shave off the moustache, it will be entering the container we drink from.
good luck, e.g. Kuti kolaa mbwela, inga wajaya nswi zinji. = If you have good luck, you may kill many fish. Also coolwe. mbwembweembwe many, e.g. Mbwembweembwe nkobali. = There are many of them.
type of sorgum eaten raw, e.g. Basinzala bakwanga mbwende. = Hungry people eat a type of sorgum raw.
ground-peas, e.g. Ndalikulya musozya wambwiila. I was eating a
a very healthy-looking cow, e.g. *Nkujana nombe nimbwindili, nkokuti ilisumbungenye, ilineneede.* = You find the cow is very healthy, it is round and smooth, it is fat.
fears after bitter experience.
flowing water, e.g. *Meenda alaleka kweenda mumulonga oyu.* = The water will stop flowing in this river.
vapour, e.g. *Cisyu nocibila tulabona meendamuya.* = When the relish is boiling we see steam.

promiscuity, e.g. *Nzila yakujaya AIDS nkucenjezya bantu kutegwa baleke meendeenda akusyoma buyo mukaintu wakwe luzutu.* = The way to defeat AIDS is to warn people to stop being promiscuous and to be faithful to his wife alone.
manners of a beast.
sand, e.g. *Mabwe, zisamu, meenga amatope zilabakakizya kuzuba.* = Stones, logs, sand and mud prevent them from fishing. Also museenga.
parallel lines, e.g. *Eeli buuku lijisi meengwe mibotu.* = This book has good parallel lines.
stripes as of a zebra Also *mabala-mabala.*
uncertainty, e.g. *Ooyu muntu nakkede waawa ulaa meezyezya, takuzyi nkwaya.* = This man as he sits there is unsure, he does not know where he is going.

horns, pl. of luja, e.g *nombe eyi ijisi meja abosya.* = This cow has sharp horns. *Cisi camena meja alimwi cazungaana mumbazu zyoonse zyabuumi.* = The country has grown horns (i.e. it has become dangerous) and again it is affecting all spheres of life.
teeth, sing. lino, e.g. Mukaintu wangu wakajugwa _meno_ ali ciloba. = My wife had seven teeth extracted. (bacibanda = molar teeth; masonga-nyama = canine teeth; masonje = sharpened teeth)
teeth, pl. of linyo, _-zipula me-nyo / -nyetula menyo_ = grin. Also *meno*.
knife, e.g. Kamuleta _mesi_ tutende cisyu. = Bring a knife so that we cut up the relish.
pl. of liso, the eye, e.g. _Meso_ anzoka taaboni kabotu. = The eyes of a snake do not see well.
*meso ampongo* = name for a shrub with edible fruits.
a traditional pipe, e.g. Amundipe _mfwebyo_ yandiletela mwee-nzuma. = Give me the pipe which my friend brought for me.
fork, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Ba-makuwa babelesya _mfwolokwe_ nobalya. = White people used forks when they eat.
ant-lion, (an insect resembling a dragon-fly - when in larvae stage it digs holes in sand to trap ants), e.g. Bana balasobanya _mfwuko-mfwuko_. = The children are playing with ant-lions.
a hole, e.g. Naakayuminina malambwa, maande akayuba _mumfwu-kula_ zyawo. = When the swamps dried up, the frogs hid in their holes.
pimple, e.g. _Imfwula_ zya-mwana zilacisa. = The pimples of the child are sore.
gizzard, bird's second stomach for grinding food mixed in the first with gastric juice, e.g. Inkuku ijisi _mfwuli_ inona kapati. = A hen has a gizzard which is tasty.
a rainbow, e.g. Mibala ili ciloba ijanwa ali _mfwulicoongo_. = Seven colours are found in the rainbow.

a wild fruit, e.g. Nse-yandi kulya _mfwulimuninga_ zisizya mu *kanwa.* = I don't want to eat *mfwulimuninga* fruit which blacken the mouth. *Mucembele wakalalila mfwulimuninga akoona mumpangala yabbwe.* = The old woman ate *mfwulimuninga* for supper and slept in a cave among the rocks.
the very first light rains before the real rainy season (*civwunanombe*) begins, e.g. *Ijilo kwakawa mvwula yamfwumpaluya.* = Yesterday the first light rains fell. Also *mpumpaluya.*
an obstacle which causes one to stumble e.g. *Kamugonka mfwumpu, ilacisa umwi.* = Cut down the obstacle, it will hurt another. Also *cifwumpu.*
grievance, e.g. *Kuli mfwundiilili ili akati kenu nyoonse.* = There is a grievance among all of you.
a filled mouth, e.g. *Wakaambwiida mumfwundo.* = He spoke with a full mouth. *Wakavwubata mfwundo yomwe.* = He took one mouthful.
hard core of tree, e.g. *Kamuleta mfwundo zyakayuma tusikke mucikko.* = Bring the hard-cores of dry wood so that we put them on the fire.
heart of tree, e.g. *Wakabeza mitanda yamfwuno zyamwaani.* = He carved the logs from the heart of a *mwaani* tree.

food left from day before, e.g. *Bacembele bakandibikkila mfwuta.* = The old lady put out food for me which had been left over from the previous night (*kulya mfwuta* = to breakfast on food prepared the previous night). Also *ndala*
a gun, e.g. *Kujaya munyati weelede kuti kojisi mfwuti.* To kill a buffalo you ought to have a gun *mfwuuma* a type of shell, e.g. *Inkumba zijisi mfwuuma ziyumu.* = Snails have hard shells.

a powerful rain spirit of Chief Sinakoma of the Zimbabwean Batonga. This spirit is referred to as the lion spirit. (Note: words used mostly in the plural with the *mi-* prefix are included below, other words used in singular and plural with *mu-mi* prefixes are found under words with *mu-* prefix)
loin cloths; *nzisani zisamwa abasankwa mucibuno alimwi amuntebe.*

fruits, e.g. *Kaindi micelo iyakaliti mbwee. Masuku aya! Inundu ezi! Manomba, mbubu, nsombo, impondo, lusala, mbula, busikka, manono, amankomone.* = Long ago fruits were plentiful. These wild loquat fruits! Wild plums, fruits from the *mabubu* shrub, blueberries, grey fruits, edible tubers, nuts, Tamarind fruits, yellow fruits, small coconuts.
perspiration, e.g. *Mulimo ukatazya uzwisya mibe.* Hard work produces sweat. Also *nkasaalo, mitukuta*
posts of kraal, sing. *mucinjili* e.g. *Aba bana bakakkede amulyango waciba canombe amicinjili.* = These children were sitting on the poles at the entrance of the cattle-kraal.
holes, perforations, e.g. *Ciluli cakajisi midonkwi.* The roof was full of holes.
Linesrt, as on a garment, e.g. *Tayelede kusama cisani cijisi mihololombi yatombe.* = He ought not to wear a garment which is streaked with dirt. Also *mibbyolombyo-mbyo*
shins (front of legs below knee) e.g. *Uulya musimbi ujisi miindi mibotu.* That girl has beautiful shins.
pounding together, e.g. *Bamakaintu bakali kutwa mapopwe mumijijiiji.* = The women were pounding togeter in threes (or fours).
sounds of footsteps, e.g. *Twakamvwa mijinci yabantu bakali kwe-enda mumudima.* = We heard the sounds of people who were walking in darkness.

sound of feet stamping when dancing, e.g. *Aya akali mazuba amijiti-jiti kutambala bantu boonse mukulitondezya kuti bayoosala Jeremiah.* These were the days of feet stamping as all the people danced happily, showing that they would choose Jeremiah.

bits of iron hung on belt which were rattled in some dances, e.g. *Batumbu bakaindi bakali kusama mikaku. Bali kunga mpobeendela balalibonya kuti mbatumbu, balombwana bambi tiibakali kubacubila.* The young mothers of the past were wearing belts with pieces of iron. It was seen when they walked around that they were young mothers, other men did not pester them.

arms full of energy, sing. *mukono*, e.g. *Nkujana musimbi kumweelede maingankwa, kutitima boya mumikono yakwe nabuntu.* You find the girl is well fitted with shoulder-straps, with the hair on the arms bristling, a real woman.
tracks made by animals, e.g. *Chuungabuluba wakanjila mikula yanombe yakali kuya kumunzi.* Chuungabuluba entered the tracks of the cattle which were leading to the village. Also *migula*
bones protruding from a lean body. e.g. *Akaambo kakutalya kabotu kabwa kakwe kakalibonya mikunya.* Because of not eating well the protruding bones of his dog were visible. Also *mafwinya, magunya*
worms, e.g. *Mumulonga wa Kafwuwe kuli milaala minji yakulobya nswi.* In the Kafuwe river there are plenty of worms for fishing.

negotiations concerning traditional customs, e.g. *Oobu buzuba zinene zyeendezya milumbe zyakaamba kuti, "Bina Simweete mbabeelede kuti bamanizye milala.* On this day the old men who supervised the discussions said, "The mother of Simweete should be cleansed." Also *milumbe*

a long line of people, e.g. *Bantu mbubakamvwida kuti kuli nanga kwasibbuku, yakaba milebe kuzya nkuko.* When the people heard that there was a witchdoctor at the headman, they make a long line to go there. Also *milongo*
fertile land on the bank of a river, e.g. *Bantu balalima myuunda yabo mumilemba.* People plough their fields on fertile patches along the river banks. Also *zilili*

bead-necklaces, e.g. *Basimbi bayanda kusama milemba, zidanda atukuze. Milemba ilalengelela kumakosi nobeenda.* Girls like wearing bead-necklaces, armlets of wound thin wire and sisal cords. The bead neck-laces hang from their necks when they walk.
beaded-veils, e.g. *Booye bakaindi bakali kusama milembalemba.* The female initiates of the past used to wear beaded-veils.
arrows, sing. *mulembe*, e.g. *Inga kabaya kukuyasa mimvwi amilembe.* Perhaps they will shoot you with unbarbed and barbed arrows.
a river-bird with brown wings, brown back and black tail, e.g. *Ndabona kayuni nkaanga milenda munsaa muonga.* I saw a small black and brown coloured bird near the river.

round objects, e.g. *Bana balayaka zizumbo zyatuyuni. Muzizumbo balabikka miliindo. Miliindo balaita kuti mai.* Children build the nests of little birds. In the nests they put round objects. They call the round objects eggs.
announcements, e.g. *Sunu kwali milumbe yamause minji.* There were many fneral announcement today.
a bottle-shaped variant of the mankuntu drum of the Valley Tonga.
heaps, e.g. sing. *mulwi*. Zipego zyakali *milwi*. = There were heaps of gifts.
ornamental beaten metal coils, coils of beads, e.g. Ndakanyandwa kubona *mimbuli* yabulungu munkanya. = I was surprised to see coils of beads around the waist.
swelling, e.g. Nobakamuuma zimboko, kwakalibonya *mimbuli* a mubili. = When they beat him with sjamboks, swellings appeared on the body. Also *mivwundu*
leaven, yeast, e.g. Bamwi bantu tabanywi cibwantu cabikkwa *mime-na*. = Some people do not drink sweet-beer in which leaven has been added. Also bumena, mamena, mumena.
dough, e.g. Bakaintu bakanda *mimpelela* yatumbuwa twakusambala. = The women knead the dough for scones to sell.
arrows, e.g. Utaindi okuya balakuyasa *mimvwi*. = Do not pass that way they will pierce you with arrows.
slopes, sing. *mungwenyu*, e.g. Wakaitanta ncinga yakwe, *mumingwenyu* moonse walo nkuselemuka tajati amabbuleki. = He got up on his bicycle in all the slopes he desended without catching the brakes.
marks, e.g. Kumeso kwakali buyo *mingwilizi* yamisozi. = On her face there were just the traces of tears.
black ashes from burnt bush, e.g. Zituta zyangu zyasiya nkwindali kweenda *mumimbi*. = My feet are black from walk-ing in the black ashes of the burnt bush.
lines, queues, e.g. Bantu bakali *mumindano* yatakali kugola kulindilizya zibaka zyakunjila mukati. = The people were in endless queues tired out waiting for places to enter inside. Also mindando
folds, wrinkles, e.g. *Minganja* ankumo yakwe yakali mbuli yamusinsi. = The wrinkles on his forehead were like the pleats on a skirt.

marks, e.g. Kuzwa mumaanza abo kusikila kutukokola, balaa *mingwilizi* yabusiciiya a buzike bwabo kumuzwakule. = From their hands to their elbows they have the signs of their training and slavery to the foreigner.
long feathers, cock's tail, e.g. Mukombwe wakomena ujisi *minimba*. = An adult cock has long feathers in the tail.
the keys or prongs of a hand piano, e.g. Cilimba eci tacilili, *minjeeya* yanyongana. = This cilimba does not play, the keys are not adjusted properly.
bead-and-wire collars, pl. of *munkonde*, e.g. Bakazingana *minkonde* munsingo. = They tied bead-and-wire collars around each other's necks.

shaven heads, pl. of *munkulu*, e.g. Kuli tunsiya-nsiya tuli mbuli kusakulwa *minkulu* bakaintu bafwidwa. = There are ancient traditions like women who have their hair completely shaven who have lost their husbands.
frowns. Also *minya*
unripe grain *minsale* sugar-cane, pl. of *munsale*, e.g. Baama bakaulisya *minsale* minji kuzisobano. = Mother sold many sticks of sugar-cane at the games. Also mulweense, minsali.
the large intestine, e.g. Muntu utalyi kabotu ukonzya kuciswa *minsano*. = The person who is not eating well may have something wrong with the large intestine.
the first ripening of a plant or crop, e.g. Minsale itaanguna kubizwa *mminsomwa*. = The sugar-cane which is first to ripen is known as *minsomwa*.
the shoots of maize, e.g. Akaambo kacilobe *minsonje* yamapopwe yakali mibi. = Because of too much rain, the shoots of the maize were bad.

when the maize is still soft, the seeds are not yet hardened e.g. Mapopwe acili _minsyanje_, nkokuti inseke zyamapopwe zizwa makupa alimwi bama-nyina balasisa _minsyanje_ kuletela bana babo. = The maize is still soft, that is the seed of the maize they produce a milk-like substance and the mothers hide it to bring it to the children.
a type of bird, the swift, pl. _baminteengwe_, e.g. _Baminteengwe bakali kulila kwaambilizya kuti bwaca_. = The swifts were singing announcing the dawn.

wrinkles, a frown, e.g. Muntu wanyema ubamba _minya_ ankumo. = A person who is angry forms wrinkles on the forehead. Mudaala wakali kulangika kuti kuli ncayeeya nkaambo _kaminya ankumo_. = The old man seemed to look as if he was thinking about something because of the wrinkles on his forehead. Also -zinga _minya_
pl. of _munyanga_, a tusk, e.g. Muzovwu wacembaala ujisi _minyanga milamfwu_. = An old elephant has long tusks.

rows of wrinkles or fur-rows, e.g. Mulawo wamutelo wandi-kkazika _minya-minya_. = The tax-law places rows of furrows on my forehead. Mulembo waligwa nombe ubaa _minya-minya_. = The cloth eaten by the cow had many wrinkles.
pl. of _mupata_, a valley, e.g. Ndabona munyati _mumupata_. = I have seen a buffalo in the valley.

territories, e.g. Banyama bakasakana, bakatija nkaambo _misanza_ yabo yakaba cimpayuma, babula kwa-kuyusila. = The animals have gone far away, they have fled because their grazing lands have become a desert, they have no shelter.
land to south e.g. Banyama banji bakapolela _kumisanza_ kwakali bwizu bunji. = Many animals moved to southern parts where there was plenty of grass.

half-green maize-cobs which are getting dry during harvesting time, pl. of _museete_, e.g. Bumwi buzuba ndaka-unka kuya kutema _miseete_ yakuyoka. = One day I went to cut half-green maize-cobs to roast.

generation, age-group, stages of life, e.g. Aba bana yakali _misela_. = These children were of the same age-group. Basimbi bakaindi bakali kwiinda _misela_ minji kabatanapandulwidwa ncoca-amba kuba mukaintu. = Girls in the past went through many phases of life before it was explained to them what it means to be a woman. Basankwa bakaindi cintu ncobakali kulwanina kapati _mmisela_. = The thing which the boys of the past fought about very much had to do with the age-groups. (Boys from different villages would fight for dominance: one could even try to buy membership into a dominant group. There was strong friend-ship among the members of a group.)
kicks, pl. of _musembela_, e.g. Maulu atalika kuyuma akusansa _mi-sembela_ canguzu. = The legs began to kick strongly.
tears, e.g. Liso litoogwa lizwa _misozi minji_. = Tears stream from an eye that is temporarily blinded.
maize-cob, e.g. Baneene baka-ndiletela _misuku_ yamapopwe yobile. = My grandfather brought me two cobs of maize.
bullets, e.g. Ndali kuyanda kuvwima pesi _misyonga_ yakamana. = I wanted to hunt but the bullets were finished.
baskets, sing. _mutaanga_, e.g. Bamakaintu bajisi masuku mumi-_taanga_. = The women have masuku fruit in their baskets.
logs, e.g. Wakabweza *mitanda* *yamfwuno zyamwaani*. = He took logs of *mwaani* wood.
the foot of the bed, e.g. *Kondipa ngubo yamwana kumitandabilo*. = Give me the baby's shawl at the foot of the bed.

newspapers, e.g. *Muli sika-pepele amumiteende moonse, mbobu-ceda twiide kumvwa milimo yamuvwuba ccacca*. = Everywhere in the media and in the newspapers from the break of day we hear about the activities of getting rich quickly.
strings of beads, e.g. *Nsengo wakasamikide mitenta yabulungu*. = The horn was covered with strings of beads.
salivary glands, e.g. *Mwana-angu uciswa mitoke yamunsingo*. = My child is suffering from glands in the neck. + a swelling in the right side of the abdomen Also *citeku, mateku*.

drops of sweat, e.g. *Mulimo muyumu uzwisya mitukuta*. = Hard work causes one to produce drops of sweat. *Cintu camitukuta yako inga tocisangauli kusowa-sowa nkaambo uzyi mbuli mbo-cakakupenzya*. = You don't wastefully throw away what you have earned by your sweat because you know how much it pained you to get it.
nakedness, e.g. *Akaambo kakuti kwakali kupya, bunji bwabana bakalede buyo amitundulu*. = Because of the fact that it was hot, many children slept naked.
rays of the sun, e.g. *Nindakasinsimuka ndakabona mitunga-zuba yalampa kale*. = When I awoke up I saw that the rays of the sun were already long.
arrows, e.g. *Mivwi yangu iyoo-loka-loka bulowa*. = My arrows will be dripping blood.
welts, cuts, slashes, sing. *muvwundu*, e.g. Wakabona *mivwundu-mivwundu amubili*. = He saw the welts on the body.

roots, e.g. *Mainza bapati balasya makuli, mapopa, mbuyumbuyu, ndigwalukanda amiyanda iligwa imwi. Basinombe balasya luseza, zyuuli, bagololo, tunkulimusanza anzimba*. = In the rainy season the elders dig makuli, mapopa, mbuyu-mbuyu, ndigwalukanda and other edible roots. The herders dig luseza, bagololo, tunkulimusanza and nzimba.
ancestral spirits, pl. of *muzimo*, e.g. *To Batonga tulalemenezya mizimo yesu*. = We Batonga venerate our ancestral spirits.
heavy falls, e.g. *Nceciindi bantu nobakali kulyuumina kapati mizinga ansi*. = That is the time when the people would throw themselves crashing to the ground.
a type of tree (Acacia nigrescens), stamped-bark used as a fish poison, fibre used as twine, e.g. *Inziba ilila mumoba*. = A dove is cooing in the acacia tree. Also *moobanziba*
large dove, e.g. *Naakasika kutooze wakajana mukooze kamwi kwacegwa mombo*. = When he reached the traps he found a large dove was caught in one trap.
the white part of *insikili* seed after the outer part has been removed, e.g. *Mombola ninseke iizwa mucikwa cansikili*. = *Mombola* is a seed which comes out from the case of the *insikili* nut.
a cone-shaped fish-trap, pl. *myono*, e.g. *Bazezi bamyono bajaya nswi zinji*. = Those fishing with the cone-shaped fish-traps catch many fish. Also *moono*
a type of bird, the giant kingfisher, e.g. *Mooba ulya nswi mumulonga*. = The giant kingfisher is eating fish in the river.
the knob-thorn tree with curved thorns, e.g. Inziba zilikkede mumoobanziba. Pidgeons are seated on the knob-thorn tree.
a tree with long flexible branches, e.g. Mamvwa amoobazyuba mmaniini. The thorns of the moobazyuba tree are small. Also moobezuba
a root with medicinal powers, e.g. Moobezuba usilika malwazi manji. = The moobezuba root heals many diseases. Also moobazyuba
a blind person, e.g. Komugwasya moofwu atanyikili mumulindi. = Help the blind person so that s/he does not fall nto a pit.
the trigger or spring of a gun, e.g. Utajati moola, ntobolo ilipakidwe. = Do not touch the trigger, the gun is loaded.
a very small barbel, e.g. Tumoola ntuswi tuniini-niini. Small barbel are very tiny fish.
a large bird, e.g. Moola ulalila mumusamu. A large bird is crying in the tree.
rinderpest (infectious viral disease of cattle charaterized by fever and dysentry), e.g. Inombe zyesu zyakafwa bulwazi bwamoolomoka. = Our cattle died from the disease of rinderpest.
marrow, e.g. Mooma wazifwuwa zyanyama ulemya musinza. = The marrow of the bones of meat thickens the soup.

a type of bird, the turkey buzzard, e.g. Moomba walila sunu. = A turkey-buzzard cried out today. Basikweendelezya mulimo wakuyandaula mali abbigwa bakali bamoomba ibataindi nsozi. = Those who were in charge of the investigation to search for the stolen money were like turkey-buzzards who do not miss a locust.
a type of tree (used to make beds), e.g. Bulo bwamoomba tabuli buyumu. = The bed made from the moomba tree is not hard.
calf, pl. boombe; moombe mufwungusi a completely weaned calf, also muleke, e.g. Moombe mulesi nguutolwa kuciko. A weaned calf is the one taken for bride wealth.
a hem, border, outside edge, e.g. Moombe wabuluke mmupati. = The hem of the trousers is big.
bridge of nose, e.g. Mulwani bamuuma amoombombo wampemo. They beat the fighter on the bridge of the nose. Also moononono
type of tree (resinous, growing from cuttings, planted in courts and kraals), e.g. Kamusyanga moombwa mumambewu nguusyuuka. = Plant a moombwa tree which sprouts in the gardens.
a type of tree, e.g. Wakaciyakila cilili kabotu alubaya Iwamasanzo amoomfwenene. = She fenced an alluvial garden with the cut branches of a moomfwenene tree.
a prolonged or sustained shout, e.g. Nobakamunyikula musankwa wakanyikila mudamu, kwakalimvwisya moompololo. When they took out the boy who had been drowned in the dam, a prolonged cry was heard.
a whipping-stick, e.g. Wakanduumya moondo amutwe. = He beat me with a whipping-stick on the head. Also muluso
prophesy, pl. myone, e.g. Banjidwe basangu bamvwula baamba myone isiyene-siyene. = Those who are possessed by rain-spirits make various kinds of prophesies.

a castrated goat/ram, e.g. Nyama yamoongo ilanona. = The meat of a castrated goat is tasty. Nibwakaca basimbi bakapobwedwa moongo. = When it was dawn the girls were feasted with a castrated goat. Usyi Kacumbika waka-ulisya moongo wambelele. = The father of Kacumbika sold a castrated ram.
the mid-rib of a palm leaf, e.g. Moongo watuvwu lyakavwuma mmupati. = The mid-rib of palm-leaves is big.

tusk, e.g. Kaindi muntu naakafwa bakali kumubikkila zintu mbuli milombwe yankaya zyamoongo wamuzovwu. = Long ago when a person died they were putting objects for him (on his body) such as rings of elephant tusks

outer edge, as of plank, outside corner, ridge, spine, e.g. Malwazi amwi akwela moongola. = Some illnesses pull the spine. Kafwuwa kamusana, moongola, kakali kulibonya atala. = The back bone, the spine, was seen protruding.

a traditional medicine said to protect from death, e.g. Bantu banji baamba kuti wakalide moongole - musamu wakutafwambaana kufwa. = Many people said he had taken preventative medicine, a medicine which prolongs life.
the spine of a fish, e.g. Moongolola wanswi ujisi mamvwa manji. = The spine of a fish has many bones.
the bridge of the nose, e.g Mamina ainda mumoongolola wampemo. = Mucous passes through the bridge of the nose. Also moombombo
spinal cord or spinal marrow, e.g. Moongonyana wakwe ulacisa akaambo kakubweza zilema. = His spinal cord is hurting because of carrying heavy things. Also mulimu-limu, musongo-songo

a charm said to produce longevity, e.g. Ooyu muntu ncatafwi kufwambaana, wakalya moongozya. = The reason why this person does not die quickly is because she used a charm which produces longevity. Also moongole

a cone-shaped unvalved fish-basket or trap, pl. myoono, e.g. Kamubweza moono tukazele. Moono ujaya zitaka zinji. Tujaya nswi zinji mumyoono. = Take the fishing-basket so that we catch fish. The fishing-basket kills many small fish. We kill many fish with the fishing-baskets. (Kuli misyobo minji yamyoono: kuli myoono mitumboono, antela coono budonga; kuli mingwala, antela masungilikwa. = There are many types of fishing-baskets: there are the mitumboono fishing-baskets or coono budonga (cidoongwe); there are mingwala fishing-baskets or masungilikwa. Masiko antela mabbinda alabelesegwa abakaintu muciindi cakuzela. = The masiko or the mabbinda are used by women when fishing.) Moono may be valved and ngoma mulonga double-valved. Nsopo, a plunge-basket, is cone-shaped and are plunged down in shallow waters and their mouths pressed firmly against the ground below. Izubo are scoop-baskets, wide-mouthed wedge-shaped and used by women to sieve the shallow water; mu-cundulusio is a roll of grass which is pushed through a pool to dredge the water of fish. Fish-poison is got from pounding seeds and pods of munga and musangu trees, which seems to asphyx-iate rather than poison.
inside cartilage of nose, bridge of nose, e.g. Isyini licisya moonono wampemo. = The common cold can make the inside of the nose sore. Also moombombo, moongolola wampemo
a stick for beating out a rhythm, e.g. Koleta moonzyo ukonkoole ngoma. = Bring a rhythm-stick and beat the (wooden side of the) drum.
a prolonged shout, e.g. Walimvwisya moopolola kuti kuli wafwa. = A prolonged cry indicated that there is one who has died. Also moompololo
a name for the city of Lusaka, e.g. Muleli wacisi ukkala Moositundwe. = The ruler of the country resides in Lusaka.
a motor-car, pl. myootokala, e.g. Tandikaunki amootokala ku Monze nkaambo nseujisi. = I will not go to Monze in a car because I haven't got one.
lots of foam, e.g. Insipa eyo taizwi moovwu manji. = Not much foam comes from that soap. Also macovwu mooya breath/air, e.g. Muno munanda kuli mooya mubi. = In this house there is bad air. Also muya.

girl undergoing initiation or when initiated or when addressed by the in-laws when married, pl. bamooye, / booye, e.g. Mooye wakazwa jilo, watizigwa sunu. = The initiate who came out of the house of seclusion yesterday was taken away in an illegal marriage today. (Note: Mooye originally meant a cocoon indicating that which was protected.)
a strong cord to catch fish, e.g. Ooyu mooze ngwakutezya nswi. = This strong cord is for catching fish.

calm and easy-going person, e.g. Ooyu mulumi wako mmoozu alimwi mmuntu wabantu. = This husband of yours is quiet and a man of the people. mopane a type of tree, e.g. Mopane mmusamu ujanwa kujwe. = Mopane is a tree which is found to the east. mowa a coward, e.g. Mowa takonzyi kuvwuna mweenzinyina. = A coward cannot protect his/her friend.

heart, pl. myoyo, e.g. Moyo wangu walela. My heart has no strength. Tobamwi myoyo njakeela, ino inga nkujana wabbila kale mubulowa. = Some of us have the hearts of the last born, you just find that you quickly sink in the blood. (i.e. one of the characteristics of the last born is to be quick to anger.)

throat, e.g. Ndatingwa kafwuwa kanswi amoyo. A small bone of a fish stuck in my throat. Also ikulumina, agoyooyo, ikulyukulyu. Igoyooyo = inside the throat; ibozu = the skin covering the throat; imbobelo = where the throat begins.
core, e.g. Moyo wamubanga mmuyumu kufwala joko. The core of the mubanga tree endures for carving a yoke.
heart, (Ila) e.g. Bakanjilwa moza wabukandu kabayeeya kuti antela kwasika lumamba. They were possessed with a heart of cowardice thinking that perhaps war had come.
sign-post, indicator, mark, e.g. Kobeleka kusikila ampaakani awa. = Work until you reach this mark here. Also mbaakani.
a part of a bird's breast, e.g. Atwaabane kayuni aumwi atole mpaandwa yomwe. Let us share the little bird and each take a part of the breast.
mahogany bean, e.g. Impaapa zikozyenye bamoomba mubala. = Mahogany beans resemble turkey-buzzards in colour.

wealth given to the girl's father before he performs his ritual act of giving the bride away, e.g. Mpaizyo inga nkutola sumo lilaa mala, amaamba aabulumbu. = The wealth given, by the parents of the bridegroom, to the father of the girl prior to the ritual act of marriage, (kupiila) is to take to the father a barbed-spear and hoes decorated with strings of beads. Also impaizyo
luggage, container of goods, e.g. Wakaula mabbokesi ampaka yakutolelela. He bought boxes and cases to take along with him.
shoots which grow between leaves, e.g. Atukapakunune mpakatwa zyalungu kumuunda. Let us go and remove the shoots between the leaves of the pumpkins in the field.

a hole, cave, bee-hive, e.g. Simugomampako uzyalila mumpako. = The woodpecker breeds in a hole. Nokuba kuti buzuba oobo kwakali kutontola anze, mukati kampako eeyo mwakali kukasaala. = Even though it was cold outside that day, within that hole it was warm.
a drinking cup a dish to wash face, e.g. Kosanzya mpali akubikka cibwantu. Wash the drinking cup and put in sweet-beer.

first rains, e.g. Kwakawa buyo mvwula itegwa lukulula-nkononga a mpampaluya, yacivwunajombe. = Only the rains fell which are called lukululankononga (this rain makes the prickly grass-seeds fall and it comes at the end of the main rainy season) and mpampaluya (rain which falls clearing away the ashes of the bush fires), or civwunanombe. (the beginning of the main rainy season providing fresh grass for the cattle)
a clever person, e.g. Ooyu mwana nimpana, ulazwidilila lyoonse mumisunko. This child is very intelligent, she always succeeds in examinations
a water-lily, e.g. Impana zijanwa mumazyiba. Water-lilies are found in the pools.
big flying ants, e.g. Mumuunda kwanjila mpanamana zinji. = Many big flying-ants entered the field.
fork in tree, a cross, e.g. Ndaunka kukugonka mpanda zyazizali. = I am going to cut forks from trees for maize-storage platforms.
a parrot, sing. of bampanda, e.g. Bampanda balazilaika kuti bakolwa lubanje. = Parrots become stupid if they are drugged with cannabis.
shell worn by important people, e.g. Mwami usama mpande acamba. The chief wears an mpande shell on his chest.

spirits of the dead who possess the living (among the southern Gwembe Batonga and very common among the Zimbabwean Batonga.) e.g. Muntu wanjilwa mpande umpilizigwa amusamu mukali. A person possessed by mpande spirits are fumigated with a very strong medicine.
face-to-face, e.g. Ndeelede kuunka kumunzi kuya kukanana mulomo mpande abazyali bangu lunywa meenda. = I ought to go home to talk to my parents face-to-face while I am sober.

cave, crevice in rock, hollow place, e.g. Zikwaba zikkala mumpangala zyamabwe. Lizards live in crevices among the rocks. Kapapa kanondo wakaimikizya akati kampangala yaminwe yamunanga. The shell of the tortoise stood in the hollow of the fingers of the witchdoctor.
a rib, e.g. Kanene bakamutyola kampango komwe amusako. = They broke one small rib of Kanene with a big stick. Also ibbambo.
a verse of a hymn, e.g. Ino eco cijanwa akampango nzi mu Bbaibbele? = Now that is found in what verse of the Bible?
bright precocious child, e.g. Ooyu mwana nimpanu-mpanu. = That child is a quick developer.
baldness, high forehead, e.g. Koya ukamwiite muntu ulya ulaa mpanza. = Go and call that man who is bald.
a bonus, something extra, e.g. Muntu wabeleka kabotu upegwa mpasela kumukulwaizya. A person who works hard is given a bonus to encourage her/him. Also mbasela
a troublesome cow, e.g. nombe mpasi yazwa muluba. A troubleome cow has come out of the kraal.
small bee, making honey in trees, e.g. Inzuki zimpasi zilaluma kapati. = The small honey-bees bite fiercely.
hip, e.g. Ndaciswa mpaso nkaambo ndeenda musinzo mulamfwu. = My hip is paining because I travelled a long distance.
difficult problem, quiz or task, e.g. Aaka kaambo katwaalila, *nimpasununa-balozi.* = We have failed to solve this case, it is a very difficult problem.
goods, riches, e.g. Sicintoolo wakaleta *mpasya* zibotu ono. = A shopkeeper has brought nice goods now.
a species of small broad fish, pl. bampata, e.g. Ndajaya *bampata* bosanwe akalobo kangu. = I have caught five flat fishes with my hook.
receptacle for fat, e.g. Kamuleta *mpau* izwide mafwuta. = Bring the container full of fat. Also *mpawo.*
problem
receptacle for fat, e.g. *Mpawo* zyakajisi mafwuta akunana. = The receptacles had oil for smearing on the body.
white paint, e.g. *Inanda izilidwe mpemba ituba buu!* = The house is painted with very white paint.

nose, nostril, e.g. *Impemo njiimvwa zinunka.* = The nose is what senses what smells. Basankwa banji mazuba ano mbeelenze, mbasyoonto balaa *mpemo ziyoya.* = Some men today are useless, few have noses which breathe. i.e. have wisdom.
stern of canoe, e.g. Muzeli wakakkede *mumpemo yabwato.* = The fisherman sat in the stern of the boat.
type of fish, bream, e.g. *Impende zilaligwa abantu banji.* = Breams are eaten by many people.

what is hard to cook and remains hard to eat in food, e.g. Nokuba kuti waijika ayeenzinyina, *mpengele taikonzyi kubizwa. = Even though it is cooked with other food like itself, it does not get cooked.
pencil, e.g. Basicikolo bayanda *mpensele* kucikolo. = Pupils need pensils at school. Also *mpesele*
tale-bearer, e.g. Muntu *wampepabami ngusibunjaka.* = A person who spreads gossip is a trouble maker.
a velvet bean whose pods cause intense itch, e.g. Mukaintu zyamubaba *mpese* kumulonga naali kusya lusala. = A woman was irritated by velvet beans at the river when she was digging lusala relish.
prickly caterpillars living on castor-oil plant, e.g. Bana bababwa zyuuka zya-*mpese.* = The children have become itchy from the prickly caterpillars.
a flute (made from a plant) e.g. Bavwimi basiba *mpeta* mucila. = The hunters are blowing flutes on the hunt. Also ceembo.
a pea-beetle, e.g. Inyabo ziligwa *mpetamuuka,* amuzipiile musamu. = The beans are eaten by the peabeetle, spray them with insect-killer.
a colonial measure of cloth (4 yards), e.g. Ndaula mulembo *wampeto* zyobilo. = I have bought two lengths of material.
rolled up cloth, e.g. *Impetu yabuluke obu nimpati.* = The rolled up edge of this trousers is big.
coldness, e.g. Masiku sunu kwali *mpeyo* kapati. = Last night it was very cold.
an army, group of fighters, e.g. Aawa kwainda *mpi* yabasikalumamba. = A band of soldiers have passed here.
a hard nut from a wild tree, e.g. Kamubungika *mpiililyo* tubambe mayaamba. = Put together the nuts so that we make a dancing belt.

the hard shell of an insect which can be used by children as a whistle, e.g. Nitwakacili bana twakali kuyandisya kusiba *mpiililyo.* = When we were still children we liked very much to blow the *mpiililyo* whistle.
a short length of wood, e.g. Basankwa bajaya babeya *ampika*. = The boys are killing birds with short lengths of wood.

a friction-stick, e.g. Wakago-nkolola cisamu ciyumu camusekese kucita cikazi amane ngooyu nkucigwama-gwama atala kupanga kalindi *kampikilo*. = He cut down a dry piece of wood from the *musekese* tree for the base. After that he removed the bark and then made a small hole in it to fit the friction-stick.
rubber football, e.g. Basimbi abalo balasobana *mpila* mazubaano. = Girls also play football these days.
a spring-hare, e.g. *Mpile mmu-nyama unona kapati*. = The spring-hare is an animal which is very tasty. Also *nalufwuma, nalufwumba-fwumba, bukuca*.
chilli, pepper, e.g. Muntu uciswa mumala tayelede kulya *mpilibili*. = A person who has a sick stomach should not eat pepper.
chilli. Also *mpilibili*.
