a rite, a ceremony, e.g. *Impimbiziko ncilengwa cabantu basiya*. = The word *impimbiziko* is used to describe a custom of the Bantu peoples. Also *ciyanza*
an amulet, medicine put between the beads which are used around the waist, e.g. Bantu balisandula basuntwe babelesya *mpimpi*. = People who change themselves into hyenas use charms.
number of times for doing anything e.g. Mbwaakalusiba Iwija *mpimpo* yomwe, kwakazuma mvwula. = As soon as he blew the horn once, it thundered. *Ukacite mpimpo zyobilo*. = Do it twice.
a short length of wood, e.g. Wakajaya nkanga zyobilo kumbali adambwa *ampinda*. = He killed two guinea-fowl beside the pond with a short stick. Also *mpika*.
difficulty, e.g. Ooyu muntu ujisi mampindaukwa manji. = This person has many difficulties. Also *mpinduukwa*
reward, profit, e.g. Sicintoolo ujana *mpindu* mpati amapopwe. = The storekeeper makes a big profit from maize.

difficulty, trying many ways of doing things to attain one's goal, e.g. Kubaa *mapinduukwa* cipa kuzwidilila muli ncoyanda. = To endure trials urges one to achieve what one wants. Also *mpindaukwa, mpinunukwa*.
the *musikili* tree, e.g. Wakasyobola nyeele zyakwe amafwuta a *mpingili*. = He polished his flutes with oil of the *musikili* tree. Also *impingili*
length between two joints as in a reed, e.g. Kondityolweda *mpingu* yomwe yamunsale. = Break off a joint of sugar cane for me. Also *mpyungu*.
a difficulty, e.g. Cikonzya kuselela, kutanta *nimpinunukwa*. Ndituvwu. (a riddle) = It can easily go down but to go up is a problem. It is a leaf. Also *mpinduukwa*
a mine-shaft, deep hole, e.g. Mubelesi wakasya *mpisi ndamfwu*. = The worker dug a deep hole.
a type of insect, e.g. Kumazuba basimpongo balaya kukuteya *mpiye*. = In the evening the goatherds are going to trap insects.
an ostrich Also *mpo*
ostritch, e.g. *Mpo* zijanwa muzimpayuma. = Ostritches are found in deserts. Also *mpye, impye*.
entrance to animal's burrow, e.g. Twakajana nsezi zinji *mumpo muya*. = We found many wild cats there at the entrance of the burrow.
the cheek-bone, e.g. Mucembele walijata mumpobe, linyo lilacisa. = The old woman is holding her jaw, the tooth is paining.
seed, e.g. Mpoka zimwi zyakazwa mucinkonti. = Some seeds came out of the cob.
a plant for making salt and relish, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kubamba munyo wampoko. = The people of the past were making salt from the *mpoko* plant.

a traditional braclet of beads, e.g. Mwana uwangwa *mpola* naulikwa. = A child is tied with a bracelet when named. Mwana napegwa zina lyanguli, ulaangwa *ampola* yabulungu. = When a child is given a name from the father's clan, it is tied with a bracelt of beads.
a waist-belt of beads used while dancing, e.g. Bamakaintu bakalyaanga *mpola* muzibuno kucizyano. = The women were tying beaded-belts around their waists at the dance.
a bullet, bullets, e.g. Bakajana *mpolopolo* zyamusyobo omwe kweendelanya anzyoobakajana mumitunta imwi. = They found bullets of the same kind matching those which were found in other corpses.

a stem of hollow grass used for plaiting and weaving and also as a whistle, pl. *bampolwe*, e.g. Beembezi balasiba *bampolwe* nibakatala kuuma mikkwilo. = The herders blow grasswhistles when they are tired of cracking whips. Also *mpoolwe*.
a place to hide food, (kuba ampomba), e.g. Muntu muunyu ulaa *mpomba*. = A greedy person has a place to hide food.
the first rains, e.g. Mweemvwe wakazwa lyakawa *mpompaluya*. = The fresh grass germinated when the first rains fell. Also *mpampaluya, mpumpaluya*.
source, e.g. Meendaa *mpo-mpo* alatontola kapati. = The water of the spring is very cold.
a grey fruit, e.g. Atuka-kwame *mpondo* kutegwa tujane cakulya. = Let us go and split the grey fruits so that we can have food.
British pound, e.g. Mukuwa wakandipa *mpondo* yomwe. = The white man gave me one pound.
a goat, e.g. *Impongo* zilacela mumusena. = The goats are grazing in the vlei.
hollow grass used for weaving or sucking liquids, e.g. Bana basiba *bampoolwe* mugumba. = The children are blowing through the hollow grass among the mugumba trees. Also *mpolwe*
a spring (of water), e.g. Kalonga aka kalijisi *mpoompo* itayuminini. = This stream has a spring which does not dry up. Also *mpompo*
Also *mpoompo*.
butterfly, e.g. Muunda wavwumpwa *mpopolofwa* tuukomenzyi zisyango. = A field taken over by butter-flies does not produce what is planted there.
post-office box (ety. Eng.), e.g. Sena mulijisi *mposo* mucilawo momu-kkala? = Do you have a post-office box in the place where you are staying?
a purse, wallet, e.g. Mukaintu bamubbida *mpotomona* yamali. = They stole the purse of money from the woman.

crested crane, ostritch, (Ila) e.g. *Impowani* zijanwa mumanyika ali ku-musanza. = Ostriches are found in countries which are to the south. *Impowani* yakatija akutalika kukkala muzibanda. = The ostrich ran away and began to live in the plains. Also impye, impo.
wart, mole, e.g. Chitenge uciswa *mpu* akuulu. = Chitenge suffers from a wart on her leg.
a cattle-disease, e.g. Inombe zyanjilwa *bulwazi bwampu* zilafwa kapati. = When cattle are infected by the mpu disease, many die.
a short-bladed spear, e.g. *Mpula ndesumo lyakali kuyasizya balozi kaindi.* = The mpula is a short-bladed spear with which people used to pierce witches long ago.
a farm, e.g. Mweenzuma ujisi lubono lunji *ampulasi* yakwe. = My friend has many possessions on his farm.
basket used as a plate, e.g. *Kamucibikka nsima mumpulilo* eyi. = Add more nsima on this plate.
lower part of the ear, e.g. Mulwati bakamuuma nyindi *yampulukutwi.* They beat the fighter on the lower part of the ear with the fist.
plant with edible leaves, e.g. Amukalete *mpululwa* ijikwa cisyu. = Go and bring the edible leaves which are cooked as relish.
a yemsbok, e.g. Meja *ampulumbu* alandabele buyo, taagogomene kapati koobokela kumakosi. = The horns of the yemsbok are pointed straight upwards and not curved towards the back of the head.
round stones or clay used to kill birds with catapults, e.g. Basankwa balabelesya *mpulumbu* kuumya tuyuni. = Boys use small round stones to kill birds.
a window, a loop-hole, e.g. Mangoye ulasondela *ampulungwido.* = The cat is peeping through the window.
honey-comb with honey, e.g. Inzuki zijisi *mpuma* zipati-pati ciindi camupeyo. = Bees have large combs filled with honey during the cold season.
a stationary mass of people, e.g. Ndajana *mpumba* yabantu mpati mumugwagwa. = I found a crowd of people massed in the road.
a collection or group of things of the same type, e.g. *Impumba* zyabasokwe zyakandiyoosya munzila. A herd of monkeys frightened me on the way.
coil or mass of hair at back of head, e.g. Basimbi balayanda kubamba *mpumbe* mumutwe mazubaano. = Girls like to make attachments of hair at the back of their heads nowadays.
fourth stomach of ruminants, e.g. Banyama bayobweda mu*mpumbwe* ncobalya. Animals keep what they eat in their fourth stomach.
small ball of feathers set in front of the hair, e.g. *Mpumbwe* zikkala kumbele lyaboya zilapepela. The small balls of feathers which are set in front of the hair are blown about.
very early rains, e.g. *Impumpaluya* njiyakamenesya mweemvwe. The first rains made the fresh grass sprout. Also mpompaluya.

an armlet of grass, an extension of hair covering the nape of the neck, e.g. Bamakaintu balayanda kubamba *mpumpu* yamasusu kumakosi. = Women like to make an extension of hair hanging from the back of the head.
head of knobkerry, e.g. Nkoli yangu ijisi *mpumpu* mpati. My knobkerry has a large head.
rice, e.g. Bansame balayanda kulya *mpunga.* Indian people like to eat rice.
a weir (large barrier in a river composed of stones and timber stakes), e.g. Meenda akakkalila *mumpuo* yabasibbuku. = The water has settled behind the weir of the headman.
a tuft of hair at end of cow's tail, e.g. Mucende okwesu ujisi *mpusa*
Our ox has a big tuft of hair at the end of the tail.
a grey snake (belts made from skin of grey snake), e.g. Mutinta usamide mpusi mucibuno. = Mutinta is wearing a grey snake belt around the waist.
a stick to stir, as sour milk, a mixer made out of a stick, e.g. Kobelesya mpusyo kupwaya makoto ansima. = Use the stick to break the lumps of nsima.
the binding around a spearshaft, made from ox-tail, e.g. Isumo lyaumya mputi mumunyama. = The spear has gone deep into the animal as far as the shaft.
a rodent living in large communities, e.g. Kuli mpuukwe zinji mumuunda oyu. There are many rodents in this field.

fame, glory, e.g. Muleya wakajisi mpuwo mpati mubbola. = Muleya had a great reputation in football. Mpuwo yakubota kwamwana wamwami yakamvwugwa mucisi coonse. = The fame of the beauty of the chief's child spread throughout the whole land.
view, opinion, talk, e.g. Sena muliimwide mpuwo yakuti munene Buumba ulalowa? Have you heard the talk that the old man Buumba bewitches?
source, e.g. Kamuya mukateke meenda kumpwaampwa. = Go and draw water at the source. Also mpompo, mpoompo.
exit of burrow, e.g. Syaanasulwe wakazwa ampwaido = The hare went out through the outlet. Also mpwido

funeral-beer, e.g. Ayoozwa kuli maila akunyikila mpwaila? = Where will the grain come from for making yeast for funeral beer? Bamwi bantu tabanywi bukoko bwampwaila, bakasilikwa. = Some people do not drink funeral-beer, they have been healed. (i.e. In their treatment for sickness they have taken medicine which does not permit them to drink funeral-beer) Also mapwaila, mweesyo

actions which can displease people and which can even lead to a court-case, e.g. Ntunjaanji twaambo twampwazinga ntwaakali kucita, pesi bunji bwato wakali kutuzunda akaambo kabumpelenge mbubona obu. = There were many bad actions which he was doing, but he could succeed in defending himself because of the same cleverness.
borer-beetle, e.g. Mumuunda omu kuli mpwe zinji. In this field there are many borer-beetles.
entrance to animal's burrow, e.g. Atukateye banyama kumpwedo. = Let us trap the animals at the entrance of the burrow. Also mpo

a murderer when troubled by the spirit of his victim will say or act in a way that reveals his/her guilt, e.g. Muntu wajaya muntu ulaa kampwelempwele. A person who has killed another will be urged by the spirit of his victim to reveal his/her crime.
a hole going right through, an escape hole in a burrow, e.g. Imbeba yazwida ampwido. A rat came out of the escape hole.
a large quail (an edible migratory bird related to the partridge), e.g. Ndajaya bampwii botatwe. = I have killed three quails.
a loop-hole, e.g. Kojalula mpwiningido unjile muya. = Open the gap to let in fresh air. Also mpulungwido.
a hole in cloth, wall or fence, e.g. Imbeba yadonkola mpwiningizyo acisani cangu. = A rat has made a hole in my cloth.
a young child characterized with running nose, e.g. Ooyu mwana ucili mpwitamanina. = This child is still very young.
a heifer (a young cow that has not more than one calf), a female calf, e.g. Ndakaula nombe: basune bobile ampwizi zyotatwe. = I bought cattle: two oxen and three heifers.
cunning, e.g. Basankwa balaa mpyata mbuli syaanamabumba. = The boys were as cunning as a hare.
an ostritch, e.g. *Mpye zilaluma.* = Ostriches bite. Also *mpo, mpowani,mpiye.*
a length between two joints in reed, any joint or nodule in grass, knuckle, e.g. Amundipe *mpyungu yamu-*
yomwe buyo. = Give me just one joint of the sugar-cane stick.
a large bushbuck, e.g. Babwa bakaluma mubabala jilo. = The dogs attacked a bushbuck yesterday.
hot milk mixed with a little flour, gruel, e.g. Beembezi bajika mubabo wamukupa mobeembelela. = The herders cook hot milk mixed with a little flour at their herding places.
gruel Also mubabo.
a person of different race or colour, pl. mibala, e.g. Kuli mweenzu wamubala umbi mumunzi wesu. = There is a visitor of a different colour in our village.

muntu weelede kumucenga kwaamba kuti oku nkotukkede tuli bamubala waandeene peepe, tatuli beenzu, pele beenzu mbabaabo batubukila. = No one should deceive you saying that here where we live we are of different colours, we are not strangers, but the strangers are those who rise up against us.
colour, e.g. *Mubala wamulembo oyu mmubotu kapati.* = The colour of this cloth is very beautiful.
types of birds, a saddle-billed stork, a wimbrel, e.g. Muyuni ngwaajaya musankwa *mmubale.* = The bird which the boy killed is a saddle-billed stork.
a collar-bone, e.g. Munene watyoka *mubalo* naawa munanda. = The old man broke his collar-bone when he fell in the house.
a hoop, a steering wheel, e.g. Namutekenya ujisi *mubalo wamoota.* = The driver is holding the steering wheel.

a type of tree, used for making torches, e.g. *Mubalubalu tuusikkwi acikko nkaambo ulapasauka.* = Wood of the mubalubalu tree is not put in the fire as it sparks. (Chips of mubalubalu wood are used to make a torch at swarming time to catch termites by attracting them from their mound into a pit.)
a kick, e.g. *nombe yauma*
mubamb= The cow has kicked it's own calf. Also *musembele*
a keeper, a maker, e.g. *Mubambi wazisuwo ujisi bubi amulimo wakwe.* = The basket-maker is busy at her work.
type of tree (Cassia singueana), wood used for sledge and building construction. e.g. Bantu bafwala ngoma bayanda *mubambiangoma.* = People who carve drums like the mubambiangoma tree.
conversation, e.g. Ino mujisi *mubandi nzi utamani?* = What kind of endless talk have you?

an ironwood tree (pericopis angolensis), hard, heavy and very durable wood, turns well, has a beautiful finish and takes a high polish, used for fence posts, turning and carving, firewood and charcoal. Leaves and bark are used in the treatment of headaches and the steam from the leaves when inhaled is said to drive out bad spirits. e.g. Cisamu camubanga tacibumbwi mulazyi. = A mubanga tree is not eaten by termites.
a meeting, e.g. Bazyali bali mumubangano wacikolo. = The parents are at a meeting at the school. Also muswaangano, mubungano.
a careless person, e.g. Mukaintu mubaya takukuli alubuwa. = A careless woman does not sweep the courtyard.
a trader, pl. babbalampoto, e.g. Tamweelede kundiita kuti ndi
nkaambo ndimwana wacisi. You should not call me a trader because I am a local inhabitant.
Christian baptism, e.g. Sunu kucikombelo kuli *mubbapatisyo* wabana. = Today there is baptism for children at the church.
a large stretch of unploughed land left between furrows, e.g. Balimi basiya *mubbanga* mupati. = The ploughers have left a large gap of unploughed land between the furrows.
a loin cloth, e.g. Nobatumbu, amumubikke *mubbangi* mwana tweende. = Woman, put a loin-cloth on the child and let us go.
a type of tree with edible fruit, e.g. Tuya kukulya *mubbayi* mumilundu. = We are going to eat *mubbayi* fruit among the hills.
a loin-cloth, e.g. Munene usamide *mubbeso*. The old man is wearing a loin-cloth. Also *mubbiindwa*
a thief, e.g. *Mubbi* wakandibbida mpongo yangu. = A thief stole my goat.
any plant cultivated under irrigation, e.g. Ku Dindi nkobalima *mubbiida*. = Down in the Valley is where they have agriculture under irrigation. Also *muliide*
a loin cloth, pl. *mibbiindwa*, e.g. Kaindi basankwa bakali kusama *mibbiindwa*. = Long ago the men wore loin-cloths. Also *mubbeso, mubangi, mubingile*.
a loin-cloth, pl. *mibbingilo*, e.g. Kaindi bakali kusama *mibbingilo*. = Long ago they used to wear loin-cloths. Also *mubbiindwa*.
the big castor-oil plant, e.g. Mafwuta *amubbono* alananwa. = The oil of the castor-oil plant is used to anoint.
a Boer, pl. Mabbunu, e.g. Ampulasi ya *Mubbunu* milimo mmiyumu kapati. = On the Boer's farm the tasks are very difficult.
a race, e.g. *Atucite mubebe kusikila kucikolo.* = Let us compete in a race as far as the school.
a liar, e.g. *Utatobeli mubeji, ulakusowa.* = Do not follow a liar, he will mislead you.
a type of tree (wood used for timber and fruit eaten by birds) e.g. *Mubele oyu ulizyede kapati mwaka uno.* = This *mubele* tree is very prolific this year.
a type of relish, e.g. *Mubele* ncisyu cinunkilila kabotu. = *Mubele* relish has a delightful smell.
a worker, e.g. *Oomu mumbewu kuli mubeleki omwe.* = Here in the garden there is one worker. Also mubelesi.
paid-work, labour, e.g. *Ndijisi mubeleko uyanda mubelesi.* = I have a job which needs a worker.
a worker, pl. *babelesi*, e.g. *Tatujisi babelesi banji.* = We do not have many workers. Also mubeleki
a rodent, e.g. *Kaaze wajaya mubende mupati.* = The cat killed a big rodent.

the spleen (abdominal organ involved in maintaining proper condition of blood in most vertebrates), e.g. *njombe yafwa denkete inga mubenqwa ulizimbide.* = The spleen of a cow which died of 'corridor' disease is swollen.
a liar, pl. *babesi*, e.g. *Bantu babesi balayanda kwaamba twakubeja.* = Liars want to speak untruths. Also mubeji.
a judge, e.g. *Mubetesi waukosola kabotu mulandu wangu.* = The judge judged my case fairly.
a type of bird, e.g. *Basankwa bajaya mubeya mupati mumusena.* = The boys have killed a big bird in the vlei.
a carver, carpenter, joiner, e.g. *Ndaunka kumubezi andifwalile joko.* = 1 am going to the carpenter so that he makes me a yoke.
a cultivated or irrigated plant, a vegetable, a vegetable garden, e.g. *Baama balabeleka mumubiida* = Mother is working in the vegetable garden. Also mubbiida.
a lion cloth Also mubbiindwa.
the first day of mourning, the loud cry of mourning, e.g. *Mubila walimvwisya kale.* The cry of mourning has already been heard. Bakatalika kukwaya *mubila.* They began to weep (at a funeral)
whistle of a train, e.g. *Citima cakawuuma mubila.* = The train whistled.
a person who is quick and efficient in acting.
the body, e.g. *Mubili wangu onse ulacisa.* = My whole body is paining.

the leadwood tree, (Combretum imberbe), the wood is dark brown to black and is extremely hard and heavy. The white ash is used as a flavouring with boiled tamarind, and makes an excellent whitewash. Used for railway-sleepers, farm implements. A dark brown dye can be obtained from the roots. Leaves and bark have medical uses. e.g. *Munjanji babikka masamu amubimba.* = They put sleepers made of *mubimba* wood for the railway line.

the quinine tree (*rauvolfia caffra*) Can exude a copious flow of white latex which is poisonous. The leaves are like mango leaves. Has yellow flower and grape-sized fruits. Its reputed efficacy against malaria is now considered doubtful. It contains various alkaloids. Used as protection against witchcraft. Bark medicine can stop nose-bleed. e.g. *Koya ukandiside miyanda yamubimbi ndisilisye.* = Go and dig for me *mubimbi* roots so that I heal myself.
a loin cloth, e.g. *Kamubbangila bana amibingililo.* = Dress the children with loin-cloths. Also mubbindwa, mubbingilo, mubbeso.

type of tree (*Boscia Angustifolia*). Has a yellowish-white wood which has a bad smell when fresh cut. Is fairly heavy and hard, saws and works easily, finishing to a fine surface. It has been used to make chessboards. Powdered bark used to treat sores. Root medicine used to promote female fertility. Also mumbombwe, musansa.
trunk of elephant, pl. *miboko*, e.g. *Muboko wamuzovwu mmupati.* = The trunk of the elephant is big. Also mubombo, muzinga.
trunk of elephant, e.g. *Muzovwu wakamunyamuna mukaintu a mubombo akumupwaila ansi.* = The elephant lifted up the woman with its trunk and smashed her on the ground.

a type of tree whose fibrous bark has many uses, e.g. *Loozi Iwamubombo ndubotu kuvwumbya maanda.* = The fibres of the *mubombo* tree are good for thatching houses. *Wakanjila mumasamu manji aamibombo kusoleka kufwunda ngozi zyakusyuunta musinza wakuti inga ulanywisya mwana.* = She entered many forests of *mubombo* trees trying to strip off the bark and suck out the juice to make her child drink. mubondo
a barbel fish, e.g. *Mubondo wajikwa kaindi ulanona.* = A barbel fish which has been cooked for a long time is tasty.
muscle of the calf of the leg, e.g. *Mubondo wakosoka mukuulu kwamoombe.* = The muscle is cut in the leg of the calf.

a young tender shoot, pl. *mibonga*, e.g. *Bakwale bamana mibonga mumuunda.* = The partridges have finished off the tender shoots in the field. Also munsonje mubono castor-oil plant, e.g. *Mafwuta amubono* akali kunanwa abooye kaindi. = The oil of the castor-oil plant was used by the girls in the past. Also mubbono.
soil which retains moisture, e.g. *Mupunga ukomena kabotu muvwu lyamubonsi.* = Rice grows well in wet soil.

a gentle, kind person, e.g. *Ooyu muntu mmubonzu.* = This person is kind and gentle. Also mubombe muboola late mealies, pl. miboola, e.g. *Mapopwe amuboola alanona kapati.* = Late mealies are very tasty. Also mutetela
a good or beautiful person, e.g. *Ndiyanda mubotu.* = I like a good person.
a bundle e.g. Basilikani bakali kuyandaula *mubu* walubanje. = The police were looking for a bundle of hemp. Also mubbu.

type of tree (Albizzia versicolor) used for making drums, e.g. Misamu *yamububa* taijaniki kuno ku Chikuni. = *Mububa* trees are not found here at Chikuni. Wakatalika kuyandaula cisamu *camububa*. Ncibotu kusambya akusanzizya nkaambo cijisi covwu libotu. = She began to search for a *mububa* tree. It is good for washing oneself or other things as it has plenty of good lather. Also cisomwe, muchacha, munsomwe, mwangule.
a plant (Vangueria tomentosa), fruit eaten raw in March-April. e.g. Basimbi balya *mububu* mumilundu. = The girls eat the fruit of the *mububu* plant in the hills. (Its fruit is imbubu)

the name of the wild-nut tree (timber used for drums and mortars) e.g. *Mubula* oyu wabizwa kale. This fruit of the *mubula* tree is already ripe. Kana kaceta kakali kusobana *mumubula*. = The young monkey was playing in the *mubula* tree.
a statue, a figurine, something moulded, e.g. Murnanda omu kuli muntu *mubumbe*. = Here in the house there is a statue of a person.
a potter, e.g. *Mubumbi* ujisi zibiya zibotu zisumikidwe kale. = The potter has good pots which are already burnt.
a type of wild-cherry tree, black grape near the ground, e.g. Bana *bamubumbu* balanona. = The fruits of the wild-cherry tree are sweet.

a medicinal plant (Lannea stuhlmannii) used for toothache you rinse the affected part of mouth with hot water containing root. e.g. Kamundipa miyanda ya *mubumbu* ndisilike linyo licisa. = Give me the roots of the *mubumbu* tree so that I heal my sore tooth.
a small fertile field, raised bed of earth in garden, e.g. Tusimpa cisyu *mumubunda*. = We are planting vegetables in a raised bed. Also mubundu
a cut, a slash, pl. mibunda, e.g. Kwacaala mubunda mpaawumwa cimboko Joojo. = The mark remains where Joojo was beaten with a sjambok.

type of tree (Ekebergia Benguelensis) Soft wood used to make pillows and bowls, leaves are used to treat snake-bite and to cure dizzy spells. Used by hunters to placate spirit of a lion they have killed. Bark is used as an enema, whilst the roots are used to promote fertility, increase desire and cure venereal disease. Also mupusho. e.g. Katucela matu *amubundikwa* tukasilike walumwa nzoka. = Let us gather the leaves of the *mubundikwa* tree so that we go and heal the one bitten by a snake.
a raised patch of soil for growing vegetables, pl. mibundu, e.g. Kuli cisyu cibotu *mumibundo* eyi. = There is good relish in these raised beds. Also mubundu.
heap of raised earth for planting sweet-potatoes, a bed for planting, pl. mibundi, e.g. Kamubamba mibundu yacimbwali. = Make heaps of raised earth for planting sweet-potatoes.
a gathering of people, e.g. Sunu kuli mubungano wamayake kucikolo. Today there is a meeting about buildings at the school.

a type of tree with good fibrous bark and good timber, e.g. Musamu mubungu-bungu mmubotu kweebela. = The mubungu-bungu tree is admirable. Miindi yamusimbi oyu yakali kubaanga njamubungu-bungu. = The lower legs of this girl were like that of a mubungu-bungu tree. Kuli Kazila buumi bwakucikolo bwakali bubotu nokuba kuti tiilyakali mbuli tuvwu lyamubungu-bungu. = To Kazila life at school was good even though it was not like the leaves of a mubungu-bungu tree. (i.e. it was not good in every way) Kazyalanzubo wakali mubotu kaka mbuli tuvwu lyamubungubungu linga ndibbotu koonse-koonse. = Kazyalanzubo was so good like the leaf of a mubungubungu tree which is good on all sides.

an unweaned calf, e.g. Moombe ucili mubutu ulayanda kusobana. = A calf which is still unweaned likes to play. Ndalindila mbuli moombe mubutu ulaa banyina basweeka. = I will wait like an unweaned-calf who has a lost mother.

a baobab tree (Adansonia digitata), pl. mibuyu, having soft spongy wood - used for fishing floats. Inner bark yields a strong fibre for rope making. Seed pods used for musical rattles, snuff boxes, containers, and for carving into curios. The fruit pulp when dissolved in water can make a refreshing drink and can be used to make porridge. Its Vitamin C content is one of the highest known in a natural fruit. e.g. Mibuyu ilajanwa kapati munsi amulonga wa Zambezi. = Baobab trees are found especially beside the Zambezi river.
a question, e.g. Ino mubuzyo oyo uwamba nzi? = What does that question mean?
a dog, e.g. Mubwa utanda kasulwe mugundu. = The dog is chasing a rabbit in the bush.

a type of tree (Commiphora mollis), resinous, grown from cuttings, planted in kraals. Root sucked for water. e.g. Zisamu zyamubwabwa zilasyuuka. = The wood of the mubwabwa tree sprouts. e.g. Mumbali-mbali acuumbwe bakasimpa masamu aamubwabwa kutegwa akukomena masamu aaya cuumbwe cakwe citakalubwi nkaambo bantu bakali kumuyanda akumulemeka. = Beside the grave they planted a mubwabwa tree so that when the trees grew his grave would not be forgotten because the people loved and respected him. Also muntyokela, mubwaabwa, mumbala.
an orphan, e.g. Ncintu cikatazya kulela mucaala. = It is difficult to rear an orphan.

a type of tree (Cassia tora), the leaves of which are used for relish, it is oil-bearing, the seeds as for mbono. Kamucela matu amucaca tujike. = Bring the leaves of the mucaca tree so that we cook them. Also cisomwe.
a wedding, e.g. Kuli mucado mupati sunu ku Chikuni. = There is a big wedding today at Chikuni.

an acacia tree (short-hooked thorns and gum arabic), a thorn tree with straight thorns, e.g. Inziba yayaswa bumvwa bwamucagwe yaalilwa kuuluka. = The dove which was pierced by the thorn of an acacia tree was unable to fly.

noisy chewing, e.g. Muntu mubaya ulaa mucamfwu mubi. = A careless person makes unpleasant noise while mucanka chewing. Also incanku, mucamfwi attractiveness, (as of food or clothes), sweetness, e.g. Cakulya cajikwa kabotu cilijisi mucanka. Well prepared food is enticing. Casiya mucanka. = It leaves a sweet taste.

witch-cleanser, diviner, witchfinder, pl. bamucape, e.g. Kwakasika mucape ubona mumunzi wesu. A witchfinder who really finds (the witch) has arrived in our village. Also munanga. mucapo an attitude of despising others, e.g. Uulya musankwa ulaa mucapo. That boy is fond of despising.
invader, e.g. Nsiyandi kujayigwa abacavwila. = I do not want to be killed by invaders.
a driver of yoked oxen, e.g. Basune bajisi mucayili mubotu baleenda kabotu. = When oxen have a good driver they move well.
one who has left home for many years, e.g. Sunu kuli mweesyo wamucconi. = Today there is a funeral remembrance for one who left home a long time ago.
younger sibling, e.g. Kapika mmuce wa Kabimba. = Kapika is the younger sibling of Kabimba.
an immature child which has no knowledge of danger, e.g. Mwana mucece usobanya mulilo. = An immature child plays with fire.

type of tree (Ziziphus abyssinica), fruits eaten May-June. Young leaves pounded and cooked after pounding for green relish. Medicinal juice from leaves applied to inner ear, juice from root bark presssed against sores (juice contains tannic acid). e.g. Kuti kotajisi muteezi nkujika mucecece. = If you do not have okra, cook the pounded leaves of the mucecece tree. Also mucecete
type of tree (hooked thorns, fruit eaten in time of famine, root used as laxative), e.g. Matuvwu amucecete alajikwa muteezi. = The leaves of the mucecete tree are cooked as relish. Also sikomwa
type of snake, (boa-constrictor, python), e.g. Ndajana muceka wamena kambaambi. = I found a python had swallowed a duiker. Also imbooma, insato.

soft-footed quadruped animal, e.g. Inkuku zyangu zyalumwa mucele. = A soft-footed quadruped animal has finished my chickens. Misyobo yanswi bazezyi bamwi njobazela mminiini-niini mbuli ntuunga bacele, babondo, atunsenga. Some kinds of fish which fishermen fish for are very small like bacele, barbel and tunsenga

fruit, pl. micelo, e.g. Misyobo yamicelo yamucisi ca Zambia mmanji. = There are many kinds of fruit in Zambia. Micelo yacisi iligwa: = native edible fruits: Manego/matobo; masaansa, masyuuntwa/mafwumo/nombe-fwumo; im'umbu zyaansi, im'umbu zyamujulu; manono/manombyo/manono, banabaciwezyezi; makumbuzu/mansangu-sangu aligwa intuumbulwa; masuku; mbula; impondo, incenje; kawi; igabo, mamvwuma; inkomone; mabuyu; insikili; mateme; munyoonyo; manomba; insombo;impana; maloolo, mikonyombwa; inkuyu, cilembela, intumbi, inkunyu-nkunyu, imvwuli; inkoloondo; imbuukuma, imbubu, masunka; in'unda; incinga; Micelo yakaletwa imported fruits: mafwuleenke, malemani, mango, magwaba, mapoposi, malubbeni. Micelo yacisi ikola native poisonous fruits: mukamba/ impaapa; syaampiki/ syaanciiki; cinyamwaaba, mudimpwinini; bana bamungunya.
medicine, drug, poison, e.g. Ngooyu mucelo wamwida. Here is a medicine for the stomach. (note: Some say that abamuzwamasi = musamu is the correct word for medicine not mucelo.)
an old woman, e.g. _Munanda yamucembele taumani mulilo._ = In the house of an old woman the fire never dies.
midwife, e.g. Mukaintu utumbusya wiitwa kuti *mucembele* mu Chitonga. = A woman who assists to deliver the child is called *mucembele* in Chitonga.

a reddish variety of sorgum, e.g. *Muceme ulaligwa kapati buyuni, aboobo kuti walima muceme uleelede kuyamina buyuni.* = Red sorgum is eaten a lot by flocks of birds, therefore if you plant red sorgum you need to guard it from the birds.

a bull/buck, e.g. *Mucende wagombe mmukali. Inombe nozitilimuka, ulatanta akalundu. Ulalangisya mumbali, ulasyulungana akusinta abukali.* = The bull of the cattle is fierce. When the cows tremble, he climbs the hill. He looks carefully on all sides. He glares and roars in anger.
medicinal root used for the disease cibongozi, e.g. Kosya miyanda yamucende usilikwe cibongozi. Dig the mucende roots so that the disease of the anus may be healed.
type of tree (grows on termite hills, leaves liked by cattle) e.g. *Akaulu alya mpaali mucende-cende.* = On that termite hill there is a mucendecende tree.

a bush with edible berries, e.g. Bana balya *mucende-cende* muluumba. = Children eat edible berries among the muumba trees. *mucendewa-basokwe* type of tree (Bridelia cathartica), e.g. Sulwe uli mujungusi *amucendewa-basokwe.* = A hare is under the *mucendewa basokwe* tree.

the red milkwood tree with fragrant white flowers and round yellow fruits (high in Vitamin C), and has a hard, heavy fine-grained wood. e.g. _Makupa a mucenenge alasubila-subila._ = The sap of the red milkwood tree is reddish.
trout, pl. baceni, e.g. Muzeli waca *muceni* mupati. The fisherman caught a big trout.
type of tree, e.g. Bana balya *ncenje mumucenjakotwe.* = The children are eating the fruit of the mucenjakotwe tree.

type of tree, (Diospyros kirkii) edible fruit, can grow to a great height on termite-hills, has good timber, also called mucenjelekete. e.g. Inkwilinti zilya *ncenje mumucenje.* Green pidgeons eat the *ncenje* fruit from the mucenje tree. *Mucenje mmubotu kufwala majoko.* *Mucenje* wood is good for making yokes. (Also known as Diospyros mespiliformis)
a termite which builds large hills, pl. bamacenje, e.g. *Bamacenje* bandiluma nindalikuteya nswa. The termites bit me when I was trapping flying-ants. Also macenya
an observant intelligent person, e.g. Muntu *mucenjezu* uleeleba milandu. An intelligent person avoids crimes.
a poor person, e.g. Kanene tajisi zisani nkaambo *mmucete.* = Kanene has no clothes because he is poor.
a rich person, e.g. Muntu ujisi lubono lunji *mmucezi.* A person who has a lot of wealth is a *mucezi.*
Saturday, e.g. Bamwi bantu bakomba Leza *Mucibelo.* Some people pray to God on a Saturday. Also Mujibelo,

a tail, a fly-whisk, e.g. Ingulube ijisi *mucila* mufwiifwi kapati. A pig has a very short tail. Kutayiisya mwana musimbi nkulilya *mucila.* (idiomatic) = Not to educate a girl child is to eat one's tail.
a clan name among the Zimbabwean Batonga whose totem is the baboon. e.g. Mukowa wa _Bacimba ngowa_
The Mucimba clan is the same as the Baloongo clan.
the post or pole at the entrance to a kraal, pl. micincili, e.g. _Mucincili watyoka, amukagonke umbi._ = The post of the krall entrance is broken, cut another one.
a foolish person, e.g. Muntu mucinda ulacita zintu zisofweede. = A foolish person does despicable things.
a member of the clan whose totem is the lion, pl. Bacindu, e.g. _Bacindu mbajwanyina a Bansaka._ = The Bacindu clan have a joking relationship with the Bansaka.

type of shrub (_Popowia obovata_), the powdered bark of root is rubbed dry into small cuts around the neck to cure stiffness, the roots are also used to prepare a drink to alleviate pain in pregnancy, a red fruit growing in bunches, also the shrub bearing that fruit. e.g. Basimbi balalya _mucinga_ musyokwe. = Girls eat _mucinga_ fruit in the bush.
the border, as of field, pl. micinga, e.g. Balimi balwanina _micinga_ yamyuunda yabo. The farmers are fighting about the borders of their fields. Also munyinza
a type of tree mucinjili a big stick used as a gate, pl. micinjili, e.g. Kamujazya _micinjili_ mipati aciba. Close the kraal with big poles. Also mucincili
sister, e.g. _Mucisi_ wangu waya kucibbadela. My sister has gone to the hospital. Also mucizyi, mucizi.
a dependant, e.g. Maambo ulela mucitwaansi omwe. = Maambo is in charge of one dependant.
a man's sister, e.g. _Mucizyi_ wakwe nguusambala cisyu mumbewu. = His sister is the one who sells the vegetables in the garden.
continuous rain, e.g. Ijilo kwakawa mvwula _yamucobocobo._ = The rain fell yesterday continually.

a large-leaved beech tree (_faurea speciosa_). The wood is light brown, mottled, hard and durable. Makes good charcoal and hut poles. used for boat-building and furniture. Roots are used for eye-infections and diarrhoea. Leaves and roots used for ear-infections. e.g. Bwato obu bwakafwalwa amusamu wamucoka. This boat was carved from a _mucoka_ tree. Also muvwunde, mungula, musenia.

a medicinal plant (_Olax disstiflora_) used for stomach upset by drinking chopped root in warm water, e.g. Muntu wakali kuciswa mwida wakaponezegwa a _mucombia-nsimba_. A person who had stomach-pains was cured by the mucombiansimba plant.
a ramrod, e.g. Bakali kubelesya mucomyo nibakali kulida buci mumpako yamusamu. = They were using a rod when they were taking the honey from a hole in the tree. (vb. -cokomya = poke out.)
a spoon, pl. baconco, e.g. Mutinta wakalijisi zyoonse zyakubelesya mbuli ncili, nsefwa, _baconco_, zinyandya azimwi Mutinta had all utensils such as mortars, sieves, spoons, dishes and other things.

the wild or sour plum-tree (_Ximenia Americana_). Edible fruits are also used to make a sour preserve or an intoxicating drink. Seed is used for soapmaking and lubrication, body and hair oil and for softening leather. e.g. Bamwi bantu balabamba nsipa zyamuconfwa. = Some people make soap from the seed of the wild plum-tree. Also muconvwa

a medicinal plant (_Ximenia americana_), also known as convwapati, the root is chopped and taken in water for stomach ache. It is also used as a cleansing agent after childbirth, the root being used as a sponge with warm water to remove the blood. e.g. Mutumbu bamusanyza meenda amusamu *muconvwa*. = They wash a mother who has given birth with water and medicine from the *muconvwa* plant. Also *muconfwa*.

an oil-bearing plant (*Ximenia americana*), the seeds are beaten and rubbed into skins to soften them. e.g. *Konana mucovwa alukanda*. = Rub the *mucovwa* oil into the skin. The fruit eaten raw Nov.- March. Seed kernel may be eaten raw also may provide oil for body anointing and softening of animal skins. Medicinally, leaves sucked for sore throat roots used as bowel medicine. e.g. *Kuti waciswa amoyo nkunywa mucovwa*. = If you have a sore throat, drink *mucovwa* medicine. Also *muconvwa*.

type of tree giving wattles, e.g. Twakabamba nzonde zya*mucuncu-cuulu*. We made sticks from the *mucuncucuulu* tree. *Mucuncu-cuulu ulasilika malwazi manji*. = The *mucuncucuulu* tree heals many diseases. Also *musunsu-cuulu*.
a grass-dredge used for fishing, e.g. Balajaya nswi zinji *amucundulusio*. They kill many fish with a grass-dredge.
elderly man, e.g. *Mudaala ulaa maano manji*. The old man has much wisdom.
a long thing, e.g. Wakakkala *amudadaada wacuuno*. = He sat on a bench.

a line of people, words, etc., e.g. Wakanjila *mumudadada wacikambe-kambe*. She entered into the line of the cikambekambe dance. Meso aakwe taakazwa *amudadada ngwaakali kubala*. = Her eyes did not leave the line she was reading.
a heavy drinker, e.g. *Wakali mudakwa wabukoko citaambiki*. = He was a very heavy drinker.
a person who has stayed for a long time in city, e.g. Moonga *mmudakwa*. = Moonga has stayed for a long time in city. *mudebweenene* soft mud Also *makandya*
okra (*Hibiscus esculentus*), fruits, leaves or seeds used for relish, e.g. *Amujike mudelele tulisye nsima*. = Cook the okra so that we dip into it when eating *nsima*.

a clan-name (kutembaula = mbakkuli, bana syaalyoonda, bana simamvwa). The totem among the Zimbabwean Batonga is the zebra, e.g. Badenda mbasyoonto muzibaka zimwi. = The Badenda are not numerous in certain places.
darkness, e.g. Nsekonzyi kubona, munanda kuli *mudima*. = I cannot see, it is dark in the house.

type of dark black creeper, e.g. *Mudima mmusamu usilisya masoto*. = Mudima is a dark black creeper which heals a disease which is said to afflict children of one of their parents who has behaved promiscuously.
type of tree, e.g. *Mudimpwinini ncisamu citeteete kapati*. = The *mudimpwinini* is a very soft tree. Also *mubbayi*

A clan-name among the Zimbabwean Batonga whose totem is the baboon. e.g. *Badinda bajanwa ku Zimbabwe*. The Badinda are found in Zimbabwe *mudinkilwa* a muzzle gun, e.g. Kakucisiya-siya ansi wakabweza ntobolo ya mu*dinkilwa ngooyu wagama kumusanza*. = When it was still dark he took the muzzlegun, there he is going to the south.

meat picked where wild dogs ---|--have been feeding, e.g. *Eeyi ninyama ya-mudobo njindasosya baumpe.* = This is the meat which was left by the wild dogs when I scared them away. up, e.g. *Basankwa abasimbi wakaba mudyobe-mudyobe.* = The boys and the girls were mixed together.
a craving for food, e.g. *Ndabaa mudokodoko kubona cakulya.* = I have a craving to eat on seeing food. Also cinyomenezi, cilakalaka mudyongoli a short eel, pl. *bamudyongoli* Also mudyanga.
plants from which salt is extracted, e.g. *Sunu bantu bakauleka munyo wamudonga.* = People have stopped extracting salt from plants these days. Also munyo wabwengwa.
a poor person, e.g. *Muntu muvwubi tayelede kukaka kugwasya mufwabi.* A rich person should not refuse to help a poor person.
a castrated goat/sheep, e.g. *Bakajaya mudoonta mupati kunkolola.* = They killed a big castrated goat at the initiation ceremony. Also mudonta
type of tree (good timber for drums, mortars, etc.), e.g. *Eeyi ngoma njamufwalandido.* This drum is made from a mufwalandido tree.
a motorbike, e.g. *Mwiiyi uyendaa mudududu kucikolo.* = The teacher goes to school on a motor-bike.
a type of tree which produces gum, e.g. *Mufwate usilika malwazi manji.* The mufwate tree cures many diseases.
dampness, moisture, e.g. *Kociyanika cisani eco, cicilaa mudumu.* = Hang up that cloth to dry, it is still damp.
a narcotic poison, e.g. *Kuti wafweba mufweba-baazi inga wafwa.* = If you smoke the mufweba-baazi you will surely die.

a ridge, e.g. *Tuleelede kusiya mudunta mumuunda kukwabilila meenda.* = We should leave a ridge in the field to prevent erosion from the water. Also cituntatunta. + ridge of house or mountain = musana, moongola.
Also mufweba-baazi.
an acacia tree with hooked thorns, e.g. *Inziba ilikkede mumufwefwe.* = The dove is sitting in the acacia tree.

mud, e.g *Tatukonzyi kukolobeka mumuunda mucili mudwebweenene.* We cannot use the cultivator in a field which is still muddy. Also mankandya mufwembe a young animal, e.g. *Moombe ucili mufwembe, ulanyonka.* = The calf is still young, it is sucking. Also keenze
type of tree (produces the mudyaka or muloolo fruit), e.g. *Twalikulya mudyaki musyokwe.* We were eating the fruit of the mudyaki tree in the bush.

a heap of something that can be gathered in abundance such as tobacco or groundnuts, e.g. *Koya kamubwiide ndongwe amufwenku ulya.* = Go and gather up for him as many groundnuts as possible from that heap.
a short eel, pl. *bamudyanga*, e.g. *Muzyiba omu muli bamudyanga banji.* In this pool there are many short eels.
a smoker, e.g. *Koya ukandilombele tombwe kumufwezima.* = Go and ask my fellow-smoker for tobacco.
a mixture, a mix

a bundle of hemp, e.g. *Basililkani bakajata muntu ujisi mufwi walubanje.* = The police caught a person who had a bundle of cannabis. Also mubbu + a jealous person, e.g. *Oonse muntu uleelede kuba mufwi kumukaintu wakwe.* = Every man should be jealous as regards his wife.
a poisoned arrow, used by the Ba Ila and Ba Mukkuni, pl. *mifwi*, e.g. *Baila balajaya banyama amifwiyabweembe*. = The Ba Ila kill animals with poisoned arrows.
star-galaxy known as the Milky Way, e.g. *Sunu masiku Mufwimbi ulibonya kabotu*. = Tonight the galaxy of the Milky Way is clearly seen. Also *Mulalabungu*
a trench, furrow, e.g. *Kosyanga mapopwe mumufwolo watatu*. = Plant the maize in the third furrow.
a dead person, e.g. *Mufwu oyu wasiya bana fwuka*. = The deceased left nine children.
bee-bread, e.g. *Mufwu wanzuki ulanunkilila*. = The bee-bread of the bees smells nicely.
a dull person, e.g. *Muntu mufwuba taciti zintu zisalala*. = A dull person does not do intelligent things.
soaked meal, e.g. *Baama babamba mufwuba wakukumbya bukoko*. = Mother is preparing soaked-meal for brewing beer.
a fool, e.g. *Mufwubafwuba tazwidilili mumisunko yakwe*. = A foolish one does not pass his/her examinations.
heart of a young palm, e.g. *Kasako kamufwubu wakavwuma nkayumu*. = Wood of the core of a young palm-tree is hard.
a thorny bush, a tree whose leaves are applied to burns, e.g. *Mufwubyabiya mmucelo mubotu*. = The *mufwubyabiya* tree is good for medicine. Also *mufwubyabuya*

type of plant (*Coccinia adoensis*) fruit and tuber eaten raw and baked during rainy season, e.g. *Mudaala ukanga nseke zyamufwufwe*. = The old man is frying the seeds of the mufwufwe plant. Also *maziula*
a type of tree, e.g. *Mufwufwuma mmusamu ujanika ku Zambezi*. The *mufwufwuma* is a tree found at the Zambezi. Also *bwazi*.

the monkey orange or wild orange tree (*strychnos pungens*). The fruits are eaten by elephant and baboon as well as humans. However unripe fruits may cause giddiness and vomiting. Roots used for snake-bite, ear-drops and other medicinal and cosmetic purposes. e.g. *Bazovwu balya bana bamufwufwuna*. = Elephants eat the fruit of the *mufwufwuma* tree. Also *muvwavwa, muwana, muwitu*.
a root said to be medicinal, e.g. *Busi bwamufwulampeyo buzwisya zeelo*. = The smoke of the *mufwulampeyo* root is said to drive away evil spirits.
a song composer, e.g. *Ziimbo zinji zibambwa amufwula-nyimbo*. = Many songs are produced by a composer.
type of tree whose leaves are eaten by cattle, e.g. *Inombe zilalya matu amufwulimuninga*. = The cattle are eating the leaves of the *mufwulimuninga* tree. Also *nkoomwa*.
two measures of cloth, e.g. *Ndiyanda kuula mufwululu wamulembo uutuba*. = I want to buy two measures of white cloth.
a very thin or lean person, e.g. *Mapulanga mmufwulusi, tayelede kubweza zilemu*. = Mapulanga is a thin person, he should not lift heavy things.

type of small tree (*diospyros batocana*) The timber is fairly heavy with a light brown sapwood and a pinkish heart-wood, and though hard it can be worked and sawn easily, makes combs, spoons, cooking sticks and tool handles, protects against snake-bite. e.g. Bantu balatvala myuunge yamufwumbo. = People carve wooden-spoons from the mufwumbo tree. Also muntu-kushia.
a kidnapper, pl. bafwumbi, e.g. *Bafivumpi* bobile bakabba mwana wamyaka ciloba. = Two kidnappers stole a seven-year old child.
a tree with edible fruit, e.g. *Mufivumo* tauzyede pe. = The mufwumo tree has no fruit. Also *mufwumu*
member of the frog clan, pl. Bafwumo, e.g. Mungaila ukwete *Mufwumo*. = Mungaila has married a woman of the Mufwumo clan. Also *Mufwumu*
The wild medlar-tree (Vangueriopsis Lanciflora). The wood is light, soft and used for spoons. e.g. *Mufwumu* oyu taujisi mafwumu manji. = This mufwumu tree has few fruits. Also *musole*

type of tree, from which handles, mortars and roofing-poles are made, e.g. Mukalete tusamu twamufwunda tuyake kaluli. = Bring small poles of the mufwunda tree so that we make a little roof. Also *mufwundabaalu*.
a line traced, e.g. Kamutobelezya mufwunda kusika kumamanino amuunda. = Follow along the traced line to the end of the field.
a type of tree, e.g. Mwami uyenzya nkoli yamufwundansofwu. = The chief moves with a knobkerrie made from the mufwundansofwu tree. Also *kafwundula*.
a teacher, e.g. Basicikolo balindilila *mufwundisi* mucikolo. = The pupils are waiting for the teacher in the school. Also *mwiiyi*.
a mouth-full of food or drink, e.g. Nsejisi akutilila cibwantu, ndabikka buyo *mufwundo*. = I have nothing to put the sweet-beer into, I just took a mouth-full.
a track of a snake, e.g. *Ndajana mufwundundu wamulala mukalonga.* = I found the track of a black mamba in a stream. Also mukondo.
a line, of dark clouds, e.g. *Kuli mufwundundu wamakumbi amvwula usiya mbi.* = There is a line of dark rain clouds which are very black.
a crazy person, e.g. *Amulange muntu oyu, ucita mbuli mufwungu, mupati onse.* = Look at this person, he acts like someone crazy and yet he is an adult. Also *ciyanga, nzyinya*
a person made dull or stupid by charms, e.g. *Sena mwati ucita caali? Oyu mmufwungule kale.* = Do you think she does it deliberately? This one is already bewitched. Also *mufwungu, nzyinya*
a weaned-calf, e.g. *Ndakaula moombe mufwungusi kuli Moonde.* = I bought a weaned-calf from Moonde.
a walking-stick, e.g. *Mucembele uyenzya mufwunkizyo.* = The old woman walks with a walking-stick. Also mufwunko.
rod used as a walking-stick, e.g. *Ndakali kweenzya mufwunko nindakafwuyukide.* = I was using a walking-stick to move when I had a sprain. Also mufwunkizyo, kafwunko.
a very dull or obtuse person, e.g. *Ooyu tali muntu, mmufwunulanio.* = This one is not fully human, he is very dull.

the carrot tree (*steganotaenia araliacea*). The wood is light, sometimes used for carving. Various parts of the tree are used as hunting charms. Roots are used for treating the bewitched and in the extraction of missiles fired by a magic gun. Also used to treat fever and ease breathing. Roots and leaves contain alkaloids and saponins - used to treat bilharzia and to cure vertigo. e.g. *Basinombe balayanda kusobana ntobolo zya*mufwuti*. = The cattle-herders like to play with (toy) guns made from the *mufwuti* tree. Also *mukanda-nombe*, *mupelwa, mutobolo, mupelempefwa*.

a blacksmith, e.g. Ndaunka kukuulisya masimbi *kumufwuzi*. = I am going to sell charcoal to the blacksmith. *Mufwuzi ufwulida avwuba mulilo wamalasya ciindi nafwula zibulo*. = The blacksmith blows on the charcoal fire with a bellows when he is forging metals.
a boundary, a border, e.g. Mugwagwa *ngomugaano* wanyika yangu ayakwe. = The road is the boundary between my land and his. Also *munyinza*.
milled-meal, e.g. Bamwi bantu tabalyi nsima *yamugailwa*. = Some people do not eat *nsima* made from milled-meal.
an indolent person, e.g. Simwaampe *ngumugala*, mwana mutolo utayandi kweembela. = Simwaampe is an idler, a lazy child who does not want to herd.
whentiff or dry, e.g. Eeyi nsima yayuma *mugalanga*, ilakatazya kumena. = This *nsima* has become stiff, it is difficult to swallow. Also cinkalantu, cigalandanda, *mugalanganga*.
a clan-name of the Zimbabwean Valley Tonga whose totem is a frog. e.g. *Mugande mmukowa wabacula*. = A *Mugande* is of the frog clan.

a demarcation line or boundary, e.g. Eeyi myuunda *mugano* nkalonga. = The boundary between these fields is the stream. *Mugano kakali kalonga ka Chiseke*. = The border was the river Chiseke. Also *mugaano, munyinza*
a kind of dye, e.g. Mulembo bakauzekaula *amugano usubila*. = They decorated the cloth with a red dye.
a traditional wooden plate Also inkwandi
a ridge, pl. *migelo*, e.g. Kamukobelela *migelo nkaambo* ivwuna bulongo. Take care of the ridges because they retain the soil.

type of tree, has hooked thorns, exudes gum, timber used for long planks, bark used for home-made containers, e.g. Kuli cikwaangala uzyede *mumugoba muya*. There is a crow which has given birth there in the *mugoba* tree.
a heavy dark rain cloud threatening to fall, e.g. Sunu kuli *mugobo* mupati, kamutola nombe muciba. = Today the sky is covered with a huge black rain- cloud, take the cattle to the kraal.
a mine, a deep well, e.g. *Mugodi* wangu tauyuminini. = My well does not become dry.

a bag, the sheath of a gun, e.g. Musambazi wakaaka mwana mumu*godya* akumutola kunselelo nkwaakali kusambalila makwebo akwe. = The trader stuffed the child in a bag and took it down to where he was selling his wares.
a long trench, e.g. Amusye *mugolo mumbali ananda*. = Dig a trench beside the house. Also *lulindi*

type of tree, has medicinal roots, makes good charcoal, poles made from it are attacked by borers, e.g. *Mugololo mmusamu uzwa meenda cilimo*. = Water oozes from a *mugololo* tree during the dry season. Also *mukololo*.

the long quill of the *sigolyo* bird, long feather of cock's tail, pl. *migolyo*, e.g. Bantu bavwima mubwizu bulamfwu basama *migolyo* kuti kababonana. = Hunters wear long feathers on their heads when hunting in long grass so that they see one another.
a container (5-20 litres) for liquids, e.g. Koungula meenda mumugomo omo. = Pour the water out of that container.

a type of plant ( *Lannea discolor, Lannea stuhlmannii*), the nuts are used for relish, e.g. Kamuleta nseke zyamugongwa tujike cisyu. = Bring the seeds of the mugongwa plant so that we make relish. Also *mugogo*
the gum of the igoni tree, e.g. Inkuni zyamugoni zilayaka kabotu. = Firewood from the *mugoni* tree burns well. Also *mugooni*
a dye, e.g. Munyinsa wamugoni ula-sandula zisani. = The juice of *mugoni* acts as a dye to change the colour of clothes.
the old name for a soldier or policeman, e.g. Kaindi basikalumamba bakali kwiitwa kuti bagoni. Also *mugooni*
an echo, e.g. Mukkwilo ujisi mugonko usabila kapati. = The whip produces an echo which reverberates very much. (a riddle, Syanaziba ulaita mutala amulonga....Mmugonko.)

a medicinal plant (*Combretum microphyllum*), used to cure diarrhoea: the roots are chopped and drunk in warm water. e.g. Kamusilisya mulwazi usoomona amugonono. = Treat the patient who has diarrhoea with *mugonono*.
a mine or hole with big mouth and narrow bottom, e.g. *Mumugonti* omu muzwa lubulo lubotu. = Good ore comes out of this mine. Also *mugoti*
the kernel, pl. *migoogo*, e.g. Bana bapwaya *migoogo* mujungusi lyamubula. = The children are splitting the kernels underneath the *mubula* tree.
a type of tree, e.g. Bana bamugoongwa balaligwa. = The fruits of the *mugoongwa* tree are edible.
type of tree out of which mortars and handles are made, e.g. Matu amugooni mmabotu kusilika mwida. = The leaves of a *mugooni* tree are good for curing stomach pains.
a well, e.g. *Mugoti* wangu tauyuminini. = My well does not dry up. Also *mugonti, mugodi*.
faint spoor in grass, e.g. *Insezi zileenda mumugula*. Wild-cats follow faint spoor in the grass. Also *ikula*
a plant with edible roots, e.g. Beembezi batafwuna miyanda yamugulumya. = The herders are chewing the roots of the *mugulumya* plant.
waterbuck, e.g. Oomu mumulonga kwanjila mugundumu. = A waterbuck has entered the river there.
the sound or echo of axe, gun, drum, e.g. Ndayoowa nindamvwa mugunku wabavwimi. = I was frightened when I heard the sound of the hunters weapons. Also *mugonko*

a medicinal plant used for excessive eye lacrimation. Drops are used from the cold water containing beaten leaves. e.g. Kamusilisya mugunya-busenga muntu uciswa meso. = Heal the person with the eye-problem with pounded leaves from the *mugunya-busenga* tree mixed with water.

type of tree (*Grewia flavescens*). The fruit is pounded and drunk in warm water like a thin porridge. e.g. Lyanzala bantu balanywa mugunyu-gunyu. = At a time of famine people drink treated juice from a *mugunyugunyu* tree.
a bull, a ram, e.g. Butanga obu tabujisi amugutu nuuba omwe. = The herd has not even a single bull.
the sound of a shot, e.g. Nkuli kwalimvwinsya mugutulo? = Where has the shot been heard?
a roan-antelope, e.g. *Muguyu* wacembaala uyenda alikke. = An old roan-antelope moves alone.
a bull-buffalo e.g. Cimwi ciindi kwakasangana munyati mucende *muguyu* mukati kabutanga bwarnombe. = Some time ago a big bull-buffalo joined the herd of cattle. Also cilumbulumbu
a fish-trap, e.g. Kamukomenzya bunjililo bwamugwala kutegwa kunjile nswi zinji. = Enlarge the entrance of the fish-trap so that many fish enter. Also mungwala
a road, e.g. Ndabona basimbi baleenda mumugwaqwa. = I saw the girls moving along the road.
a broad open entrance, Also mugwanyanya

heavy kind of spear used at close quarters, e.g. Banene bakaindi bakali kubajaya basyuumbwa amugwaza wabujisi. = The old men of the past were killing lions while holding a heavy spear. (i.e. you hold on to the spear in combat instead of throwing it at the opponent)
daughter-in-law, son-in-law, e.g. *Mugwe* wangu wakandiyakila butala. = My son-in-law built me a granary. Also mukwe.
openness, as a door, e.g. *Mmugwenyenye* kumulyango. = The door is open. Also bukwazi, igwala
second portion of meal added to matimba (mixture of boiled fermented and non-fermented mealies) to transform it into beer. Also mukwilili
fermented gruel, e.g. Kamoozeka *mugwiliwili* tuvwele bukoko. = Cool the fermented gruel so that we mix it into the beer. Also mugwilili, mukwilili, mweele.

name of a tree, e.g. Choopa naakamvwa makani akulicisa kwa Mudyaka, wakayandaula makwa amunoongwe akumukandya. = When Choopa heard that Mudyaka had injured himself, he searched for the bark of a *munoongwe* tree to knead the wound.
report, rumour, e.g. Taakali kunjila muminzi mwakali *mununununu* wantomba. = She was not entering the village where there was a report about smallpox.
a clan name among the Zimbabwean Batonga whose totem is the pigeon, pl. Bainde, e.g. Mukaintu wangu mmuzyukulu wa Bainde. My wife is a grand-daughter of the Bainde clan.

The winter-thorn tree (*Acacia albida*) The wood is whitish, coarse grained, fairly tough and hard, but not very durable. It is easy to work and can be used for buildings, canoes, tool handles and rough furniture. Pods beans and leaves are good cattle food, but unripe pods may be poisonous containing prussic acid. In famine time the seeds are boiled and eaten either whole (like beans) or as a porridge. It is an ideal farm tree, and of great value to agriculture in dry areas and can be used as an indicator of underground water and of good arable land. e.g. *Mujagwe* ulayandika kukomena mumuunda nkaambo upa mbolezi kubulongo. The winter-thorn tree is needed in fields because it's leaves give manure to the land. Also musangu, munga
a particular kind of wood used for making the budima drum, e.g. Eezi ningoma nzyamujamuja. = These drums are made of wood from the *mujamuja* tree.
a medicinal root for hastening/preventing death in hopeless cases, e.g. Ooyu wakalya *mujatilizi* ncatafwi ino. = This one ate the medicine to prevent death that is why he does not die now.
a killer, a murderer, e.g. Muntu *mujayi* tayandiki mucisi. = A murderer is not wanted in the country.
a type of tree, e.g. Matu *amujejete* ali mbuli cinkomba. = The leaves of the *mujejete* tree are like delele. Also mucecete

a medicinal plant (*Cordia ghara*), a pointed stick of which is used to lift out vein of temple during treatment. e.g. Kodadula lusinga abumvwa bwamujelabatumbu. = Lift up the vein with a thorn of the mujelabatumbu tree.
a high cliff, e.g. Munyati walokela mumujeleele. The buffalo fell over a cliff.
a male goat, e.g. Mujembwe okwa Kacokolo walumwa nzoka. = The buck-goat of Kacokolo was bitten by a snake.
treeshorthooked thorns and gum arabic, e.g. Ndayaswa mamvwa amujence. = I was pierced by the thorns of an accacia tree.
type of tree (Diospyros kirkii), e.g. Inkwilinti nkozili mumujenje. = The pidgeons are in the mujenje tree. Also mucenje.
Saturday, e.g. Tuyakubonana mu Mujibelo kupobwe lyacigayo. = We shall see one another on Saturday at the celebration for the grinding-mill.
a hunter, e.g. Amunzi wamujimba abonwa zyaanza zyabanyama. = At the home of a hunter trophies are to be seen. Also muvwimi.
the sound of a footstep, e.g. Wandiyoosya mujinci wauzyana masiku. = The sound of the footstep of the nightdancer frightened me.
type of tree, e.g. Mujinga ulanona. The fruits of the mujinga tree are sweet. Also mujingajinga, mucinga, mucingacinga.
Also mucinga

a cook, e.g. Mujisi wamana kale kujika. The cook has already finished cooking. Also mujiki. mujola-bafwa medicinal root for hastening occurence of woman's menstruation, e.g. Mukaintu uciswa kalobola usilisigwa mujola-bafwa. A woman who is suffering from a gynacological problem is healed by a medicinal root, called mujolabafwa.

an untrained ox, e.g. Basankwa bakali kusola kutambisya mujonosi. = The boys were trying to break in an untrained ox. Akubule mujononsi kutegwa kamukwelela antoomwe lyoonse. = Let there be no untrained ox so that you pull together always.

a tin container beaten as accompaniment for dancing, pl. mijoolo, e.g. Kamundipa cigabba ndibambe mujoolo. Give me a tin container so that I make a musical-rattle. Also injoolo, muyuwa, insaka, insakalala.
aloft in the air, higher, above, e.g. Kolungumana mujulu ubone nyenyezi. Look aloft and see the stars.

a medicinal plant, (Ehretia rigida), is used for excessive lacrimation the bark is soaked in water to make drops, e.g. Kasamu kamujuncucuulu nkabotu kulobya. = A stick of the mujuncu-cuulu tree is good for making a fishing-rod.
nephew or niece of a man by his sister, e.g. Ndakakwatila mujwa wangu ijilo. I had my nephew married yesterday.
a cousin of mine who is not of my clan, e.g. Mujwama walikusobana adilwe. My cousin was playing at the funeral.
type of tree, the wood is used for pestles, e.g. Munsi wamujwamaila mmuyumu kapati, tautyoki kufwambaana. A pestle made of mujwamaila wood is very strong, it does not break quickly. Also mutwa-maila.
wife of, pl. baka, e.g. Mangalita ngumuka Gamacuulu. = Mangalita is the wife of Gamacuulu. Oobu mbubwakavwuwa bakaakwe. = That is how his wife answered.

your wife, e.g. Wandipa cakulya mukaako. = *Your wife gave me food.* (mukazima = my co-wife, muka-zinyina = her co-wife; mukazinyoko = your co-wife), e.g. *Mutinta tabamvwani amukazinyina.* = Mutinta does not get on well with her co-wife.
a band around waist, as of cotton wool/beads, e.g. *Musimbi ulya usamide mukaba wabulungu mucibuno.* = That girl is wearing a band of beads around her waist.
a woman, wife, e.g. *Mukaintu wangu uli kumuswaangano.* = My wife is at the meeting.
the ritual wife of the sikatongo or officiant for the annual Iwiindi rituals. (Lit. the woman of the gourd used to offer water and beer)

a dancing-belt adorned with pieces of metal to jingle with the movement of the dancer, bits of iron hung on belt, in certain dances, which rattle when one dances. Are also worn by suckling mothers, pl. *mikaku*, e.g. *Bamatumbu bakaindi bakali kusama mikaku.* = Long ago suckling mothers used to wear pieces of iron.

a strip of cloth with which the new mother is tied around the stomach after giving birth, e.g. *Balamwaanga mutumbu muncinda mwida wiitwa kuti mukaku.* = They tie the new mother with a strip of cloth around the stomach which is called *mukaku*. Also *mumya, kkumba*.

many people which belong to one man, e.g. *Muuka wakalijisi mukaku mupati. Mukaku caamba bantu banji alimwi bunji bwabo kabali bakaintu.* = Muuka had a large number of people. Mukaku means many people and again many of them are women. Also *bubamba, bungwele*

a source of water, a well, e.g. *Meenda niyakayuminina muzyiba, coolwe ncobakajisi ncakuti bakalijisi umbi mukalo ngobakali kuteka kulubazu lumbi lwamunzi wabo.* = When the water dried up in the pond, they were lucky in that they had another source of water from where they were drawing water on another side of the village.

a criminal, pl. *bakalukuza*, e.g. *Bamasilikani bakazinguluka nanda kumwi kabajisi ntobolo, mbuli kuti bamvwa kuti kwanjila bakalukuza munanda.* = The police surrounded the house while having guns, as if they had heard that criminals had entered the house. Also *cigwebenga*
medicine for the chest, e.g. *Amumunanike mukala uciswa lusinga.* = Apply the medicine for the chest of the one who is suffering from a nerve pain.
type of tree, the wood used for canoes, paddles, and hut-poles, e.g. *Bwato bwamukala-makubi tabuzwizyi kufwambaana.* = A boat made from the *mukala-makubi* tree does not leak quickly.
type of tree, grows straight and tall, e.g. *Kamugonka makkapulosi amukala-nkanga.* = Cut the *mukalankanga* tree for the timber for the roof.
a type of tree, e.g. *Mukalantulu mmusamu ujanika muzyuulu.* = The *mukalantulu* tree is found on ant-hills. Also *mukala-ntuulu*.
a type of bird, the kroh vulture, e.g. *Mukala-ntuulu mmuyuni uluka ciindi cinji.* = The kroh vulture is a bird which flies most of the time. Also *cungwe*.
my friend, e.g. *Kosika buyo omukalima, utayoowi.* = Just come my friend, don't be afraid.
a waterhole, e.g. *Meenda ayuminina mumukalo.* = The water has dried up in the waterhole.
a big twisted bark fibre, a rope, e.g. *Basankwa balakwelana amukalo.* = The boys are pulling in a tug-of-war with a rope. =
a small locust-bird, e.g. *Insozi zilaligwa kuli mukalubale.* = Locusts are eaten by the locust-bird.
a person from the Luvale tribe, e.g. *Kakamujaya kaccasu Mukalubale.* = Kaccasu (a drink with high alchohol content) killed the Luvale person.
the African mahogany tree, gives good shade, good timber, e.g. *Kumunzi kwa Joojo kuli mumvwule mubotu wamukamba.* = In Joojo's village there is good shade of the mukamba tree.

mukamba leaves, pl. mikamba, e.g. *Mikamba imwi ilatontola, njiijikwa cisyu, imwi ilalula.* Some mikamba trees have leaves which are nice to eat, these are the ones cooked for relish, some have bitter leaves. (You select the type of mukamba tree which has nice leaves.) *Basimbi bacela matu amukamba.* = The girls are gathering the leaves of the mukamba tree (for relish).

a preacher, e.g. Taakazyalwa kali mukambausi pe, pesi naakali kukomena wakayeeya kuti awalo abe *mukambausi* kugwasilizya bantu kuzyiba nzila zya Mwami Leza. = He wasn't born a preacher, but as he grew up he thought he should become a preacher to help people know the way of the Lord God.

one who claps to encourage, or who claps profusely in gratitude, pl. bakambilizi, e.g. Basikulangilila bbola *mbakambilizi* bakukulwaizya basobana. = The spectators of the match are the encouragers to spur on those who play.
applause, e.g. Bakamupa *mukambilo* mupati Mutinta naakazyana kabotu. They gave Mutinta great applause when she danced well.

a deciduous type of tree (pterocarpus antunesii). Has hard flexible wood and it turns and polishes well. Makes good firewood. Is used for paddles, axe and pick handles and walking sticks (from the roots). The leaves and buds are used as relish in the Gwembe valley and the roots are used to make a dressing for sores and wounds. Cuttings can be used to make a live fence. e.g. *Kasako ka mukambo nkabotu kweenzya.* = A stick made from the *mukambo* tree is good for walking with.
a plant used for green relish (Baushina tomentosa), e.g. Twali kulisya matu amu*kambo.* We were eating using the leaves from a *mukamba* tree relish. Also *mukamba, mupaapa*
milking-pail, e.g. Amulete *mukamino tukame ŋombe.* = Bring the milking-container so that we milk the cattle.
loaf of unleavened-bread, cake of meal, e.g. Mucikombelo bantu balya *mukamu.* = In the church the people eat unleavened-bread.
a high price, high speed, e.g. Bantu bamvwa lufwu Iwamuntu balaa *mukampilo* mupati. = When people hear of the death of a person they become very agitated. Also *mukompelo.*
exhaustion after much walking, e.g. Baama banetuka amuka*mpilwa* mupati. = My mother fainted with severe exhaustion after walking.
a widow, e.g. Bamwi bantu bayanda kupenzya *bamukamufwu.* = Some people like to make widows suffer.
the wife of an elderly man, e.g. Ba *mukamunene* balalemekwa. = A wife of an elderly man is respected.
wife of chief, e.g. Amubatebbele nkuni *bamukamwami.* = Fetch firewood for the chief's wife.

the wife of a man, e.g. *Mukamuntu* nokuli kuti ngusicikolo, naa wamita tanyandyi nkaambo boonse balizyi kuti ulikwetwe. If the wife of a man becomes pregnant even when she is at school it is not a cause for surprise.
a talkative person, e.g. *Ooyu muntu mmukananzi*, tapi ciindi kuli bamwi. = This person is talkative, she does not give a chance to others. *Also mukanazi*
the carrot-tree, e.g. Bantu basilika zilonda *amukandanombe*. = People heal sores with medicine from the carrot tree. Also *mufwuti*.
a type of tree, e.g. Loozi *Iwamukandanjase* luvwumbya maanda. = Fibre from the *mukandanjase* tree is used for thatching houses.
kafwundula.*

light beer, porridge, sweetbeer, e.g. Amubape *mukande* basankwa bazwa musyokwe. = Give light beer to the boys who have come from the bush. Cilyo citete bapati ncebasaanguna kumulisya mwana *ntukande* tutontola. = The first food given to babies is cooled light porridge.
important person, e.g. Mainza wakali sicuuno *mukando*. = Mainza was an important chairman.
a coward, e.g. Chijanwa naakali mwana wakali *mukandu*. = When Chijanwa was a child he was a coward.
a fearful person, e.g. Muntu *mukandu-kandu* tayandiki pe. = A fearful person is not wanted at all.
a type of fighting-axe, e.g. Keembe kamukanga kalabosya kapati. = The fighting-axe is very sharp. *Also kafwulwefwulwe.*
porridge already mixed but not yet cooked, e.g. *Mukangabisi* ngwakuulika mazina. = Porridge mixed but not yet cooked is used when naming people.

type of tree (*albizzia harveyi*), looks like an acacia, but has no spines. The wood is dark, heavy and strong. It can be used for general building, furniture, door frames, sledges. Cattle eat foliage and pods. A decoction of the roots is used to treat swollen legs, e.g. Miyanda *yamukangala* ilasilisya maulu. = The roots of the *mukangala* tree are used to treat swollen legs.
mukankala.*
a type of tree, e.g. Twaakutebba nkuni *zyamukanganzovwu*. = We have collected firewood from the *mukanganzovwu* tree. *Also kafwundula*
a type of tree, e.g. Mukankala ulazwa meenda ciindi cacilimo. = In the dry season water comes out of the *mukankala* tree. *Also mukangala, mukololo.*
a handful of porridge or clay, e.g. Basa, aumwi alete *mukanya* omwe wabulongo. = My friends, each should bring a handful of clay. *Also musuma*

a type of edible-grass (*Panicum novemnerve*), the seeds are boiled as a cereal in Feb., e.g. Inseke zyamu*kaseza* zilaligwa bantu bafwa nzala. = The seeds of edible-grass are eaten when people are hungry.
a self-willed, obstinate, headstrong, insolent person, e.g. Mwana mu*kasi* tatumwi. = A self-willed child is not sent on an errand.
a widow, e.g. Muka*sikufwa* uyanda lugwasyo lunji. = A widow needs a lot of help. *Also mukamufwu*
a lonely person, an idle person, e.g. Joojo *mmukata* nkaambo bantu bamumwaika. = Joojo is a lonely person because people have ostracised him.
relish, e.g. Cisyu *camukata* cilalula-lula. = *Mukata* relish is bitter.
my father's wife, e.g. Ba *mukataata* bajika musozya wambwiila. = My father's wife cooked samp with peanuts.
a washing pot, e.g. Kamusanyza mitiba mumukate. = Wash the dishes in the washing pot.
wife, e.g. Mutinta mmukazi wa Haamape. = Mutinta is the wife of Haamape. Also muka, mukaintu, mwanakazi.

a type of green relish used from Sept. to Oct. The young leaves are cooked. The juice from pounded bark are applied to sores. Wood is used for hoehandles. Ndaula mwiini wamukazibea. = I bought a handle of mukazibea wood. Also cundwe. Mukazima-lambwa January, e.g. Mu Mukazimalambwa notubizwa tumpelya. = The early maize ripens in January.
January (the time of weeding fields and when the rivers are overflowing)
her co-wife, e.g. Bbelita balalwana amukazinyina. = Bbelita is fighting with her co-wife.
line which parts the hair, e.g. Wakalikamuna masusu akucita mukekezu. He was combing his hair and parting it.
the African blackwood tree, e.g. Mukelete oyu wakayuma. = This African blackwood tree has withered. Also cinsale, musonkomo.
a white person, pl. bamakiwa, e.g. Bamakiwa bakali kutupenzya kaindi. = The whites caused us to suffer long ago. Also mukuwa.
a camp for traditional training for manhood, e.g. Bama Lubale mbabajisi mukkanda. = The Baluvale have traditional training for manhood.
line which parts the hair, e.g. Kulyaandula mukkekkezu ncilengwa cakaindi. Making a line for parting the hair is an old custom.
a brake, pl. mikkobocco, e.g. nola azikkocci zyakale-kale zyakajisi mikkobocco. The wagons and scotchcarts of the olden days had brakes.
a person who leads yoked oxen, e.g. Kaboola mukkokkeli ainde kumbele. Let the leader of the oxen pass to the front.
the back, (Lozi) e.g. Mukkokkoto ulacisa mbuli kuti ndali kulima. The back is painful as if I have been weeding. Also musana
a clan-name, e.g. Ndabaa malweza angu endikke, nde Mukkuli. = I have my own misfortune alone, I of the Mukkuli clan.
a type of tree, gives good firewood, poles, and gum, e.g. Mukkuta-bulongo ulaa nkuni zibotu. = The mukkuta-bulongo tree gives good firewood.
a whip, pl. mikkwilo, e.g. Beembela badobola mikkwilo musyokwe. = The herders crack the whips in the bush. Also ciswepu, ciswipu, mutatula (sjambok), inondo (a flexible stick)
a type of fish, pl. miko, e.g. Baloba bajaya miko minji. = Those fishing have killed many fish.
a big long coat, e.g. Mudaala usamide mukobela mupati. = The old man is wearing a big long coat.
the secretary-bird, e.g. Kwiingililwa mukobela-nzoka mmaIweza. To have a secretary-bird cross your path is an evil omen. Also jule, luciimba-nyendo.
the handle of a cup, e.g. Mukobezyo wabuleke watyoka. = The handle of the tin cup is broken
the string or line from which a thing hangs, e.g. Kamwaanzika zisani zitete amukobezyo. = Hang the wet clothes on the line.

the umbrella thorn tree (acacia tortilis). Cattle browse on foliage and pods. It yields an edible gum. A yellow brown dye is got from bark or roots. Parts of the tree can be used for tanning. Also mujence.
filtered ash-juice used in preparing green relish. Branches used in kraal and garden fencing. e.g. Miyanda yamukoka ilanunka. = The roots of the mukoka tree stink.
a lazy and slow person, who defers doing what he should do, e.g. Musankwa oyu mmukoko. This boy is lazy and slow.
exact resemblance, e.g. Mainza wakali mukokolwede wisi kunyina mpaakamusiide. = Mainza resembled his father perfectly with nothing left out.

a plant *(Abutilon angulatum)* from which people obtain flowers to suck, e.g. Beembezi basyuunta mukokomwamomba. The shepherds are sucking the juice from the flowers of the mukokomwamomba plant. Also bukokomwa-moomba, bukoko bwamoomba.
type of tree with hooked thorns, the Knot-thorn tree. e.g. Kondijwa bumvwa bwamukokoto. Extract the thorn from me of the mukokoto tree.

an old person or animal, e.g. Mubuzuba obu mbukwakali kubala mwezi, nkujana nayabweenda mukola wakalaabwene mpalyata. On this day because the moon was shining, when the old man was walking he found that he could see where he stepped.
a fig-tree, e.g. Bayuni balayanda kulya micelo yamukolanjuni. = Birds like to eat the fruits of the mukolanjuni tree.

the lilac tree *(Lonchocarpus capassa)*. The sprays of faintly fragrant white, blue or purple flowers appear from August to December. A good bee tree. The bark is beaten and used as a curdling agent in milk. In famine time the seeds are eaten as porridge after lengthy boiling. Causes bad headaches. e.g. Mukololo mmusamu uloka meenda ciindi cacilimo. = The mukololo is a tree which drops water during the dry season.
a water-channel, e.g. Kamwiida cisyu ameenda azwa mumukololomba. Irrigate the vegetables with water coming from the water-channel.
a type of tree (produces the inkoloondo or imfwulimuninga fruit), e.g. Kamuya mukalye nkoloondo mu mukoloondo muya. Go and eat the fruit in that mukoloondo tree.
a drunkard, e.g. Twamusiya mukolwa ulilede munzila. We left the drunkard lying on the path. Also mukolwi, cakolwa
a roadside-gutter, e.g. Meenda aleenda mumukolwe. The water is flowing in the gutter.
a drunkard, e.g. Wakajaya nongo yabukoko mmukolwi. The one who broke the earthen pot of beer was a drunkard.
a calabash with long stem, e.g. Ndipe meenda mumukoma. Give me water in the long-stemmed calabash.
a common type of hammer, e.g. Koleta mukoma tugagaile mpikili. Bring a hammer so that we hammer the nail.
large trench mukombo a large navel, e.g. Ooyu mwana ujisi mukombo mupati. This child has a large navel.
a spitting-cobra, e.g. Mukombola waluma tukuku mmupati. The spitting-cobra which ate the chicks was a big one.
African mahogany tree, e.g. Mukomboolo uzyala bana basiya. The African mahogany tree bears black fruit. Also mukamba
a cock, e.g. Munene waya ku Pemba niwalila mukombwe. The old man went to Pemba when the cock crowed.
stem, as of a mushroom. Also munteela.
the handle of a spoon or knife or a calabash, stem of mushroom, e.g. *Kojata mukompwi nobweza citende*. = Hold the stem of the pumpkin as you lift it.
nsima already mixed, but not yet cooked, e.g. Bantu babelesya *mukondabwi nobaulikana mazina*. = People use uncooked mealie-meal mixed with water when they are naming. Also mukangabisi
badly-cooked porridge, e.g. *Nabwiinga wajika mukonde waya kwabo*. = The newly-married woman who badly cooked a meal went to her home.
man's necklace
a track, spoor, e.g. *Muwezi utobela mukondo wanamusya*. = The hunter follows the track of a duiker.
a rumour, e.g. *Nindakaumvwa mukondo, ndakayumuka kuya kwakwe*. = When I heard of the rumour I set out for his place.
type of tree, e.g. *Muyuni ulalila mumukondwaboomputisi*. = The bird is crying in the *mukondwa-boomputisi* tree.
vagina, e.g. *Izina Iyamukongo lilatondwa*. = The use of the word *mukongo* is taboo.
the forearm, pl. *mikono*, e.g. *Muntu mutolo ulatontola mumikono*. = The arms of a lazy person are weak.
kumik= The bangles on her arm suit her.

an evergreen tree (Garcinia Livingstonei). Its boiled fruit is cooked and eaten with porridge and is also eaten raw, or it can be fermented to make an alcoholic drink. The latex can be used to make gum. Water containing bark is used to bathe sore eyes, root chopped and beaten and soaked in hot water is rubbed on teeth, gums and outside mouth for toothache. e.g. *Mukonongo ulakumbya bukoko*. = The *mukonongo* tree is used for making an alchoholic drink. Also mulolongwe, musunka, mutunga.
type of tree (Terminalia Stuhlmanni), wood used for making handles and in building, e.g. *Ooyu mwiini wajamba ngwamukonono*. = This handle of the hoe is from a *mukonono* tree.
type of plant (Cordia gharaf), fruit juice sucked in May. e.g. *Basimpongo bakali kusyuunta misinza yamukonya-busenga*. = The goatsherds were sucking the juice of the *mukonyabusenga* plant.

the wild sop plant, e.g. *Inzoka zilatija miyanda yamukonyombwa kuti wazingulusya mpoikumba nkuku*. = Snakes keep away from the roots of the wild sop plant if you surround a brooding hen with them. Also muloolo

type of tree (Triplochiton zambesiacus), pounded, dried or singed leaves boiled or soaked in hot water to make mundyoli. Wood used for harpoon shafts, dugout poles, tool handles and building construction. e.g. *Mundyoli wamatu wamukonzo ulanona*. = Stew made from the leaves of the *mukonzo* tree is tasty.
hard stool or faeces
old animal, e.g. *Masusu akwe akalikwiide kupepela mbuli boya bwakaaze mukoole*. = Its hair was just soft like the fur of an old cat.
a sickly person, e.g. *Muntu mukoozu tabukili bulo*. = A sickly person is bed-ridden.

a girdle or strip of cloth, e.g. *Bakaintu basama mikopo nobazyana*. = Women wear girdles (around their chests) as they dance. *Munanga wakalyaanga* mukopo mucibuno. = The witchdoctor tied a girdle around his waist. Also muncinda

a large deciduous tree (Sterculia Africana), light soft and spongy wood. Inner bark yields rope for tying thatch. Small snuff boxes can be made from the fruit. e.g. Looye Iwamukosa lu-wumbya maanda. = Fibre from the mukosa tree is used for thatching houses.
the neck, e.g. Lwibbe ujisi mukosi mulamfwu. = The touraco bird has a long neck.
e.g. Mapulanga amukoso mma-botu kuvwumbya maanda. = The planks of a mukoso tree, are good for roofing a house.
a cane-rat, pl. mikoswe, e.g. Aawa kwainda mukoswe mupati. = A big cane-rat passed here. Also insezi
shade (made by putting hands over eyes), e.g. Kosisa meso acisa mukotakota. = Protect your sore eyes by shading them with your hands.
bull or ox without horns, e.g. Ndakaula musune mukotoolo. = I bought an ox without horns. Also muvwuma
fowl-excrement, e.g. Inkuku ntumbu yania mukotwe mupati. = The mother hen excreted plenty of excrement. Also munkontyo

clan, e.g. Bantu tabakwatani mumukowa. = People do not marry within the clan. To Batonga, a Bana Mweemba, a Bawe, a Bamaala, a Batwa, a Baleya, a Basubiya, a Batotela, a Ba Sala, a Balenje, a Bana Mukkuni, tuli mukowa omwe. = We Batonga, and Mweemba's people, and Gwembe Valley people and people of Maala, and the Batwa, the Toka-Leya, the Ba Subiya, the Ba Totela, the Ba Sala, the Ba Lenje and the people of Mukkuni, we are akin. (Mazina amikowa ngaaya: Baleya, Bakonka, Bansaka, Bayuni, Beetwa, Badenda, Bantanga, Bazyamba, Bainde, Bansanje, Baloongo a Bacindu.) Makowa alatobelezya kwiinda kumanyina.
image, statue, resemblance, e.g. Cibumbwa mmukozyanyo wa Maliya. = What has been moulded is an image of Mary.

copper, brass, e.g. Ku Ndola basya bulongo bwamukuba. = At Ndola they dig out copper-ore. Mainza waka-yeeya kuti nkubotu aye kumupati wakwe ku Kabwe kumukuba kutegwa akatule moyo. = Mainza thought it would be good to go to his brother at Kabwe to the copper-mine to unload his worries. Also mulabila
a maize-cob without sheath, e.g. Musune walya mukuba wapopwe. = The ox ate a maize-cob.
a youth, pl. bakubusi, e.g. Bakubusi bakali kutumwa kubanene kuya kulaigwa. = The young boys were sent to the elders to be instructed.
lunation which largely corresponds to April, e.g. Maila muceme abizwa mumwezi wa Mukubwe-kaangala. = Red millet ripens in April.
an ear of sorgum, e.g. Mukuka wamaila waligwa buyuni. = An ear of sorgum was eaten by a flock of birds.
Indian hemp, e.g. Bantu bakali kuulisya mukuku bakanjila ntolongo. = The people who were selling Indian hemp have gone into prison.
a big fowl, e.g. Tokonzyi kuula mukuku ooyu udula. = You cannot buy that big expensive fowl.

an evergreen shrub/tree (Garcinia huillensis). Yields a yellow latex. Wood is used for building poles. Bark, leaves and roots have many medicinal uses e.g. expulsion of intestinal worms, treatment of syphilis. Small branches are used as chew-sticks or throw-away toothbrushes. e.g. Makkapulosi amukukwe mmayumu kapati. = Building-poles from the mukukwe tree are very strong. Also musunka.
