type of plant (*Flacourtia indica*); the fruit is dried, boiled and eaten, *intumbulwa*. A porridge of chopped and boiled roots is eaten to cure fits. e.g. Basimankobbolyo balya *ntumbulwa mu-mutumbulwa*. = The bush black-birds eat the fruit of the *mutumbulwa* plant.
a messenger, e.g. *Batumwa* ba Jesu bakali kusyomeka. = The messengers of Jesus were trustworthy.

type of tree, has medicinal uses, also used as charm to protect a house, roots are cooked with meat to flavour it. e.g. *Miyanda yamutunda isilika makoto amoyo.* = The roots of the *mutunda* tree are used for treating tonsils. *Mutunda mmusamu wakusita nanda.* = The *mutunda* is a tree used as a charm to protect a house.
a hairy person, e.g. *Mutundu ujisi boya bunji mubili onse.* = A hairy person has hair all over the body.

type of tree (*Xeroderris Stuhlmanni*). The yellow-brown heart-wood is light and hard and splits on drying and has been used for making canoes and mortars. The seeds are poisonous. A red dye and gum come from the bark. e.g. *Cilaa ntenda kulya bana bamutundula.* = It is dangerous to eat the fruit of the *mutundula* tree.

type of shrub (*Ostryoderris stuhlmannii*) the seeds are eaten whole (like beans), wood used for tool handles and mortars, e.g. *Ndaula ncili yamutundulu.* = I bought a mortar made from the *mutundulu* shrub.
sleep naked, e.g. *Tacigwasyi koona amutundulu ciindi camupeyo.* = It does not help to sleep naked in the cold season.
ill-treatment, e.g. *Baneene bakajisi mutundululo mubi kuli bamucaala.* = My grandmother had a habit of ill-treating orphans.

a sunbeam, a ray of light, pl. *mitungazuba*, e.g. *Mutungazuba wakali kunjila kuciluli.* = A ray of sun was entering through the roof. *Mitungazuba ilakondelezya kulanga.* = Sunbeams are delightful to watch.
type of tree (high growing tree).

type of tree (straight thorns, poisonous fruit, used for fences, roots used for mental disorder, e.g. *Kamususa tusanzu twamutungambala tuyakizye lubaya.* = Collect branches of the *mutungambala* tree so that we build a fence.
type of tree (*Garcinia Livingstonei*) Also *mukwananga, muko-nongo, mulolongwe, musunka.*
a selfish person, e.g. *Ooyu muntu mmutuni, tayandi kupa zyakwe.* = This person is selfish, s/he does not want to give away her/his things.
a foolish person, e.g. *Muntu mutuni kunyina ncakonzya kwaamba.* = A foolish person is not able to say anything.
corpse already decomposing, carcass of an animal, e.g. *Mutunta wa mufwu ulilede murnanda.* = The corpse of the deceased is lying in the house.

a medicinal plant (*Solanum panduriforme*) used by chewing it and given to baby for stomach ache. Or it can be charred a little and chewed. It is also used for the vein-pain by chopping the fruit and rubbing it into small cuts on the body. e.g. *Kuti walumwa sicinsuungwe nkunywa miyanda yamutuntulwa.* = If you are bitten by a rabid dog you should drink (water which has been soaked in) the roots of the *mutuntulwa* plant.

(*Solanum incanum*) fruit-juice used in preparation of sour milk. The root-juice is swallowed for scorpion bite. e.g. *Kuti walumwa kabanze nkunywa mutuntulwa.* = If you are bitten by a scorpion you should drink root-juice from the *mutuntulwa* plant.
a valiant person, e.g. *Muntu mututubwi tayoowi nuulema mulimo.* = A brave person does not fear even when the work is heavy.
a married woman, e.g. *Ncibi kuyanda muntu mutwale kale.* = It is evil to love a woman who is already married.

type of tree (*Terminalia* Sericea). The wood is yellow, closegrained, hard, heavy, strong and very durable. It is used for hut poles, fence posts, tool handles and furniture. The bark gives a tanning extract. The roots have many medicinal uses and are also used to purify villages and people from contact with a dead body. Sticks are placed in shrines for contact with ancestral spirits at harvest and planting times. e.g. Ndiyanda mwiini wamutwamaila. = I want a handle from a mutwamaila tree. Mutinta wakali kupala makwa amusamu utegwa mutwamaila. Mucelo oyu wakauziya abbwe kutegwa lube lusu. = Mutinta was peeling off the bark of a tree called mutwamaila. This medicine she ground with a stone so that it became powder.
a servant, pl. batwanga, e.g. Mwami ujisi batwanga banji ileenda milimo yakwe. = The activities of a chief who has many servants progress.

the head, e.g. Kuti mutwe kaucisa nkuya kucibbadela. = If your head is sore you should go to the hospital. *camutwe* = registration card. Bayanzene balwanina mutwe wasulwe. = Friends fight over something insignificant.
the grain-beetle, e.g. Koleta mutwe-wanzoka tulobeeke mu bulungu. = Bring the grain beetles we will mix them among the beads (when threading a necklace).
noisy chewing, e.g. Ncibi kuba mutyamfwu nolya abuleya. = It is bad to chew noisily when eating in public.

something which brakes and remains inside, e.g. Kwacaalila mutyokela muli tinde. The sharp point of the stick has broken and has remained in the tuber. (refers to a game played by throwing sticks at the tuber) mutyola-maamba type of tree (straight thorns), e.g. Makkapulosi amutyola-maamba mmabotu. Roof timber from the mutyola-maamba tree are good.
moisture, e.g. Mumuunda muli mutyu, taafwambaani kuyuma mapopwe. = In a field where there is moisture, the maize will not dry out quickly. Also mudumu
a stripe on a cloth, pl. myuubi, Also maubi-maubi
tiny fish, pl. bamuubila, e.g. Mucizyiba omu kuli buyo ntuunga bamuubila. = In this pool there are only tiny fish.
a big insect, snake or reptile, e.g. Nobana kamucenjela, kwanjila muuka mucoonde eciya. Be careful children, a big snake has gone into that thicket.
a sore on woman's breast or child's buttocks, e.g. Mwana ulaa muuka mupati atako. The child has a big sore on the buttock.
type of tree with straight thorns, e.g. Bumvwa bwamuukila bulababa. A thorn from the muukila tree causes irritation. Also muwuukila.
a bought slave, pl. baule, e.g. Bantu baule tabalilemeki kuti bavwuzyanya. Slaves who are bought lack respect when they multiply.
the price of something, e.g. Muulo wamapopwe waya mujulu mazubaano. The price of maize has increased these days.
a baby already trying to walk, a calf beginning to graze, e.g. Mwana wafwa wali muulu kale. The baby who died was beginning to walk.
a bush-pig, a warthog, e.g. Babwa bangu bajaya muuma. = My dogs killed a warthog. Also sicipongo, nkuntula, mungundu, munyembwa, mungulumba (boar).
the dry bank of a river, e.g. Munyati waliimvwi amuuma. The buffalo was standing on the dry bank of the river.

a virgin, e.g. Ucili *muuma*, tanakusika kumulombwana. = She is still a virgin, she has not yet been with a man. Also cinsilwe, mandala. (Mooye may also originally have meant a virgin since it means a cocoon.)

a person bereaved of all his/her family, a lonely person, e.g. Ooyu mudaala *mmuumba*. = This old man is lonely. Baama ndasweeka munyika yabantu, ndapenga, *ndemuumba*. = Mother, I am lost in this world of people, I am suffering, I am all alone.

type of tree (good wood for timber, wattles, fibrous bark), e.g. Loozi Iwa*muumba* lulalula. = The fibre from a *muumba* tree is bitter. Wakali kuya busotoka tuvwuna twamubombo *amuumba*. = He was going along jumping over mubombo and *muumba* shrubs.
a fishing spear with barbs.
tree whose wood is good for handles, e.g. *Muumbankoli* ngomubotu kumiini. = The wood of the *muumbankoli* tree is good for handles.
an edible tuber (*Coleus esculentus*), e.g. Basinzala balalila *muumbu*. = The hungry eat the *muumbu* tuber for supper.
alive and healthy person, e.g. Sunu Jaliso *mmuumbula*. = Today Jaliso is alive and healthy.

a person who is intact, whole, virginal, alive, pl. *baumbulu*, e.g. Oyu mwana wakabuka cifwumofwumo *muumbulu*, pesi acilangankumo kumazuba mwana wakaciswa. = This child got up in the morning well, but in the afternoon the child was sick. Basankwa abasimbi bakali kujanana *mbaumbulu*
Boys and girls found one another as virgins. Mapenzi oonse aya naataliko kuti uso naacili *muumbulu*. = All these troubles would not be here if your father was still alive.
a stick not flexible but pointed, as for stamping earth into a hole, e.g. Sekeleti wauma muntu *amuumpa*. = Sekeleti beat a person with a pointed stick. Also musako.
a field, e.g. Kuli myungu minji *mumuunda wabataata*. = There are many pumpkins in my father's field.
a perfume used by girls, e.g. Basimbi balibambila *muunde* wakulinyunyiila akulinunkilizya kabotu amibili yabo. = Girls prepare themselves with scent for spraying and perfuming their bodies.
a gentle afternoon breeze, e.g. Ijilo mangolezya kwakali *muundwe* mubotu. = Yesterday there was a gentle afternoon breeze.

a type of tree (*Acacia albida Del.*), the seeds are eaten August-September after prolonged boiling in two changes of water and soaking in a third. Pods used as fish poison. Wood used for dug-outs. Inziba ilikkede *mumuunga*. = There is a dove sitting in the *muunga* tree. e.g. Mamvwa *amuunga* alacisa. = The thorns of the *muunga* tree can hurt.
a fabulous tree mentioned in a traditional story, e.g. *Muungaambilibili* ulaligwa. = The muungaambilibili tree is edible.
type of tree (straight thorns and dark bark, good fibre and gum) Also mukoka.
acacia tree with whitish bark, e.g. Amukakwame makwaa muu*ngaunga* tusilisye nombe. = Kindly remove the bark from the acacia tree so that we cure the cattle.
an insatiable person, e.g. Muntu mulyato ulakatazya kusanina, *mmuunga-mpuula*. = It is hard to feed a greedy person, he is never satisfied.
a porridge stick, a spoon, pl. *myuungo*, e.g. Ndiyanda *muungo* ujisya nsima. = I need a stick for cooking nsima. Also conco (cimpanzi = a piece of broken calabash used as a spoon)

*muungo wamuyaki* a builder's trowel *muungu* a pumpkin, pl. *myungu*, e.g. *Baama baakuula muungu mupati kumusyika.* = My mother has gone to buy a big pumpkin at the market. Different names for pumpkins: munte-mba, namundalanga, muzuma, kapande, kapungu-pungu, impungu, mumbale *muungula-mabele* type of tree (leaves are smoked), e.g. Baneene bafweba tombwe *wamuungula-mabele.* = My grandmother smokes a tobacco from *muungula-mabele* leaves.
unmarried youth, pl. boongwe, e.g. Musankwa oyu ucili *muungwe*, tanakwata. = This boy is still a youth, he is not yet married.
desire for food, e.g. *Ndabaa muunyaunya nindabona balya.* = An appetite arose within me when I saw others eating. Also mudokodoko, munyaanya.
a mean, stingy person, e.g. *Muntu muunyu ulya alikke.* = A mean person eats alone. Also *sinya, sinyo, mumama*
one who is fond of something, e.g. Mukaintu umitide inga waba *muunzu* kumayi kuti waņunkilwa ngawo. = A pregnant woman becomes fond of eggs if she gets the smell of them. Also *cinunki*
the space between objects, a gap, aperture, e.g. *Ukainde amuutu wa-milundu.* = You can pass through the gap between the hills. Also *mwaako, mwenya*
the wind, e.g. *Muuwo uzwida kujwe nguuleta mvwula mu Zambia.* = It is the wind which comes from the east which brings rain to Zambia. Also *muwo.*

generic term for spirit of people or animals, not possessed by plants or natural features such as rocks, rivers, waterfall, mountains etc. e.g. *Mumunzi muli muuya mubotu, bantu bakkala kabotu.* = In the village where there is a good spirit, people live in harmony. Also *muya.*
fresh air, e.g. Kamujalula mpulungwido kunjile *muuya mubotu.* = Open the windows to let in the fresh air.
the overflow of a filled basket, e.g. Niwakazula mutaanga cakulakatika, mwana wakailulula *muuyi* wakalikulakatika. = When the basket was overflowing, the child took what was flowing over.
a generous person, e.g. Muntu *muuza* ulapenzegwa abantu mbagwasya. = A generous person is troubled by the ones s/he helps. (Buuza bulanenga. = Compassion cuts. (a proverb)) cf. *muuya*
pretence not to have heard, rt. -unzya, e.g. Mutaciti *muuzyamvwide.* = Do not pretend that you have not heard.

pretence, paying no attention to what has been said or what has happened, e.g. Bakazumanana kulima akucita *muuzyamvwile.* = They continued to plough and turned a deaf ear (to what they had been told). cf. *muunzyamvwide*

a recently born child not yet speaking, an infant less than two months, pl. *bavwanda*, e.g. Bana bavwanda tabatolwi mubantu banji. = An infant (less than two months) is not taken among crowds of people.
a type of grass used for thatching, e.g. Bataata balicizyi kuvwumbya *muvwani* maanda. = My father knows how to thatch houses with *muvwani* grass. Also *mukulajamina.*
The wild orange tree, e.g. Bana bamuvwavwa tabaligwi. = The fruits of the wild orange tree are not eaten. Also *mufwufwuna.*
mixture, different kinds, e.g. Kulya kwakali kwamuvwele-muvwele. = The food was of different varieties.
a gown or long-flowing garment, e.g. Bapaizi bakaindi bakali kusama _mavweleende_. = The priests of long ago used to wear long gowns.
a mixture, e.g. Aawa kuli _muvwelevwele_ wabantu, basiya abatuba. = There is a mixture here of black and white people.
a bundle of unripe hemp, e.g. _Ndaakuula muvwi walubanje kwa Chifwepa_. = I bought a bundle of hemp at Chifwepa's.

a hunter, pl. _bavwimi_, e.g. _Bavwimi baunka kucila ku Chisoboyo_. = The hunters have gone to hunt at Chisoboyo. (Ibbalo = the encircling of game by beaters towards the hunters; _coobelo_ = when the circle closes.) Also muwezi, sibinda, cibinda, Vwambalume, mujimba. **muvwingi** ................. e.g. Mainza wakali kuyandisya kubelesya babwa bakwe mukuweza tusulwe a bakwale. = Mainza likes to use his dogs for hunting hares, and partridges.
foam, lather, pl. of _ikovwu_, e.g. Insipa eyi taizwi _muvwu_ munji. = Not much lather comes from this soap.
a big heap, e.g. Bamwi tacibeeleli kuba _amuvwuba_ wamasusu. = It does not suit some people to have a big mop of hair.

food of the spirits, e.g. Kaindi bananga bakali kwiide kutoba buyo busu mumaanzi akucita _muvwubadenda_. Bakali kucita boobo nkaambo bakali kusyoma kuti _muvwubadenda_ ncecakulya camizimo. Long ago the witchdoctors were just soaking flour in water and making _muvwubadenda_. They were doing this because they believed that _muvwubadenda_ was the food of the spirits. Also muzubadenda
a rich person, pl. _bavwubi_, e.g. Bantu _bavwubi_ bamwi tabayandisyi kuunka kucikombelo. = Some rich people do not want to go to church. Also mucezi.
Monday, e.g. Buzuba bwa _Muvwulo_ mbwakutalika milimo yansondo. = The day of Monday starts the activities of the week.
a roll of cloth, e.g. (a riddle) Walampa _muvwululu_ uzuzya nyika.
How long the roll of cloth that covers the earth. It is a rainbow.
a palm-tree, e.g. _Muvwuma mmusamu mulamfwu kapati_. = The palm-tree is a tree which is very tall. Also kalala, kankunka, mapokwe.
hornless head of cattle, e.g. Musune wangu _mmuvwuma_. = My ox is hornless.
an aromatic plant used to drive mosquitoes away, e.g. Munanda muli mansenya, muumpwa _muvwumbani_. = In a house where there are mosquitoes is where the _muvwumbani_ plant is burnt.
a voracious person, greedy in eating, e.g. Wabaa nzi yawe nkolya mbuli _muvwumbe_? = What has come over you that you eat like a ravenous person?

a medicinal plant (Pterocarpus rotundifolius) used in cases of excessive menstrual discharge, the root being chopped and drunk in warm water, e.g. Kalobola kasilisigwa _amuvwumbianteme_. = Kalobola is healed by medicine from the _muvwumbianteme_ plant.

type of plant (Vangueriopsis lanciflora), fruits eaten raw during rainy season, may be stored. e.g. Kamuvwundika micelo yamuvwumu mukalye akale. Store the fruits of the _muvwumu_ plant, they can be eaten later on. **muvwundamupati** type of tree (leaves are smoked, has poisonous fruit), e.g. Mutani kujatauki miyanda yamuvwundamupati, ilajaya. Don't touch the roots of the muvwunda-mupati tree, they branches from the muvwuumina tree and kill. plant them.

The wild orange tree, Also mufwufwuna, muwana.

the wind, e.g. Mumwezi wa Kkunkumuna-masamu kuli *muwo* munji kapati. = It is very windy in the month of July. Komuvwumba mulembo mwana ulamujazya *muwo*. = Cover the child with the citenge, the wind will kill him/her.
tubers used in famine times, e.g. Lyanzala bantu balalila *muwombwi*. = In time of famine people eat *muwombwi* tubers.
a clan name among the Zimbabwean Batonga whose totem is the zebra. e.g. *Bawonka* balakananisya kapati. = The Bawonka clan are great talkers.
a type of tree, e.g. Mamvwa *amuwuukila* alababa. = The thorns of the *muwuukila* tree irritate.

the soul, pl. *miya*, Living humans have a soul, but neither plants nor natural features have it. Mulozi ooyu ulijisi nguzu zyakulimba (antela kuzwizya *muya*.) = This witch has the power to take away the soul. Also *muuya*
air, breath, Kunyina *muya* mubotu munanda omu. = There is no fresh air here in the house.
the world of the living-dead, e.g. Ndiya *kumuya* banji, kukavvu kasalala kwakaya bana bokwesu boonse. = I am going to the spirit-world, to the red soil where all our relatives have gone.
a residential area, upper-class area, e.g. Kuli mafwuleenke manji *muyaadi* yamukuwa. = There are many orange trees in the residential area of the whiteman. Also *mayaadi*.
a careless person, e.g. Bamakaintu bayamba tamusalali muminzi yabo. = The villages of careless women are not clean.

a root, e.g. Kanene ujisi *muyanda* wamusamu wazyeelo. = Kanene has a medical root for protection against evil spirits. Luyando Iwamunanda ngo*muyanda* wabuzumi. = Love within the home is the root of life. *Edible roots* = busala or lusala, bwiidi. *Cultivated roots* = cuuwe, lumpobo, intwanga. *Found in vleis* = insyute, magonte *Used in charms* = mananda, ciyandankwela, keempula. *Medicinal* = musimbwe, mufwulampeyo, mumpempe, kanembe, mukunku, cilembela, mulimbula, mununkila, katoze, mulama, mulumbu, mobezuba
a loved one, e.g. Bbukumilo wafwidwa *muyandwa* wakwe sunu. = The beloved of Bbukumilo died today.
a poor and mentally disturbed person, e.g. Bantu *bayanga* bapona zyoolwe. = Poor and mentally-disturbed people survive miraculously. Also *muyaga*
the animal slain for sacrifice, the victim, e.g. Kwiili *miyasilo* yakumalende = There are animals or chickens brought for slaughter to the rainshrine.

soot, e.g. Omuno munanda muli *muye* ununka bubi. = Here in the house there is soot with a bad smell. Zimwi ziindi *mwula* yakali kunga yababama kuzuma, kwakali kuloka *muye* kuzwa kuziluli. = At times it was happening that when rain thundered, soot was dropping from the roofs. Also *mumbwe*
a thought, e.g. Ino ujisi *muyeeyo* uli buti kumakani ngoomvwa? = What kind of an idea do you have about the news you have heard?
a big egg, or a louse's egg, e.g. *Muyi* wadada mmupati. = The duck's egg is big. Bacembele bakajaya *muyi* wanjina mumutwe wamwana.= The old woman killed the egg of a louse in the child's head.
a broom, e.g. Koleta *muyiizyo* tuyaile nsefwa yabuntele. = Bring a brush I want to cleanse the sieve for sifting groundnuts.
the month of March, e.g. *Mumwezi wa Muyoba naabizwa mapopwe.* = During the month of March is when the maize ripens. Also *Muyobo*

rain lasting all day and night, pl. *miyoba*, e.g. *Akaambo kakuti yakabucesya muyoba, kunyina naba omwe wakazwa kuya kumuunda.* = Because it rained until dawn, not a single person went out to the field. *Izina lyamulonga wa Himayuwe lyakazwa kwiinda mukuti ciindi camiyoba mulonga ooyu wakali kuvwula akuba amayuwe citaambiki.* = The name of the river Himayuwe is derived from the time of the long rains when it was full and produced mighty waves.
helpless, e.g. *Ulaba muyobezi kuti kotacizyi kubamba lubono.* = You will become a helpless person if you do not know how to look after your wealth.

the lunation which has its greater part in March, the time or season when the grass is already high, e.g. *Mumwezi wa Muyobo nozilila ngoma zyamasabe.* = In the month of March is when the masabe drums reverberate. Also *Muyoba*
a shrub (leaves and fruit which are smoked), e.g. *Basambazi babelesya muyoboyobo.* = Traders use the *muyoboyobo* shrub.
a keeper, treasurer, gatherer, e.g. *Muyobozi wakakamu kesu wakaalya mali.* = The treasurer of our group embezzled the money.
an invalid, e.g. *Kajamba mmuyokezi wiile kuciswa-ciswa.* = Kajamba is an invalid who is continually sick.
one who despises, e.g. *Ndibbala nzi limbi lyaamba muyolo? Mmucapo.* = What is the other word with the same meaning as *muyolo*? It is *mucapo*. (one who despises)
a long-bladed spear, e.g. *Muvwimi wakajaya sicipongo amuyonga.* = The hunter killed a wild pig with a longbladed spear.
a slow poison, e.g. *Kuciswa muyongo cilamusya kufwa.* = To become ill from a slow poison prolongs the dying.

type of tree, the fruit used to fix spear-heads in their shafts and as a poison for fish, e.g. *Uleelede kunywa miyanda yamuyongolwa kuti waciswa mwida.* = You ought to drink a mixed liquid from the roots of the *muyongolwa* tree if you have stomach pains.
a black millipede, e.g. *Ndabona muyongolwa mupati usiya.* = I saw a big black millipede.
a fearing person, e.g. *Kuba muntu muyoofwu cilagwasya kwiinda mukali.* = It is better to be a fearing person than a fierce one.
type of tree (roots, pulverized and burnt, used as medicine for the itch) e.g. *Bweele busilikwa amuyotabalozi.* = Scabies is treated with the medicine of the *muyota-balozi* tree.
an elusive person, e.g. *Muntu muyubi ucizyi kwaambaula.* = A person who is hard to pin down talks a lot.
a smelter, e.g. *Muyumbi walubulo Iwamukuba wakafwa jilo.* = A smelter of copper died yesterday.

a fish-trap made of grass, e.g. *Balabamba muyumbyo wabwizu. Balatuyumbila tuswi anze. Nobayumbya muyumbyo mubotu balajaya tuswi makumi one.* = They make fish-traps out of grass. They push the small fish out of the water. When they use good traps they kill forty small fish.

a marriage-gift (originally an ox, in later times a spear, in modern times money) which the groom gives to his father-in-law as if to secure final authorization to carry the bride away, e.g. Muyumunsyo ninombe ipegwa kuli usyi musimbi ukwatwa. = The muyumunsyo is the gift of an ox which is given to the father of the girl being married. Also muyumusyo
one who can outstare another, e.g. Muntu *muyumu-meso* talangwi ciindi cilamfwu. = The one who can outstare another is not looked at for a long time.
a hard-hearted person, e.g. Bakaapa bakajaya mwana mba*yumu-moyo*. = The grandmother who killed the child is hard-hearted.
Also muyumunsyo
a stingy person, e.g. Nsekalombi cintu kumuntu *muyumuyumu*. I shall not ask anything from a stingy person.
an addition, e.g. Ino mulabikka muyungisyo uvwula buti? = How big is the addition you are going to make?

influence, persuasion, pressure, e.g. Naatali nguwe nindatakacimanizya cikolo nkaambo *muyungwe* wakasola wandilobya. If it was not for her, I would not have finished school, because (evil) influence would have caused me to be lost. Also *ijungwe*

a bird, e.g. *Muyuni* mupati waitola nkuku yakomena kale. A big bird took the chicken which had already grown. (List of birds: *sikube or ikubi or nakaleya* = vulture: *kanga ncizenciye or civwociye* = babbler; *lukongo* = bee-eater; *lincwe or incwencwe* = bishop bird, weaver, (seedeater), *sicinsangwe* = red bishop bird; *simankobbolyo* = bush blackcap; *cikambwe* blue jay or purple roller; *kaminkwengwe* = bulbul; *Iwibbe* = bustard *sicibonje or sicibobela* = giant bustard; *gombe-gofwu* = butcher bird or shrike;

turkey buzzard or ground hornbill; *sikakonze or makalila* = jackal buzzard; *simunimbaa-nimba* = bush lourie or coucal; *nakaala, namowani, impowani* = crested crane, common peafowl; *cikwaangala* = raven; *syaacilundula* = cuckoo, *kowa or kiiwa or mukwe wa Leza* = black and grey cuckoo; *inziba* = dove; *im'ombo,* blue spotted dove, *cibbululu* = tambourine dove; *ibombo, lombe* = large dove; *inyingu* = black collared dove;

the Namaqua dove; *cikwilinti* = stock dove; *cibbululu or cipipwa* = emerald-spotted dove; *incowe or ncoya* = shoveller (or white-faced) duck; *sicisunka or cisunkankumo or cisunka caankumo or siciimbacaankumo, or cikoyokoyo or cigwalugwalu = knob-billed duck; *simusika or musika or insika* = eagle; *lubanze* = crested eagle; *cuungwe* = carrion, tawny or koho eagle: *sikwaze or inkwazi* fish eagle; *indumatoongo or syaatoongo* = martial eagle; *lukobo, inkobo or nyengeenge* = cattle egret;

falcon; *bucwencwe or busumbwe or buleze* = finches; *kamabala* = fly-catcher; *syaazwezwe or simampolyo* = paradise fly-catcher; *inkuku* = hen; *kwale* = red-necked partridge, pheasant, francolin; *nkwekeke* = orange river francolin; *simuuwe* = lourie; *nacisekwe or nanjikwa or ikungubu* = spur-winged goose; *tuntengwe* = grass-birds; *inkanga* = guinea-fowl; *inkanga-ntole* = crowned guinea fowl; *lubengelele* = hammerheaded stork; *sikolyo or nakakolyo* = Goliath heron; *insolo* honey bird; *syunsyu-buluba* honey sucker or sunbird; *inkunkunkuku* = hoopoe; *lubangwa, kanga-pokopoko, silubabali* = crowned hornbill; *simwaambwaambwa* = a bluish species of hornbill; *siyaswimuumba* = ibis, locust bird; *inkolenkole or sicoombamilangu* = plover; *mooba* = giant king-fisher, *kaliyoliyo or syaatakalala or nanga-yabayuni* small kingfisher;

malachite kingfisher; *ciliwe* = lark; *poopololo* or *simuceladwadwa* or *kagwigwi* = sky lark; *kaleze* = sparrow; *kaleze kayimbi* = linnet; *ncelelebula* or *ceekela* = small locust bird; *mintengwe* = black locust bird; *kayunimbile* or *syaazimpande* or *syaazele* or *syaamabele* = small locust eaters. *Simukwe a-beenda, simunkuwe, simunguluwe, kuwe, nacoombe* (all different names for the lourie or grey touraco or plantain eater or go-away bird); *induba* = Livingstone's lourie; *lyabola* or *lyobola* = vlei lourie; *indwaantila* = nightingale; *byonta-nsuwa* = oriole; *impye, impo, impowani* = ostrich; *tumba* or *mwina* = common owl; *maciciti, macincizya, sibwi-sibwi* = eagle owl; *cilola* or *ceeba-nombe* or *ifwula-mpeyo* or *ifwibbampeyo* = barred owl; *cinkwele* or *cinkwenga* = parrot; *mpanda* = blackcheeked lovebird; *sicilenge* = Namaqua partridge;

or *inkwecece* = redwing partridge; *kancele* = small partridge, crested francolin; *sifwundwe* = pelican; *sicilenje* = bush pheasant; *inkwilimba* = pidgeon; *inziba* = wood pidgeon; *cimwanga* or *cikwilinti* = green pidgeon; *nduu* or *mpwii* = large quail; *zingi* = small quail;

or *kabaya* = button quail; *intiiti* or *syaantinga* or *intinga* = robin or waxbill; *kasise* = blue breasted robin; *katiiti kasubila* = red breasted robin; *syameeya* or *syaajee* = rock jumper; *syaankulu* = scolding cock; *jule* or *nakansakwe* = secretary bird; *idyamaila, lincwe, incwencwe, iconco* = seed-eaters; *kanga bukowa* = small shrike; *simasekelesya* = long tailed shrike; *lukukubwi* = snipe; *kanga lufwulu* = small snipe; *inkutakuta kayamba* = African spoon-bill; *sikili* or *simuluma-nsikili* = blue sprew; *luceu* = starling; *ncelelebula* = wattled starling; *inkulukuze* = emerald starling; *simasikili* = starling; *ikobondo* or *lulanzovwu* = big, white stork; *mubale* or *sibabbilabbila* = saddle-billed stork or wimbrel; *itongola* = white-bellied stork; *kamembya* or *kambebezya* = swift; *mintengwe* = swift; *dintiyo* = thrush; *kanga zwilili* = warbler;

or *imbulamweye* = shorttailed warbler; *sicinsangwe* = weaver bird; *simugoma-goma* or *simugomampako* or *simugogo-mwena* = woodpecker; *iceece* = wryneck; *nkukubwi* = bittern; *simavwupu* = steppe eagle; *Iwibbe* = blackbellied korhaan; *nkolenkole* = crowned plover; *induba* = Ross's lourie; *simuguwe* = grey lourie; *lyabola* = coppery tailed coucal; *hameya* = Senegal coucal; *maciciti* = fishing owl; *tumba* = Cape eagle owl; *intukuntuku* = whitefaced owl; *lukumba* = pennant winged nightjar; *ciyovwevwe* = speckled mousebird; *katotolubata* = bee-eater; *lubangwa* = hornbill; *cikaambilwa* = batis; *hazweezwe* = paradise flycatcher; *katiiza* = prinia; *katiiti* = waxbill; *masinja* = sunbird; *syaanakancolo* = kite.) e.g. Kuti bayanda kujaya bujwejwe, tuconco atutiiti, basala cilawo aasowelwa busenga ampobakwaapwida musozya. = If they wat to kill finches, seed-eaters or robins, they choose a place where bran has been thrown away or samp has been dished out. *muyuyu* = type of tree, the fruit, *ijuyu*, is eaten by elephants, e.g. Bazovwu balya njuyu mumuyuyu. = Elephants eat the fruit of the muyuyu tree. *muyuwa* = a musical-rattle, pl. miyuwa, e.g. Bina Buumba balayuuma miyuwa yakalyaba. = The mother of Buumba shakes the rattles for kalyaba dance very well. *muzabala* = a prodigal person, lacking resourcefulness, pl. bazabala, e.g. Bazabala mbacete. = Wasteful people are poor. Also mutapa *muzakala* = one who takes no care of what he has, pl. bazakala, e.g. Twaide kuba bazakala kuzintu nzyotujisi. = We have just become careless of the things we have.
your lover, e.g. Komwiita muzambinyoko mubuzigwe nzyomucita. Call your lover so that you explain what you do.
a long cloth (reaching from shoulder to feet), e.g. Nabwiinga nguusama muzeemo. The bride wears a long cloth.
a plan, e.g. Aawa ndijisi muzeezo wakusyanga buluba. = Here I have a plan to plant cotton.
an elusive person Also muyubi
a perverse person, a cheat, e.g. Muzelengani ujazya bana masoto. = A deceptive person kills children with the masoto disease. Also mu(m)pelenge
funeral ritual, e.g. Niwakazwa muzembo, bantu boonse bakaandaana. = When the funeral was over, all the people left.
a torch of burning grass, e.g. Kamuleta muzenge tumunike nzoka. = Bring a torch of burning grass so that we can light up the place where the snake is.
butter or cheese made out of milk, e.g. Mafwuta mazenge abikkwa mucisyu. = Butter is used for putting into relish.
a castrated male, e.g. Moombe muzibe ulafwambaana kuneneya. = A castrated calf quickly grows fat.
a stopper e.g. muzibo wansuwa = a stopper of a calabash. Also cisinsyo, muzyiko
type of plant (used for making light beer) e.g. Ndali kunywa cibwantu camuziinga. = I was drinking light beer made from muziinga roots. Also munkoyo.

a slave, e.g. Tamweelede kumucita mbuli muzike mwana mucaala. = You should not treat an orphan like a slave. Nekuba kuti muntu ulinanika twe lyaacikko uba muzike, pele mebo nsikookucita muzike wangu. Even though a person who smears ash from the fireplace becomes a slave, I will not treat you as my slave. Also mulanda, mutwanga
a long line, e.g. Kuti naa wabweza muzila wamapopwe muunda mulamfwu mpoyakuupozezya, ulamvwa musana wayuma nta. = If you take a long line of maize in a field, you will feel your back hurting.

a kind of kudu, an addax, pl. bazilawo, e.g. Kucibanda ca Kasako nkokonzya kubona muzilawo. = At the plain of Kasako is where you can see a kudu. Muvwimi wakabona bazilawo bone afwiifwi anguwe. = The hunter saw four kudus near him.
an executioner, e.g. Muzilikani wakajaya bantu bakajaninwa mulandu wabujayi. = The executioner killed people who had been found guilty of murder.
type of tree e.g. Busi bwamuzimbwa butanda nzoka. = The smoke of the burnt muzimbwa tree drives snakes away.

the spirit which leaves the human body at death. As a human dies his/her muya (soul) enters the world of the spirit as muzimo. e.g. Mujwa wangu nguwakabweza muzimo wabaama. = My niece is the one who inherited the spirit of my dead mother. Also cizimo
anus, rectum, e.g. Civwunye ncuuka cililya muzindo. A maggot eats its own anus.
noise of something falling, e.g. Musankwa watyoka naawa muzinga mupati. The boy was broken when he fell with a crash. Kulyuumina muzinga = throw oneself headlong to the ground.
an elephant's trunk, e.g. Muzinga wamuzovwu mmupati kapati. = The trunk of an elephant is very big. Also mulubalulwa, mubombo.
comb of honey, e.g. Wakaitobela nsolo kumwi ooku kayeeya kuti ulajana muzinga wabuci. = He followed the honey-bird while thinking he will find a honey-comb.
a cock, e.g. Muzingili wangu wakatalika kale kulila. My cock has already begun to crow. Also mukombwe, muzingini.
a shadow, e.g. Makumbi azimaanzya muzizimwa wangu. = The clouds have obliterated my shadow. Also cinzimweemwe
friend, e.g. Muzolani wangu nseelede kumulosya ansi. = I should not let my friend down.
pal, familiar friend Also muzolani.
type of tree, e.g. Bweele busilisigwaa muzotabalozi. = Scabies is treated with medicine from the muzotabalozi tree. Also kafwulwefwulwe, muyota-balozi
a large elephant, e.g. Muzovwu ujisi matwi mapati. = An elephant has big ears. muzuba

a dish of food containing crushed ground-nuts mixed with maize meal (and butter), shared by groom and bride, e.g. Bantu bafwukuma muzuba bayanda mali. = The people who stir up the fire where the meal is being cooked, want money.
one who is jealous in marital affairs, e.g. Ooyu mwanalumi mmuzuba, tayandi kujana muntu umbi kakkede mulubuwa. = This man is jealous, he does not like to find another man sitting in the courtyard.
a gourd used as container, used by women to store small fish, pl. mizubilo, e.g. Bamakaintu bazela nswi babikka mumizubilo. Women who fish, put what they catch into gourds.
a clan, e.g. Uli muzubo nzi? = What clan do you belong to?

a leader, head, pl. bazuluzi, e.g. Chuumangoma ngomuzuluzi abukoko aano. Chuumangoma is the organizer of the beer party here. Bazuluzi bazikolo ezi tabakonzyi kujana mali akuuzya mabbuku, zisamo akulya kwabana kuciindi cifwiifwi. = The headmasters are not able to find money to buy books, clothes and food for the pupils in a short time.
a watery pumpkin, e.g. Muungu muzuma wakabola. The watery pumpkin rotted.
type of tree, euphorbia, e.g. Ngoma zyamuzumagomba zilalila kapati. The drums from the euphorbia tree sound excellently. Also muzumangoma.
low thunder in the morning, foretelling rain, e.g. Sunu kulaba muyoba, imvwula yazuma muzumajuunza. Today there will be continuous rain, in the morning there was a rumble of thunder foretelling rain.
Also muzumagomba.
a plant which keeps mosquitoes away, e.g. Mansenya alatija kuti kwaumpwa muzumbani. = Mosquitoes fly away if the muzumbani plant is burnt.
an agreement, faith, e.g. Bakristo bajisi muzumino muli Jesu Kristo. = Christians have belief in Jesus Christ.

a sound, a peal of thunder, pl. mizumo, e.g. Kwakaba muzumo mupati akati kabasibukoko. = There was a great noise among the beer drinkers. Kana kalayoowa muzumo wandeke. = The child fears the sound of an aeroplane.

a type of rubber tree, e.g. Balwani balayanda kubelesya muzunda. = Fighters like using the wood of a rubber tree. (as a charm) muzundi a conquerer, e.g. Mucende okwa Banji ngomuzundi wabacendenyina. = The bull of Banji is the conquerer of all his fellow bulls.
a tree, e.g. Bana Haakoonde bakalya muzundangoma. = The people of Haakoonde ate the medicine of the muzundangoma tree.
a competition, e.g. Sunu kuli muzundano wabbola ku Chikuni. = Today there is a football competition at Chikuni.
a white person, e.g. Mu Muvwulo ndakaswaidwe muzungu waku Libingi. = On Monday I was visited by a white person from Livingstone. Also mukuwa.

the Sausage tree, (Kigelia Africana). It has woody, hanging, sausage-shaped fruits said to be poisonous to humans when unripe and inedible when ripe. When baked are used to ferment beer. The wood has many medicinal uses. e.g. Makwa amuzungula ngakusilisya cikoolo. = The bark of the muzungula tree cures the allergy which some people have towards certain foods. (The roots are also used to assist pregnant women.) Muzungula uzyala bana bapati. = The muzungula tree produces large fruit. Also cizutu, mvwula, mvwunguti.
the lily tree, also namuntengwa

sound, e.g. Sunu kwamvwugwa muzunzuminwa wamvwula. = Today the sound of the rain was heard. Cisaka coonse caakwiile kusabilwa muzunzuminwa wangoma. = The whole forest was just resounding to the thunder of the drum. Naakamana kupandulula ciloto cakwe kwakaba kuumuna kwamizunzuminwa. = When she explained her dream there was silence. Also muzuzumuna, muzuzumino, muzunzumina
a cone, e.g. Bana balasobana amuzuumwa wamubalo wancinga. = The children are playing with the cone of the bicycle-wheel.

a cerval, a slender wild-cat with long legs, large ears and a black-spotted orange-brown coat (any moderate-sized feline resembling the tiger), e.g. Inyama yamuzuzi ilanona. = The meat of the cerval is tasty.
sound, e.g. Ino nkuli kulimvwinsya muzuzumuna wangoma? = Where is the beat of the drum coming from? Also muzuzumina
a foreigner, a distant visitor, e.g. Twakaswaigwa muzwakule mumunzi wesu. = A visitor from far away visited our village.
the blood tree (red coloured sap, grows easily from cuttings, good timber) e.g. Mapulanga amuzwamalowa abambya zyuuno. = The planks of the muzwamulowa tree are used to make stools.
a thin and long object, e.g. Mudaala Cheembo wakalijisi musumo wakajisi muzwambalala walusako. = The old man Cheembo had a big spear which had a thin and long shaft.
a burning brand or torch, e.g. Kamuleta muzwenge tumunike nzoka munanda. = Bring a burning torch so that we throw light on the snake in the house. cf. muzenge.

type of plant, also known as soswe. The seeds are eaten whole (like beans) after boiling for one day and standing for a further two. It is used for diarrhoea: the woody root-stock is pounded and rubbed on the chair of the patient, is also used for stomach-ache, the root being chewed or chopped and drunk in cold water. e.g. Amumunywinsye muzwezio usoomona. = Make the one with diarrhoea drink the juice of the muzwezio plant.

a child who has a step father, e.g. Mukaintu wakakwata Jolezya wakalijisi mwana mulombe wamyaka yosanwe, ngotuti mumulaka mubi muzyaanyina. The woman whom Jolezya married had a son of five years (from a previous liason), whom we call in impolite language, 'the one who came with the mother'.
a native, an orginal occupant of the land, e.g. Ziindi zinji ibbuku lilelwa amuzyale wamumunzi. Usually the headmanship is given to an original inhabitant of the village.

a parent, e.g. pl. bazyali, e.g. Bazyali baloomoka, balanununa, balatongooka, balalilauka, balasyolauka akubwenta-bwenta nobalanga cisi cabo kaciyaabumenwa aziyanza zyabamuzwa kule. = Parents lament, they murmur, they complain, they bewail, they hiss in contempt and protest when they see their country being swallowed up by the culture of foreigners.
a member of the clan whose totem is the hyena, pl. Bazyamba, e.g. Bazyamba mbajwanyina a Bansaka. = The Bazyamba are joking partners with the Bansaka.
the female species, human or animal, e.g. Mukaintu muzyazyi mmuyumu kutumbuka. The female species are strong in giving birth. *(muzyazyi wansefwu = an eland cow; muzyazyi wambelele = a ewe)*
a local person who is well known, e.g. Ooyu muntu mmuzyibe mutamuumi. = This person is well known, do not beat him.

a love-potion used by women to control men, e.g. Bakaintu bamwi balayanda kubelesya musamu wamuzyondo. Some woman like to use the love-potion muzyondo (to control their husbands). Omuzyondo beleka nkaambo ndiyanda kuti kanditebbela nkuni sokwe wamuntu oyu! = O love potion work because I want this monkey of a man to gather firewood for me!
grandchild, e.g. Uubeleka ku Lusaka mmuzyukulu wangu. = The one who is working at Lusaka is my grandchild.
type of tree (roots used to mend baskets), e.g. Loozi Iwamuzyula nduyumu kapati. Fibre from the muzyula tree is very strong.
type of tree, e.g. Muzyula-matanga uzyala bana bazikotokoto. The muzyula-matanga tree produces round fruits.
manager, e.g. Twakabelesya kootokala kaniini kokwa mvwambalume wabbanki. We used the little car of the bank-manager.
grey hair, e.g. Moonga ulaa mwi ankumo. = Moonga has grey hair on his forehead.

a week, e.g. Ndakaakukkala mvwiki yoonse kumalila kwa Chipembele. = I stayed a whole week at the funeral at Chipembele. *Mumvwiki muli mazuba musanu amazuba obile.* = In a week there are five and two days. Also nsondo.
councils, assemblies, e.g. Basibunjaka balaa mwiyo lyoonse. = Trouble-makers always have their discussion groups. Also luvwiyu
a tadpole, pl. bamvwube, e.g. Kuli muvwube mupati muzyiba omu. = There is a big tadpole in the pond.
growling, complaints, e.g. Koyozya mvwulumina bulo. = Lessen the complaints while in bed.
a hat, e.g. Ndeelede kwaagusya malezu niinga yandeelela mvwuse. = I should shave off the beard that is when the hat will suit me.
type of insect, lionant, e.g. Muuka utegwa mwuku-mvwuku ukkala muvwu. = An insect called mvwukumvwuku lives in the soil. Also mfwuko-mfwuko.
rain, e.g. Yaboola *mvwula*, tulye *bowa*! = The rain has come so that we can eat mushrooms!
a willow tree, e.g. Basimaasikili balalila *mumvwule*. = Birds are chirping in the willow tree. Also cibumbya, muvwuli
a maggot, e.g. Nyama ibolede ijisi *mvwunyu zinji*. = Rotten meat has many maggots.
a place where a rabbit sleeps, e.g. *Aawa kuli mvwuta yasulwe*. = There is a place here where a rabbit sleeps.
the absence of what one would expect to be present, e.g. Wakajana kwacaala *mvwuta*, *mwana tako pe*. = She found the place was left empty, the child was not there.
hippopotamus, e.g. *Mvwuvwu mpati yakali kweenda ilikke mumeenda*. = A big hippo was moving alone in the water. Also civwubwe, *imvwuvwu*
a hat, e.g. *Imvwuze yamudaala yapya*. = The hat of the old man is burnt. Also *mvwuse, nzyeete*.
a grey-jackal, pl. *bamwaaba*, e.g. *Bamwaaba basondoka mupeyo*. = The grey-jackals go mad in the cold season.

(idiomiomatic usage) when it is bright, e.g. Uulowa wakali kuzyana kalitwa *mwaaba*. = The witch was dancing during the day. Bumwi buzuba alya eni mpolitwa *mwaaba*, bantu bakabona busi kabuunda mumulundu wa Maseke. = One day when it was bright, people saw smoke rising on Maseke Hill.
*amwaabani* = watershed. Also *muuma*
a generous person, e.g. *Amunzi wamwaabi kujanika bantu banji*. = Many people are to be found in the village of a generous person.
an albino, e.g. Baama bakazyala *mwaabi*. = My mother gave birth to an albino.
The elephant-orange or monkey-ball tree, e.g. *Mumwaabo omu kuli maabo manji*. = There are many oranges on the *mwaabo* tree. Also *muntamba*.

a gorge, an aperture between rocks, a valley, cleft, opening, e.g. Ukainde *amwaako* wamilundu noyakusika ku Nakasiikka. = Pass through a gorge that is when you can reach Nakasiikka. Munzi okwa Sikacilakanjina wakayakidwe mu *mwaako* wamalundu. = The home of Sikacilakanjina was built in a gorge between the hills. Basimbi bamwi balasama tusinsi tufwaafwi, tubalangala alimwi tulaa *mwaako* usika mukasolo. = Some girls wear short dresses which are transparent and have a cleft which reaches to the hip. Also *mwako*
the mane of a horse or lion, e.g. Syuumbwa naakanyema wakabusya *mwaala*. = When a lion got angry the mane stood up.
an elder brother, e.g. *Mwaalu wangu wasika ino-ino*. = My elder brother has just arrived.

a hunter, e.g. Nguulya *mwaalu* wakazwisya cikwama cakwe catusanga twamulilo, wadoneka cavwilima cisyokwe. = There is the hunter who takes out his box of matches, he lights it and the bush is set ablaze.
a man, e.g. *Aawa kuli mwaalumi ngubauma kapati*. = Right here there is a man whom they have severely beaten.
violet flower, e.g. Bununkilizi *bwamwaama buletelezya nzuki*. = The scent of the violet flower attracts the bees.
a quarrelsome person, e.g. Muntu *mwaambani* ulayanda kulwa- na. = A quarrelsome person likes to fight.
a speaker, e.g. Nguni *mwa- ambi* mumakani aya? = Who is the speaker in this matter?
a language, pl. myaa- mbo, e.g. Misyobo yabantu yoonse yakali- jisi myaambo antela milaka ibagaminina. All the tribes of people had their lang- uages or tongues which were specifically theirs.
a maxim, pl. myaambo, e.g. Mukaintu watusiila *mwaambo* ngotunakuyeeya lyoonse. = The woman has left us a saying which we will always remember.
an important matter, e.g. Kuli *mwaa- mbo* ngotweelede kuyeeyesya. = There is an important matter which we ought to reflect upon.
a waist-belt of broad cloth, a girdle around the chest, e.g. Kamumwaanga *mwaambo* muntu uciswa mucamba. = Tie a girdle around the person who has a sore chest.
a sexually unbridled person, e.g. Muntu *mwaamu* ulabinda kuciswa sikalileke. = A licentious person is quick to be affected with AIDS.
a frothy mixture of sour and fresh milk, e.g. Mucigabba eci kuli *mwaanda* mulemu-lemu. = In this tin there is a thick frothy mixture of sour and fresh milk. Also cipwaza, canda
a hundred, pl. myaanda, e.g. Ndakaula mayi ali *mwaanda*. = I bought a hundred eggs.
the freezer of beasts, i.e. the lion, e.g. Kuti kwasika *mwaanda-banyama* mucisi inga bantu tabayendeendi. = If a lion enters the terrritory the people do not move about.
a boulder, huge rock, e.g. Mumugoti wa Muntanga kwakajanika *mwaandami*. = In the well of Muntanga a huge rock was found.

a big pot covered with skin and used as drum on certain oсса- sions, e.g. Nikwakasika munyama mukali mucisi, bantu bakauma *mwaandu*. = When a fierce animal arrived in the terri- tory, the people beat the *mwaandu* drum.

things tied together to rattle, e.g. Ciindi cakuyaluka musimbi bantu balaanga zintu zyakulizya nzyobati '*mwaandu*'. Myaandu eyo ilalizigwa masiku onse. = When a girl menstruated the people would tie rattles together which they called *mwaandu*. These rattles would be beaten all through the night.
medicine for the chest, e.g. Muntu uciswa mucamba ka- nywa *mwaangabbwe*. A person with chest- pains should take *mwaangabbwe* medicine.
a tassel of sorgum, pl. myaangala, e.g. Uno mwaka myaangala yamaila ili kabotu nkaambo mvwula ya- kawa kapati. = This year the tassels of sorgum are good because the rain fell heavily.
a type of plant
a captive, e.g. *Mwaange* wa- kabikkwa muntolongo kwamyezi fwuka. = The prisoner was put into jail for nine months.

a mopani tree (Colopho-sper- mum mopane), wood-ashes or their juice used in cooking green relishes. Twine from bark fibre. Powdered sap used as mastic. Boiled sap used with ciwawa sap as birdlime. Wood used for pestles and for house and granary-construction. e.g. Misamu *yamwaani* mmi-botu kuyasya maanda. Mopani trees are good for building houses.
a reluctant giver, e.g. Muntu *mwaanka* tafwambi kuvwungulula janza. = A reluctant giver is not quick to open what the hand contains.
a big hand, e.g. Bbalarnombe wakajisi mwaanza mupati. = Bbalajombe had a big hand.
a composer of songs, a poet, e.g. Mwiinga mmwaanzi waziimbo zyamucikombelo. = Mwiinga is a composer of hymns for the church.
type of tree, e.g. Mukagonke ziyako zyamwaanzwa. = Cut down poles from the mwaanzwa tree.
a disobedient person, e.g. Ooyu mwana mmwaasi, tayandi kutumwa. This child is disobedient, s/he does not want to be sent on errands. Also mukasi
a gap, a gorge, lane, passage, aperture, e.g. Kunyina munyama ukonzya kweela mumwaatu wanyeleti. = There is no animal that can go through the eye of a needle. Also mwaako.
open space between houses, e.g. Koya ukaime amwaatuka wamaanda alya. Go and stand in the open space between those houses.
a narrow passage, e.g. Ndilaata kwiinda amwaatukwa. = I cannot pass through the narrow passage.
one who drives men away, e.g. Mukaintu oyu mmwaazi, ulabakaka basankwa boonse. This woman rejects all men, she does not give in to any proposal.
an obstinate person, e.g. Muntu mwaazi tazumini zyaamba bantu bambi. = An obstinate person does not agree to what other people say.

the knob-thorn tree, (Acacia Nigrecens), which has a very hard, heavy and durable wood. Is used for flooring, railway sleepers. Bark gives a good rope, leaves eaten as spinach, bark, roots and leaves have many medicinal uses. e.g. Kondipa bumvwa bwamwaba ndisongozye. = Give me a thorn of the knob-thorn tree so that I can remove a splinter.
type of tree (Stryschnos innocua), e.g. Mwabo uzyala maabo alya bantu banji. = The mwabo tree produces fruits which are eaten by many people. Also mwaabo
luck, (Chinyanja) e.g. Muntu oyu wabaa mwai wakujana mulimo. = This man has luck in finding work. Also mwao, coolwe.
a year, pl. myaka, e.g. Ino wakazyalwa mumwaka nzi? = Now in what year were you born?
the growing season, Sept. - Oct., the end of the year when much work is done, e.g. Balimi balibambila bulimi bwabo kumwaka. = Farmers are preparing for their farming season in the dry season.

last year, e.g. Baama bakafwa mwakali. My mother died last year. mwakali yuulya = the year before last, or, the year after next. e.g. Ndiya kukuswaya mwakali yuulya. = I will visit you the year after next.
thebefore last Also mwaka wakamana ulya.

a boulder, a grey stone, e.g. Sokwe mupati ulikkede amwala mupati mumulundu. = A big monkey is sitting on a huge boulder on the hill. Basankwa bakali kukkala abbwe lyamwala. = The boys were sitting on a grey rock.
The torchwood or desertdate tree, e.g. Mwalabwe ujanika mumilundu. The torchwood tree is found in hills. Also mulyabazovwu
a prisoner, e.g. Mwambe wakatija muntolongo. = The prisoner escaped from jail. Also sintolongo, mwaange, kayili/kaili.
a queen species of termite, e.g. Inswa zyakapola mucuulu nkaambo mwame wakafwa. = The termites left the termite-hill because the queen-termite had died.
a wealthy person, e.g. Muntu mwami uyandisya lubono Iwakwe. = A rich person loves her/his posessions.
a chief, e.g. Cakatola ciindi cilamfwu kusala mwami mupya. = It took a long time to choose a new chief.
a female chief, pl. bami-bakaintu, e.g. Amwi manyika alelwa abamibakaintu. = Some nations are ruled by female chiefs.
a child, e.g. Amumunyonsye mwana, wafwa kulila. = Suckle the child, it is tired of crying.
a nephew or niece, e.g. Mutinta mmwana wangu. = Mutinta is my niece.
my mother's child, friend, e.g. Koboola buyo mwanaabaama koleka kulila. = Come, my mother's child, stop crying.
a bobbin, e.g. Bunweba bwamana amwanaa-bunyweba. = The thread is finished on the bobbin.
a queen-termite of a species called lumona or mulanzyi, e.g. Komujaya mwanaacuulu mulazyi umane. Kill the queen so that the termites will be finished.
a child of my paternal uncle or maternal aunt, e.g. Joojo mmwanaakwesu kumukowa wabamatata. = Joojo is a brother of mine on the side of the father's clan.
a hand-stone for grinding, e.g. Bakaapa baziya mabele amwanaankando. = My grandmother is grinding millet with a hand-stone. Also nkando.
a free/gentle/helpful, person, pl. banababantu, e.g. Ndajana mwanaamuntu wakandigwasya mumapenzi angu. = I found a kind-hearted person who helped me in all my problems. Also mwanamuntu.
a private lover, one's beloved, e.g. Ooyu musimbi ngumwanakasuwa wangu. = This girl is my beloved. Ooyu musankwa ngumwanakasuwa wangu. = This boy is my lover.
a woman, a wife, e.g. Lina mmwanakazi wangu. = Lina is my wife. Also mukaintu
a husband, e.g. Moonga mmwanalumi wa Lina. = Moonga is Lina's husband. Also mulumi
a friend, (a non-sexual relationship), e.g. Musankwa oyu nsemusisi twaambo, ngumwanamakani wangu. = I do not hide any secrets from this man, he is my friend (to whom I reveal everything).
focus, e.g. Mazubaano bantu banji ngumwanambele kunkwela. = Nowadays many people are focused on sex.
an ordinary person, pl. banababantu, e.g. Banababantu bamwi balalaigwa. = The children of some ordinary people are well advised. Also mwanaamuntu.
a wager, a bet on a race, e.g. Atucite mwanamubeebe kusika waalya. = Let us compete in running over there.
the turpentine or mopani tree, e.g. Amugonke mwane, ngomuyumu. = Cut the mopani tree, it is the hard one. Also mwaane, mupane.
an itinerant, a homeless person, e.g. Ooyu muntu takonzyi kulela mwana nkaambo ngumwanga. = This person cannot keep a child because he is a homeless person. Also nakweenda, sicibiya-camunzila.
medicine for the chest
a type of tree, e.g. Mancwe azyalila mumwangule. = The finches are raising their young in a mwangule tree. Also cisomwe, muchaca.
the younger sister of a woman, e.g. Masowe mmwanice wabamaama. = Masowe is the younger sister of my mother.

young brother of man, pl. banike, e.g. Banike baunka kukuteya tuyuni. = My brothers have gone off to trap birds. (Amongst the Valley Batonga mwanike can refer to a man's brother or sister who is in direct lineal descent. However mwanike usually refers to children only.)
young one, e.g. Iwe tokonzyi kucita eci nkaambo ucili mwanikenike. = You cannot do this because you are still young.

cassava, manioc, e.g. Bamalozi balya nsima yabusu bwamwanja. = The Balozi eat nsima from cassava flour. Sunu mu Zambezi tulalya miyanda yamwanja muminzi yesu. = Today we people of the Zambezi eat the roots of cassava in our villages. Mfwulumende wesu ulatuma baalumi basongo bapampu bayiisya bazyali besu kulima mwanja azilyo zimwi. = Our government sends experts to teach our parents how to plant cassava and other crops. Also makamba, syaakanjungo
his/her/their brother or sister, e.g. Sena wamubona mwanookwabo Masowe? = Did you see the sibling of Masowe? Also mwanaakwabo
your brother or sister, e.g. Nguli mwanookwanu? = Where is your sibling? Also mwanaakwanu.
my/our brother or sister, e.g. Mwanookwesu nguuyiisya ku Chilindi. = Our sister is the one teaching at Chilindi. Also mwanaakwesu.
type of tree, e.g. Zicinda zyamwanazabala nziyumu. = Verandah poles of mwanazabala wood are strong. Also mululu, mupingili.
tree, e.g. Kamuleta loozi Iwamwanzwa tubangile butala. = Bring fibres from a mwanzwa tree so that we bind the maize bin.
a yawn, e.g. Sunu masiku ndamuka koona, ndabaa mwao acifwumofwumo. = Last night I was late in sleeping, I was yawning in the morning.
a structure on which firewood is placed, e.g. Baama balundika nkuni amwata. = My mother is stacking firewood on the firewood holder. Also bwalo
a heap of firewood, e.g. Ndabona mukaintu uyumwide mwaya wankuni. = I saw a woman carrying a pile of firewood. Also cileye, muleye
a woman who refuses men. Also mwaazi
jealousy, (used in Valley) e.g. Ncibi kubaa mwebwa abana babeenzinyoko. = It is bad to be jealous of your friends children. Also munyono
the jawbone, esp. of the upper jaw, pl. meebo, e.g. Mweebo wangu ulacisa, nsekonzyi kulya. = My jawbone is sore, I cannot eat. Meebo tiyaali kukonzya kuputauka. = The jaws could not move.
the main road, e.g. Mugwagwa oyu ngomweelanyika uya kumigoti. = This road is the main road going to the Copperbelt.
one who travels a lot, e.g. Utaunki kwa Joojo tokamujani nkaambo ngumweelanyika. = Do not go to Joojo's, you will not find him because he travels a lot

a person with no fixed abode, a vagrant, pl. beeleenze, e.g. Mweeleenzi ulasowaila lubono Iwakwe. = A vagrant squanders his wealth. Basankwa banji mazubaano mbeeleenze, mbasyoonto balaa mpemo ziyoya. = Many men nowadays are moving about in a useless way, there are few who have noses that breathe. i.e. they are unable to discern what is of value and what is not. Mwana utamvwi kulaigwa, uuyanda buyo kucita ciyanda moyo wakwe, waakukomena uya kuba mweeleenze. = A young person who does not listen when advised, smears herself with strongly scented who wants to do what his heart wants, perfume is followed by men. when he grows up he will become *mweemvwe* new grass, e.g. Mwakauseless. Also *mwanga* ndiimika *mumweemvwe* wanyanzabili. = *mweelo* amount, e.g. Nciyumu kuti You put me standing in fresh green grass. muntu azyibe *mweelo* wabana a zintu *mweenda-buseka* one who goes zyamunyika zyoonse. It is difficult for a about smiling, pl. *beenda-buseka*, e.g. person to know the quantity of people *Mweenda-buseka ulakkomaninwa abantu* and things in the world. *boonse*. amount, e.g. Basimbi muba- everyone. pe *mweelwe* weelene wankuni bayumune. *mweendalubi* name given to a baby = Give the girls a suitable amount of when someone dies in the house where firewood to carry. the baby is born.

aroma, scent, e.g. Lyoonse *mweendanzila* a traveller, e.g. Kundinumfwida *mweema* wanyama ijikidwe. tambula *mweendanzila* cipa zina bbotu. = = I always smell the aroma of cooked To receive a traveller creates a good meat. Ma! Ununkidwe *mweema* wanya- name for oneself. ma, ulwala manunki-nunki. = You are *mweendelezi* a leader, e.g. *Mweendeobsessed with the smell of meat, you are *lezi* wamunzi oyu ngusibbuku Haamasuffering from the disease called *ma- imbo*. The ruler of this village is headnunki-nunki*. man Haamaimbo. Also *mweendezi*.

a type of tree, e.g. Makwa *mweendo* a leg, pl. *myeendo/meendo*, *amweembe* asilisya bana bagonkwa. = e.g. *Mweendo* wangu ulacisa nkaambo The barks of the *mweembe* tree are used ndakawa. = My leg is paining because I to treat children who suffer from the fell. (*mweendo wakucamba* = foreleg) illness called *makupa*. (If a mother *mweengo* a line, e.g. Koenga *mweebecomes pregnant before weaning the *ngo* mulamfwu mumusenga. = Trace a child, the child may be afflicted with an long line in the sand. illness called *makupa* during which it *mweeni* a cousin in marriage, e.g. Mapurges frequently.) Also *mweembwe* inza nguwakali *mweeni* wangu nindaka*mweembezi* a herder of cattle, e.g. kwata. Mainza was my cousin when I *Mweembezi* wazitola kale nombe mu- married.

The herder has already taken *mweenima* child of my maternal aunt, the cattle to the bush. e.g. *Mweenima* nguwakandisindikila ku*mweembo* a side-blown musical horn, dilwe. The child of my maternal aunt pl. *myeembo/meembo*, e.g. Kamwale accompanied me to the funeral.

column1: usiba mweembo kumana bukata = The mweeninyina
column2: his/her grandfather, girl being initiated plays the *mweembo* e.g. Tacitondwi kuli nguwe kusobana horn to take away the loneliness. Chi- *amweeninyina*. = It is not taboo for her to kwamaalu wasiba *mweembo* akugawida play with her grandfather.

his/hercousin, e.g. Ukamulange *mweehorn and aroused the mourners. *ninyina* wakatumbuka. Go and look at *mweempula* a strongly scented girls her cousin who has given birth. charm, e.g. Musimbi wanana *mweempula* *mweeninyoko* your grandfather, e.g. utobelwa basankwa. = The girl who Ndakali kudilwe lyamweeninyoko wakafwa mwakali. = I was at the funeral of your grandfather who died last year.
a gap, e.g. Utasiyi mweenya awo kunjila mpeyo. = Do not leave a space there for the cold to enter.
the firmament, e.g. Sunu kunyina makumbi mumweenya. = Today there are no clouds in the sky.
male species of animal, e.g. Kuli mweenze mupati mubutanga obu. = There is a big male in this herd.
a visitor, stranger, newcomer, e.g. Amumusombe cibwantu mweenzu. Offer sweet-beer to the visitor.
wiindi= I am a stranger passing by. Also muswayi.
my friend, e.g. Cipego eci cakazyila kumweenzuma. = This gift came from my friend.

the concluding funeral ceremony which takes place some time after the burial, (or the beer made to offer to the new spirit), e.g. Mweesyo wabakaapa ulalinda juunza. = The final funeral-ceremony will take place tomorrow. Bantu bakona niwamana mweesyo. The people inherit when the mweesyo is over. Nikwakainda myezi misyoonto munene kafwide, mweesyo wakakumbwa. = When a few months had passed after the old man died, the beer of the concluding funeral-ceremony was brewed.
a fishing rod, e.g. Koleta mweeta tulobe nswi. = Bring the fishingstick so that we fish.
the rod of a trap, e.g. Munkalanga ngomuyumu kumweeta wansya. = The munkalanga tree is strong for use as a rod for trapping a duiker. Also mweeto.
the bent pole or stick which acts as a spring in the kabulindi trap, e.g. Insya yacegwa yatoleela amweeto niyaunka. The duiker which was caught took the stick-spring with it when it escaped.
the top-stick or rod tied to the string of the idiba trap, e.g. Mweeto wadiba watyoka. The rod of the idiba trap is broken.
a clan-name whose totem is the crocodile, pl. Beetwa, e.g. Beetwa mbabeendelezi bamalende. = The Beetwa clan-members are the supervisors of the rain-shrine.

a type of tree, the pods are liked by cattle and sheep, e.g. Siluwe ulaluma mbelele kumwaka noziyandaula mweeye. A leopard attacks the sheep when they go out looking for mweeye pods in the cold season. Inombe zilayanda kulya bana bamweeye. = Cattle like mweeye pods.
tail of a fish, e.g. Mweeye wamubondo mmupapali. = The tail of a barbel is flat.
a vlei/valley or open space, e.g. Impongo zilacela mumweezi. = The goats are grazing in open country.
a comparison, e.g. Aaka kaambo takakwe mweezyo. This matter has no comparison.
a clan name among the Zimbabwean Batonga whose totem is the vulture, e.g. Baleya bamu Zambia mbaba Mwembe mu Zimbabwe. The Baleya clan of Zambia is the Mwembe clan in Zimbabwe.
type of fish which move in a line, e.g. Kamubweza nkoli tukaume nswi zyamwenda-kalongo. = Bring a club so that we beat the mwendakalongo fish.
a species of sorgum which can be eaten raw, e.g. Bazyali batebula maila amwende mumuunda. = The parents are harvesting sorghum in the field. Also imbwende
a leg, e.g. Sibbola watyoka mwendo mumusobano. = The footballer broke a leg in the game. Also mweendo.
a torch, a burning brand, e.g. _Amumunike mwenge mucaanda kwanjila nzoka._ = Light a torch in the hut where a snake has entered. Also muzenge
a rash, e.g. Kaubi kabamba _mwengo alukanda._ = A caterpillar makes a rash on the skin.
a traced line, e.g. Koyenga _mwengo ansi bazikutubone nkutwagama._ = Trace a line on the ground so that they will see where we have gone.
a gap, e.g. Kamwiinda a _mwenya awa._ = Pass through the gap there. Also mweenya.
a duiker, e.g. Muvwimi wajaya _mwenze mupati masiku._ = The hunter killed a large duiker at night.
a boar
a wanderer, e.g. Ooyu _mwenzeenzi unyina cilawo._ = This wanderer has no dwelling.

season when vegetation begins to grow, the cold season, e.g. Cakali ciindi _camweto, lusamusamu kalusyuuka._ = It was the season of the beginning of growth when the trees begin to grow. _Ino nkokwakali mweto, mpeyo kakali kaambo kambi._ = As it was the season of growth, the cold was something else. Bamfwulumende balakasya kuzela mu-ciindi _camweto._ = Government officials forbid fishing during the cold season.
a friend, e.g. Tweelede kuyanda _mwenzuma lyoonse._ = We ought always to love a friend. cf. mweenzuma.
a torch, e.g. Kamumunika _mweye mubwina mubone ciliko._ = Flash the torch into the hole to see what is there. Also mwenge.

a month, pl. myezi/mezi, e.g. Ncintu cibotu kapati ku Mutonga onse kuzyiba _myezi mbwiitwa mumulaka wa-kwabo._ = It is a very good thing for every Mutonga to know how the months are called in his/her own language. Njeeyi myezi: *Mukazimaziba, Mulumi, Miyoba, Mukubwekaangala, Kaandakaniini, Gandapati, Kkunkumunamasamu, Itwi, Ivwivwi, Kavwumbikaniini, Ivwumbipati, Nalupale.* = Here are the months, January February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.

the moon, e.g. *Sunu watalika kuzyuka mwezi.* = Today the moon is late in rising from the east. *Cakabatolela ciindi kuubona mwezi nkaambo kakali keengu kasyoonto kakasendekede.* = It took them time to see the moon because it was a small crescent declining. *mwezi mutete* = a new moon; *mwezi mulamfwu-lamfwu* = a crescent-shaped moon; *mwezi ucengeme* = first quarter/last quarter

menstruate, *-ba kumwezi | -ya kumwezi, -li kumwezi,* e.g. *Ncibi kulundusya sicikolo uli kumwezi.* = It is bad to make a pupil run who is menstruating. *Mwezi oyu wakamana, tiindakaubona.* = When this month finished, I did not menstruate.

type of tree *(Ziziphus Abyssinica),* has a dark, heavy, hard wood resistant to termites and borers. Uses: fencing for kraals and villages and for covering graves. Yields abundant pollen and nectar for bees. Fruit and leaves used for relish and are finely chopped and soaked in water to make a drink for children with stomach-ache. e.g. *Sunu ndali kulya cinkomba camwicecete.* = Today I was eating a relish of *mwicecete* leaves. Also *mucecete*
a burning smell, e.g. *Kamujula nsima eyo yanunka mwidakule.* = Take off that nsima it has a smell of burning. Also syitila

oil, e.g. *Masusu ananikwa mwido ngamuntiki.* = Hair smeared with oil is called muntiki. Wakazinanika *mwido* akuziyanika ngoma zyakwe. = He smeared his drums with oil and hung them up to dry. Musamu wakali mukati wakali kusiya mbuli *mwido*. = The medicine inside was black like oil.
a type of tree, (*Berchemia Discolor*), has probably the largest timber in East and Central Africa, is used for furniture, door-frames and carvings.

nectarpowdered heartwood gives a black dye for basketmaking. Edible fruit is high in Vitamin C. Can be boiled and mixed with millet for porridge. Has ritual uses, e.g. Mukamufwu ugonka *mwii* kumana malweza. = The wife of the deceased has to cut down the *mwii* tree to blot out the evil omen. Also mwinji

the long feather of a cock's tail, e.g. Ngoma yakakondela nkabela Syaanasulwe wakaba *amwiimba* ukankamanisya. The drum was at its climax, thereupon the hare put on a wonderful feather of a cock's tail.
a talented singer, e.g. Mucisi muno kuli *baimbi banji*. In this country there are many talented singers.
a representative, e.g. Mwami wesu *ngomwiiminizi* wesu ku Bbooma. = Our chief is our representative at the government offices.
rivalry, e.g. Ono wakaba *mwiindanwa* aumwi-aumwi wakali kuyanda kwaamba caano cakwe. = Now there developed a rivalry among each one who wanted to tell his story. Also *mwiindano*
the lower leg, the calf of the leg, e.g. Ijamba lyakandiyasa *amwiindi*. = The hoe wounded me on the lower leg.
a type of tree, e.g. Bayuni balya bana *bamwiindiwakwale*. = The birds eat the fruit of the *mwiindiwakwale* tree.
a hanger, e.g. Koanzika cisani cako *amwiinga* awo. Hang up your garment on the hanger there. Also mulenga.
a warthog, e.g. *Bamwiingile* bazimana nyemu mumuunda. = The warthogs have finished the groundnuts in the field. Also *mwingile*.
a type of tree, wood used for spear shafts and clubs. e.g. Inkoli ya*mwiingili* ninjumu kapati. A club made from *mwiingili* wood is extremely hard.
a handle, pl. *miini*, e.g. Watyoka *mwiini* wajamba lyokwa Haatyoka. = The handle of Haatyoka's hoe is broken.

type of tree, the leaves are chewn, the berries eaten. e.g. Bana *bamwiinya-meezi* balasiya nibabizwa. The berries of the *mwiinya-meezi* tree become black when they are ripe. Also munonzya-meenda, munyoonyo

a small aperture, as for winged termites to come out, pl. *miinzo*, (*mwiinzo wacuulu* = the opening of the ant hill), e.g. *Amwiinzo* mupati mpaazwa nswa zinji. It is from a big opening that many flying ants come out. Meenda *ngomwiinzo wabuumi*. = Water is the opening of life.
door bold or fastener, e.g. Kamupinga *mwinzyo* acijazyo batanjili babbi. Put the bolt on the door so that thieves do not come in.
an invited guest, e.g. Amumupe cuuno *mwiitidwe*. = Give a chair to the invited guest. Also *mweenzu*
a teacher, e.g. *Mwiiyi* mupati ulayandwa abasicikolo boonse. = The head teacher is loved by all the pupils. *Mwiiyi* ulayiisya mucikolo. The teacher is teaching in the school.
a type of tree, e.g. *Mwijejete* uligwa cinkomba. The leaves of the *mwijejete* tree are eaten for relish. Also mwicecete, mucecete
a medicinal plant, (*Guibourtia cobjugata*), e.g. Mulwazi taakaponesegwa *amwijola*. The patient was not cured by the medicine of the *mwijola* plant.
a fly whisk made of elephant tail, e.g. *Mwami uleenda amwiko mujanza.* = The chief walks with a fly whisk in his hand.
an owl, e.g. *Mwina ulalila mumusamu.* = An owl is hooting in the tree. Also *tumba*.
wife of the king, e.g. *Mwinamwami mupati ulalemekwa.* = The queen is honoured.
my wife, e.g. *Mwinangu waunka kucigayo.* = My wife is gone to the mill.
calf of the leg, e.g. *Nzambalika ulaa cikoto amwindi.* = Nzambalika has a lump on the calf of the leg. Also *mwiindi, insafwu*.

a medicinal plant, the bark of the root is powdered and rubbed into small cuts and joints to strengthen the patient. e.g. *Mwindiokwale usilisya zicisa.* = The powdered root-bark of the plant, *mwindiokwale*, heals wounds.
an ointment, drum-plaster made of groundnuts and soot. e.g. *Booye banana mwindo.* = Young girls smear themselves with ointment. Also *mwido*
a warthog, e.g. *Naakavwuluma mwingile, babwa bakabbindila micila.* = When the warthog snorted, the dogs put their tails between their legs. Also *munjile*

type of tree, (*Grewia bicolor*), edible fruit used for flavouring porridge, wood used for making spears, clubs, drum-pegs, frames for fish-baskets and bird-lime traps, the flexible branches are used for binding poles for walls and roof. e.g. *Nkoli yamwingili ninjumu kapati.* = A club made of *mwingili* wood is very strong. Also *mwiingili*
payment in part, e.g. *Ulakonzya kupa mwingu buce-buce limwi uyakumaninzya.* = You can make payment in part until you clear the debt.
a glow-worm, a firefly, e.g. *Mwinimwenge zimweka mainza.* = Fireflies shine in the rainy season. Also *inguunguni, munimuni*.
a warthog, pl. *bamwinjile*, e.g. *Bamwinjile bafwumba zilindi muluumba.* = The warthogs dig holes in the *muumba* tree thicket. Also *mwingile, munjile*
salt, e.g. *Kamubikka mwino mucisyu cilweele.* = Put salt in the relish to make it tasty. also *munyo, sautu*.
your friend, e.g. *Utabbi lubono Iwamwinzinyoko.* = Do not steal the wealth of your friend. Also *mweenzinyoko*
an exit or hole for flying ants to come out, e.g. *Mwinzo oyu wakandipa nswa zinji kapati.* This hole gave me a great many flying-ants. Also *mwiinzo*
opportunity, e.g. *Kuti boonse bantu bakonzya kulemekana tuya kuba amwinzo wakuyaka cisi cesu.* If all people respect one another we will have the opportunity to build up our country. Also *mukusi*

a type of tree (*Phyllogeiton discolor*), the fruit is eaten raw Feb.March also dried and stored and can be pounded with cereals or made into a cake. Wood is used for hoe-handles. e.g. *Amufwale mwiini wajamba wamwiyi.* = Carve a handle for the hoe from a *mwiiyi* tree.
pl. of *mwaanda*, a hundred, e.g. *Ndakajana mpongo zili myaanda mumuunda.* = I found hundreds of goats in the field.
pl. of *mwaangala*, an ear of sorgum or corn, e.g. *Mu Mukubwekaangala niituba myaangala yamuceme.* = It is in April that the ears of sorgum become white.
roars, cries, pl. of mwaawu, e.g. *Mumyaawu yamulavwu njakunjila.* = I will enter where the lion is roaring.
pl. of mwaka, a year, e.g. Kwainda *myaka* ili lusele nselekede milimo. = Seven years have passed since I stopped work.
gossip, e.g. Ulaa *myalika* kumulomo wakwe. Her mouth is full of gossip. Kubaa *myalika* ncibi. = To be a gossiper is bad.
the jaws, pl. of mweebo, e.g. Kuti *myeebo* kaicisa, inga totafwuni kabotu. = If the jaws are sore, you may not be able to chew. (*mweebo* wakunsi = lower jaw; *mweebo* wakutala = upper jaw)
pl. of mweengo, a line traced on ground, e.g. Bayi bakeenga *myeengo*
ansi. The teacher traced two lines on the ground.
pl. of mwengo, a carving tool, e.g. Koleta *myengo* tufwazye ncili. = Bring carving tools so that we carve a mortar.
the time when maize is about to start flowering, e.g. Mapopwe akaligwa nombe naakabaa *myondo.* = The maize was eaten by cattle when the time came for it to flower.

strips of cloth attached to the shawl used for carrying baby, e.g. mondo, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kubikka *myondo* angubu zyabana. People of long ago attached strips of cloth to the main shawl for carrying babies.
pl. of moombe, a hem, e.g. Yazutuka *myoombe* yangubo yamwana. = The hems of the child's blanket became undone.
pl. of moyo, e.g. *Myoyo* yabantu bajayi mmiyumu. The hearts of murderers are hard.
villages, pl. of munzi, e.g. *Mumyunzi* bana balagwasya bazyali babo mumilimo yaandene. In the villages the children help their parents in various jobs. Also *minzi*
stripes on an animal or on cloth, pl. of muubi, e.g. Munyama wa-*myuubi* mmubotu kweebela. = An animal with stripes is nice to admire.
pl. of muumba, a fishingspear, e.g. Bazeli bakajaya nswi zinji *amyuumba.* The fishermen killed many fish with spears.
pl. of muunda, a field, e.g. Basibbuku bajisi *myuunda* minji. = The headman has many fields.
pl. of muungo, a spoon, e.g. Amulete *myuungo* balisye ceele bana. = Bring spoons for the children to eat porridge with.
a female baboon, pl. banaboole, e.g. Ndabona *banaboole* bobilo bajisi bana. I have seen two female baboons carrying babies.

speeding as if in a race, e.g. Bana baniini mbabakasaanguna kutapukila anze, ulati bacita *nabubeebe* nkaambo bakaliminidwe kapati. = The little children were the first to rush outside as if they were racing because they were under pressure to answer the call of nature.
a confirmed thief (habitual), a recidivist, e.g. Uulipa kuba *nabubbi* lyoonse uyendela muntolongo. = The one who had made himself a confirmed thief is always going into prison.
an iguana, pl. banabulwe, e.g. Bama Lozi bamwi balya *banabulwe.* = Some of the Lozi people eat iguana.
a humane person, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngunabuntu. This person is humane. Also mwanamuntu.

an unmarried woman, a spinster, e.g. Munanda yanabutema ulya kusika bantu banji. Many people come to that spinster's house nabuyuni a very big herd of cattle, e.g. Mulimi munkutwe ujisi *nabuyuni*. = An industrious farmer has a large herd of cattle.
a grass fishing-net, a scooper, e.g. Muzeli uzezya *nabuyuwa* ujaya nswi zinji. = The fisher who fishes with a grass fishing-net kills many fish.

a bride, e.g. *Nabwiinga* talanduki mulonga. = A bride should not cross the river. kuya kukwela = bring bride for the first time; kuya kusimuna = bring bride for the second time nacibula a flirt, e.g. Muntu ujisi moyo wabuvwuule *ngunacibula*. = A person who has strong uncontrolled sexual desires entices others playfully.
person with one eye missing or pierced, e.g. Muntu *nacimbolyo* talangisigwi. = A person with a missing eye is not stared at.
the oribi, pl. banacindwe, e.g. Bavwimi bavwima *banacindwe* mucibanda. = The hunters are hunting oribi in the plain. Also naciindwe, nakacindwe, nanzele.
a prostitute, e.g. Kasimbi aka kaya kuba nkaanga *nacinzulu*. = That young girl will become a prostitute. Also nacibula
an open person, e.g. Ooyu muntu *ngunacisala*, kunyina ncasisa pe. = This person is open, he hides nothing.
a brown-skinned person Also nacisayaya
a person of mixed blood, e.g. Mucizyi wangu wakazyala banacisandule nkaambo wakakwatwa mukuwa. My sister bore coloured-children because she was married to a white-man.
a slave made a wife
a seed of a different variety, e.g. Ndakasyanga mbuto *yanacisandule*. = I planted a seed of different variety.
a liberal person
a praise name for a brown-skinned spouse, e.g. Mweetwa ulamuyandisya *nacisayaya* wa-kwe. = Mweetwa loves his wife who is brown. Also nacisalala.
the spur-winged goose, e.g. Muwezi waakujaya *nacisekwe* omwe mucibanda. = The hunter killed one spurwinged goose on the plain.

medicines used in pregnancy if a woman is experiencing stomach pains, e.g. Kuti mukaintu umitide kamyongwa-myongwa mwida, ulabelesya misamu *yanacitontozya* mbuli musamu utegwa mukkalaatontola. If a pregnant woman has stomach pains, she uses traditional medicines to alleviate the pain.
what is fully grown, e.g. Popwe lyakumunyinza *ngunacitumpule*. = The maize-cob at the boundary is the one which is fully grown.
a type of bird, the grey touracco, pl. banacoombe, e.g. *Banacoombe* balalila mucisaka. = The grey touraco's are singing in the forest.
an old cow elephant, a cow eland, e.g. *Nadamba* ulacela mumusena. = The cow eland is grazing in the plain.
a male bee, drone, e.g. Ndabona *nadunda* mumpako yamusamu. = I saw a drone in the hole in the tree. Also simandandala.
prostitute, e.g. Ooyu musimbi *ngunajempa*, talilemeki pe. = This girl is a prostitute, she has no respect for herself. Also kapenta, nacibula, nacinzulu.
Also najempa

the crested-crane, pl. banakaala, e.g. Muyuni ulimvwisya muzyaano *ngunakaala*. = The bird which is heard about frequently in stories is the crestedcrane. Njeeyi mikondo yabayuni bapati bategwa *banakaala* ampowani. = These are the tracks of big birds which are called the crested-crane and the ostrich.
type of tree (flowers eaten, and the tubers in famine times), e.g. *Lyanzala bantu balya nakabombwe*. = In times of famine people eat from the *nakabombwe* tree.
the oribi, a small antelope, pl. *banakacindwe*, e.g. *Babwa batanda banakacindwe mucibanda*. = The dogs are chasing oribis in the plain. Also *nacindwe*.

a woman who has been initiated and wears the *musyini* (crown of beads) and is not yet married, e.g. *Kamwale ulikkede kwabo kusikila ciindi nca-gusigwa masusu alya abumwale*. *Ino ciindi eci utegwa ngunakalindu, busimbi bwamana*. = An initiated girl lives at her parent's village until the time when her hair is cut. At this time she has become a *nakalindu*, her girlhood is over.
a married woman, pl. *banakalindu*, e.g. *Banakalindu bakazyana ciyeema kunkolola*. Married women danced the *ciyeema* at an initiation ceremony.
a type of relish Also *lubanga*.
a type of bird, the grey heron, e.g. *Nakakolyo ujisi cisunka cibotu*. = The grey heron has a beautiful tuft of hair on the head. Also *sikolyo* (goliath heron).
a vulture, e.g. *Inkuku yamucembele yatolwa nakaleya*. = The hen of the old woman has been taken by a vulture. Also *sikube*
a type of bird, the swift, pl. *banakamanku*, e.g. *Banakamanku balayaka ziteente mumajeleele*. = The swifts build their nests on cliffs.
a girl who seeks attention, e.g. *Kasimbi nkaanga nakampenene kanyina mulemyo*. = A girl who pushes herself forward has no self-respect.
one who spreads idle tales, e.g. *Utamuteeleli muntu oyo ngunakampyagula*. = Do not listen to that person he spreads rumours.
the secretary-bird, e.g. *Inyama yanakansakwe ilanona kapati*. = The meat of the secretary-bird is delicious.
a duiker, e.g. *Nakasya wazimana nyemu kucindongwe*. = A duiker has finished off the groundnuts in the groundnut plot.

prostitute, e.g. *Nkobali banakatweenku banji omuno mudolopo eeli*. = There are many prostitutes in this city. *Ooyu musimbi ulaa ciimo cibotu, kutali mbuli tootu tumwi ntuunga banajempa, banakatweenku tutayandi akubeleka mumaanda mwabo-mwabo*. = This girl has good behaviour, she is not like these little ones who are whores, prostitutes who do not even want to work at their homes. Also *kapenta*
a bracelet of grass, pl. *banakaumbulu*, e.g. *Bamacembele bakali kusama banakaumbulu mumaboko*. = The elderly women used to wear bracelets of grass on their arms. Also *nsambo*
adviser, e.g. *Baneene balaba nakazulu wanabwiinga wangu*. = My grandmother will be the adviser of my bride.
prostitute, e.g. *Utamukwati musimbi oyu, ngunakeempa*. = Do not marry this girl, she is a prostitute. Also *kapenta*.
a well-built person, e.g. *Ndaswaanganya nakeme wamusimbi*. = I met with a well-built girl.
Also *nakampenene*
a drum beaten on both sides, e.g. *Ingoma mpati yabudima ngunakubili*. = The big budima drum is beaten on both sides.
the favourite wife or child, e.g. *Choombe ukobelela nakufwunwa wakwe. = Choombe protects his favourite one.
a traveller, e.g. Mutinta kunyina nalima kumunzi ngunakweenda. = Mutinta never ploughs at home, she just travels about.
strong tobacco from short-leafed plant, e.g. Tombwe wanalubotu ulalula kapati. The nalubotu type of tobacco is very strong. Mumfwuko yakwe mwakali nalubotu. There was a strong tobacco in his pipe.
a spring hare, e.g. Babwa baalilwa kujata nalufwuma. The dogs are unabe to catch the spring hare.
an antbear, e.g. Sulwe wanjila mubwina bwanalu-fwumbafwumba. The hare has entered the den of an antbear.
a spring hare Also nalufwuma.
a milch cow, e.g. Ino-mbe yabataata njiinga nalujwaajwa, ijisi mukupa munji kapati. The milch cow of my father gives much milk. (Also kujwamuna = to milk)
an old cow elephant, also nadamba.
Also nalukuba
one who spreads idle tales, e.g. Utamumvwi oyo ngunalu-myamya. Do not listen to that one, she spreads idle tales. Also nakapyagula, nakampyagula, nam-pyagula
mantis, e.g. Nalu-nkonkomozya uyubilila ntwalya. = The preying-mantis stalks what it eats.
a chameleon, e.g. Naluntaambwe ncuuka cilisandula mubala. = A chameleon is a type of lizard which changes its colour. Also camutambwe
the weeding lunation, (kupala = to weed)

December, e.g. Bantu balimina mapopwe abo mumwezi wa Nalupale. = People weed their fields in the month of December. (During this lunation, marriages were forbidden according to traditional custom nor was it permitted to go on to a roof.)
the reedbuck/waterbuck, pl. banaluvwi, e.g. Mucibanda ca Kasako mujanika banaluvwi banji. On the plain of Kasako (part of the Kafue plain), many reedbuck are found.
