the place above the knee, e.g. Mwana ulaa cuute analuzwi. = The child has an abcess above the knee.
the index-finger, left hand e.g. Ndakalipwaya nsando ali namaandaalezya. I struck my index-finger with the hammer.
a girl's visual game played during initiation, e.g. Bakamwale basobana namacaaca. = The female initiates play the game called namacaaca. Also namacaca.

television, video, e.g. Munene waka-ambila mwanaakwe kuti azime nciinga namacaaca ncaakabikkide ku 'video' kabeebelezya baimba. The old man told his son to turn off the television where he had put on a video watching the singers.
spirit, shade, shadow, pl. banamacaca, e.g. Mooye uyebela banamacaca kubwaanda. The girl being initiated was admiring the reflections on the wall. Also namacaaca.
a cobra, e.g. Munzila inzoka njiinga namaconco, yakamwiimika. = On the way, a snake, a big cobra, stopped him.
a type of vegetable relish, giant-rape, e.g. Cisyu canamajindi cijisi matuvwu mapati. The vegetable giant rape has large leaves.
boiled tobacco, e.g. Bataata babamba namakati mucidumba. = Father is preparing boiled tobacco in a shelter.
a prostitute, e.g. Ngwaanzi namakwenkwe ngoyanda? = Why is it a prostitute that you love?
the favourite wife of a polygamist, e.g. Simaali ulayungwa *anamalele wakwe*. = A polygamist is drawn by his favourite wife. Also *namalelo*
the head wife of a polygamist, e.g. Namatama wakaleka mukaintu *wakwe namalelo*. = Namatama divorced his headwife.
Also *namalwa*

pus-filled blister on knee, anthrax (painful sores and fever, transmissable to humans), e.g. Mwana wakafwa wakali kuciswa *kanamalumbe*. = The child who died was suffering from anthrax. Also *kabyaabi*

a friction-drum, e.g. Adilwe alalema kuti kwalila *namalwa*. = When a friction-drum is played, the funeral takes on a high dignity. Nobwakasika buzuba, cicili cifwumofwumo kwakalila *namalwa* kuzuma *vwuku-vwuku-vwuku Vwukuwuku-vwuku!* = When the day arrived when it was still early morning the friction drum was played sounding, "Vwukuvwuku-vwuku! Vwuku-vwuku-vwuku!"
the secretary-bird, e.g. Ndayoowa basa, *namandweza wandiindila*. = I am afraid, my friends, a secretarybird has crossed before me. Also nakansakwe, jule
mutual piercing, e.g. Yabankondo yalwa yaba *yanamanenga*. = In this battle it is a matter of the fighters piercing one another.
a steam locomotive, a train, e.g. Citima *canamangoma* cizwa busi bunji. = Much smoke comes from the steam engine.
a prostitute
one who tries ornaments or dresses of various fashions, e.g. Kuba *namansandu-nsandu* nkutasitikila. = To dress in various fashions is to be discontented.

head of witchdoctors, e.g. Oomu muganda momwakali *namanyina*, iwini-wini munanga wabananga. = It is in this house where there was the head of witchdoctors, a real witchdoctor who surpassed other witchdoctors.
a wonder-worker, e.g. Chuungabuluba wakali *namasandu*. = Chuungabuluba was a wonder-worker.
a buck oribi, e.g. Ndajaya *namasengo mupati*. = I killed a big buck oribi.
a broad pot for cooling or keeping beer, e.g. Basimabbuku banywa bukoko muli *namatimba*. = The headmen are drinking beer from a wide-brimmed pot. Also *cibuya, citalo, bbiya*.
a graveyard, e.g. Kwali kumweka mililo masiku *kunamaumbwe*. = Fires were shining at night at the graveyard.
numbers, mathamatics, e.g. Basicikolo bamazubaano tabazijani *nambala*. = Pupils nowadays do not know maths.
the dregs, e.g. Bukoko bwamana, kwacaala *nambi* zyalo. = The beer is finished, only the dregs remain. Also *busiwa*.
a bull-frog, e.g. Mucizyiba omu mulila *namongwe*. = A bull-frog is croaking here in the pond. Also *igande*.
a type of musicaldrum, e.g. Bantu bazyana ngoma yana*moondonga* acisobano. = The people were dancing to the *namoondonga* drum at the festival.

monster, e.g. Boonse mpobakakkede bakazyuuluka kulanga mbuli kuti kwabbuka *namoonsomoonso*. = All where they were sitting turned around to look as if there had appeared a monster. Also haamonzo-monzo
a small variety of groundnut, e.g. Imbuto *anamooya* ilafwamba kubizwa. = Namooya groundnut seed ripens early.
a type of bird, the crested crane, pl. banamowani, e.g. Banamowani balalila kumwaka. = Crested cranes cry towards the end of the dry season.
one who gathers, e.g. Basimbi bamwi mbaanamucelela kule mumizeezo. Some girls are ones who gather ideas from far away in their thoughts.

a train, also citima namudelele a spiders white web, also namundelele namulakata a person who talks without stopping, e.g. Ooyo ngunamulakata, taleki kwaambaula. That one is a chatterbox, she never stops talking.

the month before delivery of a baby, e.g. Mukaintu uli mumwezi wa Namulela (walusele) ulabelesya antela kunywa musamu wamasoto kutegwa mwana ulimwida atanyani. = A woman in her month of Namulela (eight) uses or drinks the medicine which protects the child from the disease of masoto (which can afflict the child) so that the child which is in her womb does not become thin.
the shortest rib, e.g. kabatuzi, imbambo
an abnormal sixth digit.
one who deviates from the path. e.g. Twakeenda anamuleleya, nkokuti mmubwa. We are going along with one who deviates from the path, that is a dog. Also namuleyaleya

the Creator, e.g. Toonse tuleelede kusyoma muli Namulenga, nguutupa zyoonse. We should all put our trust in the Creator, who is the one who gives us everything. namuleta the shortest rib, e.g. Kabambo kanamuleta kakatyoka nibakamuuma musako Mutinta. The shortest rib was broken when they beat Mutinta Also namulela with a stick.
one who deviates, as a dog running this way and that way, e.g. Utabi namuleyaleya, ulamuka. = Do not deviate, you will be late.
an abnormal sixth finger, e.g. Baama tiibakakkomana nibakatumbuka namuleza. = Mother was not happy when she gave birth to a child with a sixth finger. Also namuleta, namulela
a pidgeon born alone, e.g. Ndaula mwanaa nkwilimba namulomba omwe. I have bought a young pidgeon who was born alone. Ndime namulomba. = I am the only child of my parents.

over-planted plot or field, e.g. Bakali kunga naa batalikila antoomwe kusyanga, amena mapopwe akali kunga waile kuba namulunge-lunge. = It used to happen that if they started to plant together, when the maize germinated it just became overplanted.
a pumpkin with abundant juice, e.g. Ndayanda kulya myungu yanamundalanga, ilakkutwa kufwambaana. = I want to eat one of those juicy pumpkins, it quickly satisfies one's appetite.

the cobweb of a wall spider (which is put over the wooden hole of the frame of a kankobela (hand-piano) above the resonator, e.g. Kobikka namundelele akankobela kako. = Put a cobweb on your hand-piano. Koonse kuyabila wakali kwiide kulendema ulati ngunamundelele. All his solo singing was just vibrating with a deep hoarse sound as if like the spider's cobweb on a handpiano.
a very big herd of cattle, e.g. Mulimi munkutwe ulijisi namundindi. = An energetic farmer has a fine herd of cattle. Also nabuyuni.
an antbear, e.g. Inzuki zijisi buci mubwina bwanamunengwe. = Bees have honey in the hole of an antbear. Also namunkwize.

a type of relish, e.g. Sunu baama bandisiila namunkulungwe munji mucibiya uwakulisya kufwumbwa nkwenja kuya juunza. = Today mother has left me plenty of relish in the pot for eating with nsima wherever I go to tomorrow.
smart to attract others of opposite sex, e.g. Musimbi namunje-bwa ulalisumpula. = This girl who makes herself attactive for men is proud.
a plant with edible leaves, e.g. Ndali kulya matu anamu-nkulungu. = I was eating the leaves of the namunkulungu plant. Also bunkululu.

an ant-bear, e.g. Oobu bwina bwali kubee mbwina bwanamu-nkwize. = This hole seemed to be the hole of an antbear. Namunkwize tajisi boya bunji a mubili. = The ant-bear does not have much hair on it's body. Also galaba, nalufwumbafwumba, kwibba, cinengwe, namunengwe

a lily tree, e.g. Buyuni busyuunta maluba a namun-tengwa. = A flock of birds sucks the flowers of the lily tree. Also muzungula + one chosen to look after the family when a man dies, e.g. Muntu wasalwa kulya zina ngooyu usalwa kuti alele mu-kwasyi wamufwu. Nibazumina boonse kumuzeezo oyu, balamwaambila kuti ndu-we 'namuntengwa'. = The person chosen to inherit the name is the one chosen to look after the family of the deceased. When all agree to the idea, they tell that person that now you are the chosen caretaker of the family.
a water-melon, pl. banamunua, e.g. Banamunua basubila balanona. = Red water-melons are sweet. Also namunyo, namunyu
a medicinal root for cattle or chicken (also namununge), e.g. Amulete namununga tunywisye nkuku. = Bring the namununga root so that we treat the chickens.
water-melon Also namunywa
water-melon, e.g. Namunyo tabizwi kuvwundikwa. = The water-melon does not ripen if plucked too early.
a water-melon, e.g. Banamunyu bamana nyota. = Water-melons take away the thirst. Also namunyo, namunywa.
a water-melon, pl. banamunywa, e.g. Ndakasyangide ba-namunywa batakazyala pe. = The water-melons which I planted did not produce. Also itanga, inkondole, itopi, munkondo-bwi, ikowa
leaves smoked as a charm, (makes people smile at you) e.g. Basimbi bafwebelela basankwa babo, bafweba namusekelwa. = Girls who smoke for their boy's love, smoke the namuse-kelwa leaves.
a type of climbing-plant, e.g. Cisyu canamusinde ncibotu. = The relish of the namusinde plant is good.
a duiker, e.g. Babwa banji balasiigwa lubilo kuli namusya. = Many dogs are left behind in a chase after a duiker.
a driver, e.g. Namutekenya wabbaasi eli wakolwa, tayendi kabotu. = The driver of this bus is drunk and does not drive properly.
a bicycle, e.g. Inketani yanamutendele wangu yakosoka. = The chain of my bicycle is broken. Also incinga
the thin membrane of a spider which covers its eggs, e.g. Mayi asiluubilili avwumbidwe anamutendelele. = Spider's eggs are covered by a thin membrane. Also namundelele
the Victoria Falls, e.g. Ukasike kumweenima ubeleka ku Namutitima. = You should go and see my cousin working at the Victoria Falls. Also Musiotunya
maize planted late, e.g. Kono tatukwe kusyanga _namutompo_ ya-unka mvwula. = This year we will not plant the late maize because the rain has stopped.
a careless person, e.g. Muntu wakayaka nanda eyi _ngunamu-vwunze_. = The person who built this house is careless.
a zebra, e.g. _Banamu-wawa_ mbabotu kweebela. = Zebras are beautiful to admire. Also cibize.
a delicate person, e.g. Kokanana kabotu kumuntu oyo, _nguna-muyabwa_. = Talk gently to that person, she is delicate.
a type of fraible or easily crumbled stone, e.g. Mabwe aya mmateteete kupwaya ngaangaba _namu-yungizya_. = These rocks break easily, they are the namuyungizya type.
one who exaggerates, e.g. _Namu-yungizya_ ulayanda kuyungizya twaambo twakubeja. = One who exaggerates likes to add on lies.
a scooper, e.g. Munene ubelesya _namuyuwa_ kwiibulula mafwuta. = The old man uses a scooper to skim off the cream.
an insurpassable obstacle which makes people go around it, e.g. Inombe zyangu ndakaakuzijana kuli _namuzingulukwa_. = I found my cattle after going around the obstacle.
one who travels around, e.g. Haakweenda tajaniki ananda yakwe, _ngunamuzingalibbila_. = Haakwee-nda is not to be found at his home, he is ever travelling around.

one who is always moving about, e.g. Ncibi kuba _namu-zungalibbila_ inga munzi wako tausumbuli. = It is bad to always be on the move, as a result your village is not well kept. Also _namuzingalibbila_
malarial fever, e.g. _Keempe_ ulaciswa, wabaa _namuzyabwa_. = Keempe is sick, he has malaria. Also ntuntumaanzi.
a water-pot, e.g. Ku-nyina meenda muli _namwayemba_. = There is no water in the water-pot.
a water-melon, e.g. Koziyo-bola nseke zya_namwino_ tukasyange. = Store the seeds of the water-melon so that we plant later on.
an ordinary woman, e.g. Nibakali kuya kukuweza balombwana bakajana _banangubo_ bateka meenda. = When the men were going to hunt they found a group of women drawing water.
a kind of orchid growing on forest trees, e.g. _Nangulukila_ usilisya malwazi manji. = The orchid cures many diseases.
the lechwe-cob, e.g. Inyama _yananja_ balaiyanda banji. = Many like meat from the lechwe-cob. Also _nyanja_.
a bird, the spur-winged goose, e.g. Haakankone wakanjila ntolo-ngo akaambo kakujaya _nanjikwa_. = Haa-kankone went to prison because he killed a spur-winged goose. Also naciseke
a girl who is being initiated, an initiated girl, pl. _banankolola_, e.g. _Ba-nankolola_ balayandisya kuunka mumapo-bwe. = Initiated girls love going to parties.
a type of edible mushroom, e.g. _Banankupwi_ balafwambaana kubola. = The _nankupwi_ mushrooms quickly rot.
a roaming girl, e.g. Mutinta wakaciswa sikalileke nkaambo wakali na-_nzalu_. = Mutinta contracted AIDS because she was roaming about. Also kapenta.
an oribi, e.g. _Nanzele_ nka-nyama kalunduka kapati. = The oribi is an animal which runs very fast. Also nacindwe
a rough person, e.g. *Ncibi kuba napumpunya inga tobambi zintu zibotu.* = It is bad to be a rough person you will not care for things well.
a deceiver, e.g. *Napyagula mmuntu ubeja.* = A deceiver is a person who lies. Also nakapyagula.
a cow-eland, e.g. *Natamba ulacela mumuunda.* = The cow-eland is grazing in the field.
Also kapenta, nanzalu.
a type of medicinal tree, e.g. Inombe zyako kozinywisya *nazilyango*
bana banji. = Make your cattle drink medicine from the *nazilyango* tree so that they will give birth to many calves. (for words beginning with n, check words *under the letter i followed by n*)

special, e.g. Bulukwe bwakwe *bwancawu* bwaligwa mbeba aboobo sunu bwakabaa zipulo. = His fine clothes worn on special occasions were eaten by rats and so were just holes. *ncebu-ncebu* (*kucebauka* = to look about) e.g. Imwini *mooncebu-cebu*, mulutwe lunji. = Wherever you look in the big city, there are just the heads of the people.
type of bird, the smaller locust bird, e.g. *Ncelelebula uumauma mababa ciindi nalila.* = The smaller locust bird flaps the wings as it sings.
panic, e.g. Bantu boonse bakaile kubaa *ncence*. = All the people were filled with panic.
insanity, e.g. Naakaba masiku, Malusi *ncinko* yakatanta. = When night came, the madness of Malusi arose.
kind of medicinal shrub, also used for producing fire by friction, e.g. *Incinzya* isilisya malwazi manji. = The *ncinzya* tree cures many diseases. Also camuzaki.
type of bird, the babbler, e.g. *Incizenciye, zimwi zilasiya, zimwi zilatuba.* = Some babblers are black, some are white.

so-and-so, e.g. Muntu upegwa zina uwambililwa kuti, "*Ndaba* twakubikka ali *ndaba*." = A person who is given a name is told, "So-and-so (Kaumba - name of ancestor) we have given you to soand-so (Matimba - name of the named baby).
pl. of lulabo (lightning), e.g. Mvwula mpati yakawa antoomwe aguwo pati loko *andabo* zizungaanya nyika. = A great rain fell accompanied by a great gale with lightnings which shook the earth.

a type of drum, e.g. Wakauma *ndandala* yakwe alwija Iwamugutu wambelele. = He beat his *ndandala* drum with the horn of a ram. (used at a funeral, when Ba-Ila take their cattle to the plain; used at initiation the *ndandala* is played at any festival when it comes to its climax)
metal, e.g. Lubulo *Iwandalila lusyomezya zingomo.* = Bronze is used to mend iron water-pots. Also *mundalila*.
one who lacks money to pay tax, e.g. Kaindi *ndeenya* zizyakalikujatwa cibbalo. = Long ago those lacking money to pay tax were the ones who were caught for forced-labour. Also *indenya*
a cloth apron, e.g. Mujiki wakasamide *ndeke* naakali kujika. = The cook wore an apron when she was cooking.
an aeroplane, e.g. Ndabona *ndeke* mujulu. = I have seen an aeroplane in the sky.
type of tree, e.g. Kanene ukanda cilonda amatu *andelele*. = Kanene is pressing the wound with the leaves of the *ndelele* tree. Also kafwundula, mukanda-njase.
a bucket, e.g. Mazubaano kuvwula kapati kubelesegwa *ndelema* kutekela meenda. = Nowadays a bucket is mostly used for drawing water.

the space on back between the shoulders, e.g. *Andelo* alacisa mbuli kuti ndalikuumwa. = The back between my shoulders pains as if I have been beaten. Inga mbubakapompela, nkaanga sulwe kakamumata suntwe kasako *kandelo*. = As soon as they appeared, the hare struck the hyena on the back with a stick.
a man, my father (Valley usage), e.g. *Ndende* wandituma kusunza tombwe. = My father sent me to ask for tobacco.
a quiver, (portable holder for arrows,) e.g. Bavwimi bayumwide *ndeye* zyamasumo. = The hunters carry a quiver for spears. Also *indeye*.

a bundle of spears, e.g. Munanda ya muvwimi kuli *ndeye* zyamasumo zinji. = In the hunter's house there are many bundles of spears. Bakazyuuma *ndeye* zyamyuumba akubbabbuka antobo. = They beat the bundle of spears against the shields and swung the shields about.
dish, e.g. Akulya, kalida mundido zyokwani? = And as for eating, from whose dishes will he eat?
machine for drawing water, e.g. Atwalo tooye ntotuzezya tutuleke kutubelesya kayi *ndilayi* nkozili. = Also the ropes which we use for drawing water we should leave aside and use the winch.
an obese person, e.g. Nseyandi kulya kapati, inga ndaba *ndingambumbunga*. = I don't want to eat much. I may become obese.
type of edible mushroom, e.g. Sunu twalikulisya *ndiyo*. = Today we were eating *ndiyo*, a type of edible mushroom.
mud, e.g. Citaka cakolwa *ndobe*. = The little fish is choked wth mud.
calabash pipe used for smoking tobacco, e.g. Baku Zambezi bafwepela *mundobondo*. = The Zambezi people smoke the *ndobondo* pipe.

big and strong, e.g. Wakamanizya kuvwozya *ndulumina* zyabalombwana. = He finished paying the big strong men. Naakamana kulya wakanjila muopesi akuya kuvwununa *ndulumina* wabbuku mpoona wakatalika kubala. = When he had finished eating he went into the office and opened a big book and started to read.
a dam wall, e.g. Cakatola ciindi cilamfwu kuyaka *ndunduma*. = It took a long time to build the dam wall.
a type of bird, the wagtail, e.g. Ndajaya *nduntila* abbwe lyamaanza. = I have killed a wagtail by throwing a stone. Also *innduuntila*.
a type of bird, the large quail, pl. banduu, e.g. Basankwa baunka kukuvwima *banduu*. = The boys have gone hunting large quails.
smartness, e.g. Nindwaandwa. = He is a smart boy.
sorgum turned black, e.g. Balimi batebula *ndyomba* mumyuunda. = The farmers harvested the blackened sorgum in the fields.
a leopard, e.g. *Nemba* mmuvwimi amasiku, sikati uloona mumisamu. = The leopard is a night hunter, during the day he sleeps in the trees. Also siluwe
a blade of grass with three edges, pl. *banembaula*, e.g. *Banembaula* balanenga mumaulu. = Grass with three edges cut the feet.
a peg, as for stretching skin, e.g. Amulete *nembe* zyosanwe tugagaile cikutu ciyanikwa. = Bring five pegs so that we nail down the hide to be dried. Also *nkanka*
a green relish (*Achyranthes aspera*), e.g. Basimbi bacela *nembe zyacisyu*. = The girls are gathering a green vegetable for relish.
unusually long finger-nails, e.g. Muntu *ulaa nembe zyamala ulya tombe muli cakulya*. = A person with long finger-nails eats dirt when eating.
a spider cocoon, e.g. Mayi aba-*sicuubi alisisidwe munenda*. = The eggs of spiders are hidden in a cocoon.
the antbear, e.g. Cuku wakanjila *musempo lyanengo masiku*. = Cuku entered the den of an antbear at night.
stomach of bird, e.g. Mwanalumi *upegwa nfwuli kuti alisamune*. = The husband is given the stomach of a bird to alleviate the appetite for meat.

crest, cockscomb, cock's crest, e.g. Muzingini *ulizyibidwe ndiza nkaambo kangala yakwe ilaa mutwe*. = The cock is known perhaps because of the coxcomb on his head. Naakacebuka wakabona ndi-*nga syuumbwa lyuululusya ngala muci-vwuna*. = When he turned around he saw a huge lion with raised mane in a bush. Mubwa wabusya *ngala naabona mwee-nzu*. = The hare on the dogs neck stood out when it saw a visitor.
a band of skin used as head-dress, e.g. Basikuzyana bakasamide *ngala mumutwe*. = The dancers were wearing a band of skin on their heads. Also *ingundu*.
type of tree (*Croton gratissimus*), e.g. Ndajaya nziba *mungae omuya*. = I killed a dove in the *ngae* tree over there.
stories, e.g. Ibbuku eli lilaa *nga-no zijisi zyamasendelela asendelezya bu-kkale abweende bwabantu*. = This book has stories which speak indirectly of the life and mobility of the people.
a stilt house, e.g. Koona *mungaze ncibotu inga tolumwi banyama*. = It is good to sleep in a stilt house because it is unlikely that you will be attacked by animals.

a raised platform, e.g. Mu-*myuuunda bakali kunga nkuyaka ngazi. Ngazi iyakwa mbuli caanda cankwilimba, nkabela yalo kiili mpati akulampa. Kutanta inga kuli malele biya akutantila. Alimwi iyakilwa akati kamuunda kutegwa ijwi nosoola kalisika koonse-koonse*. = They used to build a raised platform in the fields. The raised platform was built like a pidgeon-house but bigger and longer. To ascend they used a ladder to get up. Again it was built in the middle of the field so that when the voice cried out it would reach everywhere.
ululation, e.g. Bamakaintu ba-kali kuuma *ngoloolo naakabbuka nabwii-nga*. = The women ululated when the bride approached.

a bucket-like container running on electrical wires which brings copper out of an underground mine, e.g. Bantu bobilo yabaalila kukkuba *ngolo-vwani*. = Two people have failed to run the bucket of copper ore.

a drum, e.g. Wakazinanika *mwido akuziyanika ngoma zyakwe zite-gwa, muliliko, ntakuntanda, muntundu, nkwii, camujanja, mpininga a kumbwi mpati*. = He smeared his drums with oil and dried them, which are known as, *muliliko, ntakuntanda, muntundu, nkwii, camujanja, mpininga*, and the big *kumbwi*. Also *ingoma*
life-style, e.g. Wakawida *mungoma yabugwebenga*. = He fell into the life-style of gangsterism.
a valved-trap, e.g. Nobana, kamuteya *ngoma-mulonga tuja-ye nswi*. = Children, prepare the valved traps so that we trap fish.

type of tree, from which twirlers are made, e.g. Kogonka kasamu *kangombe tubambe mpusyo*. = Cut a stick from the *ngombe* tree so that we make a twirler (for breaking up lumps in cooking nsima.) Also mubundikwa, mupusho.
an impotent man, e.g. Muntu utazyali ningomwa. A man who does not produce is impotent. cf. sicibbololo ngozi pl of loozi. Also ingozi
a blanket, e.g. Ngubo zili mu-nkwa. The blankets are under the arm.

name given by the father, e.g. Kwamana zina lyaakalo ndeliboola mazina anguli. Muntu oonse ulijisi mazina anguli obilo, lyamausyi alyamukowa. Lyoonse muntu usaanguna kupa zina lyanguli nguusyi, amana kuulika usyi nkokuya basimukowa abalo baulike. Mwana na-pegwa zina lyanguli, ulaangwa ampola isubila yabulungu kukuboko kwalulyo. = After the name has been given by the midwife that is when the names of nguli are given. Every person has two nguli names, one of the fathers side and of the mother's side. It is always the father who gives the first nguli name, when he is finished then the mother's clan gives an nguli name. When a child is given the name from the father, it is tied with a wrist-band of red beads on the right arm.
a pig, e.g. Ba Nsabata tabalyi ngulube. The Seventh Day Adventists do not eat pork.

unexpected event, e.g. Sunu ndalaa ngunzuunzu nkaambo nda-jaya mpongo nindayuuma kabwe kasyoo-nto biyo. = Today something unexpected happened to me as I unintentionally killed a goat when I struck it with just a small stone.
commotion, e.g. Bulozi lyoonse bulaa angwelele. = Witchcraft always causes a disturbance.
an undefeated champion, e.g. Lottie Mwale yakali ngwenya yamucisi ca Zambia. = Lottie Mwale was the undefeated champion of Zambia.

who it is, e.g. Kaindi twakali kwiiya mazina abanyama besu alimwi akubabona buya ameso kuti ulya nguniini. = Long ago we learnt the names of our animals and just looking at them with the eyes we could say who they were.
excrement Also maziu

lover, beloved, njabwe a type of bird, e.g. Bantu bakali kugambwa nobali kubona meso akwe nkwaasalala pyu mbubuli aankulukuze, inkwizyi-nkwizyi antela njabwe. = The people were surprised when they saw his eyes how they were very red like that of starlings or njabwe njalalando pleasure, e.g. Bana bakubusi bamazubaano balayandaula njalalando lyoonse. = Young people of these days are always searching for pleasure.
a stone used to raise the level of a firestone, e.g. Kocitabya njela cibiya cacengama. = Lift up the pot with a supporting stone which is leaning over.

fruit of the tamarind tree, e.g. Bakasusula akulalila njele zyabusiikka, mbubu, mabuyu, amicelo imwi. = At supper time they ate fruit of the tamarind tree, fruit of the mabubu bush, baobab and other fruits.
a shell-fish, mussel, e.g. Bamacembele babwezelela njili mumulonga. = The old women are collecting shell-fish in the river.
a vegetable relish (Corrigiola littoralis), e.g. Cisyu canjina nciteteete kapati. Njina relish is very tender.
a louse, e.g. Kuti tosambi inga wabaa njina. If you do not wash you will have lice.
card games, e.g. Wakali kulibanda ciindi nibakali kusobana njuka. = He was praising himself with names when they were playing cards.
a plumed head-dress (a bucks tail on a wire frame), e.g. Muvwimi usamide _njuku amutwe._ = The hunter is wearing a plumed head-dress. Also nsuku
grandmother, e.g. _Ba nkaaka ndakabatebbela nkuni jilo._ = I collected firewood for my grandmother yesterday.
a crab, e.g. _Mucitangazyiba eciya kuli nkala zipati-pati._ = In that pond there are fairly large crabs.

an elderly person, e.g. _Ala-kwe mwini wakali kulikankaizya kuti ngunkalakata._ = He himself was walking slowly as if he was an old person. _Nkalakata zyabalombwana amacembele zyaka-kkala kubamba makani akusala sikubamba munzi._ = The elderly men and women sat to chose a successor to rule the village.
a type of tree, e.g. _Nkalanga mmuyumu kugonka akeembe._ = The nkalanga tree is hard to cut with an axe.
desert e.g. _Cakamwaalila kukkala abeenzinyina munkanda._ = He was unable to stay with his friends in the desert.
type of beer, e.g. _Bukoko bwankandamaulu bwazoobizwa nzo-omutamba muzolani wangu azoonywe._ = When the beer of nkandamaulu is ready, I will invite my friend so that he drinks.
the smaller grinding stone, e.g. _Bacembele babanga nkando yaziyo._ = The old lady is sharpening the smaller grinding stone.
a group, e.g. _Nkanka zyabalombwana eezi zyakakanana twaambo tunji tugwasya._ = A group of able men spoke on many topics which were helpful.
the hips Also _inkanya_
a headpad of grass, e.g. _Kobikka nkata uyumune kabotu nongo._ = Put on the headpad so that you carry the earthen pot properly.
a cloth with designs of palm leaves, e.g. _Ndakaula mulembo wankata._ = I bought a cloth with palm-leaf designs.
divining bones, e.g. _Barnanga banji babelesya nkata nobasonda._ = Many witch-doctors use divining-bones when they divine. Also _nkakata._
bangle, e.g. _Bantu bakali kuunka kumalende a zituzyo mbuli bulungu, nkaya, Iwiili abusu._ = People used to go to the rain-shrine with beads, bangles, shells and maize flour.
a type of bird, the cattle egret, e.g. _Inkobo zilagwasya nkaambo zilya nzengene ziluma nombe._ = The cattle egrets are helpful because they eat the ticks which bite the cattle.
a red variety of sorgum, e.g. _Sena nkokwe zyatebulwa kale?_ = Has the red sorgum already been harvested?
a club or knobkerrie made of wood, e.g. _Utamuumi nkoli mweenzinyoko._ = Do not strike your friend with a club.
a cultivator, e.g. _Insimbi yankolobeki yatyoka ncibaleka kukofwola bana._ = The children have stopped cultivating because the nuts and bolts of the cultivator got broken.
a drunkard, e.g. _Jooji wakaleka cikolo nkaambo wakaba nkolwabusu._ = Jooji left school because he became a drunkard. Also _mukolwi._
a tortoise, e.g. _Inkoma ijisi cikwa ciyumu._ = The tortoise has a hard shell. _Kamubikka mali mucikwa cankoma._ = Put the money in the shell of the tortoise. Also nondo, fwulwe, ibbandwa, cibinda.

an ancient custom where an offender was left tied in the sun from morning to evening, e.g. _Mwami Nkomaangu wakali kubaanga bantu cifwumo, kumazuba bakaangununwa. Mwaange wakalibbizya zuba kasyoloma. Ncenciceeco cisubulo eci ncecitegwa nkomaabbila._ = Chief Nkomaangu used to tie up people from morning until evening when they were then released. The captive was suffering until the setting of the sun. That is why this punishment is called, `nkomaabbila.'
pocket, e.g. Ujisi mali ongaye munkomo yako? = How much money have your in your pocket?
type of tree, e.g. Mamvwa ankonde mmalamfwu a makwa alatubatuba. = The thorns of the nkonde tree are long and the bark is white. Also mutubetube, mutubatuba.
a male baboon, e.g. *Nkontwe* wanyanga mwana cinkwa. = The male baboon snatched the bread from the child.
longing for meat, e.g. Wakalya nkuku itamani *nkosya* amanunkinunki. = She ate the chicken which does not fulfill the desire for meat.
a bullet, e.g. *Inkulu* zyamana banyama kabacilibonya. = Bullets got finished off when the animals were still to be seen.
type of bird, the scarlet touracco, e.g. Mweene wajayila baneene *nkulyukuku*. = Mweene killed a scarlet touracco for my grandfather. Also inkulyunkulyu.
a snail, e.g. *Inkumba* zisiya njili mumbali amulonga. = The snails leave shells beside the river.
Also nkumba.

a hole in the ground made by termites, a cave, e.g. Inswi zinjila mu*nkumbwi* yamulonga. = Fish enter an underground cave in the river. Ciwena wakatijaana kuya kukwempa mwana akutijila munkumbwi yakwe. = The crocodile moved quickly to snatch the child and dashed to its lair.
important people, e.g. Munanda omu mukkede *nkume-nkume*. = It is in this house that important people dwell.

group of elders, e.g. *Nkunkunyenze* zyabalombwana abamakaintu zyakayeeya kuti lubono lucaale bana babelesye nkaambo mbapati kale. = Groups of elders thought that the wealth of the dead remaining should be left to the children because they had already grown up.
unborn baby, e.g. *Nkunkunyenzye* yalila ndufwu Iwamuntu, e.g. The cry of an un- born baby foretells death. (a proverb, a bad omen)
a bush pig, wild boar, pl. bankuntula, e.g. *Bankutula* bazimana zitende mumuunda. = The wild pigs have finished off the pumpkins in the field.

lice on fowl, e.g. Ncibotu kukkala akulibelekela mucisi cokwanu kwiinda kunikufwa anga *ninkuswi* zyabula cilawo. = It is better to live and work in your own country rather than dying like lice on fowl without a dwelling.

a roan-antelope, e.g. *Nkwalata ulasiya amubili, ulatuba muntebe zyamaulu amwida, masaya alatuba, cilezu cilatuba, matwi taakokonyene aliimvwi alaaboya butuba mukati, kubusyu ulaa myeengwe iituba. = The roan-antelope has a black body, it is white between the legs and stomach, the cheeks are white, the beard is white, the ears are not bent back, and it has white stripes on the face. Also cilumbulumbu, lumpelembe.

clapping, e.g. Kwakalila *nkwasi* zyakulumba kumutondezya kuti mweenzu wakatambwidwe amaanza obile abantu. = There was a clapping in thanks to show the visitor that he was received with two hands by the people.

mealie-meal added when cooking nsima, e.g. Mukaintu amana kukopela nsima ubikka *nkwasizyo*. = When the woman has finished the initial stirring of the nsima she puts in the additional mealie-meal (to thicken it.)
a yellow bird, also used to describe the colour yellow e.g. zisani zyankweegwe = yellow clothes.
sex, e.g. Cilatondwa muntu kucita nkwela ciindi cadilwe nkaambo mizimo taikkomani. It is taboo to have sex during a funeral because the spirits will not be pleased.
entrance, e.g. Mucembele wakanjila munanda akwiinda ankwidizyo. = The old lady entered the house and passed through the entrance. Also mulyango

a wooden hoe, e.g. Tiindamana kusya zilindi nkaambo lyatyoka nkwisyo. I did not finish digging holes because the wooden hoe broke. Also jamba lyacisamu. nole a wild cat, pl. banole, e.g. Bamwi bantu balabalya banole. Some people eat wild cats. Also noole.
a gourd, calabash, e.g. Nongo yabulungu civwunisyo nimpande. The cover for a calabash of beads is an mpande shell.
nipple of a woman's breast, e.g. Mukaintu namita inkolo zilafwuta akusiya kunonso. = When a woman conceives her breasts swell and the nipples become dark.
a wild cat, e.g. Noole wajata bana bankwilimba bobilo. = The wild cat has caught two young pidgeons.
a cover for a dish, e.g. Kamubikka nsabia ali cakulya. Put a cover over the food. Also civwunisyo, tampa, dekeselo
the calf of the leg, e.g. Nsafwu zya Mutinta zilapusama. The calves of Mutinta's legs have become shrunken.
the smithy, e.g. Mufwuzi ufwulila munsaka zibulo zyakwe. = The black-smith forges his irons at the smithy.
a hand-rattle, e.g. Mukaintu oyu ulicizyi kuuma nsaka. This woman knows how to beat the hand-rattle. Also nsakalala, muyuwa, musakalalu, musangu-sangu
burning torch, e.g. Moyo wangu wakali kuyaka mbuli cisisi cansama. = My heart was burning like a burning torch.

power, e.g. Basibbola bajisi nsana zinji zyakutijaana. The footballers have a lot of strength for running. Sibbuku wakabapa nsana akubayumyayumya balombwana aba. The head man gave them energy and strengthened those men. Also nguzu
a rat, e.g. Nsana ijisi mafwuta manji. = A rat has plenty of fat.

a type of grass which produces seeds which are eaten by birds, but in time of famine is used for human consumption, e.g. Bantu banji balalya nseke zyansangaaze ciindi canzala. = Many people eat the seeds of nsangaaze grass during a time of famine.
seed, e.g. Kamuleta nsangu zya-tantaacuulu tusyange. Bring rape seeds so that we plant.

a dish, e.g. Nsangwa mmutiba wakali kulukwa, wakali wakupulila nsima. The nsangwa was a dish which was woven, it was used for dishing out nsima. Naakali kuciswa muntu kaindi twakali kubweza nsangwa yamaila twakali kuunka kumuŋanga kuya kumusonda. = In the past when a person was ill we used to take a little dish of millet when we were going to the witchdoctor for divination.

a coloured person, e.g. Masowe wakakwatwa kuli nsami. Masowe was married to a coloured man. cf. nsaame nsamino clothing, e.g. Nsamino zyabo zyoonse zitondezya bucete bwabo. = All their clothig shows their poverty.

a spark, e.g. Majwi aa mulaka wamubi ali mbuli nsasi zyamusyokwe mbozyuuntumuka akulunduka julu lyoonse mbozitapauka akumwaikizyanya mubwizu koonse. = An evil tongue is like the sparks of the bush in the way they explode and run up into the sky and spread through the grass.
a gourd for storing oil, e.g. Mafwuta amunsazi alasumbuzya. = The oil in the gourd makes one clean.

crowds, committees, associations, cooperatives, e.g. *Nseba zyabantu* nkoziti zyapengana. Many crowds of people are suffering. Bubi bweelede kuIwanwa bantu boonse kwiinda mukusumpula Iwiiyo, bulimi, *nseba zyabantu*, akuzyibana buntususu. = Evil should be fought by all people through developing education, agriculture, cooperatives and human relationships.
edible termites, e.g. *Inseele* ninswa zizwa lyawa mvwula ntaanzi. = *Inseele* are the 'flying ants' that come out when the first rains fall.
a smart person, e.g. Kakacili kasankwa yakali *nseete*. When he was still young he was smart.
weeds, e.g. Kamuboola tukagusye *nsegwa-nsegwa* mumuunda. Come let us take out the weeds from the field. Also malizwida.
a type of grass, e.g. Cibawe wakazwa mumeenda akutalika kuyotela zuba abwizu *bwansekwansekwa*. The otter came out of the water and began to warm itself in the sun on soft grass.

medicine used to ease delivery at birth, e.g. Ciindi cakutumbuka casika kuti mukaintu wapenzya, ulapegwa musamu *wanselezya*. = When the time of giving birth arrives, if the woman is finding difficulty in delivering she is given the medicine of *nselezya*.

a small animal-horn used as an item of the collection of witches accoutrements (animal horns, bones, beeswax, cloth, beads, hair), e.g. Mulozi ulya ubelesya *nsengo* kulowa bantu. = That witch uses charms to bewitch people. Also *insengo*.

a wild species of cat, e.g. Katuteya cidoongwe mubwina munjila *nsezi*. = Let us set a reed-trap in the burrow of the wild cats. Myootokala ifwuuma mumigwagwa ikoya *nsezi* zyamvwa bunumfwu bwamubwa. Cars speeding along the roads are like wild cats when they have picked up the scent of a dog.
remains of villages, e.g. *Ninsilamatongo* yakacaala liya lyakainda Bamangwalu-ngwalu mucisi ca Butonga. The ruins of the village remained when the Lozi passed through the country of the Batonga.
a very old person, e.g. Ooyu mudaala *ninsilamatongo*. This old man is so old as he has lived in many ruins.

a musk-cat or genet, e.g. *Nsimba* ilalya tunyamanyina tuniini, inzoka, bacula, bayuni amayi, tuuka amicelo yamusyaka mbuli nkuyu. The genet eats other small animals, snakes, frogs, birds and eggs, insects and fruits of the bush like figs. Also *insimba*
cicatrix, cut made, e.g. Wakabayasa *nsimbo* zyakubasita. = He cut them with marks to insert charms to protect them.

grass seeds which adhere to clothing, e.g. Atukaumpe bwizu bwansi*nya* mumusena. = Let us burn the *nsinya* grass in the vlei. Also *insinya, insoke, insina*. nsiya-ncembele traditional customs, e.g. Zilengwa *zyansiya-ncembele* mudaala wakalizizyi kapati. The old man knew the inherited customs of the past extremely well.
grass-seeds which adhere to clothing, e.g. Wakajwa nsoke akulikunkumuna mamvwu. = He removed the sticking grass-seeds and shook off the clay. Also nsinya, insoke.
a honey-bird, e.g. Nsolo yakamulilila akumutondezya mpako yanzuki. = The honey-bird sang for him and showed him the bee-hive.

a Bantu game played with stones, e.g. Oyu mwana mbwatazyi misyobo minjiminji yansolo, bakaide kusobana musyobo omwe biyo utasyupi, wacilundika. = Since this child did not know many kinds of the game nsolo, they just played one game which was not difficult of gathering the small stones in a pile. Also cisolo
famine fruit, long boiling with several changes of water. e.g. Lyanzala tulalila nsonzwa. In time of famine we eat the nsonzwa fruit.
a plunge-basket for fishing, Also moono, mungwala, izubo, isyuta.
locust Also insozi.

a man's feathered head-dress made of wire and wildebeest tail. e.g. Balombe a baalumi bakalibambila nsuku zyakusama amitwe. Boys and men were making head-dresses for themselves. Also insuku, impumbe, cimvwuma, coba.
type of insect, e.g. Insundila zilaligwa abantu bamwi. = The nsundila insects are eaten by some people.

a gourd, e.g. Munsi amunene kwakali nsuwa yamukupa njaakali kusuka kati ufwambaane kubaa mafwuta akulema kabotu kutegwa bana balisye. Beside him was a gourd of milk which he was shaking saying that it should quickly become fat and nice and thick so that the children could eat.
flying termites, e.g. Nswa zilazwa muzyuulu noiwa mvwula. = Edible `flying ants' emerge from the ant-hills when the rains fall.
a duiker, e.g. Mwana ansya ufwida kucizyalilo. = The duiker dies at its birthplace. Also insya
shoots, e.g. Amunentule nsyuukwa zyacisyu cikomene kabotu. = Prune the shoots so that the vegetables grow well.
a float used in fishing, e.g. Kuti ntaangule yakalobo yabbila uleelede kukwisula. = When the float on a fishingline sinks you should pull the hook out. Also mbilibili, mbilila

what is separated by a distance, e.g. Bamadaala bakalya abana babo basankwa acipala cabo, bakaintu babo abana babo basimbi balalya ntantaanwa. Old men ate with their sons at the men's place, women ate with their daughters a distance apart.

a bag made of bark or a bundle of grass for carrying nuts, pl. of lutebe, e.g. Beenzuma bamwi bakaliko kuli nguwe zona, bakaleta ntebe zyazilyo. = Some of my friends who went to him the day before yesterday brought bags of food.
front of legs above knees, lap, e.g. Mwana naakayoowa mubwa wakaakukkala muntebe yabanyina. When the child feared the dog she went to sit on her mothers lap.

a half-skirt made of beads and cloth, e.g. Basimbi bakali kusama ntebwe zyamaaya. = Girls were wearing the ntebwe half-skirts made of beads and cloth. See maaya ntelebalo thighs, e.g. Akaambo kakuciswa musimbi wakaakwiide kusyaazya ntelebalo kukoka. Because of the girl's sickness she just remained with thin thighs.
maize when not fully developed, e.g. Mapopwe acili ntengaantenga taaligwi nkaambo taaningabizwa. = Maize which is not fully developed is not eaten because it is not yet ripe.

a disease which can afflict a child, e.g. Ncibotu kukwabilila mwana muvwanda kumalwazi mbuli cibele a *ntenga-ntenga*. = It is good to protect an infant from diseases like cibele and *ntenga-ntenga*. (These diseases may be passed on from mother to child if she goes into the field when the maize becomes ripe.)
a razor-blade, e.g. Wakafwuma kuyundwa akunyoolwa *ntengu* alunyoolo. = He went off early to have his hair cut with a scissors and to be shaved with a razor-blade. Also kagele
a type of bird, a parrot, e.g. *Ntengwa* ulakumba mumubuyu omuya. = The parrot is hatching in the baobab tree over there. Also cinkwele, cinkwenga, mpanda.
fresh meat, e.g. Munene wakali kwiile kumweta-mweta mbuli muntu wabona *ntente*. = The old man was smiling like someone who had seen fresh meat. Also *ntete*

stripes on a uniform showing rank of police officer or soldier. = Bamwi ibakali kunga balaa *ntepe*, zyakajugwa akutolwa ansi mumulimo wabo. = Some among them who had stripes had them removed and were lowererd in their rank.
a game played by boys in which they learn how to attack running animals, e.g. Bana bayasa *ntinde* mumusena. = Children are piercing the tuber in the vlei. (a game)
the sound made by using the hands to beat the water when fishing or swimming, e.g. Beembezi bauma *ntinta*
mobadubba. = The herders are beating the water with their hands in the pool where they are swimming.

a knife, e.g. Wakapandulula mbwaakayaswa *ntipa* mukaințu kumulumi wakwe akuti mulombwana wakaangwa akutolwa ku Mukobeko kuya kujaigwa. = The woman explained how she had been wounded by her husband with a knife and that the man had been taken to Mukobeko to be executed.
a shield, made of metal, e.g *Intobo* ncilivwunyo camunkondo. = The shield is for self-protection in time of war.
trolley, (ety. Eng.) e.g. Muntu weendela *antololi* munjanji wakajaigwa a citima. = The man who was travelling by trolley on the railway line was killed by the train.
small-pox, e.g. Bantu bakayambukilwa *ntomba*. = People were infected with smallpox.
a dancing-shield, e.g. Basicinande bazyanya *ntomu*. = The cinande dancers dance with dancing-shields.
rheum, mucous, e.g. Bana batalyi amatongwe kumeso antovwolomu kumilomo yabo. = Do not let the childen eat with mucous in their eyes and spittle on their mouths.
a roan-antelope, Also nkwalata, cilumbulumbu.

a small owl, e.g. *Ntukuntuku* zyakatalika kulila amunzi ciindi ca mangolezya antoomwe abamwi buyo bayuni bali mbuli bamaciciti alimwi abatumba caali kukwiizyanya kulila. = The small owls began to cry in the village in the evening with other birds like the eagle-owls and the common owls, crying out to one another.
a type of chrysalis (pupa or covering of buttefly or moth), e.g. *Ntulula* zyakomena kale. = The pupae have already grown.
a fright, sudden emotional reaction, e.g. Nzyaakabona masiku alya zyakamupa *ntulu*. = The things she saw that night gave her a shock.
courage, e.g. Kumucita boobu mukaintu kwakaba kumupa *ntunda*. = Doing this to the woman only gave her courage.
pride, e.g. Bantu tabacitilwi *ntunda* naaba mangwinini aamali. = People should not become proud or irresponsible because of money.

hump, e.g. Nokuba kuti wakasola kumana mapenzi akabajisi, pesi cakasika ciindi ncaakakwelela *antunda*. = Even though he tried to end the problems which he had, there came a time when he had to shoulder them.
possessions, e.g. Cilausisya kujana muntu wakalaa *ntundu* zyeebelwa alimwi zidula, nguuyide kusondoka. = It was sad to find a man who had admirable and rich possessions just going mad.
nakedness, e.g. Bana boonse bakajanika *muntundulu*. = All the children were found naked.

large numbers, e.g. Bananja bakafwa *ntundulu* mucibanda. The lechwe-cobs died in large numbers in the plain. Cilaa ntenda kulya banyama bakafwa *ntundulu*. = It is dangerous to eat animals which have died in large numbers.

a biting maggot, the red fly, e.g. Tiibakali koona kabotu nkaambo *ntunga* zyakali kubaluma akubasipa malowa abo. They did not sleep well because bugs were biting them and sucking their blood. Also *cuumba*

the young of a small species of fish, e.g. Tutazeli omu muzyiba, kuli *ntunga-bamuubila* twalo. = Let us not fish in that pool, there are just young fish. *ntunga-bankumbali* people who go aside to avoid trouble, e.g. Tusankwa otu tulayoowa kuumwa, *ntunga-bankumbali*. = These little boys are afraid of being beaten, they hide away from trouble.

a tuber plant eaten during times of deprivation, e.g. Basidilwe lyako bazoolya buyo *ntungulu* akumwaika waa*kufwa*. The mourners at your funeral will just eat *ntungulu* tubers and disperse when you die. (because of your laziness)
an owl, e.g. Mukaintu wakalaa meso mapati mbuli *ntungwa*. = The woman had big eyes like an owl.
top of the head, e.g. Keembe kakanjila *antuntilo* biya mane kuya kuzwidilila kumweebo aalya anselelo amulaka. The axe entered at the top of the head comig out at the lower jaw beneath the tongue.
a giraffe, e.g. Munyama ujisi nsingo ndamfwu *nintutwa*. = The animal which has the long neck is the giraffe. Also *intutwa*, *indudwa*, *intwiza*.

gifts prepared for a man's father when the son returns from working far away for a long time in order to please the spirits who will re-accept him into the village. The father then slaughters something to show that he has now received him back. e.g. Syaacaande uyanda kutula *ntwalo* zyakwe. Amumucitile nzyeelede tubone *ntwalo* nzyaamweetela. = Syaacaande wishes to offer his gifts. Do the necessary things so that we see what gifts he has brought for you.
a bud, e.g. Misamu tainingatalika kuvwunga *ntwi*. = The trees have not yet produced buds.
rumour, e.g. Wakayeeyela kuti antela bakamvwa *ntwiintwi* yabuumi mbwapona. He thought that perhaps they had heard a rumour of the kind of life he was living.
a steel instrument used to curve the inside of a mortar, e.g. *Intwisyo* yamufwali yafwumpa. The instrument of the carver is blunt.
porcupine, e.g. *Nungu* nozyakateelela ijwi lyamuntu, zyakamwaika zyoonse zyakatija. = When the porcupines heard the voice of a human, they all scattered and fled.
beads, e.g. Mucemble wakaanga kooye kakatungidwe nungu kukuboko kwamwana. = The old woman tied a string which was tied with a bead on the arm of the child.
bean(s); *mashed beans = citente*; the bean plant = *lunyabo*; *ground-beans* = *nyemu-mbwiila*; *wild beans* = *bunkululu, mundolomena*, (edible young pods and yellow flowers in October)
a carrier, e.g. *Nyakatundu wakandibwezela bbeeke lyangu.* = The porter carried my bag. Also sikatundu, simusempula, simangwanda.

a type of grass three edged, e.g. Ciindi camainza inga waakuboola kumpongo wajana kuti tulolomi toonse twatendaulwa madeenzya anyambaula. = In the rainy season when he would come home from herding goats he would find that all his toes were cut by blades of grasses. Also nembaula.

movements sideways, e.g. Mulilizyi lyamupeyo zuba mbolyeenda. Lyeenda mweenda *nyangule*. = You know how the sun moves during the cold season. It moves by moving sideways. nyangumi whale nyanja a lechwe-cob, pl. *banyanja*, e.g. *Banyanja mbanji mucibanda ca Namalyo.* = There are many lechwe-cobs on the plain of Namalyo. Also *nanja*
contempt, e.g. *Chipwetenge taakali mulombe wakajisi lunyansyo kubeenzinyina.* = Chipwetenge was a boy who did not despise his companions.

liveliness, e.g. Tee kufwumbwa kuti muntu uwakazyalwa takwe *nyanyango*, inguzu, nalya-nalya mangolomu nkulipenzya buyo. = If a person is born without liveness, strength, no matter what charm for strength he takes, he is only troubling himself.

scum on water, slime, e.g. Utalyati *anyanzabili* ulatezemuka. = Do not step on the slime it is slippery. Musankwa mulondo tayandi kunywa meenda avwelenye ntimba *anyanzabili*, minsyu amafwumba. = A neat man does not want to drink water mixed with mud and scum, urine and dung.
the colour green, e.g. Basicikolo besu basama zisani *zyanyanzabili*. = Our pupils wear green uniforms.
excitement, e.g. Munyongwe a *nyawi* yabantu ulati ndidola lyaandwa bbule. = The agitation and the excitement of the people was like a bee-hive being split open by a honey badger.

a twelve-set end-blown horn flute ensemble made of animal horn, each pitched differently, comprised of the following: mukwele, pindakati, sianseku, sikalumbu, siamupa, ifwuba nini, ifwuba pati, siamuluma sikili, cinkongwe, siamwinkula ifwumba, pagu. e.g. Wakalisiminina kusiba mukwele, *inyeele* isaanguna nyimbo. = He held his hand against his head in blowing mukwele, the reed-flute which starts off the songs. Bantu bazyana budima basiba *nyeele*. = People who dance the budima blow flutes. Bakali kusiba *nyeele* zitegwa, ntiyo, nsenseku, simulumansikili, mpindakati, mukwele, syaamupa, syacigoonta, mpaaku, fwuba a dimbila. = They were blowing the reed flutes called ntiyo, nsenseku, simuluma-nsikili, mpindakati, mukwele, syaamupa, syacigoonta, mpaaku, fwuba and dimbila. (Chibila wakasiba dimbila. = Chibila was blowing the dimbila flute.) *Nyeele* zyakatyolana kulila. = The sounds of the reed-flutes blended together. *Nyeele* impya ibambula mulomo. = A new flute is sweet in the mouth. (a proverb) (*Nyeele* can also be made of reeds.)
a traveller, e.g. *Nyenda* ulya kumukuli. = The traveller eats from what he carries.
glittering water, e.g. _Bweza mwanaako tuye kulwizi, bana bakeebe nyengeenge._ = Take your child so that we go to the lake and the children can watch the glittering water.
parts which remain when fat has been removed in frying, e.g. _Nyenye ilababotela kulya basicikolo._ = School children like to eat the fat of pork.

cicada, e.g. _Cakali ciindi cakumwaka nyenze nozikwiila cikwiile-kwiile._ = It was the cold season when the cicadas make the loud shrill sound. _Nyenze zyakali kulila kapati mbuli kuti twana twangulube twanjililwa nsilibi mucaanda._ = The cicadas were screaming like piglets whose piggery had been invaded by ants.
north-west, e.g. _nombe zyali kugama anyikalwaambo._ = The cattle were heading to the north-west.
mungoose, polecat, striped muishond, e.g. _Babwa bakaluma nyimba inunka._ = The dogs attacked a stinking polecat.

a polecat, pl. banyimbaasalama, e.g. _Nyimbaasalama nkanyama kaitwa kuti 'kununkangubo'._ = The polecat is a little animal which is called, 'the-blankets-stinks'. Mukubaa coolwe bavwimi bakajaya ntunga banyimbaasalama tobile. = The hunters luckily killed two polecats. Also nyimbansalama.
a polecat, pl. nyimbansalama, also nyimbaasalama.
an iron clamp, e.g. Wakamujana muvwimi kakankamina _nyinza_ asumo lyakwe. = He found a hunter hammering an iron-clamp at the end of a spear-shaft. Also inyinza.
the queen of termites, e.g. _Cuulu cakapola nyoola naakafwa._ = All the termites left when the queen termite died.
a big highly-sharpened blade used in the past to cut the hair, e.g. _Bazike bakali kunyoozegwa nyoolo kaindi._ = The slaves were shaved with a large blade long ago. Also lunyoolo.
the queen termite, e.g. _Kuti wajaya nyoolo, nswa zilamwaika._ = If you kill the queen termite, the flying ants will scatter.
furnace for smelting, pl. manyumbi.
a sledge-hammer, e.g. _Baalumi bapwaya mabwe anyundo zyabo._ = The men are breaking stones with their sledge-hammers. mukoma (common hammer), insando (a miner's hammer)
a type of bird, the honey-sucker, e.g. _Nyunsyu-buluba zisyuunta buluba mumaluba._ = The honeysucker sucks the juice of the flowers. Also nyonsyo-buluba, nsyuunsyu-buluba.

hunger, e.g. _Cintu cipati cimwi ciletya nzala mu Zambezi mbauka bategwa bacimvwinye._ = One important factor which brings hunger in the Zambezi Valley are the insects called bacimvwinye. _Ciindi canzala bantu bakapona kulya masenda, banzeenyuka abauka bamwi. Bakali kulya micelo yamusyokwe abuci._ = During the hunger the the people survived by eating different types of grubs, and other insects. They were eating wild fruits and honey.
pl. banzyeenuka, generic word for insect.

a craft, e.g. _Muntu ulaa nzelengo zinji ulakatazya kujanina mulandu._ = It is difficult to find fault in a person who has many crafts. _Tojisi maanu anzelengo._ You have not the wisdom of a craftsman.
bulrush millet, e.g. _Insima yanzembwe taizwi ino mwida._ = Insima made from bulrush millet does not leave the stomach quickly.
cicada, e.g. _Nzenze zilila liyanda kuboola mvwula. = The cicadas sing when the rains are about to come. Also inyenze, Iwenza.
sugar-cane, e.g. Ku Nakambala nkobalima nzimbe zinji. = At Nakambala is where they plant much sugar-cane.
couch-grass (a weed with long creeping roots), e.g. Kulima mumuunda wanzinza cilakatazya. = To plough in a field of couch grass is difficult.
sticks for playing a game in which they are thrown at a tuber, e.g. Twakabamba nzonde zyamucuncu-cuulu. = We made playing sticks from the mucuncu-cuulu tree.
a male baboon, e.g. Ndakabona nzuka mupati mumulundu. = I saw a big baboon on the hill. Also pombo.
bees, e.g. Uno mwaka nzuki nzinji. This year there are many bees.
a guessing game, (like which hand is it in?) e.g. Basankwa bakali kusobana nzukuunzuku kuzundanina mali. = The boys were playing a guessing game competing for money.
eland, e.g. Muvwimi wakajaya nzumba mupati kapati. The hunter killed a very big eland. Also musefwu.
thunder, e.g. Leza ulaleta ndabo anzumo. God brings the lightning and thunder.
a wanderer, e.g. Muntu simunzunga-nzunga tajisi cilawo. = A wanderer does not have a home.
quarrels, e.g. Murnanda yaba Haaduunku kunyina nzwanga ciindi coonse. In the home of Haaduunku there are never any quarrels at any time.
a headstrong person, e.g. Ooyu muntu ninzyundulu, mmuyumu amulomo. This person is headstrong, he is rough when speaking.

a house, e.g. Wakayaka nanda yabanyinazyala itegwa nanda yamanzaa-nino.' He built a house for his mother-in-law called 'the house of departure. (In the past when a man wished to marry he had to spend some years living with his in-laws. When he wished finally to take his wife away to his own home, he would build something special to mark his departure.) nanda yakulida dining room; zyuli = bedroom; nanda yakoona = dormitory; nanda yamizimo = museum

the housekeeper tribe or the Baleya, e.g. Bananda mbamunya mba Baleya. = The housekeeper tribe is the same as the Baleya. nanga a witchdoctor, e.g. Bantu balaunka kunanga kutegwa bazyibe ulowa. = People go to the witchdoctor so as to identify the one who was bewitching. Also munanga
a crack, e.g. Zifwuwa zyamaboko azyamaulu zyoonse zyakajisi nanzi. = All the bones of the arms and legs had fractures.

a wagon with four wheels, e.g. Kaindi bantu bakali kubelesya nola kususa masakaa mapopwe. = Long ago the people were using a four-wheeled wagon to transport maize. (nola yamabbanti = a wagon with metal wheels)

blackhite haired cattle, e.g. Bataata bakasweekelwa nombe zyamasekwe. My father lost black and white haired cattle. nombe yamakombolo/a light red haired cattle, e.g. Inombe yamakombolo yazyala sunu. = The light red haired cow gave birth today. nombe nsikili-sikili reddish ox. = a brownish nonze the male-reedbuck, e.g. Munyama nonze ulacela mucibanda. = An animal, a reedbuck, is grazing on the plain.
sleep, e.g. Mpeyo indibuzya nonzi mbuli nzala. The cold deprives me of sleep just as hunger does.

a type of grass found near the Zambezi river, e.g. *Inombe zicela nunga munsaa mulonga.* = The cattle are grazing grass near the river. *nombe ambongolo tazilyi kabotu munyengele, zilalya nunga.* = Cattle and donkeys do note eat munyengele grass, they eat *nunga* grass *ŋwadi* a letter, e.g. *Musimbi wandilembela ŋwadi mbotu kapati.* = A girl has written me a nice letter. Also *lugwalo*

a boy who works with the driver of a mini-bus in the city to help him quickly load passengers, e.g. Mainza wakamweelela mulimo mumilaka imwi ngobaita kuti *ŋwanwazi*, *kaponya* naa 'call-boys' mumulaka muubauba. = The work of the call-boy, who uses several languages, whom they call *ŋwanwazi*, *kaponya* or call-boy in English, suited Mainza.
a flat thing, pl. *mapapali*, e.g. *Mali alubulo onse mmapapali.* = All coins are flat. *Koleta ipapali lyomwe.* = Bring one flat piece.
deception, e.g. *Tiicakalampa ciindi kalindila pele musimbi katabooli, wakazyiba kuti bakamuuma pemba.* = He was not long waiting but the girl did not come, he realized that she had cheated him.
a big clay pot, pl. *zipempa*, e.g. *Kaindi bukoko bwakali kujikilwa muzipempa.* = Long ago they used to brew beer in big clay pots. Also *citalo*
punishment, e.g. *Akalala Sikabumba ulabawaalila pempya lya sikalileke.* = The Creator is angry and has thrown on them the punishment of AIDS.
a turkey, (ety. *piru*, Portugese) e.g. *Aawa ampulasi kuli mukuwa uvwubide pilu zinji.* = There at the farm there is a white-man who owns many turkeys. Also *kalukkuni*
a bull, e.g. *Mukandijaile ulya poho mupati.* = Kill that big bull for me.

a knife, e.g. *Wakasomona poko lyakwe libosya kuti aikosole nkuku mukosi ileke kubbubba.* = He took out his sharp knife so that he would cut the neck of the chicken so that it would stop flapping it's wings. Also *cipeni*
a type of bird, the crownedhornbill or toucan, e.g. *Pokooko wali kulila kubucedo.* = A crowned-hornbill was crying at dawn. Also *pokopoko*
big male baboon, pl. *bapombo*, e.g. *Nindakali kulya cinkwa, bakandinyanga bapombo.* = When I was eating bread, male baboons snatched it from me.
a pump, (ety. English). e.g. *Koleta pompi tupompe ncinga.* = Bring a pump so that we pump the bicycle. *(pompi wacisayili = a hose-pipe)*
a type of bird, the skylark, e.g. *Poopololo ulalila mujulu.* = The skylark is singing above in the sky.
a type of bird, the wagtail, e.g. *Popololo wafwa mumabuwa.* = The wagtail has died in the open country.

a pestle used by the Zambezi Batonga for pounding millet. It is long and heavy and has a wide splaying-end. e.g. *Bamakaintu batwa mabele akubelesya pubila.* = The women pound a red, short-stemed millet by using a long heavy pestle splayed at the end. Also *munsi*.
a highly-spirited child, e.g. *Chipwetenge ngupulipwipwi.* = Chipwetenge is a high-spirited child.
a baboon, pl. *bapumpulika*. e.g. *Bapumpulika balayanda kunyanga zinkwa kubeendanzila.* = Baboons like to snatch bread from travellers.
a vivacious person, *pwipwi* e.g. *Zupwi a pwipwi balalwana.* = A vicious animal is fighting with a highly- spirited child. Also *pulipwipwi*.
a waist-band of beads and thread, pl. *masaba-saba*, e.g. *Bazyana masabe balasama masaba-saba muzibuno* nobazyana. = They who dance the masabe wear beaded waist-bands when they dance.
strings hanging from waist, e.g. Basimbi basama sabi-sabi muzibuno nobazyana. = Girls wear strings hanging from the waist when they dance.

a summons to court, pl. masaimoni, (ety. English), e.g. Muunta naakaunka kuya kuula saimoni, wakaakubaambila basinkuta makani onse mbwaakacitika. = When Muunta went off to obtain a summons, he told the court officials all about how it had happened. Eelyo mabbalani wankuta wakatuma masaimoni kubasankwa aba bakali kukusonda kwa Hatubwantu. = Thereupon the court-clerk sent a summons to those men who had gone to Hatubwantu to divine.
a disgrace, a shame, e.g. Lyakaba sampu lipati kumvwa kuti sibbuku nguwakabba nombe. = It was a big disgrace to hear that the headman had stolen a cow.
type of tree, e.g. Ndali kukugonka ziyako zyasandwe. = I was off cutting poles from the sandwe tree. Also mumba.
a vegetable relish (Lactua sp.), e.g. Baama baunka kukucela cisyu casani. = My mother went to gather the sani plant from the bush for relish.
a small South African antelope. e.g. Kasese kali kulunduka mucimpayuma. = A small antelope was running in the desert.
a type of bird, the spur-winged goose, e.g. Isekwa zilakumba mazubaano. = During these days the spurwinged geese are sitting on their eggs. Also nacisekwe, nanjikwa, ikungubu.
marriage-partner, e.g. Bakati mwana ulaa coolwe kuya kujana sela limweelede. = They said that the child was fortunate to find a suitable marriage partner.
a burrow, e.g. Nengo yakasya sempo akoona muli ndilyo. = The antbear dug a burrow and slept in it.
a type of plant e.g. Bakabona senkenene, mpunga angala yacipopwe comwe munsi amunzonzo.= They saw a senkenene plant, rice and a flower of one maize-cob beside a muzonzo tree.
Also shalipopo
an edible tuber eaten raw or cooked (Ceropegia tentaculata). Also lumpobo
the Victoria Falls, e.g. Mulonga wa Zambezi ujisi mavwuumina aategwa Shuunganamutitima. = The Zambezi River has waterfalls which are called 'The Smoke that Thunders'.

a vegetable relish (Celosia trigyna), e.g. Shuunku mutalitendelezyi atantacuulu pe. = Do not cut up the shuunku relish together with the rape. Ishuunku ncisyu cilula-lula. = Shuunku is a relish which is slightly bitter. Also syuunku

type of tree (Corchorus trilocularis), pounded leaves cooked as green relish during dry season. e.g. Kamwaampa siacibwiiyi tukalisye ciindi cacilimo. = Dry some green relish so that we use it for relish during the dry season. Also syacikwiye
a man's necklace made of beads, wood and thread, e.g. Munene usamide siacikwakwa munsingo. = The old man is wearing a necklace made of beads, wood and thread around his neck.
a type of green relish (Gnaphalium micranthum), e.g. Sena wabizwa kale siamugwalu tulisye nsima? = Is the green relish cooked already so that we eat it with the nsima?
one who looks after dogs, e.g. Sibabwa wamana kale kubasanina. = The one who looks after the dogs has already finished feeding them.
a type of reed, e.g. Wakasika kuli nguwe ankata yasibbololonzya, wakamutwikka. = She came to her with a reed head-pad, she helped her to put the load on. Also sibololozi.
a headman, e.g. Sibbuku Hikampande wakafwa jilo. = Headman Hikampande died yesterday. Sunu kuli lubeta kwasibbuku. Today there is a courtcase at the headman's.

a large edible bush rodent, pl. basibende, e.g. Sibende ngutwajaya ulaa da. = The rodent we killed was pregnant. Katubweza maamba tukasye basibende. = Let us take hoes and go and dig for rodents. Also sibbende, siluumba
a hunter, e.g. Sibinda wamumunzi wajayigwa munyama musyokwe. A hunter of the village was killed by an animal in the bush.
a hard-worker e.g. Ooyu mwaalumi ngusibinda, ulabeleka milimo miyumu. = This man is a hard worker, he does difficult jobs.

a plant (Polygonum senegalense), the sliced leaves cooked for 2 hrs. and used as relish (May-August), e.g. Bamaama batola ciindi cilamfwu kujika cisyu casibololozi. = My mother took a long time to cook the relish sibololozi.

the violet tree snake, a kind of boomslang, (lit. I do not see the peak of my house) e.g. Kuti walumwa siboninsonje inga toponi kufwambaana, balaa busaki bukali. = If you are bitten by a boomslang you do not recover quickly, they have a fierce venom. Muntu walumwa siboninsonje usilikilwa musyokwe. = A person bitten by a boomslang is treated in the bush. Also kakuni (little piece of wood), kaankuni (small axe).
a type of bird, the fish-eagle, e.g. Sibooba wazimana nswi muciziba cokwa Longwe. A fish-eagle finished off the fish in the pool of Longwe. Also sikwaze.
a type of tree, e.g. Eeci cisamu ngu sibudogwi-dogwi. = This tree is a sibudogwi-dogwi.
a thing marked with small holes, one with the marks of small-pox, e.g. Muyuwa wangu ngusibudogwi-dogwi. My rattle has holes. Also sibudokwi-dokwi
an aggressive person, e.g. Musankwa oyu ngusibukali-buyuna. This boy is an aggressive person. Mulala ngusibukalibuyuna, ulalwana cibyaabi. The black-mamba is aggressive, it fights fiercely.
a name for the spitting (ringhals) cobra, e.g. Muntu walumwa sibukalibuyuna uleelede kusilikwa cakufwambaana. = A person bitten by a spitting-cobra should be treated immediately. Also nkombola.

one who is bed-ridden, e.g. Mucembele oyu ngusibukilabulo naa nkaambo kakukomena. This old woman is bed-ridden perhaps because she has grown old. Sunu Kalinda ngusibukilabulo ncaafwuluka bobuya. = Today Kalinda is bed-ridden, that is why she has become so thin. Also sibukilibulo

one feeding on roots, e.g. Ngusibukwalu-bukwalu ufwumba miyanda omu moonse muli zilindi. = It is the one who feed on roots who digs up the roots leaving these holes everywhere. Sibukwalu-bukwalu wabweza jamba kale uya kusyokwe. = The root-eater has already taken a hoe going to the bush.
a tarantula spider (lives in hole in ground), e.g. Bana bazwisya sibulibwa-libwa mukalindi. = The children have removed a tarantula spider from a hole. Also sibulibbwa-libbwa.
an eater of roots, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngusibulindilindi wali kusyaasya waawa. = This person is a rooteater who has been digging around here. Also sibudogwidogwi.
one with small-pox marks, Also sibudogwidogwi.
owner of the land, e.g. *Sibulongo nguwakandipa nyika mpekkede.* = It was the owner of the land who gave me the place where I live. Also sikatongo.

an adulterer, e.g. *Sibumambi nibakamujata bakamulunzya lubono lunji.* = When they caught the adulterer they fined him heavily. *Chizooma ngusibumambi, asunu wabbukilwa kale bulale.* = Chizooma is an adulterer, even today he has been caught in the act.
a person with many small teeth, e.g. *Sibunyo-bunyo ulasabanta kulya mango.* = A person with many small teeth gobbles up mangoes.

a clever person, e.g. *Sibusongo wakazwidilila mumisunko nokuba kuti yali miyumu kapati.* = The clever one passed the examinations even though they were very difficult. *Sibbuku wesu ngusibusongo, ubamba kabotu twaambo.* = Our headman is an intelligent person, he solves problems effectively.
an archer, pl. *basibuta*, e.g. *Basibuta bakaindi bakali kujaya banyama banji.* = The archers of the past were killing many animals.
a ravenous eater, e.g. *Syuumbwa ngusibutambo akaambo kakuyandisya kulya nyama.* = A lion is a voracious eater because of the intense desire to eat meat.
a bridegroom, e.g. *Sibwiinga wakaula zyakusama zyeebeka.* = The bridegroom bought admirable clothes. *Kupobwe lyasibwiinga kuligwa nyama inji kapati.* = At the bridegroom's feast much meat is eaten.
the eagle-owl, e.g. *Sibwi-sibwi wali kulila masiku onse.* = The eagle-owl was crying all night.
a brave person e.g. *Muntu sicamba tayoowi.* = A brave person does not fear. **sicambacilemu** = a patient person
a land-tortoise (has red stripes and lives among rocks), e.g. *Sicanga tabonwi-bonwi ccita wamujana mumabwe.* = A land-tortoise is not seen unless you find it among the rocks.
a treacherous person, e.g. *Bantu bayandisya kweena, basiccapoccapo ndibazyi.* = People are fond of deceiving, I know the treacherous ones.
a type of bird, the saddle-billed stork, e.g. *Ndabweza mayi asiceelamilandu.* = I have taken away the eggs of the saddle-billed stork.
the larger termite, pl. *basicenje*, e.g. *Bateya nswa balalumwa abasicenje.* = Those who were collectig flying ants are bitten by the larger ones. Also *macenya, sincenje*
the bushbuck, e.g. *Bataata bakajaya sicibabala antobolo.* = My father has killed a bushbuck with a gun. Also *mubabala*

one with whom one talks, e.g. *Mukaintu wakazyondwede mwaalumi wakwe wakali sicibandanyina muka Sicibende.* = The women who had used charms to subdue her husband was one who often talked with the wife of Sicibende.

one who is involved in collecting men for forced labour, pl. *basicibbalo*, e.g. *Basicibbalo bakali kuboola kujata baalumi batakali kutela.* = Those organizing forced labour used to come to catch the men who did not pay tax.

a barren or impotent person, e.g. *Sicibbololo mmusankwa naba musimbi utazyalili lyo buya.* = A `sicibbololo' is a man or a woman who never produces offspring. *Moomba wakakwatwa kuli sicibbololo.* = Moomba was married Also sicibololo. to an impotent man.
a type of lizard with a large head, e.g. Bana bayoowa nibabona sicibelele. The children feared when they see the large-headed lizard.

a person with a gap between teeth, e.g. Basyaaneene bakaba basicibende nkaambo lino lyomwe lyakazwa. = My grandfather has a gap between the teeth because one tooth came out. sicibiya-camunzila a vagabond, a tramp, e.g. Muntu mutolo ngusicibiya-camunzila, kwakwe takkali. A lazy person is a tramp, he does not stay at his home. Also mwanga, nakweenda sicibobela a type of bird, the giant bustard, e.g. Sicibobela ndamutobola abbwe lyamalekani. = I failed to kill the giant bustard with a stone from a catapult.

a person with a handless arm, e.g. Sicibokoboko bakamuuma bakaintu bakwe jilo. = Yesterday a handless man was beaten by his wife. Ino sicibokoboko ugonka buti misamu? = How can a handless person cut trees?

a childless man, an impotent man, e.g. Ooyu mwaalumi uyandika kusilikwa nkaambo ngusicibololo. = This man needs to be cured because he is impotent. Sicibololo tajisi bana. = An impotent man has no children. Also sicibbololo, ngomwa.
a type of bird, the giant bustard, e.g. Sicibonje ubililizya bana bakwe mumuumba omuya. = The giant bustard is guarding its young in that muumba tree.
a brown bat, e.g. Sicibulange uleta insinsini munanda. = The brown bat brings bugs into the house. Also sicikulangi
a spider living in a hole in the ground, e.g. Utasubili sicilibwalibwa. Do not urinate on the spider. Also sibulibwalibwa.
a water-spring, e.g. Sicidunta mmubotu kupa meenda kubantu. = A water-spring is good for providing water for people. Also nandu-maambi.
a water-buck, e.g. Siciduumuka wali kunywa meenda mumulonga. The waterbuck was drinking water in the river. Also sicikosa
a dung-beetle, e.g. Kamuzya mulange sicifwumbula mbwabumba maziu arjombe. = Come and see how the dung-beetle moulds the dung of cattle. Also siafwumbula
the sandgrouse, a seedeating ground-dwelling bird with brownish plumage, found in arid regions.
a type of bird, the knob-billed duck, e.g. Ndatiisole kuyubilila siciimbacankumo wakkede kudamu. = I was trying to stealthily approach the knob-billed duck who was sitting at the dam.

a learner, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ngusiciiya kufwala, taningacizyiba kabotu. = This boy is a learner of carving, he does not yet know it well. Ooyu mwana ucili siciiya kutanta ncinga. = This child is still learning to ride a bicycle.
a person easily provoked, e.g. Ooyu muntu ngusicikali, wanyema kale. = This person is easily provoked, she is already angry.

a person dressed in patches, e.g. Nsiyandi mwanaangu kuti akwatwe amulombe mubaya, sicikama, mutolo, mucete, sinzala. I do not want my child to marry a boy who is careless, badly dressed, lazy, poor and hungry. Also sicigamba.
one who always has plenty of money, e.g. Ooyu musankwa balamuyanda basimbi banji nkaambo ngusicikama. = Many girls love this boy because he always has plenty of money.
a water-mongoose, e.g. Kuli *basicikanda* banji mumulonga omu. = There are many water-mongooses there in the river.
a pupil, e.g. *Sicikolo* ukukula mucikolo mwayiila. = The pupil is sweeping in the school where he learns.
a waterbuck, e.g. *Ndajana sicikosa* ulacela mumulundu. = I found a waterbuck grazing on the hill. Also mugundumu, sicinduumuka, sicikulo.

a big kind of bat, e.g. *Mucimbuzi* cacikolo kuli *sicikulangi*. = There is a big bat in the school toilet. *Mumusamu omu mulila sicikulangi*. = In this tree is where a big bat is crying. Also simudima
a waterbuck, e.g. *Sicikulo* ulizyede kana kapwizyi. = The waterbuck had given birth to a female. Also sicikosa, mugundumu, sicinduumuka.
a trouble-maker, e.g. Nsi-yandi *sicikwala*, silweeno, simusuleende amunzi wangu, kozwa awa! = I do not want a trouble-maker, a deceiver, a careless person at my home, get out.
a person with diseased skin, e.g. *Ndakali kutandwa kubantuma mbuli sicikwankwa*. = I was driven away from my people as a person with a skin disease.
the larger partridge, e.g. *Nyama yasicilenje* ilanona. = The meat of the larger partridge is delicious. Also cikwalu-kwalu
the hole-dwelling spider, e.g. *Kuti wasubila sicilibwalibwa* inga wazimba cinswe. = If you urinate in a spider's hole your penis will swell. Also sibulibwalibwa, sicilibbwalibbwa.

a learner of a language with incorrect atticulation or pronunciation, as a child, e.g. *Bana boonse munyika kwaambaula balatalika kwaamba wisi. Balatalika ataata taata*. Kuti mwana kwaambaula watalika kwaamba banyina, takaambauli kabotu kubupati. Uyooba *sicilimelime*, unooluma-luma kwaambaula. = All children all over the world begin to talk by saying 'father.' They start, " Father, father!" If a a child starts to talk about its mother, it will not speak well when it gets to an older stage. It will be a stutterer, biting words when speaking.
one who ploughs everywhere, e.g. *Sicilimelime* wakalima muunda wangu. = The energetic plougher has ploughed my field.

an unhealthy person, e.g. *Ooyu muntu ulibonya mbuli kuti ngusicilwazi*. = This person seems to be unhealthy. *Ooyu muntu ngusicilwazi citasilikiki*. = This person is suffering from an incurable disease.
person with back bent inwards.
an insolent person, e.g. *Mwana waba Haamoonga ngusicimpangwe*. = The child of Haamoonga is insolent. Bantu bavwula kuuma *sicimpangwe*. = People are fond of beating an insolent person.
one disgarded then taken back, e.g. *Ooyu mwana ngusicimpongwe*. = This child was disgarded and taken back.
a bent-backed person, e.g. *Ncibi kuseka sicimuni inga wanyema*. = It is bad to laugh at a crippled person, he may become angry.
a left-handed person, e.g. *Sicimwesyi ubelesya lumwensyi zintu zyoonse*. = A left-handed person uses the left hand for everything.

a leper, e.g. *Sicinanta bakamutola kucibbadela caku Chikankata*. = They took the leper to the hospital at Chikankata. *Ndabona sicinanta wakanyongooka minwe yoonse*. = I saw a leper who had all his fingers destroyed.
a spring of water, e.g. Meenda twaateka kuli sicindunta. = We drew water at the spring. Inombe zinywa meendaa sicindunta. = The cattle drink the water from the spring. Also siciduunta
a waterbuck, e.g. Tuyanda kuya kukuvwima sicinduumuka wali kunywa meenda mudamu. = We want to go and hunt for a waterbuck which was drinking water at the dam.
an obstinate person, e.g. Mweene ngusicinguni, tamvwi kulaigwa. = Mweene is obstinate, he does not listen to advice.
a rude, quarrelsome person, e.g. Mukande ngusicinkangu, ncobatamuyandili bantu. Mukande is a rude person, that is why peple do not like him.

a type of bird, the red bishop, e.g. Ndabula malekani nindauma sicinsangwe mumuumba. = I have no catapult, I could have hit that red bishop bird in the muumba tree. Toonse tulakumvwa kutangala kwasicinsangwe amintengwe kubucedo. = We will all hear the rejoicing of the red bishops and the swifts at dawn.
a deranged person, mentally unbalanced, e.g. Sicinsondo wakalyatwa cimbayambaya jilo mumugwagwa uya ku Choma. = A deranged person was hit by a vanette yesterday on the road going to Choma.
a mad dog, e.g. Kuti walumwa sicinsuungwe nkunywa miyanda yamutuntulwa. = If you are bitten by a rabid dog you should drink the roots of the mutuntulwa tree.
a naked person, e.g. Amumusamike zisani sicintanda oyo. = Put clothes on that naked person. Ncintu cibotu kupa cisani kuli sicintanda. = It is a good thing to give clothes to a naked person.
a type of antelope e.g. Kwainda sicinzobe mumuunda okwesu. = An antelope passed through our field. Also situtenga, sicizobe.
a conceited person, e.g. Bantu tababayandi basicipaama. = People do not like conceited people.
a girl who suffers from the complaint of stomach-pains during menstruation, e.g. Mukaintu sicipala takonzyi kumita. = A girl cannot conceive due to gynacological problems.
a small type of bee (makes honey in places on the ground called mabuwa,) e.g. Tuya kukulida buci bwasi-cipansi mubbuwa. = We are going to collect honey from the bee in the plain. Also haansi
an insect said to spit poison in one's eyes, e.g. Sicipiila wandipiila mumeso nitwali kusobana. = An insect spat in my eyes when we were playing.
Also sicipiila

a wild boar, pl. basicipongo, e.g. Sicipongo waluma mubwa wabavwimi. = A wild boar has bitten the hunter's dog. Basicipongo baamana mapopwe mumuunda. = Wild boars have finished off the maize in the field. Also nkuntula

a reckless, extravagant, wasteful person, e.g. Mutinta waba mucete nkaambo lyoonse wakali sicisantwe-santwe. = Mutinta has become poor because she was always a recklessly extravagant and wasteful person.

an insolent person, e.g. Ooyu mwaalumi ngusicisapi. = This man is insolent. Tandiyandi kuswaigwa sicisapi uyiisya bana matusi. = I do not like to be visited by an insolent person who teaches the children insulting words.
a type of bird, the knob-billed duck, e.g. Bataata bajaya sicisunka. = My father has killed a knob-billed duck.

one who breaks off big lumps of nsima, e.g. Bana baniini tabeelede kulya antoomwe asicisunu inga wabaima. = Little children ought not to eat together with a greedy person as he may eat even their share.
larva, cocoon, nymph in cocoon, type of chrysalis, e.g. *Sicitebbelwa* ulaliyakila cakukkalila. = A nymph builds itself its own home. *Sicitebbelwa*
nanda njumu. = A nymph makes a strong home.
larva, e.g. Mwana uyoowa *sicitebeelelwa* pesi talumi. = A child fears larva but it does not bite.

a wild pig, pl. basiciyongo, e.g. Basinombe baya kukuyandaula basilutuba, *basiciyongo* abatimba muzisaka. = The herders are going to look for white mongoose, wild pigs and small antelopes in the bush. Also sicipongo.
a type of antelope. Also sicinzobe
the larger red ant, e.g. *Sicombolwa* wanyikila munkomeki ya mukupa. The large red ant drowned in a cup of milk.

a wildebeest, e.g. *Sicoobe* ngutwajana musyokwe mmukali. = The wildebeest which we found in the bush today is fierce. Nyama yasicoobe nimbotu kapati The meat of a wildebeest is delicious. Also munyumbwe
a lucky person, e.g. *Sicoolwe*
mali munzila. = A lucky person found money on the path.
a type of bird, the small plover, e.g. Mucoonde eciya kwali kulila *sicoombamilangu*. = A small plover was singing in that thicket.

the larger red-ant, pl. basicoombolwa, make hole and surround it with a wall of soil, e.g. nanda yabasicoombolwa ngamamvwu alambwa mukamufwu. = The house of the larger red-ant is the very soil with which a widow or widower is smeared. Also sicombolwa.
a large spider, e.g. *Sicuubi* ulya nzinini zyajatwa luubilili. = The spider eats flies which are caught in the web. Also sicuubilili, sicilibwalibwa

a spider which spins a web outside from branch to branch, e.g. Kuli *sicuubilili* uzamba mumitabi yamibanga eyi lyoonse. There is a spider which spins a web on branches of these mibanga trees every day.
a big-bellied person, a glutton, e.g. Mudaala ulya ngusidalyoombwa nkaambo kakulya kapati lyoonse. That old man has a big stomach because of always eating a lot.
a pelican, e.g. *Sifwundwe* mmuyuni mubotu. = The pelican is a beautiful bird.

a talkative person, e.g. Mukaintu wangu ngusigambaamba weelede kulaigwa. My wife is talkative and needs to be advised. Kuba sigambaamba ciletela kulitaya. To be talkative can lead to having yourself condemned.
a hornless animal, pl. basigumpu, e.g. Ndiyanda kumwaanina caano casiqumpu. = I want to tell you a story about the hornless one, i.e. the lion.
muntu uvwolekede basune balo basigumpu. = I found a man yoking oxen who were all hornless.

an excellent dancer, e.g. *Siindikazyano* waku Monze nguwakabainda bazyani boonse aboobo wakapegwa bulumbu. = The talented dancer of Monze surpassed all the other dancers and so was given the prize. Mukaintu oyu ngusiindikazyano, kunyina cizyano ncatazyi. This woman is an excellent dancer, there is no dance which she does not know.
a plant with long rows of small inverted thorns along each branch, e.g. *Sijatwa* wandiyasa mumaanza nindali kutebba nkuni. = The thorny sijatwa plant pierced my hands when I was gathering firewood.
a children's game with beetles, e.g. *Bana basobana sijatwababi munzila nobazyila kucikolo.* = The children play the beetle-game when they are returning from school.

a sensitive insect with little protuberance on it's head, the knobbed-head insect, e.g. *Kauka nkaanga sijatwa-babi nkabotu kweebela.* = The little knob-headed insect is delightful to watch. **sijatwibabi.** Also sijatwababi.
