a crocodile, e.g. *Mudaala wakali kutwaanina caano casitale.* = The old man was telling us a story about a crocodile. *Sitale waluma kale bazeli botatwe.* = The crocodile has already attacked three fishermen. Also intale, ciwena
fish poison, e.g. *Bana babikka sitinde kutegwa nswi zifwe.* = The children have put *sitinde* poison so that the fish die.
a game played by children in which they throw wooden spears at a tuber, e.g. *Bana bayasa sitinde mumusena.* = The children are 'piercing the tuber' in the vlei.

one who arranges a marriage, pl. *basityombo*, e.g. *Mwami, ndalikumbilila musimbi wakukwata nkaambo basityombo bamwi tabasyomeki.* = Chief, I am asking for a girl to marry because some of those who arrange marriages are not trustworthy.
a vegetable relish (Gynandropsis gynandra), e.g. *Baama bacela siungwa mumuunda.* = Mother is gathering *siungwa* relish in the field. Also cisiungwa

a type of bird, the ibis, e.g. *Ndeenena siyaswimuumba mumugooni munzila izyila kumuunda.* = I discovered an ibis in the *mugooni* tree on the path coming from the field. *Muyuni siyaswimuumba ulauluka atalaa cizyiba.* = The ibis is flying over the pond.
one who smiles hiding treachery, e.g. *Basilweeno mbaasiyupamenyo buyo. = Deceivers just show their teeth in a smile.
a fabulous beast of prey which does harm only in darkness and is notorious for its gluttony. It appears in many stories. e.g. *Sizimwe wakali kuya-*
kananga Ndyamaanu.* = The fabulous beast wanted to eat the little child, Ndyamaanu.
a canoe-paddle, e.g. *Kamulete soke tukwasule bwato.* = Bring a paddle so that we row the boat.
a monkey, e.g. *Sokwe waamana mapopwe mumbewu yangu.* = A monkey has finished off the maize in my field.
the bush, e.g. Syuumbwa ulalila musokwe. = The lion is roaring in the bush. Also syokwe
uncultivated grain, a type of bush-grass, relish, e.g. Mumuunda wangu kwakamena *sonkwe.* = Uncultivate grain has germinated in my field.
an edible grass, (Dactyloctenium giganteum) the seeds are boiled as a cereal in Feb. e.g. *Isyokwe lyasonkwe lilakatazya kulimina* = Bush-grass is difficult to weed.
the hermit-lizard, e.g. *Sonsoolwe ncuuka ciluma kapati.* = The hermit-lizard is a reptile which bites a lot.

one who is extra sensitive in keeping people away from his wealth, e.g. Ooyu *ngusonsoolwe mukali abwina.* = This is a sensitive person, he is exceptionally cruel in keeping people away from his home.
a hare, pl. *basulwe*, e.g. Nitwali kukuvwima, twajaya *basulwe bobile.* = When we went out to hunt, we killed two hares. *Sulwe wakasoleka kubakasya kee-*
beenzinyina.* = The hare tried to refuse to give his friends an axe. Also syaanasulwe, syaanamabumba.
a batchelor, e.g. Ooyu *mwaalumi ngusumbalume*, tajisi mukaIntu. = This man is a bachelor, he does
one who objects, e.g. Moyo _ngusungwe._ = The heart is an objector.
any poisonous mushroom, e.g. Bana bakalya _sunkula-nameele bakafwa._ = The children who ate the poisonus mushroom died.

a type of small tree (Olax Obstusifolia). Very sweet-scented white flowers and scarlet glossy fruits which are sweet and edible. The tree has one strong lateral root. e.g. Bana baya-kukucela bana _basunkumwendo musyo-kwe._ = The children have gone to gather fruit from the _sunkumwendo_ tree in the bush.
a spotted hyaena, e.g. Masiku asunu _suntwe_ walya mpongo zyobile zyabaacisya. = Last night a hyaena devoured two goats of my uncle. _Kasuntwe-malenda_ = a brown hyaena
a hair, pl. _masusu_ and _susu,_ e.g. Ooyu mwana ulaa _susu_ bbotu. = This child has lovely hair. _Masusu_ abamakuwa mma-ubauba. = The hair of white people is soft.
a six-penny coin in colonial times, e.g. Kaindi _susu_ wakali kuulwa muzingini. = In the past a cock could be bought for sixpence.
a person devoted to the service of the people, e.g. Chikuka ngu _syaabantu._ = Chimuka is a man of the people.
one who asks, e.g. _Syaabbuzya_ takolwi bowa. = The one who asks is not poisoned by a mushroom. (a proverb)

a fierce person, pl. _basyaabukali,_ e.g. Munene _syaabukali_ wabauma bana balisya mumuunda wakwe. = The fierce old man beat the children who allowed the cattle to eat in his field. Bantu _basyaabukali_ balayoosya. = Fierce people are fearsome.
an expert, e.g. Wakaba *syaabupampu* mubusilisi bwabantu. = He became highly accomplished in medical practice.
a name for God, e.g. Leza ngu Syaabusiwa mbwatembaulwa. = God is praised by the name Syaabusiwa. Syaa-busiwa nguutupa meenda. = Syaabusiwa is the one who gives us water. See Leza.

a diviner, e.g. Twali kuli *syaacibeja* kuya kumvwa cicisa mwana. = We went to the diviner to learn what was making the child sick. Atweende kuli *syaacibeja* tukasonde mwana uciswa. = Let us go to the witch-doctor to find out the cause of the child's sickness.
a frog, e.g. Inkuku zyalya *syaacicula*. = The chicken ate a frog. Mucikala omu kuli *syaacicula* mupati kapati. = There is a big frog in the well. Also *cula*
any creature covered by a shell, pl. *basyaacikwaakwa*, e.g. Inondo ngusyaacikwaakwa. = The tortoise is a shelled creature.
the Creator, e.g. *Syaacilenge* nguwakalenga zintu zyoonse munyika. = The Creator is the one who created all things in the world. See Leza.
a type of bird, the cuckoo, e.g. *Syaacilundula* ulila niyayanda kuwa mvwula. = The cuckoo twitters when the rain is about to fall.
a fringe, a Valley garment, e.g. Nindakali kujwe oku ndakali kusama *syaacimwanyu*. = When I was in the east I wore a Zambezi garment.
a selfish person, e.g. Tulizwide kuliyanda, busyaacivwuule, bumambi a bubbi. = We are full of self-love, selfishness, adultery and thievery.
one who sleeps around e.g. Mucisi coonse nkobali basyaacoonoona basimbi. = In every country there are those who sleep around with women.
a lizard, e.g. Kaaze waluma *syaadolyo*. = The cat has attacked a lizard. *Syaadolyo* ulya nzinini zinji. = The lizard eats many flies. Also syaadyolo, tombela

an endless talker, e.g. Ncobayanda buyo nkunikulilumbaizya kuti balabeleka, kakuli tababeleki pe, mbaasyaadomolitopota buyo. = They want to praise themselves that they are working while they do not work, but are just endless talkers.

the scarab or dung-beetle, e.g. *Syaafwumbula* ujanika kapati ciindi camainza alimwi mumaziu aanombe. = The dung-beetle is found especially during the rains and in cattle dung. Ndajana ndongwe zinji mubwina bwa-*syaafwumbula*. = I found plenty of groundnuts in the home of the dung-beetle.
one who gives all the news, e.g. Ukabuzye *syaaganipa* nguuzyi makani onse. = Ask the one who gives all the news, he is the one who knows current affairs.

a type of bird, the rock-jumper, e.g. Ndalikutanda *syaajeye* mumabwe, mpoona wandisiya. = I was chasing the rock-jumper from the rocks, thereupon it left me. *Syaajeye* ulaa bana mumpako yabbwe. = The rock-jumper has its young in a hole among the stones.

a lizard, with small body and large head, e.g. Munzila nindali kweenda, ndajana *syaakabelebele* uyotela zuba. = When I was walking along the path, I found a lizard basking in the sun *syaakale* an ancestor, pl. *basyaakale*, e.g. Ndajana jamba lyakasiya *syaakale* mumuunda mutwali kulima. = I found a hoe left by an ancestor in a field we were ploughing. *Basyaakale* bakatuyiisya bukkale bubotu. = The ancestors taught us about good living. Also sikale.
a miser, e.g. Nokuba kuti oyu munene wakalivwubide kapati, tanaakali *syaakalifwune*, wakali silubomba. = Even though this old man was very rich, he was not mean, he was kind to others.

a small girl attending the one being initiated, e.g. Mulimo wa-*syaakamwale* ngwakulindila kamwale amilimo imwi. = The function of the initiate's attendant was to keep company with her and do other chores. Also haakamwale, haakalindizyo
a type of cassava, e.g. *Syaakanjungo* mmusyobo wamwanja ngobalima bamwi. = *Syaakanjungo* is a type of cassava which some used to plant.

the tarantula spider, e.g. *Syaakongabajika* uile kwiilingana acikko awa. = The tarantula spider is just moving about at the fireplace here. *Syaakongabajika* wapida mucikko. = The tarantula spider was burnt in the fireplace.

expert doctor, e.g. Oyu *syaakoola* wakalidumide mpuwo yoonse mu Lusaka akaambo kamilimo mibotu yabusilisi njaakali kucitila bantu. = This experienced doctor was held in high regard in Lusaka because of the achievements in healing which he had done for people.
an unskilled Indian labourer (in colonial times), e.g. Mu Zambia kwakali *basyaakoola* banji. = There were many Indian workers in Zambia.
the last arrival, e.g. Ncibi kuba *syaalizyakusika* kumuswaangano. = It is bad to be the last to arrive at a meeting. Also ncalizyakusika
an earwig, e.g. Bana balakayoowa nkaanga *syaalumano*, bayeeya kuti kalamaka. = Children are afraid of the earwig, they think that it pinches.
a person rich in cattle, e.g. *Syaamaanza-anombe* wakatola nombe zyakwe zimwi kukusambala. = The one with abundant cattle took some to be sold.
a thief, e.g. *Syaamabba* wabba kale nkuku yamuntu. = The thief has already stolen a person's chicken.
a type of bird, the small locust-bird, e.g. *Syaamabele* ngweejaya sunu ulaa mafwuta. = The small locust-bird which I killed today has plenty of fat.
large amphibious rodent.
the circular base of a maize-bin into which the beams are fixed. e.g. Bataata baanga nsumpi zyabutala muli *syaamanga*. = My father is tying the beams of the maize-bin on the base.
the poles or wattles running horizontally above the wall of the hut, e.g. Cisamu casyaamangwa catyokela munanda. = The pole on top of the walls broke and fell into the house.

a mask, one who dances with a mask at night-time, e.g. Amumukonge *syaamankwamu* mwana oyo aleke kulila. = Frighten that child with a mask to stop her crying. Bantu batija *syaamankwamu*. = People flee from the masked dancer.
a large amphibious rodent, e.g. Ijilo twakalya kabotu nkaambo basankwa bakajaide *syaamanona*. = We ate well yesterday because the boys killed a large rodent.
a bush-cat, e.g. Babwa bajaya *syaambilwa-abana* masiku ayinda. = The dogs have killed a bush-cat during the night. Also syaambwijunza.

addax (large antelope with twisted horns), e.g. Mwakali kwakaindide *syaambololo* mumunzi kwesu. = Last year a large antelope passed through our village. Mweembo ndwija Iwasyaa-*mbololo*. = The musical horn (used at initiation) is the horn of an antelope. Also muzilawo.

a person who is always complaining, e.g. Ooyu mukaintu ngu-syaambweka ncobatamuyandi bantu bamwi. = This woman is ever complaining, that is why many people do not like her. Muntu syaambweka ngusibunjaka. = A person who always complains brings conflict.
a bush-cat, e.g. Mubwina omu mwanjila syaambwijunza. = A bush cat has entered into this hole. Also syaambilwaabana.
a type of bird, the rock jumper, e.g. Syaameya uyanda kukkala akati kamabwe amilundu. = The rock jumper likes to live among the rocks in the hills.
a scarab, e.g. Syaamfwumbula ncuuka ciyanda kusobana mutombe. = A scarab is an insect which likes to play in dirt. Also syaafwumbula

one who has a habit of frowning, e.g. Ooyu muntu inga nociceya cacitika wabamba kale minya ankumo, ngusyaaminya. = This person, no matter how insignificant a thing occurs, who makes frowns on the forehead, is a habitual frowner.
a small, hard, scarlet seed, a poisonous little red berry, pl. basyaampiki, e.g. Basimbi basobanya basyaampiki. = The girls like playing with the hard scarlet seeds.
a womanizer, e.g. Mudenda wakafwa kufwambaana nkaambo wakali syaampwizi. = Mudenda died quickly because he was a womanizer.
an eel, e.g. Eeyi nswi ilatezemuka kapati, njiinga syaamulinga. = This fish is very slippery, it is an eel. (nyinsi = an electric eel)

an alternative food used in famine times, which if not prepared in the proper way becomes poisonous, e.g. Mwana wafwa nzala mukamujikile syaamuwamba. = Cook syaamuwamba for the child who is hungry. Ilya nzala bantu balya syaamuwamba. = During a famine the people eat syaamuwamba. Also syaamuvwamba
a swing, e.g. Bana balasobana ali syaamuyumbe-yumbe. = Children play where there is a swing.
a type of fish, said to jump and bite, which pregnant women are forbidden to eat. Also simuluma.

a grub found in grain-stalks, pl. basyaamwinyongwa, e.g. Mapopwe akaligwa basyaamwinyongwa mumuunda. = The maize was eaten by destructive grubs in the field. Mapopwe anjilwa basyaamwinyongwa taabbali. = Maize attacked by grubs does not produce grains. Also syaanyoongwa

a type of bird, the black-shouldered kite, e.g. Syaanakancolo mmuyuni ukatazya kujaya. = The black-shouldered kite is a bird which is difficult to kill. Syaanakancolo ulya basyaadobelela. = The black-shouldered kite eats lizards.

one of the nicknames for the hare of traditional stories, e.g. Kuli twaano tunji twasyaanama-bumba. = There are many stories about the hare. Mubwa wakacaala kafwekemba kuli nkiinga syaanamabumba, nkanyama, nkansanje. = The dog was left panting behind the hare, the clever animal. Also syaanasulwe

the trigger of a trap, a stick which when trodden on releases the idiba trap, e.g. Kayuni kalyata syaanano nkakacegwa. = A little bird which steps on the trigger of an indiba trap, is the one which is caught.

the hare of traditional fiction, e.g. Ijilo ndakali kuswiilila caano casyaanasulwe. = Yesterday I was listening to a story about the hare. Izyaano nzinji nzyasyaanasulwe. = Many stories are about the hare.
inedible red berries with very hard seed, e.g. Basyaanciiki tabaligwi. = The red berries are inedible. Also syaampiki
grandfather, e.g. Ndiya kumunzi kukubona syaanene wangu. = I am going home to see my grandfather. Syaanene wangu wakacembaala kapati. = My grandfather has become very old. Also tatakulu.
a deaf person, e.g. Mwana angu ngusyaangwingwi. = My child is deaf. Also cuulutwi
a rhinocerous, e.g. Munyama ujisi lwija lomwe ngusyaaninga. = The animal which has one horn is a rhinocerous. Also cipembele
inedible red fruit, e.g. Mwana wakakolwa syaanjika wakaakuponena kucibbadela. = The child that was poisoned with red berries is recovering at the hospital. Also syaampiki.
cock, e.g. Masiku basyaankalu balila ziindi zotatwe. = At night the cocks cry three times. Also mukombwe, muzingini
a warthog, e.g. Mubwa walumwa kuli syaankole. = The dog has been attacked by a warthog. Also muuma, sicipongo, nkuntula
leader, governor, principal, e.g. Ooyu mudaala wakali ngosyaanondwe naa mupati wacikolo cipati. = This old man was the chancellor or the head of the University.

a small type of bee making honey in places called mabuwa on the ground, pl. basyaansi, e.g. Tuyakukulida syaansi kumabuwa. We are going to get honey from ground-bees on the open plain. Atukalide basyaansi, mbabalaa buci bunona. = Let us go and forage for honey from the ground-bees, they are the ones with sweet honey.
an edible mushroom, e.g. Aaba bana basobanya basyaansyukwa. = These children are playing with edible mushrooms.
an edible small mushroom, e.g. Ijilo twakalya basyaa-nsyuukwa mbobakaleta bana. = Yesterday we ate small mushrooms which the children brought.

a type of bird, the robin or waxbill, e.g. Njanda kuvwuba kana kasyaantiinga. = I want to own the chick of a robin. Nkaanga syaantiinga nkayuni kaniini kapati. = The little robin is a very small bird.
a person who takes liberties by entering where not wanted.
a rhinocerous, e.g. Syaanyinga ulaa bana mmukali kapati. = A rhinocerous with young is very aggresive. Also cipembele, syaaninga
a lion, e.g. Syaanyo ulalila mumalundu. A lion is growling in the hills. Also syaanza, syuumbwa.
your grandfather, e.g. Kotola mulilo kuli syaanyokokulu. = Take fire to your grandfather.
the grain-stalk grub, e.g. Mapopwe anjilwa basyaanyongwa taakomeni kabotu. Maize attacked by the grain-stalk grub does not grow well. Also syaamwinyongwa.
a lion, e.g. Syaanza mmunyama mukali. The lion is a fierce animal. Syaanza ulalila mumilundu ya Kampeenzya. The lion is roaring in the hills of Kampeenzya. Also syuumbwa, mulavwu.

one going around dancing at people's doors by night, e.g. Sunu masiku kwali syaanzyanya anze. = Last night there was a witch-dancer outside. Sunu ndamujata syaanzyanya. = Today I have caught the night-dancer. Also syaazyana
the plant known as blackjack, e.g. Cisyu casyaasipa cilanunkilila. Blackjack smells nicely. Also syaazipa.
a type of bird, the blackshouldered kite, e.g. Syaapililyo ulya tukuku. = The black-shouldered kite eats chicks. Also syaanakancolo

a dumb person, pl. basyaataambi, e.g. Ooyu mwana mukamutole kucikolo cabasyaataambi. = Take this child to the school for the dumb. Ndayaanya muntu syaataambi, wali kutambaika. I met a person who could not speak, he was waving hands.
a type of bird, the smaller kingfisher, e.g. Kayuni nkaanga syaatakalala kalya nswi mucizyiba. = The smaller kingfisher is eating fish in the pool.
e.g. Mainza wakali musimbi syaatasayi. = Mainza was a girl who did not hesitate in doing a thing.
a name for God, e.g. Leza ngu Syaateelwi. = God is the one who cannot be measured or compared. See Leza.
one who takes liberties by entering where not wanted, an intruder, e.g. Syaatompwani wanjila kale munanda iwona bapati. The intruder has already entered the bedroom of the elders.
a type of bird, the small locust-bird, pl. basyaazele, e.g. Ndajana tanga lyabasyaazele mumuunda. = I found a flock of locust-birds in the field.
a gecko (house-lizard), e.g. Mwana uyoowa syaazibumbu. = The child fears the house-lizard. Syaazibumbu balalwana anzoka. The house-lizard is fighting with a snake. Also syaazikulukulu
a witch-doctor, pl. basyaazibwenye, e.g. Bakasola basyaazibwenye kumusilika, pele cakakaka. = The witchdoctors tried to heal him, but to no avail.

a type of lizard with flat stomach which is quick in movement, e.g. Naluntaambwe wakali kuyanda kuti bafwa kabapiluka, pele waacedwa buyo, kakuli syaazikulukulu nguwakapa kuti bafwa kabafwidilila. The chameleon wanted all the dead to come back to life, but he was late, it is the lizard who decreed that the dead should die for ever.
ancin fwa. I crushed a gecko with a bicycle and it died. Syaazikulukulu uzyala mayi manji. = The gecko lays many eggs.
small locust-bird, e.g. Ndajana syaazimpande ulya nsozi. = I found a small locust-bird eating locusts. Also syaazele.

the black-jack plant with yellow flowers, black seed, used for relish, e.g. Basimbi bayakukucela syaazipa kucindongwe. = The girls are going to gather black-jack in the groundnut plot. Also syaazyipa, haasyipa.
a type of bird, the paradise-flycatcher, e.g. Kwali kulila syaazwezwe mucoonde uubililizya bana. = A paradise-flycatcher was crying out in the thicket to protect its young. Also simampolyo
one who is fond of his mother, e.g. Ooyu musankwa ngusyabanyina wakakomena kale. = This boy is one who clings to the mother yet has already grown up. Also syaabanyina

a hospitable person, e.g. Muntu oyu ngusyabeenzu, ulaswaigwa kapati. This person is hospitable, he is frequently visited. Mulubuwa muno mumwasyabeenzu tamumani beenzu pe. = In this courtyard of the hospitable, visitors are never lacking. Also syaabeenzu.

someone or something which has disappeared from view, e.g. Koya yebo Kanyoolo ukazilete ŋombe. Kunyina aicilibonya zyaba _basyabbililila_. = You, Kanyoolo, go and bring the cattle. They are no longer in sight, they have become lost ones.
a wild plant
lizard, e.g. Kuciindi eeci zuba Iwakali kale acikasaalizi, aalya _ba-syadobelela_ mpobayotela zuba. = at that time the sun was already rising, the time when the lizards are basking in the sun.
a game of hide and seek, e.g. Basicikolo basobana _syagogo_. = The school-children are playing the game of `hide-and-seek.'
the bush, wilderness, e.g. Mu-lavwu mmwami _wasyaka_. = The lion is the king of the bush.

(_Plumbago zeylanica_) pounded root mixed with water said to increase male potency. Juice from scraped root used in tatooing. e.g. Muntu mutolo kuya kubakaintu uyasaulwa _syalutenta_ kumusana. = A man who is impotent as regards women, is cut on the back and has a pounded root mixed with water rubbed into the wounds. Also halutenta.
a frog, e.g. _Basyamataaza_ balasabila kumwaka. = The frogs make noise at the beginning of the rainy season.

medicine said to increase one's number of cattle, e.g. Iŋombe wakali zijisi zyakali kutandila kumyaanda yosanwe amyaanda yobilo. Ndiza kuli nkwaakalide _syambwe_ biya! = He possessed cattle which reached to 700. Perhaps there was a place where he had taken the medicine to increase cattle. Bantu banji bakali kumuyeeyela kuti ujisi musamu _wasyambwe_ lyaŋombe. = Many people thought he had the medicine for enriching oneself with cattle. Mudaala ulasunkuta asyoonto nkaambo wakajisi dondamwaka lyalo ndyaakaliinda naakalya *syambwe lyanombe*. = The old man was slightly lame because he had a carbuncle which he inflicted on himself when he took the medicine which increases cattle.
a type of bird, the rockjumper, e.g. *Syaameeya* nkayuni kakatala kufwambaana. = The rock-jumper easily gets tired. Also *syaameya*.
cement (ety. Eng.), e.g. Inanda yokwesu izilidwe *syamende*. = Our house is plastered with cement. Also *samende*
an artificial shell once used by Batonga as currency, e.g. Kaindi Batonga bakali kubelesya mali *asyamende*. = Long ago the Batonga were using artificial shells as money.
inedible red berries, e.g. *Basyampika* tabaligwi, balakola. = Red berries are not eaten, they are poisonous. Also *syaampiika*.
thatching-grass, e.g. Basimbi bakajwe *syankonko* tuvwumbye nanda. = Let the girls cut thatching-grass so that we roof the house.
a frog, e.g. Nzoka zilayanda kujata *basyansombokelwa* mumilonga. = Snakes like to catch frogs in the rivers.
type of bird, black-shouldered kite, pl. *basyapililyo*, e.g. Bana bamisika *abasyapililyo* balalya nyama yabana bankuku. = The young of eagles and black-shouldered kites eat the flesh of chicks.
gecko (eater of wild cherries), e.g. Kwakaide kuloka *syazibumbu* munanda. = A gecko just dropped down in the house. Also *syaazibumbu*.
rough-skinned gecko, e.g. Nabwiinga wakongwa *syazikanka* naali kujika acikko. = The newly-wed woman was frightened by the gecko when she was cooking at the fireplace.
a buck-goat, e.g. Impongo zyangu tazijisi syeembwe ncozitazyali. = My goats do not produce because they have no buck-goat.
a monster, e.g. Abo bajisi mitwe mipati a masusu manji balangika mbuli ndinga syeenzimwe. = Those who have big heads and thick hair look like a big monster.
the wound that should not be tampered with, (tropical ulcer) e.g. Utacubili cilonda eco ngusyibangulwa. = Do not tamper with that wound as it is untouchable.
a headman, e.g. Kuli bukoko mumunzi wasyibbuku. = There is beer in the headman's village. Also sibbuku
a woman who can do the work which a man can do, e.g. Kachila, mukaintu wako ngusyimbilombe. = Kachila, your wife can do what men do. Also simbilombe

braided hair, e.g. Masusu akamwale akali kutalikwa kupumbwa ncobati 'syimbulumbumba' antela simpuke. = The hair of the initiate was smeared with oil to make it into a tuft that is why they call it syimbulumbumba or simpuke.
the common cold, e.g. Mwana uciswa syini. = The child has a cold.
a harmless green snake, e.g. Mainza wakajana nzoka syubusyubu munanda. Mainza found a harmless green snake in the house.
a cluster of ant-hills, e.g. Indyu izwa musyuuluulu. The mushroom known as 'indyu' germinates on a cluster of ant-hills. Also zyuuluulu
a type of hawk-like bird, e.g. Syuuluulu ulayanda kulya twana twankuku. = The hawk like to et chicks.
a type of bird, the honey-sucker, e.g. Syunsyubuluba ulasyuunta musinza wamaluba. The honey-sucker sucks the nectar of the flowers. Also kasyoma.

a lion, e.g. Syuumbwa waluma nombe muciba caba Simoonga. = A lion has attacked the cattle in Simoonga's kraal. Syuumbwa naakapenga wakabulya bwizu. = When the lion was suffering it ate grass. (i.e. In time of deprivation you have to act in an abnormal way.)

Victoria Falls, e.g. Basicikolo baya kukulanga Syuungu. Bataata babeleka kuli Syuungu Namutitima. = The pupils are going to look at the Falls. My father works at the Victoria Falls. taata my father, e.g. Taata wakanduuma nindakakaka kutumwa. = My father beat me when I refused to be sent.
my mother's brother (used by Zimbabwean Batonga), e.g. Bataatalenzi bakafwa jilo. = My matrilineal uncle died yesterday.
a net constriction-trap used in hunting cane rats and other small animals. e.g. Amukateye katabalangwe tujaye banyama. Will you set a constriction-trap so that we kill the animals. Also goba.

large earthen pot, e.g. Talo ncibiya cipati kapati icipambwa ngozi munsingo amwida. Lyakali lyakukumbila bukoko bwalo. = The 'talo' is a very big pot tied by string around the neck and stomach. It was used for brewing beer.
an old fancy name for the railway, e.g. Citima cilalunduka atalaa tandabala. = The train runs on the railway line.
a shallow bowl-cover, e.g. Kamuvwunisya tandabia ankwandi ijisi nsima. Cover the dish with a shallow bowl-cover.
crossroads, e.g. Kuli bantu basilikila bana babo _atantaanino_ anzila kutegwa bulwazi bucaale awo. = There are people who heal their children at a crossroads so that the disease remains there.
a kind of vegetable-relish (_Cissus intergrifolia_), e.g. Sunu twaliku-sunsa cisyu _catebelebe_. = Today we were dipping into a kind of vegetable-relish.
a children's traditional game, e.g. Wakajana bana ambo lyamunzi basobana _teezelele_. = He found children to the west of the village playing a traditional game.
hot ashes left by grass-fire.
a kind of vegetable-relish (_Cocculus hirsutus_), e.g. Sena mwajika _tende wakulisya nsima?_ = Have you cooked the relish for eating with the nsima?
footprint, e.g. Naakazinguluka nanda kunyina _tende_ ndyaakabona akali kuzyana syaazyana. = When he encircled the house he did not see any footprint of the dancer who was dancing.

a carrying-coop or cage for fowl, e.g. Kamuleta _tendele_ tubwezele nkuku zyabeenzu. = Bring a cage so that we take the chickens for the visitor. also cisekwe *tendemulumi* a type of vegetable relish (_Cissampelos mucronata_), e.g. Ba-simbi baunka kukucela _tendemulumi_. = The girls have gone off to gather a vegetable relish.

black locust-bird *tielele* a type of vegetable-relish (_Corchorus tridens_), e.g. Kuti wabula nyama nkulisya _tielele_. = If you have no meat you can eat the nsima with a vegetable-relish. Also kakonkwa.

a fat juicy edible insect which appears out of the ground after the first rains, e.g. Mutinta wakapiluka mbuli _tiingila_ litija muntu ulilindilila akapako mpolizwa. = Mutinta returned like a flying ant which flies away from a person who waits for it at the hole where it comes out. Also _matingatiila_.
a thrupenny piece, used in colonial times, e.g. Kaindi cinkwa cakali kuulwa buyo _tiki_. = Long ago bread was bought for three pence.

small antelope, e.g. Ndajana mwana _atimba_ musyokwe. = I have found the calf of a small antelope in the bush. _Katimba nkanyama kalunduka caampoonya._ = The small antelope is an animal which runs very fast for a short time.
a special kind of tuber, e.g. Bana basya _tinde_ wakusobanya. = The children dug out a tuber to play with.
a mason wasp, e.g. Kasana kalo kunengetela mbuli cibuno _catingatiila_. Her lower back narrowed like the waist of a mason wasp.
a monkey-apple, e.g. Wakali kutafwuna _tobo_. = He was chewing a monkey-apple.
a lizard, e.g. Kozwisya maziu _atombela mubusu_. = Remove the droppings of the lizard in the flour. Also dolo, syaadolyo. *sonsoolwe* = a lizard said to bite; _kabelebele_ = small with large head

tobacco; _tombwe wamungoma, tombwe wakufwinkila_ = snuff; _lubeko, pl. imbeko_ = snuff spoon; _mujike, namakati_ = boiled tobacco; _nalubotu_ = very strong; _mukweeka_ = less strong; _cisuku, kazyala-langa_ = tobacco plants; _cilundu_ = a tobacco cake; _kankomwa_ = small piece of tobacco cake.
or _-fwebya_ = give a little tobacco; _-sunza_ = ask for tobacco e.g. Ndisambala biyo _tombwe_ wacilundu. I am sellig a cake of tobacco. Ndifwezye tudyonko. = Give me unbaked-tobacco to taste.
dancing skirt e.g. Syaanasulwe wakasama *tubeensu* abukaano. = The hare wore a dancing skirt and a ceremonial-axe. Also *tubbesu*.
a double-valved fish-trap, e.g. Moonga ulobya *tubulu*, wajaya nswi zyobilo ciindi comwe. = Moonga who fishes with a double-valved fish trap, killed two fish at one go.
a vegetable-relish, e.g. Kauvwula mulilo cibizwe kabotu cisyu *catubwani*. = Increase the fire so that the vegetables are well cooked.
small frogs, pl. of *kadiika*, e.g. Ndalyata *tudiika* ancinga nindali kweenda munzila. = I crushed small frogs with the bicycle when I was going along the path.

wound copper, iron wire, e.g. Koleta wayile *watukakao* tuteye bakakololo. = Bring copper wire so that we trap the gerbilles. (a large burrowing mouse-like rodent found in arid regions of Africa and Asia).
beer, e.g. Mucembele ulakasaazya *tukeza* kumbali amulilo mukapali. Ulapapata *tukeza* notukasaala. = The old woman heats beer beside the fire in a small pot. She sips the beer when it is warm.
strings, e.g. Basimbi baloosa *tukole*, bazootungile bulungu buleta balombe. = The girls weave strings, they will string the beads which the boys bring.
small huts, e.g. Oyu munzi wakali mupati kapati cakuti kwakali *tukutakuta* tunji munzi oonse. = This village was so great that it was full of small huts everywhere.
small old hoes, e.g. Bamacembele balimya *tukutakuta* mumyuunda yabo. = The old women are using small old hoes in their fields.
trapping cords, e.g. *Tukuze* twabukusa ntuyumu kuteezya bakwale. = Sisal cords are strong for trapping partridges.
shoulder cords used by girls in dancing, e.g. Basimbi bakasamide *tukuze* bakazyana kabotu. = Girls who wore shouldercords danced well.
young mealie-cobs, e.g. Baceta balya *tukwapa* mucilili. = The monkeys are eating the young mealiecobs in the fertile reverine garden.

traditions, customs, practices, e.g. Kwakali *tumpiyompiyo* tumwi twakali kucitwa buzuba bunyugwa *Iwiindi*. = There were certain customs which were done on the day when they drank to honour the *Iwiindi* ceremony.
tame animals, like goats and cattle, e.g. Mebo ndiyanda buyo *tunamani*. = As for me I just like tame animals.

beer, e.g. Bukoko wakali kubupwaya ceetezya nkaambo nokuba kuti kwalampa buti kuli *tunambi* do mane mulombwana akasike. = He was addicted to beer in a sad way because no matter how far it was to the beer, the boy would reach it.
a type of small animal,/sing. kandonga, e.g. Kumazuba basimpongo balaya kukuteya *tundonga*. = In the evening the goatherds go to trap small animals.
slopes, e.g. Utani kutanti ncinga *mutungenyu* itajati ziimika. = Don't be riding the bicycle on the slopes when the brakes are not good
unanswerable guilt, e.g. Wakaba *tungungu* mpakkede nkaambo wakazulwa. = In his guilt he became unable to answer where he sat because he was convicted.

hinderances, e.g. Makani ndakaayendezya kuli bamukowa wangu, abasimukowa wamwinangu. Pele ndajana *tunkobe-tunkobe* okuya. = I took the matter to my clan and to the clan of my wife. But I found some obstacles over there.

traditions, customs, e.g. Bazyali bakacili kuyanda kutobela _tunsiyansiya_ twaciindi twakuvwuntauzya kumukwasyi nkwazyalwa musimbi. = The parents still wished to follow the traditional customs of the time in finding out about the family where the girl was born.
grass birds, e.g. Itanga _lyatuntengwe_ lilivwoomene mumbewu. = A flock of grass-birds have crowded into the garden.

type of bird (pl.) waxbill, robin, e.g. Anze kwakali kulila buyo tusise a _tuntiinga_ twakali kusekelela mvwula nkuyakali kuya kwaamuka. = Outside the blue-breasted robins and the waxbills were chirping to celebrate the rain as it was easing off. Also _intinga, syaantinga_
marshy ground, e.g. Bamwi bantu balima _mutuntulo_ twiide kumimita meenda coonse cacilimo. = Some people plough in marshy ground where water is oozing out all through the dry season.
politics, e.g. Mulwiiyo, mu bulimi a _mutunzanyu_, tweelede kugwasyigwa a bamwi. In education, in farming and in politics, we ought to be helped by others.
hollow bits of stick worn on the arms as charms.

traditions, customs, e.g. _Tupiyopiyo_ tuzumizya mujwanyoko kukusabauzya. = Traditions permit your cousin to joke with you. (Often in an unpleasant way) Bujwanyina bulaa _tupiyopiyo_ tunji. = The tradition of the 'joking relationship' has many little customs. Also _tumpiyo-piyo_
bracelets, armbands of _wijele_ grass, e.g. Bakaindi bakali kusama _tusambo_ mumaboko. The people of the past were wearing bracelets on their arms.
sandals, e.g. Simpongo usama **tusangu** (_mpato_) kumaulu akaambo kazuba litenta. The goatherd is wearing sandals on the feet because of the burning sun.

pl. of _kasise_, the blue-breasted robin **tusukuza** bundles of beads, e.g. Wakaulisya musimbi ankaya zyobile a _tusukuza_ twabulungu totatwe twampasela. He sold the girl for two bangles and three bundles of beads added on.
remnants of a liquid.
little heaps, e.g. _Atuulunzuma_ mpenja kuyotelela zuba. = On little mounds of earth is where I will warm myself in the sun.
millions, e.g. Bausyi bakabikkide kale _tuulunzuma_ twamali mubbanga. = His father had put millions of money in the bank.
the fins of a fish, e.g. Inswi ikonzya kuyamba nkaambo ilijisi _tuyambyo_. Fish are able to swim because they have fins.
footpaths, sidewalks, e.g. Mumadolopo basimaulu beendela mu _tuzilambali_. In the cities the pedestrians walk along the sidewalks.
marks, e.g. Bapulisa bakajana _tweengo_ twazisimbo zyaminwe akabbokesi. The police found the marks of fingerprints on the box.
flexible branches used for making baskets (osier = a small willow of damp habitats with long flexible shoots used in baskerwork)

a blister, pl. _matwizya_, e.g. Ndabaa _matwizya_ mumaanza nkaambo mwiini wakeembe nkindakali kubelesya tiiwakali kabotu. = I have blisters on my hands because the handle of the axe which I was using was not good.

a form of traditional marriage practiced in the Zambezi valley, e.g. Mutendu wakakwatwa kabotu munzila yalukwatano *itegwa tyombo*. = *Mutendu* got married properly according to the marriage-ritual called *tyombo*.
owner of the land, Also *sikatongo, sibulongo*

a wild dog, pl. *baumpe*, e.g. *Bana nibali kweembela basune babona tanga lyabaumpe*. When the children were herding the oxen they saw a pack of wild dogs. *Baumpe balamukoma syuumbwa*. Wild dogs can defeat a lion. (Note. the wild dog is the totem of the Bantanga clan.)

caterpillar, e.g. *Mmwanakazi muteteete mubili mbuli vwiya*. = She was a woman of soft body like a caterpillar *Mumaboko munanga wakajisi boya bunji mboojene vwiya*. = The witchdoctor had much hair just like a caterpillar.

the pouched rat, e.g. *Vwuku nimbeba ijisi masanta*. = The pouched rat is one which has protruding cheeks. *Akalo aka kana kalaa mambeke nkokaide kukomenzya masaya ulati nguvwuku*. = And that child is full of impudence as her cheeks just swell you would say she is a pouched rat. Also *vwuku-vwuku*, pl. *bavwuku-vwuku*
coconut, e.g. *Wakawidilidwe vwuma mubulimi*. = A coconut had fallen on his head in farming. (i.e. he had done very well in farming.)
hyaena, e.g. *Mweenzuma walumwa vwuunkununu*. = My friend was attacked by a hyaena. Also suntwe

an illegal marriagecustom, e.g. Wakati, *"Eeci cilengwa ca "wakamvwani" ncibi kapati nkaambo kunyina bulemu muli ncico kunze lyakutyokezya luyando lwabantu*. This custom of 'wakamvwani' is very bad because there is not honour in it but it only breaks the love of people.
a mussel shell, e.g. *Koleta wili tukwizinge cibiya*. Bring a shell so that we polish the pot. Also *Iwiili, njili*
a flood, e.g. *Izambangulwe lyameenda amvwula lyakavwumba nyika mazuba makumi one*. = The flood from rain water covered the earth for forty days.

a Zambezi shark (sharks, before Kariba was built, penetrated the Zambezi river as far as Sinazongwe), e.g. *Lusabwi Iwamudaala Iwakazapuka nikwakanjila zenimutendu*. = The net of the old man was torn when a shark entered it.
a tablet of dried clay, e.g. *Kamubikka zizetego munsi acikala tulyatile notuteka meenda*. Put slabs of dried clay near the well so that we can step on them when we are drawing water.

buy cheaply and resell at a higher price. e.g. *Oobu bukoko bwakali bukali. Bantu bakabumana kapati baya bakali kooda bwazibbejo*. = This beer was strong. The people finished it, especially those who wanted to sell it at a higher price.
bags, e.g. *Busu buli muzidubulu*. The maize-flour is in the bags. *zifwapu* shavings Also *zipapa, zifwapulo*
mirages, e.g. *Wakabona zigudugudu zilaintuka kumbele*. = He saw mirages appearing before him.
assorted items in a heap or bundle, e.g. *Zigwede-gwede zyesu zyoonse zyakabola akuyeemuka*. = All our various items in the heap got rotten and melted.
packets, e.g. *Bakabona zijumba-jumba zyabusu zyakali ambali akamando* = They saw packets of meal which were beside the tavern.
the tree-dwelling iguana, e.g. *Nkaanga zilinde kalikkede mumusamu*. = The iguana is sitting in a tree.
an iguana (lives in holes in trees), pl. *bazilindi*, e.g. *Bazilindi bamwi* bakkala mumena. = Some iguanas live in holes.
smell of burning meat.

spirits of dead relatives which may enter the living bringing sickness. Delivery comes through fumigation and the beating of metal objects. e.g. Muntu wanjilwa zilube umpililwa musamu kutegwa zizwe. = A person possessed by bad spirits is fumigated to let them out. Also zyeelo
a type of bird, the widow-bird, e.g. Ceeye eci cazilutundu ncilamfwu. = This tail of the widow-bird is long. Also zilintunda
a small type of rain-shrine, (Zimbabwe) e.g. Atukakambile mvwula kumalende a zimbahwe. = Let us go and clap for rain at the small rain-shrine.

spirits of the dead who have been killed and come back for revenge, pl. of cibandwa, e.g. Ceelo camuntu wakajaigwa, icibandwa cakajokelela kujaya muntu wakajaya. = The spirit of the murdered person, known as cibandwa, returned to kill the murderer. Also zibanda
new shoots of feathers, e.g. Bana bankuku bakatalika kale kubaa zimenenwa. = The chicks have already started to grow new feathers.

meat fat around the lips of someone who has been eating meat, e.g. Waakubujana kuli bwaawo bwanyama busakamuna mate mukanwa? Toonse twaba azimwengela kumilomo. = Where did you get this appetizing meat? All our lips have become oily.
wild thorny round fruits, e.g. Zincenya zilayasa cilimo. = Wild thorny round fruits pierce during the dry season.

a type of bird, the small quail, pl. bazingi, e.g. Basankwa bavwima bazingi mumagundu. = The boys are hunting small quails in the unused fields. Basankwa bakatandila nkiinga zingi, kayuni nkaakali kunumfwida mubwa wabo. = The boys chased a young quail which their dog had sniffed out.

a very stupid person, e.g. Ooyu musankwa mmufwubafwuba, zinya lyamuntu, utakwe maanu, utayeeyi, utalibeteki, utalibuzi. = This boy is foolish, a stupid person, who is without wisdom, who does not think, who does not judge himself, who does not question.
small pools of water after rains, e.g. Okuno mvwula tiiyakomena, yasiya buyo zinywankuku. = Here the rain did not increase, it just left small pools of water.
couch grass, (a course grass with long creeping roots) e.g. Musimbi wakalilede ansi muli zinza. = The girl was lying on the ground on the couch grass.

a medicine given to a baby to protect it from the disease called luvwume, e.g. Imwi misamu isigwa miyanda akukasaazigwa akunywisya mwana kukobelela luvwumwe njeeyi: lubabangwe, ntendele zipati a zinza. = Some medicines whose roots are dug and soaked in warm water that are given to the baby to drink to protect it from the disease called luvwumwe (non-closure of the fontanelle) are these: lubabangwe, ntendele zipati and zinza.
a type of dance. e.g. Insete basimbi bakali kuzisama kungoma akuzipelu insiku. = Long ago the girls used to wear skirts of hanging-strings when they went to dance the *ngoma* and *zipelu* dances.
immature green maize, e.g. Bana bakali kukunya zisyanje nibakafwa nzala. = The children were gnawing the unripened green maize when they were hungry. Also minyonje
a style of cutting hair, e.g. Nsiku balombe bakalikunyoolwa zitengu alunyoolo. = Long ago the boys were shaved all around the head below the ears with a razor. Also ntengu.

hiding place for a duiker e.g. Wakabweza jamba wakaya kuzuka nkwaakabwene insya. Mbwaakasikila muzuka wakasya mulindi mulamfwu. = He took a hoe and went to the animal's hiding place where he had seen a duiker. As soon as he arrived at the hiding place he dug a deep hole. Also izuka, nkona, budoli.
an addax, large antelope with twisted and curved horns, e.g. Bavwimi batanda zupwi. = The hunters are chasing a large addax. Also muzilawa, syaambololo.
a type of bird, the warbler, e.g. Kwiimba kwazwilili kulanonezya. = The chirping of the warbler is beautiful.
a wild duck, e.g. Badaala badubula bazwizwi mudamu. = The old man is shooting wild ducks in the dam.
wrists, e.g. Kutusindi amuzyaanko zyamaanza wakalikwamaukide akaambo kamamba. = Because of fighting his ankles and wrists were cracked.

medicines, e.g. Usyi wakafwumide kale kuzwa kacili kambunde kuya kuyandaula zyani-zyani mubantu banyeni (basimukobonyina). = The father had already gone out when it was still early in the morning to look for medicines from the neighbours.
the largest barbel, e.g. Muswi oyu wandaalila kuula, nguzyeni. = I cannot buy this large fish, it is a big barbel. Also heni.

an assortment of insects, e.g. Nkujana kufwumbwa mpaalyata mpaatalaa bufwefwelenga bwazyuukauka zyamyakaamyaka zyakali kufwa. = He found that wherever he trod he stepped on bits of insects that died many years ago.
